The printed edition that forms of the basis of this electronic edition is in the Devanāgarī script. The Devanāgarī version of this electronic edition was produced by double-keyboarding. The Romanized version was produced by automatic transliteration of the Devanāgarī version, using the standard IAST scheme of transliteration. Note that the printed edition is based on a single manuscript, and corrections to that manuscript are often made in the text rather than the apparatus. body.translated_text: || <s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness) ||

body.text: सिंहलाचार्यरत्नश्रीज्ञानकृतया रत्नश्रिया टीकया समलंकृतम् आचार्यदण्डिकृतं काव्यलक्षणम् ।
body.translated_text: <s>Kāvyalakṣaṇa</s> (The Characteristics of Poetry) composed by <s>Ācārya Daṇḍin</s>, adorned with the commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>) called <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, composed by <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, the jewel of wisdom of the <s>Siṃhala</s> (Sinhalese) lineage of teachers.

children.translated_text: First <s>Pariccheda</s> (<s>Mārgavibhāga</s>)
The first chapter, named <s>Mārgavibhāga</s> (Division of Paths).
May <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the swan-bride of the lotus-face of the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>), /
all white, sport forever in my mind-lake (<s>mānasa</s>)! // 1 //

children.text: मातृकाया आदिमं पत्रत्रितयं प्रच्युतम् । तेन टीकाकर्तुर्मङ्गलांचरणं व्याख्या चादिमयोः श्लोकयोः पूर्णतया, तृतीयस्य च भागशो नष्टा । आदशमं पत्रेषु पुनरांशिकी त्रुटिः ।

children.translated_text: Having collected the earlier treatises and having observed [actual] usage, /
this <s>Kāvyalakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics of Poetry) is composed by us to the best of our ability. // 2 //
Here, of the cultured and of those instructed by the cultured, and indeed of the refined in every way, /
by the grace of speech alone does the conduct of the world proceed. // 3 //
From the division of faults, properly..........mallanāga........by virtue of having the nature of established conduct of the world —

children.text: इति । विशिष्टा लोकयात्रा [अ]भिप्रेता न तु या काचित् । सा [वाक्शास्त्ररूपे]ति तदभावे यथोक्तलोकयात्रानुपपत्तेश्च अन्यत्रापि यथासम्भवं सामान्यशब्दात् विशेषः प्रसत्तव्यः । प्रसादेन प्रभावान्न..........। अतएव चतुर्वर्गशासनात् शास्त्रा[णां] चतुर्वर्गविद्याश्रयत्वात् विद्याश्रयस्थानानीति च निरुच्यते । तानि च [श्रुति]स्मृत्यादीनि संस्कृतमयानीत्याह [शिष्टानुशिष्टानामिति । शिष्टाः] [शब्दा]नुशासनकृतः पाणिनिप्रभृतयः । तैरनुशिष्टाः संस्कृताः प्रकृतिप्रत्ययादिविभागकल्पनयाऽन्वा[ख्याताः] तासां वाचां, श्रुतिस्मूत्यादीनि हि चतु[र्वर्गसाधनानि] [सं]स्कृतमयानि दृश्यन्ते ।
children.translated_text: thus. A distinguished conduct of the world is intended, not just any kind. That [distinguished conduct rests on] the form of the science of speech, and since without it the aforementioned conduct of the world would be impossible, elsewhere too, as applicable, the particular should be understood from the general term. 'By grace' means 'by power'.......... Therefore, because [the sciences] govern the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>), since the sciences depend on the four aims of life, they are etymologized as 'the abodes of knowledge.' And those [sciences] consisting of <s>Śruti</s> (revelation), <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), and so forth are in Sanskrit — thus he says 'of the cultured and those instructed by the cultured.' The cultured (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) are the authors of grammar, <s>Pāṇini</s> and others. Those instructed by them (<s>anuśiṣṭa</s>) are the Sanskrit [words] — analyzed through the division of root, suffix, and so on. Of those words — for <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and the rest, which are the means of the four aims of life, are seen to be in Sanskrit.

children.text: ननु भाषान्तरैरपि चतुर्वर्गप्रतीतिलक्षणा लोकयात्रा प्रवर्तमाना दृ[श्यमाना]स्ति । तदपि श्रुत्यादिमूलमित्यतिदिशन्नाह- शिष्टा[नाम]पीति । शिष्टानुशिष्टेभ्यो बाह्याः शिष्टाः परिशिष्टाः । उपयुक्तादन्यः शेष इति । तासां [परिशिष्टानां शास्त्रव्यवहार]स्थित्या अपभ्रंशसंगृहीतानाम् । यद् वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: 'In the treatises, whatever is other than Sanskrit is declared as <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> (corrupted form).'

children.text: एवं मन्यते...[इ]दमत्र तावत् तात्प[र्यम्]........[लो]कयात्रा शास्त्रप्रभावादेवेति । तत्तु शास्त्रं संस्कृतमयं वा । भाषान्तरस्वभावं प्रायस्तु संस्कृतमयं दृश्यत इति । अत एवाह- शि[ष्टानुशिष्टानां.........एवं शास्त्रादेव सा । संस्कृतेतरलक्षणस्तु तद्विकल्प एव । अतः सर्वथा सर्वप्रकारेण एकान्तेन संस्कृतादवशिष्टाद् वा शास्त्रादेव लोक[यात्रा प्रवर्तते ।] काव्यं चेदं चतुर्वर्गलक्षणम् । अत्रापि गुणदोषविवेचने शास्त्रं शरणमित्याकूतम् । वक्ष्यति च—
children.translated_text: Thus he holds...... The purport here is as follows: the conduct of the world is rooted in the science (<s>śāstra</s>) alone. And that science is either in Sanskrit or of the nature of another language — but predominantly it is seen to be in Sanskrit. Therefore he says 'of the cultured and those instructed by the cultured'......... thus [the conduct of the world proceeds] from science alone. That which has the character of non-Sanskrit is merely a variant of it. Therefore, in every way, by every manner, the conduct of the world proceeds exclusively from science, whether in Sanskrit or in what remains [besides Sanskrit]. And this poetry too has the character of the four aims of life. Here too, in the discernment of merits and faults, science is the refuge — this is the intention. And he will state —
'One who does not know the science, the merits and faults —'

children.text: इत्यादिना । यत् पुनर[त्र........का]रणमन्यद् वा यथा कथञ्चिद् घुणाक्षरप्रख्यं दृश्यते तत्रापि शास्त्रमस्तीति तद्विदां प्रयोगपथानुसारात् स्यात् । जन्मान्तरे वा कृतशास्त्राभ्या[सप्रति (4b) बु]द्धसंस्काराणां परिनिष्ठितमपि स्यात् । यान् सारस्वताननधीतपण्डितान् वा व्यवहरति लोकः । यदपि सरस्वतीप्रसादात् काव्यकरणादिकमिष्टम्, तदपि शास्त्रप्र[भाव]........प्रभावितत्वात् । किं बहुना ? सर्वलोकयात्रा चतुर्वर्गव्युत्पत्तिलक्षणा शास्त्रादेव । तस्मादिदमपि काव्यगुणदोषव्युत्पत्त्यर्थं करणीयमेव, यतः परिनि[ष्ठितं काव्यं जाय]त इति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: and so forth. Whatever further...... cause or other is seen here somehow, resembling chance marks of insects [on wood], even there, science exists — this would be from following the path of practice of those who know it. Or it would be fully accomplished for those whose dispositions were awakened through the practice of science in previous births — those whom the world calls 'gifted by <s>Sarasvatī</s>' or 'naturally learned scholars.' Even what is considered to come from the grace of <s>Sarasvatī</s> for the composition of poetry and the like, that too is...... because it is influenced by the power of science. In short — all conduct of the world, characterized by proficiency in the four aims of life, proceeds from science alone. Therefore, this too must be composed for the sake of proficiency in poetic merits and faults, from which perfectly accomplished poetry arises — this is the purport.

Objection: Even through other languages, the conduct of the world characterized by the understanding of the four aims of life is seen to proceed. To extend [the principle] to that as well, saying that it too is rooted in <s>Śruti</s> and the rest, he says 'and of the refined' (<s>śiṣṭānām api</s>). Those external to the ones instructed by the cultured are the 'refined' (<s>śiṣṭa</s>), meaning the 'remaining' (<s>pariśiṣṭa</s>) — 'what is other than what is useful is the remainder.' Of those remaining [words], standing in the convention of treatises, comprehended by <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> (corrupt forms). As he will state —

children.text: एवमन्वयेत लोकयात्रां शास्त्रमूलां प्रतिपाद्यैतदेव व्यतिरेकेण द्रढयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Having thus established that the conduct of the world is rooted in science through positive correlation, now strengthening the same through negative correlation, he says —
This entire universe of three worlds would become total darkness, /
if the light called 'speech' did not shine forth from the beginning of the world cycle. // 4 //

children.text: यदनन्तरमुक्तं लोकया[त्रा]...........ज्योतिरालोकः शब्दाह्वयं शास्त्रसंज्ञकं चतुर्वर्गप्रकाशकत्वात् । शब्द इत्याह्वयो यस्येति विग्रहे, यदि न दीप्यते न प्रकाशते न स्यादित्यर्थः । के...........रोऽत्र सत्त्वलोकः । यश्चतुर्वर्गमनुतिष्ठति तत् मर्यादं[?] ये तु मुक्तास्तेषां न संसारात्मकत्वम्, नापि चतुर्वर्गानुष्ठानम् । सर्व......[स्व]र्गमर्त्यपाताललक्षणं जगत्रयं सत्त्वलोकः यस्य चतुर्वर्गप्रतिपत्तिः सम्भवति । इदमिति । अत्य......तेन वा तमोऽन्ध[कारः]........[ल]क्षणलोकयात्राविगमात् । अप्रतिपत्तिकसं[सारा]त्मकं स्यादित्यर्थः । किमेकदेशेन, नेत्याह- कृत्स्नमिति । निरवशेषं नांशेन तथाप्य[ल्पम्, नेत्या]ह- अन्धमिति । अन्धं निरन्तरम[ज्ञानतमोयोगात्] चतुर्वर्गप्रतिपत्तेः कथञ्चिदप्यभावात् सर्वथा निवृत्तचतुर्वर्गज्ञानात्मकं जगत् स्यात् । न क[थञ्चिद् वस्तुप्रति]पत्तिर्भवेदित्यर्थः । यद् वा, अन्धंतम.....[पृ]षोदरादिदर्शनात् सिद्धम् । अर्थस्तु स एव । समाधिश्चैष सर्वथाऽज्ञाने निवृत्ते सर्वमत्र गृह्यते [अन्व]यव्यतिरेकाभ्याम् । शास्त्राभ्यासः काव्यगुणदोषविवेकार्थं क्रियत इति पूर्ववदाकूतम् । अत एवोच्यते—
children.translated_text: What was stated immediately after — the conduct of the world......... The light means illumination; 'called speech' means 'bearing the designation of science,' because it illuminates the four aims of life. In the analysis 'that whose designation (<s>āhvaya</s>) is speech (<s>śabda</s>)' — 'if it did not shine' means 'if it did not illuminate,' i.e. 'if it did not exist.'...... The world of sentient beings is meant here — those who practice the four aims of life, that boundary. But the liberated, they have no nature of worldly existence, nor the practice of the four aims. All...... the three worlds characterized by heaven, earth, and netherworld — the world of sentient beings for whom the attainment of the four aims is possible. 'This' means...... or darkness — the cessation of the conduct of the world characterized by...... It would become of the nature of a cycle of existence without apprehension. Why only partially? No — he says 'entirely' (<s>kṛtsnam</s>). Completely, not partially; even so, a little? No — he says 'blind' (<s>andham</s>). Blind means continuous, from being joined with the darkness of ignorance, because of the utter impossibility of the attainment of the four aims — the world would be entirely devoid of the knowledge of the four aims. There would be no apprehension of reality whatsoever — this is the meaning. Alternatively, 'andhaṃtama'...... is established from examples like <s>pṛṣodarādi</s>. The meaning is the same. And this conclusion is: when ignorance is completely removed in every way, everything here is grasped — through both positive and negative correlation. The practice of science is undertaken for the sake of discerning poetic merits and faults — this is the intention as before. Therefore it is said —
From science alone, everywhere, is the examination of merits and faults. /
Without science, that which.....................

children.text: ......घटकं शास्त्रविशेष एष वस्तुतः । तत्रापि चतुर्वर्गप्रतिपत्तेः । यद् वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: 'Dependent on the fruit of the four aims of life' — and so forth.
Poetry thus is established as..........enough with elaboration.
...... this is essentially a specific science that constitutes [all the rest]. Even therein, because of the attainment of the four aims. As he will state —
Summarizing the very same science from another perspective, he says —
Having found in the mirror of literature the reflection of the glory of the primeval kings, /
even in their absence, it does not perish by itself. // 5 //

children.text: आदयः आद्याः पूर्वे राजानः मन्वा[द्याः] तेषामादिराजानां [गुणख्यापकं कर्म] यशस्करत्वाद् यश इत्युक्तम् । गुणा हि साक्षात् तेषां शास्त्रे काव्ये वा वर्ण्यन्ते । गुणानां तु प्रसिद्धिः सर्वलोककीर्त्तनं यशः । तदेव [श]रीरं सत्पुरुषाणां........., शरीरप्र[तिमत्वात् । त]दुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: The primeval kings — the first, ancient kings, <s>Manu</s> and others. Of those primeval kings, their deeds that proclaim their virtues — these are called 'glory' (<s>yaśas</s>) because of being productive of fame. For their virtues are directly described in the sciences and in poetry. And the renown of their virtues — the celebration by all the world — is their glory. That alone is the body of great men........, because of its similarity to a bodily form. As it is said —
'Even more than one's own body, let alone sense-objects, /
for those whose wealth is fame, fame is the greater [treasure].'

children.text: तदेतत् । वागिह इतिहासकथादिलक्षणा, आदिरा[जयशः]कीर्त्तनात् । तत्स्वभावमादर्शं दर्पणम् वैमल्यात्, प्राप्य तत्र प्रतिभाय तत्प्रत्ययारूढं स्वयमात्मना न नश्यति नापगच्छति यस्येति विस्मापयन्नभिमुखयति परम् । कोऽत्र विस्मय इ[ति चेत् ?] तेषामसन्निधानेऽपीति तेषामादिराजानां येषां तद्बिम्बम् । असन्निधानेऽपि अभावेऽपि । इदमत्र चित्रं यत् तद्वतोऽपगमेऽपि बिम्बं नापैति । दर्पणे हि तावद् बिम्बं दृश्यते [यावद् वस्तुस]न्निधानम् । अपगते तु तद्वति शरीरेऽपैति । सोऽयं प्रसिद्धादर्शविलक्षणोऽपूर्व एव कश्चिदादर्शः, यत्रादिराजलक्षणस्य तद्वतोऽसन्निधावपि इदानीम्[अपि] बिम्बं दृश्यते, न केवलं सन्निधान इत्यपिशब्दार्थः । अतिशये वाऽपिशब्दो वर्तते । असन्निधानेऽप्यहो दृश्यत इत्यतिशयः । अत एव सर्वा[तिशायी] सनातनः कोऽप्ययमालोको लोकयात्राप्रवृत्तये । कुतोऽप्ययमाभाति यदुत शास्त्रं नामेति ॥
children.translated_text: This is that [principle]. Speech here means that which has the nature of <s>itihāsa</s> (epic history), narratives, and the like — because it celebrates the glory of the primeval kings. Having reached that mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>), whose nature is speech — a mirror, because of its purity — having been reflected therein, having ascended to the cognition thereof, [the glory] does not perish of itself, does not depart — this is astonishing, and he draws the listener's attention. What is the wonder here? — [He answers:] 'even in their absence' — even in the absence of those primeval kings whose reflection it is. Even in their absence, i.e. even in their non-existence. The wonder here is this: even when the possessor of the reflection has departed, the reflection does not depart. For in a [real] mirror, a reflection is seen only so long as the object is present. But when the possessor [of the reflection] — the body — departs, [the reflection] departs too. This is an extraordinary, unprecedented kind of mirror, in which the reflection of the primeval kings, even when the possessors [of those reflections] are now absent, is still seen — not only when they are present; this is the meaning of the word 'even' (<s>api</s>). Alternatively, the word 'api' functions in the sense of excess: even in their absence — astonishing! — it is seen! Therefore this is a supremely surpassing, eternal, ineffable illumination for the functioning of the world's conduct — this somehow shines from some [source], namely what is called 'science.'
Since the discernment of merits and faults proceeds from science, what constitutes a merit? To this he says —
Speech (<s>gauḥ</s>) — like a cow (<s>gauḥ</s>) — when properly employed, is celebrated by the wise as a wish-fulfilling cow (<s>kāmadudhā</s>); /
but the very same, when poorly employed, declares the bovine nature (<s>gotva</s>) of the speaker! // 6 //

children.text: गौर्वाक् काव्यादिस्वभावा । सम्यक् शास्त्रादिप्रभावेण स्वरूपतोऽर्थतश्च परिशुद्धा

प्रयुक्ता कृता प्रकाशिता सती पुरुषेणेति गम्यते । काम[दुघा]......रिति वक्ष्यमाणमत्रापि सम्बन्धनीयम् । गौः सौरभेयी स्मर्यते आम्नायते बुधैराप्तैः । एवमाप्ता उपदिशन्ति, तस्मादवितथमेतत् । आप्तोपदेशस्य प्रमाणत्व[निश्चयात्][तदनुसरणत]श्चेष्टसिद्धिदर्शनात् । या वागेवं कामधेनुर्जाता सुप्रयुक्ता सती सैव नान्या । दुष्प्रयुक्ता पुनः शास्त्रविरोधात् स्वभावाश्रयवैगुण्येनोद्भाविता तु सतो गोत्वं [पशुत्वं शं]सति ख्यापयति प्रयोक्तुः पुरुषस्य । ततश्चाशास्त्रज्ञोऽयं पुरुषाकृतिः पशुरिति विदुषां हेयः स्यादित्यनर्थे पतितः । दूर एवार्थसिद्धिः । तदिह म[हद]न्तरं शास्त्र[ज्ञानेन भवति । मनुष्यत्वा]
children.translated_text: 'employed' means made, manifested — by a person, it is understood. [The word] 'wish-fulfilling cow (<s>kāmadudhā</s>)'...... what will be stated [later] should also be connected here. [The word] 'cow' (<s>gauḥ</s>) means [literally] a bovine. 'Is celebrated' means 'is taught' by the wise, i.e. the authoritative. Thus the authoritative instruct, therefore this is not false — because of the certainty that the teaching of the authoritative is a valid means of knowledge, and because the desired result is seen from following it. That very speech which has thus become a wish-fulfilling cow when well employed — that same one, not another — when poorly employed, i.e. when manifested with defects in its essential support, contrary to science — then declares, i.e. proclaims, the bovine nature (<s>gotva</s>), i.e. the animality (<s>paśutva</s>), of the speaker, the person. Consequently, 'this person in human form is [really] an animal, ignorant of science' — he would be rejected by the learned, and thus falls into misfortune. Far indeed is the attainment of [any] purpose. Here, then, the difference [is] great through the knowledge of science. Even though both share human nature, one who knows the science is worshipped like a god by those who love virtues, while the other is regarded like an animal.

children.text: विशेषेऽपि शास्त्रज्ञो देव इव पूज्यते गुणानुरागिभिरितरस्तु पशुरिव दृश्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Even though both share human nature, one who knows the science is worshipped like a god by those who love virtues, while the other is regarded like an animal.
Speech (<s>gauḥ</s>) means words whose nature is poetry and the like. 'Properly' (<s>samyak</s>) means purified in form and meaning by the power of science and the like,

children.text: यत एवं सर्वत्र गुणदोषविवेकः शास्त्रादेव । गुणश्च पुरुषार्थेन योजयति दोषश्च [इतरेण, अतः] शास्त्रानुसारेण गुणवत् [काव्यमेकान्ततः] पुरुषार्थसाधनम् । दोषस्तु स्वल्पोऽपि शास्त्रप्रभावादेवापनेयः । अन्यथा हेयं स्यादिति प्रकृतमनुबध्नन् आह—
children.translated_text: Since thus the discernment of merits and faults everywhere proceeds from science alone, and merit connects [one] with the aims of life while fault [connects with] the opposite — therefore, following science, meritorious poetry is absolutely the means to the aims of life. But even a small fault should be removed solely by the power of science. Otherwise [the poetry] would be rejectable. Connecting this to the topic at hand, he says —
Therefore, even slightly flawed poetry should not be disregarded in any way; /
for even a beautiful body becomes unfortunate through a single [spot of] leprosy. // 7 //

'Flawed poetry should not be disregarded in any way' — here too this should be applied. By no manner whatsoever should it be disregarded. It should be corrected in every way, from the perspective of science. Otherwise it would be rejectable. Establishing this very [point]

children.text: क्ष्यं कथञ्चनेत्यत्रापि योज्यम् । केनापि प्रकारेण नोपेक्षणीयम् । सर्वथाऽपनेयमेव शास्त्रदृष्टया । अन्यथा हेयं स्यात् । तदेव प्रतिवस्तूपमया साधयन्नाहस्यादित्यादि [वपुः शरीरं सुन्दरम]पि वर्णसंस्थानसम्पन्नमपि प्रागेवासुन्दरम् । एकेन श्वित्रेण कुष्ठदोषेण दुर्भगमस्पृश्यं हेयं स्यात् । सुन्दरमपि शरीरं कुष्टेन स्वल्पेनाप्युप [पन्नं हेयं यथा] तथा कवेः काव्यमयं शरीरं शाश्वतं सर्वार्थसाधनं स्वल्पेनापि शब्दरूपेणार्थलक्षणेन वा दोषेण श्वित्रकल्पेन परिहरणीयं स्यात् । प्रागेव......द्धं कार्यं करणीयम् । दोषस्तु स्वल्पोऽपि परिहरणीयः शास्त्रदृष्टयेति ।
children.translated_text: through <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-example simile), he says 'it would be' and so forth. A body (<s>vapus</s>), though beautiful, i.e. though endowed with excellent complexion and form — even before being [considered] ugly — through a single [spot of] leprosy (<s>śvitra</s>), becomes unfortunate (<s>durbhaga</s>), untouchable, rejectable. Just as even a beautiful body, when afflicted with even a small [spot of] leprosy, becomes rejectable, so too the poet's body in the form of poetry — which is eternal and the means of all purposes — should be freed of even a small fault in word-form or meaning-form, which is like a [spot of] leprosy...... the work should be done first. Even a small fault should be corrected from the perspective of science.

children.text: क्रियत एव निर्दोषं काव्यं विनापि शास्त्रेणेत्याशङ्क्य सर्वं शास्त्रादेव गुणदोष[परिज्ञानं कर्तव्यमि]ति पूर्वोक्तक्रमेणार्थं प्रतिवस्तूपमया समर्थयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that 'flawless poetry is indeed composed even without science,' and [showing that] all discernment of merits and faults must be done from science alone, corroborating the meaning in the previously stated manner through <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-example simile), he says —
How can a person ignorant of science distinguish merits from faults? /
Does a blind person have any competence in the perception of differences in form? // 8 //

children.text: गुणा विशेषा उपादेया अर्थाः पुरुषार्थसंगृहीतास्तद्विपरीता दोषाः ।......काव्यापेक्षया तु शब्दार्थालङ्कारस्वभावा गुणाः । दोषास्त्वपार्थत्वादयः । श्लेषविपर्यासादयश्च

वैदर्भमार्गापेक्षया वक्ष्यमाणाः । अत एव सामान्येनाह—गुणदोषानशास्त्रज्ञः कथं विभजते जनःइति । सर्वमपि सा[मान्यं ए]कस्याप्यर्थस्य प्रकृतापेक्षया विशेषनिष्ठं भविष्यतीति निपुणेयं वाचोयुक्तिः । तान् गुणदोषान् यो न वेत्ति पुरुषः[स] कथं विभजते [विभक्तान्करो]ति एते गुणाः [एते दोषा इ]ति । य[तो गुणानाद]त्ते दोषान हास्यति कथञ्चित् । किं न विभजते, अशास्त्रज्ञो यतः । शास्त्रादेव हि गुणदोषा विवेच्यन्ते । यश्च शास्त्रं गुणदोषविवेक[विष]
children.translated_text: which will be stated with reference to the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path. Therefore he states in general terms: 'How can a person ignorant of science distinguish merits from faults?' All that is general, even of a single meaning, will become particular with reference to the relevant context — this is a subtle principle of verbal interpretation. Those merits and faults — one who does not know them, that person — how can he distinguish them, i.e. make the distinction 'these are merits, these are faults'? Since he neither adopts the merits nor discards the faults in any way. Why can he not distinguish? Because he is ignorant of science. For merits and faults are discerned from science alone. And one who [does not know] the science for the discernment of merits and faults —

children.text: यं न वेत्ति, कथं तस्याप्रतिपन्नोपायस्य गुणदोषविवेकलक्षणमुपेयं सेत्स्यति । यथा त्वस्य रूपव......................किमन्धस्येत्यादि । अन्धस्य चक्षुर्विकलस्य रूपभेदानां नीलपीतादीनां रूपविशेषाणां उप[ल]ब्धिषु दर्शने[षु नाधिंकारः । इ ]ह सामान्येन रूपं नाम किञ्चिदस्तीति श्रुतिमात्रकमपश्यतः स्यात् । न तु रूपविशेषसाक्षात्का[रः । विशेषज्ञानाभावे] न च तत् क्वचिदुपयुज्यते । ततो यदाहमनुष्ठाना[?]भावाद् विभागेन तु सर्वात्मना शास्त्र......[विभ]जत इत्याह । तदेवमियता ग्रन्थेन शास्त्रादेव सर्वगुणदोषविवेकतो नान्यथा काव्येऽपि......
children.translated_text: That which one does not know — how will the goal, characterized as the discrimination of merits and faults, be achieved for one who has not understood the means? Just as his form...... what [can be said] of a blind person? — and so on. A blind person, one whose eye is impaired, has no qualification for the perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>) — i.e., the seeing — of particular forms such as blue, yellow, etc. Here, a general [awareness] that 'there is something called form' may exist for one who does not see, based on mere report. But there is no direct realization of particular forms. In the absence of particular knowledge, it is not useful anywhere. Therefore, [the author] says that in the absence of practice, the <s>śāstra</s> (science) completely classifies [merits and faults] by division...... Thus, by this much text, [it is established that] the discrimination of all merits and faults in poetry too [comes] from the <s>śāstra</s> alone, and not otherwise......

Merits are specific, desirable meanings, comprehended in the aims of life; their opposites are faults...... But with respect to poetry, the merits have the nature of word, meaning, and ornament (<s>alaṃkāra</s>). The faults are meaninglessness and the like, and the opposites of <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion) and so forth,
Therefore, the wise ones, aiming at the erudition of people,
composed the rules of practice (<s>kriyāvidhi</s>) for the diverse paths of speech. // 9 //

children.text: अतः कारणात् सूरयः पूर्वाचार्याः क्रियाविधिं निबबन्धुरिति संबन्ध । क्रियाविधिं क्रियाकल्पम्.........[मल्ल]नागेन

विद्यासमुद्देशे क्रियाकल्प इति काव्यालङ्कार उक्तः । तदनुसारेणानेन क्रियाकल्पः क्रिया .........[विधी]यतेऽनेनेति क्रियाविधिः । क्रियाकल्पोऽपि एवमिति नार्थतः कश्चिद् भेदः । काव्यलक्षणं शास्त्रं कृतवन्तः । [शास्त्रानुसारेण मूर्खो]ऽपि प्रवर्तते । किं पुनर्बुद्धिमान् लोकः । तस्मात् सर्वत्र न्मतमिति । व्युत्पत्तिमभिसन्धाय काव्ये यथावद् गुणदोषपरिज्ञान[हेतुभिः शास्त्र]संगृहीतैर्गुणदोषविवेको व्युत्पत्तिः तदुपादानहानिफलाऽभिधेया । चतुवर्ग इति च नानाप्रकारः सर्वपुरुषार्थः संगृहीतः । अस्यैव तु [शास्त्रस्य प्रमेयश्च]तुर्वर्गः । तत्प्रतिपादकं शास्त्रं तादर्थ्यात् । एतावानेव च पुरुषार्थः । तत्र सर्वत्र गुणाश्च दोषाश्च ज्ञातव्याः । तत्र गुणा वस्तुतः पुरुषार्थमया एव । ततस्त उपादे[याः] उपादेयतया [च]ज्ञेयास्तथार्थेनाज्ञातानामुपादानासम्भवात् । दोषास्तु तदाभासास्तत्संभविनो हेयाः । तेऽपि हेयतया ज्ञेयास्तथा भावेनाज्ञातानां हानासंभवात् ।
children.translated_text: in the enumeration of arts, '<s>kriyākalpa</s>' (system of practice) is said to be <s>kāvyālaṅkāra</s> (poetic ornamentation). Following that, '<s>kriyākalpa</s>' means that by which practice is prescribed — hence <s>kriyāvidhi</s>. '<s>Kriyākalpa</s>' too [means] the same — thus there is no difference in meaning. [The ancient teachers] composed the science of the definition of poetry. Even a fool proceeds according to the <s>śāstra</s>. How much more [so] the intelligent world! Therefore [this science is] authoritative everywhere. 'Aiming at erudition' — erudition (<s>vyutpatti</s>) is the discrimination of merits and faults through [principles] gathered in the <s>śāstra</s>, which serve as causes for the proper understanding of merits and faults in poetry; [its] fruit is the adoption [of merits] and the avoidance [of faults]. And the <s>caturvarga</s> (four goals of life) — the entire <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human aim) of various kinds — is encompassed. The <s>caturvarga</s> is also the subject of this very <s>śāstra</s>. The <s>śāstra</s> that expounds it [is so] by virtue of its purpose. And this alone is the <s>puruṣārtha</s>. In all [domains] therein, merits and faults are to be known. Among those, merits are essentially of the nature of <s>puruṣārtha</s>. Therefore they are to be adopted, and should be known as worthy of adoption — since the adoption of what is not thus known is impossible. Faults, however, are semblances of [merits]; arising from the same [source], they are to be rejected. They too should be known as worthy of rejection — since the avoidance of what is not thus known is impossible.
And discrimination [is]
properly [obtained]

children.text: शास्त्रादेव दृष्टार्थाददृष्टार्थाद् वेति सर्वशास्त्रस्थितिरेषा । काव्यमप्येतत् त्रिविधं चतु र्वर्गरूपं चतुर्वर्गस्तदुपायश्चानेन रसान्तरपरिग्रहेण प्रतिपाद्य[प्रतिपा]दकत्वात् । शब्दात्मकमपि काव्यशरीरं चतुर्वर्गस्तादर्थ्यात् । उपायोऽपि तादर्थ्याच्चतुर्वर्गः ।
children.translated_text: from the <s>śāstra</s> alone — whether dealing with seen (worldly) matters or unseen (transcendent) matters — such is the established position of all <s>śāstras</s>. Poetry too has this threefold form of the <s>caturvarga</s>: the <s>caturvarga</s>, its means, and [the relationship of] teaching-and-taught through the inclusion of other sentiments (<s>rasa</s>). Even the verbal body of poetry is the <s>caturvarga</s>, by virtue of its purpose. The means too is the <s>caturvarga</s>, by virtue of its purpose.
The connection is: 'Therefore' — for this reason, the wise ones, the earlier teachers, composed the rules of practice. 'Rules of practice' means the system of practice....... By <s>Mallanāga</s>,
The primary <s>caturvarga</s> is the exhaustive collection of all human aims.
Because of its purposive relation to the means as well, there is regard [for it] even in the <s>śāstras</s>.
Thus the summarizing verse.

children.text: किं च काव्येनेष्टदेवताविषयविचित्रस्तोत्रलक्षणेन सम्यग्विरचितेन धर्मोऽप्रमेयः । तथात्वे च कदाचिद् वरलाभादिकोऽर्थः । सुख[म्]प्येतत्पुरुषार्थ[द्वय]निष्ठमुक्तम् ।
children.translated_text: Moreover, through poetry characterized by wonderful praise of one's chosen deity, when properly composed, immeasurable <s>dharma</s> [is gained]. And in that case, sometimes [there is] <s>artha</s> (wealth) such as the attainment of boons. And this <s>sukha</s> (happiness) has been stated as grounded in these two <s>puruṣārthas</s>.
For those engaged in composing praise of the <s>Buddha</s>, with their sense-faculties melting in devotion,

children.text: एकैकस्मिन् यः क्षणे पुण्यकोशो नासर्वज्ञस्तं प्रमातुं समर्थः ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: the treasury of merit [accumulated] in each single moment — none but an omniscient one is able to measure it. //

children.text: गुणज्ञराजादि[वर्णनातोःप्यर्याति]शयप्राप्तिस्तदर्थाच्च धर्मः सुखं च सम्पत्स्येते । किं बहुना, न सोऽस्ति पुरुषार्थः कश्चिद् यः काव्यात् परिगृहीताश्रयविशेषा[न्न जायते । इ]हानुषङ्गे गुणदोषविभागः करणीयः । स च शास्त्रादेव नान्यथेति विस्तरेण पूर्वमेव प्रतिपादितम् । ततः का[व्यक्रिया]विधिमिति प्रकृतम् । कस्य व्युत्पत्तिमभिसन्धायेत्याह-प्रजानामिति । लोकस्य सन्ताने का व्युत्पत्तिः कथं [केषां ?] नाम...... [व्युत्पादनक्रि]यामभिसन्धाय क्रियाविधिं निबबन्धुरित्याह-वाचां विचित्रमार्गाणामिति । विचित्रो नानाप्रकारः शब्दालंकारा[र्थालंकारादियुक्तो मार्गः] काव्यान्येव । ततः काव्यविषयां लोककर्तृकां काव्यगुणदोषविभागविज्ञानलक्षणां व्युत्पत्तिमुद्दिश्य [शास्त्रनिर्माणम्] । तत्संक्षेपत्वाद् इदमपि सप्रयोजनमिति कर्त्तव्यमेव । ततश्च सामान्येन काव्यलक्षणशास्त्राज्ज्ञेय इयता विशिष्योच्यते ॥
children.translated_text: From the description of a king who appreciates merit and the like, the attainment of a surplus of wealth [follows], and from that purpose, <s>dharma</s> and <s>sukha</s> will be achieved. What more [need be said]? There is no <s>puruṣārtha</s> whatsoever that does not arise from poetry when it has obtained a suitable substrate. Here, in this context, the classification of merits and faults must be made. And that [comes] from the <s>śāstra</s> alone, not otherwise — this has already been demonstrated at length. Therefore the subject is 'the rules of practice for poetry.' To whom is the erudition aimed at? — [the author] says: 'of people.' What is the erudition of the world in its continuity? How? Of whom?...... 'Aiming at the activity of instructing,' [the author] says 'he composed the rules of practice' — 'of the diverse paths of speech.' Diverse means of various kinds — [paths] equipped with verbal ornaments, meaning-ornaments, and the like — the paths are the poems themselves. Therefore, [the śāstra was composed] targeting the erudition of the world-audience, characterized as the knowledge of the classification of poetic merits and faults. Since this [commentary] is a summary of that, it too is purposeful and must be done. And from the science of poetic definition in general, what is to be known is now stated with specific distinctions.
Now [the author]
begins to make the definition of poetry —
By them, both the body of poems and the ornament have been shown.
The body, firstly, is a sequence of words (<s>padāvalī</s>) delimited by the intended meaning. // 10 //

children.text: इह योनि कानिचित् काव्यानि संभवन्ति तेषां [शरीरमलङ्कारश्च] तैः पूर्वाचार्यैः लोकस्य काव्यव्युत्पत्तये क्रियाकल्पे निबद्धे । तयोः कीदृशं शरीरम् [शब्दरूपम् । अर्थे]
नाविष्टत्वात् । यथा हि पुरुषशरीरे हारकेयूरादिरलंकारो न्यस्यते येन
children.translated_text: by which it is beautified, so upon the body of poetry — which is made of words — figures such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) etc. are placed,
from which [comes] beauty. And it will be said —
The properties that produce beauty in poetry are called <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments). //

children.text: पश्चादलङ्कारो वक्ष्यते । पदानां सुबन्तति[ङन्तानां आवली श्रेणी, तया] परिपूर्णं काव्यं [तस्य] श्लोकादयोऽवयवा अवान्तरवाक्यानि । कविना वक्तुमिष्टेऽभिप्रेतेऽर्थे कस्मिंश्चिद् रघुवंशादौ । व्यवच्छिन्ना गमकत्वे[न]...स्वीकृता । विशेषे[ण]... ......[शरी]रं विज्ञेयमितीष्टार्थव्यवच्छिन्ना पदावली प्रसिद्धत्वादनूद्याप्रसिद्धं शरीरं विधीयते । यथा यः.............
children.translated_text: The ornament will be discussed later. '<s>Padāvalī</s>' means the sequence of words — <s>subanta</s> (nominal) and <s>tiṅanta</s> (verbal) — and the poem is complete through it. Its parts are the individual verses (<s>ślokas</s>) etc., which are subordinate sentences. 'Delimited by the intended meaning' — [the word-sequence is] accepted as indicative...... of some particular subject such as the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>, etc., which the poet intends to express. The body is to be understood as...... 'a sequence of words delimited by the intended meaning.' Since this is well-known, it is restated; and the less-known 'body' is thereby prescribed. Just as......

Here, from whatever source poems arise — their body and ornament were composed by those earlier teachers in the '<s>kriyākalpa</s>' for the erudition of the world in poetry. What is the body like? — It consists of words. Because meaning has not entered [it directly]. Just as ornaments such as necklaces, bracelets, etc. are placed upon the body of a person,
How many kinds of body are there? — [the author]
says:

children.text: पद्यं गद्यं च मिश्रं च तत् त्रिधैव व्यवस्थितम् ।
children.translated_text: <s>Padya</s> (verse), <s>gadya</s> (prose), and <s>miśra</s> (mixed) — it is established in just three ways.

children.text: पद्यं चतुष्पदी तच्च वृत्तं जातिरिति द्विधा ॥ ११ ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Padya</s> is a <s>catuṣpadī</s> (four-footed [verse]), and that is twofold: <s>vṛtta</s> (metered) and <s>jāti</s> (generic). // 11 //

children.text:
यदनन्तरं लक्षणतः कथितं तच्छरीरं प्रभेदतः त्रिधैव त्रिप्रकारमेव व्यवस्थितं बोद्धव्यम् ।.........[के]वलपद्यात्मकं......[केवलगद्यात्मकं गद्यपद्योभयात्मकं च]...
इत्यनेकेन प्रकारेण त्रिधैव व्यवस्थितमिति प्रकृतम् । तत्र पद्यं न ज्ञायते किंरूपमित्यत आह-पद्यं चतुष्पदीत्यादि ।.........अनूद्य पद्यमिति ज्ञा[पयति चतुष्पदी] तत् पद्यं ज्ञेयमिति । तच्च पद्यं द्विधा द्विप्रभेदमवसेयम् । कथम्—वृत्तं जातिरित्यनेन रूपेण ॥
children.translated_text: What was just described by its definition — that body — is to be understood as established in just three ways, of three kinds...... Consisting purely of verse...... consisting purely of prose, and consisting of both prose and verse...... Thus, in many ways, it is established in just three ways — this is the subject. Among these, verse — one does not know what form it takes — therefore [the author] says: '<s>padya</s> is a <s>catuṣpadī</s>' etc......... Having restated 'verse,' he indicates: 'that verse is to be understood as a <s>catuṣpadī</s> (four-footed composition).' And that verse is to be ascertained as twofold, of two divisions. How? — By the form [called] <s>vṛtta</s> and <s>jāti</s>.

children.text: तदपि न ज्ञायते किं वृत्तं जाति[र्वा कीदृशी]ति । तदाह—
children.translated_text: Still one does not know: what is <s>vṛtta</s>, and what kind [of thing] is <s>jāti</s>? To that [the author] says —
In the <s>Chandoviciti</s> (treatise on prosody), the entire elaboration of those [types] has been shown.
That science is a boat for those wishing to cross the deep ocean of poetry. // 12 //

children.text: तयोर्वृत्तजा[त्योः प्रपञ्चो] विचित्रः प्रभेदः वक्त्रादिरूपः, आर्यादिलक्षणश्च सकलः सर्वो निदर्शितः लक्षणतो लक्षितश्च प्रतिपादितः । कुत्र छन्दो[विचित्यां छन्दांसि] विचीयन्ते [संगृह्यन्ते यत्र] यया वा तस्याम् । सा चेयं विद्या पद्यलक्षणस्य काव्यशरीरस्य साधिका । यदन[या] प्रसाध्यते ततः साप्यादरेण द्रष्टव्येति वक्रोक्त्या तदभ्यासे श्रोतृजनं नियोज[यति- सा विद्येति] काव्यमे[व सागरः तद्वद्]गम्भीरं यतः,

भावार्थगाम्भीर्यात् । न तु शब्दगाम्भीर्येण । अन्यथा प्रमादो न स्यात् । नानारसामृतत्वात् । सूक्तरत्नाकरत्वात् । अकृतधियां च [वैरस्याधायकत्वात्] काव्यसागरं वि[विक्षूणां अवगा]हितुमिच्छतां स्वयं कर्तुं परकीयं वा ज्ञातुमिच्छतामित्यर्थः । सा छन्दोविचितिविद्या नौरूपा । सापि ज्ञातव्येति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: the profundity of emotion and meaning — not through profundity of words, for otherwise there would be no error [to avoid]; because of the nectar of various <s>rasas</s>; because of being a mine of well-spoken jewels; and because of producing distaste in the undiscriminating — 'the ocean of poetry, for those wishing to cross' — i.e., for those wishing to plunge in, whether wishing to compose [poetry] themselves or to understand that of others. That science of prosody is in the form of a boat. It too must be known — such is the purport.

The elaboration — i.e., the diverse division — of those two, <s>vṛtta</s> and <s>jāti</s>, in the form of <s>Vaktra</s> and other [meters], and having the characteristics of <s>Āryā</s> and other [rhythmic types] — the entire [elaboration] has been shown, defined and expounded through definitions. Where? In the <s>Chandoviciti</s> — [the text] where meters are investigated, or through which [they are investigated]. And this science is the means of accomplishing the definition of the poetic body in verse form. Since what is accomplished through it, therefore it too should be regarded with respect — and through this oblique expression [the author] directs the audience toward its study: 'that science' — poetry itself is an ocean, profound because of
If [one asks]

children.text: ह किं न दर्शित इति चेत्, आह—
children.translated_text: why it has not been shown here, [the author] says —
There is also the verse-grouping type beginning with <s>saṃghāta</s>, [which is] a variety of <s>vṛtta</s> and <s>jāti</s>, stated in the science of prosody —

children.text: मुक्तकं कुलकं कोशः संघात इति तादृशः ।
children.translated_text: <s>Muktaka</s> (independent verse), <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster), <s>kośa</s> (anthology), <s>saṃghāta</s> (composition) — such
[types], being in the form of parts of a <s>sargabandha</s> (canto-composition), are unstated as a separate elaboration of verse. // 13 //

children.text: एकः श्लोकः समाप्तार्थः स्वतन्त्रः श्लोकान्तरनिरपेक्ष इति मुक्तकम्, न तु निबद्धमिति सर्गबन्धेन [वैषम्यं] बन्धेऽनिबन्धनात् । यद् वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: 'Being in the form of parts of a <s>sargabandha</s>'
— thus.

A single verse that is self-contained in meaning, independent, not dependent on another verse — that is <s>muktaka</s> (independent verse); it is not bound — hence its distinction from the <s>sargabandha</s>, being unbound in the composition. As will be said —

children.text: एकक्रियाद्वारेण परस्परसापेक्षाः समाप्तार्थाः प्रत्येकमसमाप्तार्थाः श्लोकाः कुलकम् । तद्विशेष एव युगलकम् । नानाभित्तयो भिन्नक्रियाः स्वतन्त्राः श्लोकाः कोशवत् स्था[पिताः कोशः] । एकां भित्तिं प्रावृडादिकां वर्णयितुं समुदायेन प्रवृत्ता भिन्नक्रियाः श्लोकाः संघातः । इति तादृशः । इत्येवंरूपश्चतुर्विधपद्यप्रकारोऽनुक्तो [विशिष्य] पृथगिह ल[क्षणतः अनुक्तः अकथित]स्त्यक्त एव । किं कारणम् । सर्गबन्धांशरूपत्वात् सर्गबन्धस्य अंशरूपा, एकदेशस्वभावास्तेषां भावस्तत्त्वम् । तस्मात् ते हि सं[गृहीताः । न] मुक्तता[दिव्यति]रेकेण सर्गबन्धः से[त्स्य]ति, तन्तुव्यतिरेकेण पटवत् । स च लक्षणत उच्यत एव । ततस्तेऽपि तदव्यतिरेका[त्] पृथगसर्गब[न्धरूप]तो नोक्ता इत्यर्थः ।
children.translated_text: Verses that are mutually dependent through a single action, individually incomplete in meaning but collectively complete — these are <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster). A special case of that is <s>yugalaka</s> (couplet). Verses that are of different themes, independent, with separate actions, arranged like [items in] a treasury — these are <s>kośa</s> (anthology). Verses that are collectively engaged in describing a single theme such as the rainy season, with different actions — these are <s>saṃghāta</s> (composition). 'Such' — of this fourfold variety of verse types — 'unstated' means not stated separately here with specific definitions, [i.e.,] omitted. For what reason? 'Being in the form of parts of a <s>sargabandha</s>' — they are in the form of parts of the <s>sargabandha</s>, having the nature of portions. Therefore they are included [in the sargabandha]. Without <s>muktaka</s> etc., the <s>sargabandha</s> would not be achieved, just as cloth without threads. And that [sargabandha] is indeed stated by definition. Therefore, they too, being non-different from it, are not separately stated in their non-<s>sargabandha</s> form — this is the meaning.

children.text: नन्वेवं स्तोत्रावदानपरिकथादिपद्यप्रपञ्चो न संगृहीतः स्यात् । संगृहीत एव । [उक्त]लक्षणयोगात्......[सं]घातः आर्या कोश इति संघातादिसंज्ञाप्रवृत्तिमात्रेण संघातादित्वं सर्गबन्धांशस्य संघातादेरत[स्तद्रूप]त्वं स्तोत्रादीनां...... । नहि सर्गबन्धस्य शिशुपालवधादिनामान्तरकरणमात्रेण सर्गबन्धत्वं हीयते । तस्मात् स्त्तोत्रादिरपि लक्षण[तः संघा]तादिसंगृहीतः ...नहि कर्कादिव्यपदेशान्तरयोगादश्वत्वं हीयते, अश्वविशेषाः कर्कादय इति चेत्-स्तोत्रादयोऽपि यथालक्ष[णं]......निमित्तं(?) यथे[ह सर्ग]बन्धे च संघातादिः परिम्फुटं लक्ष्यत एव । तत्र हि प्रावृड्वर्णनादिः
संघातः । मन्त्राद्यवसरे च यथा[मुक्तकादिस्तथो]क्तं प्राक् । मुक्तकं......[इत्य8a]त्र परिस्फुटमेवेत्यलं विस्तरेण ॥
children.translated_text: <s>saṃghāta</s>. And on the occasion of counsel etc., [there are] <s>muktaka</s> etc. as stated before. '<s>Muktaka</s>'...... herein is quite clear — enough with elaboration.

But then the verse-elaboration of <s>stotras</s> (hymns), <s>avadānas</s> (edifying tales), <s>parikathās</s> (narratives), and the like would not be included. [Reply:] They are indeed included — because they possess the stated characteristics...... <s>saṃghāta</s>, <s>āryā</s>, <s>kośa</s> — merely by the application of the designation '<s>saṃghāta</s>' etc., the <s>saṃghāta</s>-nature [belongs to] the parts of the <s>sargabandha</s>; the <s>saṃghāta</s> etc. having that form, [the same form applies to] <s>stotras</s> etc...... For the <s>sargabandha</s>'s quality of being a <s>sargabandha</s> is not diminished merely by being given another name like 'Śiśupālavadha.' Therefore <s>stotras</s> etc. are also included as <s>saṃghāta</s> etc. by definition...... For the horse-nature [of a horse] is not diminished by the application of another designation such as '<s>karka</s>.' If [one says] '<s>karka</s> etc. are particular [types of] horses' — then <s>stotras</s> etc. are also [particular types of verse-groupings] according to their definitions...... just as in the <s>sargabandha</s> itself, <s>saṃghāta</s> etc. are clearly discerned. For therein, the description of the rainy season etc. is

children.text: कः पुनः सर्गबन्धो यस्यावथवाः संघातादय इत्याह—
children.translated_text: What then is a <s>sargabandha</s>, of which <s>saṃghāta</s> etc. are parts? — [the author] says:
<s>Sargabandha</s> (canto-composition) is called <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem). Now its definition [is stated]:
A benediction, an obeisance, or the indication of the subject matter — [one of these is] its opening. // 14 //

children.text: यदेतत् प्रसिद्धं गुणतः सन्निवेशतश्च महाकाव्यमिति सर्गबन्धः...[स]...विज्ञय इति महाकाव्यानुवादेन सर्गबन्धो विधीयते । सर्गैः सर्गाख्यैः परिच्छेदविशेषैर्बध्यतेऽसाविति सर्गबन्धः । ततश्चानेकसर्गात्मकः सर्गबन्धो महाकाव्यम् । सर्गाश्च संघातादिचतुष्ट्यस्वभावा इति द्रष्टव्यम् ।
children.translated_text: What is well-known by its qualities and arrangement as '<s>mahākāvya</s>' — that is the <s>sargabandha</s>....... is to be understood — thus by the restatement of '<s>mahākāvya</s>,' the <s>sargabandha</s> is prescribed. It is called <s>sargabandha</s> because it is bound by divisions called <s>sargas</s> (cantos). Therefore, the <s>sargabandha</s>, consisting of many cantos, is the <s>mahākāvya</s>. And the cantos are to be understood as having the nature of the fourfold [grouping] — <s>saṃghāta</s> etc.

children.text: अथवा अन्यथावतार्यते । ननु मुक्तकादयो महाकाव्यस्यांशाः, तत् किमुच्यते—

children.translated_text: 'Being in the form of parts of a <s>sargabandha</s>'

children.text: इत्याह—सर्गबन्धो महाकाव्यमिति । सर्गबन्ध इत्यपि महाकाव्यमुच्यते । ततो ये [म]हाकाव्यस्यांशास्ते सर्गबन्धस्यापीत्यविरोध इत्यर्थः । शेषं समानम् ।
children.translated_text: — [the author] says: '<s>sargabandha</s> is called <s>mahākāvya</s>.' Even by [the name] '<s>sargabandha</s>,' it is [called] <s>mahākāvya</s>. Therefore, those that are parts of the <s>mahākāvya</s> are also parts of the <s>sargabandha</s> — hence there is no contradiction. The rest is the same.
Alternatively, it is explained otherwise. Objection: <s>muktaka</s> etc. are parts of the <s>mahākāvya</s> — then why is it said:

children.text: सर्गबन्धस्य तर्हि किं लक्षणं यत् तदंशस्य संघातादेरपि स्यादित्याह—उच्यते त्वस्य लक्षणम् । तुशब्दो भिन्नक्रमः । अस्य तु महाकाव्यस्य लक्षणं स्वरूपमुच्यते । तुशब्देनैतदाह-संघातादीनामवयवानां पृथग् लक्षणं नोच्यते । अवयविनस्तु महाकाव्यस्य लक्षणं क्रियते । ततस्तेऽपि तल्लक्षणा एव, वस्तुतस्तदव्यतिरेकादिति । किं पुनस्तदिति तदेव वक्तुमुपक्रमते-आशीरित्यादि । तस्य महाकाव्यस्य मुखमादिः आशीरिष्टाशंसनं वा प्रयुज्यते, नमस्क्रिया प्रणामो वा, प्रबन्धसम्बन्धिनः कस्यचिद् वस्तुनोऽर्थस्य निर्देशः कथनं वा क्रियते इति विकल्पेन त्रिविधं मुखं प्रतिपत्तव्यम् । न समुच्चयेन । तत्र
children.translated_text: Then what is the definition of a <s>sargabandha</s>, which would also apply to its parts such as <s>saṃghāta</s>? — [the author] says: 'Now its definition is stated.' The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is out of sequence. 'The definition — i.e., the nature — of this <s>mahākāvya</s> is stated.' By the word '<s>tu</s>,' this is [implied]: the separate definition of the parts — <s>saṃghāta</s> etc. — is not stated. But the definition of the whole — the <s>mahākāvya</s> — is given. Therefore, they too have that very definition, since in reality they are non-different from it. What then is that [definition]? — To state that very thing, [the author] begins: 'a benediction' etc. The opening (<s>mukha</s>) of that <s>mahākāvya</s> is either a benediction (<s>āśīḥ</s>) — an expression of auspicious wishes — or an obeisance (<s>namaskriyā</s>) — a salutation — or the indication of the subject matter — the statement of some object related to the composition. Thus the opening is to be understood as threefold, by way of alternatives — not by way of accumulation. Among those,
whose lotus-feet-dust is honored by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>,
The blessed one whose form is resplendent with the jewels of pure qualities,
may he protect the world, beset with calamity, until liberation!
the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, solely devoted to the welfare of all beings —
Such is the benediction (<s>āśīḥ</s>).
Obeisance to the Triple Jewel (<s>Ratnatraya</s>), whose nature is honored by the three worlds, /
who abides upon the crowns of gods, their enemies, men, and the king of serpents! //
"The lord of <s>Śrī</s>, in the glorious..."
and so on — this is well-known.
Such is the act of obeisance (<s>namaskriyā</s>). As for the indication of the subject-matter (<s>vastunirdeśa</s>),
The same opening (<s>mukha</s>) should be recognized in prose and mixed compositions as well.
He states what its basis is:
Arising from a narrative of history (<s>itihāsa</s>), or otherwise, with a worthy subject, /
depending on the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) as its fruit, with a clever and noble hero. // 15 //

children.text: इतिहासः पुरावृत्तम्, तत्प्रतिपादिका कथा रामायणादिका इतिहासकथा तत उद्भूतं जातम्, इतिहासकथाश्रयमित्यर्थः । का[व्यमि]ति वक्ष्यति । किमितिहासकथाश्रयमेव महाकाव्यं कर्तव्यम् । नेत्याह-इतरदिति । इतिहासकथाश्रयादपरं वा । नात्र नियमः, विशिष्टाश्रयमेव तु तत् कर्तव्यमिति- सदाश्रयमिति । सन् शोभनः अधिगुणराजचरितादिलक्षणा आश्रयो भित्तिर्यस्य तत्तथा । अनेन महाकाव्यस्य द्विधाश्रयसम्पदुक्ता ।
children.translated_text: <s>Itihāsa</s> means an ancient event; the narrative that expounds it — such as the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and the like — is the <s>itihāsa</s>-narrative; "arising from that" means born from it, i.e., having an <s>itihāsa</s>-narrative as its basis. He will say "<s>kāvya</s> (poetry)." Must a <s>mahākāvya</s> necessarily have an <s>itihāsa</s>-narrative as its basis? No, he says "or otherwise" (<s>itarad</s>) — i.e., something other than one based on an <s>itihāsa</s>-narrative. There is no restriction here, but its basis must be distinguished — hence "with a worthy subject" (<s>sadāśraya</s>). <s>Sat</s> means excellent; the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), i.e., the ground, characterized by the exploits of a virtuous king and the like, of which [the poem] has that — it is thus. By this, the twofold basis of a <s>mahākāvya</s> is stated.

children.text: चतुर्विषयत्वं प्रतिपादयन्नाह—चतुर्वर्गफलायत्तम् चतुर्णां धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां वर्गः समूहः, स एव फलं पुरुषार्थत्पत्वात् । तत्राऽभ्युदयनिःश्रेयसहेतुर्धर्म

। विद्याभूम्यादीनां यथान्यायमर्जनमर्जितानां च रक्षणमर्थः । निरपायो विषयोपभोगः कामः । [त्रैकालिक]सांसारिकदुःखनिवृत्तिर्मोक्षः । विस्तरस्तु त[त्त]च्छास्त्रेभ्यो द्रष्टव्यः । तस्मिन्नायत्तं प्रतिबद्धं तद्विषयत्वात् । अत्र न नियमोऽवश्यं चत्वारोऽपि पुरुषार्था निबध्यन्त इति । यथासंभवं क्वचिच्चतुर्वर्गः, [क्वचि]त् त्रिवर्ग इति
children.translated_text: <s>artha</s> is the proper acquisition of learning, land, and the like, and the protection of what has been acquired; <s>kāma</s> is the enjoyment of sense-objects without harm; <s>mokṣa</s> is the cessation of suffering pertaining to all three times of worldly existence. The details should be learned from the respective <s>śāstras</s>. "Depending on that" (<s>āyatta</s>) means connected with it, since it has those as its subjects. There is no strict rule here that all four <s>puruṣārthas</s> must necessarily be included. It should be understood that sometimes the four aims, sometimes three,
[are treated]. And this he himself will state:
"Even if deficient in some of these..."

children.text: इत्यादौ । चतुरोदात्तनायकम् । चतुरः कुशलः उत्याहशक्त्यादियोगात् । उदात्त उदारस्त्यागातिशयादिसंबन्धात् नायकः विपक्षः प्रतिपक्षश्च
children.translated_text: and so on. "With a clever and noble hero" (<s>caturoddttanāyaka</s>): <s>catura</s> means skilful, due to possessing initiative, ability, and the like; <s>udātta</s> means generous, due to connection with extraordinary liberality and so forth; <s>nāyaka</s> means the hero and also the adversary (<s>pratipakṣa</s>);
since both have the status of hero (<s>nāyaka</s>), [the poem] in which that [quality exists] is thus described.

Stating that it has four objects, he says: "depending on the four aims" (<s>caturvargaphalāyatta</s>). The group (<s>varga</s>) of the four — <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> — is itself the fruit, since they constitute the goals of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). Among them, <s>dharma</s> is the cause of worldly prosperity and final beatitude;
He asks what further qualities [it should have]:
With descriptions of cities, oceans, mountains, seasons, and the risings of moon and sun; /
with garden sports, water sports, drinking parties, love-making, and festivals. // 16 //

children.text: चन्द्रश्चार्कश्च तयोरुदयः । नगरं च अर्णवश्च शैलश्च ऋतुश्च चन्द्रार्कोदयश्चेति चार्थं कृत्वा तेषां वर्णनानि गुणोद्भावनानि इति षष्ठीसमासः । तानि च यथासम्भवमादौ मध्येऽन्ते वा । न चानुक्रमनिय[मेन] एतानि निबध्यन्त इति एवंपरमेतत् ।

children.translated_text: "Adorned by those" —

children.text: वक्ष्यति । उद्यानं सलिलं च तयोः क्रीडा विहारः । सा च मधुपानकं च रतोत्सवश्चेति चार्थः । रतमेवोत्सवः प्रीतिविशेषः, तेषां तु क्रमो दृश्यते । अनेन सम्भोगात्मकः श्रृङ्गार उक्तः । तैरलंकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: he will say. Garden and water — their sport (<s>krīḍā</s>) means play. That, and drinking (<s>madhupānaka</s>), and love-festival (<s>ratotsava</s>) — this is the compound meaning. Love itself is the festival, a special form of joy; and their sequence is observed. By this, <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) in its fulfilled form (<s>sambhogātmaka</s>) is indicated. "Adorned by those."

The moon and the sun — their rising. City, ocean, mountain, season, and the rising of moon and sun — taking these as a compound — their descriptions (<s>varṇana</s>), i.e., the elaboration of their qualities, is a genitive compound. And these [occur] as appropriate at the beginning, middle, or end. And these are not bound by a fixed sequence — this is the purport.
Further specifying, he says:
With separations (<s>vipralambha</s>), marriages, descriptions of the birth of princes, /
with counsel, envoys, marches, battles, and the triumph of the hero. // 17 //

children.text: विप्रलम्भा विरहाः । अयं विप्रलम्भात्मकः श्रृङ्गारः । विवाहाः शास्त्रोक्ता गन्धर्वादयः । कुमाराणामुदया जन्मानि वधनानि च बाल्यादिवयःप्राप्तिलक्षणानि । तैश्चालंकृतम् । मन्त्रः क्रियारम्भदेशकालविभागपुरुषद्रव्यसम्यग्विनिपातक्रियाकार्यसिद्धिलक्षणपञ्चाङ्गात्मककार्यनिश्चयः । यदाह

children.translated_text: <s>Māgha</s>:
"In the bodies of all undertakings, apart from the five divisions of the limbs, /
there is no other counsel for kings, just as for the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) there is no self."

children.text: इति । विस्तरस्तु तच्छास्त्रात् । दूतः वाग्मित्वादिगुणयुक्तः सन्धानप्रवृत्तः पुरुषः ।
children.translated_text: Thus. The details [should be learned] from that <s>śāstra</s>. An envoy (<s>dūta</s>) is a person possessing qualities such as eloquence, engaged in negotiation.
"Negotiation depends on the envoy; the conduct of spying rests on the spy." /

children.text: इति वचनात् । चरविशेषश्चायम् । प्रयाणं संग्रामादिनिमित्तं गमनम् । आजिविंग्रहः सन्ध्यभावे । अभ्युदयं विपक्षविजयादिलक्षण उत्सवः । नायकस्य प्रतिपक्षस्य । एषाम[प्या]नुपूर्वी दृश्यते । तैरपि ।
children.translated_text: Thus the authoritative statement. And this [envoy] is a special kind of spy. March (<s>prayāṇa</s>) is the setting forth for battle and the like. Battle (<s>āji</s>) is warfare in the absence of treaty. Triumph (<s>abhyudaya</s>) is the festival characterized by victory over the adversary. Of the hero [and] of the adversary. The sequence of these too is observed. "By those also:"

<s>Vipralambha</s> means separations. This is <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in its unfulfilled form (<s>vipralambhātmaka</s>). Marriages are those prescribed in the <s>śāstras</s>, such as <s>gāndharva</s> and the rest. The "births" (<s>udaya</s>) of princes mean their births, upbringing, and attainment of successive stages of youth and so forth. "Adorned by those also." Counsel (<s>mantra</s>) is the five-limbed deliberation concerning the commencement of action, division of place and time, proper deployment of persons and materials, execution, and accomplishment of the purpose. As stated by
"Adorned, with abundant <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> throughout, /
with cantos that are not overly expansive, in pleasing metres, with good junctures." // 18 //

children.text: भूयांसः । रसाः श्रृङ्गारवीरादयः । भावा रत्युत्सवादयः । विस्तरस्तु तच्छास्त्रात् । तैर्निरन्तरं व्याप्तम् ।
children.translated_text: means plentiful. <s>Rasas</s> are <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and the rest. <s>Bhāvas</s> are <s>rati</s> (love), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), and the rest. The details [should be learned] from that <s>śāstra</s>. "Throughout" (<s>nirantara</s>) means pervaded by those.
"Furnished with cantos" —

children.text: वक्ष्यति । अनतिविस्तीर्णैर्नातिमहद्भिर्मध्यमैरित्यर्थः । श्रव्यं श्रुति[सु]भगं वृत्तं पद्यमिन्द्रवज्रादिकं येषां तैः । सुसन्धिभिः शोभनः स्पष्टः सन्धिः परस्परसङ्गतत्वम् अन्योऽन्यव्यपेक्षा अर्थतो येषां तैः । परस्परसंबद्धार्थाः सर्गाः कर्तव्याः । नत्वयःशलाकाकल्पा इत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: he will say. "Not overly expansive" (<s>anativistīrṇa</s>) means not too large, i.e., of moderate [size]. "Pleasing" (<s>śravya</s>) means delightful to the ear; the metre (<s>vṛtta</s>) is of the <s>Indravajrā</s> type and the like — [cantos] which have those. "With good junctures" (<s>susandhi</s>) means having excellent, i.e., clear, juncture (<s>sandhi</s>), meaning mutual connection, i.e., mutual dependence in meaning — [cantos] which have that. The cantos should be mutually connected in meaning, not like iron rods [placed side by side] — that is the meaning.
"Adorned" (<s>alaṃkṛta</s>) means embellished. "Abundant" (<s>asaṃkṣipta</s>)
With different endings everywhere, furnished [with these], delighting the world, /
poetry enduring through the ages is born, with true ornamentation. // 19 //

children.text: भिन्नः प्रकृतवृत्तापेक्षया अन्यवृत्तलक्षणः सर्गाणामन्तोऽवसानं येषाम् । किं क्वचिदेव सर्गे नेत्याह-सर्वेषु सर्गेषु । सर्गाः प्रस्तुतपद्यापेक्षया वृत्तान्तरैः समापनीया इत्यर्थः । तै रेवंरूपैः सर्गैरुपेतं युक्तम् । सदलंकृति सत्यः शोभनाः सुप्रयुक्तत्वात् । नत्वलंकृतयः स्वरूपेण शोभना नाम । अलंकृतयः शब्दार्थालंकाराः यस्य यस्मिन् वा तत् तथा । सत्यो वा विद्यमाना अलंकृतयो यस्य तदेवंविधं काव्यं लोकरञ्जनं जायते । लोकं रञ्जयति गुणसंपदा परितोषयति इति लोकरञ्जनम् । ततश्च प्रतिग्राहकभूयस्त्वात् कल्पान्तरं तिष्ठन्तीति कल्पान्तरस्थायि.........[जा]यते भवति प्रवचनवत् यावज्जगत् प्रवर्तत इत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: "Different" (<s>bhinna</s>) means having endings characterized by a different metre relative to the main one — [cantos] whose conclusion (<s>anta</s>) [is thus]. Does this apply only in some cantos? No, he says: "everywhere" — in all cantos. The cantos should be concluded with metres different from the main verse — that is the meaning. "Furnished" (<s>upeta</s>) means endowed with cantos of such a nature. "With true ornamentation" (<s>sadalaṃkṛti</s>) — "true" (<s>sat</s>) means excellent, because of being well-applied; for ornaments are not beautiful merely by their own nature. Ornaments (<s>alaṃkṛti</s>) means figures of sound and sense — [a poem] which has those, or in which they exist. Or: [a poem] in which there exist excellent ornaments — such poetry is born as "delighting the world" (<s>lokarañjana</s>). It delights the world, i.e., satisfies it by the perfection of qualities — hence "world-delighting." And therefore, because of the abundance of recipients, it endures through the ages (<s>kalpāntarasthāyin</s>)... it arises, i.e., it continues as long as the world endures — that is the meaning.

children.text: ननु सर्वत्र महाकाव्ये चतुर्वर्गादीन्यङ्गानि यथोक्तानि न दृश्यन्ते । कानिचिदेव क्वचिद् [दृश्यन्ते] । तन्न किञ्चिदिदानीं महाकाव्यं स्यादित्याह—
children.translated_text: Now, an objection: not all the elements mentioned — the four aims and the rest — are seen in every <s>mahākāvya</s>; only some are seen in some. Then no [poem] would now be a <s>mahākāvya</s>. He answers:

children.text: न्यूनमप्यत्र यैः कैश्चिदङ्गेः काव्यं न वर्ज्यते ।
children.translated_text: "Even if deficient in some of these elements, the poem is not to be rejected, /
if excellence in those [elements] that are adopted pleases the connoisseurs." // 20 //

children.text: अत्रोक्तेष्वङ्गेषु अवयवेषु यैः कैश्चिद् यथासम्भवं तु मधुपानकुमारोदयपर्वतवर्णनादिभिर्न्यूनं रहित[म]पि, न के[व]लं पूर्णं काव्यं, महाकाव्यं न वर्ज्यते सद्भिरुपादीयत इत्यर्थः । न दुष्यतीत्यपि पाठः । अस्तु स एव । अस्योत्सर्गस्यापवादमाहयदीत्यादि । उपात्तेषु [गृहीते]षु सम्पत्तिर्विभूतिः शब्दार्थसाद्गुण्यलक्षणा । तद्विदः तां काव्यसम्पत्तिं ये विदन्ति तान् पुरुषान् आराधयति रञ्जयति यदि, तदा नवर्ज्यते । अर्थोपात्तान्यङ्गानि । यद् वि[गतार्थं] तद् हेयमित्यर्थाद् गम्यते ।
children.translated_text: Among the elements (<s>aṅga</s>) mentioned here, i.e., the components, even if deficient — i.e., lacking — in some of them, such as the descriptions of drinking, prince-births, mountain-descriptions and the like, not only a complete poem but a <s>mahākāvya</s> "is not rejected" — meaning, it is accepted by the learned. "Is not flawed" is also a reading. Let that be the same. He states the exception to this general rule with "if" and so forth. In those [elements] that are "adopted" (<s>upātta</s>), i.e., taken up, "excellence" (<s>sampatti</s>) means perfection characterized by the excellence of words and meanings. "Connoisseurs" (<s>tadvidaḥ</s>) — those who know that poetic excellence; if it "pleases" (<s>ārādhayati</s>), i.e., delights them — then it is not rejected. The meaning is: the elements [should be] adopted [only when] meaningful; what is devoid of purpose should be discarded — this is understood from the context.

children.text: अत्रेदं चिन्त्यते । कथमत्र क्रमः । किं पूर्ववर्णितेन नायकेन रिपोर्जयात् नायकस्योत्कर्षः कथ्यते । अथ प्राग्वर्णि[तस्य रि]पोर्नायकेन जयात् तदुत्कर्षः ख्याप्यत इति । अत्र

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāmaha</s>
prefers only the former order and disapproves of the second:

Here the following is considered: What should be the order here? Is the triumph of the hero narrated through the previously-described hero defeating his enemy? Or is the triumph conveyed through the previously-described enemy being defeated by the hero? On this point,
"Having first presented the hero with his lineage, valor, learning, and the like, /
one should not then narrate his death for the sake of proclaiming the other's excellence.
If he is not desired as pervading the body of the poem, /

children.text: न चाभ्युदयभाक् तस्य मुधाऽऽदौ ग्रहणं स्तवे ॥
children.translated_text: and if he does not partake of triumph, then his mention and praise at the beginning is in vain."
Thus. But <s>Daṇḍin</s>, considering both approaches proper, says:
"Having first presented the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) by his qualities, /
the overcoming of adversaries by him — this path is naturally beautiful." // 21 //

children.text: ना[यकं प्रति]पक्षं प्राक् प्रथममुपन्यस्याभिधाय गुणतो गुणैः शौर्यादिभिरभिलक्षितं नायकं पूर्व वर्णयित्वेत्यर्थः । तेन पूर्ववर्णितेन नायकेन विद्विषां विपक्षाणां निराकरणमभिभ[वः पराज]यः कथ्यत इति एष मार्गः क्रमः प्रकृत्या सुन्दरः शोभनः । स्वरूपसिद्ध ऋजुरयं क्रम इति मन्यते ॥
children.translated_text: Having first presented — i.e., having described — the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>), who is the adversary (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), characterized by qualities such as valor, the meaning is: having first described the hero by his qualities. "By him" — by the previously-described hero, the "overcoming" (<s>nirākaraṇa</s>), i.e., the defeat, of the adversaries (<s>vidviṣām</s>) is narrated — "this path" (<s>mārga</s>), i.e., order, is "naturally beautiful" (<s>prakṛtisundara</s>). He considers this straightforward order to be inherently beautiful, established by its own nature.
<s>Bhāmaha</s>
disapproves of:
He states the second order, which
"Having described the lineage, valor, learning, and the like of the enemy as well, /
the narration of the hero's excellence through his [the enemy's] defeat also delights us." // 22 //

children.text: रिपो[र्नायकवि]पक्षस्यापि न केवलं प्रतिपक्षस्य वंशोऽन्वयः वीर्य विक्रमः श्रतं शास्त्रकौशलं आदिर्येषां त्यागसत्यक्षान्त्यादीनां तानि गुणवस्तूनि वर्णयित्वा प्रकाश्य [तस्य] वर्णितवंशादेर्विपक्षस्य जयाद् अभिभवात् कारणात् प्रतिपक्षेण, नायकस्य प्रतिपक्षस्य उत्कर्षो विशेषः तस्य कथनमभिधानं यत्, तच्च नोऽस्मान् धिनोति प्रीण्यति । चकारात् पूर्वकं च । अयमपि क्रमोऽस्माकं प्रिय एवेत्यर्थः ।
children.translated_text: Of the enemy (<s>ripu</s>) — i.e., of the adversary (<s>vipakṣa</s>) of the hero, not merely of the opposing party (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) — the lineage (<s>vaṃśa</s>) means ancestry, valor (<s>vīrya</s>) means prowess, learning (<s>śruta</s>) means mastery of <s>śāstras</s>, and the "and the like" includes liberality, truthfulness, forbearance, and so forth — having described, i.e., displayed, those excellent qualities — through the defeat, i.e., the overcoming, of that adversary whose lineage and the rest have been described, the narration of the excellence, i.e., the special superiority, of the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>), i.e., the opposing party (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) — that "also delights us" (<s>dhinoti naḥ</s>). And by the word "also" (<s>ca</s>), the former [order] as well [is included]. The meaning is: this order too is dear to us.

children.text: अयमभिप्रायः—काव्यं हि वक्रोक्तिप्रधानम् । अयं च क्रमः वक्रोक्तिस्वभावः, यद्विपक्षवर्णनद्वारेण प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षकथनम् । एवं नामायमुक्तृष्टः, यदेवंगुणोऽपि विपक्षो[ऽनेन] निर्जित इति । अन्यश्च वर्णितोऽन्यस्योत्कर्षः ख्याप्यत इति चतुरोऽयं [न]यः ।तस्मादयमस्मान् धिनोतीति । काव्येषु हि द्वावपि वर्ण्येते केवलं पौर्वापर्ययोर्विवादः । अत्र हि प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षो विधेयः । स चोभयथाऽपि गम्यत एव । हयग्रीववधादौ चायं [प्र]
कारो दृश्यते ऋजुनैव क्रमेण । प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षः किं न कथ्यते वक्रोक्त्या किं न ख्याप्यते वक्रीक्तिप्रधानत्वात् काव्यस्येति चेत् । यत्किञ्चिदेतत् ।
children.translated_text: this pattern is seen in the straightforward order itself. Is the hero's excellence not narrated? Is it not proclaimed through figurative expression, given that poetry is characterized primarily by figurative expression? This [objection] is of little substance.
This is the objection raised [like] in the <s>Aśokavanikā</s> [episode].

This is the purport: Poetry is indeed characterized primarily by figurative expression (<s>vakrokti</s>). And this order is of the nature of figurative expression — namely, narrating the hero's excellence through the description of the adversary. Thus, [one thinks]: "So great was the adversary, and yet he was defeated by this one!" And: the excellence of one is proclaimed through the description of another — this is a clever device. Therefore it delights us. In poems, indeed, both [types of heroes] are described; the dispute is only about the sequence. Here, the hero's excellence is what is to be established. And that is conveyed in either order. And in works like the <s>Hayagrīvavadha</s>,

children.text: यदुच्यते काव्यशरीराव्यापकत्वात्, अनभ्युदयभागित्वाच्च विपक्षस्य प्रागुन्यासवर्णने विफल इति । तदसत् । कथं प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षख्यापनपरं विपक्षवर्णनं प्राक्क्रियमाणं विफलं ना[म] । एवं हि प्राक्प्रतिपक्षनायकवर्णनम्, तेन च विपक्षनायकनिराकरणमितीदमपि प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षार्थं क्रियमाणं विफलं स्यात् । अथ प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षकथनार्थत्वात् ननु

चैतत् प्रतिप[क्ष]वर्णनमपि प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षख्यापनार्थत्वात् न मुघेति न कश्चिद् विशेषोऽन्यत्राभिनिवेशात् । तस्मात् काव्यशरीराव्याप्त्यनभ्युदयभागिनोऽपि विपक्षस्य प्राक् ग्रह[ण]स्तवौ न मुधैव, प्रतिपक्षोत्कर्षख्यापनार्थत्वात्, प्रतिपक्षवर्णनादिवदिति द्वयमपि साधु दृश्यतामिति ॥
children.translated_text: this description of the adversary too, being intended to proclaim the hero's excellence, is not in vain — so there is no difference, other than mere partisan attachment. Therefore, even though the adversary does not pervade the body of the poem and does not partake of triumph, his prior mention and praise are not in vain, because they serve to proclaim the hero's excellence — just like the description of the hero and the rest. Thus both [orders] should be regarded as proper.

As for the claim that describing the adversary first is futile because he does not pervade the body of the poem and does not partake of triumph — that is incorrect. How can the description of the adversary, intended to proclaim the hero's excellence, be called futile when performed first? For by the same logic, the prior description of the hero and then the overcoming of the adversary by him — this too, being done for the sake of the hero's excellence, would be futile. If [one argues that] because it serves to narrate the hero's excellence [it is not futile], then indeed

children.text: काव्यशरीरं त्रिविधोद्दिष्टं पद्यं गद्यं च मिश्रं चेति
children.translated_text: stated as the threefold body of poetry — verse, prose, and mixed (<s>miśra</s>) —
of those, verse has been described so far. Regarding prose, he says:
What was previously
"Without feet (<s>pāda</s>), a continuous flow of words — that is prose (<s>gadya</s>). <s>Ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s> /
are its two varieties."

children.text: न विद्यते पादः पादव्यवस्था यस्मिन्निति न पादो वा अपादः पादस्वभावो न भवती-

त्यर्थः । एवलक्षणं गद्यम् । पद्यं तु पादस्वभावः पदसन्तान इत्यसङ्करः । कतिविधं
तदित्याह—आख्यायिकेत्यादि । तस्य गद्यस्य भेदौ प्रकारौ द्वौ विज्ञेयौ । कथम् । आख्यायिकाकथेत्येवं[रू]पौ । [न] अनयोर्भेदः ।
children.translated_text: that is the meaning. Such is the definition of prose (<s>gadya</s>). Verse, on the other hand, has the nature of metrical feet — [hence] "a continuous flow of words" does not [cause] confusion. How many types does it have? He says with "<s>ākhyāyikā</s>" and so forth. Its — i.e., prose's — two types (<s>bheda</s>), i.e., varieties, should be known: in the form of <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s>. What is the difference between these two?
<s>Bhāmaha</s>'s
view of the difference is stated:
"Without feet" (<s>apāda</s>) — that in which there is no arrangement of metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>), or: that which does not have the nature of metrical feet —
"Of those, the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> indeed —" // 23 //
"is narrated by the hero himself; the other (<s>kathā</s>) by the hero or by another. /
There is no fault in displaying one's own virtues here, for one is declaring what actually happened." // 24 //

children.text: तयोराख्यायिकाकथयोरयं भेदः किलेति परमतसूचने । आख्यायिका नायकेनैव [स्वयम्]
उच्यते, यस्य चरितप्रतिपादनार्थमाख्यायिका प्रवृत्ता । नान्येनेति वक्तृनियमः आख्यायिकायाम् । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: by the very person for the purpose of whose exploits the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is composed. "Not by another" — this is the restriction on the narrator in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>. As stated:
"[An <s>ākhyāyikā</s>] is that in which the hero himself narrates his own deeds." Thus.
Of those two — the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and the <s>kathā</s> — this is the difference; "indeed" (<s>kila</s>) indicates another's view. The <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is narrated by the hero himself —

children.text: अन्या कथा उक्ताया आख्यायिकाया अन्यत्वात् । नायकेन वाच्या यच्चरितप्रकाशनाय प्रवृत्ता, इतरेण वा नायकादन्येन वा, तत्सहायादिना वाच्येति न वक्तृनियमः कथायाम् । अयं तावदनयोर्भेदः ।
children.translated_text: The <s>kathā</s> (prose tale) is different from the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (narrative) that has been described, due to its being of a different kind. It is to be narrated by the protagonist for the purpose of revealing his exploits, or by another person other than the protagonist, or by his companion and the like — thus there is no restriction on the speaker in a <s>kathā</s>. This, then, is the difference between these two.

children.text: न[न्विय]माख्यायिका स्वयं नायकेनोच्यते न कथा । एवं हि स्वगुणोद्भावनप्रसङ्गः । तच्चानुचितमभिजातस्य । तदुक्तम्-

children.translated_text: How could a person of noble birth display his own virtues? Thus.

Is not this <s>ākhyāyikā</s> narrated by the protagonist himself, and not the <s>kathā</s>? For thus there would be the occasion of self-glorification. And that is unbecoming for a person of noble birth. As it has been said —

children.text: अत्राह—स्वगुणाविष्क्रियेत्यादि । अयं तावददोषः । यतः स्वस्यात्मनः स्वेषां वा गुणानां वंशस्य वीर्यादीनामाविष्क्रिया प्रस्ताववशात् कथनं न दोषः न दुष्यति । कस्य—भूतं यथावृत्तमर्थं स्वचा[रित्र्य]लक्षणं शंसतो ब्रुवतो नायकस्य । अत्राख्यायिकायां कथायां वा । तेन हि यथावृत्तं स्वचरितममिधेयं दोषरूपं गुणरूपमन्यद्वा, न विपरीतम् । तत्[अ]विपरीतं यथावृत्तमात्मनः कथयतः प्रस्ताववशप्राप्तं स्वगुणकथनं कथमाभिजात्यं हापयेत् । प्रत्युत विपरीतामिधाने आभिजात्यं हीयेत । आत्मव[ञ्चन]रूपं तु स्वगुणाविष्करणमनुचितमाभिजात्ये ।
children.translated_text: To this he replies — 'self-display of virtues' and so forth. This, to begin with, is not a fault. Because the display of one's own virtues, or those of one's lineage such as valor and the like, narrating them as occasion arises, is not a fault — it does not constitute a deficiency. For whom? For the protagonist who speaks of, who narrates, the matter as it actually occurred, characterized by his own conduct. This applies to both the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and the <s>kathā</s>. For thereby he narrates his own conduct as it actually occurred — whether it is of the nature of fault, of virtue, or of something else — not the opposite. When narrating what actually happened about oneself without distortion, how could the mention of one's own virtues arising naturally from the occasion diminish one's noble birth? On the contrary, nobility would be diminished by narrating what is contrary to fact. It is self-display of virtues in the form of self-deception that is unbecoming for one of noble birth.

children.text: ननु नात्र दोष इत्येतावदुक्तम् । गुणस्तु न कश्चित् । अयमेव गुणो यो दोषाभावः । तल्लक्षणत्वात्तस्य सर्वत्रेति यत्त्किञ्चिदेतम् । अ[नेन] चैतन्निरस्तं भङ्गया यदुक्तं
children.translated_text: But it has only been said that there is no fault here. There is, however, no merit either. This very absence of fault is the merit. Since that is its characteristic everywhere, this amounts to nothing significant. And by this, what was said by
<s>Bhāmaha</s>

children.text: , आख्यायिकायां सुखदुःखरूपं स्वचरितं यथावृत्तमाख्यायते नायकेन न तु गुणरूपमिति । वृत्तमाख्यायते यस्यां नायकेन स्वचेष्ट
children.translated_text: has been indirectly refuted — namely that in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, one's own conduct, whether of happiness or suffering, is narrated as it actually occurred by the protagonist, but not what is of the nature of virtue. 'That in which one's own conduct is narrated by the protagonist'
and so forth.

children.text: ननु सामान्यवचनमेतत् । न त्वयं विशेषो दृश्यते दुःखरूपं स्वचरितं वाच्यं न गुणरूपमिति । अर्थादेतदुक्तं तेन । यत्पश्चात् वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: 'A person of noble birth would display his own virtues'
thus. Otherwise there would be a contradiction between the earlier and later statements therein.

But this is a general statement. No such specific distinction is seen that one's conduct of suffering is to be narrated but not that of virtue. This was said by him implicitly, since he will state later —
Then what is not proper? He states his own view —
Rather, an absence of restriction is observed, since even therein narration by others is found.

children.text: अन्यो वक्ता स्वयं वेति कीदृग् वा भेदकारणम् ॥ २५ ॥
children.translated_text: Whether another is the speaker or oneself — what kind of reason for distinction would that be? || 25 ||

children.text: किं त्विदमत्र ब्रूमः । यः परेण नियमः कृतः आख्यायिका नायकेनैव वाच्येति, स नास्ति । यतस्तत्राख्यायिकायामपि न केवलं कथायाम्, अनियमः नायकेनैव वाच्येत्यस्य नियमस्याभावो दृष्टः उपलब्धः कृतः । अन्यैरुदीरणात् नायकादन्यैरपि तदनुचरादिभिराख्यायिकाया उदीरणात् वचनात् । हर्षचरितादिकायामाख्यायिकायामन्यैरपि नायकचरितकथनदर्शनादिति मन्यते । सर्वथा कविरिह वक्ता, तन्मुखेन नायको वा, स्वातन्त्र्यमत्र कवेः । ननु

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāmaha</s>
accepts that the <s>kathā</s> is narrated by another, as he states —

children.text: अन्यैः स्वचरितं तस्य नायकेन तु नोदितम् ।
children.translated_text: 'His own conduct is narrated by others, not prompted by the protagonist.'

children.text: इति । तत्र किमुच्यते कथा नायकेनेतरेण वा वाच्येति । अनुक्तोपालम्भोऽयम् । एतदेव सिद्धं कथायामप्यनियमदर्शनात् उक्तेन न्यायेनोभयथाप्यदोषात् । भवतु वायं नियमः आख्यायिका नायकेनोच्यते कथा त्वन्येनेति । तथापि नैतावता आख्यायिकाकथयोर्भिन्नजातीयत्वमिति परमतमभ्युपगम्यापि तयोरभेदमन्यतः कथयन्नाह—अन्यो वक्तेत्यादि । कथायामन्यो वक्ता, आख्यायिकायां स्वयमिति कीदृक् किं नामेदं तयोर्भेदस्य वि
children.translated_text: Thus. What is said there — whether the <s>kathā</s> is to be narrated by the protagonist or by another? This is an unspoken criticism. The very same conclusion is established by the observation of absence of restriction in the <s>kathā</s> as well, since by the reasoning stated there is no fault either way. Or let this restriction stand — that the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is narrated by the protagonist and the <s>kathā</s> by another. Even so, this alone does not establish that the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> and <s>kathā</s> are of different species — thus, even accepting the opponent's view, he argues for their non-difference from another angle, saying: 'whether another is the speaker' and so forth. In the <s>kathā</s> another is the speaker, in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> oneself — what kind, what manner of reason or cause for their difference, their being of
different species, is this? This is simply not a cause for difference of species,

children.text: कारणमित्यर्थः । अन्यथैवंविधस्य भेदस्य सर्वत्र सुलभत्वात् तावता विजातोयत्वेऽतिप्रसङ्गः स्यादिति भावः । वाच्यं हि द्वयमप्येतत् । तत् केनाप्युच्यतां स्वयं परेण[वा] यथायोगम् । किमेतावता जातेर्भेदः स्यात् । अर्थतस्त्वेकैव जातिरियं नाममात्रात्तु भिद्यते । यद्वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: such is the meaning. Otherwise, since such a difference is easily found everywhere, there would be an overextension in claiming different species on that account alone — such is the implication. For both of these are to be expressed. Let them be expressed by anyone — by oneself or by another, as appropriate. How could there be a difference of species merely on that account? In substance, this is indeed one single species, differing only in name. As he will state —
'One species marked by two designations.'

children.text: । एवं तर्हीदमनयोर्भेदकारणम्, यत्र वक्त्रापरवक्त्रयो पद्ययोर्भविष्यदर्थसूचकयोः प्रवेशः साश्वासा च या सा आख्यायिका । तद्विपरीता कथेति । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: If so, then this is the cause of distinction between them: where there is the introduction of the two verses <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> that indicate future events, and which has divisions (<s>āśvāsas</s>), that is an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>. The opposite of that is a <s>kathā</s>. As it has been said —
'The <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> meters, and those that indicate events to come,'
thus. And also —
'An <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is understood to have <s>āśvāsas</s> (chapter divisions).'
'Not furnished with <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s>, nor having <s>āśvāsas</s>,'
'A <s>kathā</s> may use refined or unrefined style, and also <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> (vernacular).' Thus.

What we say here is this: the restriction made by the other — that an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> must be narrated by the protagonist alone — does not hold. Because even therein, in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, not only in the <s>kathā</s>, an absence of restriction — the non-existence of the rule that it must be narrated by the protagonist alone — has been observed, has been found, has been established. Since narration by others — even by persons other than the protagonist, such as his attendants and the like — of the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is found. In <s>ākhyāyikās</s> such as the <s>Harṣacarita</s> and others, narration of the protagonist's deeds by others is also seen — so he thinks. In all cases, the poet is the speaker here, or the protagonist through his mouth; the poet has freedom in this matter. But
Having thus brought that up, he refutes it, saying —

children.text: वक्त्रं चापरवक्त्रं च साश्वासत्वं च भेदकम् ।
children.translated_text: 'If the <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> meters and having <s>āśvāsas</s> are the distinguishing marks,'
'the identifying features of the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — then by extension, in <s>kathās</s> too — || 26 ||'
'Why should there not be the introduction of <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s>, just as with <s>āryā</s> and other meters?'

children.text: भेदश्च दृष्टो लम्भादिराश्वासो वास्तु किं ततः ॥ २७ ॥
children.translated_text: 'And a difference is seen such as <s>lambha</s> and the like — or let there be an <s>āśvāsa</s>; what of it? || 27 ||'

children.text: वक्त्रं चापरवक्त्रं च पद्यद्वयं सहाश्वासेन वर्त्तते तद्भावः तत्त्वम् । तच्चैतत् त्रयम् आख्यायिकायाश्चिह्नं लक्षणं भेदकं कथायाः सकाशाद्विशेषकं चाप्यस्यास्य कथायामभावादितिचेन्मन्यसे, ननु यतः [प्रसङ्गेन] तत्र गद्याधिकारात् प्रस्तावेन भाव्यर्थसूचनादिलक्षणेन हेतुभूतेन नाधिकारितया वक्त्रापरवक्त्रयोः कथास्वपि आख्यायिकावत् किं कस्मान्न प्रवेशः न प्रयोगः स्यादेवेत्यर्थः । किंवत् ? आर्यादिवत् ।

आर्यादेरिव यथाप्रस्तावमन्यस्यापि पद्यस्य न स्तवादेः प्रवेशादिग्रहणम्, त्रयाणामपि पद्यत्वेनाविशेषादयमपि नियमो नास्तीत्यर्थः । तथाहि यदि तादृशः प्रस्तावः स्यात्, तदा कथास्वपि अनयोः प्रभेदो न दुष्यति, यथा आ
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>āryā</s> and other verses, or any other verse — not hymns of praise — are introduced as occasion demands, and since all three are alike in being verse, this restriction too does not hold — such is the meaning. For if such an occasion arises, then even in <s>kathās</s> the distinction between these two would not be violated, just as with the <s>āryā</s>

children.text:
र्यादेः । आख्यायिकायामपि हि प्रसङ्गेन तयोः प्रवेशः नाधिकारितया, [तत्र] गद्याधिकारात्
