तथा कथायामपि इति नेदं भेदकमसाधारणं चि[न्तनीयम् । लम्भ]स्तर्हि भेदकं चिह्नमस्तु कथायां तस्याभावात् । अत्राह—भेदश्चेत्यादि । लम्भादिर्भेदो विशेषः । आदिग्रहणात् यव[?]विश्रामादिव्यवहारः आख्यायिकाविषयः [कथायाम]पि दृष्टः । ततश्चाश्वासोऽपि यदि भवेत् को नामात्र दोषः । लम्भादिर्वा भेदो भवतु, आश्वासो वा व्यवहारः, किं ततः तस्माद् व्यवहारमात्रात्, किंजातीयत्वमनयोर्भवेत् । नैवार्थभेदः, अभेदादित्यर्थः । परिच्छेदा हि तत्र सम्पन्नाः कर्तव्या इतीदमत्र तात्पर्यम्, विपन्नानां हेयत्वात् । ते च लम्भादिव्यपदेश्या वा भवन्तु, आश्वासव्यवहार्या वेति स्वातन्त्र्यमत्र कवेः, विशेषाभावात् ।
children.translated_text: and other meters. For even in the <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, their introduction is by occasion, not as the dominant element, since prose predominates there. Similarly in the <s>kathā</s> as well — thus this should not be considered an exclusive distinguishing mark. If then <s>lambha</s> (chapter division) is the distinguishing mark, since it is absent in the <s>kathā</s> — to this he replies: 'And a difference' and so forth. The difference or distinction of <s>lambha</s> and the like — by the word 'and the like' is included the terminology of <s>yava</s>, <s>viśrāma</s>, and so forth — pertaining to <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, is also seen in <s>kathā</s>. Therefore, even if there be an <s>āśvāsa</s> or some other terminology, what of it? From mere terminology, what species-difference would there be between them? There is no difference of substance, since they are identical in meaning. For the divisions therein are to be well-made — this is the point here, since poorly made ones are to be rejected. And let them be designated as <s>lambha</s> and the like, or be termed <s>āśvāsa</s> — the poet has freedom in this, since there is no real distinction.

The <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> — these two verses — together with the <s>āśvāsa</s>: their existence is their nature. And these three constitute the identifying mark, the definition, the distinguishing feature of the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> from the <s>kathā</s>, since they are absent in the <s>kathā</s> — if you think so, then since by occasion — because of the predominance of prose therein — by way of the cause characterized by indication of future events and the like, not as a dominant element, why should there not be the introduction, the employment, of <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s> in <s>kathās</s> as well, just as in <s>ākhyāyikās</s>? This is the meaning. Like what? Like the <s>āryā</s> and other meters.
<s>Bhāmaha</s>
has made a prohibition.
'Not furnished with <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s>, nor having <s>āśvāsas</s>,'
'is a <s>kathā</s>' — thus.
But
<s>Daṇḍin</s>

children.text: कृतो विधिरस्ति, लम्भादिर्वाश्वासो वा भवत्विति । तदप्रमाणमिति चेत् ।
children.translated_text: has made an injunction — that there may be <s>lambha</s> or <s>āśvāsa</s>. If that is not authoritative, then
<s>Bhāmaha</s>'s

children.text: कृतो निषेधः प्रमाणमिति कोशपानमत्र करणीयं स्यात् । द्वयोरपि शास्त्रकारत्वात् प्रामाण्यम्, न वा कस्यापि । मतभेदस्तत्र भवत्विति चेत् ? अस्तु तत्किमस्थानाभिनिवेशः क्रियते । युक्तिपुरस्कृतं तु
children.translated_text: prohibition being authoritative would require a selective drinking of the ocean. Since both are authors of treatises, both have authority — or neither does. If one says, let there be a difference of opinion — very well, but why this insistence on a pointless matter? The view of
<s>Daṇḍin</s>,
however, appears to be supported by reasoning.
But
Therefore, <s>kathā</s> and <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — this is one single species marked by two designations.
And the remaining narrative types will be subsumed herein. || 28 ||

children.text: यत एवं निरूप्यमाणो नानयोः कश्चिज्जातिभेदो लभ्यते अन्यत्र संज्ञाभेदात्, ततस्तावदेका जातिरियं गद्यजातिः । आख्यायिकेयं कथेयमिति अनेन संज्ञाद्वयेन द्वाभ्यां नामभ्याम
ङ्किता लक्षिता व्यवहरणीया । न च नामभेदमात्रकेन जातिभेद एव सर्वथा स्यात् । ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियादिभेदेऽपि मनुष्यत्वात्तेषाम् । क्रियाभेदोऽत्र
children.translated_text: it is to be known, to be employed. And a mere difference of name does not necessarily entail a difference of species in all cases. Even in the distinction of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and so on, they share human nature. The difference of function here

children.text: संज्ञाभेदनिमित्तमिति चेत्—किं वै सर्वा नैमित्तिकी संज्ञा, यादृच्छिक्यपि हि सा दृश्यते, मण्डपादिवत् । निमित्तं वा किंचिन्मृग्यतां यदि तेन विना दौःस्थ्यम् । नन्वपरेऽपि गद्यप्रभेदा दृश्यन्ते, किं ते नोक्ता इति चेदाह—अत्रैवेत्यादि । शेषां आख्यानपर्याया ये सम्भवन्ति आख्यानजातयः, आख्यानकप्रभेदाः ता अत्रैवानयोरेव कथाख्यायिकयोरन्तर्भविष्यन्ति गद्यजातित्वेनाभेदात् लक्षणतः । चकारः [अन्]उक्तसमुच्चये । तस्मात् पृथक् तासां लक्षणं नोक्तम् । तल्लक्षणेनैव कृतलक्षणत्वादित्यर्थ इति ॥
children.translated_text: is the cause of the difference of designation — if so, is every designation causal? For arbitrary naming is also seen, as in the case of <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion) and the like. Or let some cause be sought if one feels uneasy without it. But there are also other sub-types of prose seen — why have they not been mentioned? To this he replies: 'herein' and so forth. The remaining narrative types, synonyms of <s>ākhyāna</s>, that may exist — sub-types of <s>ākhyānaka</s> — will be subsumed herein, within these two, <s>kathā</s> and <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, since they are identical in being of the prose type by definition. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for the inclusion of what is unmentioned. Therefore, a separate definition for them has not been stated, since they are already defined by that very definition — such is the meaning.

Since, when examined thus, no difference of species between these two can be found apart from a difference of name, therefore this is indeed one species, one type of prose. Marked by these two designations, by the two names — '<s>ākhyāyikā</s>' and '<s>kathā</s>' —

children.text: अयं तर्हि विशेष आख्यायिकायाः । सा हि—

children.translated_text: 'Is endowed with the abduction of a maiden, battle, separation, and triumph.'
'The <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, not the <s>kathā</s>' — thus says
<s>Bhāmaha</s>.
To that he replies —
Then this is the specific feature of the <s>ākhyāyikā</s>. For it —
'The abduction of a maiden, battle, separation, triumph, and so forth —'

children.text: सर्गबन्धसमा एव न ते वैशेषिका गुणाः ॥ २९ ॥
children.translated_text: 'These are similar to what is found in verse-composition (<s>sargabandha</s>) and are not distinctive qualities. || 29 ||'

children.text: कन्याया हरणं संग्रामस्तन्निमित्तोऽन्यो वा, विप्रलम्भो वियोगः, उदयोऽभ्युदयः रिपुविजयादिलक्षणः । आदिशब्देन मत्ततासुरतोत्सवादिपरिग्रहः । ननु

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāmaha</s>
has indeed stated —
'Endowed with the abduction of a maiden, battle, separation, and triumph.' Thus.

children.text: तत्किमपि सूच्यते । एवं मन्यते । सोऽपि नियमो [नापो]ह्यते, अधिकदर्शनात् । उपलक्षणं वा तद्वचनं, तेऽपि गुणाः [अ]थ न वैशेषिकाः, कथायाः सकाशादाख्यायिकां न भेदयन्तीत्यर्थः । विशेषा [भे]दाः [यैः] कथ्यन्ते आख्यायिकायाः, प्रयोजनमेषामिति वैशेषिकास्तथा न भवन्तीत्यर्थः । किं कारणम् । यतः सर्गबन्धेऽपि समानाः । सा[धारणाः, तेषां त]त्रापि दर्शनात् । तद् यदि [कथा]
children.translated_text: What is implied by this? He thinks as follows. That restriction too is not removed, since more are observed. Or that statement is illustrative, and those qualities too are not distinctive — they do not distinguish the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> from the <s>kathā</s>, such is the meaning. The specific features, the distinguishing marks by which the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is differentiated — these serving that purpose — are not such, meaning they do not function as distinguishing marks. For what reason? Because they are found equally even in verse-composition (<s>sargabandha</s>). They are common, being observed therein too. If then in the <s>kathā</s>
too they occur as occasion demands, who can prohibit them?
<s>Bhāmaha</s>?

children.text: इति चेत् । उक्तमत्र, किं चर्वितचर्वणेन । दृश्यन्ते च कथायां लीलावतीत्यादिकायामपि तेऽर्थास्तत्कथं भिन्त्स्यते आख्यायिकां कथात इति ॥
children.translated_text: If so — the answer to that has already been given. Why chew what has already been chewed? And those narrative elements are also seen in <s>kathās</s> such as the <s>Līlāvatī</s> and others. How then can the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> be separated from the <s>kathā</s> on that basis?

The abduction of a maiden; battle, whether caused by that or by something else; <s>vipralambha</s> (separation); <s>udaya</s> (triumph), characterized by victory over enemies and the like. By the word 'and so forth,' intoxication, love-play, festivals, and the like are included. Now

children.text: यत्र तर्हि कवेरभिप्रायेण कथनमङ्कनं किञ्चिद् दृश्यते सा आख्यायिका तदन्या कथेति
children.translated_text: If then wherever some marking is seen according to the poet's intention, that is an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, and what is otherwise is a <s>kathā</s> — thus says
<s>Bhāmaha</s>.
'Marked by certain markings made according to the poet's intention' — thus.
Refuting both of these, he says —
'A mark made by the poet's intention is not faulty even elsewhere.'

children.text: मुखमिष्टार्थसंसिद्धौ किं हि न स्यात् कृतात्मनाम् ॥ ३० ॥
children.translated_text: 'For those who are accomplished, what device could not serve as a means to the desired end? || 30 ||'

children.text: कवेः प्रयोक्तुर्भावेनाभिप्रायेण कृतं प्रयुक्तं चिह्नमङ्कनम् अन्यत्रापि कथायामपि सर्गबन्धेऽपि वा, न केवलमाख्यायिकायाम् न दुष्यति न दोषाय कल्पते निषेधाभावात् ।
children.translated_text: A mark or emblem made, that is, employed, by the intention or purpose of the poet, the author, is not faulty even elsewhere — in a <s>kathā</s> too, or in a verse-composition too, not only in an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — it does not amount to a fault, since there is no prohibition against it.
by <s>Bhāmaha</s>

children.text: कथायाम्, आख्यायिकामेव कबिभावकृतचिह्नविधानात् । उक्तमत्र । तेनापि च नियमो न कृतः काचिदङ्कितेति वचनात् । तस्मादिदमपि सर्गबन्धादिसाधारणं न समर्थयति कथात आख्यायिकाया भेदम् । किरातादौ च लक्ष्म्या ग्रहणादिकं कविभावकृतं चिह्नं दृश्यते, स्यादेतत् आख्यायिकायामिति । तदसत् । यस्मान्मुस्वमिष्टार्थसंसिद्धौ किं हि न स्यात् कृतात्मनाम् । कृतः संस्कृतः व्युत्पन्न आत्मा चित्तं येषां, कृतात्मनां सुधियाम् । इष्टस्यार्थस्य स्वनामाङ्कनादेरन्येनापदेशेन विदग्धेन क्रमेण किं नाम मुखमुपायो न स्यात् । सर्वमेव हि तेषामिष्टसिद्धिद्वारीभवति कौशलविशेषात् । तस्माद् यदीच्छन्ति कथायामन्यत्र वा सर्वत्रेदृशं कर्तुमुपायज्ञास्ते [कु]र्वन्त्येव, न चेत् न क्वचिदपीति । नेदमपि भेदकं चिह्नम् । तस्मा
children.translated_text: in the <s>kathā</s>, since the provision of marks made by the poet's intention is specific to the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> alone. The answer to that has already been given. And no restriction was made by him either, since the statement is 'a certain one is marked.' Therefore this too, being common to verse-composition and the like, does not justify the distinction of the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> from the <s>kathā</s>. And in the <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> and such works, the acceptance of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the like is seen as a mark made by the poet's intention — one might say this belongs to the <s>ākhyāyikā</s>. That is wrong. Because for those who are accomplished — those whose minds are cultivated, refined, and learned — what device or means could not exist for the attainment of the desired end, such as the marking of one's own name and the like, through another pretext, in a clever manner? For everything indeed becomes a door to the attainment of their desired goal, due to their particular skill. Therefore, if they wish to do such a thing in a <s>kathā</s> or elsewhere, anywhere — those who know the means will certainly do it; and if not, then nowhere at all. This too is not a distinguishing mark. There-
fore this alone stands firm —
'<s>Kathā</s> and <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — this is one species marked by two designations.' Thus.

children.text: स्यादेतत्, आख्यायिका संस्कृतेनैव दृश्यते । आख्यायिकापि भाषान्तरेण दृश्यते, असंस्कृतापेक्षयेति । किं न कथा । अथ संस्कृतापेक्षया भाषान्तरेण [न] दृश्यते आख्यायिका सर्वसंस्कृता कथाप्येवमिति माभूत् कथा । अथ मिश्रापि कथा दृश्यते नाख्यायिका । तथा अमिश्रा सर्वसंस्कृता साख्यायिका स्यात्, कादम्बर्यादिवत् ।
children.translated_text: One might object: the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is seen only in Sanskrit. The <s>ākhyāyikā</s> too is seen in another language, in relation to non-Sanskrit — then why not the <s>kathā</s>? Or if in relation to Sanskrit, the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is not seen in another language — then the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is entirely in Sanskrit, and the <s>kathā</s> likewise — so let there be no <s>kathā</s>. Or if the <s>kathā</s> is also seen in mixed form but not the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> — then one that is unmixed, entirely in Sanskrit, would be an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, like the <s>Kādambarī</s> and the like.

children.text: कथं तर्हि आख्यायिकेति व्यपदिश्यते इति चेत् । अत एवं संज्ञाद्वयाङ्किता एका जातिरित्युक्तम् । जातिभेदोऽत्र निषिध्यते, न संज्ञाभेदः । एवं कथाविशेषः आख्यायिका स्यात्, न जातिभेदः । यथा कथाविशेषाणां संज्ञाभेदा यथेष्टम् । न च भाषाभेद—मात्राद्विजातीयत्वम् । कथानामपि परस्परविजातीयत्वप्रसङ्गात् एतावन्तः स्यात् । काचित् कथा संस्कृतमयी । काचित् प्राकृतमयी । काचित् अपभ्रंशस्वभावा । काचित् भूतभाषामयी । काचित् मिश्रेति । यथा वाचां भाषाभेदेऽपि न कथात्वं हीयते गद्यमयत्वात्, प्रसङ्गे तु पद्यप्रवेशः, तथा संस्कृतमय्या आख्यायिकायाः कथात्वं न विरुद्धयते । अत एवोक्तम् । एका जातिः कथाजातिरेव यथेष्टं संज्ञा अनुभवति, यथा मनुष्यजातिरेका क्षत्रिय जातिसंज्ञाम् । भाषान्तरमयीनामपि कथानां गद्येनार्थोपक्षेपः लम्भादिपरिच्छेदादौ न दूष्यते निषेधाभावात् ।
children.translated_text: If it is asked, 'How then is it designated as <s>ākhyāyikā</s>?' — for this very reason it has been stated that a single genre is marked by two designations. A distinction of genre is here denied, not a distinction of designation. Thus, a particular kind of <s>kathā</s> would be an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, not a different genre. Just as particular kinds of <s>kathā</s> have different designations as desired. Nor does mere difference of language make them of a different genre — since the consequence would be that even stories among themselves would be of different genres: one <s>kathā</s> is in Sanskrit, another in Prakrit, another in Apabhraṃśa, another in <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s> (Paiśācī), and another is mixed. Just as, despite the difference of language in speech, the nature of being a <s>kathā</s> is not lost because it is in prose — though in context there is entry of verse — so too the nature of being a <s>kathā</s> is not contradicted for an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> composed in Sanskrit. Therefore it has been stated: a single genre — the genre of <s>kathā</s> itself — assumes designations as desired, just as the single human genus [admits of] the designation of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> caste. Even for stories composed in other languages, the introduction of content in prose at the beginning of sections (<s>lambhādi-pariccheda</s>) and so forth is not to be faulted, since there is no prohibition.
If it is said that <s>Bhāmaha</s>
has prohibited it,
[we reply]: by <s>Daṇḍin</s>

children.text: विहितमिति किं न प्रत्येषि । तस्मात् काचित् कथा [आश्वासादौ] गद्याक्षिप्तार्था, काचिन्न । [न]ह्येतावता आख्यायिका कथात्वं नानुभवति । कथा वाऽऽख्यायिका
children.translated_text: it has been enjoined — why do you not accept this? Therefore, some stories have their content introduced in prose [at the beginning of sections], and some do not. By this much, an <s>ākhyāyikā</s> does not fail to have the nature of a <s>kathā</s>. That '<s>Kathā</s>' or '<s>Ākhyāyikā</s>'
are merely designations — a single genre marked by two names — is well stated indeed.
But it has indeed been prohibited

children.text: तदेवं लक्षणतः [प्रचि]न्वन् कथां, आश्वासादिभेदं च गद्यं निर्दिश्य, तृतीयं मिश्रकाव्ये शरीरमधिकृत्याह—
children.translated_text: Having thus examined the <s>kathā</s> from the standpoint of its definition, and having specified prose with its divisions beginning with <s>āśvāsa</s> and the like, he states regarding the third body — the mixed composition (<s>miśrakāvya</s>):
The mixed [compositions] are <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) and the rest; their elaboration is elsewhere. /
A certain [composition] made of both prose and verse is called <s>campū</s> // 31 //

children.text: नाटकमादिर्येषाम् प्रकरणादीनां तानि नाटकादीनि काव्यानीत्यत्र मिश्राणि गद्यपद्यमयानि वेदितव्यानि इति मिश्रविधिः । ननु कथादिकमपि मिश्रं तत्रापि पद्यप्रवेशात् । प्रसङ्गेन तत्र पद्यप्रवेशः, नाधिकारितया । अतएवोक्तं प्रसङ्गेन

children.translated_text: 'even in stories.'

children.text: । नाटकादिषूभयमपि अधिकृतमिति नाटकान्येव मिश्राणि । किमेषां लक्षणं लक्षणप्रभेदो वेत्यत आह—तेषामित्यादि । तेषां नाटकादीनां मिश्राणां मिश्रप्रबन्धानामन्यत्र भरतकोहलादौ नाट्यशास्त्रे विस्तरः नान्दीप्ररोचनादिस्वरूपनिरूपणादिरूपः प्रपञ्चोऽधिकृतो नेह । ततस्ततोऽसौ द्रष्टव्यः । गद्यपद्यप्रबन्धस्त्विह विस्तरतोऽधिकृतः । स चोक्तः । किं नाटकादिकमेव मिश्रं नेत्याह—गद्यपद्येत्यादि । गद्यपद्ययोविकारः गद्यपद्यमयी मिश्रा चम्पूरित्यपेक्ष्य स्त्रीत्वम् । यदाह चम्पूरिति । चम्पूर्नाम विद्यते । कापि काचिदित्यसाकल्य[म्] । अपिशब्दो न केवलं पूर्वकमिति समुच्चिनोति । अयमपि
children.translated_text: In <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like, both [prose and verse] are employed as principal elements, hence dramas alone are mixed. 'What is their definition or subdivision?' — to this he says 'of those' etc. Of those mixed compositions — the <s>nāṭaka</s> and the rest — the elaboration, i.e., the detailed exposition in the form of the examination of the nature of <s>nāndī</s>, <s>prarocanā</s>, etc., is undertaken elsewhere, in the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s> of <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Kohala</s>, etc., not here. That should be seen there. But the literary composition of prose and verse [<s>campū</s>] is here treated in detail. And that has been stated. 'Is only <s>nāṭaka</s> and the like mixed, or not?' — to this he says 'prose-verse' etc. A modification of prose and verse — 'made of prose and verse' — is mixed; it is feminine [in gender] because it is to be connected with '<s>campū</s>.' As he says, '<s>campū</s>.' A <s>campū</s> indeed exists. '<s>kāpi</s>' — 'a certain one,' indicating non-totality. The word '<s>api</s>' connects [it] with what precedes, meaning 'not only the former.' This too

children.text: मिश्रप्रकारोऽस्ति । यद्वच्चम्पूरिति यावत् । सा च जातकमालादमयन्त्यादि ॥
children.translated_text: is a type of mixed [composition] — namely the <s>campū</s>. And that includes the <s>Jātakamālā</s>, <s>Damayantī</s>, etc.

Those beginning with <s>nāṭaka</s>, i.e., <s>prakaraṇa</s> and the rest — they are called '<s>nāṭaka</s> and the rest' — [the verse says that] among compositions, these are 'mixed,' i.e., to be understood as made of both prose and verse — this is the rule regarding the mixed [genre]. 'But <s>kathā</s> and the like are also mixed, since verse enters there too.' [Reply:] Verse enters there only incidentally, not as the principal element. Therefore it has been said 'incidentally'

children.text: तदेवं शरीरभेदकृतं त्रैविध्यं काव्यानां परिसमाप्य भाषाभेदकृतं चातुर्विध्यं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Having thus concluded the threefold classification of compositions based on the difference of body, he states the fourfold [classification] based on the difference of language:

children.text: तदिदं वाङ्मयं भूयः संस्कृतं प्राकृतं तथा ।
children.translated_text: This verbal [composition] is again [classified as] Sanskrit and Prakrit, /
Apabhraṃśa and mixed — thus the authoritative ones declare it fourfold // 32 //

children.text: यत् काव्यशरीरं त्रिविधमुक्तं तदिदं वाङ्मयं काव्यशरीरं भूयः पुनश्चत्वारो विधाः प्रकारा भाषामया यस्य

तत् प्रत्येकं चतुर्विधमाहुरामनन्ति । आप्ता आचार्याः । कथं—पद्यं काव्यशरीरं संस्कृतं शुद्धम्, प्राकृतं शुद्धम्, अपभ्रंशः शुद्धः, मिश्रं च तैः पैशाचिकेन चाशुद्ध्यधिका तु पृथगुक्ता । [यथा] पश्चाद्वक्ष्यति, भूतभाषामयीमित्यादिना । एवं गद्यं मिश्रं च काव्यशरीरं योज्यम् । पूर्वं गद्यपद्याभ्यां मिश्रमुक्तमिदानीं संस्कृतप्राकृतापभ्रंशैः प्रत्येकं त्रिविधं शरीरं मिश्रमुक्तामिति मिश्रयोर्भेद इति ॥
children.translated_text: each of which is fourfold — so the authoritative teachers declare. How? — Verse as a poetic body is pure Sanskrit, pure Prakrit, pure Apabhraṃśa, and mixed — with those [three] and Paiśācī — but the impure [mixed] has been stated separately. As he will say later, with the words 'made of <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s>' etc. In the same way, prose and the mixed body of poetry should be applied. Previously, 'mixed' was stated with reference to prose and verse; now 'mixed' is stated with reference to each of the three — Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Apabhraṃśa — [being mixed together]; thus there is a distinction between the two [uses of] 'mixed.'
That body of poetry which has been stated to be threefold — this verbal body of poetry is further [divided into] four types, i.e., kinds based on language,
Explaining the nature of Sanskrit and the others, he says:
That which is called Sanskrit is the divine speech, expounded by the great sages; /
<s>Tadbhava</s> (derived from that), <s>Tatsama</s> (identical to that), and <s>Deśī</s> (regional) — such is the manifold sequence of Prakrit // 33 //

children.text: देवानामियं दैवी वाक् भाषा संस्कृतमिति विज्ञायते । यद्येवं कथमिह संस्कृतं ज्ञातमिति चेदाह—अन्वाख्याता महर्षिभिरिति महद्भिरुदात्तैर्गुणमाहात्म्यात् ऋषिभिर्मुनिभिर्देशभाषावद्भिरन्वाख्याता अनुशिष्टा सतीह संस्कृतमिति ज्ञातेत्यर्थः । ततश्चैकप्रकारं संस्कृतं, प्राकृतं त्वनेकप्रकारम् । यदाह, तद्भवमित्यादि । प्राकृतस्य क्रमः प्रकारः अनेको भिन्नः कथं तद्भवं तस्मात् संस्कृतात् वर्णान्यत्वेन उत्पत्तिर्यस्य तत्तद्भवं शब्दभवमित्यर्थः । तच्च महिन्दसिन्धवबहिरादिकं यथोक्तं

children.translated_text: <s>Harivṛddha</s>.

children.text: । तत्समम् तेन संस्कृतेन समं तत्समम्, प्राकृतशब्दमपीत्यर्थः । तच्च हरिहरकमलादिकं यथोक्तं तत्रैव । देशी प्राकृतं महाराष्ट्रप्रसिद्धम् । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: '<s>Tatsama</s>' — identical to that Sanskrit — is also a Prakrit word, meaning [a Prakrit word identical to its Sanskrit form]. And that includes <s>hari</s>, <s>hara</s>, <s>kamala</s>, etc., as stated in the same [work]. '<s>Deśī</s>' — the Prakrit well-known in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>. As stated:
'Those words that are recognized by convention in the <s>Marhaṭṭha</s> (Mahārāṣṭra) region are called <s>Deśī</s>.'
And that includes <s>vokkaṇaka</s>, <s>kelli</s>, <s>cirihirahi</s>, <s>rasiccha</s>, etc.

children.text: यथोक्तं तत्रैव । इत्येवमनेन रूपेणानेकः प्राकृतक्रम इति ॥
children.translated_text: As stated in the same [work]. Thus, in this manner, the manifold sequence of Prakrit is [established].

The speech of the gods — this divine speech is known as Sanskrit. 'If so, how is Sanskrit known here [in the human world]?' — to this he says, 'expounded by the great sages.' By great, exalted ones — <s>ṛṣis</s>, sages who know the regional languages — through the greatness of their qualities, [this divine speech] has been 'expounded,' i.e., taught; and thus it is known here as Sanskrit — this is the meaning. Furthermore, Sanskrit is of one kind, but Prakrit is of many kinds. As he says, '<s>Tadbhava</s>' etc. The sequence — i.e., variety — of Prakrit is manifold. How? '<s>Tadbhava</s>' — that which is born from that, i.e., from Sanskrit, through alteration of phonemes — that is <s>Tadbhava</s>, meaning 'born from words.' And that includes <s>mahinda</s>, <s>sindhava</s>, <s>bahira</s>, etc., as stated by
Which Prakrit is the most excellent among these? — to this he says:
The language based in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s> is known as the pre-eminent Prakrit — /
the ocean of jewels of fine speech — of which the <s>Setubandha</s> and the like are composed // 34 //

children.text: राष्ट्राश्रयां भाषां वाचं प्रकृष्टं प्राकृतेषु शोभनतमं प्राकृतं विदुः उपदिशन्ति बहुज्ञाः । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: that <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>-based language, the most excellent among Prakrits, the most beautiful — the knowledgeable ones teach [to be] Prakrit. As stated:

children.text: ऊहइ अ विविह भासा परिरि (?) हिअअं य मोत्तूणं ।
children.translated_text: 'Setting aside the various languages and [other] Prakrits, /
the <s>Marhaṭṭhiyā</s> (Mahārāṣṭrī) has been adopted by poets.' [?]

children.text: इति । कुत्रैतद् दृश्यते इति चेदाह-सागर इत्यादि । सेतुबन्धः प्रवरसेनरचितः । स्कन्धकमर्यः आदिर्यस्य मथनादेस्तत्सेतुबन्धादि काव्यम् यन्मयं यस्य प्राकृतस्य विकारः, तत्प्राकृतं प्रकृष्टमिति प्रकृतम् । तत्काव्यं सदिति प्रशंसयन्नाह—सागरः सूक्तरत्नानामिति । सूक्तानि शब्दार्थोत्कर्षयोगात् । तान्येव प्रीतिकरत्वादिसाधर्म्येण रत्नानि, तेषां सागर आस्पदम् । रत्नानां हि सागर आश्रयः, सूक्तानां च रत्नकल्पानां तत्काव्यमाश्रय इति सागर उक्त इति । ननु प्राकृतान्तरमयमपि सेतुबन्धादि, तत् किमुच्यते महाराष्ट्रप्राकृतमयमिति । न चात्र पठ्यते महाराष्ट्रप्राकृतमयमेवेति । प्राधान्यात्तत् तन्मयमुक्तम् । यथा हयमयमनीकमिति ततेन्नश्यत(?) इत्येवंपरमेतत् ॥
children.translated_text: Thus. 'Where is this seen?' — to this he says, 'ocean' etc. The <s>Setubandha</s> was composed by <s>Pravarasena</s>. <s>Skandhaka</s> is the beginning, of which <s>Mathana</s> and the rest [follow] — that <s>Setubandha</s> and other poetry, 'of which' — i.e., the poetry which is a modification of that Prakrit — that Prakrit is the pre-eminent, the principal one. Praising that poetry as excellent, he says, 'ocean of jewels of fine speech.' Fine sayings (<s>sūktas</s>) — because of their excellence of word and meaning. Those very [sayings] are jewels, because of their shared characteristic of causing delight; the ocean is their abode. For the ocean is the abode of jewels, and that poetry is the abode of fine sayings that are like jewels — hence it is called an 'ocean.' 'But the <s>Setubandha</s> and the like are also composed in another Prakrit — why then is it said to be composed in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s> Prakrit?' It is not read here [as saying] that it is composed exclusively in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s> Prakrit. It is said to be composed of that by reason of predominance — just as 'an army composed of horses' [does not exclude other elements].

The <s>Mahārāṣṭras</s> include <s>Kuntala</s>, <s>Āmuralāsaka</s>, <s>Vidarbha</s>, <s>Māhivācara</s>, <s>Traivaiśya</s>, and other sub-divisions (?). The language that has these <s>Mahārāṣṭras</s> as its abode and foundation —
<s>Harivṛddha</s>:

children.text: अण्णेहि अ एएहि अ सरिसं च अ होइ सामण्णे इति ।
children.translated_text: 'Common [language] is similar to both these and the others.'
There is another [variety] — he says:
But common language (<s>sāmānya</s>) too is a variety of Prakrit. As stated by

children.text: सौरसेनी च गौडी च लाटी चान्या च तादृशी ।
children.translated_text: <s>Śaurasenī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, and <s>Lāṭī</s>, and another such [language] — /
these come to be designated simply as 'Prakrit' in [literary] usage // 35 //

children.text: लाटाधिष्ठाना लाटी । अन्या च पाञ्चालीमागधीत्यादिका तादृशी तथाविधा एवंप्रकारा सामान्यभाषा प्राकृतमित्यनेनैव नाम्ना नापभ्रंश इत्यनेन सन्निधिं प्रयोगं याति । कुत्र, व्यवहारेषु नाटकादिषु । व्यवह्रियते [शि]क्षणं व्यवहारः [तत्र] प्रवर्तते एभिरिति सा च मुसुमुरिअ मूअच्छि
children.translated_text: based in <s>Lāṭa</s> is <s>Lāṭī</s>. 'And another' — <s>Pāñcālī</s>, <s>Māgadhī</s>, and the like — 'such,' i.e., of this kind, of this nature — this common language attains usage under the name 'Prakrit' alone, not under the name 'Apabhraṃśa.' Where? 'In usages' — i.e., in dramas and the like. That by which instruction is conducted, is 'usage' — [the common language] operates in those [contexts]. And that includes <s>musumuriya</s>, <s>mūyacchi</s>,
<s>acchike</s>, etc., as stated by
<s>Harivṛddha</s>.

children.text: । एवं कृत्वा चतस्रः प्राकृ[त]मय्यो भाषा दर्शिताः भवन्ति । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: Thus, four Prakrit languages have been shown. As stated:

children.text: सद्दभवा सद्दसमा देसीत्ति अ तिण्णिया अ अण्णेहि ।
children.translated_text: '<s>Tadbhava</s> (word-born), <s>Tatsama</s> (word-identical), and <s>Deśī</s> — these three, and the others: /

children.text: सामण्णया अइ सहि आया अअय इतराणि आउ ॥ इति ।[?]
children.translated_text: the common [language] — my friend, these have come [to be known], and the rest are subsidiary.' [?]
But the details should be [sought] from that [specialized] treatise.
Based in <s>Sūrasena</s> is <s>Śaurasenī</s>; based in <s>Gauḍa</s> is <s>Gauḍī</s>;
What is Apabhraṃśa? — to this he says:
The languages of the <s>Ābhīras</s> and others are known as Apabhraṃśa in poetry; /
but in [grammatical] treatises, everything other than Sanskrit is declared as Apabhraṃśa // 36 //

children.text: आभीरा वाहिकाः । आदिशब्देन ढक्कादिपरिग्रहः । तेषां गिरो भाषा अपभ्रंश इति, अपभ्रंशनाम्ना व्यपदिश्यन्त इति स्थितिर्व्यवस्था । कुत्रेत्याह—काव्येषु गद्यपद्यमिश्रात्मकेषु कविप्रयोगेषु । अपभ्रंशोऽपि प्राकृतवच्चतुर्धा स्मर्यते । यदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: The <s>Ābhīras</s> are the <s>Vāhīkas</s>. By the word 'and others,' the <s>Ḍhakkas</s> and others are included. Their languages are Apabhraṃśa — i.e., they are designated by the name 'Apabhraṃśa' — this is the established convention. Where? — he says, 'in poetry' — in compositions that are of the nature of prose, verse, and mixed — in the usages of poets. Apabhraṃśa too, like Prakrit, is remembered as fourfold. As stated:
'<s>Śabdabhava</s> (word-derived), <s>Śabdasama</s> (word-identical), <s>Deśīya</s> (regional), and <s>Sarvaśabdasāmānya</s> (common to all words) — /
know Apabhraṃśa as fourfold, properly established.' Thus.

children.text: त्रिधाप्याम्नायते । यथोक्तम्—अपरं त्रिप्रकारत्वं शास्त्रस्थित्या प्राकृतमपभ्रंशः पैशाचिकं चेति ॥
children.translated_text: It is also traditionally known as threefold. As stated: 'Another threefold classification according to the convention of treatises: Prakrit, Apabhraṃśa, and Paiśācika.'
Showing what constitutes the full range of Sanskrit literary composition, he says:
Sanskrit [includes] <s>sargabandha</s> (canto-composition) and the rest; Prakrit is that which is <s>skandhaka</s> and the like; /
<s>Osara</s> and the rest are Apabhraṃśa; <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) and the like are mixed // 37 //

children.text: यत् सर्गबन्धादि तत्सर्वं संस्कृतं वाङ्मयं वेदितव्यम् । आदिशब्देन पृथक् संघातादिपरिग्रहः । यत् स्कन्धकादिवाङ्मयं तत्सर्वं प्राकृतं वेदितव्यम् । अत्रापि आदिशब्देन गाव्याद्युपादानं सेतुबन्धादिवद् द्रष्टव्यम् ।
ओसरादीनि काव्यानि यानि तानि सर्वा[ण्य]पभ्रंशो विज्ञायताम् । तानि वलयकरम्बकादीनि । आदिशब्देन रासकादिपरिग्रहः । नाटकादि तु यत्तत् मिश्रकं संस्कृतादिभिर्वेदितव्यम् । आदिशब्देन भाणकादिपरिग्रहः ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>osara</s> and other compositions — all those should be understood as Apabhraṃśa. Those include <s>valayaka</s>, <s>karambaka</s>, and the like. By the word 'and the rest,' <s>rāsaka</s> and the like are included. <s>Nāṭaka</s> and the like — that is mixed, to be understood through Sanskrit and the rest. By the word 'and the rest,' <s>bhāṇaka</s> and the like are included.

Whatever is <s>sargabandha</s> and the rest — all that is to be understood as Sanskrit literary composition. By the word 'and the rest,' <s>pṛthak-saṃghāta</s> (separate aggregation) and the like are included. Whatever is <s>skandhaka</s> and the rest — all that is to be understood as Prakrit. Here too, by the word 'and the rest,' the inclusion of <s>gāvya</s> and the like is to be understood, just as the <s>Setubandha</s> and so forth.
'How is <s>kathā</s> and the like [classified]?' — to this he says:
<s>Kathā</s> and the rest are recited in all languages and in Sanskrit; /
but the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>, of wondrous content, they declare to be composed in <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s> (the language of spirits) // 38 //

children.text: कथा आदिर्यस्याख्यानकादेः स कथादिः प्रबन्धः । सर्वाभिर्भाषाभिः संस्कृतप्राकृतापभ्रंशपैशाचिका[दि]भिः । समुच्चयविकल्पाभ्यां यथासम्भवं

पठ्यते विरच्यते । संस्कृतेन चेति गतार्थमपि पृथगुक्तम् । प्राधान्यख्यापनार्थं न तु केवलार्थम्, प्राकृतादेरत्रातिपृथगभिधानप्रसङ्गात् । यथा संस्कृतप्राकृतापभ्रंशाख्यं भाषात्रयं शुद्धमपि प्रयुक्तं दृश्यते, न तथा पैशाचिकम् । भाषानुगतमेव तु दृश्यते चेदाह । भूतभाषामयीत्यादि । भूतभाषा पैशाचिकवाक् तद्विकारस्तन्मयीं शुद्धपैशाचिकाम् । तुशब्दोऽर्थान्तरविवक्षायाम् । बृहत्कथामाहुः कथयन्ति तद्विदः । केवलपैशाचिकी बृहत्कथा दृश्यते इत्यर्थः । किंविशिष्टामित्याह—अद्भुतार्थामिति । अद्भुतः प्रकृष्टो नानाविधः अपूर्वः अर्थोऽभिधेयं यस्यां तामाहुरिति प्रकृतं प्रधानकथनं चैतत् । अतएवाद्भुतार्थामिति । न त्वयमेव, अन्यस्या अपि भूतभाषामय्या रत्नप्रभादिकाया दर्शनात् ॥
children.translated_text: as the case may be, [it] is 'recited' — i.e., composed. 'And in Sanskrit' — though this is already included [in 'all languages'], it is stated separately for the purpose of indicating [Sanskrit's] pre-eminence, not for the sake of isolation alone, since [otherwise] there would be occasion for stating Prakrit and the rest separately too. Just as Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Apabhraṃśa — the triad of languages — is seen used in pure form, Paiśācika is not [seen in pure form]. But if it is seen only as accompanying [another] language — he says 'made of <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s>' etc. '<s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s>' is the Paiśācika speech; its modification — 'made of it' — means pure Paiśācika. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates a different topic. 'The <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>' — those who know it declare [it to be so]. The meaning is that the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s> is seen to be in pure Paiśācika. 'Of what character?' — he says, 'of wondrous content.' '<s>Adbhuta</s>' — extraordinary, of various kinds, unprecedented — the content, i.e., the subject matter of which is [such] — this is the principal statement. Therefore 'of wondrous content.' But this [the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>] is not the only one, since another [work] also composed in <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s>, such as the <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, is seen.

A composition beginning with <s>kathā</s> — i.e., <s>ākhyānaka</s> and the rest — is the '<s>kathā</s> and the rest.' 'In all languages' — Sanskrit, Prakrit, Apabhraṃśa, Paiśācika, and the like. By conjunction and alternative,

children.text: यदेतत्त्रिविधं काव्यशरीरं भाषाभेदाच्चतुर्विधमुक्तम्, तदेव द्विधाविनियोगभेदाद् दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: That which has been stated as this threefold body of poetry, fourfold by difference of language — showing the same in two [divisions] by the difference of purpose, he says:
<s>Lāsya</s>, <s>chalinā</s>, <s>śamyā</s>, and the rest are for viewing (<s>prekṣā</s>); the other, /
is indeed for hearing (<s>śravya</s>) — this too is declared as a twofold classification // 39 //
<s>Lāsya</s> is dance in which <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) is predominant. As stated:
'Dance performed by one unable [to perform] <s>tāṇḍava</s>, mixed with <s>āviddhakaraṇa</s> movements — /

children.text: प्रियकारिणा प्रियाया हरेण लास्यं पुरा सृष्टम् ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: <s>Lāsya</s> was formerly created by <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who wished to please his beloved.' Thus.

children.text: छलिनं [छद्म]प्रधानं नृत्तम् । लस्या तालविशेषप्राधान्यम् । सा च दक्षिणपाणिपातलक्षणा । यथोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: <s>Chalinā</s> is dance in which deception (<s>chadma</s>) is predominant. <s>Lasyā</s> has the predominance of a particular type of rhythmic beat. And that is characterized by the fall of the right hand. As stated:
'The fall of the left hand is [called <s>lasyā</s>]; <s>tāla</s> (rhythmic beat) with the left hand is <s>vāmaka</s>; /
the fall of both hands is known as <s>sannipāta</s>' (conjunction).

children.text: तत्प्रतिपादकं काव्यं लास्याद्यक्तं तादर्थ्यात् । आदिशब्देन च स्कन्धकादि-

परिग्रहः । तदेतत् प्रेक्षार्थम् । प्रेक्षा प्रेक्षणं चक्षुषा ग्रहणम् । तस्यै इदं प्रेक्षैवार्थः प्रयोजनं तदालम्ब्य प्रवृत्तिर्यस्य तत् प्रेक्षार्थम् । प्रेक्षा तदर्थस्याभिनयप्रधानत्वात् प्रेक्षणे विनियुज्यते, तत्श्रव
children.translated_text: are included. All this is 'for viewing' (<s>prekṣārtha</s>). <s>Prekṣā</s> is viewing, apprehension by the eye. That for which this [viewing] — viewing itself — is the purpose, i.e., the goal in relation to which activity [proceeds] — that is <s>prekṣārtha</s>. Since the purpose of viewing is primarily enactment (<s>abhinaya</s>), it is applied to viewing; as for the auditory

children.text: णं तु सदपि न विवक्षितम् । तस्माल्लास्यादेरितरत् अन्यत् सर्गबन्धादि श्रव्यमेव श्रवण एव विनियुज्यते, अनभिनेयार्थत्वात्, न प्रेक्षणे इति । सैषा एवं रूपा द्वयी द्विविधा गतिर्व्यवस्था विनियोगकृता उदाहृता कथिता । तस्य त्रिविधस्य काव्यस्य न केवलं चतुर्विधेत्यपि शब्दः । यदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: However, [the dramatic element] though present, is not intended [here]. Therefore, other than <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) and the like — that is, <s>sargabandha</s> (canto-composition) and so forth — is employed only in hearing, i.e., it belongs only to the audible (<s>śravya</s>) category, since its meaning is not suitable for dramatic enactment, not in visual performance. This twofold arrangement, of such a nature, has been stated as governing the application. Of that threefold poetry — not merely fourfold, as the word also [implies]. As has been said —
"By these, both the body of poetry and its ornamentation have been shown."
Thus, to this extent the body — the substratum of ornamentation — has been indicated.
The poetry that presents these [dance forms] is called '<s>lāsya</s> and the rest' by reason of its purpose. By the word 'and the rest,' <s>skandhaka</s> and the like
Now, wishing to indicate the ornamentation of that [poetry], and laying out the approach, he says —
There exists more than one path of speech, with subtle mutual differences;
Among these, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> [paths] are described, as their distinction is manifest. [verse 40]

children.text: गिरां काव्यानां मार्गो रचनाप्रकारः, अनेको भिन्नो विजातीयः उदीच्यादिदिग्देशभेदेन अस्ति प्रवर्त्तते । किमेकान्तविसदृशोऽसौ, नेत्याह—सूक्ष्मभेदः परस्परमिति । परस्परमन्यो यम् सूक्ष्मः स्वल्पः भेदोऽन्तरं यस्य स तथा । विजातीयत्वेऽपि सदृशोऽस्ति मार्गः, गोगवयादिवदित्युत्सर्गः । तस्यापवादमाह—तत्रेत्यादि । तत्र तस्मिन्ननेकस्मिन् मार्गे वैदर्भगौडीयौ प्रस्फुटान्तरौ । विदर्भा दाक्षिणात्याः, एकदेशेन समुदायोपलक्षणत्वात् । तेषामयं वैदर्भः । गौडाः पौरस्त्याः तेषामयं गौडीयः । तौ मार्गौ प्रस्फुटौ । महदन्तरं भेदोऽनयोरिति प्रस्फुटान्तरौ । विजातीयत्वेऽपि शेषो मार्गो वैदर्भेण सदृशः, गवेव गवयः । गौडीयस्तु विसदृशः । गवेव करभः । व्यक्तिभेदस्त्वेकैकस्यामप्यनन्तः प्रतिकविस्थितः स इह न विवक्षितः । तद् वक्ष्यति—
तद्भेदास्तु न शक्यन्ते वक्तुं प्रतिकविस्थिताः । इति ।
children.translated_text: "Their subdivisions, residing in each individual poet, cannot be enumerated." Thus.

The path of speech — that is, of poetry — means the mode of composition. It is manifold, diverse, of different kinds, existing according to the distinctions of direction and region such as northern and so forth. Is it then entirely dissimilar? No, he says — 'with subtle mutual differences.' Mutually, one from another, the difference is subtle, i.e., slight — that is the meaning. Even though of different kinds, there is a similar path, like the cow and the <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) and so forth — this is the general rule. He states the exception to this — 'among these' and so forth. Among these, in that manifold path, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> have manifest distinction. The <s>Vidarbha</s> people are southerners — since a part represents the whole. Theirs is the <s>Vaidarbha</s> [path]. The <s>Gauḍa</s> people are easterners; theirs is the <s>Gauḍīya</s> [path]. Those two paths have manifest [distinction] — the difference between them is great, hence they are 'of manifest distinction.' Even though of different kinds, the remaining paths are similar to the <s>Vaidarbha</s>, as the <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is to the cow. But the <s>Gauḍīya</s> is dissimilar — as the camel is to the cow. The distinction among individual [poets], however, being infinite and residing in each individual poet, is not intended here. That he will state —

children.text: यदि नामैवं ततः किमित्याह—ततश्च तावेव वर्ण्येते विभज्येते । प्रस्फुटान्तरयोः सुविभजत्वात् । शेषस्तु वैदर्भप्रायत्वात् पृथग् नोच्यते ।
children.translated_text: If that is indeed so, then what [follows]? He says — therefore those two alone are described, i.e., distinguished, because the two of manifest distinction are easy to differentiate. The remainder, however, being mostly similar to <s>Vaidarbha</s>, is not mentioned separately.
And having done thus, what was said
by <s>Bhāmaha</s> —
"Other wise men hold that there exists [a path] other than the <s>Vaidarbha</s>;

children.text: तदेव च किल ज्यायः सदर्थमपि नापरम् ॥
children.translated_text: And that [<s>Vaidarbha</s>] alone is indeed superior, even if [the other] has good meaning, the other is not [superior]."
"'This is <s>Gauḍīya</s>, that is <s>Vaidarbha</s>' — why [make] a separate [distinction]?
By the principle of following convention, those of no intelligence call them by different names."

children.text: इति, तद् भङ्ग्या निरस्तम् । तथाहि—कश्चित्काव्यरचनाप्रकारः शब्दालंकारलक्षणो दाक्षिणात्यानां निजो वैदर्भमार्ग इति व्यवह्रियते, यथा यानविशेषो दक्षिणमार्ग इति । तद्विपरीतस्तु पौरस्त्यानां काव्यरचनाप्रकारो गौडीय इति व्यपदिश्यते । यथा दक्षिणमार्गविलक्षणो यानप्रकार उत्तरमार्ग इति । ततश्च वास्तवीयं नानाता कथममेधसाम् । या हि भ्रान्तिकृता सा भवेदमेधसां विपरीतदृशाम्, यथैकस्मिन्न[पि] चन्द्रमसि । इयं तु सुमेधसामपि, विपरीतदृशामेव, वस्तुभेदकृतत्वात् सू[र्या]चन्द्रमसोरिव । तस्मात् स्वभावत एव विलक्षणावेतौ मार्गौ । यद्वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: — that has been indirectly refuted. For thus: a certain mode of poetic composition, characterized by verbal ornamentation, natural to the southerners, is conventionally called the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path — just as a particular mode of travel is called 'the southern route.' Its opposite, the mode of poetic composition natural to the easterners, is designated as <s>Gauḍīya</s> — just as a mode of travel different from the southern route is called 'the northern route.' Therefore, how can the real diversity be [the product] of those without intelligence? For that which is produced by error would belong to the unintelligent, those of distorted vision, as with a single moon [appearing double]. But this [distinction] exists even for the highly intelligent, precisely because it is produced by a real difference in the objects — like [the distinction between] the sun and the moon. Therefore, these two paths are by nature distinct. As he will state —
"Thus the twofold path is distinct, from the determination of their respective natures." Thus.

children.text: अथ मतं कथं तर्हि पौरस्त्येषु वैदर्भो दृश्यते पद्यसाधारणो यथा दाक्षिणात्यानामेव । दाक्षिणात्येषु वा गौडीय इति । तत्किमेतावता तेषामसौ निजः स्यात् । तेष्वसौ दृश्यमानोऽपि न निजः दक्षिणमार्गवत्, यथा दाक्षिणात्यानाम् । नहि चन्दनं देशान्तरे दृश्यत इति तज्जमेव स्यात् । देशान्तरदृष्टमपि हि मलयजमेव तत् । तथा वैदर्भः पौरस्त्येषु कथञ्चित् दृश्यमानोऽपि वैदर्भ एव, यो दाक्षिणात्यानां सहजः । गौडीयोऽपि दाक्षिणात्येषु कथञ्चिद् दृश्यते तथापि पौरस्त्यानामेवासौ निजत्वात् । तदेतौ काव्यरचनाप्रकारौ मार्गौ प्रकृतिविलक्षणो दक्षिणात्यैर्गौडैश्च व्यपदिश्ये
ते । निजत्वाद् देशभाषादिवत् वैदर्भगौडीय इति । एतावत्तु स्यात् ।
children.translated_text: respectively, as <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s>, due to their being native [to each], like regional dialects and so forth. But this much may be [asked] —

Now, if one objects: how then is the <s>Vaidarbha</s> [style] seen among the easterners, as commonly [found] in verse just as among the southerners themselves? Or the <s>Gauḍīya</s> among the southerners? Does it thereby become their own? Even though seen among them, it is not their own — like the southern route; just as it belongs to the southerners [by nature]. For sandalwood is not native to another region merely because it is seen there. Even when seen in another region, it is still <s>malayaja</s> (born of the Malaya mountains). Similarly, the <s>Vaidarbha</s>, even when somehow seen among the easterners, is still <s>Vaidarbha</s> alone — that which is innate to the southerners. The <s>Gauḍīya</s> too, even when somehow seen among the southerners, still belongs to the easterners alone, due to its being native [to them]. Thus these two modes of poetic composition, paths distinct in nature, are designated by the southerners and the <s>Gauḍa</s> people

children.text: प्रतिविशिष्ट इति तच्च मार्गद्वयमिदानीं विभज्यते । प्रतिविशेषे तु सन्तः प्रमाणमिति विभजन्नाह—
children.translated_text: is distinguished in what respect? And that twofold path is now differentiated. Regarding the specific distinction, the authoritative scholars are the standard — thus differentiating, he says —
What are the characteristics of those two, and which of them
<s>Śleṣa</s> (compactness), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy),
<s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), <s>udāratva</s> (nobility), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>kānti</s> (grace), and <s>samādhi</s> (figurative propriety). [verse 41]

children.text: श्लिष्टिः श्लेषो वार्थगौरवम् । प्रसत्तिः प्रसादः प्रकाशार्थता । समता पद्यापेक्षया [बन्धतुल्यतो]पादानम् । माधुर्यं शब्दे अर्थे च रसवत्ता । सुकुमारता अपरुषाक्षरबाहुल्यम् । अर्थस्याभिधेयस्य व्यक्तिः शब्देन न्यायेन वा ग्रहणम् । अन्यथा दुष्प्रापत्वाद् वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: <s>Śliṣṭi</s> is <s>śleṣa</s>, or [it means] weightiness of meaning. <s>Prasatti</s> is <s>prasāda</s>, meaning transparency of sense. <s>Samatā</s> is the employment of [compositional] equality in relation to verse — uniformity of construction. <s>Mādhurya</s> is the quality of being flavorful (<s>rasavattā</s>) in both word and meaning. <s>Sukumāratā</s> is the predominance of non-harsh, soft letters. <s>Vyakti</s> of <s>artha</s> — the expressed meaning — is its apprehension through word or through logical propriety. Otherwise, since it would be difficult to grasp, he will state —
"For comprehension that violates word and logic is not felicitous." Thus.

children.text: उदारत्वं प्रकृष्टता केनचिदर्थेन सनाथत्वम् । ओजः समासवृत्तिबाहुल्यम् । कान्तिः सर्वलोकमनोहरत्वम् । समाधिर्भगवत्प्रतीत्यनुसारिणी गौणार्थता ।
children.translated_text: <s>Udāratva</s> (nobility) is excellence, being endowed with some [special] significance. <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is the predominance of compound constructions. <s>Kānti</s> (grace) is the quality of captivating the minds of all people. <s>Samādhi</s> (figurative propriety) is the use of secondary meaning (<s>gauṇārtha</s>) in accordance with the understanding of the Lord [i.e., established convention].
These ten qualities are known as the life-breath of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path;
Their reversal is mostly seen in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path. [verse 42]

children.text: इत्येवंरूपा दश गुणाः शब्दालङ्कारस्वभावाः प्राणाः जीवितं स्मृता दृश्यन्त इति यावत् । कस्य वैदर्भमार्गस्य दाक्षिणात्यकाव्यपद्धतेः सम्बन्धिनः । तैर्हि वैदर्भमार्गः काव्यशरीरं प्राणिति । तदभावे त्वसन्नेव । ततश्च शब्दालङ्कारभूतः श्लेषादिदशगुणात्मकः काव्यरचनाविशेषो दाक्षिणात्यानां स्वाभाविको वैदर्भमार्ग इत्यर्थः सम्पद्यते । एवंरूपस्तावद्वैदर्भमार्गः । गौडीयः किंरूपः, तद्विपरीतस्वभाव इति दर्शयन्नाह—एषामित्यादि । एषां श्लेषादीनां विपर्ययो विपक्षोऽश्लेषादिः लक्ष्यते दृश्यते, कुत्र ? गौडानां वर्त्मनि काव्ये । अर्थव्यक्त्या देः कस्यचिद् गुणस्य साधारणत्वात् प्राय इत्याह । बाहुल्येनेत्यर्थः । प्रायोग्रहणसंगृहीतं साधारणगुणं स्वयमेव यथावसरं दर्शयिष्यति । स्वाभाविकस्तेषामेषा रच

children.translated_text: The <s>Vaidarbha</s>, however,
would exist [among them] only in an artificial manner — such is the implication.

Thus these ten qualities, whose nature is verbal ornamentation, are known as the life-breath — that is, the vital force — [of that path]. Of which? Of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path, belonging to the poetic tradition of the southerners. For by these the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path, the body of poetry, is animated. In their absence, it is as good as dead. Therefore, the specific mode of poetic composition that constitutes verbal ornamentation, consisting of the ten qualities beginning with <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness), natural to the southerners — this is what is meant by the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path. Such is the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path in its form. What then is the form of the <s>Gauḍīya</s>? Showing that it is of the opposite nature, he says — 'of these' and so forth. The reversal of these [qualities] beginning with <s>śleṣa</s> — that is, their opposites such as absence of compactness — is seen. Where? In the path, i.e., the poetry, of the <s>Gauḍa</s> people. He says 'mostly' because some qualities like <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) are common [to both]. The meaning is 'predominantly.' The quality that is common, included by the word 'mostly,' he himself will show as occasion arises. This is their natural mode of composition.

children.text: इदानीं यथोद्देशमेषां निर्देशं सविपर्ययं सोदाहरणं कुर्वन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Now, explaining these in order of enumeration, with their opposites and with examples, he says —
Compact [composition] is that which is untouched by looseness, abounding in letters of slight aspiration;
Loose [composition] is like '<s>mālatī</s>-garland swarming with wandering bees.' [verse 43]

children.text: शिथिलस्य भाव शैथिल्यं बन्धलाघवम् । अस्पृष्टं त्यक्तम् । अस्पृष्टं शैथिल्यं

येन तदस्पृष्टशैथिल्यमित्यत्र श्लिष्टं विधीयते । यद् दृढबन्धकाव्यं तत् श्लिष्टं श्लेषयोगाद्वेदितव्यमिति । स्वतन्त्रस्य धर्मस्यासम्भवात् धर्मिनिष्ठः श्लेषो दर्शितः प्राक् । तन्मते विवक्षया स्वशब्देनोपात्तः । एवं प्रसादादिष्वप्यनुसर्त्तव्यम् । श्लेषविपर्ययं दर्शयन्नाह—अल्पप्राणेत्यादि । अल्पप्राणानि वर्गप्रथमादीनि अक्षराणि उत्तराणि भूयांसि यस्मिन् तैर्वोत्तरमधिकं तदनूद्य शिथिलं विधीयते । अल्पप्राणवर्णप्रायं तच्छिथिलं श्लिष्टविपरीतं काव्यं वेदितव्यम् इति । यथेत्युदाहरति । यथेदं शिथिलं तथान्यदप्येवंजातीयकं द्रष्टव्यमिति यथाशब्दार्थः । एवमुत्तरत्राप्यनुगन्तव्यम् । मालतीमाला जातिपुष्पस्त्रगियं लोलैः कुसुमसौरभलोलुपैरलिभिर्भ्रभरैः कलिला व्याप्ता इत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: that which is untouched by looseness — in this [expression], <s>śliṣṭa</s> (compact) is predicated. That which is poetry of firm composition should be understood as <s>śliṣṭa</s>, through its connection with <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness). Since an independent quality cannot exist [by itself], <s>śleṣa</s> as residing in the qualified entity was shown earlier. In that view, it is taken up by its own term according to the intended meaning. The same should be followed for <s>prasāda</s> and the other [qualities] as well. Showing the opposite of <s>śleṣa</s>, he says — 'of slight aspiration' and so forth. Letters of slight aspiration — the first [and other unaspirated consonants] of the <s>varga</s> (consonant groups) — are predominant, i.e., more numerous in which [composition]; having cited that as the subject, 'loose' is predicated [of it]. That which predominantly consists of unaspirated letters should be understood as loose — the opposite of compact composition. 'As' introduces the example. Just as this is loose, so too other compositions of the same kind should be understood — that is the meaning of the word 'as.' The same should be followed in subsequent cases as well. The <s>mālatī</s>-garland — a string of jasmine flowers — is <s>kalilā</s> (swarming), i.e., pervaded, by wandering (<s>lola</s>) bees, greedy for the fragrance of the blossoms — that is the meaning.
The state of being loose is <s>śaithilya</s> (looseness) — lightness of composition. 'Untouched' means abandoned. 'Untouched by looseness' —

children.text: यदि शैथिल्यं दुष्टमेवंविधं गौडैरादृतम्, तदिहापि केनचित् गुणेन भवितव्यम् अन्यथा सर्वथा निर्गुणं कथमाद्रियत इत्याह—
children.translated_text: If looseness of this kind, being a fault, is favored by the <s>Gauḍa</s> poets, then there must be some quality in it here too; otherwise, how would something entirely devoid of quality be favored? Thus he says —
That [looseness] is favored by the <s>Gauḍa</s> poets on account of [its] compositional weightiness, through the perception of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration);
The <s>Vaidarbha</s> poets [would say]: 'A <s>mālatī</s>-garland overrun by bees.' [verse 44]

children.text: तदिति शिथिलमिष्टमादृतं गौड़ैरनुप्रासो माधुर्यसंगृहीतः शब्दालङ्कारस्तस्य तस्मिन् बुद्ध्याऽनुप्रासः शब्दरसो गुणोऽस्तीति तैरेवंविधमिष्टम् । शैथिल्यं तु दोषो न दृष्टः । अनुप्रासधियेत्यनेन चैतत् कथयति । अनुप्रासोऽपि गौडानामेवंविधो यः शैथिल्यमा

children.translated_text: and also harshness (<s>pāruṣya</s>). As he will state —
"Such [alliteration] brings about harshness and looseness of composition;
Therefore the southerners do not employ <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) in this manner."

children.text: इति दाक्षिणात्येष्टं पश्चाद् दर्शयिष्यति । श्लेषमुदाहरन्नाह—वैदर्भैः दाक्षिणात्यैर्मालतीदाम लंघितं भ्रमरैरिति ईदृशं श्लिष्ट[मिष्ट]मिति प्रकृतम् । कुतः ? बन्धस्य रचनायागौरवात् शैथिल्यात् कारणात् । अर्थस्तु पूर्वक एव । नन्वत्रापि दोषोऽस्ति माधुर्यलक्षणस्यानुप्रासस्याभावात् । अमाधुर्यं लक्षणम् (?) ॥
children.translated_text: What is favored by the southerners he will show later. Illustrating <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness), he says — by the <s>Vaidarbha</s> poets, i.e., the southerners, 'a <s>mālatī</s>-garland overrun by bees' — such compact [composition] is favored: this is what is understood [from the context]. Why? Because of the weightiness — that is, the [absence of] looseness — of the composition (<s>bandha</s>). The meaning is the same as before. But is there not a fault here too, namely the absence of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) characterized by <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness)? The absence of sweetness is the characteristic [fault here] (?).

'That' refers to the loose [composition] — it is favored, cherished, by the <s>Gauḍa</s> poets. <s>Anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), included under <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), is a verbal ornamentation; through the perception of it — the understanding that there is the quality of phonetic charm (<s>śabdarasa</s>) in the form of <s>anuprāsa</s> — such [composition] is favored by them. But the looseness is not regarded [by them] as a fault. And by [the expression] 'through the perception of <s>anuprāsa</s>,' he conveys this: the <s>anuprāsa</s> of the <s>Gauḍa</s> poets, being of such a kind, brings about looseness
What is <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity) like? He says —
Lucid [speech] has well-known meaning: 'The mark of the moon, having the luster of a blue lotus,
bestows splendor' — [such] speech is felicitous through [immediate] comprehension. [verse 45]

children.text: प्रसिद्धः प्रकाशः सुगमोऽर्थोऽभिधेयं शब्दार्था यस्य तत्तथा । नतु भावार्थः, तस्य स्वभावगम्भीरत्वात् । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: That whose meaning — the expressed sense, the word-meanings — is well-known, i.e., clear, easily accessible, is thus [called <s>prasāda</s>]. But not the implied meaning (<s>bhāvārtha</s>), for that is profound by nature. As has been said —
"The intention of the poet, beyond the reach of words, through luminous words alone,
is entered into by those who have labored with the knowledge of inner sentiment; [they reveal the depth of meaning through the profundity of sense.]" [?]

children.text: इति । ततः प्रसिद्धार्थमनूद्य प्रसादवत्प्रसादगुणयुक्तं प्रसन्नं वेदिव्यमिति विधीयते । कथयन्नेव उदाहरति- इन्दोश्चन्द्रस्य लक्ष्म चिह्नम् इन्दीवरद्युति नीलोत्पलशोभं लक्ष्मीं श्रियं तनोति विस्तारयति इन्दावेव । नीलोत्पलरुचिना चिह्नेन चन्द्रः शोभत इत्यर्थः । इत्येवंविधं वचः काव्यम् । प्रतीत्या भ्फटित्यर्थावगमेन सुतरां मनोहरं प्रसन्नमिति यावत् । भावार्थगम्भीरं तु यद् भवेत् तदपि प्रसन्नमेव । शब्दार्थप्रसत्तेः प्रतिविशिष्टमेव च तादृशम् । यदाह भारविः—
children.translated_text: Thus, having cited 'of well-known meaning' as the subject, 'endowed with <s>prasāda</s>' — possessing the quality of lucidity, i.e., clear — is predicated. Even while stating [the definition], he gives an example: the <s>lakṣman</s> (mark) of <s>Indu</s> (the moon), having the radiance of a blue lotus (<s>indīvara</s>), bestows <s>Lakṣmī</s> (splendor) — that is, it extends beauty to the moon itself. The moon is beautified by the mark that has the luster of a blue lotus — that is the meaning. Such speech, such poetry, is supremely captivating through <s>pratīti</s> (immediate comprehension), through the instant apprehension of meaning — that is, it is clear. But that which is profound in implied meaning (<s>bhāvārtha</s>) is also clear [in this sense]. And such [poetry] is indeed distinguished by the clarity of its word-meaning. As <s>Bhāravi</s> says —
"<s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech/the goddess of learning), whose words are clear and profound, does not proceed for those who have not performed meritorious deeds."
"The red rays of the sun, falling upon the lotus cups,
appear like corals upon the feet of beautiful women."
This is another example.
in the other path, he shows, saying —
The opposite of <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity)
What is not well-established is also favored by the <s>Gauḍīya</s> poets, [considering it] 'learned';
For example: 'The one whose mark resembles the not-very-white water-born [lotus], the white-rayed one [i.e., the moon].' [verse 46]

children.text: गौडीयैः पौरस्त्यैर्नातिरूढमपि अतिरूढमत्यन्तप्रसिद्धार्थम् । तद्विपरीतं नातिरूढमत्यन्ताप्रसिद्धार्थमपि । न केवलमप्रसिद्धमित्यपिशब्दः । अप्रसिद्धार्थमिष्यत एव । यद्यपि अतिशयेनाप्य प्रसिद्धार्थं गूढ़ामिधेयमप्रसन्नतरं तदपीष्यते इत्यर्थः । किं पुनः कारणं प्रसन्नं परित्यज्य अप्रसन्नमिष्यतो निष्कारणमेतन्न सम्भाव्यत इति चेदाह—व्युत्पन्नमिति कृत्वा प्रसिद्धं सुकरमेवायत्ने[ना]पूर्वशब्दकल्पनया व्युत्पन्नं संस्कृतं विशिष्टं तद् व्युत्पन्नमन्यै रेतादिष्यते इतीदमत्र कारणम् । यथेत्युदाहरति । वलक्षाः शुक्ला

गावो रश्मयो यस्य स वलक्षगुश्चन्द्रः अत्यर्जुनं [अति]शुक्लं [न] तथाऽनत्यर्जुनं नीलम् अप्सु जन्म यस्य तदब्जन्म तच्च नीलसन्निधानान्नीलोत्पलम् । तेन सदृक्षः समानः [अङ्कः] चिह्नं यस्य सः । तथा नीलोत्पलसमानचिह्नश्चन्द्र इत्येतावत्यर्थे इयती व्युत्पत्तिः कृतेति व्युत्पन्ना गौडा इति ॥
children.translated_text: one whose rays (<s>gāvas</s>) are white is <s>valakṣagu</s> — the moon. <s>Atyarjuna</s> means exceedingly white; 'not so,' i.e., <s>anatyarjuna</s>, means dark/blue. That which is born in water (<s>abjanma</s>) — and through association with blue, [it means] a blue lotus. One whose mark (<s>aṅka</s>) is similar (<s>sadṛkṣa</s>) to that — [the compound means] one having a mark resembling a blue lotus. Thus, for just this much meaning — 'the moon with a mark resembling a blue lotus' — this much learned elaboration (<s>vyutpatti</s>) has been employed, and so the <s>Gauḍa</s> poets are [called] 'learned.'

By the <s>Gauḍīya</s> poets, the easterners, 'not well-established' — 'well-established' means having extremely well-known meaning; its opposite, 'not well-established,' means having not entirely well-known meaning. Not merely obscure — the word 'also' [indicates]: even that which has obscure meaning is indeed favored. Even though the expressed meaning is exceedingly obscure, deeply hidden, and most unclear, it is still favored — that is the meaning. What then is the reason that, abandoning the clear, they favor the unclear? It is not possible that this should be without reason — if so objected, he says: thinking it 'learned,' i.e., [regarding] the well-known as easy and [achievable] without effort, [while] through the invention of novel words [it becomes] learned, refined, distinguished — that it is learned is considered [superior] by others: this is the reason here. He gives an example with 'as.' <s>Valakṣa</s> means white;
Indicating <s>samatva</s> (evenness), he says —
Even [composition] is that which is uniform in its constructions — [with] soft, clear, and middle [sounds];
The constructions are arrangements of letters that are a mixture of soft, clear, and [middle sounds]. [verse 47]

children.text: बन्धेषु रचनासु विषये यदविषमम् समम् आदिमध्यान्तेषु चतुर्णामपि पादानां सजातीयबन्धत्वादित्यनूद्य तत्समं काव्यं ज्ञेयमिति विधीयते । कियन्तस्ते बन्धा येष्वविषमं समं स्यादिति चेदाह—त इत्यादि । ते बन्धा मृदुस्फुटमध्यमाः त्रयः सम्भवन्ति । मृदुरशिथिलः कोमलः । शिथिलकोमलस्य श्लेषविपर्ययत्वात् । यथोक्तं प्राक् । मृदुश्रुतिरिति यावत् । स्फुटोऽधिमात्रश्रुतिः । क्रुद्धोद्यस्य सुकुमारविपर्ययत्वात् । यद् वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: 'With subtlety' and so forth.

children.text: उन्मिश्रो मध्यमश्रुतिः । कः पुनरेषां प्रभव इत्याह—मृद्वित्यादि । मृदवो मृदुश्रुतयः ककारादयः यथासम्भवम् । स्फुटा अधिमात्रश्रुतयः घकारादयः । उन्मिश्रा मृदुस्फुटाः संसृष्टा ये वर्णास्तेषां विन्यासो रचना योनिः प्रभवो येषां ते तथा । ते च त्रयः मृदुमध्योऽधिमात्रभेदेन प्रत्येकं त्रिधा सम्भवन्ति । स[मे] तु तेषामेवा[वा]न्तरो भेदः स्यात् । मौलास्त्रय एव बन्धाः । तत्र पद्यं गद्यं द्विधा । यद्येकेन बन्धेन समाप्यते तदा
children.translated_text: <s>Unmiśra</s> (mixed) means 'of middle sound-quality.' What then is their source? — To this he says '<s>mṛdu</s>' and so forth. The soft ones — those of soft sound-quality — are the <s>ka</s>-class letters and others, as applicable. The distinct ones — those of excessive sound-quality — are the <s>gha</s>-class letters and others. The mixed — those in which soft and distinct letters are intermingled — their arrangement, their composition, is the source, the origin — those [compositions] are thus. And those three, by the division of soft, middle, and excessive, each become threefold. In the even [type], there would be a further subdivision of just those. The fundamental compositions are three only. Therein, verse and prose are twofold. When [a poem] is completed with a single [type of] composition, then

children.text: समं काव्यम्, विजातीयबन्धकृतवैषम्याभावात् । अत एवोक्तं बन्धेष्वविषममिति । साम्यं पृथगुदाहृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: the poetry is 'even' (<s>sama</s>), due to the absence of unevenness caused by a different type of composition. Hence it is said 'uniform in compositions.' Evenness has been illustrated separately.

In the subject of compositions (<s>bandha</s>), what is 'uniform' (<s>aviṣama</s>) means 'even' (<s>sama</s>) — because in the beginning, middle, and end, all four quarters have the same type of composition — this having been restated, the rule is prescribed that 'such poetry is to be known as even.' How many are those compositions in which [the poetry] would be uniform? — To this he says 'those' and so forth. Those compositions are three in number: <s>mṛdu</s> (soft), <s>sphuṭa</s> (distinct/hard), and <s>madhyama</s> (middle). <s>Mṛdu</s> means 'not loose' (<s>aśithila</s>), i.e. 'delicate' — since loose-delicate is the opposite of <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion), as stated before. It means 'soft to the ear.' <s>Sphuṭa</s> means 'of excessive sound-quality' — since it is the opposite of <s>sukumāra</s> (tenderness), [being what is] harsh and forceful. As he will state —

children.text: अथ विजातीयबन्धत्वसङ्करस्तदा विषमं काव्यं जायते विजातीयबन्धकृतवैषम्ययोगात् । तदेवमुदाहरन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Now, when there is a mixture of different types of composition, then 'uneven' (<s>viṣama</s>) poetry arises, due to the presence of unevenness caused by a different type of composition. Illustrating this very [principle], he says —
Vocal with the cooing of cuckoos, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze approaches me, /
sprinkled with the drops of crystal-clear, overflowing, splashing water! // 48 //

children.text: कोकिलानामालापैः कूजितैर्वाचालो मुखरो मृदुवसन्ते कोकिलालापस्य मलयानिलस्य च सम्भवादेवमुक्तम् । उच्छलन्तः शीकरा येषां विकीर्यमाणकणानामच्छ-

च्छानामत्यन्तप्रसन्नानां निर्भ्फराणां प्रश्रवणानामम्भस उदकस्य कणैः बिन्दुभिरुक्षितः सिक्तः शीतः मलयानिलो दक्षिणमारुतः मामेति [मा]मुपसर्पतीति योज्यम् । एतद्द्वये मृदुस्फुटविजातीयवर्णसङ्कराद् विषमम् । एतदेव च [वि]जातीयबन्धपूरितमर्द्धद्वयं केवलमृदुबन्धं केवलस्फुटबन्धं च श्लोकद्वितयं भवत् समोदाहरणं सम्पद्यते । तद्यथा—
children.translated_text: supremely pure, flowing — sprinkled, i.e. moistened and cooled, by the drops, the particles of water — the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, the southern wind, approaches me — this should be construed [with the verb]. In these two [halves], due to the mixture of soft and distinct letters of different types, it is uneven. And this very [verse], when the two halves filled with different-type compositions become [instead] a purely soft composition and a purely distinct composition, results in a two-verse [example of] even [poetry]. Namely —
Vocal with the cooing of cuckoos, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze approaches me, /
as if proclaiming the command of <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Spring), whose desire is unbridled. //
Having arisen, the wind bears the bewilderment of bees; /
sprinkled with the drops of crystal-clear, overflowing, splashing water. //
For this [very]
reason, by the master (<s>ārya</s>),
<s>Daṇḍin</s>,
[evenness] was not illustrated separately.

Vocal with the cooings, the songs of cuckoos — [the word] 'vocal' (<s>mukhara</s>) is said because both the cuckoo's cooing and the <s>Malaya</s> breeze naturally occur together in the gentle spring. 'Overflowing' — whose sprays are scattered, whose drops are crystal-clear,

children.text: यत्तर्हि पादे विजातीयवत्त्वं संकीर्णं तदविषममिति कश्चित् मन्यते तन्निषेधार्थं पादमात्रेणापि विषममुदाहरन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Now, if someone thinks that 'unevenness is that which has different types mixed within a single quarter,' to negate this, illustrating unevenness even by a single quarter, he says —
Fragrant from intimacy with sandalwood, the gentle <s>Malaya</s> breeze, /
its steadfastness shattered, competes with the breath from the face of a beautiful woman! // 49 //

children.text: चन्दनानां तरूणां प्रणयः परिचयः सादेश्यात् । ततस्तेनोद्गन्धिः उद्गतो गन्धोऽस्येति चन्दनगन्वगर्भः सुरभिः शिशिरोऽपि वा । निरस्तं समाधिंनिर्विकारत्वं येनोपनीतमन्मथविकारत्वात् स मन्दो मृदुर्मलयमारुतो दक्षिणपवनः । [वररामामुखानिलै]रुत्तमस्त्रीवदनश्वसनैः सह स्पर्द्धते [तान्] निगृह्णाति सुरभितया मृदुत्वेन [रुद्ध]मद्धैर्यतया च साम्यात् । स्पर्द्धायाश्च समानविषयत्वात् तैरुपमीयत इति यावत् । अत्र तृतीयपादेन स्फुटत्वेन विजातीयेन मध्यमबन्धं पादत्रयं संसृष्टमिति विषममेवेदृशम् । एतदेव सजातीयैकपादप्रवेशे समं जायते । तद्यथा—

children.translated_text: Fragrant from intimacy with sandalwood, the gentle <s>Malaya</s> breeze /
competes with the breath from the faces of beautiful women intoxicated by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love). //

Of the sandalwood trees, the intimacy (<s>praṇaya</s>) means familiarity, due to being from the same region. From that, 'fragrant' means 'having an arisen fragrance' — pervaded by the scent of sandalwood, or cool. Its composure of steadiness having been destroyed — because of having acquired the agitation of love — that gentle, i.e. soft, <s>Malaya</s> breeze, the southern wind, competes with, i.e. rivals the breath from the faces of excellent women, through equality in fragrance, softness, and steadiness-disrupting quality. And since competition is between equals, the meaning is that [the breeze] is compared with them. Here, by the third quarter with its distinct [letters] being of a different type, the three quarters of middle composition are mixed — hence this type too is uneven. This very [verse], when a quarter of the same type is introduced, becomes even. Namely —
Now, concluding this [discussion of] the <s>Gauḍīya</s> [path], he says —
Thus, without considering the unevenness, [but] regarding the substance and the profusion of ornament — /
the eastern path of poetry proceeded. // 50 //

children.text: इतीदृशं वैषम्यमसाम्यं विजातीयबन्धसंकरलक्षणम् अनालोच्य अदृष्ट्वाअस्वीकृत्येति यावत् । काव्यपद्धतिः काव्यरचना ववृते प्रवर्त्तते । कालस्येहानन्तत्वादद्यापि प्रवृत्तेः । कतमा पौरस्त्या । पुरः शब्देन पूर्वस्यां दिशि देशे वा व्यवस्थितो जन उक्तः । तस्मात्तत्र भवा [पौरस्त्या] । गौडीयेति यावत् । बन्धविषममेवंविधं काव्यं गौड़ाः कुर्वन्ति । न दाक्षिणात्या इत्यर्थः । कस्तर्हित्वया काव्यपक्षः स्वीकृतो येन काव्यपद्धतिरिति यदुच्यत इति चेदाह—अर्थालङ्कारो जात्यादि
children.translated_text: Thus — such unevenness, characterized by the mixture of different-type compositions, 'without considering' — without seeing, i.e. without adopting. The path of poetry, i.e. the poetic composition, proceeded, i.e. progresses — since time here is endless, the progress continues even today. Which [path]? The eastern (<s>paurastyā</s>). By the word <s>puraḥ</s> (east/before), the people established in the eastern direction or region are denoted. Therefore, that which belongs to them is 'eastern.' This means the <s>Gauḍīya</s> [path]. Poetry with uneven composition of this type is what the <s>Gauḍas</s> compose, not the southerners (<s>dākṣiṇātyāḥ</s>) — this is the meaning. 'Then what poetic side have you adopted, that you speak of a 'path of poetry'?' — To this he says: '<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>' — ornamentation of meaning, characterized by <s>jāti</s> (type) and the like;

children.text: लक्षणः डम्बरोऽक्षरडम्बरः । 'गौडेष्वक्षरडम्बर' इति । तावुभौ [अवेक्ष]माणा स्वीकुर्वती ववृते इति प्रकृतम् । द्वयमेतत् गौडवर्त्मनि दृश्यते । शब्दालङ्कारस्तु बन्धसाम्यलक्षणो नेक्षत इत्यर्थः । एते च बन्धास्त्रयोऽपि यथावसरं विनियुक्ताः शोभामा[त]न्वन्तीति दाक्षिणात्यैरिष्यत एव ।
children.translated_text: '<s>ḍambara</s>' means 'profusion of syllables' (<s>akṣaraḍambara</s>). As in '<s>gauḍeṣu akṣaraḍambara</s>' (in the <s>Gauḍa</s> [style], profusion of syllables). 'Regarding' both of these, i.e. adopting them, [the poetry] proceeded — this is the main point. These two are seen in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path. But the ornament of sound (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>), characterized by evenness of composition, is not regarded [by them] — this is the meaning. And all three of these compositions, when employed as appropriate to the occasion, produce beauty — this is indeed accepted by the southerners.

children.text: केचित्तु व्याचक्षते—उन्मिश्र एकैको बन्धो दाक्षिणात्यैरिष्यते । न तु मृदुः स्फुटश्च शैथिल्यकृच्छ्रोद्यत्वाभ्यां दुष्टत्वादिति । तदसत्, मृदुबन्धस्याप्यशिथिलस्य स्फुटबन्धस्यापि वा कृच्छ्रोद्यस्य रघुवंशजातकमालादौ दाक्षिणात्यमहाकविकाव्येषु दर्शनात् । तद्यथा—

children.translated_text: In the grounds of <s>Malaya</s>, where betel-vines embrace areca palms, where <s>elā</s> (cardamom) creepers embrace sandalwood trees, /
carpeted with <s>tamāla</s> leaves — does your mind [wish] to sport [there]? //
The king, his blood-red [wounds] being examined, shone with a golden body, /
embraced by clouds bowed with burdens of water, crimson with twilight, like <s>Meru</s>! //

Some, however, explain: only the mixed (<s>unmiśra</s>) type of composition is accepted by the southerners, but not the soft or the distinct, since [the latter two] are faulty due to [respectively] producing looseness and strain. That is incorrect, since even the soft composition that is not loose, and the distinct composition that involves [manageable] strain, are seen in the great poems of southern poets such as the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> and the <s>Jātakamālā</s>. For example —
<s>Daṇḍin</s> too

children.text: नाप्यत्यन्तसंराधितमिति श्रूयते । अपि च कियदिह वक्तुं शक्यते । सर्वमेव हि वैदर्भकाव्यं बन्धत्रयात्मकमुपलभ्यते । तदनेन व्याख्यानेन अवैदर्भः प्रसज्येत । नचैवम् । दृष्टविरोधात् । तदन[व]गाहितग्रन्थकाराभिप्रायस्यैतत् व्याख्या[न]मिति प्रतीमः । तस्मात्त्रयोऽपि बन्धा यथावसरमिष्यन्ते दाक्षिणात्यैः, बन्धवै[ष]म्यमेव तु तैर्बहु मन्यते ।
children.translated_text: did not fully agree with, it is said. Moreover, how much can be said here? For all <s>Vaidarbha</s> poetry is found to consist of [all] three types of composition. By that interpretation, the non-<s>Vaidarbha</s> [character] would follow [for Vaidarbha poetry itself]. But that is not so — because it contradicts observation. We understand this to be the interpretation of one who has not fathomed the author's intention. Therefore, all three compositions are accepted by the southerners as appropriate to the occasion, but unevenness of composition is not highly regarded by them.
And this
'The fault of looseness of composition has been shown [to be] entirely soft' — and so forth.
And what
'is strained' — 'with subtlety' and so forth —

children.text: तत्सुकुमारावसरे चिन्तितम् । बन्धशैथिल्यकरोऽनुप्रासः, दीप्तमिति च कृच्छ्रोद्यं गौडैर्बध्यते, न वैदर्भैरित्यन्यत्र वा तत्रार्थः । नत्वयं मृदुस्फुटबन्धनिषेधः । इति किं केन सं
children.translated_text: that was considered in the context of <s>sukumāra</s> (tenderness). The <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) that causes looseness of composition, and the 'flaming' [i.e. harsh] composition that is strained — these are employed by the <s>Gauḍas</s>, not by the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> — or the meaning lies elsewhere. But this is not a prohibition of soft or distinct composition [per se]. So what is concluded from what?

children.text: गतम् । तस्मात् त्रयोऽपि बन्धा दाक्षिणात्यैरिष्यन्ते, बन्धवैषम्यं तु नेष्टमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Therefore, all three compositions are accepted by the southerners; but unevenness of composition is not accepted [by them].
As for what is [said] —
Prescribing <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), he says —
That which is possessed of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) — in word and in substance too <s>rasa</s> abides — is sweet (<s>madhura</s>); /
by which the wise become intoxicated, like bees by honey. // 51 //

children.text: यत्काव्यं रसवत्सरसमित्यनूद्य मधुरमिति विधीयते । क्व पुनरसौ वर्त्तते येन युक्तं मधुरं स्यात् । शब्देऽर्थे च । प्रकर[ण]सम्भवादिति दर्शयन्नाह—वाचीत्यादि । [वाचि] शब्दे [वस्तुनि अ]र्थे च । रसः स्थितः तिष्ठति । उभयं रसवत् मधुरमित्यर्थः । किं तेनेति चेदाह—येनेत्यादि । येन रसेन येन रसवता काव्येन आस्वादितेन हेतुना माद्यन्ति प्रीतिविशेषं निर्विशन्ति धीमन्तः कवयो रसज्ञाः । कथमित्याह—मधुनेत्यादि । मधुना कुसुमासवेन मधुव्रता भ्रमरा इव । मधु व्रतं भोजनं येषामिति । यथा मधुनात्यन्तं प्रीयन्ते मधुलिहः तथा कवयस्तादृशेन काव्येनेत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: Restating that 'poetry which is possessed of <s>rasa</s>, i.e. is flavorful,' the rule prescribes [that it is] 'sweet.' Where then does this [rasa] reside, conjunction with which makes [poetry] sweet? In word and in meaning. Showing that [this follows] from the contextual possibility, he says 'in word' and so forth. In word (<s>vāci</s>), i.e. in sound; in substance (<s>vastuni</s>), i.e. in meaning. '<s>Rasa</s> abides' means 'rasa resides.' Both [word and meaning] being possessed of <s>rasa</s> means sweet — this is the meaning. 'What of it?' — To this he says 'by which' and so forth. By which <s>rasa</s>, i.e. by which poetry possessed of <s>rasa</s>, when savored, the wise — the poets, the connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> — become intoxicated, i.e. experience a special delight. How? — He says 'by honey' and so forth. Like bees by honey, i.e. the nectar of flowers. '<s>Madhuvrata</s>' means those whose sustenance (<s>vrata</s>) is honey (<s>madhu</s>), i.e. bees. Just as bees are exceedingly delighted by honey, so are poets by such poetry — this is the meaning.

children.text: न ज्ञायते कीदृशोऽसौ इति विशेषेण दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: It is not known what kind [of sweetness] this is — showing this specifically, he says —
That which is experienced as similar [in sound] by whatever auditory quality — /
that proximity of words having similar form, accompanied by <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), conveys <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor). // 52 //

children.text: यत् पदं समानं सदृशं पदान्तरेणानुभूयते श्रूयते । किं वर्णावृत्या नेत्याह—यया कयापि श्रुत्येति । येन केनचित् [का]रणेन पदावयवभूतेन यथाकथञ्चित् स्थानमात्रासंयोगादिकृतसाम्येन लक्षितं सत् तद्रूपस्तथाविधः सदृशपदलक्षण आदिरुत्तरोत्तरविजातीयपदापेक्षया येषां पदानां तानि तद्रूपादीनि पदानि तद्वा रूपं शब्दरूपं समानं पदमादिरादिरुत्तरोत्तरापेक्षया पूर्वं येषामिति विग्रहः । तेषामासत्तिरासन्नता यथाकथञ्चित् समानश्रुतीनां पदानामासन्नता रसमावहति श्रुतिसुभगतामातनोतीति रसावहा भवति । यथाकथञ्चित् समानश्रुतीनि पदानि
अदूरवर्त्तीनि काव्ये रसवत्तां संपादयन्ति यतो मधुरं स्यात् । अयं च समानपदासत्तिर्नाम समानश्रुतिर्नाम वा
children.translated_text: occurring in close proximity in poetry, produce the quality of being possessed of <s>rasa</s>, whereby [the poetry] becomes sweet. And this proximity of similar words (<s>samānapadāsatti</s>), also called similarity of sound (<s>samānaśruti</s>),

children.text:
शब्दरसः दाक्षिणात्यैरत्यन्तमिष्यते । अनुप्रासोऽपि शब्दरसोऽस्ति, स किं दाक्षिणात्यैर्नेष्यते । सोऽपीष्यत इत्याह-सानुप्रासेति । अनुप्रासस्य लक्षणं वक्ष्यति । सह तेन वर्त्तते सानुप्रासा, रसावहा [इत्यने]नावधार्यते । समानश्रुतेरेव रसावहेति । अनुप्रासोऽपि
च रसमावहति । ततश्च शब्दरसो द्विविधो दर्शितो भवति । समानपदासत्तिरनुप्रासश्च । अनयोश्च न सहभावनियमः । यथासम्भवं क्वचित् काव्ये समानपदासत्तिः । क्वचिदनुप्रासः । क्वचिदुभयाम् । द्वयेन तु रहितं विरसं काव्यं न स्वाद्यते क विभिरितीदृशं माधुर्यं द्विविधं प्रतिपत्तव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: [which is] the <s>rasa</s> of sound (<s>śabdarasa</s>), is greatly esteemed by the southerners. <s>Anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is also a <s>rasa</s> of sound — is it then not esteemed by the southerners? It too is esteemed — thus he says 'accompanied by <s>anuprāsa</s>.' The definition of <s>anuprāsa</s> will be stated [later]. It co-occurs with it — 'accompanied by <s>anuprāsa</s>.' 'Conveying <s>rasa</s>' — by this it is determined that only the similarity of sound conveys <s>rasa</s>. <s>Anuprāsa</s> also conveys <s>rasa</s>. Thus the <s>rasa</s> of sound is shown to be twofold: proximity of similar words and <s>anuprāsa</s>. And there is no rule that both must co-occur. As applicable, in some poetry there is proximity of similar words, in some <s>anuprāsa</s>, in some both. But poetry devoid of both is tasteless and not savored by poets — thus this <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) should be understood as twofold.

A word (<s>pada</s>) that is similar, i.e. resembling another word, is experienced, i.e. heard. Is it [only] by repetition of letters? No — he says 'by whatever auditory quality.' By whatever cause belonging to the components of the word — by however constituted similarity of place of articulation, contact, etc. — when thus marked, that which has such a form, i.e. the character of similar words, the 'initial' [words] relative to successively different types of words that follow — those words having such form are the 'words of similar form.' Or: the form, i.e. the sound-form, is the similar word, and [that which is] first relative to successively following [words] — this is the analysis. Their proximity — the nearness of words having somehow similar sound — conveys <s>rasa</s>, i.e. produces aural charm — thus it is 'conveying <s>rasa</s>.' Words having somehow similar sounds,
Illustrating the proximity of similar words, he says —

children.text: एष राजा यथा लक्ष्मीं प्राप्तवान् ब्राह्मणप्रियः ।
children.translated_text: This king, since he attained <s>Lakṣmī</s> (royal fortune), being dear to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — /
from that time onward, there has been a festival of <s>Dharma</s> in this world! // 53 //

children.text: कञ्चित् राजानमुद्दिश्योच्यते । एष राजा अयं नृपः यथा यतः प्रभृति राज्यलक्ष्मीं प्राप्तवान् नराधिपतामधिगतः, तदा प्रभृति तत आरभ्य धर्मस्य श्रुतिस्मृतिविहितस्य सनातनस्य वर्णाश्रमाचारमार्गस्य लोकयात्राया उत्सवोऽभ्युदयो निर्विशङ्का प्रवृत्तिरभवत् । लोकेऽस्मिन् अत्र वर्णाश्रमलक्षणे जगति । कुतः ब्राह्मणप्रियो यतः । ब्राह्मणाः प्रिया अस्येति । ब्राह्मणप्रियो हि तद्वचनानुवर्त्ती शास्त्रविहितं [धर्मं] प्रवर्त्तयतीत्यर्थः । क्वचिदिह दीर्घकृतं सादृश्यं क्वचित् स्थानकृतं क्वचित् संयोगकृतं क्वचित् कथाञ्चिदित्यनुव चनगम्यमेतत् । अत एवाह—

children.translated_text: 'is experienced.'
'By whatever auditory quality, that which is similar —'
Thus.

This is said with reference to some particular king. 'This king' — this monarch — 'since' (<s>yathā</s>), i.e. from the time — he attained the royal <s>Lakṣmī</s>, i.e. achieved sovereignty — 'from that time onward,' i.e. from then on — there was a festival, i.e. a flourishing, an unhindered progress, of <s>Dharma</s> — the eternal [law] prescribed by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, the path of the conduct of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> — of the conduct of the world. 'In this world' — in this universe characterized by <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>. Why? Because he is 'dear to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.' '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are dear to him' — thus [the compound]. For one dear to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, following their words, promotes the <s>Dharma</s> prescribed by the sciences — this is the meaning. Somewhere here the similarity is produced by vowel-length, somewhere by place of articulation, somewhere by conjunct consonants, somewhere in some other way — this is to be understood from the recitation. Hence he says —
Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, who has accomplished his purpose, who seeks the welfare of the world, /
