who destroys the bewilderments of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), who is hostile to the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). //
This is another illustration.

children.text: अस्य समानश्रुतिलक्षणस्य माधुर्यस्य गौडवर्त्मनि विपर्ययं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Showing the opposite of this sweetness characterized by similarity of sound in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path, he says —
Thus this [similarity of sound] is not regarded by the <s>Gauḍas</s>; but <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is dear to them; /
yet even more than <s>anuprāsa</s>, this [similarity of sound] is generally desired by the <s>Vaidarbhas</s>. // 54 //

children.text: इतीदम् एवंबिधं समानपदासत्तिलक्षणं माधुर्यं गौड़ैर्नादृतम्, न बहु मन्यते ।

तेषामिदमविदितमिति यावत् । नीरसं तर्हि तेषां काव्यमिति चेदाह—अनुप्रासस्तु तत्प्रिय इति । तेषां गौडानां प्रियो बहुमान्यः । विदितानुप्रास[स्य] तु अनुप्रास एव शब्दरसः । दाक्षिणात्यानां तु समानपदासत्तिलक्षणः शब्दरसः प्रेयानित्याह—अनुप्रासादपीत्यादि । अनुप्रासादप्यधिकमिदं समानपदासत्तिलक्षणं माधुर्यमीप्सितमिष्टं वैदर्भैर्दाक्षिणात्यैः प्रायो बाहुल्येन तत्प्रयोगात् । ततश्च अनुप्रासोऽपि तैरिष्यत इत्युक्तं भवति । न तु तथासौ प्रियस्तेषां यथा समानपदासत्तिः । तादृशं हि माधुर्यं व्यापकं सर्वत्र सम्भवात् । अनुप्रासस्तु न तथा व्यापकः क्वचिद् दर्शनात् । अत एव प्राय इदमीप्सितमित्युक्तम् । शब्दरसस्तूभयमपि । द्वयेन तु हीनं नीरसं नास्वाद्यते कविभिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: This is unknown to them — that is the purport. If then their poetry is tasteless (<s>nīrasa</s>)? He answers: "But <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is dear to them." It is dear, i.e., highly esteemed, by the <s>Gauḍas</s>. For those who understand <s>anuprāsa</s>, <s>anuprāsa</s> alone is the verbal flavour (<s>śabdarasa</s>). But for the southerners (<s>Dākṣiṇātyas</s>), the verbal flavour characterized by the proximity of similar words (<s>samānapadāsatti</s>) is more beloved — he says: "More than <s>anuprāsa</s>" and so on. This sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) characterized by the proximity of similar words is desired, i.e., preferred, by the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> (southerners), mostly because of their frequent use of it. And thereby it is implied that <s>anuprāsa</s> too is desired by them, but it is not as dear to them as the proximity of similar words. For such sweetness is pervasive, being possible everywhere, whereas <s>anuprāsa</s> is not equally pervasive, being seen only occasionally. For this very reason it is said "mostly this is desired." Verbal flavour, however, encompasses both. But [poetry] devoid of both is tasteless — it is not savoured by poets.
Thus — this kind of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) characterized by proximity of similar words is 'not regarded' by the <s>Gauḍas</s>, i.e. not highly valued [by them].

children.text: कः पुनरसावनुप्रासो यो गौडानां प्रियः? दाक्षिणात्यानां चेत्यवसरप्राप्तमनुप्रासं लक्षणतो लक्ष्यतश्च दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: What then is that <s>anuprāsa</s> which is dear to the <s>Gauḍas</s>? And to the southerners? Having arrived at the appropriate occasion, he shows <s>anuprāsa</s> both by definition and by example:
The repetition of phonemes is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), in metrical feet and in words, /
if the proximity awakens the impression of prior experience. // 55 //

children.text: वर्णस्य स्वरव्यञ्जनलक्षणस्य आवृत्तिः पुनःपुनरुच्चारणम् इत्यनूद्यानुप्रासो वेदितव्य इति विघीयते । प्रथमस्तस्य प्रथमप्रयुक्तस्याक्षरस्य
अनु पश्चादास उपक्षेपः प्रयोगः अनुप्रासः । क्वासौ सम्भवीत्याह—पादेष्वित्यादि । पादेषु पर्वापेक्षया पदेषु चेत्येतत्तु गद्यापेक्षया द्रष्टव्यम् । द्वयोरपि काव्यतयाधिकारात् । यद्वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: <s>anu</s> (after) and <s>āsa</s> (employment, application) — <s>anuprāsa</s> is the subsequent employment of [the same phoneme]. Where does it occur? He says: "in metrical feet" and so on. "In feet" should be understood in relation to verse; "and in words" should be understood in relation to prose, since both are within the domain of poetry. As he will say:
"This is the life of prose."

The repetition, i.e., the repeated pronunciation, of a phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) — characterized as vowel or consonant — is thus stated; having cited this, it is prescribed that <s>anuprāsa</s> is to be understood. "Of the first" — of the first-employed syllable,

children.text: अनुष्टुबादौ बृहति च वृत्ते गद्ये च सर्वत्र सन्निकर्षतो द्रष्टव्यः यतः प्रत्यासन्नतयाऽनुप्रासो गृह्येत । यदाह—पूर्वानुभवेत्यादि । पूर्वस्य पूर्वप्रयुक्तस्य वर्णस्य अनुभवः श्रोत्रेण ग्रहणं पूर्वो वा पूर्वप्रयुक्तवर्णविषयत्वात् तस्य सम्बन्धी तदन्वितत्त्वात् । पूर्वानुभवेनाहितः संस्कारः पूर्वानुभवसंस्कार इति वा मध्यपदलोपी समास एव । वर्णः तज्जातीय इति वा एकाकारस्मार्त्तविकल्पजननशक्तिलक्षणः । तस्य बोधनी प्रबोधिका स्वानुरूपविकल्पोत्पादनाभिमुख्यकारिणी अदूरता प्रत्यासन्नता पुनस्तद्वर्णानुभवस्वभावा यदि भवति तदा वर्णावृत्तिरनुप्रासः पादेषु पदेषु च सम्पत्स्यते । अन्यथा तथाविधानुभवसंस्कारप्रबोधाभावात्तादृशविकल्पानुदयात् अनुप्रासो न
स्यात् । तस्मात् स एवायं वर्ण आवृत्त इति यावतानुप्रासप्रतीतिः क्रमते तावदन्तरं कर्त्तव्यम् । अतिव्यवधाने त्वनुप्रासो न लभ्यते । यद्वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: obtain. Therefore, the interval should be maintained only to the extent that the perception "this is indeed the same phoneme repeated" can proceed. When the gap is too great, <s>anuprāsa</s> is not achieved. As he will say:
"Not like: <s>rāmā</s>-face-lotus..."

children.text: इत्यादि । अत्र चानुभव एव प्रमाणम्, यथोक्तं प्राक् ॥
children.translated_text: and so on. Here, experience alone is the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), as stated earlier.

In the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> and other metres, in the <s>bṛhatī</s> metre, in verse, and in prose everywhere, it should be observed from proximity — where <s>anuprāsa</s> is apprehended by closeness. As he says: "prior experience" and so on. The experience of the prior — i.e., previously employed — phoneme by the ear, or: "prior" because it pertains to the previously employed phoneme, and related to it because of being connected with it. The impression produced by prior experience is the "prior-experience-impression" — or this is an elided-middle-term compound. A phoneme of the same class — characterized as the capacity to generate a recollective cognition of a single form. Its "awakening" means making it inclined toward producing a corresponding recollective cognition; "proximity" (<s>adūratā</s>) means closeness, which itself has the nature of re-experiencing that phoneme — if this obtains, then the repetition of phonemes as <s>anuprāsa</s> in feet and words will be accomplished. Otherwise, in the absence of the awakening of such an experiential impression, since no such recollective cognition would arise, <s>anuprāsa</s> would not
Illustrating <s>anuprāsa</s> in a context of "proximity of similar words" (<s>samānapadāsatti</s>) through an example, he says:
When the moon, the crest-jewel of autumn nights, displays the semblance of a <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) cluster, /
the bee bestows a mark like an <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) upon its beauty. // 56 //

children.text: समानपदासत्तौ तु रसावहत्वं प्रसङ्गेनोक्तम् । समानपदासत्तिरपि तु लक्षण

तो लक्ष्यतश्च प्राधान्येन प्रागुक्ता । इन्द्रनीलनिभम् इन्द्रनीलमणिसदृशं नीलत्वात् । लक्ष्म चिह्नम् । अलिनो भ्रमरस्य श्रियं शोभां संदवाति बिभर्ति । कुत्र ? चन्द्रै शंशाङ्के शरदि वर्षात्यये शरदो वा निशाया रात्रेरुत्तंसे शिरश्शेखरे । उत्तंसो मूर्ध्नि शेखर इत्यभिधानात् । कथमुत्तंसश्चन्द्रो रूप्यत इत्याह—कुन्दस्तबकविभ्रमेति । कुन्दस्तबकस्यैव विभ्रमः शोभा शौक्ल्यात् । यतः कुसुमसंदोहसदृशश्चन्द्रस्ततः शरन्निशोत्तंसत्वेन रूष्यते [तदनुपाति] च लक्ष्म नीलमणिनोपनीयते । अत्र चन्द्र कुन्द इन्द्र सन्द इतिं पादेष्वनुप्रासः ॥
children.translated_text: and by example. "Like an <s>indranīla</s>" means resembling a sapphire gem, because of its blue colour. "<s>Lakṣma</s>" means a mark. Of the bee (<s>alin</s>) — it bestows, i.e., bears, the beauty (<s>śrī</s>). Where? On the moon (<s>candra</s>), i.e., the <s>śaśāṅka</s>; in autumn (<s>śarad</s>), i.e., after the rains; as the crest-ornament (<s>uttaṃsa</s>) of the night of autumn. Since the lexicon states "<s>uttaṃsa</s> is a crest-ornament on the head." How is the moon represented as a crest-ornament? He says: "with the semblance of a <s>kunda</s> cluster." The beauty of the <s>kunda</s> cluster itself, because of its whiteness. Since the moon resembles a mass of flowers, it is represented as the crest-ornament of autumn nights, and the mark is brought in comparison with a blue gem. Here, <s>candra</s>, <s>kunda</s>, <s>indra</s>, <s>sanda</s> — this is <s>anuprāsa</s> across the feet.
The flavour-bearing quality of the proximity of similar words is mentioned incidentally here. And the proximity of similar words has already been primarily stated above, both by definition
"O timid one, behold this lovely lunar disc in the sky, /
risen to make my heart, afflicted by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), pitiless!" // 57 //

children.text: मम मनश्चित्तं मन्मथक्लान्तं कामातुरं निर्दयमत्यर्थं कर्तुम् । करोतिक्रियाविशेषणं निर्दयमिति । उद्यतमुत्थितमम्बरे नभसीदमेतत् चन्द्रमस इदं चान्द्रमसम् ऐन्दवम् बिम्बं मण्डलं पश्य भीरु प्रिये । इति चन्द्रोदयोपनीतां स्वामनङ्ग[पीडां] भङ्ग्या निवेदयति कश्चित् कामी । बकारस्य मकारसहितस्य, मकारस्य नकारेण सह, मकारस्य रेफस्यान्यस्य वा यथासम्भवमावृत्तिरनुप्रासः पादेषु ।
children.translated_text: "My mind" (<s>mama manaḥ</s>) means my heart; "afflicted by <s>Manmatha</s>" means tormented by desire; "pitiless" (<s>nirdaya</s>) means exceedingly — this qualifies the action of "making." "Risen" (<s>udyata</s>) means appeared; "in the sky" (<s>ambare</s>), i.e., in the heavens; "this" — this "lunar" (<s>cāndramasa</s>), i.e., belonging to the moon, "disc" (<s>bimba</s>) means orb; "behold" — O timid one (<s>bhīru</s>), O beloved! Thus some lover obliquely communicates the torment of love (<s>anaṅga</s>-pain) occasioned by the moonrise. The repetition of the letter <s>ba</s> together with <s>ma</s>, of <s>ma</s> together with <s>na</s>, of <s>ma</s> with <s>ra</s> or another [consonant] as appropriate — this is <s>anuprāsa</s> in the feet.
"The face of the beloved, gentle with playful smiles and measured speech, /
with hand raised, with eyes impassioned, delighting the world" //
This is another example.
Illustrating the desirable type of <s>anuprāsa</s>, he says:
"They desire <s>anuprāsa</s> to be heard at not-too-distant intervals; /
not like: 'the moon is similar to the lotus-face of the beautiful woman.'" // 58 //

children.text: इत्येवंरूपमनन्तरोक्तप्रकारं नातिदूरान्तरश्रुतिमनतिविप्रकृष्टव्यवधानश्रवणम् । यावता पूर्वानुभवसंस्कारप्रबोधः प्रभवति तावदन्तरश्रुतिमनुप्रासमिच्छन्ति । सामान्यवचनादुभयेऽपि ।

नातिदूरमन्तरं यस्याः सा श्रुतिर्यस्येति ह्यन्यपदार्थः । कीदृशः पुनर्दूरान्तरश्रुतिर्नेष्यत इति तमपि हेयत्वेनोदाहरति—नात्वित्यादि । रामाणां स्त्रीणां मुखं वदनमेवाम्भोजं पद्मं तेन सदृशः समानश्चन्द्रमाः शशाङ्क इति योज्यम् । अत्र रामा इत्ययं मकारः मुखाम्भोजसदृशश्चन्द्रमा इति दूरमागम्यावृत्तः । ततोऽयं दूरान्तरश्रुतिरनुप्रासो व्यपदेशमात्रेण न तु ग्रहणतः । तमीदृशं नेच्छन्त्युभयेऽपि । वैदर्भा एकान्तेन नेच्छन्ति । गौड़ैस्तु तादृशोऽपीष्यत इति वा द्रष्टव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: "Not too distant" — the hearing (<s>śruti</s>) whose interval is not too far, of which [the <s>anuprāsa</s> partakes] — such is the alternative word-meaning. What kind of far-interval hearing is not desired? He illustrates that as something to be avoided: "Not like" and so on. The face of <s>rāmā</s> (beautiful woman), i.e., the face of a woman, which is itself a lotus (<s>ambhoja</s>) — similar to that is the moon (<s>candramā</s>) — this should be construed. Here, the <s>ma</s> in "<s>rāmā</s>" is repeated only at a great distance in "<s>mukhāmbhojasadṛśaścandramā</s>." Therefore this <s>anuprāsa</s> with far-interval hearing is such only in name, not in actual perception. Both [schools] do not desire such a type. The <s>Vaidarbhas</s> absolutely do not desire it. But it may be observed that even such a type is desired by the <s>Gauḍas</s>.

Of such a form as just described — "heard at not-too-distant intervals" means heard with a not-overly-separated gap. They desire <s>anuprāsa</s> to the extent that the awakening of the impression from prior experience can prevail — that much of an interval in hearing. Since the statement is general, both [schools approve of this].

children.text: अपरोऽप्यनुप्रासप्रकारोऽस्ति यः श्लेषसौकुमार्यादिशब्दालङ्कारविरोधी । तं गौड़ाः प्रयुञ्जते न वैदर्भा इति दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: There is yet another type of <s>anuprāsa</s> which is contrary to <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy), and other sound-figures. The <s>Gauḍas</s> employ it, not the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> — showing this, he says:

children.text: स्मरः खरः खलः कान्तः कायः कोपश्च नः कृशः ।
children.translated_text: "<s>Smara</s> (Love) is cruel, the rogue is harsh, the beloved one's body and anger — both are emaciated; /

children.text: च्युतो मानोऽधिको रागो मोहो जातोऽसवो गताः ॥ ५९ ॥
children.translated_text: pride has fallen away, passion has increased, delusion has arisen, and life-breaths have departed!" // 59 //

children.text: स्मरः कामः खरो नृशंसः प्रमादित्वात् । कान्तः पतिश्च खलः प्रतिकूलवर्त्ती व्यलीकशीलत्वात् । कायः शरीरम् कृशः क्षीणः विरहदौर्बल्यात् । कोपश्च कान्तविषयः कृशो निवृत्तः । मानश्च तद्विषयः किं तेनेति चेतोवष्टम्भलक्षणश्च्यतो गलितः रागाद्यभिभूतत्वात् । यदाह रागोऽधिक इति । रागोऽभिषङ्गः पतिविषयः अधिकः प्रबलो वर्त्तते । ततश्च मोहो मूर्च्छा जातः प्रवृत्तः रागपक्षत्वात् । तदुक्तम्—

children.translated_text: "By the delusion born of intense passion, which arrests the functioning of the senses, /
<s>Rati</s> (Love's consort), unaware of her husband's calamity, became for a moment as one who has rendered a service." Thus.

<s>Smara</s> (Love) means <s>Kāma</s>; "cruel" (<s>khara</s>) means merciless, because of being heedless. The beloved (<s>kānta</s>), i.e., the husband, is also a "rogue" (<s>khala</s>), i.e., one who acts contrary, because of his deceptive nature. The body (<s>kāya</s>) is emaciated (<s>kṛśa</s>), i.e., wasted, due to the weakness of separation. Anger (<s>kopa</s>) too, directed toward the beloved, is "emaciated," i.e., subsided. Pride (<s>māna</s>) too, directed toward him — "what is the use of it?" — characterized by mental resistance, has "fallen away" (<s>cyuta</s>), i.e., dissipated, because of being overcome by passion and the rest. As he says: "passion has increased" — passion (<s>rāga</s>), i.e., attachment directed toward the husband, is "excessive" (<s>adhika</s>), i.e., powerful. And therefore delusion (<s>moha</s>), i.e., swooning, has "arisen" (<s>jāta</s>), i.e., commenced, because it belongs to the side of passion. As stated:

children.text: असवः प्राणा गता दशमी दशा जातास्माकमिति काचित् विरहिणी विरौतीत्यर्थो योजनीयः ॥
children.translated_text: "Life-breaths" (<s>asavaḥ</s>) means <s>prāṇas</s>; "departed" (<s>gatāḥ</s>) means the tenth state has arrived — thus some woman in separation laments: such is the meaning to be construed.
"Such and similar [verse] involves harshness and looseness of composition; /
therefore the southerners (<s>Dākṣiṇātyas</s>) do not employ such <s>anuprāsa</s>." // 60 //

children.text: इत्यादि काव्यम् एवंविधोऽनुप्रासो बन्धस्य रचनायाः पारुष्यं यत्र सौकुमार्यविपर्ययः शैथिल्यं च श्लेषविपक्षं चकाराद्वैषम्यं च नियच्छति स्वीकरोति यतः, अतः कारणात्, एवमीदृशमनुप्राशं न प्रयुञ्जते दाक्षिणात्या वैदर्भाः । गौडास्तु प्र
युञ्जत इत्यर्थादुक्तं भवति । ततश्चानुप्रासेऽपि वैदर्भगौडीययोरस्ति कथञ्चिद्विशेष इति ॥
children.translated_text: do employ it — this is implicitly stated. Therefore, even in <s>anuprāsa</s>, there is some distinction between the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> [styles].

"Such and similar poetry" — such a type of <s>anuprāsa</s> "involves" (<s>niyacchati</s>), i.e., takes on, the "harshness" (<s>pāruṣya</s>) of composition (<s>bandha</s>), which is the opposite of delicacy (<s>saukumārya</s>), and also "looseness" (<s>śaithilya</s>), which is the opposite of <s>śleṣa</s> (close-joining), and by the word "and" (<s>ca</s>), also unevenness; since [it does so], for that reason, the southerners, i.e., the <s>Vaidarbhas</s>, do not employ such <s>anuprāsa</s>. But the <s>Gauḍas</s>
Since <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming figure) is a special type of <s>anuprāsa</s>, in that connection he explains <s>yamaka</s>:
"They know <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming figure) as the repetition [of phonemes] occurring in a cluster (<s>saṃghāta</s>); /
but that is not uniformly sweet; therefore it will be treated later." // 61 //

children.text: वर्णावृत्तिमेव नान्यत् यमकं विदुः विदन्ति कथयन्ति तज्ज्ञाः इति परमुखेन । तद्विदग्धोचितेयं वाचोयुक्तिरिति सर्वत्रानुसरत्वेनाम् । कोऽनयोर्भेद इत्याह—संघातगोचरामिति । अयमनयोर्भेदः । एकवर्णविषयावृत्तिरनुप्रासः । अनेकवर्णविषया तु यमकमिति । संघातः वर्णसमुदायो गोचरो विषयो यस्या इति विग्रह[ः/?/] । तत् किं नोच्यते इत्याह—तत्त्वित्यादि । तत्तु यमकम् । तुशब्दोऽर्थान्तरविवक्षायाम् । एकान्तेन साकल्येन सर्वेण, मधुरं च सर्वं न भवति, प्रायो गूढ़ार्थत्वेन अप्रसन्नत्वात् । तत्तु मधुरमेव यत्प्रसन्नम् । समानश्रुत्यनुप्रासयोस्त्वेकान्तमधुरता सर्वथा प्रसन्नत्वात् । एकान्तमधुरं चात्र प्रस्तुतम् । अतः नैकान्तमधुरत्त्वात् पश्चाद् दुष्करे विधास्यते प्रतिपादयिष्यते । प्रभेदतो लक्षणतस्तूक्तमेवेति ॥
children.translated_text: "They know" — the experts declare, putting it in another's voice — that <s>yamaka</s> is nothing but the repetition of phonemes. This is the mode of discourse appropriate to the learned — let it apply everywhere. What is the difference between the two? He says: "occurring in a cluster." This is the difference: repetition involving a single phoneme is <s>anuprāsa</s>; that involving multiple phonemes is <s>yamaka</s>. A cluster (<s>saṃghāta</s>) is a group of phonemes — the domain or subject of which — thus the analysis. Why is it not discussed [here]? He says: "But that" and so on. <s>Yamaka</s>, however — the word "but" (<s>tu</s>) indicates a shift of topic — is not uniformly, i.e., completely, sweet, because it is mostly obscure in meaning and hence not perspicuous. That <s>yamaka</s> alone is sweet which is perspicuous. But in the case of <s>samānaśruti</s> (assonance) and <s>anuprāsa</s>, there is uniform sweetness, because of their complete perspicuity. And what is uniformly sweet is the present topic. Therefore, because it is not uniformly sweet, it will be treated "later" (<s>paścāt</s>), in the section on difficult [compositions]. Its varieties and definition have already been stated.
"Flavour resides in speech and in content" —

children.text: इति तत्रेयता वाचि रसो दर्शितः । सम्प्रति वस्तुनि रसं विवरीतुमुपक्रमते—
children.translated_text: In that context, the flavour in speech has thus far been shown. Now he undertakes to explain the flavour in content:
What was said —
"Granted, every ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) pours flavour (<s>rasa</s>) into the content; /
nevertheless, it is refinement (<s>agrāmyatā</s>) alone that bears the greater burden." // 62 //

children.text: काममित्यभ्युपगमे यदि नामेत्यर्थः । अलङ्कारोऽर्थालङ्कारः जात्यादिप्रभेदः सर्वोऽपि नैक एव कश्चित् अर्थे वस्तुनि रसं माधुर्यं निषिञ्चति आवहति । तथापि एवमपि इति विशेषविवक्षायां तां दर्शयति--अग्राम्यतेत्यादि । अग्राम्यतै

children.translated_text: i.e., urbanity (<s>asābhyatā</s>) alone

children.text: अर्थस्य भूयसात्यर्थं व्यापकत्वात् एनं रसनिषेकलक्षणं भारं धुरं वहति धत्ते नान्यत् ।
children.translated_text: of the content, "to the greater extent" (<s>bhūyasā</s>), i.e., exceedingly, because of being pervasive, bears this burden (<s>bhāra</s>), i.e., this load characterized by the pouring of flavour — nothing else [does so].

children.text: यद्यग्राम्यतैव रसस्तत् किं भेदो नोच्यते, सामान्यविशेषभावेन भेदसम्भवात् । रसो हि माधुर्यसामान्यम्, समानश्रुत्यनुप्रासाग्राम्यतादिसाधारणत्वेन [तस्य] प्रतीतेः । समानश्रुत्यादेस्तु विशेषाव्यावृत्तितयावगमात् । अन्यदप्येवंजातीयकमुन्नेयम् । जात्याद्यर्थालङ्कारमुक्तमपि काव्यमग्राम्यार्थमेकान्तमधुरमित्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: If refinement itself is the flavour, then why is the distinction not stated, since a distinction is possible in terms of the general-particular relationship? For flavour is the general concept of sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), since it is perceived as common to assonance, <s>anuprāsa</s>, refinement, and the like. But assonance and the rest are understood as particular, through differentiation. Other things of the same kind should also be inferred. Poetry endowed with content-figures like <s>jāti</s> and the rest, if possessing refined content, is uniformly sweet — that is the meaning.

"Granted" (<s>kāmam</s>) — in the sense of concession, meaning "even if." An ornament, i.e., a content-ornament (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>), of various types such as <s>jāti</s> (species) and the rest, every one, not just some particular one, "pours" (<s>niṣiñcati</s>), i.e., brings, flavour, i.e., sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), into the content. "Nevertheless" (<s>tathāpi</s>) — "even so" — wishing to indicate a distinction, he shows it: "refinement" and so on. Refinement (<s>agrāmyatā</s>),

children.text: कीदृशी तावद् ग्राम्यता यद्विपर्ययोऽग्राम्यता वस्तुरसः स्यादिति ग्राम्यताप्रतिपक्षेण अग्राम्यतां दर्शयितुकामः ग्राम्यतां तावदुदाहरति—
children.translated_text: What, then, is that vulgarity (<s>grāmyatā</s>) whose opposite — refinement (<s>agrāmyatā</s>) — would be the flavour of content? Wishing to show refinement by way of its opposite, he first illustrates vulgarity:

children.text: कन्ये कामयमानं मां न त्वं कामयसे कथम् ।
children.translated_text: "O maiden, how is it that you do not desire me, who desire you? /
This content-form is vulgar — it serves only to produce distaste." // 63 //

children.text: कन्ये बाले त्वं कामयमानं सन्तं मां कथं किं न कामयसे नाभिलषसि । एवं नाम त्वं निष्ठुरेति । अयमेवंविधोऽर्थात्मा वस्तुरूपं ग्राम्यः अविदग्धोचितः । ततश्च वैरस्यायैव अमाधुर्यार्थमेव कल्पते सम्पद्यते न कथमपि रसवत्तायै । विरस एव तादृशोऽर्थ इति यावत् । वैरस्यं च न काव्योचितमिति नेदृशं कवयः स्पृ[श]न्तीत्याकूतम् ॥
children.translated_text: "O maiden" — O young woman! "You" — "me who desire [you]" — being such — "how" — why — "do you not desire," i.e., do you not long for [me]? "Are you truly so heartless?" — such is the sense. Such a content-form (<s>arthātman</s>) is vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>), i.e., befitting the uncultured. And therefore it "serves only to produce distaste" (<s>vairasyāya</s>), i.e., it results in the absence of sweetness, not in any way in the possession of flavour. Such content is simply tasteless — that is the purport. And since distaste is not befitting poetry, poets do not touch such [content] — this is the intent.
What, then, is that refined content-form which conveys flavour? He says:
"Granted, the outcaste that is <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love) is cruel to me, O lovely-eyed one; /
but toward you he is free from malice — by good fortune!" — this refined content conveys flavour. // 64 //

children.text: वामाक्षि मञ्जुलोचने इति प्रियामन्त्रणम् । कन्दर्पः काम एव चण्डालः अकाण्डप्रहारित्वात् । मयि मद्विषये निष्ठुरः क्रूरं प्रहरतीत्यर्थः । कामं यदि नाम तथापि सानुग्रह एवास्माकं यत्त्वयि निर्मत्सरः निर्वैरः सानुक्रोशस्त्वां न बाधते । अत एवाहदिष्ट्येति आनन्दनिवेदनम् । अयमस्माकमानन्दो महान् यत्त्वयि न

प्रहरति । त्वत्सुखेनैव सुखिता वयम् । किं कन्दर्पचण्डालेन निष्ठुरेणापि कृतमिति वक्रोक्त्या आत्मनस्तद्विषयमनुगत[त्वं] तस्याश्च वैमुख्यमात्मनि दर्शयतीति अयमीदृशोऽर्थः अग्राम्यः सभ्यः काव्योचितः ततश्च रसावहः एकान्तमघुरः । एवंविधो वस्तुन्यग्राम्यतारसः प्रतिपत्तव्यः । अपरमत्रोदाह्रियते—
children.translated_text: strikes. 'We are happy by your happiness alone. What has that cruel wretch, the outcaste <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), done?' — thus, through <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique speech), she reveals her own devotion to that subject and his aversion toward herself. Such a meaning is non-vulgar (<s>agrāmya</s>), refined (<s>sabhya</s>), suitable for poetry, and therefore productive of <s>rasa</s>, and absolutely sweet. Such is the non-vulgarity of subject-matter (<s>vastuny agrāmyatā-rasa</s>) to be understood. Another example is cited here —

"O lovely-eyed one" (<s>vāmākṣi</s>), i.e., "O one with beautiful eyes" — this is an address to the beloved. <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), who is himself "an outcaste" (<s>caṇḍāla</s>), because of striking without cause. "Toward me" — "is cruel" (<s>niṣṭhura</s>), i.e., strikes cruelly — that is the meaning. "Granted" (<s>kāmam</s>) — even if so, nevertheless he is gracious toward us, in that "toward you he is free from malice" (<s>nirmatsara</s>), i.e., without enmity, compassionate — he does not afflict you. Therefore he says "by good fortune" (<s>diṣṭyā</s>) — this is an expression of joy. This is our great joy — that toward you he does not

children.text: नन्वहं प्रणत एव, मानिनी सा भवन्तमवधीर्य वर्तते ।
children.translated_text: Indeed, I am bowing before [you], yet that proud woman disregards you and persists.

children.text: मन्मथस्त्वमसि किं न तन्मथः कुत्र वा न तव काम ! वामता ॥ इति ॥
children.translated_text: You are <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) — why then not '<s>Tanmatha</s>' (one who churns her)? Or where, O <s>Kāma</s>, is your perversity not [present]? //

children.text: यथार्थो ग्राम्यस्तथा शब्दोऽपि ग्राम्योऽस्ति, सोऽपि वर्जनीय इति दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Just as meaning can be vulgar, so too can the word (<s>śabda</s>) be vulgar; that too is to be avoided — showing this, [the author] says:
In words too there is indeed vulgarity; that is the utterance of what is unrefined.
For example, a word beginning with 'ya' in the depiction of amorous sport. // 65 //

children.text: न केवलमर्थे शब्दे वाचकेऽपि ग्राम्यतास्त्वेव न नास्ति । कीदृशीत्याह—सेत्यादि । सा ग्राम्यता सभ्येतरे असभ्या रथ्यापुरुषास्तेषां कीर्तनं यत् कियदसभ्यसमुदाहृतं वचनं ग्राम्यता । पदगतग्राम्यतेत्युक्तम् । यथेति निदर्शनेन व्यनक्ति—रत्युत्सवस्य निधुवनानन्दस्य निरूपणे प्रकाशने कर्त्तव्ये यकारादिपदं यकारमादिर्यस्य तच्च तत् पदं चेति विग्रहः । सुसिद्धं खल्वेतदशिष्टवचनम् ।तथाविधं सर्वं ग्राम्यं द्रष्टव्यम् । नेदमेवेति यथाशब्दस्यार्थः ॥
children.translated_text: Not only in meaning — in the word, the signifier, too there is vulgarity; it is not that there is none. What is it like? — he says with 'that' etc. That vulgarity consists in the utterance of what is 'other than refined' (<s>sabhyetara</s>) — i.e., the unrefined, street-persons; their utterance, which is a statement cited by the vulgar, is vulgarity. Thus word-level vulgarity has been stated. He clarifies with an example using 'for instance': in the depiction — i.e., the portrayal — of amorous sport (<s>ratyutsava</s>), i.e., the joy of union, a word beginning with 'ya' — the compound is: that whose initial [letter] is 'ya,' and which is a word. This is well-known as an unrefined expression. All such [expressions] should be regarded as vulgar. 'For instance' (<s>yathā</s>) means [the example given] is not the only one.

children.text: अन्यः शब्दे ग्राम्यताप्रकारोऽस्ति, सोऽपि वर्जनीय इति व्युत्पादयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: There is another type of vulgarity in words, which too is to be avoided — teaching this, [the author] says:
Through the juxtaposition of words, or by way of sentence-meaning,

children.text: दुष्प्रतीतिकरं ग्राम्यं यथा या भवतः प्रिया ॥ ६६ ॥
children.translated_text: that which produces a bad impression is vulgar — for example, '<s>yā bhavataḥ priyā</s>' (she who is your beloved). // 66 //

children.text: पदयोः सन्धानं सङ्गतिरानन्तर्यं तस्य वृत्त्या स्थित्या । वेति समुच्चये । वाक्यस्य पदसमुदायस्यास[त्त्यादियुक्त]

स्यार्थः क्रियाकारकविशेषलक्षणममिधेयं तद्भावः । स एव वाक्यार्थत्वं तेन वा तेन च हेतुना पुनरपरमेतत् । न केवलं पूर्वकं नैकैकपदार्थनिरूपणेन किं तु वाक्यार्थस्य विभावनेनेत्यर्थः । दुष्टामसभ्यां शब्दतः न तु वस्तुतः, तस्यैव वस्तुनः शब्दान्तरेणादुष्टत्वात् प्रतीतिमवगमं करोतीति दुष्प्रतीतिकरं वाक्यं ततश्च ग्राम्यमसभ्यं विद्यते । यथेत्युदाहरणेन स्पष्ट्यति । या इत्यस्य पदस्य भवत इत्यनेन पदेन सन्धाने सति ग्राम्यं प्रतीयते । या तव प्रियेति पदान्तरसन्धाने निवर्तते । तदीदृशं पदसन्धानं ग्राम्यं बुद्ध्या परिहरणीयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: the meaning is the signified, characterized by the specific relation of action and case-relations; its nature is that [sentence-meaning]. By that or by that cause, furthermore — this is yet another [type]. Not only the previous one, based on the examination of individual word-meanings, but also through the consideration of sentence-meaning — that is the sense. [That which] produces a bad — i.e., unrefined, in terms of words, not in terms of the thing itself, since that very thing is not bad when expressed by another word — impression, i.e., understanding, is 'producing a bad impression' (<s>duṣpratītikara</s>); such a sentence is vulgar, unrefined. He clarifies with an example: when the word '<s>yā</s>' is juxtaposed with the word '<s>bhavataḥ</s>,' a vulgar [meaning] is perceived. When juxtaposed with another word — '<s>yā tava priyā</s>' — [the vulgarity] is removed. Such juxtaposition of words that is vulgar should be carefully avoided.

The 'juxtaposition' (<s>sandhāna</s>) of words is their conjunction, their contiguity; 'by its occurrence' means by its presence. 'Or' is in the sense of aggregation. Of the sentence — i.e., the collection of words —
He gives an example of sentence-meaning vulgarity:
'Having struck the enemy, the man of valor has rested' —
such [expressions] are not approved in either of the two paths. // 67 //

children.text: परं शत्रुं प्रहृत्य हत्वा वीर्यवान् शूरः पुरुषो विश्रान्तो व्यवस्थित इत्येकोऽर्थस्तावदग्राम्यः । परम् अत्यर्थं प्रहृत्याभिहत्य वीर्यवानुपचितप्रधानधातुः पुरुषः विश्रान्तो विरतः पतित इत्यपरो ग्राम्यो वाक्यार्थः प्रतीयत इति वाक्यार्थग्राम्यमेतत् । एवमादीदृशमर्थग्राम्यं शब्दग्राम्यं चोभयोरपि वैदर्भगौडीययोर्मार्गयोरेकस्मिन्नपि न शंसन्ति नाद्रियन्ते तद्विद एव । तच्च प्रायोग्रहणसंगृहीतम् ।
children.translated_text: 'Having struck' (<s>prahṛtya</s>) the enemy, having killed [him], the man of valor (<s>vīryavān</s>), the brave one, has 'rested' (<s>viśrānta</s>), i.e., has settled — one meaning is thus non-vulgar. [But:] 'exceedingly' (<s>param</s>), having struck hard (<s>abhihṛtya</s>), the man of valor — one of augmented vital essence (<s>upacitapradhānadhātu</s>) — has 'rested,' i.e., ceased, fallen — this other vulgar sentence-meaning is perceived; thus this is sentence-meaning vulgarity. 'Such and similar' (<s>evamādi</s>) — such vulgarity of meaning and vulgarity of words, in both paths — the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> — even in one of them, 'are not approved' (<s>na śaṃsanti</s>), i.e., are not valued by the experts themselves. And this is included under the word 'mostly' (<s>prāya</s>).
When someone, out of pride, rises suddenly to the fore
and engages in striking the enemy, [it results] only in a fall.
This is another example of sentence-meaning vulgarity. //
What about [words like] '<s>bhaginī</s>' (sister) and the like? — he says:
'-<s>gavatī</s>' (blessed one), and the like are approved everywhere.
'<s>Bhaginī</s>' (sister), '<s>Bha-</s>'
Thus delicacy (<s>mādhurya</s>) is described; [now] tenderness (<s>sukumāratā</s>) is stated. // 68 //

children.text: भगिनी भगवती सुभगा दुर्भगेत्यादि सर्वत्रैव शास्त्रे काव्ये लोके चानुमन्यते आद्रियते । ततस्तादृशमग्राम्यं सभ्यमेव । ततश्च प्रयुज्यते एव कविभिः ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhaginī</s>' (sister), '<s>Bhagavatī</s>' (blessed one), '<s>Subhagā</s>' (fortunate), '<s>Durbhagā</s>' (unfortunate), and the like are 'approved everywhere' — in <s>śāstra</s>, in poetry, and in common usage — i.e., they are valued. Therefore, such [expressions] are non-vulgar, refined indeed. Hence they are used by poets.

children.text: माधुर्यं निगमयन्नाह—विभक्तमित्यादि । इत्यनेन प्रकारेण माधुर्यं विभक्तं निर्दिष्टम् । सुकुमारतेदानीमुच्यते निर्दिश्यते तदनन्तरमुपदिष्टत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Concluding [the discussion of] delicacy, [the author] says: 'Thus described' and so forth. By this method, delicacy (<s>mādhurya</s>) has been 'described' (<s>vibhakta</s>), i.e., specified. Tenderness (<s>sukumāratā</s>) is now 'stated,' i.e., specified, because it is taught immediately after.
'That which mostly consists of non-harsh syllables is considered tender here.
For the fault of looseness of composition has been demonstrated in [verse] that is entirely soft.' // 69 //

children.text: अनिष्ठुराणि अपरुषाणि अक्षराणि वर्णाः प्रायाणि भूयांसि यस्मिंस्तथा अनिष्ठुरैर्वाक्षरैः प्रायं समधिकं काव्यमित्यनूद्य सुकुमारमपरुषमिष्यत इति विधिः । निष्ठुराणि तु स्वल्पानीति प्रायग्रहणेन सूचितम । इहेति वैदर्भमार्गे सर्वानिष्ठुराक्षरं किं न सुकुमारमिंष्यत इति चेदाह—बन्धेत्यादिं । हिर्यस्मात्सर्वाणिं अक्षराणि कोमलानिं सुकुमाराणि यस्मिंस्तत्तथा । सर्वैरेवाक्षरैः कोमलं तस्मिन् काव्ये बन्धस्य निवेशनस्य शैथिल्यं लाघवं तदेव दोषो वैकृतं दर्शित उदाहृतः पूर्वम् ।

children.translated_text: '<s>Mālatīmālā lolāliṅkalita</s>' (a garland of jasmine entwined by swaying bees) —
thus. Therefore 'that which mostly consists of non-harsh syllables is considered tender here, not that which consists entirely of non-harsh syllables' — this is to be understood.

'Non-harsh' (<s>aniṣṭhura</s>) means not rough; 'syllables' (<s>akṣara</s>) means phonemes; 'mostly' (<s>prāya</s>) [means] the majority [consist] of those — i.e., poetry in which non-harsh syllables predominate. Having restated [this], the rule is: it 'is considered' (<s>iṣyate</s>) tender, i.e., non-rough. But a few harsh [syllables are present] — this is indicated by the word 'mostly.' 'Here' means in the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path. If [one asks:] why not [verse] with all non-harsh syllables considered tender? — he says with 'composition' etc. '<s>Hi</s>' means 'because': when all the syllables are soft, i.e., tender — in such [poetry], the 'looseness' (<s>śaithilya</s>), i.e., lightness, of 'composition' (<s>bandha</s>), i.e., arrangement — that itself being a 'fault' (<s>doṣa</s>), a deficiency — has been 'demonstrated,' i.e., illustrated earlier.
Illustrating tenderness, [the author] says:
Having fanned out their tail-feathers in a circle, with throats [producing] sweet songs,
the peacocks dance exuberantly in the season adorned with clouds. // 70 //

children.text: वर्हाण्यङ्गरुहाणिं मण्डलीकृत्य छत्राकारेण विंतत्य मधुरा मनोहरा गीतिःकेकालक्षणं गानं येषां तैः कण्ठैर्लक्षिता मधुरं गायन्त इत्यर्थः । कला
पिनो मयूराः प्रनृत्यन्ति जीमूतमालिनि मेघधारिणि । मलमल्लधारणे । काले समये प्रावृषीति यावत् ॥
children.translated_text: cocks dance exuberantly in the season 'adorned with clouds' (<s>jīmūtamālin</s>), i.e., bearing rain-clouds. '<s>Malamalla</s>' [means] bearing, wearing. In [that] season, i.e., the rainy period — that is the meaning.

Having fanned out — i.e., having spread in the form of an umbrella — their tail-feathers (<s>barhāṇi</s>), their plumage; 'sweet' means charming; the 'song' (<s>gīti</s>), characterized as the <s>kekā</s> cry, is their singing — those who have that [quality] in their 'throats' — i.e., they are described as singing sweetly — that is the meaning. The pea-

children.text: प्रतिविशिष्टस्यानेकस्य काव्यधर्मस्याभावेऽपि सौकुमार्यगुणादीदृशं काव्यमुपादेयमिति सौकुमार्यं वर्णयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Explaining that even in the absence of many particular poetic virtues, such poetry is worthy of adoption by virtue of the quality of tenderness, [the author] says:
'Thus the meaning is indeed not forceful, nor is the ornament such;
by tenderness alone, this ascends to the delight of the good.' // 71 //

children.text: इत्ययमेवंविधोऽर्थः अभिधेयशरीरम् । ऊर्जितो दीप्तः प्रतिविशिष्टः । न तथाऽनूर्जित एव नोर्जितोऽपि । अलंकारस्तर्हि प्रतिविशिष्टस्तेनेदमादेयं काव्यं न सौकुमार्यगुणादिति चेदाह—नालंकारोऽपि तादृश इति । अलंकारोऽप्यत्र स्वभावोक्तिलक्षणः तादृशस्तथाभूतः प्रतिविशिष्टो न भवति यादृशोऽ[न्य]त्र । स च विभावनादिः । न केवलमर्थ इत्यपिशब्दार्थः । कोऽत्रार्थस्यालङ्कारस्य च भेदः येनोच्यतेऽलंकारोऽर्थश्चानूर्जित इति । य एवार्थः स एवालंकाराऽस्मिन् गम्यते । नैतदेवम् । अर्थो हि धर्मी, स्वभावोक्तिश्चालंकारो धर्मः प्रतीयत इति महान् भेदः, धर्मधर्मिभेदस्य सुप्रसिद्धत्वात् । अन्यत्राप्येवंविधोऽत्र भेदः । तथापि एतदिदमीदृशं काव्यं सुकुमारतयैव सौकुमार्येण केवलेन शब्दालंकारेण पुरस्कृतं सतां विदग्धानां मुखम् आननम् आरोहति गोचरीकरोति सुकुमारमित्येवेदृशं कविभिरुपादीयत इति यावत् । यदि पुनरर्थ ऊजिताऽलंकारश्च, सुतरां सुकुमारं काव्यं रमणीयमित्याकूतम् ॥
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — the meaning of this kind, the body of the subject matter — 'forceful' (<s>ūrjita</s>) means brilliant, special. 'Not forceful indeed' — not forceful at all. [If one says:] 'Then the ornament is special, and by that this poetry is worthy of adoption, not by the quality of tenderness' — he replies: 'nor is the ornament such.' The ornament here, characterized as <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), is not 'such,' i.e., not so distinguished as [it is] elsewhere. And that [elsewhere] is <s>vibhāvanā</s> etc. 'Not only the meaning' — such is the force of the word 'also' (<s>api</s>). [One asks:] What is the difference here between meaning and ornament, such that one says both the ornament and the meaning are not forceful? The very meaning is the ornament perceived here. This is not so. For the meaning is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), and <s>svabhāvokti</s>, which is the ornament, is the property (<s>dharma</s>) perceived — thus there is a great difference, since the distinction between property and property-bearer is well established. Elsewhere too such a distinction [applies] here. Nevertheless, 'this' — such poetry — 'by tenderness alone' (<s>sukumāratayaiva</s>), by delicacy alone, by verbal ornament alone as the leading [quality], 'ascends' (<s>ārohati</s>) the 'mouth' (<s>mukha</s>), i.e., the face, of 'the good' (<s>satām</s>), i.e., the discerning — i.e., comes within their range. It means: such [poetry] is adopted by poets precisely as tender. If, moreover, the meaning were forceful and the ornament [also forceful], then all the more would tender poetry be delightful — such is the implication.
slowly,
Swans wander in the garden of lotuses, intoxicated,
with charming sounds, [perceived] by the ears, with their feet, with the play of colors. //
This is another example. //
Showing the opposite of tenderness in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path, [the author] says:
'Forceful' — by others, [verse] that is mostly difficult to utter is also composed.
'The faction of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> was annihilated completely in an instant' — thus. // 72 //

children.text: दीप्तमूर्जितं साटोपमेतदिति मन्यमानैरपरैः पौरस्त्यैः कृच्छ्रोद्यं दुर्वचं कष्टोच्चारणमसुकुमारतरमपि काव्यं बध्यते प्रयुज्यते न केवलसुकुमारमात्रमित्यपिंशब्दः । भूम्ना प्रायः । ततश्च सुकुमारमपि किंचिदुष्णमधुन्यायेन येनोपयुज्यत इति सूचयति तदुदाहरति ।
न्यक्षं कात्स्नै निकृष्ठे च इति वैजयन्ती ।

न्यक्षेण निःशेषेण क्षपितः निहतः क्षणात् सपदि स्तोकेन कालेनेत्यर्थः । क्षत्रियाणां राज्ञां पक्षो वर्गः परशुरामेणान्येन वा केनचिदिति गम्यते । नन्वेतद्विवक्षितं कृच्छ्रोद्यमात्रं तूदाहृतमिति यथा तादृशमित्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: 'Completely' (<s>nyakṣeṇa</s>), i.e., without remainder, 'annihilated' (<s>kṣapita</s>), i.e., destroyed, 'in an instant' (<s>kṣaṇāt</s>), i.e., immediately, in a short time — that is the meaning. 'The faction' (<s>pakṣa</s>), i.e., the party, 'of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,' i.e., of the kings — by <s>Paraśurāma</s> or some other [warrior], as is understood. Now, the intended meaning is not in itself difficult to utter, but what is illustrated is merely of that [harsh-sounding] kind — 'such as that' is the meaning of '<s>yathā</s>.'

'Forceful' (<s>dīpta</s>), i.e., vigorous, pompous — considering it thus, 'by others,' the Easterners, even [poetry that is] 'difficult to utter' (<s>kṛcchrodya</s>), hard to pronounce, of harsh articulation, not at all tender, 'is also composed,' i.e., employed — not merely tender [poetry] alone; such is the force of the word 'also.' 'Mostly' (<s>bhūmnā</s>). And thus he suggests that some tender [verse] too is employed, by the analogy of hot-and-honey, and he illustrates that.
In order to explain clarity of meaning (<s>arthavyakti</s>), [the author] says:
Clarity of meaning (<s>arthavyakti</s>) is the non-ambiguity of meaning. Illustrated by [the verse about] <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu):
'The earth [was lifted] from the ocean reddened by the blood of serpents crushed by [his] hooves.' // 73 //

children.text: अर्थस्य काव्याभिधेयवस्तुनो नेयत्वं शब्दतोऽर्थतो वाप्रतीतिरन्यथावगमः स्यात् । गत्यन्तराभावात् । यद्वक्ष्यति—
न हि प्रतीतिः सुलभा शब्दन्यायविलंघिनी । इति ।
children.translated_text: 'For comprehension that violates the principles of word and logic is not easy to attain.' — Thus.

Of the meaning — i.e., the subject matter of poetry — 'ambiguity' (<s>neyatva</s>) is the non-comprehension or wrong comprehension from words or meaning. Because there is no other way [to understand it]. As will be said:

children.text: नेयत्वभेदमनूद्यार्थव्यक्तिर्विधीयते । तदुदाहरति । हरीत्यादि, हरिणा वराहरूपधारिणा विष्णुना पृथिवी भूरुद्धृता समुत्तारिता उदधेः समुद्रात् । किंविशिष्टात् । खुरैर्महावराहस्येत्यर्थाद्गम्यते । चरणाग्रैः क्षुण्णानां चूणितानां नागानामुरगाणामसृजा रुधिरेण लोहितादरुणात्
इतीदृशमनेयं काव्यम् । अत्र हि नागशोणितं शब्दोपात्तं यदुपाधिकमरुणत्वमर्णवस्य । न्यायोपात्तं तु ।
children.translated_text: thus is this unambiguous poetry. Here, the blood of serpents is verbally conveyed; the redness of the ocean, which is conditional upon it, [is thus explained]. But what is conveyed by logical inference is:

Having restated the distinction of ambiguity, clarity of meaning is prescribed. He illustrates it with '<s>Hari</s>' and so forth. By <s>Hari</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of the Boar (<s>Varāha</s>), the earth was 'lifted' (<s>uddhṛtā</s>), i.e., rescued, from the ocean. Of what kind [was that ocean]? — 'Crushed by the hooves' — of the Great Boar, as understood from context — i.e., by the tips of the feet; 'of the serpents' (<s>nāga</s>), i.e., the snakes; by the 'blood' (<s>asṛj</s>), i.e., gore, of [those serpents]; 'reddened' (<s>lohita</s>), i.e., crimson —
'The Great Boar lifted the earth from the ocean that was turbulent with serpent-families crushed by [his] hooves,
[the ocean] crimson, in an instant.' //

children.text: अत्र यद्यपि नागरुधिरमशब्दोपात्तं यदुपाधिकलोहितत्वमुदधेः, तथापि खुरक्षुण्णमहोरगकुलाकुलादर्णवादरुणादित्युक्तेः सामर्थ्यात् स्फुटं नागरुधिरं गम्यते ।
तथाविधस्योदधेर्नागरुधिराव्यभिचारात् । न हि सर्वत्र शाब्दी प्रतीतिः काव्ये, अर्थे अपि तस्या दर्शनात् । यदाह कालिदासः—
children.translated_text: Because an ocean of that kind is invariably [associated with] serpent-blood. For not everywhere in poetry is comprehension [based on] verbal expression alone; it is also seen [to arise] from meaning. As <s>Kālidāsa</s> says:
'He who, having assumed the form of the Great Bull, now seated upon <s>Mahendra</s> [mountain], having attained the sport of the Bearer-of-Pināka (<s>Śiva</s>),
made the cheeks of the <s>Asura</s>-women bereft of their painted leaf-ornaments with his arrows.' //

Here, although the serpent-blood is not verbally conveyed [directly] and the redness of the ocean is conditional upon it, nevertheless, from the statement 'from the ocean crimson, turbulent with great serpent-families crushed by hooves,' by the force of coherence, the serpent-blood is clearly understood.

children.text: अत्र हि तेन राज्ञा बाणैरसुराः समरे हता इत्यर्थो विवक्षितः कविना । न चासुरवधः शब्दोपात्तः । तथापि असुराङ्गनानां गण्डस्थलीः प्रोषितपत्रलेखाश्चकार बाणैरित्युक्ते सामान्यादसुरा हता इति न्यायोपात्तोऽसुरवधस्तादृशस्य पत्रलेखाप्रवासस्यासुरवधाव्यभिचारात् । न चेदृशं नेयत्वम्, प्रत्युत वक्रोक्तिरीदृशी गुण एव काव्यस्य । ततः शब्देन न्यायेन वाचिना यत्रार्थो नेतव्यस्तादृशं नेयं विज्ञेयमन्यथा तथाविधं काव्यं सर्वं दुष्येदिति ॥
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning intended by the poet is that the king killed the <s>Asuras</s> in battle with his arrows. Yet the killing of the <s>Asuras</s> is not verbally stated. Nevertheless, when it is said 'he made the cheeks of the <s>Asura</s>-women bereft of their painted leaf-ornaments with his arrows,' by general inference, 'the <s>Asuras</s> were killed' — the killing of the <s>Asuras</s> is conveyed by logical inference, because such removal of painted leaf-ornaments is invariably [associated with] the killing of <s>Asuras</s>. And such [an inference] is not ambiguity; rather, such figurative expression is indeed a virtue of poetry. Therefore, where the meaning must be led [to a conclusion] by word or by an adequate logical principle — such poetry is not 'ambiguous' in the [faulty] sense; otherwise all such poetry would be flawed.
Illustrating the ambiguous, [the author] says:
'The earth was lifted by the Great Boar from the ocean that was reddened' —
when stated just this much, there is ambiguity regarding the serpent-blood. // 74 //

children.text: लोहितादुदधेरुद्धृता मही महावराहेनेत्युक्ते कथं लोहितत्वमुदधेरिति नयं न तावत्स्वाभाविकम् । औपाधिकं तु भवेत् । न चोपाधिस्तादृशः शब्दोपात्तो न्यायलब्धो वा येन लोहितत्वमुदधेः स्यात् ।

यथोक्तं प्राक् । तस्मादभिप्रायमात्रमेतत् मयैवं विवक्षितमिति । न चैतावता प्रतीतिः प्राप्यते, शब्दस्य न्यायस्य तादृशस्यानुपादानात् । यदि पुनरपरः कश्चित्तादृशमर्थं कथञ्चित् स्वयमभ्यूह्य गृह्णीयात्तस्यैवासौ गुणः । काव्यं तु तादृशं दृष्टमेव । अत एव लोहितादुदधेरित्येतावद् वक्तुं न तु तथाविधः कश्चिद्विशेष उपात्तः, यतो नागरुधिरलोहितत्वमुदधेर्गम्येत । यथोक्तं प्राक् । ततश्चेयत्येव लोहितादुदधेरुद्धृता महावराहेण महीति एतावत्येव निर्विशेषशब्देन न्यायेन वा तादृशेन रहिते वाक्ये निर्दिष्टेन प्रयुज्य उरगासृजो नागरक्तस्य न्येत्वं मयैवं विवक्षितमितिं विवक्षामात्रगम्यत्वं जायते । न तु शब्दोपात्तं न्यायोपात्तं वा नागशोणितं यदुपाधिंकमरुणत्वमर्णवस्य । न च तादृशं सुलभं न्यायशब्दानां रूढ़स्यार्थस्य विवक्षामात्रेण दुष्प्रापत्वात् । तस्मादीदृशं नेयमवगम्यं परिंहर्त्तंव्यम् इति ॥
children.translated_text: As stated before. Therefore this is merely the author's intention — 'I intended it thus.' But comprehension is not thereby attained, because no such word or logical principle has been employed. If, however, some other person were to somehow infer and grasp such a meaning by himself, that would be his own merit. But the poetry [itself] is seen to be of that [deficient] kind. For this very reason, [the author] can only say 'from the reddened ocean' — but no particular specification is conveyed from which the redness of the ocean due to serpent-blood could be understood. As stated before. Therefore, 'when stated just this much' — when the statement is 'the earth was lifted by the Great Boar from the reddened ocean' — in this sentence alone, lacking specific word or logical principle, there is 'ambiguity' (<s>neyatva</s>) regarding 'the serpent-blood' — i.e., [the redness being] comprehensible only through [the author's] mere intention, not through verbal expression or logical inference — this arises. And such [comprehension] is not easy, because the established meaning of words and logical principles is difficult to attain through mere intention alone. Therefore, such ambiguity is to be understood [as a fault] and avoided.

When it is said 'the earth was lifted by the Great Boar from the ocean that was reddened,' how is the redness of the ocean [to be explained]? The inference [leads one to think] — it is not natural [redness]. It could be conditional. But no such conditioning agent is verbally conveyed or logically obtainable by which the ocean would be reddened.
Showing that the ambiguous is not esteemed by all, [the author] says:
Such [poetry] is not greatly esteemed in either of the two paths.
For comprehension that transgresses word and logical reasoning is not easily attained. || 75 ||

children.text: ईदृशमनन्तरोक्तप्रकारं नेयमुभयोरपि वैदर्भगौडीययोर्मार्गयोर्वर्त्मनोः । न वैदर्भ एव । न बहु मन्यन्ते नाद्रियन्ते न प्रयुज्यन्ते तद्विदः ।
children.translated_text: Such is <s>neya</s> (what requires interpretation), of the kind just described, belonging to both paths — the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and the <s>Gauḍīya</s>. Not only to the <s>Vaidarbha</s> alone. Those who are knowledgeable do not value it highly, do not favor it, and do not employ it.
The reversal of these [qualities] is mostly observed in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path.

children.text: इति प्रायोग्रहणेन संगृहीतं किं बहु मन्यत इति चे
children.translated_text: If one asks whether [the point] is sufficiently covered by the word 'mostly' (<s>prāyaḥ</s>) in that [verse],

children.text: दाह—न हीत्यादि । हिशब्दो यस्मादर्थे । यतः प्रतीतिरर्थस्यावगमः शब्दं वाचकं न्यायसामर्थ्यं च तादृशमनुपदर्शनाल्लङ्घयति त्यजत्यनुपादा[ना]दिति, शब्दन्यायविंलङ्घिनी न सुलभा न प्राप्यते कस्यचिद् विंवक्षामात्रेण तादृशेन । तस्मान्नेच्छन्ति मूलहानेः । न्यायोपात्तः शब्दोपात्तो वा योऽर्थो न भवति स न प्रतीयतेऽन्तस्तत्त्वमात्रेणेत्यर्थः । तस्मात् शब्दादर्थाद्वा प्रतीतार्थमनेयं तद्विपरीतं तु नेयमिति स्थितम् ॥
children.translated_text: He answers — 'na hi' ('for not') and so on. The word 'hi' is used in the sense of 'because.' Since comprehension (<s>pratīti</s>), which is the apprehension of meaning, transgresses — that is, abandons by not employing — the expressive word (<s>śabda</s>) and the force of logical reasoning (<s>nyāya</s>) when such [grounds] are not shown, [such comprehension] that transgresses word and reasoning is not easily attained — it is not achieved merely by someone's wish to express [a meaning] in that manner. Therefore they do not desire [it], because the foundation would be lost. The meaning is: a meaning that is neither obtained through reasoning nor obtained through words is not comprehended merely by [knowing] the inner truth alone. Therefore, what is understood from the word or from the [conventional] meaning is <s>aneya</s> (not requiring interpretation); that which is contrary to this is <s>neya</s> (requiring interpretation) — this is established.
And that [is shown by]:
Indicating <s>udāratva</s> (the quality of being sublime), he says —
When in some [composition] a certain <s>guṇa</s> (virtue) possessing excellence is perceived,
That [composition] is called <s>udāra</s> (sublime); by that [virtue], the entire composition is graced. || 76 ||

children.text: यस्मिन् कस्मिंश्चित् उक्ते प्रयुक्ते कश्चिद्विवक्षिंतो गुणो विशेषस्त्यागादिलक्षण उक्तर्षवानधिमात्रः प्रतीयते अवगम्यते तत् काव्यमुदाराह्वयमुदारं नाम वेदितव्यमिति विधिः । उदारमित्याह्वयः संज्ञा यस्येति विग्रहः । यद्येवं स एवोत्कर्षवान् गुण उदारोऽस्तु, काव्यं कथमुदारमुच्यते इति चेदाह—तेनेत्यादि । यतस्तेनोत्कर्षवता गुणेन वाच्यत्वेनापिं रूपेण सर्वा पद्धतिः सर्वं तत्काव्यं विवक्षितं यत्किञ्चित् सनाथा युक्ता, तस्मादुदारगुणयोगात् सर्वं तत् काव्यमुदारमिति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: When in some [composition] that is expressed, a certain intended <s>guṇa</s> (virtue) — a special quality characterized by generosity (<s>tyāga</s>) and the like — possessing supreme excellence is perceived and apprehended, that <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) is to be known as having the designation <s>udāra</s> (sublime) — this is the rule. The compound is analyzed as: 'that whose designation (<s>āhvaya</s>) is <s>udāra</s>.' If so, let that excellent <s>guṇa</s> itself be called <s>udāra</s> — how can the <s>kāvya</s> be called <s>udāra</s>? To this he says — 'tena' ('by that') and so on. Since by that excellent <s>guṇa</s>, in the form of being the expressed content, the entire composition — whatever <s>kāvya</s> is intended — is graced, therefore, due to its connection with the <s>udāra</s> quality, the entire <s>kāvya</s> is to be regarded as <s>udāra</s>.
Illustrating that, he says —

children.text: अर्थिनां कृपणा दृष्टिः स्त्वन्मुखे पतिता सकृत् ।
children.translated_text: The pitiful gaze of supplicants, once it has fallen upon your face,
Remaining in that same state, O king, does not look upon the face of another. || 77 ||

children.text: अर्थिनां याचकानां दृष्टिश्चक्षुः कृपणा दीना निरानन्ददौर्गत्योपहतत्वात् याच्ञामरणावस्थाप्राप्तत्वाच्च त्वन्मुखे वदने सकृदेकवारं पतिता प्रवृत्ता सती तदवस्था सा

कृपणा अवस्था यस्या इति विग्रहः । पुनस्तथैव कृपणा अप्राप्तकामत्वादन्यस्य दातुर्मुखं नेक्षते न पश्यति देवेति कश्चिद्राजा स्तूयते । त्वामेकवारमर्थितया प्राप्य पुनरन्यं न याचते त्वत्त एव पूर्णमनोरथत्वात् । आकारमात्रेण वार्थितां ज्ञात्वा कृतार्थयसि यावद् याच्ञाक्षराणि कृपणानि नोद्गीरन्तीत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: remaining in that same state — 'pitiful' is the state of which, thus the compound is analyzed — again still pitiful because its desire is unfulfilled, does not look upon, does not see, the face of another patron. 'O king' — some king is being praised. Having approached you once with a petition, [the supplicant] does not petition another again, because his wishes are fully satisfied by you alone. Merely from [seeing your] expression, knowing the petition, you fulfill it before the pitiful syllables of supplication are even uttered — this is the meaning.

The gaze — the eyes — of supplicants (<s>arthin</s>s), that is, petitioners, being pitiful — wretched — because it is afflicted by joyless misfortune, and because it has reached the state of begging at the point of death, having once — a single time — fallen upon, that is, turned toward, your face,

children.text: कः पुनरिहोत्कर्षवान् गुणो येन सनाथं सर्व तत्काव्यमुदारं स्यादिति विवृण्वन्नाह—
children.translated_text: What then is the excellent <s>guṇa</s> (virtue) here by which the entire <s>kāvya</s> is graced and becomes <s>udāra</s>? Explaining this, he says —
Thus, in this verse, the excellence of <s>tyāga</s> (generosity) is well perceived.
By this same method, other [instances] too, following the same principle, should be inferred. || 78 ||

children.text: इत्यस्मिन्न[न]न्तरोक्ते वाक्ये काव्ये त्यागस्य दानस्य गुणोत्कर्षः अतिशयः साधु सम्यक् परिस्फुटं क्रियाविशेषणं, लक्ष्यते प्रतीयते । तस्मात्तद्योगेनोत्कर्षवता गुणेनेदं काव्यं सर्वं सनाथमुदारमाख्यायत इति योज्यम् । प्रकारमिममन्यत्राति[दि]शन्नाह—अनेनेत्यादि । अनेनैवोक्तेन पथा विधिना अन्यच्च परमपि समानः सदृशः न्यायः प्रकारो यस्य तत् समानन्यायमेवंजातीयकमू[ह्य]तां स्वयमनुगम्यताम् । दिशो दर्शितत्वाच्च शक्यमनुसर्तुमीदृशमिति भावः । तद्यथा—

children.translated_text: Merely by the utterance of your name, O king, the wives of your enemies

children.text: शोकारुणानि चक्षूंषि वहन्ति विधवा इव ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: bear eyes reddened with grief, as if they were widows. Thus [ends the illustration].

In this verse just stated, the excellence — the surpassing degree — of <s>tyāga</s> (generosity), that is, giving, is well and clearly perceived — 'well' (<s>sādhu</s>) being an adverb modifying the verb. Therefore, by connection with that — by the excellent <s>guṇa</s> — this entire <s>kāvya</s> is graced and designated as <s>udāra</s> — this should be supplied. Extending this method to other cases, he says — 'anena' ('by this') and so on. By this very stated method, other [instances] too — that is, additional ones — following the same principle, being of the same kind, should be inferred — that is, understood by oneself. Since the direction has been shown, such [cases] can be followed — this is the implication. For example:
Showing another type, he says —
That which is endowed with praiseworthy qualifiers is considered <s>udāra</s> (sublime) by some,
such as 'sport-lotus,' 'play-lake,' 'golden armlet,' and the like. || 79 ||
that is, by the Easterners (<s>Paurastyāḥ</s>),

children.text: रिष्यते । [तन्मते] तदप्यस्त्विति भावः । यथेत्युदाहरति । लीलार्थमम्बुजं, क्रीडार्थं सरः, हेममयमङ्गदमिति [सर्वत्र] मध्यपदलोपी समासः । लीलाम्बुजक्रीडासरोहेमा[ङ्गदा......आ]दिर्येषां ते । इमे श्लाघ्यविशेषणयुक्तप्रकारा लीलादीनां विशेषणानां श्लाघ्यत्वात् । तद्योगात् काव्यमुदारं द्रष्टव्यम् । आदिशब्देनादर्शभित्तिमणिमेखलाकुसुमस्रग्विभ्रममण्डनाङ्गलेखादिपरिग्रहः ॥
children.translated_text: it is so regarded. [According to their view] let that also be so — this is the implication. He illustrates with 'yathā' ('such as'). A lotus for sport, a lake for play, an armlet made of gold — in each case the compound involves ellipsis of the middle term (<s>madhyapadalopī samāsa</s>). 'Sport-lotus, play-lake, golden armlet, and so on' — those [compositions] having these [as qualifiers]. These are examples of the type endowed with praiseworthy qualifiers, since qualifiers like 'sport' and the rest are praiseworthy. By their connection, the <s>kāvya</s> is to be regarded as <s>udāra</s>. By the word 'and so on' (<s>ādi</s>), [we understand] the inclusion of [compounds like] 'mirror-wall,' 'jeweled girdle,' 'flower-garland,' 'graceful ornament,' 'body-painting,' and so forth.
That which is endowed — conjoined — with praiseworthy, that is, excellent qualifiers — epithets — is [considered] <s>udāra</s> by some,
Indicating what characterizes <s>ojas</s> (vigor), he says —
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is the preponderance of compounds (<s>samāsa</s>); this is the life-force of prose.
Even in verse, for the non-Southerners, this alone is the chief resource. || 80 ||

children.text: समासस्यैकार्थवृत्तेर्भूयस्त्वं बाहुल्यमित्यनूद्य ओजो विधीयते । तदेतदोजः समासबाहुल्यलक्षणं गद्यस्योक्तरूपस्य जीवितं हृदयं सारं न पद्यस्य तत्प्रधानत्वाद्नद्यस्येतिं । वैदर्भाणां दाक्षिणात्यानाम् । गौडानां तु इदमोज एकं केवलं परायणं शरणं पद्येऽपि विषये न केवलं गद्ये ततश्चात्रापि मतभेद इति ॥
children.translated_text: Having stated that the preponderance — the abundance — of compounds (<s>samāsa</s>), which express a unified meaning, [defines <s>ojas</s>], <s>ojas</s> is prescribed. This <s>ojas</s>, characterized by abundance of compounds, is the life-force — the heart, the essence — of prose of the described type, not of verse, because it is primary in prose. The <s>Vaidarbhas</s> are the Southerners (<s>Dākṣiṇātyāḥ</s>). For the <s>Gauḍas</s>, however, this <s>ojas</s> alone is the sole refuge — the chief resource — even in verse, not only in prose. Thus here too there is a difference of views.
Showing another variety and the scope of that [ojas], he says —
That [ojas], through the admixtures of abundance, scarcity, and balance of heavy and light [syllables],
being of varied kinds, is to be observed in <s>ākhyāyikā</s>s (narrative prose works) and the like. || 81 ||

children.text: तदोजः उच्चावचो व्याकुलः अनियतः प्रकारो गतिः प्रयोगो यस्य तदुच्चावचप्रकारं सत् भवत् दृश्यं विज्ञेयमाख्यायिकादिंषु गद्यप्रबन्धेषु । आदिंशब्देन कथादिपरिग्रहः । कथमुच्चावचप्रकारान्तरं भवतीत्याह—गुरूणां संयोगपराणां दीर्घाणां च लघूनामक्षरा

णां च बाहुल्येनोपचयेन अल्पत्वेनासञ्चयेन मिश्रणं समत्वेन चेत्येवं बाहुल्याल्पत्वमिंश्रणैः कारणैरुच्चावचप्रकारम् । नियमाभावात् क्वचिद् गुरूणां बाहुल्यं लघूनामल्पत्वं, क्वचिल्लघूनां बाहुल्यं गुरूणामल्पत्वं, क्वचिदुभयेषां समत्वमितीयन्तः प्रकारा भवेयुरिति ॥
children.translated_text: by abundance — by accumulation — by scarcity — by non-accumulation — and by admixture — by equality — thus through these [factors of] abundance, scarcity, and admixture, [it becomes] of varied kinds. Since there is no fixed rule: sometimes there is abundance of heavy syllables and scarcity of light ones, sometimes abundance of light syllables and scarcity of heavy ones, and sometimes equality of both — these are the kinds that may occur.

That <s>ojas</s>, having varied — irregular, unfixed — kinds of modes and employment, being of varied kinds, is to be known and observed in <s>ākhyāyikā</s>s (narrative prose) and similar prose compositions. By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), <s>kathā</s> (tale) and other forms are included. How does it become of varied kinds? He says — of heavy [syllables], that is, those with conjunct consonants and long vowels, and of light syllables,
Illustrating the use of <s>ojas</s> in verse by the Easterners (<s>Paurastyāḥ</s>), he says —
The western quarter, spread with the complete carpet of the sun's rays cast upon the summit of the setting mountain,
[shines] like a woman with a beautiful crimson garment clinging to her full breasts — [such is] the western direction. || 82 ||

children.text: वारुणी पश्चिमा दिक । भातीति गम्यते । किभूता ? अस्तस्य पर्वतस्य मस्तके शिरसि शिखरे पर्यस्तः पतितः समस्तो निरवशेषः, दिनपरिणतेः तत्र संहारात् । अर्कस्यादित्यस्यांशूनां रश्मीनां संस्तरः सन्तानो यस्यामिति समासबाहुल्यं सामान्येन दर्शितम् । विशे[षेणा]तिप्रसङ्गात् । एवंविधा कथमिव भातीत्याह—पीनेत्यादि । पीने महति स्तने पयोधरे स्थितं सक्तम् आताम्रं लोहितं कम्रं कान्तं वस्त्रं वसनं यस्यास्तथेति भाति । इह लोहितत्वं शब्दोपात्तमाताम्रशब्दप्रयोगात् । पूर्वं तु न्यायोपात्तम्, अस्तपर्वतपतितानामादित्यरश्मीनां लोहितत्वाव्यभिचारात् । न चेदृशी नेयं यथोक्तं प्राक् । अत एवोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: <s>Vāruṇī</s> means the western direction. [The verb] 'shines' is understood. Of what kind? Upon the summit — the peak, the crest — of the setting mountain (<s>Asta</s>), [the rays are] cast — fallen; they are complete — without remainder, because at the end of the day they are gathered there. Of the sun (<s>Arka</s>) — of <s>Āditya</s> — the rays' (<s>aṃśu</s>) carpet — spread — [covers] her: thus the abundance of compounds is demonstrated in general. [He does not go into] specifics, as that would lead to over-extension. How does she shine in this manner? He says — 'pīna' ('full') and so on. On the full — large — breast, a crimson — reddish — beautiful garment clings — adheres. Here the redness is obtained through the word itself, due to the use of the term 'ātāmra' (coppery). In the former [part of the verse], however, [the redness] is obtained through logical reasoning (<s>nyāya</s>), because the rays of the sun that have fallen on the setting mountain are invariably red. And such [meaning] is not <s>neya</s> (requiring interpretation) as was explained before. Hence it was said —
For comprehension that transgresses word and logical reasoning is not easily attained.

children.text: अस्तपर्वतः स्तनसदृशो वारुण्याः । अर्कांशुसंस्तर[स्तत्र] पतितः ताम्रवस्त्रतुल्य इति द्रष्ट
children.translated_text: The setting mountain resembles the breast of <s>Vāruṇī</s> (the western direction). The carpet of sun's rays fallen upon it is comparable to the crimson garment — this is to be understood.
[End of explanation.]
Thus, even in verse, the Easterners compose vigorous (<s>ojasvinī</s>) utterances.
Others, however, desire <s>ojas</s> in speech that is unconfused and pleasing. || 83 ||

children.text: इत्येवंविधा अहृद्या ओजस्विनीः समासबाहुल्यवतीः गिरः शब्दान् पद्येऽपि काव्ये, न केवलं गद्ये । बध्नन्ति रचयन्ति पौरस्त्या गौडाः । दाक्षिणात्या अपि क्वचित् पद्येऽप्योजः प्रयुञ्जते । तत्तु विशेषविवक्षायां तुशब्दः । अनाकुलमगहनम् । अत एव हृद्यं सुभगम् ओजः कथितलक्षणम् इच्छन्ति प्रयुञ्जते इति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, [composing] in this manner — which is not pleasing — vigorous (<s>ojasvinī</s>) utterances, that is, words abounding in compounds, even in verse — in <s>kāvya</s> — not only in prose, the Easterners — the <s>Gauḍas</s> — compose [them]. The Southerners (<s>Dākṣiṇātyāḥ</s>) also sometimes employ <s>ojas</s> even in verse. But that [they do so with a difference] — the word 'tu' ('however') indicates a distinction. [They desire it to be] unconfused — not dense. And therefore pleasing — attractive. [They] desire — employ — <s>ojas</s> of the described nature.
He illustrates what that is like —
The western direction, with the cloth of twilight's glow clinging to the region of her cloud-breasts,

children.text: कस्य कामातुरं चेतो वारुणी न करिष्यति ॥ ८४ ॥
children.translated_text: whose heart will she not make love-sick? || 84 ||

children.text: वारुणी दिगपरा । किंभूता ? पयोधरो मेघः स्तनश्च । शब्दश्लेषोऽयम् । तस्य तटः एकदेशः स एवोत्सङ्गो मध्यभागः । तत्र लग्नः स्थितः सन्ध्यातपः । दिनपरिणतिः स एवांशुकं रक्तं वस्त्रं यस्याः सा तथाभूता कस्य नाम कामिनश्चेतश्चित्तं कामातुरं मन्मथाक्रान्तं न करिष्यति ? सर्वस्यैव करोति रागानुकूलत्वात्तस्या अवस्थायाः । तादृशमनाकुलं हृद्यमोजः प्रयुञ्जते वैदर्भाः ।
children.translated_text: <s>Vāruṇī</s> is the western direction, and also [suggests] a woman. Of what kind? <s>Payodhara</s> means both 'cloud' and 'breast' — this is a verbal <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). Its slope — one portion — that is the lap, the middle region. There the twilight glow clings — is situated; that itself is the garment (<s>aṃśuka</s>) — a red cloth — of hers, she being thus described. Whose heart — whose mind — of what lover will it not make love-sick — seized by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of desire)? It will do so for everyone, since that state is conducive to passion. Such is the unconfused and pleasing <s>ojas</s> that the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> employ.
The face [of beautiful women], with the moonlight of playful laughter spreading over [their] lip-petals,

children.text: मुखं मृगदृशां कस्य हृदयं न हरिष्यति ॥
children.translated_text: whose heart will it not steal?

children.text: धाविता अपि ते दन्ताः श्यामा मुग्धे मुधा श्रमः ।
children.translated_text: Your teeth have been cleaned, O naive one, but the effort is in vain, dark girl,
[for] the bees are [merely] reflections attracted by the fragrance of your lotus-face.
With eyes that are clever, sweet, tender, naive, and bewildered,
your face, charming with the display of laughter [playing] upon graceful eyebrow-creepers, [is captivating].
Thus [end] three additional illustrations.
he says —
Analyzing <s>kānta</s> (the charming quality),
<s>Kānta</s> (charming) is that which is beloved of all the world, because it does not transgress worldly meaning (<s>laukikārtha</s>).
And that is observed in narrations of events and also in descriptions. || 85 ||

children.text: सर्वस्य वैदर्भस्येतरस्य वा जगतो जनस्य कान्तं मनोहरं यत् तत् कान्तं विज्ञेयमितिविधिः कुत एवमित्याह—लौकिकार्थानतिक्रमादिति । लोकविदितोऽर्थो लौकिकम् । तस्य लौकिकस्यार्थस्याभिधेयस्यानतिक्रमात् अनुवृत्तेः कारणात् । लौकिकार्थानुवृत्तेर्हि काव्यं साधारणं सर्वेषां कान्तं भवति । तस्य विनियोगविषयं दर्शयन्नाह—तच्चेत्यादि । तच्च कान्तम् । अर्थान्तरसमुच्चये चकारः । तदाह—वार्ताभिधानेषु प्रवृत्तिनिवेदनेषु वर्णनास्वपि वस्तुगुणोद्भाविनीषु च दृश्यते प्रयुज्यते ॥
children.translated_text: That which is <s>kānta</s> — pleasing — to all the world (<s>jagat</s>), whether <s>Vaidarbha</s> or otherwise, that is, to all people, is to be known as <s>kānta</s> — this is the rule. Why is this so? He says — 'because of not transgressing worldly meaning.' A meaning known to the world is <s>laukika</s> (worldly). Because of not transgressing — because of conforming to — that worldly meaning, that is, the expressed content: because when <s>kāvya</s> follows worldly meaning, it becomes universally attractive (<s>kānta</s>) to all. Showing its domain of application, he says — 'and that' and so on. And that <s>kānta</s> [quality] — the word 'ca' ('and') indicates conjunction with another topic. He states: it is observed — employed — in narrations of events (<s>vārtābhidhāna</s>), that is, reports of happenings, and also in descriptions (<s>varṇanā</s>), that is, [passages] that bring out the qualities of things.
He illustrates that —
Those houses alone are truly homes, which a heap of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) such as yourself
honors thus with purifying foot-dust. || 86 ||

children.text: केनचित् तपोधनेन कश्चिद् गृहमेधी स्वगृहागतेन वार्तापृष्टः सन् अभिधत्ते गृहाणि गेहानि नाम तान्येवोच्यन्तेऽर्थतो नामतश्च नान्यानि । अत एव नामेत्युक्तम् । संभावनायां वा नामशब्दः । कतमानि ? यानि गृहाणि एवमागमनोत्सवेन पादपांसुभिश्चरणरेणुभिः पावनैः पवित्रैः जाह्नवीजलैरिव संभावयति मानयति पुनाति भवादृशः त्वद्विधः तपोराशिः साक्षाद्धर्मसञ्चयः । तथाभिधं वार्ताभिधानं सर्वजगत्कान्तं लौकित्वात् तादृशस्यार्थस्य । उक्तं च—

children.translated_text: One who has maintained the sacred fire, a tawny cow, a [virtuous] wife, a king, a mendicant, the great ocean,

children.text: दृष्टा माता पुनन्त्येते त्वं पुनः स्मरणादपि ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: [and] a mother, when seen, purify — but you purify even by being remembered. Thus [ends the citation].

Some householder, questioned about news by an ascetic who has come to his house, declares: 'Those houses alone are called homes — in substance and in name, and no others.' Hence the word 'nāma' is used. Or the word 'nāma' is used in the sense of supposition. Which ones? Those houses which, on the occasion of [your] arrival, [one] such as yourself — a heap of <s>tapas</s>, a veritable accumulation of <s>dharma</s> — honors, purifies, with foot-dust — the dust of [your] feet — that is purifying, sanctifying, like the waters of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges). Such a narration of events is beloved of all the world, because the meaning is worldly in nature. And it has been said:
O woman of faultless limbs, of these two swelling breasts of yours,
the space between your vine-like arms is not sufficient. || 87 ||

children.text: अनवद्याङ्गि सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरि ! अनयाः तव स्तनयोः जृम्भमाणयोः परिवर्द्धमाण्योः बाहुलतान्तरं हृदयं पर्याप्तः परिपूर्णः अवकाशः स्थानं, [न] भवति । स्वल्पमेतत्स्थानं यत् बाहुलतान्तरं नाम । अतिमात्रस्तनौन्नत्याद् इत्ययमपि लौकिक एवार्थः । [ ततः सर्वजगत्कान्तमीदृशं वर्णनमिति ॥
children.translated_text: O woman of faultless limbs (<s>anavadyāṅgi</s>), that is, O woman beautiful in all limbs! Of these your two breasts, which are swelling — growing — the space between the vine-like arms, that is, the chest, is not sufficient — not adequate — as a place [for them]. This space called 'between the vine-like arms' is small indeed. Because of the exceeding prominence of the breasts — this too is a worldly meaning alone. [Therefore such description is beloved of all the world.]

children.text: कीदृशं सम्भाव्यते येन सर्वजगत्कान्तं स्यादिति चेदाह—
children.translated_text: If one asks what kind [of composition] can be supposed to be beloved of all the world, he says —
Thus, this very [quality], refined by the depiction of particularities, being something that can be experienced [by all],
becomes <s>kānta</s> (charming) for everyone who follows the course of worldly life. || 88 ||

children.text: इति परत इदमेवंविधं विशेषाख्यानसंस्कृतं संभाव्यं नैव लोके न सम्भाव्यत एव लौकिकार्थानुसारेण प्रयुक्तत्वात् । प्रकृतापेक्षया तयोर्विशेषः पादपांसूनां च पावनत्वं स्तनयोश्च तादृशविजृम्भनं विशेषोऽतिशयः तस्याख्यानेनोद्भावनेनासंस्कृतं व्युत्पन्नम् । विशेषो वा आख्यायते येन तदेव संस्कृतं सुप्रयुक्तत्वात् । काव्यं सम्भाव्यमिति प्रकृतम् । ततश्च लोकयात्रानुवर्तिनः लोकार्थानुसारिणः सर्वविदग्धस्येतरस्य वा जनस्य कान्तं मनोहरम्, तादृशं काव्यं भवति जायते ।
children.translated_text: Thus, hereafter, this kind of [poetry] — refined through the narration of distinction (<s>viśeṣākhyāna</s>) — is plausible (<s>sambhāvya</s>); it is not that it is implausible in the world, since it is employed in accordance with worldly meaning. In relation to the subject at hand, the distinction between the two — namely, the purifying nature of the foot-dust and such a swelling of the breasts — the distinction, i.e. the superlative quality, is derived (<s>vyutpanna</s>) through its narration, i.e. its evocation, being 'refined' (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Or: 'refined' [means] that by which a distinction is narrated — that itself is 'refined,' since it is well-employed. Poetry is 'plausible' — this is the main point. And thus, for one who follows the course of worldly affairs, who accords with worldly meanings — for any person, whether fully cultivated or otherwise — such poetry becomes, i.e. arises as, charming (<s>kānta</s>), delightful.

children.text: अद्य जाता वयं देव प्राप्ताः सर्वाश्च सिद्धयः ।
children.translated_text: Today we are [truly] born, O Lord, and all accomplishments have been attained, /
since [we have been] thus touched by your auspicious, smile-brightened gaze. //
Behold yourself in this radiant cheek-surface; /
O slender one, why do you torment yourself in vain with the fatigue of [seeking] mirrors? //
Thus — a
second pair of illustrations. //
Showing the narration and description favored by the <s>Gauḍas</s>, he says —
A meaning that is intended by superimposing [it] excessively, as if transcending the world — /
by that [meaning], the cultivated [connoisseurs] are exceedingly delighted, not other people // 89 //

children.text: लोकातीतोऽलौकिक इव लोकरञ्नात् । व्युत्पन्नास्तु रज्यन्ते । अत एव इवशब्दप्रयोगः । योऽर्थोऽत्यर्थमतिमात्रमध्यारोप्यते परिकल्प्यते, यथा च सर्वजगत्कान्तं काव्यं जायते । अध्यारोपमात्रं तु पूर्वस्मिन्नपि विद्यते इति अत्यर्थमित्युक्तम् । विवक्षितः प्रयुक्तः काव्यरूपेण तेन तथाविधेनार्थेन अभिधेयेन तथाविधार्थानुवर्तिना काव्येनेति यावत् । विदग्धा व्युत्पन्ना अतितुष्यन्ति अनुरज्यन्ते सुतरां तथाविधोक्त्या, अहतबुद्धित्वात् । इतरेऽविदग्धा नातितुष्यन्ति, तादृशामभावितस्वभावत्वात् । असंभाव्यमेतदतिप्रसङ्गोऽयमिति नानुरज्यन्ते इत्यर्थः । अत, एव सर्वजगत्कान्तं न भवति, विदग्धानामेव रञ्जनात् । यथेत्युदाहरति—
children.translated_text: Transcending the world (<s>lokātīta</s>) — 'as if' unworldly, since it [still] delights the world. But the cultivated are [indeed] delighted. For this very reason the word '<s>iva</s>' (as if) is employed. The meaning that is excessively, i.e. extremely, superimposed, i.e. imagined — and thus universally charming poetry arises. But superimposition alone exists in the former [type] too — hence 'excessively' is said. 'Intended' means employed in the form of poetry — by that meaning of such a kind, i.e. by poetry that follows such meaning — so much is meant. The cultivated, i.e. the learned, are 'exceedingly delighted,' i.e. are greatly enamored by such expression, because their intellect is unimpaired. Others, the uncultivated, are not exceedingly delighted, because their nature is not [similarly] refined. 'This is implausible, this is excessive' — thus they are not enamored: this is the meaning. For this very reason, it is not universally charming, since only the cultivated are delighted. He illustrates with 'as follows' —
Like a temple of the gods, from this day forth our house is to be worshipped, /
its every sin washed away by the fall of the dust of your feet // 90 //

children.text: देवायतनमिव यथा अद्य प्रभृति एतद्दिनमारभ्य नोऽस्माकं गृहमिदमाराध्यमुपास्यं यूजनीयं कृतम् । युष्माकं पादयोश्चरणपद्मयो रजसां रेणूनां पातेन संसर्गेणाघमर्षणेन धौतमपनीतं निःशेष समस्तं किल्विषं पापं यस्मिस्तथा । यत एवं तस्मादाराध्यमितिःप्रकृतम् । वार्ताभिधानमात्रमीदृशमलौकि कार्थमेव । ततश्च सर्वजगत्कान्तमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Like a temple of the gods — just as [a temple is worshipped], from this day forth, i.e. beginning from this day, our house, this [house], has been made worshipful, fit for veneration and service. By the fall, i.e. the contact, of the dust, i.e. particles, of your feet, i.e. lotus-feet — by that purification from sin — [the house has been] washed, i.e. cleansed of all, i.e. every, sin. Since this is so, therefore it is 'worshipful' — this is the main point. This is merely a narration in the manner of the <s>Gauḍas</s>, concerning an unworldly meaning. And thus it is universally charming. //
Without even considering, the Creator fashioned this narrow space of the sky — /
such will be the swelling of your breasts, O lady! // 91 //

children.text: इदं प्रत्यक्षम् एवंविधमतिशयं भवत्याः तव स्तनयाजृ म्भणं व्यापन भावि भविष्यत्कालापेक्षया अनालोच्यादृष्ट्वैवाल्पं संकीर्णं यथा न मातः स्तनौ, आकाशं व्योम निर्मितं विहितं वेधसा विधिना यद्यालोचयिष्यन्नैवं स्तोकमाकाशं निरमास्यत् प्रथमं तावत् जातवेदा इति वर्णनमसंस्कृतमेव ॥ नेदृशं सर्वजगत्कान्तं लौकिकार्थातिक्रमात् ॥
children.translated_text: This visible [phenomenon] — of such a kind, i.e. of superlative quality — the swelling, i.e. the expansion, of your breasts — will be (<s>bhāvi</s>), i.e. with reference to future time. Without considering, i.e. without seeing, [how] narrow and confined [the sky would be] — 'it will not accommodate the breasts,' so [the Creator should have thought] — the sky, i.e. the firmament, was fashioned, i.e. made, by the Creator (<s>Vedhas</s>), i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>. Had he considered, he would not have made the sky so small — [we should understand that] first 'the fire was born' — this is description (<s>varṇana</s>), which is 'unrefined' (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). // Such [poetry] is not universally charming, because it transgresses worldly meaning. //
What then is this called? — To this he says —
This is called '<s>atyukti</s>' (hyperbole) — this is cherished by the <s>Gauḍas</s>; /
but the path previously established is the essence of another path // 92 //

children.text: इदमीदृशमनन्तरोक्तं काव्यमत्युक्तिरित्युक्तमाख्यायते तज्ज्ञैरिति अत्युक्तिर्नामेदमित्यर्थः । एतदिदमनन्तरोक्तं गौडैः पौरस्त्यैरुपलालितमिष्टमत्यन्तं न वैदर्भसंमतमित्याह—प्रस्थानमित्यादि । प्राक्प्रणीतं पूर्वमुदाहृतं गृहाणि नामेत्यादि प्रस्थानं प्रकारः सारं जीवितमन्यस्य वैदर्भस्य वर्त्मनो मार्गस्य । तादृशं दाक्षिणात्यैः प्रयु[ज्य]त इति यावत् ॥
children.translated_text: 'This' — such poetry as was just stated — is called, i.e. is designated by the knowledgeable, as '<s>atyukti</s>' (hyperbole) — meaning, this is named <s>atyukti</s>. 'This' — what was just stated — is 'cherished by the <s>Gauḍas</s>,' i.e. is favored by the easterners, [but] not approved by the <s>Vaidarbhas</s> — he says 'the path' and so forth. 'Previously established' means 'illustrated earlier' — namely 'receive [our] houses' and the like — 'the path,' i.e. the mode, is 'the essence,' i.e. the life, of the other, i.e. the <s>Vaidarbha</s>, path (<s>vartman</s>). Such [poetry] is employed by the southerners — so much is meant. //
Regarding <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition), he says —
A property of one thing [superimposed] upon another, by one who follows the limits of worldly [convention] — /

children.text: सम्यगाधीयते यत्र स समाधिः स्मृतो यथा ॥ ९३ ॥
children.translated_text: where [it is] properly placed — that is called <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition); as follows // 93 //

children.text: अन्यस्य वस्तुनः प्रकृतापेक्षया । धर्मः गुणः प्रसिद्धस्ततस्तस्मान्मुख्यादन्यत्र गौणविषये सम्यक् साधु । लोकसीमानुवर्तित्वमेव सम्यक्त्वमिह द्रष्टव्यम् । आधीयतेऽध्यारोप्यते यत्र । केन ? लोकसीमानुरोधिना लोकप्रतीत्यनुवर्तिना कविना । यथा लोकप्रतीतिः समाद

धीत नान्यथेत्यर्थः । स एवंविधो धर्मः समाधिर्नाम काव्ये स्मृतो विज्ञेय इति विधिः । समाधीयतेऽध्यारोप्यते यस्मिन्निति समाधिः समारोपविषय उच्यते । यद्यपि समाधीयमानाद्धर्मादन्यो नास्ति समाधिः तथापि सामान्यविशेषभावेन भेदविवक्षया यत्रान्यधर्मः समाधीयते तत् समाधिरित्युक्तम् । गौणशब्दव्यवहारः काव्योपयोगी समाधिरिति यावत् । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: not otherwise — this is the meaning. That property of such a kind is known in poetry as <s>samādhi</s>, i.e. under the name <s>samādhi</s> — [it] is to be understood — this is the prescription. <s>Samādhi</s> means the locus upon which [a property] is superimposed — thus '<s>samādhi</s>' denotes the object of superimposition. Although there is no <s>samādhi</s> other than the superimposed property itself, nevertheless, with the intention of distinguishing between the general and the particular, [the text says] 'where another property is superimposed — that is <s>samādhi</s>.' The secondary use of words (<s>gauṇa-śabda-vyavahāra</s>) useful for poetry — that much is <s>samādhi</s>. He illustrates with 'as follows' —

Of another thing — in relation to the subject at hand. A property, i.e. a well-known quality — from that, i.e. from the primary [referent] — upon another, i.e. upon a secondary object — 'properly,' i.e. well. Following the limits of the world is itself the criterion of 'properly' here. [It] is placed, i.e. superimposed — where [this occurs]. By whom? — He says, 'by one who follows the limits of the world,' i.e. by a poet who accords with worldly perception. Just as worldly perception supports [the superimposition],
The night-lotuses close and the day-lotuses open — /
thus, by the superimposition of the action of the eye, the expression denoting that [action] has been obtained // 94 //

children.text: कुमुदानि कैरवा निमीलन्ति निमिषन्ति कमलानि पद्मानि उन्मिषन्ति चेत्यत्र कतमो धर्मः समाहितः इत्याह—नेत्रेत्यादि । नेत्रस्य क्रिया निमेषोन्मेषलक्षणा प्रसिद्धो धर्मः तस्मात्ततोऽन्यत्र कुमुदादिषु अध्यासात् समाधानात् समारोपात् कारणात् । तद्वाचिनी नेत्रक्रियाभिधायिनी श्रुतिर्निमीलन्तीत्यादिका लब्धा प्राप्ता प्रयुक्तेति यावत् । अर्थानुगामित्वाच्छब्दस्य इत्येवंभूतो भाक्तः शाब्दो व्यवहारः काव्ये समाधिनाम्ना ख्यायते ॥
children.translated_text: The night-lotuses (<s>kumuda</s>) close (<s>nimīlanti</s>); the day-lotuses (<s>kamala</s>) open (<s>unmiṣanti</s>) — in this, which property has been superimposed? — He says, 'of the eye' and so forth.
