The action of the eye — the well-known property characterized by closing and opening — from that, i.e. from the primary [referent], upon another, i.e. upon the night-lotuses and the like — by superimposition, i.e. by placement, i.e. by the act of superimposing — for this reason — the expression denoting that, i.e. the expression '<s>nimīlanti</s>' (they close) etc. that designates the action of the eye, has been obtained, i.e. has been attained, i.e. has been employed — so much is meant. Because words follow their meanings, such a secondary verbal usage (<s>bhākta śābda vyavahāra</s>) is known in poetry by the name <s>samādhi</s>. //

children.text: कश्चिद्धर्मः गौणविषय एव शोभते काव्ये न मुख्यगोचर इति दशयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Showing that a certain property shines in poetry only in a secondary application, not in a primary one, he says —
'Spat out,' 'disgorged,' 'vomited,' and the like — [when] dependent on secondary usage — /
are extremely beautiful; but otherwise they fall into the realm of the vulgar // 95 //

children.text: निष्ठ्यूतं वान्तम्, उद्गीर्णं च । आदिशब्देन रिक्तादिपरिग्रहः । तदीदृशं वचनं गौणी प्रधा

नेतरा निरूढ़विषयाद्विषयान्तरपरिग्रहलक्षणवृत्तिप्रयोगरूपा व्यपाश्रयो यस्य तत्तथा । गौणमिति यावत् । अतिसुन्दरमत्यन्तमनोहरमलंकाररूपत्वात् । अन्यत्तु इतरत् पुनः गौणवृत्त्यव्यपाश्रयात् मुख्यमिति यावत् । ग्राम्यकक्षाम् असभ्यपदवीं विगाहते प्रतिपद्यते । ग्राम्यमहृद्यमिति काव्ये तदुक्तेरनुचितत्वादिति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: usage characterized by the application to a domain other than the established domain — [that which has] this as its basis — that is thus, i.e. secondary. [Such language is] 'extremely beautiful,' i.e. exceedingly charming, because it has the nature of an ornament. But 'otherwise' — the other, i.e. that which is not dependent on secondary usage, meaning the primary [usage] — falls into the realm of the vulgar, i.e. enters the path of the unseemly. The purport is that [primary usage of such words] is inappropriate in poetry because it is unpleasing. //

'Spat out' (<s>niṣṭhyūta</s>) [means] 'vomited,' and 'disgorged' (<s>udgīrṇa</s>) [as well]. By the word 'and the like,' 'emptied' (<s>rikta</s>) and such are included. Such language — the secondary (<s>gauṇī</s>), i.e. not the primary,
He illustrates that —
The lotuses, having drunk the fire-sparks spat out by the sun's rays, /
seem to vomit them again through their mouths, with disgorged red pollen // 96 //

children.text: पावकविप्रुषः तेजःकणिकाः अर्कांशुभिरादित्यकिरणैर्निष्ठ्यूता निरस्ताः पीत्वा भूयोऽत्यर्थम् । अतश्च वमन्तीव उद्गिरन्तीव पद्मानीत्युत्प्रेक्षते मुखैरुद्गीर्णा मुक्ताः अरुणा लोहिताः रेणवः परागा यैरिति विग्रहः । उत्प्रेक्षाबीजमनेन सूचितम् । सूर्योदये हि विकसन्ति पद्मानि तेजःकणान् पिवन्तीव लक्ष्यन्ते रक्तान्परागान्मुञ्चन्ति च पीतानग्निकणान् वमन्तीव दृश्यन्ते । निष्ठीवनादिकं हि सचेतनकर्तृकं श्लेष्मादिकर्मकम् । मुख्यकाव्ये च तादृशमनुचितम् । इह त्वर्कांशुपद्ममुखकर्तृकं तेजो रेणुकर्मकं प्रयुक्तमिति अतिसुन्दरम् । सचेतनकर्मकमपि यदि गौणकर्तृकं प्रयुज्येत तदा न ग्रास्यम् । यथा—निष्ठ्यतमिति

children.translated_text: 'exhaling the joy harbored in the heart.' //

The fire-sparks, i.e. particles of radiance — spat out, i.e. cast forth, by the sun's rays, i.e. the beams of the sun — having drunk [them], i.e. excessively. And therefore they seem to vomit, i.e. seem to disgorge — the lotuses — thus he employs poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>) — through their mouths, disgorged, i.e. released — red, i.e. crimson — pollen, i.e. particles — such is the analysis. The basis of the poetic fancy is indicated by this. For at sunrise, lotuses bloom and appear as if drinking the particles of radiance; and they release red pollen and appear as if vomiting the consumed fire-particles. For spitting and the like are [actions] with a sentient agent and [with] phlegm and such as the object. In primary [i.e. literal] poetry, such [usage] is inappropriate. But here, with the sun's rays and the lotus-mouths as agents and radiance and pollen as objects, it is employed — hence it is 'extremely beautiful.' Even when the object is sentient, if employed with a secondary agent, it is not vulgar. As follows — 'you speak the name <s>niṣṭhyūta</s>,'
Thus this secondary [usage] is pleasing; but vulgar [is the following:] 'the bride spits.' /
The simultaneous superimposition of multiple properties is also accepted; as follows // 97 //

children.text: इतीदृशं गौणं हृद्यम् अतिसुन्दरम् । अहृद्यं तु ग्राम्यं पुनरुच्यते—निष्ठीवति वधूरिति सचेतनायाः ष्ठीवनं मुख्यं प्रसिद्धमेव । एकधर्मसमाधिरयं दर्शितः । युगपत्
एककालम् नैकेषां बहूनां धर्माणा क्रियादिरूपाणामध्यासः समाधिश्च मत इष्यते । चकार उक्तसमुच्चये । यथेत्युदाहरति ।
children.translated_text: the superimposition, i.e. the <s>samādhi</s>, of multiple, i.e. many, properties — [actions] of the nature of actions and the like — is also accepted, i.e. is approved. The particle '<s>ca</s>' (and) is for aggregation with what was stated. He illustrates with 'as follows.' //

Thus — such secondary [usage] is 'pleasing,' i.e. extremely beautiful. But the vulgar, i.e. unpleasing, is further stated — 'the bride spits' — for a sentient woman, spitting is primary, i.e. well-established. This was a demonstration of the superimposition of a single property. 'Simultaneously,' i.e. at a single time,
'Heavy with child' and so forth —
Heavy with the burden of their pregnancy, exhausted, groaning, the rows of clouds /
lie down upon the lap of the mountain plateau // 98 //

children.text: गुरुर्गृहीतसारत्वात् गर्भोऽन्तर्भागः स एव भरो भारः दुर्वहत्वात् तस्य वा भरोऽवसादः । तेन ल्कान्ता ग्लानाः स्तनन्त्यः ल्कान्त्यनुरूपं शब्दं कुर्वाणाः मेघपङ्क्तयः पयोदमाला इमा एता अचलस्य पर्वतस्य अधित्यकायाः उपरिभूमेरुत्सङ्गं समधिशेरतेऽध्यासते ॥
children.translated_text: 'Heavy' (<s>guru</s>) — because of having taken in the essence, i.e. the substance; the 'womb' (<s>garbha</s>) is the inner part — that itself is the 'burden' (<s>bhara</s>), being difficult to bear, or: the distress (<s>avasāda</s>) [caused] by it. 'Exhausted' (<s>klānta</s>) — wearied by that. 'Groaning' (<s>stanantya</s>) — making sounds appropriate to exhaustion. The 'rows of clouds' — these, i.e. these [clouds] — lie upon the 'lap' (<s>utsaṅga</s>) of the plateau, i.e. the upper surface, of the mountain. //
Showing how many properties are superimposed here, he says —

children.text: उत्सङ्गे शयनं सख्याः स्तननं गौरवं क्लमः ।
children.translated_text: Lying in the lap of a friend, groaning, heaviness, fatigue — /
these many properties of a pregnant woman have been shown [superimposed] upon another [subject] // 99 //

children.text: सख्याः कस्याश्चित् उत्सङ्गे शयनं स्तननमार्तरुतं गौरवं गर्भकृत[दुर्भरत्वा]दिलक्षणं तत्कृतश्च ल्कमः ग्लानिरित्येते गर्भिण्या अन्तर्वत्न्या धर्माः प्रसिद्धा बहवोऽनेके अन्यत्र मेघपङ्क्तिषु.........दर्शिता अध्यस्ता इत्ययमनेकधर्मसमाधिः ॥
children.translated_text: Of a certain friend — lying in [her] lap; groaning, i.e. crying in distress; heaviness — characterized by the difficulty of bearing [caused by] the pregnancy; and the fatigue caused by that, i.e. weariness — these, the well-known properties of a pregnant woman, i.e. of one who is with child — many, i.e. numerous — have been shown, i.e. superimposed, upon another [subject], i.e. upon the rows of clouds......... — this is the superimposition of multiple properties. //
concluding with praise, he says —
That <s>samādhi</s> is pervasive and beautiful —
This indeed is the entirety of poetry — the quality called <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition); /
the entire community of poets follows it // 100 //

children.text: तदेतदनन्तरोक्तं काव्यस् यथोक्तस्य गद्यपद्यमिश्रात्मकस्य सर्वस्वं सारं तत्परायणत्वात्काव्यस्येति सामान्योक्तिरियम् । किं तदिति निर्मिनत्ति । समाधिर्नाम यो गुण इति योऽयमनन्तरं विभक्तः समाधिर्नाम समाधिसमाख्यो गुणो धर्मस्ततश्च समग्रः सर्वोऽपि नैक एंव, कविसार्थः कविजनः तमेनं प्रकृतं समाधिमनुगच्छति समाश्रयति प्रयुङ्क्त इति यावत् । ततश्चोभयोरपि वर्त्मनोरयं साधारण इतीदमपि प्रायो गुणेषु संगृहीतं दृष्टमिति ॥
children.translated_text: 'This' — what was just stated — is the 'entirety,' i.e. the essence, of poetry as described — consisting of prose, verse, and mixed [composition] — because poetry is wholly devoted to it: this is a general statement. 'What is that?' — he specifies. 'The quality called <s>samādhi</s>' — this quality, i.e. property, that was just analyzed, called <s>samādhi</s>, i.e. bearing the name <s>samādhi</s>. And therefore the entire, i.e. all, not just one, community of poets, i.e. the assembly of poets, follows, i.e. resorts to, i.e. employs, this, the <s>samādhi</s> under discussion — so much is meant. And thus this [<s>samādhi</s>] is common to both paths — this too is largely seen as included among the qualities. //
Thus, having established the manifest difference between the two paths as promised, concluding, he says —
Thus the two paths are distinct, through the examination of their respective natures; /

children.text: तद्भेदास्तु न शक्यन्ते वक्तुं प्रतिकवि स्थिताः ॥ १०१ ॥
children.translated_text: but their subdivisions cannot be stated, being situated in each individual poet // 101 //

children.text: इति यथोक्तेन प्रकारेण मार्गद्वयं वैदर्भो गौडीयश्च मार्गः भिन्नं प्रस्फुटान्तरम । कुतः ? तस्य मार्गद्वयस्य स्वरूपम् अविपरीतस्वभावः, श्लेषादिस्वरूपं विदर्भमार्गस्य तद्विपर्ययस्वरूपं गौडीयस्य । तस्य निरूपणात् विवेचनात् यथाविहिताद् हेतोः । यदि मार्गद्वयं विविच्यते यथावत् ततो लभ्यते परिस्फुटमन्तरम् । ये तु न विजानन्ति तैरेकीकृतमेतत् । ततश्चाभेदोऽत्र समारोपितः । भेदस्तु वास्तव इत्याकूतम् । यथोक्तं प्राक् । कियन्तस्तर्हि प्रभेदा वैदर्भमार्गस्य कियन्तो वा

गौडीयस्य यतः परिस्फुटमन्तरं भेदसामान्यप्रविशेषमिदं तदिति गम्यत इत्याह—तद्भेदास्त्वित्यादि । तुशब्दोऽर्थान्तरविवक्षायाम् । तस्य मार्गद्वयस्य भेदा अवान्तराः प्रकाराः । यथोक्तसामान्यलक्षणन्यस्ता अनन्ताः गवाश्वप्रभेदवत्, किमाश्रयाः ? प्रतिकवि स्थिताः कविं कविं प्रति प्रतिकवि । ये केचिदिह कवयः सम्भवन्ति मार्गद्वयानुसारिणस्ते तदाश्रया इतस्ततो व्यवस्थिताः । न तु क्वचिदेकत्र परिसंख्यातास्तिष्ठन्ति । तस्मात् वक्तुं साकल्येन विवरीतुं न शक्यन्ते आनन्त्यादिति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: of the <s>Gauḍīya</s>, such that from [understanding] this — the general and the particular of the difference — that is grasped?' — To this he says, 'but their subdivisions' and so forth. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates a different topic. The subdivisions, i.e. the sub-varieties, of those two paths — as established under the general definition stated — are infinite, like the varieties of cows and horses. What are they based on? They are 'situated in each individual poet' — for each and every poet, whoever they may be, who follow the two paths — they are based on those [individual poets], established here and there in various ways. But they do not stand enumerated anywhere in one place. Therefore, they 'cannot be stated,' i.e. cannot be fully elaborated, because of their infinity — such is the purport. //

Thus — in the manner described — the two paths, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and the <s>Gauḍīya</s> path, are distinct, i.e. have a manifest difference. Why? Because of the examination, i.e. the analysis, of the nature, i.e. the true character, of those two paths — [namely] the nature characterized by <s>śleṣa</s> and the like for the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path, and the nature opposite to that for the <s>Gauḍīya</s>. 'From the prescribed cause' — if the two paths are properly analyzed, then the manifest difference is obtained. But those who do not understand have conflated them. And thus non-difference has been superimposed here. But difference is real — such is the purport. As was stated previously. 'How many then are the subdivisions of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> path, and how many

children.text: यदि तावत्सन्ति किं न वक्तुं शक्यन्ते ? वक्तुमशक्यास्तु न सन्त्येव ते । ततश्च यथोक्तमपि भेदसामान्यमसदिव ।
children.translated_text: If they exist, why can they not be stated? Those that cannot be stated simply do not exist. And thus even the general difference that was stated would be as if non-existent.
And a universal without particulars would be like a hare's horn. //

children.text: इत्येव शङ्कानैकान्तिकमेतत् । सतोऽपि कथञ्चिद् वक्तुमशक्यस्य दर्शनादिति प्रतिपादयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Such an objection is inconclusive. Showing that even something that exists can somehow be incapable of being stated, he says —
The difference in sweetness among sugarcane, milk, and jaggery is great; /
yet even <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech) herself cannot describe it // 102 //

children.text: इक्षुक्षीरगुडद्राक्षादीनां मधुरद्रव्याणां माधुर्यस्य सामान्यधर्मस्य प्रतिद्रव्यं विशेषात्मना अन्तरं भेदो महत् परिस्फुटम् । तथापि तदन्तरं सरस्वत्यापि वागधिदेवतयापि आख्यातुं वक्तुं विभागेनास्येदृशं माधुर्यमस्येदृशमिति न शक्यते । प्रागेवान्येन । केवलमनुभवगम्यं तत् । सामान्यशब्देन मधुरमिति तु व्यपदिश्यते । यद्यपीक्षो
रन्यादृशं माधुर्यं क्षीरस्यान्यादृशमित्यादि कथ्यते तथापि न तथा शब्दाद् गम्यते यथानुभूयते परिस्फुटं तदन्तरम् । न चैतावता तदसदेवानुभव
children.translated_text: is of one kind, the sweetness of milk of another, and so on — yet that difference is not apprehended from words as distinctly as it is experienced. Nor does this mean that it is non-existent, since what is established by experience

children.text: सिद्धस्य दुरपह्न[व]त्वात् । तथा मालतीमल्लिकाचम्पकपाटलादीनां सौरभ्यस्य महदन्तरं तथापि न तत्तथा वक्तुं शक्यते, यथानुभूयते । तथाविधा हि वाचिका शक्तिः सामान्यैकता नाम । को नु पर्यनुयुज्यताम् ? यथोक्तमाचार्यधर्मकीर्तिना सकलविद्वज्जनचूडामणिना—
children.translated_text: is difficult to deny. Similarly, the great difference in the fragrance of <s>mālatī</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭala</s>, and other flowers cannot be articulated as distinctly as it is experienced. For such is the nature of verbal capacity — it operates only through universals. Who can be blamed? As stated by <s>Ācārya Dharmakīrti</s>, the crest-jewel of all learned persons:
"Its form, being entirely unique, and likewise that which expresses it — /

children.text: न श्रुतिः कल्पना [वा]स्ति सामान्येनैव वृत्तितः । इति ॥
children.translated_text: neither perception nor conception [can grasp it]; it functions only through the universal." //

The difference — the distinction — between the sweetness of sugarcane, milk, molasses, grapes, and other sweet substances, which is a universal property, is great and manifest in its particular form for each substance. Yet even <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the presiding deity of speech, cannot articulate that difference by analysis — saying "the sweetness of this is of such a kind, that of such a kind." Much less anyone else. It is apprehensible only through experience. By the general word, it is merely designated as "sweet." Even though it is said that the sweetness of sugarcane

children.text: यथा सुरभिकुसु[मान्तर्भूतं] पारिजातं स्यात् । यदुक्तं सरस्वत्यापि च वक्तुं न शक्यत इति, [तत् साधु,] तयापि वाचकशब्दशक्तेरन्यथा कर्तृमशक्यत्वात् । तदेवं मार्गद्वयस्य प्रभेदाः यद्यपि प्रतिकवि स्थिता विद्यन्ते वस्तुतस्तथापि वक्तुमान[न्त्या]त्...... अतिप्रसङ्गाच्च न शक्यन्ते विशेषेण प्रत्येकम् । नैतावता न सन्त्येव । सामान्येन तु मार्गद्वयस्य वैलक्षण्यं दर्शितमेव व्यक्तम् । प्रतिव्यक्ति तु वक्तुं को नाम शक्नुयात् । सर्वत्रैव लक्षणशास्त्रे सर्वभेदव्यापि सामान्यलक्षणमुच्यते । न तु तद्भेदाः परिसंख्यायन्ते । अत्रापि सैव व्यवस्था काव्यलक्षणशास्त्रत्वादस्य । न तु यथोक्तं सामान्यं भेदलक्षणपरिस्फुटाभमनुसरद्भिरभियुक्तैस्ते भेदा मार्गद्वयसंभविनो विवेचयितुं शक्यन्ते । यथेदृशं नीलमीदृशं पीतमिति व्युत्पादिते
न भेदलक्षणेन व्यक्तमुभयसम्भविनः प्रतिभेदा यथादर्शनं विभज्यन्ते इत्यलं विस्तरेण ॥
children.translated_text: the sub-varieties possible in both [categories] are not clearly divided according to each observation by means of specific definitions. Enough of elaboration.

Just as there would be a <s>Pārijāta</s> (celestial tree) among fragrant flowers. What was said — that even <s>Sarasvatī</s> cannot articulate it — that is correct, since even she cannot alter the nature of the expressive power of words. Thus, although the varieties of the two paths [of style] exist in reality, established in each individual poet, nevertheless because of their infinity... and because of over-extension, they cannot be stated individually in detail. This does not mean they do not exist at all. The distinctiveness of the two paths has been clearly shown in general terms. But who indeed could state it for each individual instance? In every definitional science (<s>lakṣaṇaśāstra</s>), a general definition covering all varieties is stated; but the varieties themselves are not exhaustively enumerated. Here too the same procedure [applies], since this is a definitional science of poetry. But those varieties pertaining to the two paths cannot be discriminated by the competent who follow the general [definition] as though it were clearly marked with specific definitions — just as when one is taught "this is blue, this is yellow,"

children.text: सेयं काव्यलक्षणप्रयोजनस्वभावा काव्यगुणदोषविवेकरूपा व्युत्पत्तिर्यामभिसन्धाय क्रियाविधिं निबबन्धुः सूरयः, तस्य किं प्रयोजनमितीदानीमवसरं प्राप्य प्रयोजनं वर्ण्यन्नाह—
children.translated_text: This poetic training (<s>vyutpatti</s>), whose nature is the purpose of poetic definition and whose form is the discrimination of poetic merits and faults — for the prescriptive rule of [poetic] practice which the wise composed with this in view — what is its purpose? Now, having arrived at the appropriate occasion, stating the purpose, he says:

children.text: नैसर्गिकी च प्रतिभा श्रुतं च बहु निर्मलम् ।
children.translated_text: Innate talent (<s>pratibhā</s>), abundant and pure learning (<s>śruta</s>), /
and diligent application (<s>abhiyoga</s>) — these are the causes of poetic excellence. // 103 //

children.text: नैसर्गिकी स्वाभाविकी जन्मान्तराभ्यास[स]म्भविनी । सहजेति यावत् । प्रतिभा हेयोपादेयपरिच्छेदलक्षणा । सा च प्रकरणात् काव्यविषया । सहजा शक्तिरियम् । उत्पाद्यां दर्शयन्नाह—श्रुतं चेत्यादि । श्रुतं काव्याङ्गविद्याश्रवणं श्रुतमयं तच्च

व्याकरणक्रियाकल्पछन्दोविचित्याद्यनेकविद्याविषयत्वात्, अनेकशः प्रवृत्तत्वाच्च बहु पर्याप्तं निर्मलं परिशुद्धम्, आम्नायविशुद्ध्या सन्देहविपर्यासविरहात् । एवं श्रुतमयं ज्ञानं परिपूर्णमभिधाय चिन्तामयं भावनामयं च दर्शयन्नाह—अमन्दश्चाभियोग इति । श्रुतस्य चिन्तनमूहापोहमुखेन यथाम्नायमविपरीतार्थनिश्चयनम् । निश्चितस्य च भावनमभ्यासः आवृत्तिः स्थिरीकरणमिति द्विविधोऽभियोगः अभ्यासः । स चामन्दः पर्याप्तः यावद्भावितत्वात् । तदेतत्त्रयरूपा काव्यविषया व्यु[त्प]
children.translated_text: because it pertains to many disciplines — grammar, compositional technique, prosody, metrics, and the like — and because it proceeds in many [directions], is "abundant" (<s>bahu</s>), i.e., sufficient; "pure" (<s>nirmala</s>) means thoroughly clear, free from doubt and error through the purity of the [textual] tradition. Having thus described the knowledge born of learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>) in its completeness, showing the [knowledge] born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>) and meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>), he says: "and diligent application." Reflection on what has been learned — the ascertainment of the correct meaning through deliberation and counter-deliberation according to the tradition. And the cultivation, i.e., practice, i.e., repetition, i.e., stabilization, of what has been ascertained — thus application (<s>abhiyoga</s>) is of two kinds. And that is "not slack" (<s>amanda</s>), i.e., sufficient, because of thorough cultivation. This threefold [training] constitutes the poetic

children.text: त्तिः । एवं हि काव्यं व्युत्पन्नं भवति यदि तदङ्गं विद्यास्थानं श्रुतं चिन्तितं भावितं च यथावद् भवेत् । अन्यथा कीदृशी काव्यव्युत्पत्तिः सर्वत्रोपायव्युत्पत्तिलक्षणत्वादुपेयव्युत्पत्तेः । [तदृते चो]पेयव्युत्पत्तिरसूत्रपटात् न हीयते । अभिमानमात्रं तु विजृम्भताम् । कस्तस्य निषेद्धा ? तदेवंविधाः काव्यव्युत्पत्तिः कारणं काव्यसम्पदः काव्यरचनाया निरवद्यायाः हेतुः । अस्याः प्रस्तुताया यदर्था काव्यव्युत्पत्तिः । परकीयकाव्यपरिज्ञानं तु सुलभमेवेदृशीं काव्यव्युत्पत्तिमाश्रितवता । ततश्च कीर्तिलाभः सत्कारः अन्यो वा पुरुषार्थ इति गम्यत एव । वक्ष्यति च
children.translated_text: training. For poetry becomes well-trained when its ancillary disciplines have been properly learned, reflected upon, and cultivated. Otherwise, what kind of poetic training [would there be]? — since the training in the end (<s>upeya</s>) always has the character of training in the means (<s>upāya</s>). And without that, training in the end is no better than cloth without thread. But let mere conceit flourish — who can prevent it? Such poetic training is "the cause of poetic excellence" (<s>kāvyasampatti</s>), i.e., the cause of faultless poetic composition. "Of this" — of the [excellence] that is being discussed and for whose sake poetic training [exists]. The knowledge of others' poetry, however, comes easily to one who has resort to such training. And from that, the attainment of fame, honour, or other human goals — this is understood. He will also say:
"by those desiring fame"
and so on.

"Innate" (<s>naisargikī</s>) means natural, arising from practice in previous lives. "Inborn" — that is the sense. <s>Pratibhā</s> (talent) is characterized by the capacity to discriminate what is to be adopted and what rejected. And this, from the context, pertains to poetry. This is the inborn faculty. Showing the acquirable [faculty], he says: "learning" and so on. "Learning" (<s>śruta</s>) means the hearing of the ancillary sciences of poetry; and that

children.text: ननु केचिदेव सहजशक्तियुक्ताः । तत्किमिदानीं मा भूदन्येषामिह प्रवृत्तिः ? येनोच्यते नैसर्गिकी च प्रतिभेत्यत्र आह—
children.translated_text: But only some [people] are endowed with innate talent. Then should others have no engagement in this [pursuit]? In response to [the concern] expressed in "innate talent" — he says:
of prior impressions (<s>pūrvavāsanā</s>), does not exist [in someone],
Even if the wondrous talent, attended by the merits /
will surely bestow some measure of grace. // 104 //
speech, cultivated through learning and effort, /
by <s>Ācārya Śūra</s>
actions become second nature to people;
"Through the connection with practice, good and bad /
they perform such deeds as in a dream." //
and in another birth, without effort, /
<s>Pūrvavāsanā</s> (prior impressions) means the latent disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced by practice in previous lives, because of being connected with practice. As stated

children.text: पूर्वा चासौ पूर्वजन्मभावितत्वात्, वासना चेति विग्रहः । सैव गुणो विशेषः, सद्भिः स्तुतत्वात् ।
children.translated_text: "Prior" (<s>pūrva</s>) — it is so because of having been cultivated in previous lives — "and impressions" — thus the analysis. That itself is a "merit" (<s>guṇa</s>), i.e., a distinction, because it is praised by the good.

children.text: तस्या वा गुणः यथाप्रत्ययं प्रबोधः स्वानुरूपकार्यजननाभिमुखलक्षणो विशेषस्तं हेतुभावेन अनुबध्नाति, अपेक्षत इति पूर्ववासनागुणानुबन्धि । प्रतिभानं प्रज्ञा तच्च प्रकरणात् काव्यविषयकम् । अद्भुतमाश्चर्यं लोकस्य कथमीदृशं प्रतिभानं यथेति विस्मयजनकत्वाद् दुर्लभं वाद्भुतम् । नैसर्गिकी प्रतिभेति यावत् । यद्यपिन विद्यते येषां तैरपि काव्याभ्यासः करणीयः । एवं नासौ निष्फला भविष्यतीत्याह—श्रुतेनेत्यादि । श्रुतेन काव्याङ्गविद्याविषयेण श्रवणेन बहुना निर्मलेन । यथोक्तं प्राक् । यत्नेन चाभियोगेन अमन्देन यथोक्तं पूर्वम् । करणेन हेतुना पुरुषेणोपासिता समाराधिता अभ्यस्तेति यावत् । वाक् काव्याङ्गक्रियाकल्पादिविद्यालक्षणविशिष्टा अर्थात्प्रकरणाद्वा तदन्यथानुपपत्त्या काव्यसम्पदोऽर्थः सामर्थ्यम् । काव्यव्युत्पत्तिप्रस्तावः प्रकरणम् । यथोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: Or: the "merit" of that [prior impression] is the awakening according to its own nature — the distinction characterized by becoming inclined toward producing an effect corresponding to itself — it "attends" (<s>anubadhnāti</s>), i.e., requires as a cause. Hence "attended by the merits of prior impressions." <s>Pratibhāna</s> (talent) means insight, and from the context it pertains to poetry. "Wondrous" (<s>adbhuta</s>) means marvellous, causing wonder in the world — "How can there be such talent?" — or "wondrous" means rare, because of being hard to obtain. "Innate talent" — that is the sense. Even for those in whom it does not exist, the practice of poetry should still be undertaken. It will not be fruitless — he says: "through learning" and so on. "Through learning" (<s>śrutena</s>) — by hearing pertaining to the ancillary sciences of poetry, abundant and pure, as stated before. "And through effort" (<s>yatnena</s>) — through application that is not slack, as stated before. By this means, "speech" (<s>vāk</s>) — characterized by the ancillary sciences of poetry such as compositional technique and the like — when "cultivated" (<s>upāsitā</s>), i.e., worshipped, i.e., practised — the meaning of "poetic excellence" (<s>kāvyasampad</s>) is capacity [for poetry], from the context or from the impossibility of it being otherwise. The context is the discussion of poetic training. As stated:
"Meaning, context, indicator, the proximity of another word — /
these are the causes for determining the specific sense of words with general denotation." //

children.text: अपरन्यायो यथासम्भवमिह सर्वोऽनुसर्तव्यः सामान्योक्तिभूयस्त्वात् । कमपि कञ्चित् सहजशक्त्यविरहे यादृशं तत्कल्पमनुग्रहं काव्यरचनासाम[र्थ्यदान]लक्षणम् । ध्रुवमवश्यं करो
त्येव उपासितुः पुरुषस्य । नात्र सन्देहः । तस्मान्नैसर्गिकी प्रतिभा नास्ति ममेति नोपासितव्यैव सरस्वती । कामधेनुरवश्यमेवानुग्रहीष्यतीति [ध्येयम्] ॥
children.translated_text: bestow [this] upon the person who cultivates [speech]. There is no doubt in this. Therefore, one should not think "I do not have innate talent" and refuse to worship <s>Sarasvatī</s>. She will surely bestow her grace, like a wish-fulfilling cow — this should be contemplated.

Other principles too should be applied here as appropriate, since general statements predominate. "Some" (<s>kamapi</s>) — some measure of grace, in the absence of innate talent — of such a kind as approximates that [talent], characterized by the bestowal of capacity for poetic composition. "Surely" (<s>dhruvam</s>) — certainly — it will
through effort, by those desiring fame. //
Therefore, <s>Sarasvatī</s> must be worshipped untiringly, always, /
are able to participate in the assemblies of the learned. // 105 //
Even with meagre poetic talent, people who have made the effort /

children.text: यत एवं न निष्फलं वागुपासनं तत्तस्मात् कारणात् अस्ततन्द्रैरनलसो भूत्वा अनिशम् अनवरतम् अभियोगाविच्छेदात् क्रमात् श्रुतचिन्ताभावनाक्रमेण सम्प्रदायसाद्गुण्यार्थवर्तिना यथोक्तं प्राक् । उपास्या समाराध्या । अभ्यसनीया यावत्प्रसीदति । यथोक्त

children.translated_text: by <s>Ācārya Mātṛceṭa</s>

Since thus the cultivation of speech is not fruitless, therefore — "untiringly" (<s>astatandra</s>), i.e., having become unslothful; "always" (<s>aniśam</s>), i.e., unceasingly, due to the continuity of application, gradually, through the stages of hearing, reflection, and cultivation, with a practice that upholds the goodness of the tradition, as stated before — "she is to be worshipped" (<s>upāsyā</s>), i.e., to be reverently approached, to be practised until she is pleased. As stated
then through exertion the cultivation [of that ground] is accomplished.
"First, after study, only the fallow ground is broken; /
and the sprout, nourished by the limb of deliberation, grows.
Then the seed born of one's own reflection is sown, /
by those of firm conviction, sufficient in method." //
Then the excellent crop of [the goddess's] grace is obtained /

children.text: सरस्वती काव्याङ्गविद्यालक्षणा प्रकरणादेर्यथोक्तं प्राक् । खलु [ऐ]कान्तेन असंशयम् वा । कीर्तिः परिशुद्धकाव्यक्रियालक्षणा पूर्वोक्ता, काव्यसम्पदः एकान्तेन कीर्तिहेतुत्वात् । आवर्तते स एवार्थः पुनरर्थान्तराश्रयादिति न्यायात् । तत्सम्भवा ख्यातिर्वा, गुणेभ्य एव प्रभवन्ति कीर्तय इति वचनात् । तामनश्वरीं सत्पुरुषतनुमशेषजनसुभगां व्यापिनीं गुणाधिराजवैजयन्तीमीप्सुभि[रवाप्तु]कामैः पु
रुषैः । उपास्येति प्रकृतम् । तथा लाभसत्कारादिकमपि द्रष्टव्यम् । न तु [सा वासना] मम नास्तीति आलस्यमालम्बनीयं तस्यानर्थहेतुत्वात् । यथोक्त
children.translated_text: "Is to be worshipped" — this is the main [verb]. Similarly, gain, honour, and the like should also be understood [as motivations]. One should not adopt laziness [thinking] "I do not have that disposition" — since laziness is the cause of misfortune. As stated
by <s>Ācārya Aśvaghoṣa</s>

<s>Sarasvatī</s> — characterized as the ancillary sciences of poetry, from the context and as stated before. "Indeed" (<s>khalu</s>) — certainly, or: without doubt. "Fame" (<s>kīrti</s>) — characterized by the creation of pure poetry, as mentioned before — "of poetic excellence" — since fame is invariably caused by [poetic excellence]. The same meaning recurs because it is grounded in a different aspect — thus the principle. Or: the renown that arises from it, since "fame originates from virtues alone" — as the saying goes. That [fame] which is imperishable, which is the body of the virtuous, which is delightful to all people, which is all-pervading, which is the victory-banner of the king of virtues — "by those desiring" (<s>īpsubhiḥ</s>), i.e., by persons wishing to obtain [it].
What learned person here would not become a lord of wealth?
"If laziness did not exist in the world, what misfortune [would there be]? /
filled with man-beasts and the impoverished!"
This earth with its oceans is a forest of laziness, /

children.text: अथ कथञ्चित् स्वयं काव्यक्रियालसश्चेतत् तादृशः तथापि परकाव्यकोविदः स्वयं च किञ्चित्करः तद्विदामादेयो भविष्यतीति सर्वथावैफल्यपरिहारमाह—कृश इत्यादि । कवित्वे स्वयं काव्यकरणे कृशे मन्देऽपि सति सर्गबन्धाद्यनिर्वहणात् । कृशे वा असति कवित्वेऽपि मुक्तकादेरपि अकरणात् । तथापि दर्शनात् । भिन्ना हि शक्तिः पुंसाम् । यथोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: Now, if someone is somehow lazy in poetic creation himself — even such a person, if he is skilled in the poetry of others and himself creates something, will be valued by connoisseurs — thus stating the avoidance of complete futility, he says: "meagre" and so on. "In poetic talent" — in the making of poetry oneself — even if "meagre," i.e., slight, due to inability to sustain a composition of cantos and the like; or: even in the absence of poetic talent, even being unable to compose even standalone verses. Nevertheless, [this is justified] by observation. For the faculties of people are diverse. As stated:
yet another to do both, and one is skilled in judging.
"One person is able to compose, another only to listen; /
one produces gold from a stone, another is capable of testing it." //
The congregation of supreme qualities does not occur in one person — /

children.text: कृतश्रमा यथाविधानमुपासितवाचो जनाः पुरुषाः कृतोऽनुष्ठितः श्रमः श्रवणादिलक्षणो व्यवहारो यैरिति
children.translated_text: "People who have made the effort" — those who have cultivated speech as prescribed, i.e., persons in whom the effort (<s>śrama</s>) characterized by hearing and the like has been accomplished — thus

children.translated_text: the analysis — because of being skilled in the poetry of others. "Are able to participate in the assemblies of the learned." children.text: ते चाद्यापि विकल्प्यन्ते कस्तान् कार्त्स्न्येन वक्ष्यति ॥ १ ॥
children.translated_text: They are being classified even to this day — who shall describe them in their entirety? (1)

children.text: काव्यस्य पद्यगद्यमिश्रात्मकस्य यथोक्तस्य शोभां सौन्दर्यं कुर्वन्ति ये धर्मा गुणास्तान् । अनुवादोऽयम् । अलङ्कारान् प्रचक्षते कथयन्ति । तद्विद इति विधिः । ये केचित् काव्यशोभाकरा विशेषास्ते अलङ्कारा विज्ञेया इति यावत् । अलंक्रियते शोभां नीयते काव्यमेभिः शरीरनिष्ठहारादिभिरित्यलङ्काराः । एवंलक्षणा अलङ्काराः, कियन्तस्त इत्याह—ते चेत्यादि । ते चालङ्काराः किमपि दीर्घं कालमारभ्याद्यापि इदानीं यावद्विकल्प्यन्ते प्रभिद्यन्ते, अभियुक्तैरयमयमिति प्रतिपुरुषमपरापरोक्तिविशेषानिवृत्तेः, न त्वियत्ता लभ्यते । ततश्च तानेवमनन्तालङ्कारान् कार्त्स्न्येन लक्षितान् कृत्स्नान् को नाम पुरुषोऽर्वाग्दर्शी इदानीन्तनदर्शी वक्ष्यति वक्तुं शक्नुयात् । नैव निरवशेषमभिधातुमीदृशः कश्चिदीष्ट इत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: The qualities that produce the beauty, the loveliness, of <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) — whether consisting of verse, prose, or a mixture, as previously described — those qualities are referred to. This is a restatement. They are called <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) — so say the knowers of that subject. This means that whatever special features produce the beauty of poetry are to be understood as <s>alaṅkāras</s>. Poetry is adorned, brought to beauty, by these — like necklaces and other ornaments that belong to the body — hence they are <s>alaṅkāras</s>. Having such a definition, how many are they? He says 'te ca' and so forth. These <s>alaṅkāras</s>, from some long time past up to the present day, are being classified, differentiated, by the skilled — 'this one is this, that one is that' — because novel expressions by different authorities remain unceasing, and no fixed number can be obtained. Therefore, who — any person of limited vision, of present-day perspective — could describe all these infinite <s>alaṅkāras</s> in their entirety, having fully defined them? The meaning is that no such person capable of describing them exhaustively is found.

children.text: यद्येवमानन्त्यात् कार्त्स्न्ये न वक्तुं न शक्यन्ते, किमिदानीं क्रियतामित्याह—
children.translated_text: If this is so — if due to their infinity they cannot be described in their entirety — then what should be done now? He says —

children.translated_text: However, the seed of their varieties has been shown by the earlier <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers).
This effort of ours is to refine that very [teaching]. (2)

children.text: किं त्वपि त्वित्यर्थान्तरविवक्षायां तदाह—बीजमित्यादि । विकल्पानामलङ्कारप्रभेदानां जात्युपमारूपकादीनां बीजं प्रतिनियतं सकलव्यक्तिव्यापि सामान्यं रूपम् । यतः प्रभेदा विविधास्तदनुसृताः प्रवर्तन्ते । पूर्वाचार्यैश्चिरन्तनैः काव्यलक्षणकारैः मेधाविश्यामवादि[प्रभृति]भिः प्रदर्शितम् निर्दिष्टं यत्तदेव नान्यत् । प्रतिसंस्कर्तुं संक्षेपेण
परिस्फुटं यथावदभिधातुमयं प्रकृतः अस्माकं परिश्रमो यत्नो वर्तते, नतु सर्वमलङ्कारमभिधातुम् । आनन्त्यादशक्तेश्च । किं तु परिमिताः केचिदलङ्काराः पूर्वाचार्योपदिष्टाः प्रतिसंस्क्रियन्ते । तथा च वक्ष्यति—

Rather, certain limited <s>alaṅkāras</s> taught by the earlier masters are being refined. And he will state later —
This path has been laid open through measured practice,
condensing the endless expanse of embellishments.
And so forth.

'<s>Kiṃ tu</s>' (however) means 'api tu' (nevertheless), expressing a different intent. He says 'bījam' and so forth. The seed of the varieties — the divisions of <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>jāti</s> (genre), <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), and so on — is the invariably fixed, universally pervading generic form. From which the manifold divisions proceed in accordance with it. By the earlier <s>ācāryas</s>, the ancient authors of treatises on poetic definition, beginning with <s>Medhāvin</s>, <s>Śyāmavādin</s>, and others, it has been shown, indicated — that very thing and nothing else. To refine it — to state it concisely,

children.text: पूर्वं श्लेषादयः शब्दालङ्कारा मार्गनियताः कथिताः । इदानीं सर्वमार्गसाधारणा अलंकारा उच्यन्त इति दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Previously, <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) and other word-ornaments specific to particular styles were described. Now, ornaments common to all styles are being discussed — showing this, he says —
Certain embellishments were stated earlier for the purpose of classifying the styles.
The remaining class of <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), which is common [to all styles], is now being examined. (3)

children.text: काश्चिदलंक्रियाः केचिदलङ्काराः श्लेषप्रसादादयः न सर्वाः, प्रागपि प्रथमे परिच्छेदेऽपि उक्ताः श्लिष्टा[दयः] न केवलमिदानीमुच्यन्ते । प्राक् किमर्थमुक्ता इत्याह—मार्गविभागार्थमिति । मार्गयार्वैदर्भगौड़ीययोर्विभागो विवेकः उक्तलक्षणः अर्थः प्रयोजनं यस्मिन् वचन इति क्रियाविशेषणम् । श्लेषादिषु हि कथितेषु तत्स्वभावो वैदर्भमार्गः प्रतीयते । तद्विपर्ययस्वभावश्च गोड़ीय इति श्लेषाद्यलङ्कारवचनात् मार्गविभागो जायते । नान्ययेति श्लेषादिववनं मार्गविभागार्थं सम्पद्यते । किमिदानों वाच्यमित्याह—साधारणमित्यादि । वैदर्भादिषु सर्वमार्गेषु साधारणं सामान्यं न प्रागिवासाधारणम् । अलङ्कारजातम् अर्थालङ्कारवृन्दम् अन्यत् इदानीं निरूप्यते शिष्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Certain embellishments, certain <s>alaṅkāras</s> such as <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), and so on — not all of them — were stated earlier, in the first chapter too. <s>Śliṣṭa</s> and the rest were [stated] not only now but also before. For what purpose were they stated before? He says 'mārgavibhāgārtham' (for the purpose of classifying styles). The distinguishing, the discernment of the two styles — <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> — described with the stated characteristics, is the purpose of that statement — this is an adverbial qualifier of the verbal action. For when <s>śleṣa</s> and the rest are described, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style, whose nature consists of those [qualities], is understood; and the <s>Gauḍīya</s>, whose nature is the opposite, is also understood. Thus from the statement of <s>śleṣa</s> and other <s>alaṅkāras</s>, the classification of styles arises — not from anything else. So the statement of <s>śleṣa</s> and the rest serves the purpose of style classification. What is to be stated now? He says 'sādhāraṇam' and so forth. Common to all styles — <s>Vaidarbha</s> and the rest — that is, general, not restricted [to one style] as before. The class of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, the collection of <s>arthālaṅkāras</s> (figures of sense), the remaining one, is now being examined, taught.
Intending to enumerate the <s>alaṅkāras</s> in their order of listing, he first lists them —
<s>Svabhāvākhyāna</s> (description of natural form), <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>āvṛtti</s> (repetition),
<s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic fancy), (4)

<s>samāsa</s> (condensed expression), <s>atiśaya</s> (hyperbole), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic imagination), <s>hetu</s> (cause), <s>sūkṣma</s> (the subtle), <s>lava</s> (a portion), <s>krama</s> (sequence),
<s>preyas</s> (the endearing), <s>rasavat</s> (possessing <s>rasa</s>), <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous), <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution), <s>samāhita</s> (the composed), (5)
<s>udātta</s> (the exalted), <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment), <s>śliṣṭa</s> (the closely joined), <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal pairing),
<s>virodha</s> (contradiction), <s>aprastutastotra</s> (praise of the irrelevant), <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), <s>nidarśana</s> (illustration), (6)
<s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression), <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), <s>āśīḥ</s> (benediction), <s>saṃkīrṇa</s> (the mixed), and then <s>bhāvika</s> (the suggestive).
These <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) of speech are remembered by the earlier masters. (7)

children.text: दीपकमावृतिरावृत्तिश्च औणादिक इकारः । समासश्च समासोक्तिः । अतिशयश्च अतिशयोक्तिः उत्प्रेक्षा च । उदात्तम्, अपह्नुतिः, श्लिष्टम्, विशेषश्च । विरोधोऽप्रस्तुत स्तोत्रं च । व्याजस्तुतिः निदर्शनं च, परिवृत्तिराशीः संकीर्णं च । अथ भाविकं च इत्येते यथोक्ताः अलङ्काराः उक्तलक्षणाः स्मर्यन्ते आम्नायन्ते पूर्वसूरिभिः आद्यैराचार्यैः रामशर्मादिभिः काव्यालङ्कारकारैः । कस्येत्याह—वाचामिति । काव्यानां सम्बन्धिनः ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpaka</s> and <s>āvṛti</s> — <s>āvṛtti</s> has the Uṇādi suffix '-ika'. <s>Samāsa</s> means <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). <s>Atiśaya</s> means <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic imagination). <s>Udātta</s> (the exalted), <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment), <s>śliṣṭa</s> (closely joined), and <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction). <s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) and <s>aprastutastotra</s> (praise of the irrelevant). <s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) and <s>nidarśana</s> (illustration). <s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange), <s>āśīḥ</s> (benediction), <s>saṃkīrṇa</s> (the mixed), and then <s>bhāvika</s> (the suggestive). These <s>alaṅkāras</s>, as stated, having the described characteristics, are remembered — that is, handed down — by the earlier masters, the first teachers, the authors of works on poetic ornamentation beginning with <s>Rāmaśarman</s> and others. Of what? He says 'vācām' (of speech) — pertaining to <s>kāvya</s> (poetry).
Therein, illustrating <s>svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form) first, he says —
Presenting directly the form of things in their various states,
[this figure] called <s>svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form) or <s>jāti</s> (genre) is the first ornament, as follows: (8)

children.text: पदार्थानां वस्तूनां जातिक्रियागुणद्रव्याणां रूपं स्वभावम् । किंविशिष्टम् ? नानावस्थं नाना विचित्रा न त्वेकैव काचित्, अवस्था दशा यस्य तादृशमनेकप्रकारं साक्षात् अञ्जसा अभिधानव्यापारेण न तु सामर्थ्यात् । विवृण्वती प्रकाशयन्ती सती या प्रवर्तते सा तादृश्यलंकृ

तिः । आद्या प्रथमा अलङ्कारेष्विह स्वभावोक्तिर्नाम वेदितव्या, जातिर्नाम वा । अनेन संज्ञाद्वयेन अयमलङ्कारो व्यवह्नियते । स्वभावं पदार्थानां विचित्रं वक्तीति स्वभावोक्तिः । जातेः पदार्थस्वरूपस्य तथा तथा प्रतिपादकत्वेन तादर्थ्याज्जातिः । यथेत्युदाहरति । यथेदं तथान्यदपि तादृशं सर्वमेव द्रष्टव्यम् । न त्विदमेवेत्यर्थः । एवमुत्तरत्राप्यनुगन्तव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: That which presents, makes manifest [things in this way], and proceeds in this manner — such an ornament is to be understood as the first among the <s>alaṅkāras</s>, called <s>svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form), or alternatively called <s>jāti</s> (genre). By these two designations this <s>alaṅkāra</s> is known. It describes the varied essential nature of things — hence <s>svabhāvokti</s>. Because it serves to present the natural form of things in various ways — hence, by virtue of that purpose, [it is called] <s>jāti</s>. 'Yathā' (as follows) introduces an example. As this [example shows], so too should all other similar instances be understood. The meaning is: not only this one. This principle should be followed in the subsequent [discussions] as well.

The form — the essential nature — of things, of entities, namely <s>jāti</s> (class), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>dravya</s> (substance). Of what kind? In various states — that is, the states are manifold and diverse, not just one single condition — such a multifaceted [nature], directly, straightforwardly, through the operation of denotation, not through implication.
With beaks that are reddish and curved, with wings that are green and tender,
with throats marked by three-colored stripes — these are the sweet-voiced parrots. (9)

children.text: एते प्रत्यक्षवर्तिनः शुकाः तुण्डैः चञ्चुभिः आताम्रैः लोहितैः, कुटिलैः वक्रैश्च, पक्षैश्च हरितवर्णैः, कोमलैः मृदुभिः कण्ठैश्च, त्रिभिर्वर्णैः सितासितलोहितैः राजिभिः लक्षिताः । मञ्जर्मधुरा गीः शब्दो येषां ते मञ्जुगिरः । इयं शुकजातेः पदार्थस्य विचित्रं स्वरूपं वक्तीति जातिस्वभावोक्तिरीदृशी द्रष्टव्या ॥
children.translated_text: These parrots, [seen] before one's eyes, [are characterized] by beaks — bills — that are reddish, crimson, and curved, bent; by wings that are green-colored and tender, soft; and by throats marked by stripes of three colors — white, dark, and red. Those whose cry, whose sound, is sweet — they are the sweet-voiced ones. This describes the varied essential nature of the parrot species as an entity — thus this type of <s>jāti-svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form pertaining to class) should be understood.

children.text: विशालाः श्रोणिषु क्षामा मध्ये दीर्घा विलोचने ।
children.translated_text: Broad at the hips, slender at the waist, with large eyes,
with full, prominent breasts — those beautiful women of excellence.
This is another example.
Illustrating <s>kriyā-svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form pertaining to action), he says —
With a throat containing soft cooing sounds, with rolling eyes,
the pigeon, circling around, desirous of mating, kisses his beloved. (10)

children.text: पारावतः प्रियां पारावतीं चुम्बति रिरंसू रन्तुकामः परिक्षिप्य परिभ्रम्य कलमव्यक्तमधुरं क्वणितं शब्दो गर्भोऽन्तर्वर्ती यस्मिन् तेन कण्ठेन लक्षितः । आधूणिते भ्रमिते ईक्षणे नेत्रे यस्य स तथा । इह क्वणनाघूर्णनादेः क्रियापदार्थस्य स्वभावः प्रकाश्यत इति क्रियास्वभावोक्तिरेवंविधा विज्ञेयेति ।
children.translated_text: The pigeon kisses his beloved, the female pigeon, being desirous of mating, having circled around her, characterized by a throat in which there is a soft, indistinct, sweet cooing sound — the sound — contained within. His eyes, his gaze, whirls, rolls. Here, the essential nature of the action-entity — the cooing, the rolling [of eyes], and so forth — is being revealed; thus <s>kriyā-svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form pertaining to action) of this type should be understood.
She trembles, she sighs, she yearns, she gazes intently, she weeps,
she is frightened, she draws back her own limbs — such is a young woman at her first union.
This is another example.
Illustrating <s>guṇa-svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural form pertaining to quality), he says —
Producing goosebumps on the limbs, creating bliss in the mind,
and even causing the eyes to close — the touch of the beloved proceeds thus. (11)

children.text: प्रियायाः प्रणयिन्याः स्पर्शो गुणः पृथिव्यादिभूताश्रयत्वात् । स प्रवर्तते । कथम् ? अङ्गेषु प्रियस्य गात्रेषु रोमाञ्चं रोमहर्षं बध्नन् उत्पादयन् मनस्यन्तरात्मनि निर्वृतिं कुर्वन्नानन्दममन्दं सन्दधानः । नेत्रे च प्रियतमस्य दृशौ हर्षभरसञ्चरे आमीलयन् मुकुलयन्नेव । एष इत्यपि पाठः । प्रवर्ततामिति प्रकृतम् । अत्र स्पर्शाख्यस्य गुणपदार्थस्य स्वरूपं रोमाञ्चादि विचित्रं

children.translated_text: accomplished — thus this is <s>guṇa-svabhāvokti</s> (natural description of quality), and it should be followed as having this form.

The touch of the beloved, the affectionate one, is a <s>guṇa</s> (quality), because it resides in the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) such as earth and so forth. It manifests. How? Binding — that is, producing — <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation) on the limbs, the body of the beloved, and creating in the mind, in the inner self, abundant bliss — bestowing joy that is not slight. And causing the eyes of the most beloved to close — to shut like buds — through the rush of delight. The reading 'eṣa' is also found. 'Let it manifest' is the subject under discussion. Here, the natural form of the category of quality called touch, namely the variety of horripilation and so forth, is
The rolling of the eyes, speech stumbling with passion, on the cheeks —

children.text: मदः करोति नारीणां भ्रुवोर्वल्गु च वल्गितम् ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Mada</s> (intoxication) produces in women a charming play of the eyebrows.
This is another illustration.
He illustrates <s>dravya-svabhāvokti</s> (natural description of substance) —
With darkness at the throat, with a skull in hand, with the moon as crest-jewel,
with matted locks moist and coppery, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (the Bull-bannered one) appeared. [verse 12]

children.text: वृषध्वजः शङ्करः आविरासीत् प्रकाशीबभूव । कण्ठे कालः कालकूटलक्षणो यस्य कण्ठेकालो वा सप्तम्या अलुक् । इन्दुरर्धचन्द्रः शेखर उत्तंसो यस्य । करस्थेन हस्तवर्तिना कपालेन भिक्षापात्रेण स्निग्धाभिरपरुषाभिस्ताम्राभिः पाटलाभिर्जटाभिश्च लक्षित इति योज्यम् । शङ्कराख्यस्य द्रव्यस्य नानाप्रकारं स्वरूपमिंहोपवर्णितमिति द्रव्यपदार्थस्वभावोक्तिरित्थम्भूता बोद्धव्येति ।
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> means <s>Śaṅkara</s>; 'appeared' means became manifest. 'Darkness at the throat' — one who has <s>kālakūṭa</s> (poison) characterized as 'kāla' at his throat, or alternatively the seventh case ending remains undropped (i.e., <s>aluk samāsa</s>). 'Moon' means the half-moon; '<s>śekhara</s>' means ornament — one who has that as his crest. 'With a skull held in hand' means with a begging-bowl; 'with matted locks that are smooth — not rough — and coppery, that is, pinkish' — the word 'distinguished by' should be supplied. The various aspects of the natural form of the substance called <s>Śaṅkara</s> are described here — thus <s>dravya-padārtha-svabhāvokti</s> (natural description of the substance category) should be understood as being of this kind.
With drops of sweat, with bristling hair standing on end, trembling and agitated —
upon seeing him, each limb of that woman with arched brows became thus.
This is another illustration.
Having thus set forth <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), concluding, he says —
Such is the description of the nature of <s>jāti</s> (universal/class), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>dravya</s> (substance).
In the <s>śāstras</s> (sciences/treatises) this alone holds sovereignty; in <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) too this is desired. [verse 13]

children.text: जातिः क्रिया गुणो द्रव्यं च तेषां स्वभावो लक्षणं नानावस्थस्तस्याख्यानमाख्यायतेऽनेनेतीदृशमेवंजातीयं द्रष्टव्यमिति शेषः । क्वास्य विनियोग इत्याह—शास्त्रेष्वित्यादि । शास्त्रेषु आन्वीक्षिंक्यादिषु विद्यास्थानेषु । अस्यैव स्वभावाख्यानस्यालङ्कारस्य नान्यस्योपमादेः साम्राज्यं प्राधान्यम्, तस्यैव तत्र प्रायः प्रयोगात् । काव्येष्वपि सर्गबन्धादिष्वेतत् स्वभावाख्यानमीप्सितमिष्टम्, तत्रापि यथावसरं प्रयुक्तस्य शोभाकरत्वात् । अपिशब्दान्न केवलं शास्त्रेष्वित्याचष्टे ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> (universal), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>dravya</s> (substance) — the nature, that is, the characteristic and various states of these — their description, meaning 'that by which they are described,' is of this kind, of this sort — the remainder being 'it should be understood thus.' Where is its application? To this he says — 'in the <s>śāstras</s>' and so forth. In the <s>śāstras</s> means in the branches of knowledge such as <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (logic/philosophy) and the rest. Of this alone — of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) called description of nature, and not of any other such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) — there is sovereignty, that is, predominance, because it is mostly employed there. In <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) too — in compositions such as <s>sargabandha</s> (cantos) and the rest — this description of nature is desired, that is, wished for, because when employed at the appropriate occasion there too, it produces beauty. The word 'api' (also) indicates 'not only in the <s>śāstras</s>.'
Because <s>upamā</s> (simile) was listed immediately after <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), expounding <s>upamā</s> immediately after the exposition of that, he says —
Wherever a resemblance, arisen in whatever manner, is perceived —

children.text: उपमा नाम सा तस्याः प्रपञ्चोऽयं प्रदर्श्यते ॥ १४ ॥
children.translated_text: that is called <s>upamā</s> (simile); its elaboration is now demonstrated. [verse 14]

children.text: एवमुत्तरत्राप्यनुसर्तव्यम् । यत्र विषये सादृश्यं पदार्थयोः कयोश्चित्साम्यं यथाकथञ्चित् येन केनचित् प्रकारेण, गुणादिना सर्वथा साम्यस्य दुर्लभत्वात् । तत्त्वे[चैक्य]-
प्रसङ्गात् । प्रतीयते गम्यते शब्दादर्थतो वा यथासम्भवम् । ननु रूपकेऽपि सादृश्यं प्रतीयत इति लक्षणसंकर इति चेदाह—उद्भूतमिति । व्यक्तम्, भेदस्य परिस्फुटत्वादुपमानोपमे
children.translated_text: identity. 'Is perceived' means is apprehended — either through words or through meaning, as the case may be. Now, if one objects that resemblance is perceived in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) too, and hence there is a confusion of definitions, he says — 'arisen' (udbhūta). That means 'manifest,' because the distinction between <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object compared) is

children.text: ययोः । रूपके तु तत्त्वारोप इत्यसङ्करः । अत एव वक्ष्यति—
children.translated_text: clearly apparent in both. In <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), however, there is superimposition of identity — hence there is no confusion. For this very reason he will say later —
<s>Upamā</s> (simile) itself, when the distinction is concealed, is considered to be <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).

children.text: इति । सा सादृश्योक्तिरुपमानामालंक्रिया वेदितव्या । उपमितिः साधर्म्यकथनमुपमेति कृत्वा । तस्या एवंलक्षणायाः अयं प्रस्तुतः प्रपञ्चः विचित्रः प्रभेदः प्रदर्श्यते उदाह्रियते ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, that expression of resemblance should be understood as the <s>alaṅkriyā</s> (figure of speech) called <s>upamā</s>. <s>Upamiti</s> means the statement of common properties — this is the etymological derivation of <s>upamā</s>. Of that figure thus defined, this present elaboration — the varied classification — is demonstrated, that is, illustrated.

This pattern should be followed in what follows as well. 'Wherever' means in whatever subject matter; 'resemblance' means the similarity of any two objects; 'in whatever manner' means by whatever mode — through quality and so forth, since complete similarity in all respects is rare. For in that case there would be the problem of
Your palm, O innocent one, is reddish like a lotus —
this is <s>dharmopamā</s> (simile through attribute), because of the direct indication of a common attribute. [verse 15]

children.text: मुग्धे बाले ! प्रियामन्त्रण[मेतत् ।] तव करतलं हस्तोपरिभागः आताम्रमरुणम् । किमिव ? अम्भोरुहमिव कमलमिव इतीयमेवंजातीया धर्मोपमा ज्ञेया । कुतः ? करतलाम्भोरुहयोर्द्वयोः समानस्य धर्मस्य गुणस्याताम्रलक्षणस्य निदर्शनात् प्रतिपादनात् कारणात् । कथम् ? साक्षाद्वाचकव्यापारेणाताम्रपदप्रयोगात्, न त्वर्थात् । ततः शब्दोपात्तत्वात् साधारणस्य धर्मस्य । तेनैवेयं व्यपदिश्यते नान्यथा, तथा विवक्षितत्वात् ॥
children.translated_text: 'O innocent one' — O young woman! This is a term of address to a beloved. Your palm, the upper part of the hand, is reddish. Like what? Like a lotus — like a <s>ambhoruha</s>. A simile of this kind should be known as <s>dharmopamā</s> (simile through attribute). Why? Because of the indication, that is, the demonstration — the reason being — of a common <s>dharma</s> (attribute), a quality characterized as redness, belonging to both the palm and the lotus. How? Directly, through the function of an explicit word, through the use of the word 'reddish' — not through implication. Therefore, because the common attribute is verbally expressed, it is designated by that very name and not otherwise, since that is what is intended.

children.text: राजीवमिव ते वक्त्रं नेत्रे नीलोत्पले इव ।
children.translated_text: Your face is like a <s>rājīva</s> (lotus), your eyes are like blue lotuses —
this is indeed <s>vastūpamā</s> (simile through substance), where the common attribute is only implied. [verse 16]

children.text: ते तव वक्त्रं मुखं राजीवमिव पद्ममिव, नेत्रे चक्षुषी नीलोत्पले इवेति एवंविधा या सा वस्तूपमैव । धर्मिण एव साक्षादादानात् । तेनैवं व्यपदिश्यते । न धर्मेण तस्य साक्षादग्रहणात् । कथं तर्हि तदवसाय इत्याह—प्रतीयमानेत्यादि । प्रतीयमानस्य उपात्तस्य वस्तुनो राजीवादेस्तदव्यभिचारादर्थाद् गम्यमान एकः समानो धर्मः कान्त्यादिलक्षणो गुणो यस्याः । सेयमीदृशी वस्तूपमेति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: Your face, your countenance, is like a <s>rājīva</s>, like a lotus; your eyes, your orbs of sight, are like blue lotuses — a simile of this kind is indeed <s>vastūpamā</s> (simile through substance). Because only the objects themselves are directly taken up. Hence it is designated thus — not through an attribute, since that is not directly grasped. How then is it ascertained? To this he says — 'implied' and so forth. One common attribute — a quality characterized by lustre and the like — which is implied, that is, understood from the meaning, through its invariable association with the substance mentioned such as the lotus, and which belongs to the object taken up — this is of such a nature, and this is what is meant by <s>vastūpamā</s> (simile through substance).
The lotus bloomed as if it were your face —
this, due to the reversal of the conventional order, is considered <s>viparyāsopamā</s> (reversed simile). [verse 17]

children.text: उन्निद्रं विकसितमरविन्दं पद्मं तवाननं मुखमिवाभूत् । ईदृशी या सादृश्योक्तिः सा विपर्यासोपमेष्यते कविभिः । पद्ममुपमानमुपमेयं मुखमिति या प्रसिद्धिः निरुढिस्तस्याः विपर्यासाद् वैपरीत्यात् कारणात् । पद्मस्योपमेयीकरणात् वक्त्रस्योपमानीकृतेः ततो विपर्यासोपमैवेदृशी द्रष्टव्या । कान्त्यादिविशेषश्चाननम्यात्र कश्चिद् विवक्षित इति गम्यते । अन्यथा किं विपर्यासेनेति ॥
children.translated_text: The bloomed — that is, fully opened — lotus became as if it were your face, your countenance. Such an expression of resemblance is considered by poets to be <s>viparyāsopamā</s> (reversed simile). The established convention that the lotus is the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and the face is the <s>upameya</s> (object compared) — because of the reversal, the inversion of that convention, as the reason. Because the lotus is made the object of comparison and the face is made the standard of comparison — therefore such a reversed simile should be understood. And some particular excellence of lustre and the like in the face is here understood to be intended. Otherwise, what would be the point of the reversal?
The lotus is like your face, your face is like a lotus —
this is <s>anyonyopamā</s> (mutual simile), proclaiming the excellence of each in relation to the other. [verse 18]

children.text: तवाननमिवाम्भोजं पद्मम् । अम्भोजमिव ते तव मुखमिति । एवं जातीया अन्योन्योपमेष्यते । अन्योन्यस्य परस्परस्य मुखस्याम्भोजस्य चान्योन्येन तेनैव द्वयेन उपमानात् साम्यकथनात् । सा चेयमन्योन्यस्य मुखस्याम्भोजस्य चोत्कर्षं विशेषं कान्त्यादिलक्षणं शंसति प्रकाशयति । अन्योन्येनैवेतद् द्वयं समानं
नान्येन केनचिदिति द्वयोरतिशयः कश्चिदवसीयत इति । अनेन
children.translated_text: and not by anything else — thus some surpassing quality of the two is ascertained. By this means,
where the roles of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object compared) alternate —
that is called <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile), as described.
Thus the <s>upameyopamā</s> accepted by other authorities is here subsumed under <s>upamā</s> (simile) as a separate category.

Your face is like a lotus. The lotus is like your face — a simile of this kind is considered <s>anyonyopamā</s> (mutual simile). Because of the mutual comparison — the statement of similarity of the face and the lotus with each other, by means of that very pair — this proclaims the excellence, the distinction characterized by lustre and the like, of each — the face and the lotus — in relation to the other. By each other alone is this pair equal,
Your face is comparable only to a lotus, and to nothing else —
this, because of the exclusion of similarity with anything else, is <s>niyamopamā</s> (restrictive simile). [verse 19]

children.text: तव मुखं कमलेनैव तुल्यम् । नान्येन केनचित् कमलव्यतिरिक्तेन वस्तुनेति । एवंविधा या सादृश्योक्तिः सेयं नियमोपमा कथ्यते । नियमस्य साक्षादुपादानात् । यदाह—अन्यसाम्यव्यावृत्तेरिति । कमलादन्येन केनचिद्वस्तुना साम्यस्य सादृश्यस्य व्यावृत्तेर्व्यवच्छेदात् कारणात् । तेनैव च नियमेन व्यपदिश्यते, नान्यथेति ॥
children.translated_text: Your face is comparable only to a lotus — and to no other thing apart from the lotus. An expression of resemblance of this kind is called <s>niyamopamā</s> (restrictive simile). Because the restriction is directly expressed. As he states — 'because of the exclusion of similarity with anything else.' Because of the exclusion, the delimitation, of similarity, of resemblance, with any object other than the lotus — that being the reason. And it is designated by that very restriction and not otherwise.
A lotus at least matches your face, and if there is anything else of that kind,
let it be so — this is <s>aniyamopamā</s> (non-restrictive simile). [verse 20]

children.text: तव मुखं कतृ पद्मं कर्मभूतम् । अन्वेत्यनुगच्छति पद्मेन तुल्यं तावत् । एतन्निश्चितम् । वाचोयुक्तौ वा । अन्यच्चापरमपि किञ्चिद्वस्तु तादृशं पद्मसमम् । तत्कारि त्वन्मुखान्वयकारि त्वदाननस्योपमानमस्ति चेत् यदि भवेत्, अस्तु भवतु न वार्यत इति एवंरूपा यासौ तादृशी अनियमोपमा स्मर्यते तज्ज्ञैः । पद्मेनैव तुल्यमित्यस्य नियमस्यानपेक्षणात्, अन्यस्यापि तादृशस्याभ्यनुज्ञानादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Your face is the agent, the lotus the object. It 'follows' — it matches — the lotus, at least. This much is certain. Or this is merely a manner of speaking. And if any other thing too, of such a kind, equal to the lotus, were to exist somewhere — if it should be the means of comparison to your face, let it be, it is not prohibited. Thus an expression of this form is remembered by connoisseurs as <s>aniyamopamā</s> (non-restrictive simile). Because the restriction 'comparable only to a lotus' is not insisted upon, and because something else of that sort is also permitted.
<s>Samuccayopamā</s> (cumulative simile) also exists — your face resembles the moon not by lustre alone
but also by the action called gladdening — such is its form. [verse 21]

children.text: क्वचिदेकत्र क्रियादावनेकपदार्थातिसर्जनं समुच्चयः । तन्मुखेनोपमा समुच्चयोपमाप्यस्ति वक्ष्यमाणा, न केवलं पूर्वाक्ताः । कीदृशी ? तव मुखं कर्तृभूतमिन्दुमन्वेत्यनुगच्छति । न कान्त्यैव न सौम्यत्वेन गुणेन केवलेन, किं तु ह्लादनाख्येन प्रीणनेन च कर्मणा क्रियया अन्वेति ईदृशी एवंप्रकारावस्थया ह्लादनमित्याख्या संज्ञा यस्य कर्मण इति विग्रहः । कान्त्या ह्लादकत्वेन च त्वन्मुखमिन्दुनोपमीयत इत्यर्थ इति ॥
children.translated_text: The accumulation of multiple properties in a single locus such as an action is called <s>samuccaya</s> (cumulation). A simile through that means is <s>samuccayopamā</s> (cumulative simile), which also exists as will be described — not only the previously stated types. Of what kind? Your face, as the agent, follows — matches — the moon. Not by lustre alone, not by the quality of gentleness alone, but also by the action, the activity, called gladdening — that is, pleasing. In this manner, the compound is analyzed as: that action whose name is 'gladdening.' Your face is compared to the moon through both lustre and the capacity to gladden — this is the meaning.

children.text: त्वय्येव त्वन्मुखं दृष्टं दृश्यते दिवि चन्द्रमाः ।
children.translated_text: Your face is seen only upon you; the moon is seen in the sky —
only this much is the difference, nothing else — this is <s>atiśayopamā</s> (hyperbolic simile). [verse 22]

children.text: तव मुखं त्वय्येव भवत्यामेव दृष्टम्, न दिवि । चन्द्रमाश्चन्द्रस्तु दिवि नभस्येव दृश्यते, न त्वयि । इयत्येव परिमाणभिन्नाश्रयतामात्रलक्षणा भिदा भेदो विद्यते नान्या काचिद् एतद्व्यतिरिक्ता । अन्यथा सर्वथा साम्यमेवानयोरित्यनेकभेदसम्भवे अपि अतिशयस्येदृशस्य विवक्षया कविनानयोः साम्यकथनातिशयपरत्वेनातिशयोपमा आख्यायत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Your face is seen only upon you, upon your person, not in the sky. But the moon is seen only in the sky, in the heavens, not upon you. Only this much — a difference characterized merely by difference of locus in a measured degree — exists; no other difference apart from this. Otherwise, there is complete similarity between the two — though many differences are possible, through the poet's intention of expressing such a hyperbole, this is called <s>atiśayopamā</s> (hyperbolic simile) because it conveys the excess of the statement of similarity between the two.
The splendor of her face belongs to me alone — let the moon cease its boasting!
Since that very splendor exists in the lotus too — this is <s>utprekṣitopamā</s> (simile through fancy). [verse 23]

children.text: यस्या मृगदृशो मुखश्रीर्वदनकान्तिर्मय्येव वर्तते, नान्यत्रेत्येवंरूपैर्विकत्थनैः श्लाघयाऽलम् । कृतमिन्दोश्चन्द्रस्य ।

न विकत्थनीयमित्थमिन्दुना । किमिति ? यद् यस्मात् । सा मुखश्रीः पद्मेऽपि न केवलमिन्दौ । अस्त्येव न नास्ति । इत्युत्प्रेक्षया असतोऽपि तथाविकत्थनस्याध्यासेन वदनमिन्दुनोपमीयत इति । उत्प्रेक्षितोपमैवासौ तादृशी वेदितव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: The moon should not boast thus. Why? Because (yad = yasmāt) that facial beauty exists in the lotus too, not in the moon alone. Indeed it does exist — it is not absent. Thus, through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), by superimposing such boasting even upon what does not actually possess it, the face is compared to the moon. This is <s>utprekṣitopamā</s> (simile through fancy) — it should be understood as being of that nature.

The facial beauty, the radiance of the countenance, of that doe-eyed woman exists in me alone and nowhere else — enough with such boasting, with such self-praise, of the moon, of <s>Indu</s> (the moon).
If there were to exist some lotus with raised brows and wandering eyes,
let it bear the beauty of your face — this is <s>adbhutopamā</s> (wondrous simile). [verse 24]

children.text: उद्धृते भ्रुवौ विभ्रान्ते च लोचने यस्मिन् । तत्तादृशं किञ्चित् किमपि यदि भवेत् क्वचित् तदीदृशं ते तव सुन्दरि मुखश्रियं धत्तां न निषिध्यते । किं त्वाश्चर्यमिदं दुर्लभमीदृशमिति । अभूतोद्भावनेन वदनपद्मेनोपमीयत इति । असावियमेवंभूता अद्भुतोपमा ज्ञातव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: That in which the brows are raised and the eyes are wandering — if such a thing, some lotus of whatever kind, were to exist anywhere, then such a one may bear the beauty of your face, O beautiful one — it is not prohibited. But this very thing is a wonder, something rare of this kind. Through the imagining of what does not exist, the face is compared to the lotus. This kind of simile should be known as <s>adbhutopamā</s> (wondrous simile).
Thinking 'this is the moon,' O slender-limbed one, mistaking your face, with the hope of seeing your face,
I chase even the moon — this is known as <s>mohopamā</s> (simile through delusion). [verse 25]

children.text: तन्वङ्गीति प्रियामन्त्रणम् । अयमसौ शशी चन्द्र इति तव मुखमुत्प्रेक्ष्य अध्यवसाय चन्द्रबुद्ध्यानुधावामि । न केवलमेषा भ्रान्तिः । किं तु त्वन्मुखाशया तवाननमिदमिति त्वद्वदनबुद्ध्या इन्दुमप्यनुधावामीति अनुगच्छामि । अयमपरो विपर्यासः । इत्येवं मोहेन भ्रान्त्या चन्द्रमुखयोरुपमानोपमेयभावप्रतीतिरिति । एषा इयमीदृशी मोहोपमाख्यायत इति ॥
children.translated_text: 'O slender-limbed one' is a term of address to the beloved. Mistaking your face for the moon, that is, superimposing the notion of moon upon it, I chase after it. Nor is this merely a delusion. Rather, with the hope of your face — with the thought 'this is your countenance' — I chase even the moon. This is another reversal. Thus, through delusion, through confusion, the relationship of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object compared) between the moon and the face is perceived. This is what is called <s>mohopamā</s> (simile through delusion).

children.text: किं पद्ममन्तर्भ्रान्तालि किं ते लोलेक्षणं मुखम् ।
children.translated_text: Is this a lotus with bees wandering inside, or is it your face with restless eyes?
My mind swings like a pendulum — this is <s>saṃśayopamā</s> (simile through doubt). [verse 26]

children.text: अन्तर्भ्रान्तौ अलो भ्रमरौ यस्मिन् तदीदृशं पद्मं किमिदम् । लोले चले ईक्षणे लोचने यस्मिन् तादृशं वा तवेदं मुखम् । इति मम चित्तं मनो दोलायते दोलेवाचरति । एवं पद्मद्वयपरिग्रहात् संशेत इत्यर्थः । इतीयमीदृशी संशयावेशेन पद्ममुखेनौपम्यावगमात् संशयोपमा प्रतीयत इति ॥
children.translated_text: That in which the two bees are wandering inside — is this such a lotus? Or is it your face, in which the eyes, the pupils, are restless, moving? Thus my mind, my heart, swings like a pendulum — it moves as a swing does. Thus, because both alternatives are entertained as a lotus, there is doubt — this is the meaning. This is <s>saṃśayopamā</s> (simile through doubt), because through the intrusion of doubt, the similarity between the lotus and the face is apprehended.
The lotus, which is overpowered by the moon, does not have a radiance that puts the moon to shame —
therefore this must be your face — this is <s>nirṇayopamā</s> (simile through determination). [verse 27]

children.text: पद्मस्य द्युतिः कान्तिः इन्दोर्लज्जाकरी न भवति । नेन्दुं ह्नेपयतीत्यर्थः । किं विशिष्टस्य इन्दुना निग्राह्यस्य अभिभवनीयस्य । तदुदये सङ्कोचात् । इदमत्र कारणम् यदि तु पद्ममिदमभविष्यत्, नेन्दुमह्रेपयिष्यत् । ह्रेपयति च । अतोवसीयते तव मुख-
मेवेदं तस्यैव तादृशत्वात् न पद्ममिति । असावियमेवंविधा निर्णयोपमा विज्ञायते मुखमिदं न पद्ममिति निश्चयमुखेनोपमावगमादिति ॥
children.translated_text: alone, because only that has such a nature — it is not a lotus. This kind of simile is recognized as <s>nirṇayopamā</s> (simile through determination), because through the mode of ascertainment — 'this is a face, not a lotus' — the simile is apprehended.

The radiance, the lustre, of the lotus does not cause shame to the moon — it does not humiliate the moon, this is the meaning. Of what kind of lotus? One that is overpowered by the moon — that is, one that can be subdued by it, because it closes at moonrise. This is the reason here: if this had been a lotus, it would not have put the moon to shame. But it does put it to shame. Therefore it is concluded that this is your face
Rivaling the cool-rayed [moon], resplendent, and of sweet fragrance — /
"Your face is like a lotus" — this is known as <s>śleṣopamā</s> (paronomastic simile). // 28 //

children.text: द्वन्द्वि प्रत्यनीकं मुखस्य तत्समानकान्तित्वात् । अम्भोजस्य च तदुदये सङ्कोचभजनात् । शब्दश्लेषः । श्रीमत् कान्तियुक्तं मुखमम्भोजं च श्रीर्देवता तत्र वसतीति श्रुतेः । अयमपि शब्दश्लेषः । उभयोरपि कान्तियोगादर्थश्लेषो वा । सुरभिरिष्टो गन्धोऽस्येति सुरभिगन्धि द्वयमपीत्यर्थश्लेषः । चकारः समुच्चये । इत्येवं श्लेषपरिग्रहणे चन्द्रवक्त्रयोरुपमाप्रयोगात् श्लेषोपमैवेदृशी मतेति ।
children.translated_text: rival, i.e., adversary, of the face because of possessing equal lustre; and of the lotus because of its closing at his [the moon's] rising. This is verbal paronomasia (<s>śabdaśleṣa</s>). "Resplendent" (<s>śrīmat</s>) — endowed with lustre, both the face and the lotus; or: <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess) dwells there, according to scripture. This too is verbal paronomasia. Or, since both possess lustre, it is paronomasia of meaning (<s>arthaśleṣa</s>). "Of sweet fragrance" (<s>surabhigandhi</s>) — having a pleasant scent — both [face and lotus] — this is paronomasia of meaning. The particle "and" (<s>ca</s>) is in the sense of conjunction. Thus, when paronomasia is employed, since there is a simile between the moon and the face, such is the <s>śleṣopamā</s> that is accepted.
Your face is like a lotus — "rivaling the cool-rayed [moon]," i.e., the moon — it is a
Since it is expressed by a word of identical form, that is the <s>samānopamā</s> (homonymous simile), as follows: /
"This garden-row, graced by a grove of <s>sāla</s> trees, is like a young woman adorned with locks of hair (<s>sālaka</s>)." // 29 //

children.text: इयमुद्यानमाला प्रमदवनराजिर्बालेव स्त्रीव । कथं ? सालकाननशोभिनी । बाला तावत् सहालकेन केशसन्निवेशविशेषेण वर्तते यत् सालकमाननं तेन शोभते सालकाननशोभिनी । उद्यानमालापिं सालानां वृक्षविशेषाणां काननेन वनेन शोभते । एवंरूपा या सा तादृशी समानोपमा समाख्यायते । कुतः सरूपेण सदृशेन स्वरूपतो नार्थतः तस्य भेदात्, यथोक्तमनन्तरम् । शब्देन सालकाननशोभिनीत्येवंविधेन वाच्यत्वात्, प्रकाश्यत्वात् तस्या इति गम्यते । यथेति निदर्शने । ननु श्लेषोपमैवेयं, सालकाननशोभिनीति शब्दश्लेषात् । सा च पूर्वमुक्ता, तत्किमनया ? को वा तयोर्भेदः ? उच्यते । पूर्वं श्लेषाप्रयोगेऽप्युपमा गम्यते । अम्भोजमिव ते वक्त्रमिति श्लेषानुवेधादृते व्यापदिश्यते । इह तु श्लेषानुत्प्रेक्षायामुपमैव नावसीयते । बालेवोद्यानमालेति । श्लेषाभिधान एव केवलमवगम्यते सालकाननशोभिनीति । अतस्तादृशेन शब्देनेयमुच्यते । अत एवाह—सरूपशब्दवाच्यत्वादिति । ततः समानोपमैवेयमाख्यायते, न श्लेषोपमेत्यलं प्रपञ्चेन ॥
children.translated_text: This garden-row (<s>udyānamālā</s>), i.e., a series of pleasure-gardens, is "like a young woman" (<s>bālā</s>). How? "Adorned by a <s>sāla</s>-grove" (<s>sālakānanśobhinī</s>). The young woman has a particular arrangement of hair called <s>sālaka</s> (locks), by which her face (<s>ānana</s>) is adorned — hence <s>sālakānanśobhinī</s>. The garden-row too is adorned by a forest (<s>kānana</s>) of <s>sāla</s> trees (a particular species of tree). Such a [simile] is called <s>samānopamā</s> (homonymous simile). Why? Because it is expressed (<s>vācyatva</s>) — i.e., manifested — through a word of identical form (<s>sarūpa</s>), i.e., similar in appearance, not in meaning, since the meanings differ, as stated immediately after. By a word such as "<s>sālakānanaśobhinī</s>" — this is understood. "As follows" (<s>yathā</s>) introduces the example. But is this not simply a <s>śleṣopamā</s>, since there is verbal paronomasia in "<s>sālakānanaśobhinī</s>"? And that was already stated before — so what is the need for this? What is the difference between the two? The answer is: in the former case, even without the employment of paronomasia, the simile is apprehended — "Your face is like a lotus" is stated independently of the paronomastic element. Here, however, without imagining the paronomasia, no simile at all is ascertained — "This garden-row is like a young woman." Only through the utterance of the paronomasia is it understood — "<s>sālakānanaśobhinī</s>." Therefore this [simile] is expressed by such a word. For this very reason he says: "Since it is expressed by a word of identical form." Therefore this is designated as <s>samānopamā</s>, not <s>śleṣopamā</s> — enough of elaboration.
The lotus has much pollen; the moon wanes. Compared to these, your face, /
though equal [in beauty], is yet superior — this is considered <s>nindopamā</s> (deprecating simile). // 30 //

children.text: बहूनि रजांसि पांसवो यस्मिन् इति । चन्द्रः क्षयी क्षयोऽपचयोऽस्येति । ताभ्यामेवंभूताभ्यां पद्मचन्द्राभ्यां कान्त्यादिना समानं तुल्यमपि सत्तवाननं सोत्सेकमुत्कर्षयुक्तं प्रतिविशिष्टं वर्तते । रजःशब्दस्य दोषेऽपि वृत्तेः । बहुरजस्त्वस्य शब्दलक्षणेन दोषरूपस्य क्षयित्वस्य च तत्राभावात्, एवंविधा निन्दोपमा मता स्मृता । कथञ्चिंन्निन्दितेन पद्मा
children.translated_text: "Much pollen" (<s>bahurajas</s>) — [the lotus] in which there are many particles of pollen-dust. The moon is "waning" (<s>kṣayī</s>) — characterized by diminution. Compared to those two — the lotus and moon, thus characterized — your face, though equal (<s>samāna</s>) in lustre and the like, is yet "superior" (<s>sotseka</s>), i.e., endowed with excellence, possessing distinction. Since the word <s>rajas</s> also denotes a fault (passion/dust), and since the defect-nature of having much <s>rajas</s> (at the verbal level) and the quality of waning do not exist in the face — such is the <s>nindopamā</s> that is recognized. Because the face, whose intended superiority [is established] through the comparison with the lotus and the like which are somehow depreciated,
is the object of comparison.
The lotus is the birth-place of <s>Brahmā</s> himself; the moon is borne on <s>Śambhu</s>'s head; /
those two are equal to your face — this is considered <s>praśaṃsopamā</s> (laudatory simile). // 31 //

children.text: यो विश्वं सृजति तस्यापि ब्रह्मणः स्रष्टुरुद्भवत्यस्मादित्युद्भवः पद्म इत्यतिशये अपिशब्दः । नारायणनाभिनलिनयोनिः पितामह [इति] श्रुंतेः । चन्द्रः शम्भोः शङ्करस्य शिरसा मौलिना धृतः । तावेवं श्लाघनीयौ पद्मचन्द्रौ तव मुखेन तुल्यौ कान्त्यापि साधर्म्येण ताभ्यां तस्योपमितेस्तेन तुल्यौ भवतः । एवंविधा या सा प्रशंसोपमेष्यते, यथोक्तविशेषयोगेन प्रशंसास्पदाभ्यां पद्मचन्द्राभ्यामाननस्योपमानादिति ॥
children.translated_text: The lotus, from which is born even <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator who creates the universe — the word "even" (<s>api</s>) conveys hyperbole — since from scripture: "<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s navel-lotus is the birth-place of the Grandsire." The moon is "borne" (<s>dhṛta</s>) by the head, i.e., the crown, of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>). Those two — the lotus and moon, thus laudable — are "equal" (<s>tulya</s>) to your face in lustre and through the similarity of qualities; by being compared to it, they become equal. Such is the <s>praśaṃsopamā</s> that is recognized — through the comparison of the face with the lotus and moon, which are standards of praise by virtue of the special qualities described.
My mind wishes to declare that your face is equal to the moon; /

children.text: स गुणो वास्तु दोषो वेत्याचिख्यासोपमा मता ॥ ३२ ॥
children.translated_text: whether that be a merit or a fault — this is considered <s>ācakhyāsopamā</s> (simile of desire-to-declare). // 32 //

children.text: तव मुखं चन्द्रेण तुल्यमित्येवमाख्यातुमिच्छति मम मनः कर्तृ । ननु चन्द्रः क्षयादिदूषितः, मुखं त्वखण्डमण्डलं तत्किमेवमुच्यत इति चेत्—सत्यं यदाह—स इत्यादि । सोऽयं, चन्द्रमुखयोस्तुल्यतावादः गुणो वास्तु [उचितो] वा भवतु, दोषो वास्तु अनुचितो वा भ[वतु] । नेदृशं विमर्शमपेक्षते मे, मनः । केवलमभिधातुमभिलषतीति । एवमाचिख्यासामुखेन, सादृश्यप्रकाशनादाचिख्यासोपमेतीदृशी मतेष्टेति । निन्दोपमाद्युदाहरणेन चानेन

children.translated_text: what was said — "The threefold nature of that [simile] is stated by some great souls /
on the basis of the distinction of deprecation, praise, and desire-to-declare" —
"All three are already expressed by the general statement of common qualities; /

children.text: मालोपमादि तत्सर्वं न ज्यायान् विस्तरो वृथा ॥
children.translated_text: the <s>mālopamā</s> and the rest — all of that [elaboration] is not greater; the elaboration is in vain" —
this alternative view is refuted. For thus:
"By the juxtaposition of an equivalent subject-matter, the <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile) is recognized, /
even without the word 'like,' through the apprehension of similarity of qualities" —

children.text: इत्यादिना प्रतिंवस्तूपमादिरपि कथं न वृथा स्यात्, सामान्यगुणनिर्देशेनैव गतार्थत्वात् ? अर्थप्रपञ्चार्थमेतदिष्यते [चेत्,] तदिंहापि समानमिति यत्किञ्चिदेतत् ॥
children.translated_text: by this and similar [arguments], would not the <s>prativastūpamā</s> and the rest also become superfluous, since their purpose is already served by the general statement of common qualities? If this [detailed classification] is desired for the purpose of elaborating the meanings, then the same applies here — so this [objection] is of little substance.

My mind, as agent, wishes to declare (<s>ācakhyāsu</s>) that your face is equal to the moon. But the moon is flawed by waning and the like, while the face is an undiminished orb — so why is this said? True — to which he responds: "Whether that" and so forth. Let this assertion of equality between moon and face be a merit, i.e., appropriate, or let it be a fault, i.e., inappropriate. My mind does not care for such deliberation; it simply desires to declare [it]. Thus, through the desire-to-declare as the medium, since similarity is revealed, it is the <s>ācakhyāsopamā</s> — such should be understood. And by this example of <s>nindopamā</s> and the rest,
The hundred-petalled [lotus], the autumn moon, and your face — these three /
are mutually rival — this is considered <s>virodhopamā</s> (rivalry simile). // 33 //

children.text: शतपत्रं पद्मं शरदि चन्द्रः तवाननमित्येतद् वस्तुत्रयं त्रयोऽवयवा अस्येति । परस्परेणान्योन्येन सह परस्परस्य वा विरोधिं प्रतिद्वन्द्वि समानगुणत्वात्, कान्त्यादिविशेषणयोगात् । इत्येवंविधा या सा विरोधोद्भावनेन साधर्म्यवर्णनाद् विरोधोपमा मतेति ॥
children.translated_text: The hundred-petalled [lotus] (<s>śatapatra</s>), i.e., a lotus; the moon in autumn; and your face — this triad of entities, i.e., having three components. "Mutually rival" — rival with one another, or rival of each other, because of possessing equal qualities, due to the conjunction of qualities such as lustre and the like. Such is the <s>virodhopamā</s> that is recognized — since through the expression of rivalry, the similarity is described.
The moon can never compete with your face, /
for it is blemished and dull — this is indeed the <s>pratiṣedhopamā</s> (prohibitive simile). // 34 //

children.text: तव मुखेन सह प्रतिगर्जितुं स्पर्द्धां कर्तुमिन्दोः । न जातु न क

दाचिदपि शक्तिः सामर्थ्यमस्ति । कलङ्किनो जडस्य कलङ्कित्वात् जडत्वाच्चेत्यर्थः । कलङ्को मृगलाञ्छनलक्षणो दोषः । जाड्यं शैत्यमकौशलं चेति शब्दच्छलेन दोषोक्तिः । मुखं तु निंष्कलङ्कं विदग्धं चेति । कथमनेन [स]दृशं इति निषेधद्वारेण साधर्म्यावगमात् । प्रतिषेधोपमैव सा या ईदृशीति ॥
children.translated_text: that is the meaning. The blemish (<s>kalaṅka</s>) is the defect characterized by the mark of a deer [on the moon's surface]. Dullness (<s>jāḍya</s>) means coldness and lack of skill — through verbal play (<s>śabdacchala</s>), defects are stated. The face, however, is unblemished and skilful. How then can [the moon] be similar to it? — through the door of prohibition, the similarity is apprehended. Such is the <s>pratiṣedhopamā</s>.
The moon has no capacity — never, not at any time — to compete with, i.e., to rival, your face. Because it is blemished and dull —
Your face is marked by the eyes of a deer; the moon is likewise marked by a deer; /
yet even so, he is merely equal, not superior — this is the <s>caṭūpamā</s> (flattering simile). // 35 //
