children.text: तन्वि ! तव वक्त्रं मृगस्येक्षणमेकदेशोऽत्यन्तसाम्येनाभेदविवक्षया अङ्कश्चिह्नं यस्य तत्तथा । शशी तु मृगेणैव सकलेनाङ्कितो लक्षितः ततश्चाधिक्यं शशिनः प्राप्तं तथापि नाधिकः । नोत्कर्षी । किं तु सम एव मुखेनासौ शशी । इत्येवं चटुना प्रियालापप्रकारेणेदृशेन सादृश्यप्रकाशनात् चटूपमेदृशी द्रष्टव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: O slender one! Your face — the eyes of a deer (<s>mṛga</s>) are a partial feature [of it], and through the intention of non-difference based on extreme similarity, they are its "mark" (<s>aṅka</s>), i.e., sign. The moon, however, is marked by the deer itself in its entirety. Therefore the superiority of the moon should be established; yet even so, he is not superior — not excelling — but merely equal to the face. Thus, through such a mode of flattering address (<s>caṭu</s>), i.e., a form of sweet speech, since similarity is revealed, such is the <s>caṭūpamā</s> to be understood.

children.text: न पद्मं मुखमेवेदं न भृङ्गौ चक्षुषी इमे ।
children.translated_text: This is not a lotus — it is indeed a face! These are not bees — they are eyes! /
Due to the manifest similarity, this is indeed the <s>tattvākhyānopamā</s> (reality-declaring simile). // 36 //

children.text: पद्ममुखयोर्भृङ्गचक्षुषोश्च विस्पष्टं परिस्फुटं यत्सादृश्यं कान्तिंचञ्चलत्वादिलक्षणं, तस्मादभेदशङ्कापूर्वकमेवंविधमुच्यते । न पद्ममेतत् किं । तु मुखमेवेदम् । एतौ चात्र [न] भृङ्गौ, किं तर्हि ? चक्षुषी इमे । इत्येवंरूपा या सा तत्त्वाख्यानोपमा ख्याता । पद्मादीनामविपरीतस्य रूपस्य परिदीपनेन साम्यावसायात् ।
children.translated_text: Because of the manifest, i.e., evident, similarity between lotus and face, and between bees and eyes — characterized by lustre, restlessness, and the like — preceded by a doubt of identity, such a statement is made: "This is not a lotus" — then what? "It is indeed a face." And "these are not bees" — then what? "They are eyes." Such is the <s>tattvākhyānopamā</s> that is declared — since similarity is ascertained through the illumination of the true nature of the lotus and the rest, without distortion.

children.text: निर्णयोपमाया अस्याश्च को भेद ? उभयत्रापि तत्त्वनिश्चयाविशेषात् । यद्यपि तत्त्वनिश्चयस्तुल्यः, तथापि संशयच्छेदेन निश्चयः, इह तु विपर्यासनिरासेनेति महान् भेदः । अन्यत्राप्येवं क्वचित् कथञ्चित् अपेक्षाविशेषाद् व्याख्येयो भेद इति ॥
children.translated_text: What is the difference between the <s>nirṇayopamā</s> (ascertainment simile) and this one? Since in both there is no difference in the ascertainment of truth. Although the ascertainment of truth is the same, nevertheless [in the former case] the ascertainment is through the resolution of doubt, while here it is through the removal of misidentification — hence there is a great difference. Elsewhere too, a difference should be explained in similar fashion through some specific aspect of the relational context.
Your face, transcending the rank of moon and lotus, /
became equal only to itself — this is the <s>asādhāraṇopamā</s> (unique simile). // 37 //

children.text: चन्द्रस्यारविन्दस्य च कक्ष्यां पदवीं तुल्यताम् अतिक्रम्य अवधूय तयोरवकर्षात् । आत्मना स्वरूपेणैव तुल्यम् अभवत्, अनन्यसामान्यगुणयोगात् । इत्येवंरूपासाधारणताभिधानद्वारेण सादृश्यप्रतीतेः असाधारणोपमा निगद्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Having transcended, i.e., surpassed, the rank (<s>kakṣyā</s>), i.e., level of equality, of the moon and the lotus — due to their inferiority — it became equal to itself alone, i.e., to its own nature, because of possessing no other [entity with] common qualities. Such is the <s>asādhāraṇopamā</s> — since similarity is perceived through the expression of uniqueness.
As if the essence of the splendor of all lotuses has been gathered together somewhere — /
your face shines — they know that as the <s>abhūtopamā</s> (counterfactual simile). // 38 //

children.text: क्वचित् एकत्रस्थाने समाहृतः प्रचितः सर्वेषां पद्मानां प्रभास्वभावः सारो हृदयमिव तवाननं विभातीत्येवं भूता या तामभूतोपमां विदुः स्मरन्ति तद्विदः । अभूतेनासना क्वचित् समाहृतेन सर्वपद्मप्रभासारेण आननस्योपमितेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: "Somewhere" — in one place — "gathered" means collected; the essence (<s>sāra</s>), i.e., the heart, of the splendor of all lotuses — "as if" your face shines thus. Those who know it recognize such [a simile] as the <s>abhūtopamā</s>. Because the face is compared by a non-existent [situation] — the essence of all lotus-splendor gathered somewhere — that does not actually exist.
As if poison from the orb of the moon, as if fire from sandalwood — /
harsh speech from this face — this is the <s>asambhāvitopamā</s> (inconceivable simile). // 39 //

children.text: मञ्जुभाषिणि ! इतः तव वक्त्रात् एकान्तमधुरात् वाक भारती परुषा निष्ठुरा निष्क्रामति चन्द्रबिम्बात् अमृतमयात् विषमिव चन्दनाच्च एकान्तशिशिंरात् पावकः
अग्निरिव । नैतत्संभाव्यत इति असम्भावनाभिप्रायेण सारूप्यनिरूपणात् असम्भावितोपमैवेदृशी दृश्येति ॥
children.translated_text: "This cannot be conceived" — since through the intention of inconceivability the similarity is established, such is the <s>asambhāvitopamā</s> to be recognized.

O sweet-speaking one! From this face of yours, which is exclusively sweet, speech (<s>vāk</s>) issues forth that is harsh (<s>paruṣā</s>), i.e., cruel — as if poison from the orb of the moon, which is made of nectar; and as if fire from sandalwood, which is exclusively cool.
Cool like sandalwood-water, moonbeams, moonstones, and the like — /
your touch, proclaiming excellence, is the <s>bahūpamā</s> (multiple simile). // 40 //

children.text: वराङ्गि ! तव स्पर्शः स्पृश्यतेऽसाविति चन्दनोदकं चन्द्रांशुः चन्द्रकान्तश्च मणिविशेषः । आदिग्रहणेन अन्यस्यापि हिमादेः शीतवस्तुनः परिग्रहः । तद्वत् शीतलः शिशिर इत्येवं बहुभिरुपमानात् बहूपमेयमीदृशी । नन्वेकेनापि शैत्यप्रतीतेः किं बहुभिरित्याह—अतिशयं प्रथयन्तीति । अतिशयं प्रियास्पर्शस्य शैत्यगतमुत्कर्षं कमपि प्रकाशयन्ती प्रवर्तते । ततो बहूपादानमीदृशं विवक्षितमिति बहूपमोपकल्प्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: O fair-limbed one! Your touch — that which is touched — sandalwood-water, moonbeams, moonstone (a particular gem). By the word "and the like" (<s>ādi</s>), other cool substances like snow are also included. "Similarly cool" (<s>śītala</s>), i.e., chilly — thus, because of comparison with many standards, this is the <s>bahūpamā</s>. But since coolness is understood even from a single [comparison], what is the need for many? He answers: "proclaiming excellence." Proclaiming the excellence — some special degree of coolness — of the beloved's touch, it operates. Therefore, such multiple adoption [of standards] is intended, and thus the <s>bahūpamā</s> is constituted.
As if carved out from the orb of the moon, as if extracted from the heart of a lotus — /
your face, O slender-limbed one! — this is the <s>vikriyopamā</s> (transformation simile). // 41 //

children.text: तन्वङ्गि ! तव वदनम् इन्दुबिम्बादुत्कीर्णम् निर्मायोत्क्षिप्तमिव, पद्मगर्भात् अम्भोरुहकुहरात् उद्धृतमिव, सृष्टिद्वारेण उत्कीर्णमिव कान्तिसर्वस्वमयत्वात् । इत्येवंरूपा या असौ तादृशी विक्रियोपमा इष्यते । चन्द्रादिविकारविशेषपरिग्रहेण उपमानोपमेयभावोद्भावनादिति ॥
children.translated_text: O slender-limbed one! Your face — "carved out" (<s>utkīrṇa</s>) from the orb of the moon, i.e., as if fashioned and extracted; "extracted" (<s>uddhṛta</s>) from the heart of a lotus, i.e., from the interior of the lotus — as if extracted through the process of creation, because of being the very essence of lustre. Such is the <s>vikriyopamā</s> that is accepted — since the relationship of standard and object of comparison is established through the appropriation of a particular transformation of the moon and the like.
As the sun's heat in the sun, as the sun in the day, as the day in the sky — /
so valor bestowed beauty upon you — this is considered <s>mālopamā</s> (garland simile). // 42 //

children.text: पूष्णि सूर्यातपः प्रकाशविशेषो यथा लक्ष्मीमधात्, स च पूषा वासरे यथा, सोऽपि वासरो यथा व्योम्नि आकाशे लक्ष्मीमधादिति प्रकृतं, तथा त्वयि राजनि विक्रमः शौर्यं लक्ष्मीं श्रियमधात् अकृत । इत्येवमुपमावस्तूनां पौर्वापर्येण घटनात् मालोपमायाः क्रमः प्रकारोऽयमीदृशः प्रतिपत्तव्य इति ॥
children.translated_text: In the sun (<s>Pūṣan</s>), the sun's heat (<s>ātapa</s>), i.e., a particular [kind of] radiance, bestowed beauty (<s>lakṣmī</s>); and that sun bestowed [beauty] upon the day; and that day bestowed [beauty] upon the sky (<s>vyoman</s>) — this is the main point; similarly, in you, O king, valor (<s>vikrama</s>), i.e., prowess, bestowed beauty (<s>lakṣmī</s>), i.e., splendor. Thus, through the sequential linking of the objects of comparison, this is the pattern of the <s>mālopamā</s> (garland simile) — such should be understood.
When some sentence-meaning is compared with another sentence-meaning, /
with one or many occurrences of the word 'like' — that <s>vākyārthopamā</s> (sentence-meaning simile) is of two kinds. // 43 //

children.text: वाक्यस्यार्थः क्रियाकारकसम्बन्धविशेषः । तेनैव पदार्थमात्रेण वाक्यार्थ उक्तलक्षणः कोऽपि विवक्षितः कश्चित् यद्युपमीयते सदृशः कथ्यते, सा सादृशी वाक्यार्थोपमा मता । सा च द्विधा भिद्यते । कथम् ? एकोऽनेकश्च इवशब्दः सादृश्यसूचको यत्र तद्भावस्तत्त्वं तस्मिन् । कारणात्तस्मादिति गम्यते ॥
children.translated_text: The meaning of a sentence is a particular relation of action, agent, and instruments. When some intended sentence-meaning is compared, i.e., declared similar, with just that — i.e., with a word-meaning [of the same kind] — that is the <s>vākyārthopamā</s>. And it is divided into two kinds. How? Where the word "like" (<s>iva</s>), indicating similarity, occurs once or many times — on the basis of that [distinction].
Your face, with restless eyes, with the radiance of visible teeth, /
with roaming bees, with barely visible filaments — shines like a lotus! // 44 //

children.text: ननम् अधीरे लोले अक्षिणी यत्र । आविर्भृता दशनदीधितयो दन्तकान्तयो यस्मिन् तदीदृशं भातीति । एवं तावद् वाक्यमुपमेयभूतम् । किमिवेत्याह—भ्रमन्तौ भ्रमरौ यस्मिन्नालक्ष्याणि [ईषत्]प्रकटानि केसराणि यत्र तादृशं पङ्कजमिवेति द्वितीयं वाक्यमुपमाभूतमियमेकेवशब्दा वाक्यार्थोपमा बोद्धव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: face — in which the eyes (<s>akṣi</s>) are restless (<s>adhīra</s>), i.e., wavering; in which the radiance of the teeth (<s>daśanadīdhiti</s>) is visible — it thus shines. This is the sentence constituting the object of comparison. "Like what?" he says: in which bees (<s>bhramara</s>) roam, in which the filaments (<s>kesara</s>) are barely visible (<s>ālakṣya</s>) — like such a lotus — this is the second sentence constituting the standard of comparison. This should be understood as a <s>vākyārthopamā</s> with a single occurrence of the word "like" (<s>iva</s>).
Your
Illustrating [the type] with multiple occurrences of the word "like," he says:
Like a lotus-pond [she is], the slender-limbed one; like a lotus, her face; /
by me, like a bee — it was drunk again and again with delight! // 45 //

children.text: तस्यास्तन्वङ्गयाः कस्याश्चिदिष्टाया आननं पायं पायम् अभीक्ष्णं पीत्वा निषेव्य मया अरम्यत क्रीड़ितमिति उपमेयार्थमेकं वाक्यं तावन्नलिन्या इव पद्ममिव मधुव्रतेनेवेति द्वितीयमुपमारूपं वाक्यमियमनेकेवशब्दा वाक्यार्थोपमा ज्ञातव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: Having drunk — that is, having repeatedly enjoyed — the face of that slender-limbed beloved woman, I delighted — that is, I sported. This is one sentence constituting the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>). The second sentence, in the form of a simile, is 'like a lotus-pond,' 'like a lotus,' 'like a bee.' This should be understood as a <s>vākyārthopamā</s> (sentence-meaning simile) with multiple occurrences of the word 'like' (<s>iva</s>).
Having presented some object, by the placement of something sharing its qualities,
there arises an apprehension of similarity — this is <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-example simile), as follows: // 46 //

children.text: किञ्चिद् विवक्षितं पुरुषादि वस्तु उपक्षिप्य उपन्यस्य तेनोपन्यस्तेन वस्तुना सधर्मणस्तुल्यस्य वस्तुनोऽन्यस्य न्यसनात् अभिधानाद्धेतोः साम्यस्य तयोर्द्वयोः सादृश्यस्य प्रतीतिः अवसायोऽस्ति इति हेतोः प्रतिवस्तूपमा ईदृशी इष्यते, प्रतिवस्तुना तथाविधेन अर्थान्तरेण प्रस्तुतस्य वस्तुनस्तुल्यताप्रतिपत्तेः । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Having set forth, that is, presented, some intended object such as a person, by the placement — that is, by the statement — of another object that is similar, i.e., equal in qualities, to that presented object, the apprehension — that is, the ascertainment — of similarity between those two exists; for this reason, this kind of figure is recognized as <s>prativastūpamā</s>, because the equality of the subject under discussion is apprehended through a counter-object, i.e., through another meaning of that kind. He illustrates with 'as follows.'
Not even one [king] like you has yet appeared among kings being born;
indeed, there simply is no second tree equal to the <s>Pārijāta</s>! // 47 //

children.text: जगति चिरमारभ्य जायमानेषु राजसु मध्ये त्वादृशः त्वमिव गुणवान् एकोऽपि राजा, प्रागेवानेकः । अद्यापि न विद्यते न केवलं प्राक्, इत्येवं तावद् वस्तूपन्यस्तमेतत् । नन्वित्यादिना प्रतिवस्तूपन्यासः । नन्वित्यनुमतौ । पारिजातस्य दिव्यवृक्षविशेषस्य द्वितीयः समानः पादपो नास्त्येव । यथा पारिजात एको वृक्षजातिषूत्तमः तथा त्वं राजस्विति द्वयोः साम्यप्रतीतिरस्तीति योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: Among kings being born in the world from time immemorial, not even one king as virtuous as you — let alone many — is found even to this day, not merely in the past. Thus far the subject has been presented. By 'indeed' and so forth, the counter-object is presented. 'Indeed' is used in the sense of agreement. There simply is no second tree equal to the <s>Pārijāta</s>, the particular celestial tree. Just as the <s>Pārijāta</s> is the foremost among species of trees, so are you among kings — thus the apprehension of similarity between the two should be supplied.
When something inferior is equated with something superior in the performance of a single action,

children.text: यद् ब्रुवन्ति स्मृता सेयं तुल्ययोगोपमा यथा ॥ ४८ ॥
children.translated_text: what [the poets] express — that is recognized as <s>tulyayogopamā</s> (simile through equal attribution), as follows: // 48 //

children.text: अधिकेन केनचित् जात्यादिना हीनं किञ्चिदेकस्याः क्रियाया विधौ सम्पादने समीकृत्य समानीकृत्य ब्रुवन्ति प्रयुञ्चते कवयो यत् । सामान्योक्तिरियं यदिति । यद्वेदृशं वचनं किं तत् ? सेयमीदृशी तुल्ययोगोपमा स्मृतेति विशेषः । एकक्रियासम्बद्धस्य द्वयोः साधारणत्वात् तद्द्वारेण उपमा तुल्ययोगोपमा । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: When poets employ [a simile] by equating — that is, making equal — something inferior with something superior in birth and so forth, in the performance — that is, in the accomplishment — of a single action, what [they express] — this is a general statement, indicated by 'what.' Or, what kind of expression is this? The specific point is that this kind is recognized as <s>tulyayogopamā</s>. Because a single action is shared by both, the simile operating through that [shared action] is <s>tulyayogopamā</s>. He illustrates with 'as follows.'
<s>Pulomāri</s> (Indra) keeps watch for the protection of heaven; you, for [the protection of] the earth.
Demons are slain by him; arrogant kings, by you, O king! // 49 //

children.text: गर्ति कार्येष्ववधत्ते । किमर्थम् ? दिवः स्वर्गलोकस्य रक्षायै परिपालनार्थम् । भुवः पृथिव्या रक्षायै भवान् विवक्षितः कश्चिन्नरेश्वरो जागर्तीत्युत्प्रेक्ष्यम् । तेन पुलोमारिणा सावलेपा दृप्ता असुरा हन्यन्ते, त्वया च नृपाः सावलेपा हन्यन्ते । अत्र देवराजस्य अधिकस्य नृपस्य च कस्यचित् तदपेक्षया जात्यादिना हीनस्य रक्षाद्येकक्रियायोगस्तुल्य इति तद्द्वारेण तयोः साम्यावगतेस्तुल्ययोगोपमा ईदृशी द्रष्टव्येति ॥
children.translated_text: watch — that is, attends to affairs. For what purpose? For the protection — that is, for the guarding — of heaven. For the protection of the earth, you — meaning some particular lord of men who is intended — keeps watch; this is to be understood. By him, <s>Pulomāri</s>, arrogant demons are slain, and by you, arrogant kings are slain. Here, the king of gods, who is superior, and some king, who is inferior to him in birth and so forth, share equally the single action of protection and the like; through that, the apprehension of their similarity constitutes <s>tulyayogopamā</s> — this kind should be recognized.
<s>Pulomāri</s>, the king of gods, by dispelling the sleep of negligence, keeps

children.text: कान्त्या चन्द्रमसं धाम्न सूर्यं धैर्येण चार्णवम् ।
children.translated_text: In beauty you imitate the moon, in splendor the sun, in steadfastness the ocean —
O king! This is recognized as <s>hetūpamā</s> (simile with a reason). // 50 //

children.text: राजन्नित्यामन्त्रणम् । कान्त्या सौम्यतया चन्द्रमसम् अनुकरोषि । तेन तुल्योऽसीत्यर्थः । धाम्ना तेजसा सूर्यमनुकरोषि । धैर्येण स्थित्या अर्णवं सागरमनुकरोषि । एवंविधा या सैषा तादृशी हेतूपमा स्मृता तज्ज्ञैः । कान्त्यादिहेतूपन्यासेन साम्यप्रतीतेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: 'O king' is a form of address. You imitate the moon in beauty — that is, in gentleness. The meaning is that you are equal to it. You imitate the sun in splendor — that is, in radiance. You imitate the ocean in steadfastness — that is, in constancy. Such a [simile] as this is recognized by the learned as <s>hetūpamā</s>. Because the apprehension of similarity arises through the presentation of reasons such as beauty and so forth.
same number? Or can it be otherwise? To this he replies:
How is the rule determined here? Must the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) necessarily share the same grammatical gender, and also the

children.text: न लिङ्गवचने भिन्ने न हीनाधिकतापि वा ।
children.translated_text: Difference in gender or number, nor inferiority or superiority,
suffices to vitiate a simile, where the wise feel no discomfort. // 51 //

children.text: लिङ्गमिदं प्रसिद्धमङ्गसन्निवेशादिलक्षणं स्त्रीत्वादि । वचनमेकवचनादि । ते द्वे भिन्ने विजातीये । हीनतोपमावस्तुनो जात्यादिना अधिकतापि वा । सर्वमेतत् उपमायां दूषणाय विरोधार्थं नालं न समर्थमित्युत्सर्गः । तत्रापवादमाह—यत्रेत्यादि । यत्र क्वचिद् विषये धीमतां कवीनामुद्वेगोऽप्रीतिरसम्मतिर्न भवति तादृशि प्रहते प्रयोगमार्गे नायं दोषः । यस्त्वप्रहतोऽशिष्टो विषयः तत्रायं दोष इत्यर्थादुक्तं भवति । तं च दर्शयिष्यतीति ॥
children.translated_text: Gender here refers to the well-known characteristic of sex and the like, such as femininity, determined by the configuration of bodily features. Number means singular and so forth. When these two are different — that is, of dissimilar kinds — and [likewise] the inferiority of the object of comparison in birth and so forth, or its superiority — all of this is not sufficient to vitiate the simile, i.e., is not capable of creating a fault; this is the general rule. He then states the exception with 'where' and so forth: wherever — in whatever domain — the wise poets feel no discomfort, no displeasure, no disapproval, in such a well-trodden path of usage, this is not a fault. But in a domain that is not well-trodden, i.e., not sanctioned by good usage, this is indeed a fault — such is the implicit meaning. And he will demonstrate that.
He illustrates that:

children.text: स्त्रीव गच्छति षण्डोऽयं वक्त्येषा स्त्री पुमानिव ।
children.translated_text: This eunuch walks like a woman; this woman speaks like a man.

children.text: प्राणा इव प्रियोऽयं मे विद्या धनमिवार्जिता ॥ ५२ ॥
children.translated_text: This beloved of mine is like my very life-breath; knowledge has been acquired like wealth. // 52 //

children.text: अयं षण्डः षण्डकः स्त्रीव गच्छति तच्चेष्टानुवृत्तेः । एषा स्त्री पुमानिव पुरुष इव वक्ति तादृशप्रागल्भ्ययोगात् । अत्र लिङ्गनानात्वमुपमानोपमेययोः । अयं विवक्षितः कश्चिन्मम प्रिय इष्टः प्राणा इव । विद्या व्याकरणादयः अर्जिता धनमिवेति वचनभेदः । एवंविधे समुचिते विषये लिङ्गवचनभेदो नोपमां दूषयति । प्रत्युत रसावह इति ॥
children.translated_text: This <s>ṣaṇḍa</s> (eunuch) walks like a woman, because he imitates her behavior. This woman speaks like a man — that is, like a male — because she possesses such boldness. Here there is difference of gender between the standard and the object of comparison. This intended person is dear to me — that is, beloved — like my life-breath. Learning such as grammar and the like has been acquired like wealth — here there is difference of number. In such an appropriate domain, difference of gender and number does not vitiate the simile. On the contrary, it enhances the aesthetic sentiment.
Illustrating inferiority and superiority, he says:
Like you, O lord of the earth, the king of gods shines!
This king is able to ascend to the level of the sun by his splendor! // 53 //

children.text: महीपालेत्यामन्त्रणम् । भवानिव देवराजो विराजत इति । हीनेनाधिक

उपमीयते । अयं नृपो विवक्षितः कश्चित् । अंशुमतः सूर्यस्य कक्षां पदवीं समताम् आरोढुमलं शक्तः । तेजसा हेतुनेति । अधिकेन हीन उपमितः । अत्यन्तभद्रतामेकान्ततेजस्वितां च प्रतीतामाश्रित्य अयमेवंविधः प्रयोगः । तथा भावनायांशोभत इत्यवसेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: is compared to the inferior. This king — some intended [ruler] — is able to ascend to the level, the rank, the equality of the sun (<s>Aṃśumat</s>). By his splendor — this is the reason. Here, the inferior is compared to the superior. Relying on the well-known extreme benevolence and unparalleled brilliance [of both], such a usage is [accepted]. Thus it should be understood that it succeeds through poetic imagination.
'Lord of the earth' is a form of address. The king of gods shines like you — here, the superior
He shows that all such [usage] of this kind is beautiful:
Such [usage] as described above never indeed loses its charm;

children.text: अस्ति च क्वचिदुद्वेगः प्रयोगे वाग्विदां यथा ॥ ५४ ॥
children.translated_text: but in some cases there is discomfort among the learned in [certain] usages, as follows: // 54 //

children.text: इत्येवमनन्तरोक्तं लक्ष्ममादिर्यस्यान्यस्यापि तज्जातीयस्य लक्ष्यजातस्य तद् [वर्णनं] न जातुचित् न कदाचिदपि सौभाग्यं शोभां जहाति त्यजत्येव । सदैव सुभगमीदृशमित्यर्थः । भिन्नलिङ्गवचनादि किञ्चिदुद्वेगकरं विपश्चितामिति कथयतिक्वचित् प्रयोगे लक्ष्ये न सर्वत्र । उद्वेगे वैमुख्यमनादरः । अस्ति, च न केवलं नास्ति । वाग्विदां शब्दहृदयज्ञानां कवीनाम् । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: 'Such as described above' — the class of examples whose character is as just stated, and others of the same kind — never, not even once, loses its charm — that is, its beauty. It is always beautiful — this is the meaning. He says that some things with difference of gender, number, and so forth cause discomfort to the discerning: 'in some usages' — that is, in some examples, not everywhere. Discomfort means aversion, disregard. [Such discomfort] does exist, and it is not merely absent. 'Among the learned' — among poets who know the heart of language. He illustrates with 'as follows.'
The moon is white like a female goose; the sky is spotless like ponds.

children.text: भर्तृभक्तो भटः श्वेव खद्योतो भाति भानुवत् ॥ ५५ ॥
children.translated_text: A soldier devoted to his master is like a dog; a firefly shines like the sun. // 55 //

children.text: हंसीव धवलश्चन्द्र इति लिङ्गभेदः । सरांसीवामलं नभ इति वचनभेदः । भर्तृभक्तो भटः श्वेवेति हीनेन जात्यादिना अधिक उपमितः । खद्योतो ज्योतिरिङ्गणः भाति भानुवत् इत्यधिकेन हीन उपमीयत इति ॥
children.translated_text: 'The moon is white like a female goose' — here there is difference of gender. 'The sky is spotless like ponds' — here there is difference of number. 'A soldier devoted to his master is like a dog' — here the superior is compared to something inferior in birth and so forth. 'A firefly shines like the sun' — here the inferior is compared to the superior.
He shows that such [usage] of this kind is to be avoided:

children.text: ईदृशं वर्ज्यते सद्भिः कारणं तत्र चिन्त्यताम् ।
children.translated_text: Such [usage] is rejected by the good; let the reason for that be considered
by the wise themselves, for the discrimination of merits and faults. // 56 //

children.text: ईदृशम् इत्थंमूतं सद्भिः कविभिरुचितविद्वद्भिः वर्ज्यते नाद्रियते । नियतं तावदेतत् । किं कारणमिति चेत् ? अत्रेदृशस्य वर्जने कारणं तु निमित्तं पुनः किञ्चित् स्वयमेव चिन्त्यतां निरूप्यताम् । नात्रास्माकमभिनिवेशः । अयमाशयः । ईदृशमशिष्टेष्टमप्रतीतं न सौभाग्यभाजनम् । अतश्चोद्वेगकरत्वाद् वर्ज्यते । न च ते पर्यनुयोगमर्हन्ति, प्रमाणत्वात् सर्वथा तेषाम् । केवलं तत्प्रयोगमार्गः प्रकृतिसुभगोऽस्माभिरनुगम्यते । यदि पुनस्तैराद्रियेत, के वयं वर्जयितुम् ? सुभगमेव तदेदृशं तल्लक्षणत्वादिह सौभाग्यस्येति । तथा च व[क्ष्य]ते

children.translated_text: 'But what is sanctioned by the cultured is not faulty.'
And in this manner, the following is objectionable:

Such — of this nature — is rejected, that is, not accepted, by the good — that is, by poets who are properly learned. This much is certain. If asked, 'What is the reason?' — the reason, that is, the cause, for rejecting such [usage] should be considered, that is, examined, by [the reader] himself. We do not insist on this point. The purport is this: such [usage], which is not sanctioned by the cultured, which is unfamiliar, is not a vessel of charm. Therefore, because it causes discomfort, it is rejected. Nor do those [authorities] deserve to be questioned, since they are authoritative in every respect. We merely follow their well-trodden path of usage, which is naturally beautiful. If, however, it were accepted by them, who are we to reject it? It would indeed be beautiful, being characterized by their standard of charm. And thus it will be said:

children.text: चन्द्रो हंस इवाभाति नभः सर इवामलम् ।
children.translated_text: The moon shines like a goose; the sky is spotless like a lake.

children.text: भटो बन्धुरिव स्निग्ध खद्योतो भाति दीपवत् ॥
children.translated_text: A soldier is affectionate like a kinsman; a firefly shines like a lamp.

children.text: प्रतीतमीदृशं सदा तत्समुचित[मनु]द्वेजनीयमेव, तद्विपर्ययात्तु पूर्वकमरञ्जकम् । अनेन

children.translated_text: [he addresses the following]:
Inferiority, impossibility, difference of gender and number, reversal,
and superiority of the standard of comparison, and thereby dissimilarity too —
these seven faults of simile have been stated by the wise.
This alternative view has been rendered non-absolute [by <s>Daṇḍin</s>].
Such [usage], which is well-established, is always appropriate and unobjectionable. The previous [examples], being the opposite of that, are unpleasing. By all this —

children.text: यद्यप्युपमानोपमेयभूतं वस्तु चन्द्रमुखादिशब्दवाच्यम्, तथापि इवादिशब्दव्यतिरेकेण सादृश्यमभिव्यक्ति न यातीति तदभिव्यञ्जकान् शब्दान् व्यवहारं व्युत्पत्तये दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Although the object that serves as standard or subject of comparison is denoted by words like 'moon-face' and so forth, still, without words such as 'like' (<s>iva</s>) and others, the similarity does not become manifest. Therefore, in order to teach the words that indicate similarity — that is, their usage and derivation — he says:
The words <s>iva</s>, <s>vat</s>, <s>vā</s>, <s>yathā</s>; <s>samāna</s>, <s>nibha</s>, <s>sannibha</s>;
<s>tulya</s>, <s>saṃkāśa</s>, <s>nokāśa</s>, <s>prakāśa</s>, <s>pratirūpaka</s>; // 57 //
<s>pratipakṣa</s>, <s>pratidvandvin</s>, <s>pratyanīka</s>, <s>virodhin</s>;
<s>sadṛk</s>, <s>sadṛśa</s>, <s>saṃvādin</s>, <s>sajātīya</s>, <s>anuvādin</s>; // 58 //
<s>pratibimba</s>, <s>praticchanda</s>, <s>sarūpa</s>, <s>sama</s>, <s>sammita</s>;
<s>salakṣaṇa</s>, <s>sadṛkṣa</s>, <s>ābha</s>, <s>sapakṣa</s>, <s>upamita</s>, <s>upamā</s>; // 59 //
<s>kalpa</s>, <s>deśīya</s>, <s>deśya</s>, and so forth; also <s>prakhya</s> and <s>pratinidhi</s>;
<s>savarṇa</s> and <s>tulita</s> — and whatever other words are synonymous with these; // 60 //
and the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound in expressions like 'moon-faced' (<s>śaśāṅkavadana</s>) and the like;
[verbs such as] 'rivals' (<s>spardhate</s>), 'surpasses' (<s>jayati</s>), 'envies' (<s>dveṣṭi</s>), 'bears malice' (<s>druhyati</s>), 'roars back at' (<s>pratigarjati</s>); // 61 //
'reviles' (<s>ākrośati</s>), 'disdains' (<s>avajānāti</s>), 'ill-treats' (<s>kadarthayati</s>), 'reproaches' (<s>nindati</s>);
'mimics' (<s>viḍambayati</s>), 'obstructs' (<s>saṃrunddhe</s>), 'laughs at' (<s>hasati</s>), 'is jealous of' (<s>īṣyati</s>), 'is envious of' (<s>asūyati</s>); // 62 //

children.text: तस्य मुष्णाति सौभाग्यं तस्य कान्तिं विलुम्पति ।
children.translated_text: 'steals the beauty of that one,' 'robs the radiance of that one,'
'contends with that one,' 'ascends the scale against that one'; // 63 //

children.text: तत्पदव्यां पदं धत्ते तस्य कक्षां विगाहते ।
children.translated_text: 'sets foot in that one's path,' 'enters that one's domain,'
'follows and pursues that one,' 'emulates that one's nature,' 'challenges that one'; // 64 //
and 'imitates that one' — these are the words that indicate similarity.
These have been declared [as operative] in simile, giving delight to the intellect of poets. // 65 //

children.text: इवश्च वच्च यथा च ते शब्दाश्चेति विग्रहः । समाननिभसन्निभाः पूर्ववच्चार्थः । शब्दा इति वक्ष्यमाणमपेक्ष्य पुंस्त्वमिति ॥ तुल्यादिष्वप्यनन्तरो[क्तेषु तथैव] वाच्यमिति । सदृशादिकमपि पूर्ववत् सुगममिति ॥ सलक्षणादीनामपि सैव रीतिः ॥ आदिशब्देन बहुजादिपरिग्रहः ।
children.translated_text: The analysis is: <s>iva</s>, <s>vat</s>, <s>yathā</s>, and those other words. <s>Samāna</s>, <s>nibha</s>, <s>sannibha</s> — these have the same meaning as the preceding. The masculine gender [of 'words'] is used in anticipation of what will be stated later. The same should be said regarding <s>tulya</s> and the other terms [listed] immediately after. <s>Sadṛśa</s> and the rest are also easy to understand, as before. The same procedure applies to <s>salakṣaṇa</s> and the rest as well. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), terms like <s>bahuja</s> and others are included.
'This <s>Kuṇāla</s> is [like] one of many oceans, the beloved' [?]

children.text: इत्यादि च लक्ष्यमालक्ष्यमिति ॥ सवर्णेत्यादि । ये चान्यूनं सममर्थं वदन्ति सधर्मसाधारणसच्छायादयोऽनुक्ताः तेऽपि शब्दाः सादृश्यसूचिन इत्यवेक्षणीयम् । शशाङ्क इव वदनं यस्याः सा तथा । आदि शब्देनोत्पलाक्ष्यादिपरिग्रहः । तेषु प्रयोगेषु समासश्च बहुव्रीहिरन्यपदार्थः । सादृश्यसूचक इत्यपेक्षमिति ॥ स्पर्द्धत इत्यादि सुगममिति । एते सर्वे शब्दा यथोक्ताः सादृश्यम् उपमानोपमेययोः साम्यं सूचयन्ति व्यञ्जयन्तीति सादृश्यसूचिनः प्रतिपत्तव्या इति उपमाप्रपञ्चः ॥
children.translated_text: — such and other examples should be noted as illustrative instances. Regarding <s>savarṇa</s> and so forth: other words not explicitly mentioned that express equal meaning — such as <s>sadharma</s>, <s>sādhāraṇa</s>, <s>sacchāya</s>, and the like — should also be recognized as indicators of similarity. In [the compound] 'one whose face is like the moon' (<s>śaśāṅkavadanā</s>) — she is so described. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), [compounds like] <s>utpalākṣī</s> (lotus-eyed) and others are included. In those usages, the compound — specifically the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, which conveys the meaning of another word — is to be understood as an indicator of similarity. [The verbs] 'rivals' (<s>spardhate</s>) and so forth are easy to understand. All these words as described indicate similarity — that is, the likeness between the standard and the object of comparison — and should be understood as indicators of similarity. Thus concludes the elaboration of <s>upamā</s> (simile).
Thus ends the chapter on <s>upamā</s> (simile).
Defining <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), he says:
Simile itself, with the distinction [between the two] concealed, is called <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor),
as in: 'arm-creeper,' 'hand-lotus,' 'foot-sprout.' // 66 //

children.text: उपमैव यथोक्तलक्षणा रूपकमिष्यते तज्ज्ञैः । न कश्चित् तर्हि विशेषः तयोर्नाममात्रं भिद्यत इत्याह—तिरोभूतभेदेति । तिरोभूतोऽप्रकटो भेदो नानात्वम् उपमानोप-

मेययोरभेदारोपणात् यस्यां तथाभूता सती रूपकं नाम अलङ्कारः कल्प्यत इति भेदोद्भवाभिभवप्रभावितं नानात्वम् अनयोर्व्यञ्जनेन शब्दाभेदमात्रं रूपयति । उपमा[नोपमेययो]रभेदमारोपयति इति रूपकम् । यथेत्युदाहरति—बाहुर्लतातुल्यो लतारूपेण निरूप्यते इत्यभेदारोपः । तिरोहितो भेदः । नतूद्भेदः । बाहुर्लते एवेति
children.translated_text: is concealed, i.e., not manifest, due to the superimposition of non-difference between them — [the simile] being of such a nature is conceived as the ornament called <s>rūpaka</s>. The diversity produced by the emergence and suppression of difference between these two is expressed merely through verbal non-differentiation — it gives form to [the comparison]. [The figure] that superimposes non-difference upon the standard and the object of comparison is <s>rūpaka</s>. He illustrates with 'as follows' — the arm is equal to a creeper and is represented in the form of a creeper; this is the superimposition of non-difference. The distinction is concealed, not manifest. It is not the case that the arm simply is a creeper.

children.text: । पाणिरेव पद्मं चरण एव पल्लवमित्यभेदाध्यासः पूर्ववदिति ॥
children.translated_text: The hand itself is the lotus; the foot itself is the sprout — this is the superimposition of non-difference, as before.

Simile itself, having the characteristics as described, is regarded by the learned as <s>rūpaka</s>. If there is no difference between them, then only the name differs — to this he says: 'with the distinction concealed.' Where the distinction — that is, the difference, the separateness — between the standard and the object of comparison
The fingers became sprouts, the nails' radiance [became] blossoms;
the arms [became] creepers — you are the beauty of spring walking before us! // 67 //

children.text: हे वसन्तश्रीः कुसुमागमलक्ष्मीः ! त्वं भवती नः अस्माकम् प्रत्यक्षेऽर्थसाक्षात्कारिणि ज्ञाने चरसि प्रतिभासि । न परोक्षवर्तिनी । प्रत्यक्षं यथा भवति तथा चरसीति क्रियाविशेषणोपपदाद्वा क्रियार्थाद्विधिः । कथयामि तावत् पल्लवानि किसलयसम्पदस्तानि ताम्रतादेस्तवाङ्गुल्य आसन् अभूवन् अदृश्यन्त इति यावत् । यानि चेमानि पल्लवसङ्गतानि कुसुमानि तानि तव नखार्चिषः कररुहरुचयः शौक्ल्यादिना, लते च द्वे विवक्षिंते केचित् तव बाहु[भूते] मार्दवादेः । इति प्रत्यक्षाङ्गत्वात् त्वं नश्चाक्षुषी । यद्वा, वराङ्गि ! प्र[त्यक्ष]चारिणी वसन्तश्रीस्त्वमेवास्माकम्, किमन्यया अप्रत्यक्षया । यास्तवाङ्गुल्य[स्ताः] पल्लवान्यासन् । नखार्चिषश्च कुसुमानि । बाहू ते लते । ततस्त्वं नश्चाक्षुषी प्रत्यक्षा वसन्तश्रीः । शेषं पूर्ववत् ॥
children.translated_text: O beauty of spring, <s>kusumāgamalakṣmī</s> (splendor of the flower season)! You move in our direct perception — not in the realm of the imperceptible. 'You move as direct perception does' — thus the injunction arises from the qualifying adverb of the action, or from the purpose of the action. Let me explain: the <s>pallavas</s> (sprouts), those riches of new shoots — they were your fingers, due to their coppery hue and so forth. And these flowers attached to the sprouts — they were the radiance of your nails, the luster of your fingernails, due to their whiteness and the like. Some interpret the two creepers as [being] your arms, due to softness and so forth. Thus, because of having perceptible limbs, you are visible to our eyes. Alternatively: O beautiful one! You who move visibly are the beauty of spring itself for us — what need is there of another, imperceptible one? Your fingers were the sprouts; the radiance of your nails, the flowers; your arms, the creepers. Therefore you are our visible beauty of spring, perceptible to the eyes. The rest is as before.
By what name is this called? He says —
This is called <s>asamasta</s> (uncompounded); the earlier <s>rūpaka</s> was <s>samasta</s> (compounded);
'The smile is the moonlight of the moon-face' — this is <s>samasta-vyasta rūpaka</s> (mixed compounded-and-uncompounded metaphor). // 68 //

children.text: इत्येतदीदृशम् अस[म]स्तमित्याख्या संज्ञा यस्येत्यसमस्ताख्यं व्यस्तं नाम रूपकं प्रतिपत्तव्यम्, उपमानोपमेयरोरकृतसमासत्वात् । यत्र समासः । तत् किमाख्यायते ? पूर्वरूपकं बाहू लतेत्यादि । कृतसमासं प्रथममुदाहरणम् । समस्तं तादृशं वेदितव्यम्, समासयोगात् । मुखमिवेन्दुर्मुखेन्दुरिति समस्तम् । स्मितं लीलाहसितं ज्योत्स्ना चन्द्रिकेति व्यस्तम् । अतश्च समस्तं तद् व्यस्तं चेति समस्तव्यस्तं नामेदृशं रूपकमवगन्तव्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: This of such a kind, whose designation is '<s>asamasta</s>' (uncompounded), should be understood as <s>vyasta</s> (separated) <s>rūpaka</s>, because no compound has been formed between the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison). Where there is a compound — what is that called? The earlier <s>rūpaka</s>, 'arms are creepers' and so forth. The first example, which has a compound, should be known as <s>samasta</s> (compounded), because of the employment of a compound. 'The face is like the moon — <s>mukhendu</s> (face-moon)' — this is compounded. 'The smile, the playful laughter, is moonlight' — this is uncompounded. And thus, what is both compounded and uncompounded — such a <s>rūpaka</s> should be understood as <s>samasta-vyasta</s> (compounded-and-uncompounded).
With coppery fingers as the row of petals, with the radiance of nails as filaments,
your foot-lotus is held upon the heads by kings. // 69 //

children.text: राजन्, भवतश्चरण एव पङ्कजं भूपालैः ध्रियते धार्यते मूर्ध्नि शिरसि । किम्भूतम् ? ताम्राङ्गुलयो दलश्रेणिः पत्रपंक्तिर्यस्य । नखानां दीधितयः किरणाः केसराणि यत्र तादृशं ध्रियते इति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: O king, your foot itself is the lotus, held — that is, borne — upon the head by kings. Of what nature? That whose coppery fingers are the row of petals, whose nails' rays are the filaments — such it is that is held. This is the main point.
Which <s>rūpaka</s> is this? He says —
Superimposing petal-nature and the like upon the fingers and the like, and lotus-nature upon the foot,
because of placement in an appropriate location, this is <s>sakala rūpaka</s> (complete metaphor). // 70 //

children.text: एतदनन्तरोक्तमीदृशं सकलरूपकम् आख्यायते । सकलस्याङ्गिनः पादस्याङ्गस्य चाङ्गुल्यादीनां रूपणात् । अङ्गुलिरादिर्यस्या नखदीधितेस्तत्र दलमादिर्यस्य केसरस्य तस्य भावः तत्त्वं तदारोप्य इत्यङ्गरूप
णमुक्तम् । पादे च पद्मतामारोप्य उपचर्येति अङ्गिरूपणं तस्येदृशस्य पद्मस्य योग्यमुचितम् । स्थीयते इति स्थानम् आधारो मूर्द्धा तत्र विन्यासात् निवेशनात् । सकलरूपकमेतदिति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: And superimposing lotus-nature upon the foot — this is the identification of the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>). The appropriate, fitting location of such a lotus — '<s>sthīyate</s>' means '<s>sthāna</s>' (place), the support being the head — because of placement there, this is <s>sakala rūpaka</s>. This is the main point.

This, described immediately after, is designated as <s>sakala rūpaka</s> (complete metaphor) — because of the metaphorical identification of both the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>, the foot) and the parts (<s>aṅga</s>, the fingers and the like). The finger is the first among the nails' radiance; upon that, the petal is the first among the filaments — superimposing the nature of that, the identification of the parts is stated.
Suddenly, O angry one! Your face with its quivering lip-sprout
bears clusters of perspiration-drops with the luster of pearls. // 71 //

children.text: चण्डि कोपने ! ते तव मुखं स्फुरिताधरपल्लवं स्फुरितः कोपकम्पनः अधरः ताम्रतादेः पल्लवो यस्येति । घर्माम्भःकणाः प्रणयकोपजन्मानः स्वेदबिन्दव एव मञ्जयः कुसुमस्तबकाः शौक्ल्यादिना । यदाह—मुक्तारुच इति । मुक्तानां रुचयो दीप्तयो यासां ता धत्ते । अकस्मादेव विना व्यलीकेन केनचित् तादृशेन, कोऽयमस्थानकोप इति ॥
children.translated_text: O angry one (<s>caṇḍī</s>)! Your face has a quivering lip-sprout — 'quivering' means trembling with anger; the lip, due to its coppery hue, is the sprout. The drops of perspiration (<s>gharmāmbhaḥkaṇa</s>), born of lovers' anger, are themselves the flower-clusters (<s>mañjarī</s>), due to their whiteness and the like. As stated — 'with the luster of pearls' (<s>muktāruci</s>): those which have the brilliance of pearls — it bears them. 'Suddenly' — without any reason whatsoever, such as an offense. 'What is this misplaced anger?' — this is the import.
Which <s>rūpaka</s> is this? He says —
Making the perspiration into flower-clusters, and making the lip into a sprout,
the face here is not otherwise transformed — therefore this is <s>avayava rūpaka</s> (partial metaphor). // 72 //

children.text: धर्माम्बु मञ्जरीत्वेन परिकल्प्य । अधरं चैकदेशं पल्लवीकृत्य पल्लवोऽयमिति रूपयित्वा । आस्यं मुखम् अङ्गि अन्यथा नःकृतम् । पद्मादित्वेन न रूपितमत्र प्रयोगे ।

children.translated_text: For this reason, such a <s>rūpaka</s> is called <s>avayava rūpaka</s> (partial metaphor), because only the parts such as the lip are metaphorically identified.

Having conceived the perspiration as flower-clusters, and having made the lip, a single part, into a sprout — that is, having metaphorically identified it as 'this is a sprout' — the face, the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>), is not otherwise transformed; it is not identified as a lotus or the like in this usage.
With dancing eyebrows, with flowing perspiration, with reddened eyes,
this face-lotus reveals the state of intoxication. // 73 //

children.text: वल्गिते आरेचिते भ्रुवौ । गलच्च घर्मजलम् । आलोहिते च ईक्षणे यत्र तदिदं वदनं पङ्कजं मदस्य मधुपानजनितस्य हर्षविशेषस्य अवस्थाम् ईदृशविकारलीलाजनितलक्षणां दशां विवृणोति प्रकाशयतीति ॥
children.translated_text: The eyebrows are dancing, that is, raised up. The perspiration is flowing. And the eyes are reddened — such is this face, [called] a lotus, which reveals, that is, manifests, the state of intoxication (<s>mada</s>), the particular joy born of drinking, the condition characterized by such playful transformations.
What <s>rūpaka</s> is this called? He says —
Without transforming the parts of the face, the face itself was made into a lotus;
therefore this is <s>avayavi rūpaka</s> (whole-metaphor). // 74 //

children.text: मुखस्य अङ्गिनः अङ्गानि अवयवान् नेत्रादीन् अविकृत्य रूपयित्वा मुखमेवाङ्गि अरविन्दतां गमितमासीत् पद्मत्वेन रूपितम् । अत्र लक्ष्ये । अतोऽवयविरूपकमिदमीदृशम्, अवयविन एव रूपितत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Without metaphorically transforming the parts — the eyes and the like — of the face, the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>), the face itself, the whole, was made into a lotus, that is, identified as a lotus. In this example — therefore this is <s>avayavi rūpaka</s>, of such a kind, because only the whole is metaphorically identified.
With cheeks reddened by intoxication, with reddened eye-lotuses,

children.text: मुखेन मुग्धे ! सोऽप्येष जनो रागमयः कृतः ॥ ७५ ॥
children.translated_text: by your face, O innocent one, even that person has been made full of passion! // 75 //

children.text: मदेन पाटलौ गण्डौ कपोलौ रक्ते च नेत्रे उत्पले यत्र तेन ते मुखेन सोऽप्येष जनो यः त्वत्प्रसादैकवृत्तिः परमुखेनात्मानमाह कश्चित्कामुको रागमयो रागविकारः किमपि रक्तः कृतः न केवलं स्वयं रक्तमित्यपि शब्दः । मुग्ध इत्यामन्त्रणम् इति ॥
children.translated_text: The cheeks are reddened by intoxication, and the eyes are lotuses in which there is redness — by such a face of yours, even that person, who depends solely on your favor (speaking of himself in the third person), a certain lover, has been made full of passion (<s>rāgamaya</s>), transformed by passion, somehow reddened — not merely the face itself is reddened; thus the word applies [to both]. '<s>Mugdha</s>' is a vocative address, meaning 'O innocent one.'
This is a one-part metaphor; similarly, those with two parts and more also [exist];
the parts are metaphorically identified here — their compatibility and incompatibility create the distinction. // 76 //

children.text: एतच्च एकाङ्गरूपकम् एकस्यैव नेत्रलक्ष्मस्याङ्गस्य रूपणात् । एवम् अनेन प्रकारेण द्विप्रभृतीन्यपि न केवलमेकम् । द्वे त्रीणि चत्वारि इति यथासम्भवमङ्गानि अवयवान् रूपयन्ति यथायोगमर्थान्तररूपेण आरोप्य प्रयुञ्जते कवयः । अत्राङ्गरूपणे योगः सङ्गतिः अङ्गानामयोगश्च विरोधः । भिदाकरौ रूपकभेदव्यवस्थापकौ । योगायोग
भेदेनैतद्रूपकं व्यवह्नियते । न तु पूर्ववत् संख्याभेदेनेत्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: this <s>rūpaka</s> is designated. But not by distinction of number as before — this is the meaning.

This is <s>ekāṅga rūpaka</s> (one-part metaphor), because only one part, the beauty of the eye, is metaphorically identified. Similarly, by this method, there are also those beginning with two — not merely one. Two, three, four — poets metaphorically identify as many parts as is appropriate, superimposing them in the form of something else, and employ them accordingly. Here in the metaphorical identification of parts, <s>yoga</s> (compatibility) means the congruence of the parts, and <s>ayoga</s> (incompatibility) means their contradiction — these two create the distinction, that is, they establish the varieties of <s>rūpaka</s>. Through the distinction of compatibility and incompatibility,
This face, radiant with smile-flowers, with restless eye-bees,
is called <s>yukta rūpaka</s> (congruent metaphor), due to the congruence of flowers and bees. // 77 //

children.text: स्मितं पुष्पं शौक्ल्यादिना तेन उज्ज्वलं सुभगं लोले नेत्रे भृङ्गौ चञ्चलत्वादिना यस्य मुखस्येतीदृशम् [युक्त]रूपकमाख्यायते । ननु कथम् ? पुष्पाणां द्विरेफाणां च सङ्गत्या परस्परसम्बन्धादिति ॥
children.translated_text: The smile is the flower, due to whiteness and the like; by it [the face is] radiant, beautiful. The restless eyes are the bees, due to their fickleness and the like — of such a face, this is designated as <s>yukta rūpaka</s> (congruent metaphor). But how? Because of the congruence (<s>saṅgati</s>), the mutual relationship, of flowers and bees.
This face has moist smile-moonlight and tender eye-lotuses —
due to the incongruence of moonlight and lotuses, this is called <s>ayukta rūpaka</s> (incongruent metaphor). // 78 //

children.text: इदं मुखम् आर्द्रं स्निग्धं स्मितं ज्योत्स्ना, स्निग्धे नेत्रे उत्पले [च] यस्य इत्येवंविधमयुक्तं नाम रूपकम् । कुतः ज्योत्स्नया उत्पलस्य अयोगात् विरोधात्, ज्योत्स्नायामुत्पलस्य सङ्कोचादिति ॥
children.translated_text: This face — the moist, tender smile is the moonlight; the tender eyes are the lotuses — such is the <s>ayukta rūpaka</s> (incongruent metaphor). Why? Because of the incongruence, the contradiction, of moonlight with the lotus, since the lotus closes in moonlight.
Through the metaphorical identification of the whole, and through recourse to both identification and non-identification of the parts,

children.text: रूपकं विषमं नाम ललितं जायते यथा ॥ ७९ ॥
children.translated_text: a <s>rūpaka</s> called <s>viṣama</s> (uneven) arises beautifully, as follows: // 79 //

children.text: अङ्गिनोऽवयविनः रूपणात् यथायोगम् अर्थान्तरीकरणात् । अङ्गानां रूपणमरूपणं च तयोराश्रयणम् [तस्माद्][आ]श्रयात् अपेक्षणाद्रूपणादरूपणाच्चेत्यर्थः । ततो विषमं रूपकं ललितं चारुजायते । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Through the metaphorical identification of the whole (<s>avayavin</s>), that is, the appropriate superimposition of another meaning. And through recourse to both the identification and non-identification of the parts — that is, depending on both identification and non-identification. From that, the <s>viṣama rūpaka</s> (uneven metaphor) arises beautifully. 'As follows' — he gives an example:
With cheeks reddened by intoxication, <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), by means of your face-moon
with dancing brow-creepers, is able to crush the three worlds! // 80 //

children.text: भुवनत्रयं मर्दितुं जेतुम् अलम् समर्थो मन्मथः । केन ? मदेन रक्तौ कपोलौ यस्य नर्तिते भ्रुवौ लते लोलतादिना येन तेन तव मुखेन इन्दुना करणेन च मुखस्याङ्गिनो रूपणं भ्रूलक्षणस्य च तदङ्गस्य रूपणमेव । कपोलरूपस्य त्वङ्गस्यारूपणमिति ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Manmatha</s> is able, that is, capable of crushing, conquering, the three worlds. By what means? By your face, which is the moon — whose cheeks are reddened by intoxication, whose eyebrows are creepers set dancing by their restlessness — as the instrument. Here the metaphorical identification of the face, the whole, and of the eyebrow, its part, is maintained. But there is no metaphorical identification of the cheek, which is also a part.
The foot of <s>Hari</s>, with the water of <s>Jahnukanyā</s> (the Ganges) clinging to its tip as a garment,
is victorious — it is the banner of the festival of joy for the gods, freed from fear of the <s>Asuras</s>! // 81 //

children.text: हरेर्विष्णोः विक्रममाणस्य पादो जयति विपक्षमभिभवति । शिरस्यग्रे भागेऽङ्गुलीदेशे लग्नमवस्थितं जह्नुकन्याजलम् । ब्रह्मणा किल तदानीम् अर्घीकृतं गाङ्गम्
उदकम् । अंशुकं पताकारूपं यत्र स तथा । असुरेभ्यो हरिनिर्जितेभ्यो निःशंका निर्भयास्तदुपक्रमशङ्काविगमात् । ये सुराः, तेषामानन्दः प्रीतिरुत्सवो महस्तत्रोच्छ्रितो ध्वजः केतुरिति ।
children.translated_text: The water serves as the garment, in the form of a flag-cloth. Free from fear of the <s>Asuras</s>, who were defeated by <s>Hari</s>, their apprehension having been removed — the gods, whose joy, delight, and festival were elevated there, have their banner, the flag, raised aloft.

The foot of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who is striding forth, is victorious — that is, it conquers the adversary. Clinging to the top, the tip, the region of the toes, is the water of <s>Jahnukanyā</s> (the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>, i.e., the Ganges). Indeed, at that time, <s>Brahmā</s> offered the Ganges water as an <s>arghya</s> (offering).
What <s>rūpaka</s> is this called? He says —
The form of a banner complete with its qualifiers,
being superimposed upon the foot in such manner — this is <s>saviśeṣaṇa rūpaka</s> (metaphor with qualifiers). // 82 //

children.text: विशेषणेन उपाधिना पताकोत्सवसम्भवरूपेण समग्रस्य सूक्तस्य केतोर्ध्वजस्य यदीदृशस्य अनन्तरोक्तप्रकारं रूपं स्वभावः तस्यार्पणादारोपात् पादे वैष्णवेऽयं ध्वज इति एतदीदृशं सविशेषणं नाम रूपकं व्यपदिश्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: A banner complete with its qualifier — with the attribute in the form of a flag-cloth and the festive occasion — its form, that is, its nature, of such a kind as described, being superimposed upon the foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, saying 'this is a banner' — such is the <s>rūpaka</s> designated as <s>saviśeṣaṇa</s> (with qualifiers).
It does not close the lotuses, nor does it traverse the sky;
your face-moon strives only to steal my life-breaths! // 83 //

children.text: तव मुखम् इन्दुः, पद्मानि न मीलयति न संकोचयति
नभोऽपि नावगाहते । किं तर्हि करोति ? मम असूनां प्राणानां हरणायैव व्यवस्यति प्रयतते । किमिदमिति ॥
children.translated_text: nor does it traverse the sky. What then does it do? It strives, endeavors, only to steal my life-breaths. 'What is this?' —
Your face is the moon — it does not close the lotuses, does not cause them to contract;
He explains that —
The non-performance of the moon's functions and the performance of another's function
are shown here; therefore this is called <s>viruddha rūpaka</s> (contradictory metaphor). // 84 //

children.text: चन्द्रकार्याणां पद्मनिमीलनादीनाम् अक्रिया अकरणम् । अन्यस्य शस्त्रादेर्यत् कार्यं प्राणहरणं तस्य क्रिया अत्र प्रयोगे सन्दर्श्यते प्रतिपाद्यते यस्मात्, अतो विरुद्धं नामेदृशं रूपकमवगन्तव्यम् इति ॥
children.translated_text: The non-performance, the non-execution, of the moon's functions such as closing lotuses. And the performance of the function of something else, such as a weapon — namely, the taking of life — is shown, that is, demonstrated, in this usage. Therefore, such a <s>rūpaka</s> should be understood as <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory).
In depth, you are the ocean; in gravity, you are the mountain;
and because you grant the wishes of the people, you are the <s>kalpa</s>-tree (wish-fulfilling tree). // 85 //

children.text: गाम्भीर्येणानुत्तानचित्ततया समुद्रोऽसि । गौरवेण गुणलक्षणेन पर्वतोऽसि । लोकानां कामम् इष्टं ददासीति कामदत्वाच्च कल्पपादपोऽसि इति कश्चित् स्तूयत् इति ॥
children.translated_text: In depth — through the profundity of your mind — you are the ocean. In gravity — by the quality thus characterized — you are the mountain. Because you give the people their desires, their wishes — because of being a wish-granter — you are the <s>kalpapādapa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree). Thus someone is praised.
What <s>rūpaka</s> is this? He says —
Here, through causes such as depth and the others,
one is made into the ocean, the mountain, and the <s>kalpa</s>-tree — therefore this is <s>hetu rūpaka</s> (causal metaphor). // 86 //

children.text: अत्र प्रयोगे गाम्भीर्यं प्रमुखमादि येषां गौरवादीनां तैः हेतुभिः कारणैः कश्चित् विवक्षितः पुरुषः सागरः क्रियते, गिरिश्च कल्पद्रुमश्च क्रियते रूप्यते यतः, तत् तस्मात् इदम् एवंविधं हेतुरूपकम् अवसेयम् । तदिदमनन्तरोक्तं हेतुरूपकमिति योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: In this usage, through causes — reasons — such as depth being the foremost, along with gravity and the rest, a certain intended person is made into the ocean, made into the mountain, and made into the <s>kalpa</s>-tree — that is, metaphorically identified. Because of that, this kind is to be understood as <s>hetu rūpaka</s> (causal metaphor). This just-described is to be construed as <s>hetu rūpaka</s>.
Worthy of enjoyment by the <s>rājahaṃsa</s> (royal swan), with fragrance sought by bees —
O friend, this face-lotus of yours — thus it is <s>śliṣṭa rūpaka</s> (punning metaphor). // 87 //

children.text: सखि, तव वक्त्राम्बुजमिदं चारु [राज]हंसोपभोगार्हम् । पद्मं तावत् राजहंसैः पक्षिविशेषैः उपभोगं निषेवणम् अर्हति, तदुपभोग्यमिति यावत् । तव वक्त्राम्बुजं तु राजहंसैः नृपवरैः उपभोगमर्हतीति शब्दश्लेषः । उभयमपि भ्रमरैः प्रार्थ्यम् अभिलषणीयं सौरभं गन्धविशेषोऽस्येति भ्रमरप्रार्थ्यसौरभमित्यर्थश्लेषः । ईदृशं श्लिष्टरूपकमिष्टम्, श्लेषानुविद्धत्वात् इति ॥
children.translated_text: O friend, this face-lotus of yours is beautiful, worthy of enjoyment by the <s>rājahaṃsa</s>. A lotus is enjoyed — that is, frequented — by <s>rājahaṃsas</s> (a particular species of birds); it is worthy of their enjoyment. But your face-lotus is worthy of enjoyment by <s>rājahaṃsas</s> (eminent kings) — this is the verbal <s>śleṣa</s> (pun). Both are <s>bhramaraprārthyasaurabha</s> — having fragrance desirable to bees — this is the semantic <s>śleṣa</s>. Such is the <s>śliṣṭa rūpaka</s> (punning metaphor), because it is pervaded by <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).
The showing of similarity and dissimilarity between the secondary and the primary [senses] is approved;
accordingly, there is a pair of <s>rūpakas</s> called <s>upamā</s>-<s>rūpaka</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>-<s>rūpaka</s>, as follows: // 88 //

children.text: उपमारूपकं व्यतिरेकरूपकमिति रूपकद्वितयमिदमपरमिष्टं शिष्टैः । उपमेति व्यतिरेक इति वा आख्या संज्ञा तदेकदेशत्वाद्यस्येति विग्रहः कृतः । गौणस्य आरोपितस्य मुखस्य च प्रधानस्यानुपचितस्य साधर्म्यं साम्यं वैधर्म्यम् असाम्यं च तयोर्दशनात् प्रकाशनात् कारणात् । यथेति उदाहरति—
children.translated_text: The pair of <s>rūpakas</s> — <s>upamā rūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) and <s>vyatireka rūpaka</s> (contrast-metaphor) — is another pair approved by the learned. The compound is analyzed as: that whose designation is '<s>upamā</s>' or '<s>vyatireka</s>', because of partially partaking in the nature of those [figures]. Because of showing — that is, revealing — the similarity and dissimilarity of the secondary (superimposed) and the primary (un-superimposed), this is the cause. 'As follows' — he gives an example:
This face-moon, reddened in hue by intoxication,
rivals the moon whose redness belongs to the time of rising. // 89 //

children.text: अयं मुखचन्द्रमाः, आलोहिता छाया प्रभा यस्य स तथा । केन ? मदेन हेतुना सन्नद्धोऽवस्थितः उदयकालभावी रागो यस्य तस्य चन्द्रस्य प्रतिगर्जति तेनोपमीयते । गौणमुख्ययोरिह रक्ततासाधर्म्यादुपमारूपकमीदृशं दृश्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: This face-moon (<s>mukhacandramā</s>) — whose hue, whose radiance, is reddened. By what? By intoxication, as the cause. It rivals — that is, it is compared with — the moon whose redness belongs to the time of rising, whose redness is present at the time of its appearance. Here, because of the similarity in redness between the secondary and the primary, this should be seen as <s>upamā rūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor).
The moon is drunk by the gods; your face-moon is drunk by me;
although that one is ever incomplete, this one is always of full orb. // 90 //

children.text: चन्द्रमा मुख्यः पीयते देवैरमृतमयत्वात् पर्यायेण सुरैः चन्द्रः पीयते यतः क्रमेणापचीयत इति श्रुतेः । अत एवासमग्रोऽप्यसौ मुख्यश्चन्द्रः । न केवलं समग्र एवेत्यपिशब्दः । मया तव मुखचन्द्रमाः पीयते निषेव्यते । तथाप्ययं तव मुखचन्द्रमाः आपूर्णमखण्डं मण्डलं यस्येत्यापूर्णमण्डलः शश्वत् अनवरतं न कदाचित् अन्यथेति गौणमुख्ययोर्वैधर्म्यात् व्यतिरेकरूपकमिदमीदृशमिति ॥
children.translated_text: The moon in the primary sense is drunk by the gods because it is made of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) — as the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) states, 'the moon is drunk by the gods in turn, since it wanes gradually.' Therefore, even when incomplete, that primary moon [wanes]. The word 'api' (even) means: not only when full. By me, your face-moon is drunk — that is, enjoyed. Nevertheless, your face-moon is <s>āpūrṇamaṇḍala</s> (of ever-full orb), meaning one whose disc is unbroken and complete, perpetually, unceasingly, never otherwise — thus, due to the dissimilarity between the secondary and primary [senses], this is such a <s>vyatireka rūpaka</s> (contrast-metaphor).
The moon-nature of your face-moon, which thus torments another,
is not fitting, O beautiful one — this is <s>ākṣepa rūpaka</s> (rejection-metaphor). // 91 //

children.text: सुन्दरि ! तव मुखचन्द्रस्येत्थमेवमिति आत्मसंवेद्यतामुपतापस्य दर्शयति । अन्यमिमं जनमुपतापयतः । परमुखेन आत्मानमाह—चन्द्रत्वं न संवादि न यथार्थमेकान्तशीतत्वाच्चन्द्रस्यास्य च तद्विपरीतत्वात् । इतीदृशं चन्द्रत्वनिषेधादाक्षेपरूप[क]मवसेयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: O beautiful one! 'Thus' means 'in this manner' — he shows that the torment is self-experienced. Of [the face-moon] that torments this other person — he speaks of himself indirectly — the moon-nature is not fitting, is not accurate, because the [real] moon is exclusively cool while this [face-moon] is the opposite thereof. Thus, because of the negation of moon-nature, this should be understood as <s>ākṣepa rūpaka</s> (rejection-metaphor).

children.text: मुखेन्दुरपि ते चण्डि ! मां निर्दहति निर्दयम् ।
children.translated_text: Your face-moon too, O fierce one, burns me mercilessly;
it is merely the fault of my destiny — that is <s>samādhāna rūpaka</s> (reconciliation-metaphor). // 92 //

children.text: चण्डि निर्दये ! एकान्तप्रीतिकरः तव मुखेन्दुः अतिनिर्दयम् अत्यर्थं मां निर्दहति । नैतद्युज्यत इत्ययोगमपिशब्दः सूचयति । न केवलम् इन्दुरिंति वा [अपि] शब्दः समुच्चिनोति । अथवा किं न युज्यते ? संभाव्यते सर्वमीदृशमपि भाग्यपरावृत्तौ, यदाह—भाग्यदोषो ममैव इति ममैवायं भाग्यदोषः अभाग्यं यदेवं भवति । न तव मुखचन्द्रस्यायं दोषः । इत्येवंरूपं यत् तदीदृशं समाधानरूपकमित्थं समाधानाभिधानादिति ॥
children.translated_text: O fierce one, O merciless one! Your face-moon, which should be exclusively pleasing, burns me exceedingly, most mercilessly. The word 'api' (even) indicates the impropriety — it suggests: this is not fitting. Or the word 'api' conjoins: not only the [real] moon [burns]. Or alternatively, what is not fitting? Everything of this sort can be accounted for when fortune is reversed, as he says — 'it is merely the fault of my destiny' — this fault of fortune is mine alone, [meaning] my misfortune is that it happens thus. This is not the fault of your face-moon. What is of such form is this kind of <s>samādhāna rūpaka</s> (reconciliation-metaphor), so called because of the statement of reconciliation.
On this stage of the face-lotus, your eyebrow-creeper, a dancer,
performs a graceful dance — this is a delightful <s>rūpaka-rūpaka</s> (metaphor-upon-metaphor). // 93 //

children.text: सुन्दरि ! तव भ्रूलता लोलतादिना । सा च नर्तकी चित्तहरत्वादिना लीलाप्रधानं शृङ्गारमयं नृत्तं वर्णितरूपं करोति । कुत्र ? मुखं पङ्कजं कान्त्यादिना तच्च रङ्गो
नृत्यभूमिः । तत्रास्मिन्नितिं प्रत्यक्षवर्तिनि । ईदृशं रूपकरूपकं रम्यं मनोज्ञं लतीकृतायाः भ्रुवो नर्तकीकरणात् पङ्कजीकृतस्य च मुखस्य सङ्गीकृतेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: (dance-stage). 'There, in this' refers to what is present before one's eyes. Such a <s>rūpaka-rūpaka</s> (metaphor-upon-metaphor) is charming and delightful, because the eyebrow is made into a creeper and then into a dancer, and the face, made into a lotus, is then made into a stage.

O beautiful one! Your eyebrow-creeper [is called so] because of its undulating nature and so forth. And she is a dancer because of her capacity to captivate the mind and so forth; she performs a dance that is predominantly playful, full of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), of the form described. Where? The face is a lotus because of its radiance and so forth, and that [lotus] is a <s>raṅga</s>
This is not a face — this is a lotus; these are not eyes — these are two bees;
these are nothing but filaments, not the rays of your teeth. // 94 //

children.text: तव एतत् मुखं न भवति । किं तर्हि पद्मम् इदम् । एते च अत्र नेत्रे न भवतः । किं तर्हि ? भ्रमराविमौ । एताश्च दन्तार्चिषो न भवन्ति किं तु केसराण्येतानि इति ॥
children.translated_text: Your face — this is not [a face]. What then? This is a lotus. And these eyes here are not [eyes]. What then? These two are bees. And these rays of the teeth are not [rays of teeth] — rather, these are filaments.
He explains that —
By the depiction of the face and so forth as lotus and so forth,
which brings out the excellence of qualities, the true nature is concealed — this is <s>tattvāpahnava rūpaka</s> (reality-concealment metaphor). // 95 //

children.text: मुखमादिर्यस्य नेत्रादेः तस्य भावः । तत्त्वम् । तद् विनिवर्त्यैव अपहृत्यैव । न तु मुखादिकमेवैतत् पद्मादिकमिति तत्त्वम्

अपलाप्यते [अत]एवाक्षेपरूपकविलक्षणमेतत् । पद्ममादिर्यस्य भ्रमरादेः तस्य, भावः तेन लक्षितस्य रूपणात् परिकल्पनात् । मुखादेरिति गम्यते । तत्त्वापह्नवरूपकमीदृशं तत्त्वस्य वस्तुरूपस्य अपह्नवेन रूपकमिति । किमेवमाविष्कृतं स्यादित्याह—उद्भावितः प्रकाशितः । गुणस्य कान्त्यादेरुत्कर्षा[ति]शयो येन यत्र वा तत्तथोक्तमिति ॥
children.translated_text: is denied. Therefore this is distinct from <s>ākṣepa rūpaka</s> (rejection-metaphor). The state of that whose beginning is the lotus — that is, of the bee and so forth — through the depiction, the imaginative construction, marked by that [lotus-nature], of the face and so forth — this is understood. Such a <s>tattvāpahnava rūpaka</s> (reality-concealment metaphor) is a metaphor through the concealment of the true nature of the object. What is thus made manifest? He says: the excellence, the surpassing degree, of qualities such as radiance is brought out (<s>udbhāvita</s>) — that which is so described is thus termed.

The state of that whose beginning is the face — that is, of the eyes and so forth — is the true nature (<s>tattva</s>). That [true nature] is removed, taken away. It is not that the face and so forth are themselves the lotus and so forth — rather, the true nature

body.text: कि[मि]यन्त एव रूप[क]भेदाः ? नेत्यपर्यवसायेन उपमासामान्येन निगमयन्नाह—
body.translated_text: Are these the only varieties of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor)? No — with the indication that they are inexhaustible, and concluding with the general [topic of] <s>upamā</s> (simile), he says —

children.translated_text: There is no end to the varieties of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>upamā</s> (simile); therefore
only a direction has been shown by the wise — let what is unstated be inferred. // 96 //

body.text: रूपकस्योपमायाश्च विकल्पाः प्रभेदाः सामान्यलक्षणव्याप्ताः । तेषां पर्यन्तोऽवसानं नास्ति यतस्ततः कारणात्, दिङ्मात्रं सर्वविकल्पव्यापकसामान्यलक्षणानुगतविशेषरूपं कियदपि लक्ष्यं शेषविकल्पानुगमद्वारं दर्शितम् उक्तं धीरैः कविभिरिति परमुखेनाचष्टे । शेषमतिदिशति—अनुक्तमिहानुपात्तं विकल्पजातं सामान्यविशेष

children.text: लक्षणात्मकं तादृशमुक्तविकल्पानुसारेणानुमीयताम् ऊह्यताम् । तस्याप्येवंप्रकारत्वात् शक्यमनया दिशा तदप्यवसातुमभियुक्तैरिति ॥
children.translated_text: definitions, being of such nature, should be inferred, should be reasoned out, by following the stated varieties — since those [unstated varieties] too are of the same kind, the skilled can determine them by means of this direction.

body.translated_text: The varieties, the sub-types, of <s>rūpaka</s> and <s>upamā</s> are pervaded by a general definition. There is no end, no limit, to them; for that reason, only a direction — a few examples having the form of specific instances conforming to the general definition that pervades all varieties, serving as a gateway to the remaining varieties — has been shown, stated, by the wise, by the poets — he says this through another's words. He extends [the principle] to the rest: what is unstated here, the class of varieties not taken up, following the general and specific
For example —
O slender-limbed one, your face is equal to the moon — let this
be said by others; I do not dare to say such a thing.
Your face, with its hissing sound, is like a lotus with buzzing bees;
it is not fitting to have no courage to say this, O sweet-voiced one.
On the pair of your breasts, O slender one, a pair of <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy geese)
appears as if inseparable, resplendent with the lustre of saffron.
Thus other varieties of <s>upamā</s> (simile) too should be inferred.
Only on your face-moon, O slender one, skilled with the arrows of passion and eyelashes,
<s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) merely places his bow made of flowers.
Having reached the lovely lake that is a woman, with its blossomed face-lotuses,
how will this [person] attain peace from anguish?
Against the will of that slender woman, having abandoned her face-lotus,
O deluded mind, why do you now repent?
Thus other varieties of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) too should be inferred. This concludes the elaboration of <s>rūpaka</s>.
Thus ends the cycle of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).

children.translated_text: Illuminating <s>dīpaka</s> (the illumination figure), he says —
By a word denoting class, action, quality, or substance, occurring in one place,
if it serves all the sentences, that is called <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), as follows: // 97 //

children.text: जातिवाचिना क्रियाभिधायिना गुणप्रकाशिना द्रव्याभिलापिना वा शब्देन वाक्यावयवभूतेन केनचित् एकत्र वाक्यस्यादौ मध्येऽन्ते वा वर्तमाने[न] कर्तृभूतेन सर्वस्याभिमतस्य कस्यचिद् वाक्यस्य क्रियाकारकसम्बन्धाभिधायिनः
children.translated_text: By a word denoting class, or expressing action, or revealing quality, or naming substance — by some such word that is a component of a sentence, occurring in one place — at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence — functioning as the agent, [if it provides] service to the entire intended sentence, which expresses the relation of action and its factors (<s>kāraka</s>),

children.text: पदसन्तानस्यार्थद्वारेण सा[धन]संभवादुपकारः साध्यसाधनभावेन तदपेक्षालक्षणश्चेत् यदि भवति तदेवंरूपं दीपकमाहुः उपदिशन्ति तद्विदः । सर्व वाक्यं दीपयत्युपकरोतीति दीपकम् । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: and the service is through the meaning of the sequence of words, being possible as an instrument — if the service, characterized by the relation of means and end and the dependence thereon, exists, then such a thing is what the knowers call <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). It illuminates, that is, serves all the sentences — hence <s>dīpaka</s>. He illustrates with 'as follows.'

children.text: पवनो दक्षिणः पणें जीणें हरति वीरुधाम् ।
children.translated_text: The southern wind carries away the withered leaves of plants;
that same [wind] serves to break the pride of women with bowed limbs. // 98 //

children.text: पवनो दक्षिणो मलयानिलः । वीरुधां लतानां गुल्मानां वा सम्बन्धि पणें शीर्णं हरति क्षिपति, नताङ्गीनां मानवतीनां नवाय प्रत्यग्राय मानस्य विषयस्य वामताविशेषस्य भङ्गाय विगमार्थं च कल्पते संपद्यते । किम् ? पवनो दक्षिण इत्यपेक्षते । इह पवनजातिवाचिनादिवर्तिना सर्वमेतत् वाक्यमुपक्रियत इति जात्यादिदीपकमीदृशमवसेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: The southern wind is the <s>Malaya</s> breeze. It carries away, casts off, the withered [leaves] belonging to the plants, the creepers or shrubs. It serves, it is suited, for the breaking — the removal — of the pride, the disposition of disdain, that is fresh, that is new, of women with bowed limbs, women possessed of pride. What [serves]? It expects [the answer]: the southern wind. Here, by the word denoting the class 'wind,' placed at the beginning, this entire sentence is served — thus this should be understood as a <s>dīpaka</s> beginning with class-[word] and so forth.
Your war-elephants roam in the pleasure-gardens on the shores of the four oceans,
and your virtues, bright as <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, [roam] in the groves of the <s>Cakravāla</s> mountain. // 99 //

children.text: ते तव दन्तिनो जयकुञ्जराः चतुर्णां पूर्वादीनाम् अम्भोधीनां वेलोद्यानेषु वेलायां वेलारूपाणि वा उद्यानानीति समासः । चरन्ति क्रीडन्ति चक्रवालाद्रेर्लोकालोकाचलस्य कुञ्जेषु सिद्धाध्यासितेषु प्रदेशेषु कुन्दस्येव भासो दीप्तयो येषामिति कुन्दभासो विशदाः, तव गुणाश्च त्यागसत्यशौर्यादयः । किम् ? चरन्ति श्रुतिपथमवतरन्ति उदधिवासिनामिति कश्चित् राजा स्तूयते । अत्र चरन्तीति क्रियावाची प्रथमप्रयुक्तः सर्वमेतद्वाक्यमुपकरोतीति क्रियादीपकमेवंजातीयं विज्ञेयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Your war-elephants roam, sport, in the pleasure-gardens on the shores of the four oceans beginning with the eastern. The compound means: gardens that are on the shores, or gardens that are in the form of shores. [They roam] in the groves, in the regions inhabited by <s>Siddhas</s>, of the <s>Cakravāla</s> mountain, the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain. Having the brightness of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) — that is, radiant, lustrous — your virtues such as generosity, truthfulness, and valor — what [about them]? They roam, they reach the path of hearing. Some [commentator explains that] a certain king is being praised with 'of the ocean-dwellers.' Here the action-word 'roam,' employed first, serves this entire sentence — thus this should be known as an action-<s>dīpaka</s> of this kind.
The directions are darkened by the rows of rainy-season clouds,
and the lands [are darkened] by the delicate rows of fresh green grass. // 100 //

children.text: प्रावृषेण्याभिः वर्षासमयवर्तिनीभिः जीमूतपंक्तिभिः मेघमालाभिः दिशः श्यामलाः नीलाः वर्तन्ते । सुकुमाराभिः शाद्वलराजिभिः शष्पोद्गमैः । भुवश्च भूमयः किम् ? श्यामला इत्यपेक्षते । इह श्यामला इति पूर्ववर्तिना गुणवाचिना सर्वमिदं वाक्यमुपक्रियते इति गुणादिदीपकमित्थंभूतं विभाव्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: By the rows of clouds (<s>jīmūta</s>) belonging to the rainy season (<s>prāvṛṣ</s>), the directions are dark, blue. By the delicate rows of green grass, the sprouts — the lands too — what [about them]? It expects [the answer]: dark. Here, by the quality-word 'dark,' placed at the beginning, this entire sentence is served — thus this should be understood as a quality-<s>dīpaka</s> of this kind.
By <s>Viṣṇu</s>, exerting his valor, the splendors of the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons)
were taken somewhere [and destroyed], and the prosperities of the gods were brought from somewhere. // 101 //

children.text: विक्रमस्थेन बलिबन्धसंनद्धेन विक्रममाणेन दानवानां विभूतयः श्रियः । क्वापि क्वचित् इदन्तया अनिर्देश्ये स्थाने नीताः ।

नाशिता इति यावत् । देवतानामृद्धयो विभूतयः । कुतोऽपि स्थानादव्यपदेश्यात् । आनीता आसन् । अभूवन् । उत्पादिता इति यावत् । इह विष्णुना इति द्रव्यशब्दोऽयं सर्वमेतद्वाक्यमुपजीवयतीति द्रव्यादिदीपकमेवंविधं बोद्धव्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: That is, they were destroyed. The prosperities, the splendors, of the gods — from some place, from an undesignable location — were brought. They existed [again]. That is, they were produced. Here, by the substance-word '<s>Viṣṇu</s>,' this entire sentence is sustained — thus this should be understood as a substance-<s>dīpaka</s> of this kind.

By [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] exerting his valor — that is, girded for the binding of <s>Bali</s>, striding forth — the splendors, the glories, of the <s>Dānavas</s> were taken somewhere, to some indeterminable place.
Which are these <s>dīpakas</s>? He says —
Thus beginning-<s>dīpakas</s> have been stated; similarly, in the middle and at the end
of sentences too we shall demonstrate some of those, as follows: // 102 //

children.text: इत्येवंरूपाणि वाक्यादौ प्रयुक्तान्यादिदीपकान्युक्तानि जात्यादिभेदेन चत्वारि वेदितव्यानि । एवमनेन प्रकारेण तानि दीपकानि का[नि]चित् कतिपयानि न सर्वाणि वाक्ययोः वाक्यद्वयस्य काव्यरूपस्य मध्येऽन्ते च दर्शयिष्याम उदाहरिष्यामः । तद् यथेति निदर्शयन्ति ॥
children.translated_text: Those of such form, employed at the beginning of a sentence, are the beginning-<s>dīpakas</s> that have been stated — four types should be known, according to the division into class and so forth. In the same manner, those <s>dīpakas</s> — some, a few, not all — in the middle and at the end of a pair of verses in the form of poetry, we shall demonstrate, we shall illustrate. 'As follows' — they exemplify.
Peacocks dance and sing in the lap of the <s>niculas</s> (barringtonia trees),

children.text: ब नन्ति च पयोदेषु दृशो हर्षाश्रुगर्भिणीः ॥ १०३ ॥
children.translated_text: and they fix their eyes, pregnant with tears of joy, upon the rain-clouds. // 103 //

children.text: कलापिनो मयृरा नृत्यन्ति गायन्ति च निचुलानाम् अभिंनवमञ्जरीपुञ्जरञ्जितानाम् उत्सङ्गे विटपरूपे पयोदेषु जलधरोत्सवजन्महर्षाश्रु गर्भोऽन्तर्वर्ति यासां ता दृशश्चक्षूं षि बध्नन्ति नियच्छन्ति च । कलापिन इत्यपेक्षते । इह कलापिन इत्यनेन जातिवाचिना वाक्यमध्यवर्तिना सर्वमेतद्वाक्यमुपक्रियत इति जातिमध्यदीपकम् ईदृशं दृश्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: The peacocks (<s>kalāpin</s>) dance and sing in the lap — in the form of branches — of the <s>nicula</s> trees adorned with clusters of fresh blossoms. Upon the rain-clouds, they fix, they direct, their eyes, whose interior holds tears of joy born from the festivity of the clouds. It expects [the subject]: the peacocks. Here, by the class-word 'peacocks,' placed in the middle of the sentence, this entire sentence is served — thus this is a class-middle-<s>dīpaka</s>, to be seen as being of this kind.
The gentle breeze becomes acrid, the moon becomes fire,
and the application of sandal-paste becomes a blow of a weapon — for those away from home. // 104 //

children.text: मन्दो गन्धवहो मृदुः पवनः प्रवासिनां विरहिणां क्षारो जायते, व्यथाहेतु

त्वात् । इन्दुश्च वह्निः अग्निः जायते, दाहकत्वात् । चर्चारूपश्च स्थासकस्वभावः चन्दनस्य पातोऽनुलेपश्च शस्त्रपातोऽसिपातो जायते, दुःखजनकत्वात् । इह जायत इति क्रियापदेन मध्यवर्तिना सर्ववाक्योपकार इति क्रियामध्यदीपकमीदृशं वेदितव्यमिति । गुणदीपकं द्रव्यदीपकं च मध्यवर्ति नोदाहृतम् । अत एव कानिचिदित्युक्तम् । तत्तु यथा—
children.translated_text: pain. And the moon becomes fire, because it burns. And the application of sandal-paste — whose nature is coolness — the anointing of sandalwood becomes a blow of a weapon, a stroke of a sword, because it produces suffering. Here, by the action-word 'becomes' (<s>jāyate</s>), placed in the middle, all the sentences are served — thus this should be known as an action-middle-<s>dīpaka</s> of this kind. The quality-<s>dīpaka</s> and substance-<s>dīpaka</s> placed in the middle have not been illustrated; hence 'some' was said [earlier]. But those are as follows —
Your valor even burns the minds of kings,
and the doubt regarding [their] fortune extinguishes the hearts of beautiful women.
A glorious, [knowledge]-filled illumination was made by the all-seeing one,

children.text: हृतं च सर्वदिग्व्यापिं दुर्जयं जगतां तमः ॥
children.translated_text: and the darkness of the worlds, all-pervading and unconquerable, was removed.
Thus.
The gentle breeze (<s>gandhavaha</s>), the soft wind, becomes acrid (<s>kṣāra</s>) for those away from home, the love-sick, because it causes
The water poured forth by clouds, the flock of household peacocks,

children.text: चलं च तड़ितां दाम बलं कुसुमधन्वनः ॥ १०५ ॥
children.translated_text: the trembling garland of lightning flashes — [all these are] the army of the flower-arrowed <s>Kāma</s>. // 105 //

children.text: जलधरैः उद्गीर्णं विमुक्तं जलं गृहेषु शिखण्डिनां कुलं वृन्दं तडितां च दाम गुणः चलं सर्वमेतत् वस्तु मनोज्ञं कुसुमधन्वनः कामस्य बलम् अनीकं जगद्विजयिनः आत्मोदयानुगुणत्वात् । इह बलमात्रं जलधरोद्गीर्णजलादिभेदत्रयानुगत[मपोढप्रत्येक]विशेषं विवक्षिंतमिति जात्यन्तदीपकमेतत्, तेन सर्ववाक्योपकारादिति ॥
children.translated_text: The water released by the clouds, the flock — the multitude — of peacocks in the houses, and the garland — the string — of lightning flashes: all this, delightful, trembling — is the army, the force, of the flower-arrowed <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), the conqueror of the world, because [these phenomena] are conducive to his arising. Here, only the word 'army' (<s>bala</s>), which subsumes the three types — water poured by clouds and the rest — with the specific [differences] removed and the general intended, is an end-class-<s>dīpaka</s>, because it serves all the sentences.
By you, a blue-lotus earring on the ear; by <s>Smara</s> (Love), a weapon on the bow;
by me too, the mind on dying — these three were done simultaneously. // 106 //

children.text: वराङ्गि, त्वया कर्णे कर्णोत्पलम् अवतंसकुवलयं कृतं यदा तदैव स्मरेण शरासने धनुषि कृतम् अस्त्रं शरः, मया च रागवेगमूर्च्छितेन मरणे दशम्यां दशायां चेतः कृतमित्येतत्त्रयम् । त्रिभिरेभिरस्माभिरेतेषु त्रिंषु समं युगपत् कृतमिति क्रियान्तदीपकमिदं कृतमित्यन्तवर्तिना क्रियावचनेन सर्ववाक्योपकृतेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: O beautiful-limbed one, by you the <s>karṇotpala</s> (ear-lotus), the ear-ornament of <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus), was placed on the ear; at that very moment, by <s>Smara</s> (Love), a weapon, an arrow, was placed on the bow; and by me, overwhelmed by the surge of passion, the mind was placed on dying, on the state of death — thus these three [acts]. By these three — by us — in these three [targets], simultaneously, at once, it was done — this is an action-end-<s>dīpaka</s>, because the action-word 'done' (<s>kṛta</s>), placed at the end, serves all the sentences.

children.text: इहापि गुणद्रव्यलक्षणमन्तदीपकद्वयं न निदर्शितं तदपि यथा—

children.translated_text: He gathered the provisions for enlightenment, he conquered the knowledge of truth,
he lifted the world from suffering — O chief of sages, your compassion [did all this].
He churned the <s>Kṣīrasāgara</s> (milk ocean) with a roar reverberating to the ends of the directions,
and as the labor of churning subsided, <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) obtained <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Thus.
Here too the quality-end-<s>dīpaka</s> and substance-end-<s>dīpaka</s>, being two, have not been illustrated; those too are as follows —

children.text: शुक्लः श्वेतार्चिषो वृद्ध्यै पक्षः पञ्चशरस्य सः ।
children.translated_text: The bright fortnight exists for the increase of the white-rayed one (<s>Candra</s>), and that for the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>);

children.text: स च रागस्य रागोऽपि यूनां रत्युत्सवश्रियः ॥ १०७ ॥
children.translated_text: and that for passion, and passion too for the splendor of the love-festival of the young. (verse 107)

children.text: शुक्लः पक्षः श्वेतार्चिषः चन्द्रस्य वृद्ध्यै उपचयार्थं प्रवर्तते । स श्वेतार्चिः पञ्चशरस्य वृद्ध्यै । स पञ्चशरो यूनां रागस्य वृद्ध्यै । रागोऽप्यसौ रत्युत्सवश्रियो वृद्ध्यै कल्पते । रतिः सम्भोग एवोत्सवः प्रीतिलक्षणत्वात् । तस्य श्रीः उत्कर्षः स एव वा श्रीः विभूतिरूपत्वात् योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: The bright fortnight (<s>śukla pakṣa</s>) functions for the increase, i.e., the augmentation, of the white-rayed moon. That white-rayed one serves for the increase of the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>). That five-arrowed one serves for the increase of passion among the young. Passion too serves for the increase of the splendor of the love-festival. <s>Rati</s> (love) itself is the festival of sexual union, because it has the nature of delight. Its <s>śrī</s> (splendor) means excellence; or that itself is <s>śrī</s>, because it has the nature of magnificence — this should be construed thus.
Asking 'What kind of <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) is this?' he says —
Even though this has the nature of <s>ādidīpaka</s> (initial illumination), a garland of sentences is employed,
each depending on the preceding one — therefore this is considered <s>mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illumination). (verse 108)

children.text: इत्येवंविधं यत्तन्मालादीपकं मतम् इष्टम् । ननु क्रियादिदीपकमेतद् वृद्ध्यै इति क्रियावाचिनादिवर्तिना सर्ववाक्योपकारादित्याह—आदिदीपकत्वेऽपीति । यद्यप्यादिदीपकमेतत्तथापि विशेषापेक्षया मालादीपकमुच्यते । कः पुनरसौ विशेषः येनैवं व्यपदिश्यत इत्याह—पूर्वेत्यादि । वाक्यानां श्वेतार्चिषो वृद्ध्यै शुक्लः पक्षो भवति, स च पञ्चशरस्य वृद्ध्यै भवतीत्येवमादीनां माला पंक्तिः पूर्वं पूर्वं यथोक्तेन विधिना अपेक्षमाणा प्रयुक्तेति । अयमत्र विशेषोऽपेक्षितः । तस्मान्मालादीपकमीदृशमाख्यायते, नादिदीपकमिति ॥
