children.translated_text: What is of this kind, that is considered, i.e., accepted, as <s>mālādīpaka</s> (garland-illumination). Objection: this is <s>kriyādidīpaka</s> (action-initial illumination), since the action-denoting word 'for the increase' occurring at the beginning benefits all sentences — to this he says 'even though it has the nature of <s>ādidīpaka</s>.' Although this is an <s>ādidīpaka</s>, nevertheless with reference to a special feature it is called <s>mālādīpaka</s>. What then is that special feature by which it is so designated? To this he says 'preceding' etc. The garland, i.e., series, of sentences such as 'the bright fortnight exists for the increase of the white-rayed one,' 'and that exists for the increase of the five-arrowed one,' and so forth — each depending on the preceding one according to the stated method, is employed thus. This is the special feature intended here. Therefore such a figure is designated as <s>mālādīpaka</s>, not as <s>ādidīpaka</s>.
The rain clouds increase the arrogance of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love),
but they diminish that of summer, their sprays being scattered by the wind. (verse 109)

children.text: अनङ्गस्य अवलेपं दर्पं वर्धयन्ति उपचिन्वन्ति बलाहकाः । मारुतोद्धूतशीकराः
मारुतैरुद्धूता विकीर्णाः शीकरा जलकणा येषां येरिति वा विग्रहः । घमेस्य तु निदाघस्य पुनः अवलेपं कर्षयन्ति कृ[शं कुर्व]न्ति इति ॥
children.translated_text: the sprays, i.e., water-droplets, scattered and dispersed by the winds — this is the compound analysis, or alternatively with the suffix 'era.' But they diminish, i.e., make thin, the arrogance of summer (<s>gharma</s>), i.e., the hot season.
The rain clouds (<s>balāhaka</s>) increase, i.e., augment, the arrogance (<s>avalepa</s>), i.e., pride, of <s>Anaṅga</s>. 'Whose sprays are scattered by the wind' —
He explains that —
Here, by the word '<s>avalepa</s>' (arrogance) and by the word '<s>balāhaka</s>' (rain cloud),
two contradictory actions are conjoined — therefore this is <s>viruddhārthadīpaka</s> (contradictory-meaning illumination). (verse 110)

children.text: अवलेपपदेन व्याप्यभूतेन बलाहकपदेन कर्तृवाचिना सह विरुद्धे परस्परव्याहते क्रिये वर्द्धनकर्षणे संप्रयुक्ते सम्बद्धे अवलेपविषयत्वात्, बलाहककर्तृकत्वाच्च भवतः यतः तत्तस्मात् विरुद्धार्थदीपकमीदृशमिदम् । यद्वेदृशं तद् विरुद्धार्थदीपकमिति योज्यत् ॥
children.translated_text: With the word '<s>avalepa</s>' (arrogance), which denotes the pervaded element, and with the word '<s>balāhaka</s>' (rain cloud), which denotes the agent, two contradictory, i.e., mutually opposed, actions — increasing and diminishing — are conjoined, i.e., connected, because they pertain to arrogance and because they have the rain cloud as their agent. Since this is so, therefore such a figure is <s>viruddhārthadīpaka</s> (contradictory-meaning illumination). Alternatively, one should construe: what is of this kind, that is <s>viruddhārthadīpaka</s>.
It carries away the expanse of the directions, it seizes the host of luminaries,
and today it takes away my very life-breaths — that row of rain clouds! (verse 111)

children.text: आशानां दिशाम् आभोगं विस्तारं हरति गृह्णाति । ज्योतिषां नक्षत्राणां गणं गृह्णाति हरति । योऽहमेवं विरहविधुरः, तस्य मे मम प्राणान् आदत्ते गृह्णाति । असौ इयं जलधरावली मेघपंक्तिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: It carries away, i.e., takes, the expanse, i.e., extent, of the directions (<s>āśā</s>). It seizes, i.e., takes, the host of luminaries, i.e., stars. And it takes away the life-breaths of me, who am thus tormented by separation. This row of rain clouds (<s>jaladharāvalī</s>), i.e., this line of clouds.
He elucidates that —
Here, because of the employment of multiple words, a single action is illuminated;
since it is by the row of rain clouds, therefore this is <s>ekārthadīpaka</s> (single-meaning illumination). (verse 112)

children.text: अनेकस्य हरत्यादेः शब्दस्य क्रियापदस्य पर्यायरूपस्य उपादानात् प्रयोगेण एकैवापघातलक्षणा क्रिया दीप्यते उपक्रियते जलधरावल्या कर्तृभूतया यतः तस्मादेकार्थदीपकमीदृशमवसेयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Because of the employment, i.e., usage, of multiple synonymous verbal words such as 'carries away' etc., a single action characterized by removal is illuminated, i.e., brought forth, by the row of rain clouds which serves as the agent — since this is so, therefore one should understand this as <s>ekārthadīpaka</s> (single-meaning illumination).
Bearing pleasant fragrance on the wind, towering, dark as <s>tamāla</s> trees in complexion,

children.text: दिवि भ्रमन्ति जीमूता भुवि चैते मतङ्गजाः ॥ ११३ ॥
children.translated_text: the clouds wander in the sky, and these elephants upon the earth. (verse 113)

children.text: जीमूता मेघाः दिवि नभसि भ्रमन्ति अमी । मतङ्गजा हस्तिनश्च एते भुवि भ्रमन्ति । हृद्यो मनोहरो गन्धवहः पवनो येषाम् जीमूतानां ते, तथा हृद्यं गन्धं

मदमयं वहन्ति क्षिपन्ति समन्तादिति हृद्यगन्धवहाः मतङ्गजा इति शब्दश्लेषः । हृद्यो वा मदमिश्रः गन्धवहः पवनो येषामित्यर्थश्लेषः । तुङ्गा महान्तः तमालवत् श्यामला नीला [त्विट् कान्तिर्येषां ते ।] उभयेऽपीत्यर्थश्लेषः ॥
children.translated_text: consisting of ichor' — this applies to the elephants — thus there is <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia). Or alternatively, 'those whose wind is mixed with a pleasant ichor-fragrance' — this is <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (meaning-based paronomasia). 'Towering,' i.e., great; 'dark like <s>tamāla</s> trees in complexion' — both apply to both — thus there is <s>arthaśleṣa</s>.

The clouds (<s>jīmūta</s>) wander in the sky. And these elephants (<s>mataṅgaja</s>) wander upon the earth. 'Those whose wind carries a pleasant fragrance' — this applies to the clouds; and similarly, 'those who carry, i.e., emit in all directions, a pleasant fragrance
He analyzes that —
Here, of the clouds and elephants which are undifferentiated in their qualities,
the connection with a single act of wandering — therefore this is <s>śliṣṭārthadīpaka</s> (paronomasia-illumination). (verse 114)

children.text: अत्र प्रयोगे धर्मैर्हृद्यगन्धवहत्वादिभिः गुणैरभिन्नानां समानामभ्राणां हस्तिनां च भ्रमेणैव एकेन कर्मणा दीपकेन सम्बन्धः साध्यसाधनलक्षणः प्रतीयत इति हेतोः श्लिष्टार्थदीपकमीदृशम्, श्लेषानुगतत्वात् इति ॥
children.translated_text: Here in this usage, of the clouds and elephants which are undifferentiated, i.e., identical, in their qualities such as bearing pleasant fragrance etc., the connection characterized by the relation of means and end is perceived through a single action, namely wandering, serving as the <s>dīpaka</s> — since this is so, this is <s>śliṣṭārthadīpaka</s>, because it is pervaded by <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).
Extending [the principle] to the unmentioned varieties of <s>dīpaka</s>, he concludes —
In this very manner, the conformity of the remaining varieties too
in the case of <s>dīpaka</s> should be accomplished by the discerning. (verse 115)

body.text: अनेनव अनन्तरोक्तेन प्रकारेण विधिना दीपके दीपकविषयाणां शेषाणामनुक्तानामपि विकल्पानां भेदानामनुगतिरवबोधः । विधातव्या क्रियतां विचक्षणैः कविभिरिति ॥ सा चानुगतिरेवं विधातव्या—
body.translated_text: In this very manner, i.e., by the method just stated, the conformity, i.e., understanding, of the remaining, i.e., unmentioned, varieties, i.e., sub-types, of those that fall within the domain of <s>dīpaka</s>, should be accomplished by the discerning, i.e., by poets. And that conformity should be accomplished as follows —
O slender-limbed one, your lip-color appears as if it were passion itself made visible;
it delights the heart and takes away my life-breaths.
The glances of the doe-eyed women, languid with passion, steal [hearts];
as if to say to people: 'We are the extended bolts of liberation.'

body.text: न खङ्गधारा निशिता निशाता नापि सायकाः ।
body.translated_text: Neither the edge of a sword, nor sharpened arrows,

body.text: हरन्ति [च] मम प्राणान् मृगाक्षि तव विभ्रमाः ॥
body.translated_text: take away my life-breaths — O doe-eyed one, your coquetries [do].
In this way, the other varieties of <s>dīpaka</s> too should be traced.
Thus concludes the <s>dīpakacakra</s> (cycle of illumination figures).

children.translated_text: Taking up <s>āvṛtti</s> (repetition), he says —
<s>Arthāvṛtti</s> (repetition of meaning), <s>padāvṛtti</s> (repetition of word), and <s>ubhayāvṛtti</s> (repetition of both) —
these three ornaments are accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s>. (verse 116)

children.text: अर्थस्य अभिधेयस्य आवृत्तिः पुनः पुनरुद्भावनम् । पदस्य शब्दस्य आवृतिः भूयः समुच्चारणम् । उभयस्यार्थस्य पदस्य चावृत्तिरप्यावृत्तिश्चेति । एवंलक्षणम् अलङ्कारत्रयम् आवृत्तिविशेषात्मकमिष्टं दीपकस्य स्थाने विषय एव नान्यत्र । दीपकेनापि तादृशार्थप्रतीतिसम्भवात् नार्थतः तयोः भेद इति दीपकस्थान एवेष्टमित्युक्तम् । अन्ये त्वेकत्र दीपकस्थान इति विशेषेण व्याचक्षते तदसारम् । एवं हि अर्थावृत्तिरेव दीपकस्थाने स्यात्, न शेषमावृत्तिद्वयम् । आवृत्तित्रयमपि च दीपकस्थान इत्युक्तं शास्त्रकृता दीपकस्थान एवेष्टमलङ्कारत्रयमिति साक्षादमिधानात् । ततः शास्त्रविरुद्धमेव व्याख्यानम् । तस्माद्दीपकावृत्त्योः समानो विषयः, उभयथापि तदर्थावगमसम्भवात् । प्रयोगतस्त्वनयोर्भेदः । न चैवमवगन्तव्यम्- यदि सोऽर्थो दीपकेनापि गम्यते किमनयेति दीपकसमानत्वादस्य पर्यनुयोगस्य । दीपकवच्चास्यापि शिष्टैरिष्टत्वात् कथमियमतिरिच्यते ? तेषां सर्वथेह प्रमाणत्वात् । कथं न दिष्टातिक्रमः ? तस्मात् अर्थाभेदेऽपि दीपकवदियमप्यनुगम्यते, द्वयोरप्यलङ्कारतयेष्टत्वात् । अत एवोक्तम्— दीपकस्थान एवेष्टमिति । शिष्टैरितिगम्यते । तस्मादभिन्नस्थानत्वेऽपि प्रयोगभेदा

children.translated_text: both are accepted by the learned — enough of excessive disputation.

<s>Arthāvṛtti</s> is the repeated evocation of meaning, i.e., of the signified content. <s>Padāvṛtti</s> is the repeated utterance of a word, i.e., of a linguistic expression. And <s>ubhayāvṛtti</s> is the repetition of both meaning and word. These three ornaments, characterized by varieties of <s>āvṛtti</s> (repetition), are accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s> and nowhere else, because even through <s>dīpaka</s> the apprehension of such meaning is possible; hence there is no real distinction between them in terms of meaning — thus it is said 'accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s>.' Others, however, explain 'in the domain of <s>dīpaka</s>' with particular reference to one [type only] — that is without substance. For thus only <s>arthāvṛtti</s> would belong to the domain of <s>dīpaka</s>, not the remaining two types of <s>āvṛtti</s>. But the author of the treatise has stated that all three types of <s>āvṛtti</s> belong to the domain of <s>dīpaka</s>, by directly declaring 'these three ornaments are accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s>.' Therefore that interpretation contradicts the treatise. Hence, <s>dīpaka</s> and <s>āvṛtti</s> share the same domain, because in both cases the apprehension of that meaning is possible. The difference between them, however, is in usage. Nor should one think thus: 'If that meaning is also conveyed by <s>dīpaka</s>, what need is there for this?' — for this objection equally applies to <s>dīpaka</s> itself, given their similarity. And since this [figure] too is accepted by the learned just as <s>dīpaka</s> is, how can it be dismissed? For their authority here is absolute in every way. How can there be a violation of what is established? Therefore, even though there is no difference in meaning, this too, like <s>dīpaka</s>, is to be followed, since both are accepted as ornaments. For this very reason it is said: 'accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s>' — 'by the learned' is implied. Therefore, even though the domain is the same, because of the difference in usage,
The <s>kadamba</s> blossoms bloom, the <s>kuṭaja</s> buds burst open,

children.text: उन्मीलन्ति च कन्दल्यो दलन्ति ककुभानि च ॥ ११७ ॥
children.translated_text: the <s>kandalī</s> flowers unfurl, and the <s>kakubha</s> buds split apart. (verse 117)

children.text: कदम्बानि मुकुलानि विकसन्ति । कुटजानां कुटजरूपा वा उद्गमाः कुड्मलानि स्फुटन्ति विकसन्ति । कन्दल्यश्च कुसुमान्युन्मीलन्ति विकसन्ति । ककुभानि कोरकाणि च दलन्ति विकसन्ति । इत्यर्थावृत्तिरियमुदाहृता । विकासलक्षणस्यैकस्यार्थस्यानेकैः पर्यायैरभीक्ष्णमाविष्करणादिति । दीपकेनाप्ययमर्थः प्रकाश्यते । तद्यथा—

children.translated_text: The <s>kadamba</s> blossoms bloom, and likewise the <s>kuṭaja</s> buds,
and the fragrant <s>kandalī</s> flowers, and the beautiful <s>kakubha</s> buds.
Thus.

The <s>kadamba</s> buds bloom (<s>vikasanti</s>). The shoots of the <s>kuṭaja</s>, or buds in the form of <s>kuṭaja</s>, burst open (<s>sphuṭanti</s>), i.e., bloom. The <s>kandalī</s> flowers unfurl (<s>unmīlanti</s>), i.e., bloom. And the <s>kakubha</s> buds split apart (<s>dalanti</s>), i.e., bloom. Thus this is illustrated as <s>arthāvṛtti</s> (repetition of meaning), because a single meaning characterized by blooming is repeatedly manifested through multiple synonyms. Even through <s>dīpaka</s> this meaning can be illuminated. For example —
The garland of clouds makes eager the flock of peacocks,
and the god of love makes eager the minds of the young today. (verse 118)

children.text: कलापिनां वर्गमुत्कण्ठयति उद्ग्रीवयति मेघानां माला यूनां च मानसं मकरध्वजः उत्कण्ठयति पर्युत्सुकयति अद्य प्रावृषि । पदावृत्तेरिदमुदाहरणम् । पदस्यैवोत्कण्ठयतीत्यस्यावृत्तेः । अर्थस्य तु भेदादयमप्यर्थो दीपकेन परिदीप्यते । तद्यथा—

children.translated_text: The garland of clouds makes eager the flock of peacocks,
and <s>Makaradhvaja</s> makes eager the minds of the young, the very essence of passion.
Thus.

The garland of clouds makes eager, i.e., makes crane-necked (looking upward), the flock of peacocks (<s>kalāpin</s>). And <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the god of love) makes eager, i.e., makes anxious, the minds of the young today, i.e., in the rainy season. This is an example of <s>padāvṛtti</s> (repetition of word), because the very word 'makes eager' (<s>utkaṇṭhayati</s>) is repeated. But since the meaning differs, this meaning too can be illuminated by <s>dīpaka</s>. For example —
Having conquered the world, you sport here with the ladies of the inner apartments;
your host of enemies, having gone to heaven, sports with the <s>Apsaras</s>. (verse 119)

children.text: विश्वं जगत् जित्वा अत्र महीमण्डले अद्य च अधुना अवरोधनैः अन्तःपुरसुन्दरीभिः सह भवान् विहरति रमते । तव रिपुवर्गो दिवं स्वर्गं तवासिधारापथेन गतः सह अप्सरोभिः दिव्याङ्गनाभिः सह विहरति इत्युभयावृत्तिर्निदर्शिता, विहरति इत्यर्थस्य पदस्यावृत्तेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: Having conquered the world, i.e., the earth, here on this terrestrial sphere, and also now at this time, you sport, i.e., take delight, with the ladies of the inner apartments (<s>avarodhanā</s>), i.e., the beauties of the harem. Your host of enemies, having gone to heaven, i.e., to the celestial realm by the path of your sword's edge, sports with <s>Apsaras</s>, i.e., celestial maidens — thus <s>ubhayāvṛtti</s> (repetition of both) is illustrated, because both the meaning and the word 'sports' (<s>viharati</s>) are repeated.
Having conquered the world, you sport here with the ladies of the inner apartments;
your host of enemies, having gone to heaven, with the lovely <s>Apsaras</s>.
Thus.
This too is a domain of <s>dīpaka</s>. For example —
For this very reason it has been stated in general terms that 'these three ornaments are accepted as belonging to the very domain of <s>dīpaka</s>.'
Thus concludes the <s>āvṛtticakra</s> (cycle of repetition figures).
Introducing <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection/denial), he says —
<s>Ākṣepa</s> (objection) is an expression of denial; it is threefold with reference to the three times;
and furthermore, its infinity arises from the infinity of the varieties of what is objected to. (verse 120)

children.text: प्रतिषेधस्योक्तिर्वचनमित्यनूद्य आक्षेप इति विधीयते । स च त्रिधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैस्तावद् भिद्यते । कथम् । त्रयोऽतीतानागतवर्तमानाः कालास्त्रैकाल्यम् । तस्या पेक्षया
आश्रयणेन हेतुना भूताक्षेपः, भविष्यदापेक्षः, वर्तमानापेक्ष इति । अत्र त्रिधाभेदानन्तरमस्याक्षेपस्य अनन्तता अनवसितभेदता । कुतः ? आक्षेपस्य निषेधस्यार्थसा
children.translated_text: by reason of dependence [on each time], there are: objection relating to the past (<s>bhūtākṣepa</s>), objection relating to the future, and objection relating to the present. After this threefold division, the infinity of this <s>ākṣepa</s>, i.e., its limitless variety, [is stated]. Why? The varieties of <s>ākṣepa</s>, i.e., the sub-types having the form of objection, relate to the semantic

children.text: मान्यस्य भेदाः विकल्पा आक्षेपरूपा वा भेदाः । तेषामानन्त्यादपर्यवसानात् कारणादिति ॥
children.translated_text: commonality of negation — because of their infinity, i.e., their inexhaustibility.

Having cited 'an expression of denial' (<s>pratiṣedha</s>), he establishes that this is <s>ākṣepa</s>. And it is first divided into three kinds by three modes. How? The three times — past, future, and present — constitute <s>traikālya</s> (the triad of times). With reference to that,
<s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love) conquered the entire world with his five floral arrows —
this is inconceivable; but then again, the powers of things are wondrous! (verse 121)

children.text: पौष्पैः पुष्पमयैः एकान्तमृदुभिस्तैरपि पञ्चभिः स्वल्पैरिषुमिः शरैः स पञ्चेषुरनङ्गः विश्वं जगत् सर्वं व्यजयत विजितवानिति असम्भाव्यमयुक्तमेतत् । कथमस्याः सामग्र्याः कार्यमीदृशं संभाव्यते ? अथवा किं न सम्भाव्यते ? यतो वस्तूनां पदार्थानां शक्तयः विचित्रा नानाप्रकारा अचिन्त्यास्तदेषामपि तादृशी शक्तिर्भवेत् । न किञ्चिद्वाधकमिति ॥
children.translated_text: With floral, i.e., made of flowers, hence utterly soft, and moreover only five, i.e., few, arrows (<s>iṣu</s>), that five-arrowed <s>Anaṅga</s> conquered, i.e., subjugated, the entire world — this is inconceivable (<s>asambhāvya</s>), i.e., impossible. How can such an effect be conceived from such a combination of causes? But then again — why should it not be conceived? Since the powers (<s>śakti</s>) of things are wondrous, i.e., of manifold kinds and inconceivable, their power too could be of such a nature. There is no obstacle whatsoever.
Asking 'What kind of <s>ākṣepa</s> is this?' he says —
Thus the notion of the impossibility of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s conquest, which arose here by the force of reasoning,
is itself objected to by the very course [of argument] — such is <s>vṛttākṣepa</s> (past-tense objection). (verse 122)

children.text: इत्येवमनन्तरोक्तस्य अनुरूपस्य च हेतोः कारणस्य पौष्पपञ्चशरत्वादेः । बलात् सामर्थ्यात् प्रवृत्ता भूतैवानङ्गजयायोगबुद्धिः । अनङ्गस्य जयो विश्ववशीकरणम् । तस्यायोगोऽसम्भावना तत्र बुद्धिः अनङ्गो व्यजयतेत्यसम्भाव्यमित्येवाकाराक्षिप्ता निषिद्धा । हेतुबलादित्यत्राप्यपेक्षणीयम् । भाववदभावस्यापि सहेतुकत्वात् । हेतुबलं चात्र विचित्रवस्तुशक्तिदर्शनम् । यद् यतः तत् तस्मात् ईदृशः एवंप्रकारो वृत्तस्याक्षेपो भूतकालाक्षेपोऽवसेय इति ॥
children.translated_text: In this manner, by the force, i.e., power, of the appropriate reason (<s>hetu</s>) such as his having five floral arrows, the notion of the impossibility of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s conquest — <s>Anaṅga</s>'s conquest being his subjugation of the world, and its impossibility being the inconceivability thereof, and the notion being the cognition 'this is inconceivable that <s>Anaṅga</s> conquered' — is objected to, i.e., denied, by the very course of the [past] event itself. 'By the force of reasoning' should be understood here as well, since non-existence too, like existence, has a cause. And the force of reasoning here is the observation of the wondrous powers of things. Since this is so, therefore one should understand such a figure as <s>vṛttākṣepa</s> (objection regarding what has [already] occurred), i.e., objection relating to the past.
Why do you place a blue lotus on your ear, O sweet-voiced one?
Do you consider your sidelong glance insufficient for this task? (verse 123)

children.text: कलभाषिणि मञ्जुवचने ! प्रियामन्त्रणम् । कर्णे कुवलयम् अवतंसोत्पलम् कुतः कस्मात् करोपि ? वृथैव तत् क्रियते, अपाङ्गेन कर्णपूरकार्याचरणादित्याहकिमित्यादि । अपाङ्गं नयनोपान्तम् अस्मिन् प्रस्तुते कर्मणि कर्णावतंसोत्पलकृत्ये
अपर्याप्तम् असमर्थम् मन्यसे ? किमिति क्षेपे प्रश्ने वा । नैवं मन्तव्यं पर्याप्तमिदमस्मिन् कर्मणीति ॥
children.translated_text: do you consider it insufficient, i.e., incapable? The word 'kim' is used in the sense of reproach or question. One should not think thus: 'it is sufficient for this task.'

O sweet-voiced one (<s>kalabhāṣiṇī</s>) — this is an address to the beloved. Why, i.e., for what reason, do you place a blue lotus (<s>kuvalaya</s>) as an ear-ornament on your ear? That is done in vain, since the sidelong glance (<s>apāṅga</s>) already accomplishes the function of the ear-ornament — to this he says 'do you consider' etc. The sidelong glance, i.e., the corner of the eye, in this present task of serving as an ear-ornament of blue lotus —
He explains that —
This is <s>vartamānākṣepa</s> (present-tense objection), since even as she is placing the blue lotus,
A certain woman, while [placing a blue lotus] at her ear, is thus restrained by her flattering lover. || 124 ||

children.text: सोऽयमीदृशो वर्त[मा]नस्य करणस्य आक्षेपः । वर्तमानकालविषयो निषेधः । कथम् ? काचित् प्रिया कर्णे स्वस्मिन् असितोत्पलमिन्दीवरं कुर्वती कुर्वाणेव, न कृतवती करिष्यन्ती वा । रुध्यते आक्षिप्यते प्रियेण चाटुकारेण प्रियाचरणचतुरेण । एवमनन्तरोक्तेन प्रकारेण यतस्तस्माद्वर्तमानाक्षेपोऽयमिति निगमनीयम् इति ॥
children.translated_text: This is such an <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) of a present action. It is a prohibition pertaining to the present tense. How? A certain beloved woman, while placing a blue lotus (<s>asitotpala</s>) at her ear — that is, while in the act of doing so, not having already done it or being about to do it — is restrained, that is, objected to, by her flattering lover, one who is skilled in pleasing conduct. In the manner stated immediately above, therefore it should be concluded that this is <s>vartamānākṣepa</s> (objection to a present action).

children.text: सत्यं ब्रवीमि न त्वं मां द्रष्टं वल्लभ ! लप्स्यसे ।
children.translated_text: I tell you truly, O beloved, you shall not succeed in seeing me
with eyes reddened by lac-dye transferred from kissing another woman. || 125 ||

children.text: वल्लभ ! सत्यं नियतमिदम् अहं त्वां ब्रवीमि मा अन्यथा मंस्थाः । किं तदित्यादि । नेत्यादि । अन्यथा प्रतियोषिता अन्यस्या वा विलासलाक्षारागरञ्जिताधरपल्लवया । चुम्बनात् वक्त्रयोगात् संक्रान्तः संचरितो लाक्षारागो यत्र तेन चक्षुषा मां द्रष्टुं त्वं न लप्स्यसे नाहमीदृशं व्यतिकरमपरेव सोढुं शक्नोमि । तदैव मे लोकान्तरप्रस्थानम् । ईदृशीयं सृष्टिः किं करवाणीति ॥
children.translated_text: O beloved! I tell you this as certain truth — do not think otherwise. What is that? And so forth. 'Not' and so forth. Otherwise, by a rival woman or another whose lip-buds are colored with the hue of ornamental lac — from kissing, that is, from the union of mouths, the lac-dye has been transferred; with such eyes you shall not succeed in seeing me. I cannot bear even this much impropriety. At that very moment would be my departure to another world. Such is the nature of creation — what can I do?
He explains that —
This is <s>bhāviṣyadākṣepa</s> (objection to a future event); because a most proud woman,
suspecting that 'perhaps his offense will occur in the future,' thus restrains him even beforehand. || 126 ||

children.text: यद् यस्मात् अतिमनस्विनी सर्वथा दोषमर्षणपराङ्मुखस्वभावा काचित् प्रणयिनी कदाचिदस्य पुनरपराधो व्यलीकं भावी भवेदिति शङ्कमाना प्रागेवानागतविधायितयारुन्ध्द आक्षिपत् । एवमनन्तरोक्तेन प्रकारेण । तस्मात्सोऽयमीदृशः भविष्यदाक्षेपो भविष्यत एव दर्शनलाभादेराक्षेपादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yad</s>) a certain beloved woman who is exceedingly proud (<s>atimānasvinī</s>), whose nature is entirely averse to tolerating faults, suspecting that perhaps his offense or transgression might occur in the future, restrained him, that is, objected, even beforehand, acting as one who provides for what has not yet come. In the manner stated immediately above. Therefore this is such a <s>bhāviṣyadākṣepa</s> (objection to a future event), since the objection is to the very future occurrence of seeing and so forth.
O slender-limbed one! The softness renowned in your limbs is merely false,

children.text: यदि सत्यं मृदून्येव किमकाण्डे रुजन्ति माम् ॥ १२७ ॥
children.translated_text: for if they are truly soft, why do they pain me without cause? || 127 ||

children.text: तन्वङ्गि ! तवाङ्गेषु मार्दवं सौकुमार्यं मिथ्यैव असत्यमपि रूढ़ं प्रसिद्धमासीत् । मिथ्याप्रसिद्धिरेवेयं यत् तवाङ्गानि मृदूनि इति यावत् । तथाहि यदि सत्यं परमार्थतो मृद्वङ्गानि भवेयुः, नोपचारमात्रम् । सत्यमिति भवनक्रियाविशेषणम् । मां किं कस्मात् रुजन्ति पीडयन्ति । अकाण्डे अकस्मात् । क्रूरकार्यं हि पीडनम् । तत्कथं मादवे युज्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: O slender-limbed one (<s>tanvaṅgi</s>)! The softness, the delicacy, in your limbs was renowned as merely false, that is, untrue. This is a false reputation indeed — that your limbs are soft, in short. For thus, if they were truly, in reality, soft-limbed, and not merely by figurative usage — 'truly' here qualifies the verb of being — then why do they pain me, cause me suffering? Unexpectedly (<s>akāṇḍe</s>). For causing pain is a cruel act. How then can it be appropriate for softness?
Which type of <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) is this? He says —
This is <s>dharmākṣepa</s> (objection to an attribute); the softness of the woman's body has been objected to
by a lover, through an action that is opposed to it. || 128 ||

children.text: यद् यस्मात् अत्र प्रयोगे कामुकेन केनचित् चाटुकारेण कर्तृभूतेन तद्विरोधिना प्रतिद्वन्द्विना कर्मणा[न]ङ्गरुजारूपेण करणभूतेनाङ्गनाया गात्रेषु मार्दवमेवमुक्तेन प्रकारेणाक्षिप्तं निषिद्धम् । तस्मादयमीदृशो धर्मस्याक्षेप इति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yad</s>) here in this composition, by a certain lover, a flatterer who is the agent, the softness in the woman's limbs has been objected to, that is, negated, in the manner stated above, through an action in the form of bodily pain that serves as the instrument and is opposed to it. Therefore this is such an <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) of an attribute (<s>dharma</s>).

children.text: सुन्दरी सा न वेत्येष विवेकः केन जायते ।
children.translated_text: Is she beautiful or not? This discrimination — by whom can it be made?

children.text: प्रभामात्रं हि तरलं दृश्यते न तदाश्रयः ॥ १२९ ॥
children.translated_text: For only a mere radiance, flickering, is seen — not its substratum. || 129 ||

children.text: सा विवक्षिता काचित् सुन्दरी भवतीति तावन्निश्चयरूपो विवेकः विभागप्रतिपत्तिः । न वा सा भवतीत्यभावनिर्णयलक्षणो विवेकः । एषोऽयं केन हेतुना जायते ?  न केनचिदित्यर्थः । किं कारणमित्याह— प्रभेत्यादि । हिर्यस्मादर्थे । तत्र तस्यां तरलम् उज्ज्वलम् प्रभा कान्तिः धर्म एव मात्रं न धर्मी दृश्यते गृह्यते । यदाह—नाश्रय इति । प्रभानाम्नो धर्मस्य आश्रयः अधिकरणं देहे न दृश्यते ।

children.translated_text: Then how can this discrimination be made? — thus the topic should be concluded.

The discrimination, that is, the discernment of distinction — whether a certain intended woman is beautiful or whether she is not, that is, the determination of non-existence — this, by what cause does it arise? By no cause at all — such is the meaning. Why so? He says: 'radiance' and so forth. <s>Hi</s> is used in the sense of 'because.' There, in her, only the mere <s>prabhā</s> (radiance), the quality of brilliance, which is flickering (<s>tarala</s>), that is, dazzling, is seen, is perceived — not the substratum. As he says — 'not the substratum.' The substratum, that is, the locus, of the quality called radiance — the body — is not seen.
He categorizes that —
<s>Dharmyākṣepa</s> (objection to the substratum) is this; the substratum has been objected to, while the attribute called radiance
has been conceded, by one who wishes to express the extraordinary nature of her beauty. || 130 ||

children.text: यद् यस्मात् अत्र विषये रूपं वर्णसंस्थानात्मकं भूतगुणम् अत्याश्चर्यम् अत्यन्ताद्भतम्, एवं नामेदं प्रतिविशिष्टं यदाश्रयोऽपि तत्र लावण्यराशौ निमग्नो न
दृश्यते इति वक्तुम् इच्छता चाटुकारेण केनचिदाक्षिप्तो धर्मी आश्रयः । धर्मं गुणं प्रभाह्वयं कान्त्यभिधानम[नु]ज्ञाय अनाक्षिप्य । प्रभेत्याह्वयो नाम यस्येति विग्रहः । तस्माद्धर्मिण आक्षेपो निराशः ॥
children.translated_text: seen — by a certain flatterer wishing to say this, the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>), the locus, has been objected to, while conceding, that is, not objecting to, the attribute (<s>dharma</s>), the quality called <s>prabhā</s> (radiance). The compound is analyzed as: that whose name is <s>prabhā</s>. Therefore this objection of the substratum (<s>dharmin</s>) is without remainder.

Because (<s>yad</s>) here in this context, the beauty (<s>rūpa</s>), consisting of color and form, a quality of the elements, is extraordinarily, supremely wondrous — so much so that even the substratum is submerged in that mass of loveliness and is not
Your eyes are inflamed with passion, your lip-bud is trembling,

children.text: भ्रुवौ च भुग्ने न तथाप्यदुष्टस्यास्ति मे भयम् ॥ १३१ ॥
children.translated_text: and your eyebrows are curved — yet I who am without fault have no fear. || 131 ||

children.text: चण्डि ! चक्षुषी तव इमे रज्येते रोषरागमागच्छतः । अधरश्च पल्लवोऽयं स्फुरति कोपकम्पमनुगच्छति । भ्रुवौ च इमे भुग्ने जिह्मभावमाभजतः । कामं तथापि । अदुष्टस्यानिरागसो मे मम भयं त्रासो नास्ति । सापराधो हि बिभीयात् । किमहमवाच्यो बिभेमीति ॥
children.translated_text: O wrathful one (<s>caṇḍi</s>)! These eyes of yours are inflamed, they are acquiring the color of anger. And this lip-bud is trembling, following the quivering of anger. And these eyebrows are curved, assuming a crooked form. Let it be so, nevertheless — I who am without fault, who am innocent, have no fear, no terror. For only one who has committed an offense would be afraid. Why should I, who am blameless, be afraid?
He explains that —

children.text: स एष कारणाक्षेपः प्रधानं कारणं भियः ।
children.translated_text: This is <s>kāraṇākṣepa</s> (objection to the cause); the principal cause of fear,
namely one's own offense, has been negated here by the clever lover. || 132 ||

children.text: यद् यस्मात् पटीयसा दोषपरिहारचतुरेण प्रियेण भियो भयस्य प्रधानम् उचितं कारणम् अन्यद् भवदपि अनुचितं स्वस्य स्वो वा अपरावो दोषो निषिद्धः अत्र प्रयोगे । तस्मात् स एष ईदृशः कारणस्य [आ]क्षेपो विज्ञेय इति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yad</s>) by the clever lover, one who is skilled in averting blame, the principal, that is, appropriate, cause of fear — even though other causes may exist — one's own offense or fault has been negated in this composition. Even though the inappropriate cause exists, the appropriate one has been denied. Therefore this is such an <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) of the cause.
The beloved is far away; this onset of the rainy season has arrived;

children.text: दृष्टाश्च फुल्ला निचुला न मृता चास्मि किं न्विदम् ॥ १३३ ॥
children.translated_text: and the <s>niculas</s> (barringtonia trees) have been seen in full bloom — yet I have not died. What is this? || 133 ||

children.text: प्रियतमो दूरे प्रेषितो वर्तते । योऽसौ विरहिणीप्राणप्रयाणसमयः सोऽयं जलदागमोऽप्यागतः । फुल्ला निचुला वञ्जुला मञ्जुमञ्जरीजालजटिलशिरसो दृष्टा दृष्टिकटवः । एवं [सन्निहित]समग्रमरणकारणा साहं न च मृतास्मि । किं न्विदं विधिविलसितं दीर्घदुःखभाजनतां नीता वयम् अमुना दग्धदैवेनेति ॥
children.translated_text: The beloved has been dispatched far away. That time which causes the departure of the life-breath of women in separation — this onset of clouds (<s>jaladāgama</s>, the rainy season) has also arrived. The <s>niculas</s> (barringtonia trees), that is, <s>vañjulas</s>, with their heads dense with clusters of beautiful flower-bunches, have been seen in full bloom — a sight painful to the eyes. Thus, though all causes of death are present together, I have not died. What is this sport of fate? We have been led to be vessels of prolonged suffering by this accursed destiny.
He explains that —
<s>Kāryākṣepa</s> (objection to the effect) is this, since the effect, namely death, has been averted
even after presenting the terrible cause — the onset of the rainy season. || 134 ||

children.text: तस्य मरणस्य कारणं दारुणम् अतिदुःसहं जलदागममुत्फुल्लनिचुलं प्रियवियोगसचिवमुपन्यस्य प्रतिपाद्य कार्यस्य मरणस्य निवर्तनात् न मृतास्मीति सोऽयमीदृशः कार्यस्याक्षेपः प्रतिपत्तव्य इति ॥
children.translated_text: Having presented, that is, having set forth, the cause of that death — the terrible, utterly unbearable onset of the rainy season together with the blooming <s>niculas</s> (barringtonia trees), the companions of separation from the beloved — because of the averting of the effect, namely death, through the statement 'I have not died,' this is such an <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) of the effect, which should be understood.

children.text: न चिरं तापाय तव यात्रा भविष्यति ।
children.translated_text: Your journey will not be a source of torment for long,
so if you must go, then go — enough of your apprehension here. || 135 ||

children.text: वल्लभ ! तव यात्रा गमनं चिरं दीर्घं मम तापाय दुःखार्थं न भविष्यति । स्वल्पोऽपि तापस्त्वया विना मृताया न मे सम्भवति । जीवन्ती हि तमनुभवेत् । न च मरणसुखं परित्यज्य काचित्सचेतना दुःख
भावमीदृशं प्रतीच्छतीति पञ्चतां सूचयतीति । अत्र च वस्तुनि ते तव शङ्क्या अन्यथासम्भावनयालं नान्यथा शङ्कनीयं नियतमेतत । तस्मात् यदि यास्यसि यातव्यं गम्यतां किं स्थीयत इति ॥
children.translated_text: suffering — thus she hints at her own death. And in this matter, enough with your apprehension (<s>śaṅkā</s>), that is, imagining otherwise — this is certain, it should not be suspected to be otherwise. Therefore, if you will go, then go — why do you linger?

O beloved! Your journey, your departure, will not be for long, for the sake of my torment, my suffering. Even the slightest torment without you is impossible for me who will be dead. For only one who is alive could experience it. And no sentient being would, abandoning the happiness of death, accept such a state of
He explains that —
Thus, in the guise of permission, the beloved's departure is objected to;
while hinting at her own death, this is recognized as <s>anujñākṣepa</s> (objection through permission). || 136 ||

children.text: इत्युक्तेन विधिना अनुज्ञामुखेन अनुमतिद्वारेणैवं यातव्यमिति कान्यस्य गतिः आक्षिप्यते मरणमात्मनः सूचयन्त्या भङ्ग्या कथयन्त्यैव प्रियया । इदमाक्षेपनिमित्तम् । तस्मात् स तादृशोऽनुज्ञाक्षेप इष्यते तज्ज्ञैरिति ॥
children.translated_text: By the method stated above, through the door of permission (<s>anujñā</s>), that is, through the gate of consent — thus, 'you should go' — the departure of the beloved is objected to, by the beloved woman who, by suggestion, is indicating, that is, declaring, her own death. This is the basis for the objection. Therefore, such is recognized by the learned as <s>anujñākṣepa</s> (objection through permission).

children.text: धनं च बहु लभ्यं ते सुखं क्षेमं च वर्त्मनि ।
children.translated_text: You will obtain abundant wealth, and comfort and safety on the road;

children.text: न च मे प्राणसन्देहस्तथापि प्रिय ! मा स्म गाः ॥ १३७ ॥
children.translated_text: and there is no danger to my life — yet, O dear one, do not go! || 137 ||

children.text: बहु प्रभूतं धनं लभ्यं ते तवास्तु । अनेन योगो दर्शितः । क्षेमश्च लब्धधनरक्षणलक्षणः । सुखं च वर्त्मनि क्लेशाभावात् भवतु नाम । न च मे त्वद्वियुक्तायाः प्राणसन्देहो मरणमप्युपगतम् । तथाप्येवं गमनपरिपन्थिनिमित्ताभावेऽपि प्रिय मा स्म गाः न गन्तव्यम् । एवं तावन्मयेष्टमिंति अव्याहतप्रण्यप्रसरा काचिदाक्षिपति ॥
children.translated_text: May abundant, plentiful wealth be obtained by you. By this, the gain (<s>yoga</s>) has been indicated. And safety (<s>kṣema</s>), characterized by the protection of wealth already obtained. And comfort on the road, due to the absence of hardship — let all this be so. And there is no doubt about my life, that is, even death has been accepted, while separated from you. Yet even so, even when there is no obstacle to the journey, O dear one, do not go, you must not depart. Thus does a certain woman, with her affectionate feelings flowing unobstructed, make her objection.
He explains that —
By one who dismisses the reasons that would obstruct her beloved's journey,
it is restrained by sheer authority alone — therefore this is recognized as <s>prabhūtvākṣepa</s> (objection through authority). || 138 ||

children.text: प्रियस्य यात्रां विबध्नतो विरुद्धान् हेतून् अयोगक्षेमादीन् तत्प्रतिपक्षप्रकाशनेन प्रत्याचक्षाण्या निवारयन्त्या गन्तुकामस्य कस्यचित् प्रभुत्वेनैव कान्तविषयेण स्वातन्त्र्येण रुद्ध आक्षिंप्तो यतस्तत् तस्मादीदृश एवंजातीयः प्रभुत्वाक्षेप इष्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: By a woman who wards off, that is, removes, the contrary reasons such as lack of gain and safety and so forth, by revealing their opposites, and who restrains the journey of her beloved who wishes to depart, by sheer authority alone, that is, by her sovereign power over her lover — because it is thus objected to, therefore this type is recognized as <s>prabhūtvākṣepa</s> (objection through authority).
My desire for life is strong, but my desire for wealth is weak;

children.text: गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा कान्त ! स्वावस्था तु निवेदिता ॥ १३९ ॥
children.translated_text: go or stay, O beloved — but my own condition has been declared. || 139 ||

children.text: जीविंते प्राणेष्वाशा आसक्तिः बलवती गरीयसी । मम धनेष्वाशा अभिलाषः पुनर्दुर्बला तन्वी । धनादपि मे जीवितं प्रियमिंत्यर्थः । ततो नाहं जीवितव्ययेन त्वद्यात्रासाध्यं धनमभिलषामि । त्वं पुनर्यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु । गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा । न किंचित् मम अनया चिन्तया । तदपि किं त्वमीच्छसीत्याह— स्वावस्था तु निवेदिंतेति । स्वाभिप्रायः पुनर्मया दर्शित एव, न मे जीविताद्धनं दयितम्, यतः प्राणमूल्येन तदुपादास्ये । जीवितमेवा[भिलषामि] । न किञ्चिन्मे तेन धनेनेति ॥
children.translated_text: The desire, the attachment, for life, for the vital breaths, is strong, is weighty. My desire, my longing, for wealth is weak, is feeble. Life is dearer to me than wealth — such is the meaning. Therefore I do not desire wealth that is to be obtained through your journey at the cost of my life. But you, do as you wish — go or stay. I have no concern with this worry. And then, what do you wish? She says: 'But my own condition has been declared.' My own intention has indeed been shown by me — wealth is not dearer to me than life, for I would have to procure it at the price of my life. It is life alone that I desire. I have no use for that wealth.
He categorizes that —
This is <s>anādarākṣepa</s> (objection through indifference), because a word of seeming indifference
has been employed here by a passionate woman who obstructs her beloved's departure. || 140 ||

Because (<s>yat</s>) here in this composition, by a certain passionate woman who obstructs, that is, objects to, the departure of her beloved, a word of seeming indifference — that is, one in which there appears to be a lack of care, devoid of attachment — the statement 'go or stay' has been employed; therefore this is such an <s>anādarākṣepa</s> (objection through indifference).

children.text: यस्मादिह प्रयोगे रक्तया कयाचित् प्रियस्य प्रयाणं रुन्धत्या आक्षिपन्त्या अनादरवदनादरोऽस्मिन्नस्तीति आस्थाशून्यं वचो वचनं गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा इति प्रयुक्तम्, तस्मात् असौ ईदृशोऽनादराक्षेपः ॥
गच्छ गच्छसि चेत् कान्त ! पन्थानः सन्तु ते शिवाः ।
children.translated_text: Go, if you must go, O beloved! May your paths be auspicious;

children.text: ममापि जन्म तत्रैव भूयाद् यत्र गतो भवान् ॥ १४१ ॥
children.translated_text: and may my birth too occur in that very place where you have gone. || 141 ||

children.text: कान्त, गच्छसि चेत् । यदि निश्चितं गमनम्, गच्छ । किं स्थीयते, [ते तव] पन्थानः शिवाः सुखावहाः सन्तु इदमाशास्महे । इदं चापरम्, ममापि
children.translated_text: O beloved, if you must go, if the departure is certain, then go. Why do you linger? May your paths be auspicious, bringing happiness — this is what I pray for. And here is another thing: may my

children.text: तद्विंरहग्रहापहृतजीवितायाः जन्म प्रादुर्भावस्तत्रैव भूयात्, यत्र देशे गतो भवान् । न केवलं तव तत्र गमनमित्यपि शब्दः ॥
children.translated_text: birth, that is, the re-emergence of one whose life has been seized by the demon of separation from you, occur in that very place, in that very land where you have gone. The word 'also' (<s>api</s>) indicates that not merely is your going there intended.
He demonstrates that —
This is <s>āśīrvacanākṣepa</s> (objection through words of blessing), since through the path of benediction,
while hinting at her own condition, the beloved's journey is prohibited. || 142 ||

children.text: यस्मादित्येवमाशीर्वादवर्त्मना इष्टाशंसनमुखेन कान्तस्य [यात्रा] गमनं निषिध्यते । स्वामवस्थां निधनप्राप्तिं कान्तप्रयाणकारणां सूचयन्त्या सव्याजमावेद्यन्त्या कयाचित् प्रियया । तस्मात् आशीर्वचनाक्षेपस्तादृश इति ॥
children.translated_text: Since (<s>yasmāt</s>) in this manner, through the path of benediction, that is, through the guise of expressing good wishes, the journey, that is, the departure, of the beloved is prohibited — by a certain beloved woman who hints at, that is, who with a pretext reveals, her own condition, namely that death will result from the beloved's departure. Therefore, such is the <s>āśīrvacanākṣepa</s> (objection through words of blessing).

children.text: यदि सत्यैव ते यात्रा काप्यन्या मृग्यतां त्वया ।
children.translated_text: If your journey is truly certain, then let some other woman be sought by you,
for I am already seized today by death, which awaits an opening. || 143 ||

children.text: ते तव यात्रा गमनं सत्यैव नियतैव यदि [न] वचनमात्रं, तदा कापि काचिदन्या प्रिया मृग्यताम् अन्विष्यताम् त्वया स्त्रीवधवल्लभेन । पूर्णो ममावधिः । यदाहअद्यैव न कालान्तरे साहं रुद्धा क्रोड़ीकृता अस्मि मृत्युना रन्ध्रं त्वद्विरहादिलक्षणम् अवकाशम् अपेक्षमाणेन । त्यज्यतामस्मत्प्रत्याशा । न चाहं तव किञ्चिदिति ॥
children.translated_text: If your journey, your departure, is truly certain, not mere words, then let some other beloved woman be sought, be searched for, by you, O one fond of women's destruction. My allotted time is complete. As she says: today itself, not at some later time, I have been seized, that is, embraced, by death, which is watching for an opening (<s>randhra</s>) in the form of separation from you and the like. Abandon your expectation regarding me. I am nothing to you anymore.
He states that —
This is <s>paruṣākṣepa</s> (objection through harsh words), since, preceded by harsh syllables,
the departure of the beloved is objected to by a woman overwhelmed with love. || 144 ||

children.text: इत्येवं परुषं निरपेक्षमक्षरं वचनं पूर्वं यस्मिन् आक्षेप इति क्रियाविशेषणम् । कान्तस्य प्रस्थानं यात्रा आक्षिप्यते । प्रेमनिंध्नया कयाचिदनुरागपरवशया यस्मात् ततः परुषाक्षेप एष इति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, a harsh, indifferent word or utterance precedes the objection — this qualifies the action. The departure, the journey, of the beloved is objected to by a certain woman overwhelmed with love (<s>premanidhna</s>), completely subjugated by passion. Because of this, this is the <s>paruṣākṣepa</s> (objection through harsh words).

children.text: गन्ता चेद् गच्छ तूर्णं ते कर्णौ यन्ति पुरा रवाः ।
children.translated_text: If you are resolved to go, then go quickly, before the cries reach your ears —
those cries uttered from the mouths of anguished kinsmen, which would obstruct your departure. || 145 ||

children.text: गन्ता गच्छसि चेत् । गच्छ तूर्णं शीघ्रं मा विलम्बिंष्ठाः, यतोऽमङ्गलपरिहारः स्यात् । यदाह—आर्तानामेतन्मरणशोका तुराणां बन्धूनां मुखैरुद्गीर्णा मुक्ता रवा
आक्रन्दाः प्रयाणं प्रतिबध्नन्तः तव कर्णं पुरा यन्ति यास्यन्ति यावत् ते नोत्तिष्ठन्ति तावदेव गच्छेति ॥
children.translated_text: The cries that obstruct the departure will reach your ears before — those that will come — go only while they have not yet arisen!

If you are resolved to go, if you will depart — then go quickly, swiftly, do not delay, so that the inauspicious may be avoided. As she says: the cries released from the mouths of anguished kinsmen, those who are afflicted with grief at this death,
He analyzes that —
This is indeed <s>sācivyākṣepa</s> (objection through companionship), since what is prohibited here
is the departure of the beloved, by an excessively passionate woman who acts as a companion. || 146 ||

children.text: यद्यस्मात् । अत्र प्रयाणे सा[चि]व्यं सहायभावं कुर्वत्यैव कयाचिंत् अतिंरक्तया प्रियस्य प्रयाणं निपुणं प्रतिषिध्यते । ततः साचिव्ययोगादेष ईदृशः साचिव्याक्षेप एवेति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yad</s>): here in the matter of departure, by a certain excessively passionate woman who acts as a companion (<s>sācivya</s>), that is, who assumes the role of an ally, the departure of the beloved is skillfully prohibited. Therefore, due to the association with companionship, this is such a <s>sācivyākṣepa</s> (objection through companionship).
O my beloved! Desiring what is pleasing to you, I wish to say 'Go,'

children.text: निर्गच्छति मुखाद् वाणी मा गा इति करोमि किम् ॥ १४७ ॥
children.translated_text: but the words that issue from my mouth say 'Do not go!' — what am I to do? || 147 ||

children.text: मम प्रिय वल्लभ ! तव प्रियं प्रयाणमिच्छन्ती सती गच्छेति वक्तुमिच्छामि । तथाप्यनिच्छन्त्या एव मे मुखात् मा गास्त्वमिति वाणी
वचनं निर्गच्छति । किमहं करोमि । न मे कश्चित् तावद्दोषः । त्वत्प्रियं मत्प्रियैषिणीति पाठे गच्छेत्येतत् तव प्रियं वक्तुमिच्छामि मम प्रियमिच्छन्ती वाणी मा गा इति निर्गच्छतीति व्याख्येयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: 'Do not go!' What am I to do? I am not at fault in this. In the reading <s>tvatpriyaṃ matpriyaiṣiṇī</s>, the explanation should be: I wish to say that which is pleasing to you, namely 'Go,' but the speech desiring my own happiness issues forth as 'Do not go!'
O my beloved, my dear one! Desiring your happiness, wishing for your departure, I wish to say 'Go.' Yet, involuntarily, from my mouth issues the speech
He elaborates on that —
<s>Yatnākṣepa</s> (objection to effort) is that in which, when effort has been made toward an undesired object,
the opposite result arises, demonstrating its futility. || 148 ||

children.text: स तादृशः यत्नाक्षेपो ज्ञेयः । अतः अनिष्टे वस्तुनि प्रियप्रयाणे तत्सिद्धये कृतस्य यत्नस्य श्रमस्ये[ति यावत्] गच्छेति वक्तुमिच्छामीति विपरीतं विरुद्धं मा गा इति वचनरूपं फलं कार्यमुत्पन्नम् । तस्योत्पत्तेः कारणात् स यत्नोऽनर्थको जातः । तस्मादानर्थक्योपदर्शनात् प्रकाशनाद् यत्नाक्षेपः स इति निगमयितव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: That should be understood as such a <s>yatnākṣepa</s> (objection to effort). Because: in the undesired matter, namely the departure of the beloved, the effort made for its accomplishment — that is, the exertion [of trying] to say 'I wish to say Go' — has produced a contrary, opposite result in the form of the words 'Do not go!' Because of the arising of that result, that effort has become futile. Therefore, because of the demonstration of its futility, it should be concluded as <s>yatnākṣepa</s> (objection to effort).
Tell the love that grows angry even at a momentary hindrance to sight, at the blinking of the eyelashes,

children.text: प्रेम्णः प्रयाणं ते ब्रूहि मया तस्येष्टमिष्यते ॥ १४९ ॥
children.translated_text: about your departure — whatever it desires shall be carried out by me. || 149 ||

children.text: ते तव प्रयाणक्षणं दर्शनस्य विघ्नाय पक्ष्मास्पन्दाय चक्षुनिंमेषाय कुप्यतः प्रेम्णः स्नेहस्य ब्रूहि कथय । वचनविषयस्य सम्बन्धित्वेन वितक्षितत्वात् षष्ठी । किमेवमित्याह— यत् तस्य प्रेम्णोपदिष्टमनुमतं किञ्चित् तन्मयेष्यते । नाहं स्वतन्त्रा किं तवाविदितम् ? तस्मात् प्रेमैव भावय । तच्चेदनुमन्यते के वयमन्यथाकर्तुमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Tell, declare to the love (<s>preman</s>), the affection, that grows angry even at a momentary hindrance to seeing and at the blinking of the eyelashes, about your departure. The genitive case is used because it is conceived as being related to the topic of speech. Why so? She says: whatever that love has instructed or approved shall be carried out by me. Am I not independent — is this unknown to you? Therefore, cultivate love alone. If it consents, who are we to act otherwise?
He elucidates that —
This is <s>paravaśākṣepa</s> (objection through dependence on another), since by one who is subject to love,
the journey is prohibited, through the suggestion of that state of affairs. || 150 ||

children.text: अयमीदृशः परवशाक्षेपः कुतः प्रेमपरतन्त्रया स्नेहनिघ्नया तया प्रियया कयाचित् यात्रा प्रियस्य निषिध्यते इति यदेतत् तस्येदृशस्यार्थस्य वस्तुन उपसूचनादुद्भावनादिंति ॥
children.translated_text: This is such a <s>paravaśākṣepa</s> (objection through dependence on another). Why? Because by a certain beloved woman who is subject to love (<s>premaparatantrā</s>), overwhelmed by affection, the journey of the beloved is prohibited — through the suggestion, the evocation of this state of affairs.
I shall endure the separation, O lord! Give me the <s>adṛśyāñjana</s> (ointment of invisibility),

children.text: यदक्तनेत्रां कन्दर्पः प्रहर्ता मां न पश्यति ॥ १५१ ॥
children.translated_text: so that <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), the striker, does not see me whose eyes have been anointed with it. || 151 ||

children.text: नाथ ! तव विरहं दुःसहमप्यहं सहिष्ये यापयामि । किं तु अ[दर्शनसाधन]मञ्जनं किञ्चिन्मे देहि । किं तेन ? येनादृश्याञ्जनेनाक्ते स्पृष्टे नेत्रे यस्यास्तां मां न पश्यति कन्दर्पः कामः प्रहर्ता हन्ता । अपश्यतः कथं प्रहरेदिति ॥
children.translated_text: O lord! I shall endure, I shall bear through, the separation from you, unbearable though it is. But give me some ointment that is the [means of becoming invisible]. What would I do with it? By that ointment of invisibility, when applied to, when touching, the eyes — <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), <s>Kāma</s>, the striker, the destroyer, does not see me whose eyes have been so anointed. If he does not see, how would he strike?
He makes that clear —
Having proposed a difficult means of survival, the husband's departure is objected to;
the learned call such a thing <s>upāyākṣepa</s> (objection through the means). || 152 ||

children.text: दुष्करं दुर्लभं जीवितस्योपायं अदृश्याञ्जनरूपमुपन्यस्य पत्युः प्रस्थानमुपरुध्यते इति हेतोरीदृशमुपायाक्षेपमाहुस्तद्विद इति ॥
बुध्वा वक्ति प्रियं दृष्ट्वा किं चिरेणागतो भवान् ॥

children.translated_text: Having proposed a difficult, unattainable means of survival — in the form of the ointment of invisibility — the departure of the husband is objected to. For this reason, the knowledgeable call this <s>upāyākṣepa</s> (objection through the means).

children.text: प्रवृत्तैव प्रयामीति वाणी वल्लभ ! ते मुखात् ।
children.translated_text: O beloved! From your mouth the words 'I shall go' have already issued forth;
even without your having departed now, O one of feeble love — what remains for me? || 153 ||

children.text: वल्लभ ! ते तव मुखात् प्रवृत्ता एव तावत्प्रयामीति वाणी वचनम् । तदेवं मन्दप्रेम्णा मन्दं प्रेमा अस्येति निरपेक्षेण त्वया कथञ्चित् अयता अगच्छतापि सता
इदानीं मम किमस्ति कार्यम् ? न किञ्चित् । [मनसि शिथिलादरस्य तव] गमनमगमनं चेदानीं तुल्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: what is there now for me to do? Nothing at all. [In the mind of one whose regard has become slack] going and not going are now the same.

O beloved! From your mouth has indeed issued forth the speech, the words 'I shall go.' Thus, by you whose love is feeble (<s>mandapreman</s>), who is indifferent, even without having gone, without having departed,
He explains that —
This is <s>roṣākṣepa</s> (objection through anger), by one whose mind is unrestrained due to excessive love,
who, enraged, prevents the departure undertaken by the beloved. || 154 ||

children.text: यद् यस्मात् उद्रिक्तेनाधिमात्रेण स्नेहेन निर्यन्त्रण उद्दामः आत्मा चित्तं यस्याः तया अत एव संरब्धया आविष्कृतरोषया प्रियेणारब्धं कर्तुमभिप्रेतं प्रयाणं निवार्यते । तस्मादयमीदृशो रोषाक्षेपः, कोपावेशेन निषेधादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yad</s>): by one whose mind (<s>ātman</s>) is unrestrained (<s>niryantrana</s>), unbridled, due to excessive, extreme love (<s>sneha</s>), and who is therefore enraged (<s>saṃrabdha</s>), with manifest anger, the departure intended to be undertaken by the beloved is prevented. Therefore this is such a <s>roṣākṣepa</s> (objection through anger), since the prohibition arises from an outburst of fury.

children.text: नाघ्रातं न कृतं कर्णे स्त्रीभिर्मधुनि नार्पितम् ।
children.translated_text: Not smelled, not placed upon the ear, by women; not offered in honey —
the lotus has withered and decayed in the ponds of your enemies alone. || 155 ||

children.text: स्त्रीभिर्नाघ्रातं न च कर्णे कृतं श्रवणावतंसकृत्ये नियुक्तम् । मधुनि च नार्पितम् । एतावानेवोत्पलस्योपयोगः । केवलं तव द्विषामरातीनां हतानां दीर्घिकास्वेव शून्यासु विशीर्णं परिक्षतं जीर्णं परिणतं उत्पलमभवदिति ॥
children.translated_text: Not smelled by women, nor placed upon the ear for the purpose of an ear-ornament, nor offered in honey — such is the extent of a lotus's utility. It has merely withered and decayed, perished, in the empty ponds of your enemies, the slain foes.
He reveals that —
This is <s>anukrośākṣepa</s> (objection through compassion), as if showing compassion toward the lotus,
by turning away from its proper function and depicting its pitiable condition. || 156 ||

children.text: असौ तादृशः अनुक्रोशाक्षेपो ज्ञेयः । कुतः ? उत्पले उत्पलविषये सानुक्रोशमिव सकरुणमिव । उत्पलेऽचेतने साक्षादनुक्रोशाभावादिव [शब्द] प्रयोगः । व्यावर्तनक्रियाविशेषणं चैतत् । यदाह—तस्योत्पलस्य योग्यमुचिंतं कर्म घ्राणादि व्यावृत्य निराकृत्य नाघ्रातमित्यादिना शोच्यायाः क्रियापदस्यावस्थाया विशीर्णत्वादेरुपदर्शनादिति ॥
children.translated_text: That should be understood as such an <s>anukrośākṣepa</s> (objection through compassion). Why? Because it is as if showing compassion (<s>sānukrośam iva</s>) toward the lotus. Since compassion is not literally possible toward an inanimate lotus, the word 'as if' (<s>iva</s>) is used. This qualifies the action of turning away. As stated: by turning away from, by negating, the proper, fitting function of that lotus — such as being smelled and so forth — through the words 'not smelled' and the rest, and through the depiction of its pitiable condition of withering and so forth, [this is the objection through compassion].

children.text: अर्थो न सम्भृतः कश्चिन्न विद्या काचिदर्जिता ।
children.translated_text: No wealth has been acquired, no knowledge has been gained,

children.text: न तपः सञ्चितं किञ्चिद् गतं च सकलं वयः ॥ १५७ ॥
children.translated_text: no austerity has been accumulated, and the entire lifespan has passed. || 157 ||

children.text: कञ्चिद् विवक्षितोऽर्थो धनं न सम्भृतः नोपार्जितः । विद्यापि काचित् आन्वीक्षिक्यादिर्नार्जिता । तपश्च धर्मः किञ्चित् अभिमतं न सञ्चितम् । गतम् अतीतं च सकलं वयः पुरुषायुषम् अपुरुषार्थोपयोगेन । किमेवमात्मैवमात्मना वञ्चितः ॥
children.translated_text: Some intended wealth, property, has not been acquired, not earned. Nor has any knowledge — such as logic (<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>) and the like — been gained. And no desired austerity, that is, <s>dharma</s>, has been accumulated. The entire lifespan has passed, elapsed, without serving any of the <s>puruṣārthas</s> (goals of human life). What then — one has thus been deceived by oneself.
He categorizes that —
This is <s>anuśayākṣepa</s> (objection through remorse), since, accompanied by remorse,
the failure to acquire wealth and so forth has been shown here by one whose life has passed. || 158 ||

children.text: यस्मात् अर्थस्यार्जनमादिर्यस्य विद्यार्जनादेः तस्य व्यावृत्तिः अभावः [दर्शिता] कथम् ? अनुशयः पश्चाताप उत्तरोऽधिको यस्मिन् दर्शन इति क्रियाविशेषणम् । गतायुषा गतवयसा पुंसा केनचित् । तस्मात् असौ ईदृशोऽनुशयाक्षेप इति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yasmāt</s>): the failure, the absence, of the acquisition of wealth and the rest — knowledge and so forth — has been shown. How? In a manner in which remorse (<s>anuśaya</s>), regret, is predominant — this qualifies the showing. By a person whose life has passed, whose lifespan is spent. Therefore, this is such an <s>anuśayākṣepa</s> (objection through remorse).
Whose essence is nectar like that of lotuses, who is the enemy of the bright stars,
when this moon of your face truly exists, what need is there for another moon? || 159 ||

children.text: तव मुखे इन्दौ सति अस्मिन् प्रत्यक्षवर्तिनि इतरेण मुखेन इन्दुना किमधिकं कार्यम् ? न किञ्चित् । अमृतमिवात्मा स्वरूपमेकान्तप्रीतिकरत्वात् यस्य मुखेन्दोः स तथा । अमृतं सुधैव

आत्मा यस्येन्दोरिति शब्दश्लेषः । पद्मानां द्वेष्टा मुखेन्दुः तत्सदृशत्वादिन्दुश्च तत्सं[को]चकारित्वात् । अयमपि शब्दश्लेषः । स्निग्धे रक्ते तारके नेत्रमध्यभागे ततो वा समुदायोपलक्षणाच्चक्षुषी यस्य मुखेन्दोः । स्निग्धाः तारका रोहिण्यादयो यस्येन्दोरिति शब्दश्लेष एव । एवम[क्षी]णगुणे मुखेणे मुखेन्दौ सति किमितरेणेन्दुनेति प्रत्याम्नायः ॥
children.translated_text: the essence of the moon — this is a <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal pun). The moon-face is an enemy of lotuses because of its resemblance to the moon, and the moon because it causes them to close — this too is a <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal pun). The moon-face has tender, loving pupils (<s>tārakā</s>) in the center of its eyes, or by synecdoche, the eyes; the moon has bright stars (<s>tārakā</s>) like <s>Rohiṇī</s> and others — this again is a <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal pun). Thus, when the moon-face of inexhaustible qualities exists, what need for another moon — this is the substitution (<s>pratyāmnāya</s>).

When there exists this moon of your face, present before one's eyes — what further purpose is there for the other moon? None at all. That whose essence (<s>ātman</s>) is nectar, due to being entirely delightful — this describes the moon-face. Nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) is indeed
He explains that —
Thus the moon-face has objected to the [real] moon; having shown qualities residing in the secondary moon
that are common to it — this is <s>śliṣṭākṣepa</s> (objection through punning), of such a kind. || 160 ||

children.text: इति एवं तत्समान् मुखेन्दुसाधारणान् गुणान् अमृतात्मत्वादीन् गौणे मुखेन्दौ वर्तमानान् दर्शयित्वा प्रतिपाद्य मुखेन्दुराक्षिप्तः किमिन्दुनेति । तस्मात् श्लिष्टाक्षेपः तथाविधः तादृशोऽवगन्तव्यः श्लेषप्रयोगादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, in this manner, having shown, having demonstrated, the qualities common to the moon-face — such as having nectar as its essence and so forth — that reside in the secondary moon, the moon-face has objected to the [real] moon with the words 'what need is there for the moon?' Therefore, <s>śliṣṭākṣepa</s> (objection through punning) should be understood as such, due to the employment of <s>śleṣa</s> (punning).
Is this an autumn cloud, or is it a flock of swans?

children.text: रुतं नू पुरसंवादि श्रूयते तन्न तोयदः ॥ १६१ ॥
children.translated_text: Since a sound concordant with anklet-bells is heard, it is not a rain-cloud. || 161 ||

children.text: अयं दृश्यमानः किं शरदि शरदो वा अम्मोदः, किं वा आहोस्वित् हंसानां कदम्बकं वृन्दमिदम् ? भवतु, विदितम् । नूपुरनिनादसदृशमनुरुतं श्रूयते यतः, तत् तस्मात् नायं तोयदः किं तु हंसकदम्बकमेवेति ॥
children.translated_text: This that is being seen — is it a cloud in autumn, or of autumn? Or is it a flock (<s>kadambaka</s>), a group of swans? Let it be so, it is understood. Since a sound resembling the tinkling of anklets is heard, therefore it is not a rain-cloud; rather, it is indeed a flock of swans.
He explains that —
This is <s>saṃśayākṣepa</s> (objection through doubt), since the doubt is resolved
by a property readily found in swans but not touching the cloud-species. || 162 ||

children.text: यत् यस्मात् संशयः, शरदम्भोदो हंसकदम्बकं वेति सन्देहो न निवर्त्यते हंसे हंसेन वा सुलभेन तत्रैव सम्भवात् । धर्मेण गुणेन नूपुरसंवादिना रुतेनास्पृष्टा तत्रासम्भवात्, घनजातिः मेघो येन तेन हेतुना कर्तृभूतेन वा । तस्मादित्ययमीदृशः संशयाक्षेप इति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yat</s>): the doubt — whether it is an autumn cloud or a flock of swans — is resolved. Not [merely resolved], but by a property, a quality — namely the sound concordant with anklet-bells — that is readily found in swans, since it naturally occurs there; and that is untouched by the cloud-species, since it does not occur there. By this reason, or by this as the agent. Therefore, this is such a <s>saṃśayākṣepa</s> (objection through doubt).
It is astonishing! Though you have conquered the entire world, your valor is not satiated;
but then, when is satiation ever seen in a blazing fire? || 163 ||

children.text: चित्रमद्भतमेतत् । आक्रान्तममिभूतं विश्वं जगद्येन स तथाभूतोऽपि तव विक्रमः शौर्यं न तृप्यति नाभिलाषपर्यन्तमधिगच्छति । अथवा किं चित्रम् ?  उदीर्णस्याधिमात्रस्य हविर्भुजोऽग्नेः कदा तृप्तिर्दृश्यते ? न कदाचित् । तथा विक्रमस्तव जगदाक्रम्यापि न तृप्यतीति योज्यम् ।
children.translated_text: This is astonishing, marvelous. Even though the entire world has been conquered, subdued by your valor, your prowess is not satiated, does not reach the limit of its ambition. Or, what is so astonishing? When is satiation of a blazing, mighty fire (<s>havirbhuj</s>) ever seen? Never. Likewise, your valor, even after conquering the world, is not satiated — this should be construed.
He explains that —
This is <s>arthāntarākṣepa</s> (objection through another matter), since the wonder at the matter at hand is resolved
by showing another matter that shares the same property. || 164 ||

children.text: यत् यस्मात्प्रक्रान्तः प्रस्तुतो विस्मयो निवर्त्यते अर्थान्तरस्याग्नेः । तेन विक्रमेण सधर्मणस्तुल्यस्य दर्शनादवगमात् । ततोऽर्थान्तराक्षेपोऽयम्, अर्थान्तरेण तादृशेन विस्मयस्य निषेधादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Because (<s>yat</s>): the wonder at the matter at hand — the present topic — is resolved by the perception, the understanding, of another matter, namely fire, which shares the same property, which is similar, to that valor. Therefore this is <s>arthāntarākṣepa</s> (objection through another matter), since the wonder is negated by such another matter.

children.text: न स्तूयसे नरेन्द्र ! त्वं ददासीति कदाचन ।
children.translated_text: O king, you are never praised as one who gives,
for the supplicants, considering your wealth as their own, simply take it. || 165 ||

children.text: नरेन्द्र, ददासि त्वं धनमर्थिभ्य इति कथञ्चन केनापि प्रकारेण न स्तूयसे । किं कारणम् ? यतः कारणात्
तव धनमर्थिनः स्वम् आत्मीयमेव मत्वा गृह्णन्ति । नास्येदं धनम् अस्माकमेवेदम्, वयमुपभोक्तारः केवलमस्मदर्थं रक्षति । यद्वा अस्य धनं तदस्माकमपि सर्वसाधारणविभवत्वादस्येति ॥
children.translated_text: the supplicants take your wealth, considering it as their own. 'This wealth is not his; it is ours alone; he merely guards it for our sake. Or rather, his wealth is also ours, since his affluence is common to all' — thus they reason.
O king, you are not praised in any manner whatsoever by anyone as one who gives wealth to supplicants. For what reason? Because

body.translated_text: He states —

children.translated_text: Such and similar is the <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) known as <s>hetvākṣepa</s> (objection through reason);
following this very direction, other varieties too may be inferred. || 166 ||

body.text: इत्येवमनन्तरोक्तः प्रकारः आदिर्यस्येति एवमादिराक्षेपः हेत्वाक्षेप इति स्मृतः तज्जैः । हेतूपन्यासेन निषेधात् । शेषानाक्षेपविकल्पानतिदिशन्ति गमयन्ति । अनयैव अनन्तरदर्शितया दिशा आक्षेपविकल्पगत्या अन्येऽप्यनुक्ता विकल्पा आक्षेपप्रभेदा ऊहितुमनुगन्तुं शक्यम् ।
body.translated_text: The form just described above is the foremost example of such an <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), known by the learned as <s>hetvākṣepa</s> (objection through reason), since the prohibition is accomplished by presenting a reason. They then extend the remaining varieties of <s>ākṣepa</s>: following this very direction, this approach to the varieties of <s>ākṣepa</s> just demonstrated, other unstated varieties, subspecies of <s>ākṣepa</s>, may be inferred, may be deduced.

body.text: ननु वाच्यलिङ्गत्वात् तव्यादेः विकल्पो इत्यपेक्ष्य शक्या इति युक्तम् । उच्यते, इह शक्यमिति सामान्यविवक्षया प्रयुज्यते । ततः किं शक्यमिति विशेषापेक्षायां विकल्पा इति सं[भ]न्स्यते । तत्र यद्यपि बहुत्वं पुंस्त्वं च गम्यते, तथापि पदसंस्कारकालापेक्षितमन्तरङ्गमव्यक्तपुंस्त्वम्, एकवचनं च उत्तरकालभावि । तेन बहिरङ्गं बहुवचनं चन बाधितुं शक्नोति । अयं च न्यायोऽन्यत्रापि यथासम्भवमनुसर्तव्य इति ॥
body.translated_text: Now, since the desiderative suffix <s>tavya</s> and the like have the gender of their referent, the form should be <s>śakyā</s> (feminine) — anticipating this objection, [the author says] <s>śakyam</s> (neuter) is appropriate. It is explained: here <s>śakyam</s> is used with the intention of a general sense. Then, when the specific referent is sought — 'what is possible?' — it will connect with <s>vikalpāḥ</s> (varieties). Although plurality and masculine gender are understood there, the neuter singular form, which is determined at the time of word-formation and is therefore more proximate, cannot be overridden by the remote plural number. This principle should be applied elsewhere too as appropriate.
And those should be inferred as follows —
This one appears to be somehow one of the divine women, seen here by some chance;
yet she does not belong to the heavenly realm — her eyes are familiar with blinking.
This one appears to be the first creation of <s>Vidhī</s> (the Creator), seen among mortal women;
whence would those others have such beauty? — She must be some divine woman.
O slender-limbed one! You are not pleased even when my very life-breaths are offered;
what greater gift is there than this? Why are you so cruel even so?
In this manner, other varieties of <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) too should be deduced.
|| Thus ends the <s>ākṣepacakra</s> (cycle of objections). ||

children.translated_text: He introduces <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration through another matter) —
That which is known as <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) is, having presented some subject matter,
the introduction of another thing that is capable of proving it. || 167 ||

children.text: विवक्षितं किञ्चिद्वस्तु अर्थरूपं प्रस्तुत्याभिधाय तस्य प्रस्तुतस्य वस्तुनः साधने समर्थस्य योग्यस्यान्यस्य वस्तुनः कस्यचित् न्यासः प्रयोगो यः, स एवंलक्षणोऽर्थान्तरन्यासो नामालङ्कारो ज्ञेयः प्रतिपत्तव्यः । प्रतिवस्तूपमा[या] अस्य च को भेदः उभयत्राप्यर्थान्तरोपन्यासात् ? महान् भेदः । तत्र हि सदृशस्यार्थान्तरस्योपन्यासः केवल
मपेक्षते, न साधनभूतस्य । अत्र तु साधनरूपस्यैवार्थान्तरस्य । सादृश्यं भवतु मा [वा] भूत्, न तदपेक्षते । अत एवोक्तं तत्साधनसमर्थस्येति ॥
children.translated_text: is required, not one that serves as proof. Here, however, the other matter must specifically serve as proof. Whether there is similarity or not, that is not required here. Therefore it was stated 'capable of proving it.' ||

Having presented, that is, having stated, some intended subject matter in the form of meaning, the introduction, that is, the employment, of some other thing that is capable, that is, fit, for proving that presented subject — that which is of such a nature is to be known, that is, understood, as the figure of speech called <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). What is the difference between this and <s>prativastūpamā</s> (analogy through counterpart), since in both cases another matter is introduced? The difference is great. In that figure, the introduction of another matter that is merely similar
He states what varieties this <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) of such definition has —
Universally applicable, particular, intertwined with <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), containing contradiction,
producing the unfitting, having fitness as its nature, fitting-and-unfitting, and the reverse. || 168 ||

children.text: विश्वं जगत्सर्वं व्याप्नोति सर्वत्र सम्भवादिति विश्वव्यापी । विशेषे क्वचित् विषये तिष्ठति न विश्वं व्याप्नोति विशेषस्थः । श्लेषः एकार्थता एकशब्दता वा तेनाविद्धोऽनुगतः श्लेषाविद्धः । विरोधः परस्परव्याघातो विद्यतेऽस्मिन्निति विरोधवान् । अयुक्तम् अनुचितं करोतीति अयुक्तकारी । अयुक्त इत्यर्थः । युक्तः समुचितः
आत्मा स्वरूपं यस्य स तथा । युक्त इति यावत् । युक्तश्चासौ कथञ्चिदयुक्तश्चेति युक्तायुक्तः । विपर्ययोऽयुक्तयुक्त इति ॥
children.translated_text: that is, fitting. <s>Yuktāyukta</s> (fitting-and-unfitting) — that which is somehow both fitting and unfitting. <s>Viparyaya</s> (the reverse) — unfitting-and-fitting. ||

<s>Viśvavyāpī</s> (universally applicable) — because it pervades the entire world, being possible everywhere. <s>Viśeṣastha</s> (particular) — it stands in a particular domain and does not pervade the entire world. <s>Śleṣāviddha</s> (intertwined with paronomasia) — pervaded by, that is, accompanied by, <s>śleṣa</s>, which is identity of meaning or identity of word. <s>Virodhavān</s> (containing contradiction) — that in which there is contradiction, mutual opposition. <s>Ayuktakāra</s> (producing the unfitting) — that which produces what is unfitting, inappropriate. The meaning is: unfitting. <s>Yuktātmā</s> — whose nature, whose essential character, is fitting;
These and other such varieties have been observed in poetic compositions;
a garland of examples of these is shown for the understanding of their nature. || 169 ||

children.text: इत्येवम् अनन्तरोक्तो विचित्रो भेद आदिर्येषां यथासम्भवमविरोधादीनां ते भेदाः विकल्पाः प्रयोगेषु काव्येषु लक्षिताः दृष्टाः कविभिः अस्य अर्थान्तरन्यासस्य सम्बन्धिनः । एषां भेदानां रूपस्य स्वभावस्य युक्त्यै प्रत्यवगमार्थम् । उदाहरणानां प्रयोगाणां माला वर्गो निदर्श्यते इति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, those of which the diverse variety just described is the beginning — the varieties of those such as non-contradiction and so forth, as applicable — these divisions have been observed, that is, seen by poets, in compositions, in poetic works, pertaining to this <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). For the understanding, that is, for the comprehension, of the nature, the essential character, of these varieties, a garland, a group, of examples, of instances, is shown. ||
The two lords, the eyes of the world — even the sun and the moon —

children.text: पश्य गच्छत एवास्तं नियतिः केन लङ्घ्यते ॥ १७० ॥
children.translated_text: behold, they go to their setting; who can transgress destiny? || 170 ||

children.text: भगवन्तौ गुणराशा । जगतो लोकस्य नेत्र चक्षुषी, प्रकाशकरत्वात् । सूर्याचन्द्रमसावपि, किमुतान्यद् वस्तुजातम् ? अस्तमुदयविपर्ययमभावं गच्छत एव । न पुनस्तत्रैव तिष्ठतः । पश्य । कथमेतत् ? किमत्र चित्रम् ! नियतिर्भावानामनपायिनी व्यवस्था काचित्, उदयः सर्व एव व्ययनिष्ठ इति । सा केन नाम वस्तुना लङ्घ्य विक्रमितुं शक्यते ? न केनचित् । सर्वमेवेह वस्तूदितमवश्यं व्येति । ततः सूर्याचन्द्रमसोरपि तथाभावो नाद्भुत इति प्रस्तुतं वस्तु साधितम् । अयं च विश्वव्यापी, तथाभावस्य सर्वत्रगत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: The two lords, treasures of virtues. The two eyes of the world, of people, because they illuminate. Even the sun and the moon — how much more so other things? They go to their setting, to decline and disappearance, inevitably. They do not remain there forever. Behold! How is this? What is surprising about it? <s>Niyati</s> (destiny) — some inviolable order of things: every rising thing is bound to perish. By what thing, by what entity, can that be transgressed, overcome? By nothing. Everything in this world that has arisen must certainly perish. Therefore, the fact that even the sun and moon are subject to this is not astonishing — thus the presented matter has been established. And this is <s>viśvavyāpī</s> (universally applicable), because such a state obtains everywhere. ||
The rain clouds indeed relieve the torment of living beings;
surely the birth of the great ones is for the alleviation of others' suffering. || 171 ||

children.text: एते पयोमुचो मेघाः शरीरिणां स्थावरजङ्गमानां परीतापं ज्वरं हरन्ति शमयन्ति । किमेतत् ? न हि तेषाममी किञ्चित्प्रत्युपकुर्वन्ति । किमेवमुच्यते ? ननु प्रसिद्धावनुमतौ वा । महताम् उत्ता[ना]नां न क्षुद्राणां तेषामात्मकल्याणेऽप्यकल्पत्वात्

आत्मलाभ उदयः परेषां सर्वेषामेव सम्भूतानामसम्भूतानां च दुःखस्य तापस्य उपशान्तये निवर्तनार्थं जायते । स्थितिरेषा महताम् । इदमेव च तेषां माहात्म्यम् । अन्यथा स्वार्थपरे जगति कस्तेषां विशेषो यदि तेऽपि तथैव स्युः ? ततः पयोमुचः
children.translated_text: their birth, their arising, is for the alleviation, the removal, of suffering, of torment, of all others — both those who have come into existence and those who have not. This is the way of the great ones. This alone is their greatness. Otherwise, in a world devoted to self-interest, what distinction would they have if they too were just the same? Therefore, the rain clouds

children.text: प्रत्युपकारनिरपेक्षाः जगत्तापं नुदन्तीति उपपादितम् । अयं च विशेषस्थो महतामेव तथात्वात् [न] विश्वव्यापीति ॥
children.translated_text: dispel the world's torment without expectation of return — this has been demonstrated. And this is <s>viśeṣastha</s> (particular), because only the great are thus, not universally applicable. ||

These rain clouds (<s>payomuca</s>) relieve, that is, pacify, the torment, the fever, of living beings — both stationary and moving. What is this about? For these beings do nothing in return for the clouds. Why is this said? Surely — in the sense of what is well-known or accepted. Of the great, the exalted ones — not of the petty, for they are incapable even of their own welfare —
The <s>Malaya</s> breeze produces delight in the world;
surely one endowed with <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (graciousness) is dear to all. || 172 ||

children.text: मलयमारुतो दक्षिणः पवनः लोकस्य जगतः प्रीतिमुत्पादयति । किं पुनः कारणं येनायं सर्वेषां प्रिय इति साधयन्नाह- नन्वित्यादि । नन्वित्यनुमतौ । दाक्षिंण्यं परच्छन्दानुवर्तित्वम् । सर्वप्रीतिजननानुगुणो गुणः पौरुषेयः, दक्षिणदेशभवत्वं चेति शब्दश्लेषः । तेन सम्पन्नः सुभगः सर्वस्य जनस्य प्रियो भवति । न कस्यचिदप्रियः । कथमनुकूलवर्ती कस्यचिदप्रियोऽप्रीतिकरः स्यात् । तस्मान्मलयजमारुतो दक्षिणः सर्वेषां प्रीतिंमुत्पादयतीति समर्थितम् । अयं च श्लेषाविद्धो दाक्षिण्यसंपन्न इत्यस्य श्लिष्टत्वादुक्तेन विधिनेति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>Malaya</s> breeze, the southern wind, produces delight in the world, in people. What then is the reason that this wind is dear to all? Establishing this, he says 'surely' and so forth. 'Surely' in the sense of acceptance. <s>Dākṣiṇya</s> (graciousness) means conformity to others' wishes. There is a <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) on the word: a personal quality conducive to producing delight in all, and also originating from the southern (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>) region. One endowed with, that is, blessed with, that quality is dear to everyone, to all people. Not displeasing to anyone. How could one who acts in accord with others' wishes be displeasing or cause displeasure to anyone? Therefore, it has been demonstrated that the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, being southern, produces delight in all. And this is <s>śleṣāviddha</s> (intertwined with paronomasia), because the expression 'endowed with <s>dākṣiṇya</s>' is ambiguous, as stated by the prescribed method. ||
This moon delights the world even though it is blemished;
indeed, even one who has faults bestows grace upon others, if he is a lord among the twice-born. || 173 ||

children.text: एष निशाकरश्चन्द्रो मलिनोऽपि कलङ्कयोगात् अशुद्धोऽपि जगत् लोकमाह्लादयति प्रीणयति । विरुद्धमेतत्, कथं सकलङ्कः प्रीतिकरोऽदोषस्य तथाभावात् । तत्साधयतिभवत्येवम् । हिः यस्मादर्थे । यतः सदोषोऽपि कथञ्चित् कलङ्कवानपि न केवलमदोषः । द्विजेश्वरश्चन्द्रो विप्रश्चेति श्लेषः । स त्विह तु न विवक्षितः, विरोधस्यैवाभिधित्सितत्वात् । अनुगृह्णाति उपकरोति ह्लादयति परान् धर्मोपदेशादिना । तस्मान्मलिनोऽपि निशाकरो जगदाह्लादयतीत्युपपद्यते । अयं च विरोधवान् । उक्तेन विधिना विरोधदर्शनादिति ॥
children.translated_text: This moon (<s>niśākara</s>), even though blemished — due to the mark upon it — even though impure, delights, gladdens the world. This is contradictory — how can something blemished cause delight, when only the faultless should do so? He establishes this — it is indeed so. 'Indeed' (<s>hi</s>) means 'because.' Because even one who has faults, who has some blemish — not merely one without faults — there is a <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia): <s>dvija-īśvara</s> means both the moon and the lord of the twice-born (a Brahmin). But here that meaning is not intended, since only the contradiction is meant to be expressed. He bestows grace upon, benefits, delights others through teaching of <s>dharma</s> and the like. Therefore, that even though blemished the moon delights the world is established. And this is <s>virodhavān</s> (containing contradiction), because contradiction is perceived by the stated method. ||
The buzzing of bees, though emanating from throats sweetened by drinking nectar,
becomes harsh to the ears of lovers — such is the evil of passion. || 174 ||

children.text: मधुनः कुसुमासवस्य पानेन कलान्मधुरात् कण्ठान्निर्गतोऽलिनां मधुलिहां मधुरोऽपि ध्वनिः कामिनां विरहिणा
मपि कर्णस्य कटुरुद्वेजनीयोऽत्यन्तोत्कण्ठाकरत्वाद् भवति । एतच्चायुक्तम् । कथमीदृशः प्रीतिकरो ध्वनिः उद्वेजयति तत्साध्यते-
children.translated_text: because it causes extreme longing. And this is unfitting. How can such a delightful sound cause distress? This is established —

children.text: किं न युक्तम्, यतः पापमीदृशं कामिनां रागिणाम् एवंरूपं कर्म यतोऽयमेवंविधो मधुरो ध्वनिः अन्यथा प्रतिभाति । किमत्र क्रियताम् ! तस्मात्सम्भवत्येतदिति साधितम् । अयमयुक्तकारी मधुरस्य ध्वनेः उद्वेगहेतुत्वायोगादिति ॥
children.translated_text: What is unfitting about it? Because such is the evil, such is the nature of the action, of lovers, of those consumed by passion — that this kind of sweet sound appears otherwise. What can be done about it? Therefore, this is possible — thus it is established. This is <s>ayuktakārī</s> (producing the unfitting), because of the unfittingness of a sweet buzzing causing distress, as stated by the method. ||

From the sweet throat, sweetened by the drinking of nectar, that is, the essence of flowers — the buzzing of bees (<s>alin</s>), though itself sweet, becomes harsh, that is, distressing, to the ears of lovers, of those in separation,
This bed of lotus petals burns my body;
is it not fitting that a substitute for fire should be of a burning nature? || 175 ||

children.text: अम्भोजानां कमलानां दलानि पत्राणि तेषां तन्मयो वा संस्तरः तल्पम् । अयम् अनुभूयमानः मम अङ्गं देहं दहति तापयति । युक्तं चैतत् । कथम् ? हुताशनस्य अग्नेः प्रतिनिधिः सदृशः पाटलत्वात् दाहात्मा दाहस्वभावो रक्तपद्मपत्रसंस्तरो युज्यते नन्विति साधितम् । अयं च युक्तात्मा कथितेन विधिना दाहकत्वयोगादिति ॥
children.translated_text: A bed made of the petals, the leaves, of lotuses — this, as experienced, burns, that is, scorches, my body. And this is fitting. How? A substitute, a likeness, of fire — because of its redness — having a burning nature, the bed of red lotus petals, is fittingly so — 'surely' (<s>nanu</s>) establishes it. And this is <s>yuktātmā</s> (having fitness as its nature), because the burning quality is fitting, as described by the stated method. ||

children.text: क्षिणोतु कामं शीतांशुः किं वसन्तो दुनोति माम् ।
children.translated_text: Let the cool-rayed moon torment me as it pleases; but why does spring afflict me?
Surely the tainted deed of the moon is unbecoming of the fragrant one (spring). || 176 ||

children.text: कामं नामाभ्युपगमे शीतांशुश्चन्द्रः मां क्षिणोतु तापयतु युक्तमेतत् । वसन्तः किं कस्मात् मां दुनोति तापयति ? नैतद् युक्तम् । इदं त्वयुक्तमिति साधयन्नाहमलिनेत्यादि । मलिनेन कलङ्किना शीतांशुना आचरितम् अनुष्ठितं कर्म क्रिया तापलक्षणम् असाम्प्रतम् अयुक्तम् । ननु कस्य ? सुरभेर्वसन्तस्य सुरभेश्चाभिलषितस्येति श्लेषः । कथं दुष्टानुष्ठितं कर्म निर्दोषो जुषति । तस्मात् क्षिणोतु शीतांशुः । वसन्तः किं दुनोतीति पूर्वं समर्थितम् । अयं युक्तायुक्तः, शीतांशुना तापस्य योगात् वसन्तेनायोगादुक्तेन विधिनेति ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmam</s> means 'granted' — let the cool-rayed moon torment me; this is fitting. But why does spring afflict me, torment me? This is not fitting. Establishing that this is unfitting, he says 'tainted' and so forth. The deed, the action of tormenting, performed by the tainted one, the moon with its blemish, is unbecoming, unfitting, of the fragrant one (<s>surabhi</s>) — that is, of spring, and also of the desired one — there is a <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). How would a faultless one engage in a deed performed by a flawed one? Therefore, let the cool-rayed moon torment — but why does spring? This was established earlier. This is <s>yuktāyukta</s> (fitting-and-unfitting), because torment by the cool-rayed moon is fitting but by spring is unfitting, as stated by the method. ||
Even the <s>kumudas</s> (night lotuses) serve to torment — how much more the lotus pond!
For when those belonging to the moon are fierce, one belonging to the sun would not be gentle. || 177 ||
