The praise of the excellence of valor is itself blame for the maiden,
as it serves to avert her feelings, she who desires uninterrupted pleasures. || 268 ||

children.text: वीर्यस्य विक्रमस्योत्कर्षोऽधिमात्राता तस्य स्तुतिः वर्णनं निन्दैव दोषोक्तिरेव जायते । कथम् ? यतः कन्याया निरन्तरानविच्छेदवर्तिनो भोगान्

सुरतसुखानि विविक्षोरनुबुभूषोः सम्बन्धिनो भावस्य स्वीकाराभिप्रायस्यास्मिन् यथोपवर्णिते पुंसि तन्मनोरथप्रतिकूलवर्तिनि विषये वैमुख्याय कल्पते । ततो निन्दैवेयं जाता स्तुतिः, अन्यथा भावनिवृत्ययोगात् । नहि गुणवत्तया प्रतीतः परित्यज्यते किं तु दोषवानेव । तथा असौ अलीकरणरागव्यसनी सुरतसमरमहोत्सवपराङ्मुखः प्रतीतो यतस्तं विभावयतीति निन्दैवेयं लेशतः कृतेति ॥
children.translated_text: the delights of lovemaking — who wishes to experience them; when the man is described in such a manner, acting contrary to her heart's desires, in such a subject — it serves to create aversion toward the acceptance, the intent to receive, of the related feeling. Thus this praise has become blame itself, otherwise there would be no occasion for averting the feeling. For one perceived as virtuous is not rejected, but only one perceived as faulty. And since he is perceived as one addicted to the vice of making love false, averse to the great festival of the battle of love — because [the verse] makes that apparent — this is indeed blame performed through a trace. ||

The excellence, the supreme degree, of valor, of martial prowess — the praise, the description, of that becomes itself blame, a statement of fault. How so? Because for the maiden who desires uninterrupted, unceasing pleasures —
Simple-hearted
is this lord of men, immovable like Mount <s>Sumeru</s>,
who never feels distress even at the sufferings of his dependents. ||
This is another illustration. ||

children.text: चपलो निर्दयश्चासौ जनः किं तेन मे सखि ।
children.translated_text: That person is fickle and merciless — what use is he to me, O friend,
he who has learned flattering ways solely for the purpose of effacing his offenses! || 269 ||

children.text: चपलो दुर्विनीतः यत्किञ्चनकारी निर्दयः क्ररश्च । किं तेनैवं दुःखदायिना जनेन निर्गुणेन ? पुनस्तादृश एवासौ येनागसामपराधानां प्रतिक्षणभाविनामात्मीयानां प्रमार्जनाय परिशोधनार्थमेव केवलम्, नानुग्रहाय कस्मैचित्तादृशाय चाटवोऽनेकविधा लोलनप्रकाराः शिक्षिताः स्वभ्यस्ताः । किं तेन चाटुचुञ्चुटनेति निगमनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Fickle, ill-mannered, acting at whim; merciless, cruel. What use is such a person who brings only suffering, devoid of merit? Moreover, he is indeed of such a nature that solely for the purpose of effacing, of cleansing, his constantly recurring offenses, his faults — not for bestowing any kindness on anyone — various kinds of flattering ways, modes of cajoling, have been learned, have been practiced by him. 'What use is such a master of flattery?' — this should be understood as the conclusion. ||

children.text: ननु दोष एवात्र सर्वथोक्तो न गुणः क्वचित् यतो लेशतः स्तुतिः स्यात् इत्यत आह—
children.translated_text: But here only faults have been stated in every way, and no merit whatsoever by which there could be praise through a trace — to this he responds —
An apparent fault is actually some merit: his skill in flattery has been shown,
by one who, out of passion, is unable to maintain the sulking prescribed by her circle of friends. || 270 ||

children.text: सखि ! त्वया किमतिदाक्षिण्येन अस्य दास्या भूयते ? अणुभिरपिन कदाचिदञ्च्यसे । मानिन्यो हि वयम् । किमपरमस्माकमस्त्रमिति सखीजनेनोद्दिष्टम् उपदिष्टम् मानमुन्नतिं चित्तस्य कर्तुमनुष्ठातुमशक्ततया कयाचिदङ्गनया । कुतः ? रागात् तद्विंषयाभिषङ्गान्मानविरोधिनो हेतोश्चाटुकारिता उपचारचातुर्यं नाम गुणो विशेषः कोऽपि कश्चिदुपात्तो नागरकजनोचितः कोऽपि वा कश्चिदेकः सर्वदोषवदाभासते । अपराधप्रमार्जनपरत्वेनैव प्रकाशनात् दोषाभासो दर्शितः । ततो लेशतः स्तुति[रि]यं कल्पत इति ।
children.translated_text: O friend! Why do you serve as his slave with such excessive courtesy? You are never honored even with trifles. For we are proud women. What other weapon do we have? — thus instructed, thus advised by her circle of friends to assume <s>māna</s> (pride), the haughtiness of mind, a certain woman is unable to carry it out. Why? Because of passion, attachment toward him — the cause that opposes <s>māna</s> — the flattery, the skill in courteous behavior, a certain quality, something particular, has been adopted, befitting a refined urbanite, or rather some single thing appears to have the character of all faults. Because it manifests solely as being devoted to the wiping away of offenses, the appearance of fault has been shown. Therefore, this constitutes praise in trace (<s>leśa</s>).
This king is cruel, a gambler, indifferent to statecraft;
his generosity manifests solely for the purpose of cleansing his faults.
This is another example.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>leśa</s> (trace). ||
He undertakes to explain <s>krama</s> (sequence) —
The successive corresponding assignment of items previously enumerated
is called <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (according to number); it is also termed <s>saṃkhyāta</s> (enumerated) or <s>krama</s> (sequence). || 271 ||

children.text: उद्दिष्टानां पूर्वप्रयुक्तानामर्थानां वस्तूनां केषाञ्चिंद् यथाक्रममुद्देशक्रमानतिक्रमेण अनुदेशः प्रत्याम्नायः पुनरर्थान्तराश्रयेण परामर्शः

यथासंख्यमिति यथासंख्यं प्रोक्तम् । यथासंख्यमित्यपेक्ष्य नपुंस[क]त्वम् तस्य विधेयत्वात् । अनुदेशस्यानूद्यतया अप्रधानत्वान्न तल्लिङ्गपरिग्रहः । प्रोक्तम् इति संख्यातमित्यपि प्रोक्तम् । क्रम इत्यपि प्रोक्त इति लिङ्गपरिणामेन योज्यम् । क्रम इत्यपि उपदिश्यत इति वा अध्याहार्यम् इति ॥
children.translated_text: is called <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (according to number). The neuter gender of '<s>yathāsaṃkhyam</s>' is because it is the predicate. Since the <s>anudeśa</s> (corresponding assignment) is subordinate, being the topic restated, its gender is not adopted. 'It is called' — it is also called '<s>saṃkhyāta</s>' (enumerated). 'Also termed <s>krama</s>' — this should be construed with a change of gender to '<s>proktaḥ</s>.' Or it should be supplied: 'is also taught [as <s>krama</s>].'

Of certain things, objects, that have been enumerated, previously employed — in the order of enumeration, without transgressing the sequence of the original listing — the corresponding assignment (<s>anudeśa</s>), the substitution, the reconsideration by way of reference to another meaning,
Illustrating that, he says —
Surely, O slender one, the radiance of your smile, your glance, and your face has been stolen,
when you entered the water to bathe, by the night-lotuses, the blue lotuses, and the day-lotuses. || 272 ||

children.text: तन्वि ! ते स्नातुमम्भ [प्रविष्टायाः] सरःप्रविष्टायाः स्मितं चेक्षणं च मुखं च तेषां द्युतिरित्युद्देशः कुमुदान्युत्पलानि पङ्कजानि च तैश्चोरिता मुषिता कुमुदैः स्मितद्युति-

children.translated_text: by the <s>utpalas</s> the radiance of the glance, by the <s>paṅkajas</s> the radiance of the face — 'stolen' — this is the corresponding assignment following the order of enumeration. Since in reality this is not so, 'surely' (<s>dhruvam</s>) indicates that it is imagined through <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).

O slender one! When you [entered] the water, entered the lake, to bathe — the smile, the glance, and the face, and their radiance — this is the enumeration. The night-lotuses (<s>kumuda</s>), the blue lotuses (<s>utpala</s>), and the day-lotuses (<s>paṅkaja</s>) — by these, stolen, robbed: by the <s>kumudas</s> the radiance of the smile,

children.text: यद्येवमुत्प्रेक्षेयं कथं यथासंख्यमिति चेत् ? यद्येवं निरूप्यते, उपमाप्यत्र विद्यते, स्मितादीनां कुमुदादिभिः सादृश्यप्रतीतेः । तस्माद्यत्रालङ्कारान्तरमपि प्रतीयते, तत्रापि उद्देशानुरूपानुदेशसंख्यातमेवालङ्कारो व्यवह्रियते । तायैव मुख्यता, विवक्षितत्वात् । यत्र तु अलङ्कारान्तरं न गम्यते तत्र सुतरामेव क्रम इति विज्ञेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: If it is objected: if this is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), how is it <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>? If examined thus, <s>upamā</s> (simile) also exists here, since similarity is perceived between smile and the like and <s>kumuda</s> and the like. Therefore, even where another ornament is also perceived, the ornament designated by the enumeration-following-correspondence (<s>uddeśānurūpānudeśa-saṃkhyāta</s>) is what is recognized. That alone has primacy, because it is the intended meaning. But where no other ornament is apprehended, there it is all the more <s>krama</s> (sequence) — this should be understood.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>krama</s> (sequence). ||
Defining the triad of ornaments <s>preyas</s>, <s>rasavat</s>, and <s>ūrjasvin</s>, he says —
<s>Preyas</s> (the endearing) is the expression of what is exceedingly dear; <s>rasavat</s> (the flavorful) is that which is graceful with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment);

children.text: ऊर्जस्वि रूढ़ाहङ्कारं युक्तोत्कर्ष च तत् त्रयम् ॥ २७३ ॥
children.translated_text: <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous) has firmly established pride — and that triad possesses fitting excellence. || 273 ||

children.text: प्रियतरस्यातिशयेन प्रियस्यार्थरूपस्य कस्यचिदाख्यानं प्रतिपादनम् आख्यायते अनेनेत्यनूद्य प्रेय इति ज्ञाप्यते । रसेन शृङ्गारादिना प्रतिपाद्येन पेशलं मनोज्ञं रसवद् वाक्यं विज्ञेयम् । रूढ़ो दीप्तोऽहङ्कारः सौटीर्यं यत्र तादृशं वचनमूर्जस्वि ज्ञेयम् । तच्चैतत्त्रयं प्रेयो रसवत् ऊर्जस्वि च युक्तः सङ्गतः उत्कर्षोऽधिमात्रता येनेति युक्तोत्कर्षमत्यन्तप्रियमेकान्तरसवत् भृशमूर्जस्वीत्यर्थः । अयं चार्थः- अयमु[प]मादिभिरतिशयविधिभिरुक्तो युक्तोत्कर्ष इति ॥
children.translated_text: The expression, the presentation, of what is exceedingly dear (<s>priyatara</s>), some object of an extremely beloved nature — that by which it is expressed, having been thus referred to, is made known as <s>preyas</s>. A sentence that is graceful, beautiful, through <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and the like, which is to be conveyed, should be understood as <s>rasavat</s>. An utterance in which there is firmly established (<s>rūḍha</s>), blazing pride (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), a boldness of spirit, should be known as <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous). And this triad — <s>preyas</s>, <s>rasavat</s>, and <s>ūrjasvin</s> — possesses fitting, appropriate excellence — meaning it is exceedingly dear, entirely imbued with <s>rasa</s>, and intensely vigorous. And this is the meaning: the fitting excellence that has been stated through <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other methods of intensification.
First illustrating <s>preyas</s> (the endearing), he says —

children.text: अद्य या मम गोविन्द ! जाता त्वयि गृहागते ।
children.translated_text: O <s>Govinda</s>! The joy that has arisen in me today, upon your coming home —
such a joy could arise again in time only from your arrival once more. || 274 ||

children.text: गोविन्द विष्णो ! त्वयि गृहमिदमस्मदीयमतिधन्यमागते सति या प्रीतिः तुष्टिः अद्य अस्मिन् पुण्याहे मम जाता एषा इयं प्रीतिः कालेन पुनरीदृशेन शुभेन समयेन केनचित् तवैव नान्यस्य । कस्त्वादृशः ? आगमनादुपसंक्रमण
महोत्सवात्कारणात् भवेत् जायते । त्वदागमनमे[कारण]मस्याः, ज्योत्स्नाया इव चन्द्र इति ॥
children.translated_text: of you alone, not of anyone else. For who is like you? From the great festival of your arrival alone is it caused to arise. Your arrival is the sole cause of this joy, just as the moon is of moonlight.

O <s>Govinda</s>, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! When you have come to this most blessed home of ours — the joy, the satisfaction, that has arisen in me today, on this auspicious day — this very joy could arise again at some such blessed time, from the arrival, the festive approach,
He explains that —
Thus <s>Vidura</s> says what is fitting — for such contentment comes from no other source;
and <s>Hari</s>, who can be worshipped through devotion alone, was thereby greatly pleased. || 275 ||

children.text: इत्येतदनन्तरोक्तं युक्तं प्राप्तकालमाह ब्रवीति विदुरो नरोत्तमः कश्चिदेवमभिधानः । यतो नैव गोविन्दागमनादृतेऽन्यतः कुतश्चिदपि तादृशी गोविन्दागमनभाविनी धृतिः प्रीतिर्जायते । यतो युक्तमाहेत्यपीक्षणीयं ततः ईदृशात् प्राप्तकालात् । सुप्रीतोः अत्यन्तप्रसन्नो हरिर्विष्णुरभूत् । किमेतावता सुप्रीतः स्यात् ? नकिञ्चिद् गृहागताय तस्मै तथाविधायातिथये तादृशं वस्तूपहृतं यतः सुप्रीतः स्यादित्याह- भक्तिरीदृशी वचनादिरूपा यथाभाविनी सेवा सैव तन्मात्रम् बहिर्वस्तूपहाराद्यनपेक्षणात् । तेन समाराध्यः प्रतिपूजनीयो यतस्तस्मात् तत एव भक्तेः सुप्रीत इति निगमनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, this statement just made is fitting, timely — says <s>Vidura</s>, a certain excellent man of that name. Since from no source other than the arrival of <s>Govinda</s> does such contentment, such joy resembling that born of <s>Govinda</s>'s arrival, arise. Since he says what is fitting, the consequence should also be noted: from this very timeliness, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, was greatly pleased, exceedingly gratified. Would he be so greatly pleased by just this much? Nothing material was offered to him as such a distinguished guest, on account of which he might be pleased. Thus he says: such devotion as this, in the form of words and the like, the natural service — that alone, its mere essence, without regard for external material offerings and the like — by that he can be worshipped, can be honored. Because of that, from devotion alone, he was greatly pleased — this should be concluded.

children.text: सोमः सूर्यो मरुद् भूमिर्व्योम होतानलो जलम् ।
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Marut</s>, <s>Bhūmi</s>, <s>Vyoman</s>, the sacrificer, <s>Anala</s>, and water —

children.text: इति मूर्त्तीरतिक्रम्य त्वां द्रष्टुं देव ! के वयम् ॥ २७६ ॥
children.translated_text: having transcended these forms, who are we, O Lord, to behold you? || 276 ||

children.text: होता यजमानः । इत्येवंभूतानि रूपाणि व्यक्तानि अष्टौ मूर्त्तीस्तवातिक्रम्य मु[क्त्वा] देव ! त्वामत्यन्ताव्यक्तपरमतत्त्वं योगिभिरपि महद्भिरगम्यं द्रष्टुं साक्षात्कर्तु के वयमितरे प्राणिनः ? नैवास्मादृशोऽगोचरो देवः । सोमादीनि व्यक्तानि रूपाणि देवस्य यदि वयं पश्येम इति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Hotā</s>' means the sacrificer. Having transcended, having passed beyond, these eight manifest forms of yours — O Lord! To behold you, the utterly unmanifest supreme reality (<s>paramatattva</s>), inaccessible even to great yogins — who are we, ordinary beings? The Lord is certainly beyond the reach of such as ourselves. If only we could see the manifest forms of the Lord such as <s>Soma</s> and the rest.
Categorizing that, he says —
Thus, when the Lord was beheld directly, this expression of joy by King <s>Rātavarman</s>
should be understood as <s>preyas</s> (the endearing). || 277 ||

children.text: इतीदृशं यत् प्रीतिप्रकाशनं तत् प्रेयोवचनम् प्रकाश्यतेऽनेनेति कृत्वा रातवर्मणः तन्नाम्नो रघुवंशजन्मनो राज्ञः सम्बन्धि तत्प्रयुक्तत्वात् । देवे शंकरे परमभक्तिसमाराधिते प्रसन्ने किल दत्तदर्शने साक्षात्कृते दृष्टे सति । तेनेत्यर्थाद् गम्यते । तच्च तादृशं वचनमीश्वरविषयं रातवर्मप्रयुक्तं प्रेय इत्येवमनुगम्यतां ज्ञातव्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, this expression of joy is a <s>preyas</s> utterance — it is so determined because it is expressed by this. It belongs to a king named <s>Rātavarman</s>, born of the <s>Raghu</s> lineage, since it was spoken by him. When the Lord, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, propitiated through supreme devotion, being pleased, having granted a vision, was beheld directly. By him — this is understood from the context. And such an utterance — concerning the Lord, spoken by <s>Rātavarman</s> — should be understood, should be known, as <s>preyas</s> (the endearing).
|| Thus ends the section on <s>preyas</s> (the endearing). ||
Illustrating <s>rasavat</s> (the flavorful), he says —

children.text: मृतेति प्रेत्य संगन्तुं यया मे मरणं मतम् ।
children.translated_text: 'She is dead' — to meet her in the hereafter, death was resolved upon by me;
yet that very <s>Āvantī</s> has been found by me — how? — in this very lifetime. || 278 ||

children.text: इयं किल प्रेयसी मृता स्वर्गमगमदिति हेतोः प्रेतलोकान्तरे क्वचित्

children.translated_text: with her,

children.text: संगन्तुं योगार्थं मरणं देहविसर्जनं मतमिष्टं मम । मृत्वाप्यवश्यं तया संगंस्ये इति । सैव या परासुः किलासीत् नान्या अवन्ती अवन्तिराजतनया मया [अयातजीवि]तेन तथाव्यवसितेनात्रैव जन्मनि न प्रेत्य कथं लब्धा, किमिद
children.translated_text: to meet, to unite — death, the abandoning of the body, was desired, resolved upon, by me. 'Having died, I shall surely unite with her' — thus. That very one who had supposedly died, not another — <s>Āvantī</s>, the daughter of the king of <s>Avantī</s> — has been found by me, [one who had not yet departed life], who had so resolved, in this very lifetime, not in the hereafter. How is this

children.text: मद्भुतम् । नास्ति भाग्यानां दुष्करम् । उदयनः किल वत्सराजः अवन्तिराजसुतायां वासवदत्तायामासक्तः राज्यचिन्ताविमुखोऽवर्तत इति मन्त्रिभिः सा क्वचिन्निगूह्य मृतेति ख्यापिता । स च तद्विरहमसहमानोऽतिरक्ततयाऽनुमरणं तत्सङ्गमवर्त्म व्यवससौ । ततस्तैः पुनर्जह्रे इति कथोदाहृता ॥
children.translated_text: possible? What a wonder! Nothing is impossible for good fortune. The story cited is as follows: King <s>Udayana</s>, the ruler of <s>Vatsa</s>, being attached to <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, the daughter of the king of <s>Avantī</s>, was neglecting affairs of state. Therefore, the ministers concealed her somewhere and proclaimed her dead. He, unable to bear the separation from her, out of excessive passion resolved upon following her in death, as the path to union with her. Then by them she was restored — thus the story is cited as an example.
This beloved, having died, went to heaven — for this reason, in some other world beyond death,

children.text: ननु प्रीतिरियं पूर्वोदाहृता । तत्किमनयेति विशेषं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Now, this is the joy previously illustrated. What is different about this? Showing the distinction, he says —

children.text: प्राक् प्रीतिर्दर्शिता सेयं रतिः शृङ्गारतां गता ।
children.translated_text: Previously joy was shown; this very same emotion, having become love, has attained the nature of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment),
through the connection with an abundance of its own nature — hence this is a <s>rasavat</s> (flavorful) utterance. || 279 ||

children.text: प्राक् प्रेयस्यलङ्कारे प्रीतिस्तुष्टिः पुरुषविषया दर्शिता । या

children.translated_text: this which has now been

children.text: उदाहृता सा त्वियंरतिः स्त्रीविषयानुरक्तिः भावविशेषः शृङ्गाररसयोनिस्तादृशविभावजन्यस्तथाविधानुभावगम्यः । यदाह—शृङ्गारतां शृङ्गाराख्यरसविशेषत्वं गता तद्रूपेण परिणता । कुतः ? रूपस्य स्वभावास्यात्मीयस्य संकल्पविशेषलक्षणस्य बाहुल्येनोदीर्णतया अत्युपचयेन सह योगेन सम्बन्धेन हेतुना । एतदुक्तं भवति- रतिरियमव्यक्ता अनुपचिता अन्तस्तत्त्वेन वर्तमाना संकल्पविशेषस्वभावा भाव उच्यते । अत एव विकारो मानसो भाव इत्यमिधीयते । सैव यदा समुदीर्णा अनुभावात् कुतश्चिन्नाटिकाभिनयादिलक्षणात् व्यक्तिमायाति तदा शृङ्गारो नाम रसः सम्पद्यत इत्यत एवोच्यते- अभिव्यक्ता भावा एव रसाख्यां प्रतिलभन्ते । विस्तरस्तु तच्छास्त्रात् । वक्ष्यमाणेषु रौद्रादिषु रसेषु क्रोधादिभावपरिणामविशेषरूपेष्वप्ययं न्यायोऽनुगन्तव्य इत्यलं विस्तरेण । तत्तस्मादिदमीदृशं वचः काव्यं रसवद्विज्ञेयम्, शृङ्गार[र]सयोगात् । यद्वेदृशं तद्रसवद्वचनमिति योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: illustrated — this is <s>rati</s> (erotic love), the specific attachment toward a woman, a particular <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state), the source of <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment), born of such <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and apprehended through such <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents). As stated: it has attained <s>śṛṅgāratā</s>, the nature of the particular aesthetic sentiment called <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, has been transformed into that form. Why? Through the connection with, the reason being, the abundance, the heightened intensity, of its own nature, its inherent character in the form of a particular mental resolution. This is what is meant: this <s>rati</s> (love), when unexpressed, unintensified, existing inwardly in its essential nature, characterized by a particular mental resolution, is called a <s>bhāva</s> (emotion). Hence it is said: a mental modification is called a <s>bhāva</s>. When that very same emotion, having been intensified, attains manifestation through some <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) — such as dramatic representation in a play — then it becomes the aesthetic sentiment called <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. Hence it is said: <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) that have been made manifest obtain the designation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). The details should be learned from that treatise [the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>]. In the <s>raudra</s> (furious) and other <s>rasas</s> to be described, which are forms of particular transformations of <s>bhāvas</s> such as anger and the like, this same principle should be followed — enough with the elaboration. Therefore, such an utterance, such poetry, should be known as <s>rasavat</s> (flavorful), because of its connection with <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s>. Or: that which is of such a kind is a <s>rasavat</s> utterance — this should be construed.
Previously, in the ornament of <s>preyas</s>, joy, satisfaction, directed toward a person, was shown. But
Having seized her by the hair, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (Draupadī) was dragged before me by him —

children.text: सोऽयं दुःशासनः पापो लब्धः किं जीवति क्षणम् ॥ २८० ॥
children.translated_text: this <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, this sinner, has been caught — does he live even for a moment? || 280 ||

children.text: येन दुरात्मना ममाग्रतः पुरस्तात् केशेषु निगृह्य अवष्टभ्य कृष्णा द्रौपदी प्रिया आकृष्टा आक्षिप्ता परिभूता, सोऽयमेप पापो दुरात्मा दुःशासनो मया भीमेन लब्धः प्राप्तः किं क्षणमेकं जीवति ? नैव जीवितुं लभते । एष मया हतो वर्तते कौरवाणां पश्यताम् । त्रिभुवनमपि संहतमेतत्परित्राणे न समर्थमिति भीमो गर्जति ॥
children.translated_text: By that vile person, before me, in my presence, having seized her by the hair, having grasped them, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Draupadī</s>, the beloved, was dragged, was thrown about, was humiliated — that very sinner, vile-souled <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, has been caught, obtained, by me, <s>Bhīma</s>. Does he live even for a single moment? He shall not be permitted to live. He has been slain by me, while the <s>Kauravas</s> watch. Even the three worlds united are not capable of saving him — thus <s>Bhīma</s> roars.
Showing what <s>rasa</s> this is, he says —

children.text: इत्यारुह्य परां कोटिं क्रोधो रौद्रात्प्रतां गतः ।
children.translated_text: Thus, the anger, having reached its supreme peak, has attained the nature of <s>raudra</s> (the furious sentiment);
of <s>Bhīma</s> beholding his enemy — this is a <s>rasavat</s> (flavorful) utterance. || 281 ||

children.text: इति उक्तेन प्रकारेण परां कोटिं प्रकर्षनिष्टामारुह्य प्राप्य अनुभावेनाभिव्यक्तिमागम्य क्रोधो भावविशेषो रौद्रात्मतां रौद्ररसविशेषम्वभावतां गतः । कस्यासौ क्रोधो य एवमवदत् ? भीमस्य शत्रुं दुःशासनं पश्यतः । अनेन तादृशवस्तुस्वभावो विभावो भावयोनिः सूचित इत्येवंविधं वचः काव्यं रसवद्रौद्ररसयोगादिति ।
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner described, having reached the supreme peak, the ultimate degree — having attained manifestation through <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — the anger, a particular <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), whose essence is intensified, having reached the highest point and being fully manifested, has attained the nature of <s>raudra</s> (the furious), has assumed the essential nature of the particular <s>raudra rasa</s> (furious sentiment). Whose is that anger? Of <s>Bhīma</s>, beholding the enemy <s>Duḥśāsana</s>. By this, the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) — the essential nature of such an object, the source of the emotion — has been indicated. Thus such an utterance, such poetry, is <s>rasavat</s> (flavorful) because of its connection with <s>raudra rasa</s> (the furious sentiment).
Without having conquered the earth girt by oceans, without having sacrificed with various <s>yajñas</s>,
and without having given wealth to supplicants — how could I be a king? || 282 ||

children.text: उर्वीं महीं सार्णवां सहार्णवैर्वर्तत इति चतुःसमुद्रपर्यन्तामजित्वा अनिर्जित्य अनात्मसात्कृत्वा तज्जयलब्धया च धनसम्पदा विविधैविचित्रैः शास्त्रोक्तैरश्वमेधविश्वजिद्वाजपेयराजसूयादिभिर्मखैर्यागविशेषैः करणभूतैः यागसामान्ये तद्विशेषस्य साधकतमत्वात् । अनिष्ट्वा यजनमकृत्वा अर्थिभ्यश्च वनीयकेभ्योऽर्थ यथार्थं यथाकाममदत्त्वा अप्रतिपाद्य अहं राजधर्मशून्यः कथं पार्थिवः पृथिवीपतिः भवेयम् ? नैव, पृथिवीजयादिलक्षणत्वात् पार्थिवताया इति ॥
children.translated_text: Without having conquered, without having subdued, without having made one's own, the earth (<s>urvī</s>) together with its oceans, extending to the four seas; and with the wealth obtained from that conquest, without having performed worship with various, diverse <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices) prescribed by scripture — <s>aśvamedha</s>, <s>viśvajit</s>, <s>vājapeya</s>, <s>rājasūya</s>, and the like — particular types of sacrifice as instrumental means, since specific sacrifices are the most effective within the general category of sacrifice; without having sacrificed, without having performed worship; and without having given wealth as desired to supplicants, those who seek — without providing it — how could I, devoid of kingly duties, be a king, a lord of the earth? Not at all, since kingship consists precisely of conquering the earth and the like.
Explaining what <s>rasa</s> this is, he says —
Thus, the enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>), with its intensified essence, standing in the form of <s>vīra rasa</s> (the heroic sentiment),
is capable of establishing the <s>rasavat</s> (flavorful) quality of those words. || 283 ||

children.text: इत्युक्तेन विधिना उत्साहो भावविशेषः प्रकृष्ट आत्मा अस्येति प्रकृष्टात्मा परां कोटिमारूढ़ोऽभिव्यक्तत्वात् । वीरश्चासो रसश्च तस्य स एवात्मा स्वभावः तेन लक्षितः तिष्ठन् वर्तमानो वीररसतामापन्नः । तासामनन्तरोक्तानां गिरां काव्यरूपाणां रसवत्त्वं वीररसयोगितां समर्थयितुं कर्तुमीश्वरः समर्थ इति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner described, the enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>), a particular <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), whose essence is intensified — having reached the supreme peak and being manifested — standing, existing, in the form whose essential nature is that of <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) as a <s>rasa</s> (sentiment), characterized by it, having attained the nature of <s>vīra rasa</s> (the heroic sentiment). It is capable, competent, to establish, to bring about, the <s>rasavat</s> quality, the connection with <s>vīra rasa</s>, of those words just stated, which are in the form of poetry.
She for whom even a bed of flowers, tender-limbed as she is, causes pain —
how does that queen lie upon the funeral pyre containing the blazing fire? || 284 ||

children.text: यस्या देव्याः कोमलमङ्गमस्या इति कोमलाङ्ग्याः मार्दवगुणेनैव केवलेन निर्मिताया अत एव कुसुममयी शय्या कुसुमशय्या पुष्पतल्पमत्यन्तकोमलं किमुतान्यत् ?  रुजाकरी पीड़ाहेतुः । सेयमेकान्तसुकुमारदेहा देवी हुताशनवतीमनलज्वालाकरालां चितां चितिमन्तशय्यां कथं नामाधिशेते ? तस्य मार्दवस्य किमिदं शयनम् ? हा दग्धदैव ! किमिदं व्यवसितं त्वया इति ॥
children.translated_text: Of this queen whose body is delicate — the one fashioned by the quality of softness alone — even a bed of flowers, a floral couch, exceedingly soft as it is (how much more so anything else?), causes pain, is a source of suffering. How then does this queen of absolutely delicate body lie upon a funeral pyre, blazing with the flames of fire? What kind of bed is this for such tenderness? Alas, accursed fate! What have you resolved upon! ||
He makes manifest what <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) this is —
Thus, the <s>kāruṇya</s> (pathos) that is heightened is considered as an ornament of speech;
likewise the remaining four: <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgust), <s>hāsya</s> (comedy), <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder), and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terror). || 285 ||

children.text: इति कथितेन [पथा] यथा कारुण्यं शोको भावविशेषः कारुण्याख्यरसविशेषाश्रयः उद्रिक्तमभिव्यक्तमागतं करुणरसात्मना वर्तमानमलङ्कारतया काव्यभूषणत्वेन स्मृतम् इष्टं तज्ज्ञैरिति । तथेत्यादि । यथा रतिक्रोधोत्साहशोकोद्रेकरूपाश्च
त्वारो [शृङ्गार]रौद्रवीरकरुणा रसा निदर्शितास्तथाऽपरे शेषाश्चत्वारो जुगुप्साहासविस्मयभयभावोद्भावस्वभावाः, बीभत्सश्च हास्यश्च अद्भुतश्च भयानकश्चेति बीभत्सहास्याद्भुतभयानका रसा निदर्श्यन्त इति शेषः ॥
children.translated_text: have been illustrated as <s>rasas</s>, likewise the remaining four — whose natures consist of the arousal of the <s>bhāvas</s> of disgust, laughter, wonder, and fear — namely <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgust), <s>hāsya</s> (comedy), <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder), and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terror) — are to be illustrated as <s>rasas</s> — this is the remainder. ||

Thus, by the method described: <s>kāruṇya</s> (pathos) — grief, a particular <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state), which is the substrate of the particular <s>rasa</s> called <s>karuṇa</s> — when heightened, manifested, having come into being as the essence of the <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (pathetic sentiment), is considered, accepted by the learned, as an ornament of poetry. 'Likewise' and so forth: just as the four — <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) — whose forms are the heightening of love, anger, vigor, and grief respectively,
Drinking and drinking the blood of your enemies from cupped hands,
the ghouls dance together with headless torsos, adorned with entrails. || 286 ||

children.text: देव ! तवारीणां त्वत्कृपाणकृतान्तपीतजीवितानां शोणितं रक्तं पाणिसम्पुटैः अञ्जलिभिः पायं पायमभीक्ष्णं पीत्वा मत्ताः कौणपाः राक्षसा अन्त्राणि भूषणानि रक्तकुसुमदामायमानानि येषामित्यन्त्रभूषणाः कबन्धैः विशिरोभिः शरीरैः सह

तवारीणामित्यपेक्षणीयम् । नृत्यन्ति [इति] उत्प्रेक्षा, तेषामपि नृत्ययोगात् । अत्र जुगुप्साख्यो भावः तादृशविभावजनितः, अनुभावेन तद्रूपेणाभिव्यक्तः । विकृतरूपबीभत्सरसस्वभावतामनुभवन्नलङ्कारत्वेनेष्ट इति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: 'of your enemies' should be understood. 'They dance' — this is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), since even those [torsos] are capable of dancing. Here, the <s>bhāva</s> called disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>), produced by such <s>vibhāvas</s> (stimuli), is manifested through such <s>anubhāvas</s> (responses). It should be seen as accepted as an ornament while partaking of the nature of the <s>bībhatsa rasa</s> (sentiment of disgust) with its distorted forms. ||

O lord! The blood, the gore, of your enemies — those whose lives have been drunk by the death-dealing edge of your sword — drinking it again and again from cupped hands, from joined palms, intoxicated, the ghouls (<s>kauṇapa</s>), the <s>rākṣasas</s>, wearing entrails as ornaments — appearing like garlands of red flowers — together with headless torsos (<s>kabandha</s>),
This fresh nail-mark on the slope of your breast, stuck to your unwilted garland —
cover it with your upper garment, O friend! || 287 ||

children.text: सखि ! तवाद्यापि अम्लाना प्रत्यग्रा परिणयोत्सवनिवेशिता माला कुसुमदामानि यस्या इत्यम्लानमालायाः । अन्ये तु पुरुषायितपरिश्रमेण म्लानमालत्वेऽपि अम्लानमालाया इति विशेषणमुपहासपरम् इति व्याचक्षते । स्तनस्य तटे प्रदेशे लग्नं व्यवस्थितं नखपदमिदं दृश्यमानं मयूरपदकशशप्लुतकादिरूपं

नवमभिनवमार्द्रं छाद्यतां संव्रियतामुत्तरीयेण संव्यानेन । किमेवमतित्वरितम् । आनन्दिताः सखि !  वयम् । साधु कुतम् । अत्रानुचितार्थदर्शनविभावात् कृतो हासाख्यो भावः समुद्रिक्तरूपो हास्यरसतामागतः । काव्यशोभाकरमिदं विज्ञेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: fresh, new, moist — let it be covered, concealed, with the upper garment, the shawl. Why such haste? We are delighted, O friend! Well done! Here, from the <s>vibhāva</s> (stimulus) of perceiving the inappropriate meaning, the <s>bhāva</s> called laughter (<s>hāsa</s>) arises, and in its heightened form, it attains the nature of the <s>hāsya rasa</s> (comic sentiment). This should be recognized as an embellishment of poetry. ||

O friend! Of your garland that is still even now unwilted, fresh — placed during the wedding celebration — that is, of her who has unwilted garlands. Others, however, explain: despite the garland being wilted from the exertion of <s>puruṣāyita</s> (the woman-on-top position), the qualifier 'unwilted garland' is employed with humorous intent. On the slope, the area, of the breast, this nail-mark that is lodged, situated — visible, in the form of a peacock-foot or a hare's-leap pattern —
Their garments are young shoots, their flowers are ornaments like necklaces,
and the branches are their mansions — wonderful are these trees of <s>Nandana</s> (Indra's paradise)! || 288 ||

children.text: एषां नन्दने उद्यान शाखिनाम् अंशुकानि वस्त्राणि प्रवालानि पल्लवानि हारादि च भूषणमलङ्कारः पुष्पम् । आदिशब्देनाङ्गदकुण्डलादिपरिग्रहः । शाखाश्च विचित्रसंनिवेशविशेषाः । मन्दिराणि प्रासादाः । [अ]हो चित्रमिदमपूर्वमिदं दृष्टम् ! इह विस्मयो नाम भावः परिस्फुटीभूतोऽद्भुतरसतामासेवत इति वेदितव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: Of these trees in <s>Nandana</s>, the pleasure garden: their garments are the young shoots (<s>pravāla</s>); their ornaments, decorations, such as necklaces and the like, are the flowers. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), bracelets, earrings, and such are included. And the branches, with their particular arrangements of marvelous configurations, are their mansions, their palaces. Oh, how wonderful, how unprecedented is this sight! Here, the <s>bhāva</s> called wonder (<s>vismaya</s>) becomes fully manifest and attains the nature of the <s>adbhuta rasa</s> (sentiment of wonder) — this should be understood. ||
This is the thunderbolt of <s>Maghavān</s> (Indra), with fire residing in its edges;
the mere recollection of which suffices to cause miscarriage in the wombs of <s>Daitya</s> women. || 289 ||

children.text: मघोनः शक्रस्य कुलिशं वज्रमिदं दृश्यते । धारासु कोटिषु सन्निहितो व्यवस्थितोऽनलोऽग्निरस्येति धारासन्नि

हितानलम् । यस्य कुलिशस्य स्मरणं किमु दर्शनम् ? दैत्यानामसुराणामन्तर्वत्न्यो याः स्त्रियस्तासामतिभयग्रस्तानां गर्भाणां पाताय नाशार्थं कल्पते सम्पद्यते । यस्य स्मरणादप्यसुरस्त्रीणां गर्भाः पतन्ति तदिदं कुलिशमिति
children.translated_text: (<s>dhārāsannihitānala</s>). The mere recollection — to say nothing of the sight! — of this thunderbolt suffices, serves, for the destruction, the falling, of the fetuses of the <s>Daitya</s> women, the wives of the <s>Asuras</s>, who are seized by extreme fear. This thunderbolt, whose mere recollection causes the miscarriage of <s>Asura</s> women's fetuses —

children.text: प्रकृतम् । अत्र भयाख्यो भावः समुद्भूतो भयानकरसरूपेण तिष्ठन्नलङ्कारः स्मृत इत्यवसेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: this is the subject. Here, the <s>bhāva</s> called fear (<s>bhaya</s>), having arisen, standing in the form of the <s>bhayānaka rasa</s> (sentiment of terror), is regarded as an ornament — this should be concluded. ||

This thunderbolt (<s>kuliśa</s>), the <s>vajra</s>, of <s>Maghavān</s>, that is, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), is seen. In the edges, the points, fire is stationed, residing — thus 'with fire residing in its edges'

children.text: नन्वियं रसवत्ता प्रागेव माधुर्यप्रस्तावे दर्शिता । तत् किं पुनरुच्यत इति चेदाह—
children.translated_text: But this <s>rasavattā</s> (sentiment-imbued quality) was already shown earlier in the discussion of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). Why then is it stated again? To this he says —
In [the discussion of] <s>mādhurya</s>, <s>rasa</s> was shown as the source of the non-vulgarity of the expressed meaning;
here, however, the <s>rasavattā</s> (sentiment-imbued quality) of speech, dependent on the eight <s>rasas</s>, is what is regarded [as the figure]. || 290 ||

children.text: वाच्यस्य काव्याधेयवस्तुनः सम्बधिनी सा ग्राम्यता असभ्यता योनिः प्रभवः अस्येति अग्राम्यतायोनिः । गमकत्वाद्वाच्यस्येति सापेक्षत्वेऽपि समस्यते । रसोऽर्थरसः । माधुर्ये शब्दार्थसाधारणे विभज्यमाने दर्शितः कामं सर्वोऽप्यलङ्कार
इत्यादिना । इह तु रसवदलङ्कारेऽष्टौ यथोक्ता रसास्तेष्वायत्ता प्रतिबद्धा रसवत्ता रसयोगिता अष्टरसा इति यावत् । गिरां काव्यानां सम्बन्धिनः स्मृता अभिमता इति ।
children.translated_text: and so forth. Here, however, in the figure <s>rasavat</s> (sentiment-imbued), the <s>rasavattā</s> (sentiment-imbued quality), which is dependent on, bound to, the eight <s>rasas</s> as described — meaning, consisting of the eight <s>rasas</s> — of speech, of poetry, is regarded, is accepted [as the figure].

Of the expressed meaning — the content conveyed by poetry — <s>agrāmyatā</s> means 'non-vulgarity, non-coarseness'; <s>yoni</s> means 'source' — thus '<s>agrāmyatāyoni</s>' (the source of non-vulgarity). Despite being dependent [on the word 'expressed'], it is compounded because of its indicative function. <s>Rasa</s> means the flavor of meaning. In [the discussion of] <s>mādhurya</s>, which is common to both word and meaning, when being analyzed, it was shown — 'indeed, every ornament' —
<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (vigor), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) — these are declared as the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotional states). ||
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible),
<s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) — these eight are regarded as the <s>rasas</s> of dramatic art. ||
These are the summary verses on <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states) and <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments). ||
|| Thus ends the section on <s>rasavat</s> (sentiment-imbued). ||
Illustrating <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the forceful), he says —

children.text: अपकर्ताहमस्मीति हृदि ते मा स्म भूद्भयम् ।
children.translated_text: 'I am one who has wronged you' — let there be no fear in your heart on this account;

children.text: विमुखेषु न मे खङ्गः ग्रहर्तुं जातु वाञ्छति ॥ २९१ ॥
children.translated_text: my sword never desires to strike those who have turned away [from battle]. || 291 ||

children.text: अहमस्यापकर्ता प्रतिकूलवर्ती प्राप्तश्चेदानीमनेनास्मि भवामीति हेतोस्ते तव हृदि चित्ते भयं त्रासो मृतोऽस्मीति मा स्म भूत् मा भैषीः । न त्वां हन्मि । नहि जातु
कदाचिदपि मे मम खड्गो विमुखेषु समरनिरास्थेषु अप्रतिप्रहरत्सु अप्रहर्तृषु क्रमितुं वाञ्छति । नास्त्यस्येदृशी स्थितिः यद्विमुखेषु प्रहरतीति ॥
children.translated_text: not even once, does my sword desire to strike those who have turned away, those who have withdrawn from battle, who do not fight back, who are non-combatants. It is not its way to strike those who have turned away. ||

'I am the adversary, the hostile one, of this person, and I have now been encountered by him' — on this account, let there be no fear, no terror, in your heart, your mind — do not think 'I am dead,' do not be afraid. I will not kill you. For never,
He explains that —

children.text: इति मुक्तः परो युद्धे निरुद्धो दर्पशालिना ।
children.translated_text: Thus, the enemy is released in battle, restrained [only momentarily] by one endowed with pride;
such and similar [expressions] should be known as <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the forceful). || 292 ||

children.text: इत्यनन्तरोक्तेन क्रमेण पुंसा केनापि केनचित् अनिर्दिष्टगोत्रनामधेयेन दर्पशालिना सौटीर्यसम्बन्धितेन युद्धे निरुद्धः प्राप्तः परः शत्रुः मुक्तस्त्यक्तो न हतः । यदीदृशं वचनं तदेवमादिकमन्यदपि तादृशम्—

children.translated_text: 'I will offer my life-breaths in the fire of battle, if my enemy is mighty;
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> will not go on living, humiliated by the ignominy of surrendering <s>Sītā</s>.' ||
Such and similar [expressions] should be known as <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the forceful), should be understood. ||

In the manner just stated: by some man, some unnamed person whose clan-name and personal name are unspecified, endowed with pride, possessed of valor, the enemy (<s>para</s>), the foe, is released, let go, not killed, in battle, though having been restrained, captured. If there is such a statement, that and others of the like kind —
|| Thus ends the section on <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the forceful). ||
Without directly stating the intended meaning, for the accomplishment of that very thing,
the narration by an alternative method — such is <s>paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis). || 293 ||

children.text: इष्टमभिमतमर्थं कञ्चित्प्रियसमागमादिलक्षणं साक्षादञ्जसा वाचकव्यापारेण अनाख्याय अप्रतिपाद्य तस्यैवेष्टस्यार्थस्य सिद्धये निष्पत्त्यर्थं प्रकारान्तरस्य तत्मिद्ध्यनुगुणस्य अन्यस्यार्थस्याख्यानम् आख्यायतेऽनेनेति वाक्यं तादृशम् इति अनूद्य तदीदृशं वचनं पर्यायोक्तमिष्टं मनीषिभिरिति विधिः ॥
children.translated_text: Without directly stating, without conveying through the function of denotative words, the intended, desired meaning — some matter characterized by the meeting of lovers and the like — for the accomplishment, the realization, of that very intended meaning, the narration of another matter through an alternative method, one that is conducive to its realization — this statement which narrates thus — having stated this in the resumptive mode, it is prescribed: such a statement is <s>paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis), accepted by the learned. ||
He illustrates that —
This <s>parabhr̥ta</s> (cuckoo) is biting the mango blossom;
I shall go and restrain him — you two may remain at ease. || 294 ||

children.text: परभृतः कोकिलोऽसावयं सहकारस्य सम्बन्धिनीं मञ्जरीं कलिकां दशति भिनत्ति । तमहं परभृतं वारयिष्यामि गत्वा, युवाभ्यां दम्पतीभ्यां स्वैरं स्वतन्त्रम्

children.translated_text: may remain at ease, freely, without concern for me. Enough of depending on me. ||
The <s>parabhr̥ta</s>, the cuckoo — this one — is biting, piercing, the blossom, the bud, belonging to the mango tree. I shall go and restrain that cuckoo; you two, the couple,
He explains that —
Having brought her friend together with a young man at the appointed place, in order to bring about their amorous festival,
some [woman] thus withdrew under that pretext. || 295 ||

children.text: सङ्केते कृतसंविदि कस्मिंश्चित् स्थाने सखीमात्मनो यूना केनचित् सह सङ्गमय्य सङ्गतां कृत्वा तयो रतोत्सवं रहो निर्वर्तयितुं साधयितुमीच्छन्त्या कयापि कयाचिद् विदग्धया संख्या तथा अनन्तरोक्तेन प्रकारेण परभृतवारणव्यपदेशेनापसृतं ततः सङ्केतादिति ॥
children.translated_text: At the appointed place, a location where an assignation had been arranged, having brought her own friend together with some young man, having united them, in order to bring about, to accomplish, their amorous festival in private — some clever woman, by the pretext of restraining the cuckoo, withdrew from that place of assignation in the manner just described. ||
|| Thus ends the section on <s>paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis). ||
Defining <s>samāhita</s> (providential coincidence), he says —
When one who is undertaking some task, by the force of destiny,
encounters the means for its accomplishment — that is what they call <s>samāhita</s> (providential coincidence). || 296 ||

children.text: किञ्चित्कार्यं प्रसादनादिकमारभमाणस्य साधयितुं सज्जीभूतस्य पुंसो दैववशात् विधिबलात् कारणात् न तु स्वसामर्थ्यात् । तस्य सिषाधयिषितस्य कार्यस्य साधनं साध्यते अनेनेति तस्य पुनरपरस्य प्रत्ययस्य कस्यचित्समापत्तिः सन्निधानं या तदेवंलक्षणं समाहितमाहुः ब्रुवते कवय इति ॥
children.translated_text: Of a man who is undertaking, who has prepared himself to accomplish, some task such as winning favor and the like — by the force of destiny, by the power of fate, as the cause — not by his own power. The occurrence, the coming into proximity, of some other factor, some means, by which that intended task is accomplished — that which has such characteristics is called <s>samāhita</s> (providential coincidence) by poets. ||
He illustrates that —
To overcome the anger of this beloved woman, as I bow at her feet,
by good fortune this thundering of clouds has arisen to aid me. || 297 ||

children.text: अस्याः प्रियाया मानं प्रतिकूलवर्तितां निराकर्तुं पादयोरेनामस्या वा नमस्यतः नमतो मे ममोपकाराय आरब्धकार्यानुग्रहार्थं घनस्य मेघस्य गर्जितं मन्मथनिर्भर्त्सितमिव मानिनीमानदुःसहमुदीर्णम् उदितं दिष्ट्येत्यानन्दनिवेदनमिष्टसिद्धेः । इह मान-
निराकरणं कार्यमारब्धम्, तत्र विधिवशाद् घनगर्जितमपरं साधनं च समापन्नमिति लक्षणं योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: overcoming her anger has been undertaken; therein, by the force of destiny, the thundering of the cloud, an additional means, has come about — thus the definition should be applied. ||

To overcome, to remove, the hostility, the adverse attitude, of this beloved woman, as I bow, as I prostrate myself, at her feet — for my benefit, for the assistance of the task I have undertaken — the thundering of the cloud (<s>ghana</s>), resembling the threatening rebuke of the god of love, unbearable for a proud woman's pride, has arisen, has emerged. 'By good fortune' (<s>diṣṭyā</s>) is an exclamation of joy at the fulfillment of what was desired. Here, the task of
|| Thus ends the section on <s>samāhita</s> (providential coincidence). ||
Displaying <s>udātta</s> (the sublime), he says —
The unsurpassed greatness of either one's intent or one's splendor —
the learned call that figure of speech <s>udātta</s> (the sublime). || 298 ||

children.text: आशयस्याभिप्रायस्य कस्यचिद्विभूतेः सम्पदो वा यन्महत्वमौदार्यमनुत्तरं नास्मादुत्तरमधिकमस्ति प्रकर्ष
निष्ठाधिष्ठानत्वादिति । तमलङ्कारं निरतिशयोदात्तत्वप्रकाशनरूपमुदात्तं नाम प्राहुर्मनीषिणः कवय इति ॥
children.translated_text: — that figure which manifests the unsurpassably exalted nature is called <s>udātta</s> (the sublime) by the learned, the poets. ||

Of one's intent, one's inner purpose — or of one's splendor, one's glory — the greatness, the nobility, that is unsurpassed, than which nothing higher exists, because it occupies the ground of the highest excellence

children.text: गुरोः शासमत्येतुं न शशाक स राघवः ।
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> (Rāma), who was undaunted even under the burden of the task of severing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s heads,
was unable to transgress the command of his father. || 299 ||

children.text: गुरोः पितुर्दशरथस्य शासनं राज्यमिदं मया भरताय दत्तं त्वया वनमावस्तव्यमित्याज्ञामत्येतुं लङ्घितुं न शशाक न समर्थोऽभूत् विनयपरवशतया स राघवो रामः । किमसावित्थमकिञ्चित्करो यत् स्वभाव्यं राज्यमन्यस्मै दीयमानमात्मानं च वने क्षिप्यमाणमपेक्षते ? नैवम् । गुरुभक्तिः कापि सा तस्येत्याह- य इत्यादि । यो राघवः रावणस्य दशकन्धरस्य राक्षसराजस्य दासीकृतत्रैलोक्यस्य शिरसां छेदः कार्य त्रैलोक्यार्थमनुष्ठेयत्वात् तदेव भारोऽतिदुर्वहत्वात् । तत्रापि किम् ? पुनरात्मविपक्षनिग्रहमात्रेऽविक्लवः शक्तः स तादृशः गुरोराज्ञां नातिचक्रामेत्याशयमाहात्म्यं विनयोत्कर्षराज्यलोभानभिभवादिलक्षणमालक्ष्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: The command of his father (<s>guru</s>), <s>Daśaratha</s> — 'This kingdom has been given by me to <s>Bharata</s>; you are to dwell in the forest' — this injunction, <s>Rāghava</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, was unable to transgress, to violate, due to being under the sway of filial devotion. Is he then so powerless that he watches his rightful kingdom being given to another and himself being cast into the forest? Not at all. His devotion to his father is something extraordinary — he says 'who' (<s>yaḥ</s>) and so forth. This <s>Rāghava</s> — for whom the severing of the heads of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the ten-headed lord of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, who had enslaved the three worlds, was a task to be performed for the sake of the three worlds, and was itself an exceedingly heavy burden — yet even in that, what of it? He was undaunted, capable, even in the matter of subduing his own adversary — and such a one did not transgress his father's command. Thus the greatness of his inner resolve, characterized by the excellence of his filial devotion and his non-subjugation to the greed for kingship, is perceived. ||
Surrounded by hundreds of reflections cast upon the gem-encrusted walls,
the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> was identified with difficulty by <s>Āñjaneya</s> (Hanumān) in his true form. || 300 ||

children.text: पद्मरागादिरत्नविकारा भित्तयः कुड्यानि रत्नभित्तयस्तासु संक्रान्तैरुदितैः प्रतिबिम्बानां प्रतिशरीराणां शतैर्वृतः परिक्षिप्तो लङ्केश्वरो [रा]वणः आञ्जनेयेन हनूमता सीतान्वेषणार्थ तत्र गतेनायं रावणः, प्रतिबिम्बान्येतानीति तत्त्वतः सम्यग् ज्ञातो
निर्धारितः कृच्छ्राद्यत्नेन निपुणं निरूपयता न झटित्येवेति भूतिमहत्त्वमनतिशयमुक्तं गृहाण्यपि रत्नमयानि इति ॥
children.translated_text: identified, ascertained — with difficulty, with effort, by one who was examining carefully, not in an instant — thus the greatness of his glory, his splendor, is stated as unsurpassable, since even his palaces are made of gems. ||

The walls (<s>bhitti</s>), the ramparts, made of gems such as rubies and the like — on those gem-walls, by the hundreds of reflections, counter-images, that had appeared, cast upon them — surrounded, encircled — the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, was, by <s>Āñjaneya</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, who had gone there in search of <s>Sītā</s> — this <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, 'these are reflections' — thus in his true form, correctly,
Explaining both of those, he says —
In the former, the greatness of inner resolve; here, the gravity of prosperity —
both have been well expressed; thus this pair of <s>udātta</s> (the sublime) is evident. || 301 ||

children.text: पूर्वत्र गुरोरित्यादौ प्रयोगे आशयस्य चित्तस्य माहात्म्यमत्युदात्तत्वमुक्तरूपम् । अत्रा[न]न्तरे रत्नभित्तिष्वित्यादौ अभ्युदयस्य विभूतेर्गौरवं माहात्म्यमुक्तरूपं सुव्यञ्जितमाख्यातमितीदृशमिति वा हेतोरदस्तदुदात्तयोर्द्वयमपि नैकम् । आशयोपात्तं च व्यक्तं परिस्फुटमभवदिति ॥
children.translated_text: In the former — in the composition beginning with 'of the father' (<s>guroḥ</s>) and so forth — the greatness, the supreme exaltedness, of the inner resolve (<s>āśaya</s>), of the mind, is of the form described. Here, in the immediately following one beginning with 'on the gem-walls' and so forth — the gravity, the greatness, of prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>), of splendor, is of the form described — both have been well expressed, proclaimed — for this reason, or being of this nature, both types of <s>udātta</s> (the sublime) — not just one — have been made evident, fully manifest. ||
|| Thus ends the section on <s>udātta</s> (the sublime). ||
Addressing <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment/denial), he says —
<s>Apahnutī</s> (denial) is the showing of another meaning after denying something;
<s>Smara</s> (the god of love) is not five-arrowed — his arrows number a thousand. || 302 ||

children.text: किञ्चिद्वस्तुरूपमपह्नुत्य निराकृत्य नेदमिति, अन्यस्यार्थस्य धर्मरूपस्य वा दर्शनं विधानं यदित्यनूद्य सापह्नुतिरित्यभिधीयते । तामुदाहरति-

स्मरः कामः पञ्चेषवोऽस्येति पञ्चेषुर्न भवतीति । इषूणां पञ्चत्वं धर्मोऽत्रापह्नूयते । न स्मर इषवो वा । यदाह—तस्य स्मरस्य पत्रिणामिषूणां सम्बन्धि सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्यता । अन्यथा कथं भुवनत्रयं जयेदिति । अन्यस्य सहस्रसंख्यालक्षणस्यार्थस्य धर्मान्तरस्य दर्शनमितीदृशी धर्मापह्नतिरवसेयेति ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> is <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love); he whose arrows are five is called <s>pañceṣu</s> (five-arrowed) — [the verse says] he is not so. The five-ness of the arrows, a property, is here denied. Not <s>Smara</s> himself or the arrows themselves. As it says: of that <s>Smara</s>, the thousand, the number of a thousand, pertains to his arrows (<s>patrin</s>). Otherwise, how would he conquer the three worlds? The showing of another property characterized by the number of a thousand — thus such a denial of a property (<s>dharmāpahnutī</s>) should be understood.

Having denied, that is, negated, some real object — 'this is not so' — the showing, the setting forth, of another meaning or another property — having stated this definition, it is designated as <s>apahnutī</s> (denial). He illustrates it —

children.text: चन्दनं चन्द्रिका मन्दो गन्धवाही च दक्षिणः ।
children.translated_text: Sandalwood, moonlight, a gentle fragrance-bearing southern breeze —

children.text: सेयमग्निमयी सृष्टिः शीता किल परान् प्रति ॥ ३०३ ॥
children.translated_text: this creation is made of fire for us; it is cool, they say, for others. || 303 ||

children.text: चन्दनं मलयजं चन्द्रिका ज्योत्स्ना मन्दो मृदुर्गन्धवाही पवनो दक्षिण इति यदेतत् सेयमीदृशी सृष्टिः स्रष्टुरग्निमयी दहनस्वभावा अस्माकम् [कृते] । परान् प्रति

children.translated_text: they say, this creation is cool, delightful. By the word '<s>kila</s>' (they say),

children.text: मयि शीतेति मुद्रितपुस्तकेषु । शीता किलेति रत्नश्रियः । एष एव वादिजङ्घालाद्यभिमतः पाठः ।
श्रुतगम्यतां शीततायाः सूचयति । दुष्टताया एवानुभवगम्यत्वात् । विरहविप्लुतचित्तः कश्चित्कामुकः कथयतीति ॥
children.translated_text: he indicates that the coolness is known only by hearsay, since the burning nature alone is known from direct experience. A certain lover whose mind is distraught with separation speaks thus.

Sandalwood, that is, <s>Malaya</s>-born; moonlight, that is, the radiance of the moon; a gentle, soft, fragrance-bearing wind, the southern breeze — this creation of the Creator, of such a nature, is made of fire, of a burning nature, for us. For others,
What kind of <s>apahnutī</s> (denial) is this? He says —
Having conceded the coolness with respect to others, by the lover with respect to himself,
because of the demonstration of heat in that [substance] — this is <s>viṣayāpahnutī</s> (denial of domain). || 304 ||

children.text: तस्य चन्दनादेर्वस्तुनः परेष्वन्येषु स्वस्थेषु विषये शैशिर्यं शैत्यमभ्युपेत्याग्निकृत्यापह्नुत्या एवात्मनि विषये केनचित् कामिना वियुक्तेन औष्ण्यस्य चन्दनादिगतस्य प्रदर्शनादुद्भावनात्कारणात् सैषा तादृशी विषयापह्नुतिः । विषये क्वचिद्वस्तुरूपापह्नुतेः, न सर्वत्रेति ॥
children.translated_text: Of that substance such as sandalwood and the like, having conceded the coolness with respect to others, those who are composed, in that domain — and then, through the concealment as if by fire's effect, with respect to himself as the domain, by a certain lover who is separated — because of the demonstration, the evoking, of the heat inherent in the sandalwood and the like — this is such a <s>viṣayāpahnutī</s> (denial of domain). The denial of the real nature applies in a particular domain, not universally.
The moon, whose rays drip nectar — that is not what we believe it to be;
this is something else entirely, whose rays drip poison. || 305 ||

children.text: अमृतं सुधा स्यन्दन्ते स्रवन्तीत्यमृतस्यन्दिनः किरणाः अस्येति अमृतस्यन्दिकिरणः पदार्थविशेषश्चन्द्रमा नाम नोऽस्माकं मतः प्रसिद्धः । अयं तु अन्य एवार्थात्मा पदार्थः । कुतः ? विषममृतविरुद्धं निष्यन्दमानाः क्षरन्त्यो दीधितयः किरणा अस्येति विषनिष्यन्दिनो दीधितयो यतस्तस्मात्कथमयं चन्द्रस्तद्विरुद्धलक्षण इति कश्चिद्विरही विप्लवत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Nectar, that is, ambrosia; whose rays flow, drip — thus one 'whose rays drip nectar' (<s>amṛtasyandikiranā</s>). The particular entity called the moon is known to us, is well-established. But this one is an entirely different entity. Why? Because the rays, the beams, of this one drip, flow with, poison — the opposite of nectar. Therefore, how can this be the moon, which has the opposite characteristics? — thus some person in separation is distraught.
What kind of <s>apahnutī</s> (denial) is this? He says —
Thus, the very moon-nature of the moon is denied, and it is presented as having a different nature;
spoken by one afflicted by love — this is recognized as <s>svarūpāpahnutī</s> (denial of essential nature). || 306 ||

children.text: इत्युक्तेन विधिना इन्दोश्चन्द्रत्वममृतमयत्वं स्वरूपं निवर्त्यापह्नुत्यार्थान्तरात्मना विषरूपेणोक्तः उद्भावित इन्दुः । उक्तमित्यपि पाठः । तत्र चन्द्रत्वमुक्तं स्वरूपेण निवर्त्य रूपान्तरेणोक्तमिति योज्यम् । स्मरार्तेन कामातुरेण विरहिणा केनचिदिति हेतोः स्वरूपापह्नुतिरेषा [मता] ज्ञेया, चन्द्रस्वरूपस्या
children.translated_text: In the manner stated, the moon-nature of the moon, its ambrosia-essence, its essential form, is denied, negated, and it is presented in the form of another nature, as having the nature of poison. The moon has been characterized thus. There is also the reading '<s>uktam</s>' (it has been stated). In that case, the moon-nature having been denied in its own form, it should be construed as stated in another form. By one afflicted by <s>Smara</s> (love), by some person tormented by passion, in separation — for this reason, this is [recognized as] <s>svarūpāpahnutī</s> (denial of essential nature), because of the denial of the moon's own nature.

children.text: ननूपमापह्नुतिरिह संगृहीता । सा हि कथञ्चिदन्तर्भूतोपमेष्यते । यदाहुः—
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>upamāpahnutī</s> (denial-with-simile) has been included here. For it is accepted as somehow having an implicit simile. As they say —
The desired <s>apahnutī</s> (denial) is one with a somewhat implicit simile;
it is made through the denial of a real fact, like the sacrificial kindling. ||

children.text: नेयं विरौति भृङ्गाली मदेन मुखरा मुहुः ।
children.translated_text: It is not this swarm of bees that hums repeatedly, intoxicated;
this is the sound of the bow of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) being drawn. ||
And the following has been given as an example:

body.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that this does not conform to the definition of <s>apahnutī</s> as stated here, he says —

children.translated_text: <s>Upamāpahnutī</s> (denial-with-simile) has already been shown earlier among the varieties of <s>upamā</s> (simile);
thus, the elaboration of the varieties of <s>apahnutī</s> should be observed in illustrative examples. || 307 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Upamāpahnutī</s> (denial-with-simile) of this kind has already been shown, incorporated, earlier among the varieties of <s>upamā</s> (simile).

children.translated_text: The moon can never roar back at your face —
being blemished and dull, that is merely a <s>pratiṣedhopamā</s> (simile by negation). ||

body.text: इति संगृहीता । तन्नास्याः पृथग्लक्षणं लक्ष्यं चोच्यते । इति कथितपथानुसारेण अपह्नुतेर्भेदानां विकल्पानां विस्तरः प्रपञ्चो लक्ष्यो द्रष्टव्यः । लक्ष्येषु प्रयोगेषु सर्गबन्धादिषु स्वयं चैते प्रयोक्तव्याः । तद्यथा—
body.translated_text: Thus it has been included. Therefore no separate definition and example are given for it. Thus, following the path that has been described, the elaboration, the expansion, of the varieties of <s>apahnutī</s> (denial) should be observed, should be sought. In examples, in compositions such as narrative poems and the like, one should also employ these oneself. For instance —
This entire world is the beloved — nothing at all is just the world;
yet you do not attain contentment of mind, nor do you attain the beloved. ||
This is not the beloved at all — some other woman entirely appears;
for she would not thus serve without any compassion. ||
These are not your two breasts — this is some unbearable burden;
how do I survive, O slender-limbed one! You are greatly distressed by this. ||
Thus, other varieties of <s>apahnutī</s> (denial) should also be conceived.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>apahnutī</s> (denial). ||

children.translated_text: He defines <s>śliṣṭa</s> (pun), which comes next in order —
<s>Śliṣṭa</s> (pun) is a desired expression that conveys multiple meanings through a single form;
it is of two kinds: one with undivided words and one predominantly with divided words. || 308 ||

children.text: यद् वचो वचनमनेको भिन्नोऽर्थोऽभिधेयं यस्येत्यनेकार्थम् । एकेन समानेन रूपेण शब्दस्वभावेन अन्वितं युक्तं सरूपम् इत्यनूद्य श्लिष्टं तदिष्टं स्मर्यत इति विधीयते । तच्चैवं लक्षणं श्लिष्टं द्विधा प्रकारद्वयेन भिद्यते । कथम् ? अभिन्नमेकं पदं सुबन्ततिङन्तरूपं यत्र तदभिन्नपदमविकृतशब्दं भिन्नमनेकम्, पदं भङ्गेन योजनात्, प्रायमधिकं यत्र तद् भिन्नपदप्रायम् । तेन वा प्रायमधिकं किञ्चिदभिन्नमिति प्रायोग्रहणेन सूचयति । अनेन रूपेण द्विधेति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: That expression, that utterance, which has multiple, different meanings or referents — thus '<s>anekārtha</s>' (having multiple meanings) — endowed with, united with, a single, identical form, a verbal nature — that is called <s>śliṣṭa</s> (pun), having been stated in the definition. And this <s>śliṣṭa</s>, having such a definition, is divided in two ways, by two modes. How? Where there is one undivided word, in the form of a nominal or verbal unit, that is '<s>abhinnapada</s>' (with undivided word), having an unaltered word-form. Where the words are multiple, divided, through different parsing — and this is predominant, constituting the majority — that is '<s>bhinnapadaprāya</s>' (predominantly with divided words). Or, by the word '<s>prāya</s>' (predominantly), he indicates that the majority is divided while some are undivided. In this form, it is twofold — this is the basic meaning.
Illustrating, he says —
This one has risen to eminence, is radiant, has a crimson circle,

children.text: राजा हरति लोकस्य हृदयं मृदुभिः करैः ॥ ३०९ ॥
children.translated_text: and this king captivates the heart of the people with his gentle rays. || 309 ||

children.text: असावयं राजा चन्द्रो नृपतिश्च । तत्र चन्द्रस्तावदुदयं पर्वतमारूढ़ः । नृपतिस्तूदयमभ्युदयं राज्यरूपमारूढ़ः प्राप्तः । चन्द्रः कान्तिमान् सौम्यः । नृपतिः कान्तिमानभिरूपः । चन्द्रो रक्तमरुणमुद

यावस्थाभावित्वान्मण्डलं बिम्बमस्येति रक्तमण्डलः । नृपतिस्तु रक्तमनुरक्तं स्निग्धं मण्डलममात्यादिप्रकृतिवृन्दं यस्येति रक्तमण्डलः । लोकस्य हृदयं जनस्य मनः प्रीतियोगेन हरति रञ्जयति । चन्द्रो मृदुभिः शीतैः करैः किरणैर्हरति । नृपतिस्तु मृदुभिरनुद्वेजनीयैः करैरुचितषड्भागादिस्वभावैः हरति । इति श्लिष्टमभिन्नपदं भङ्गेन विना यथावस्थानमुभयत्र पदयोजनादिति ॥
children.translated_text: because its orb takes on a reddish hue at the time of rising. The king, however, has a <s>raktamaṇḍala</s> — an affectionate, devoted circle of ministers and courtiers. He captivates, delights, the heart, the mind, of the people through love. The moon captivates with its gentle, cool rays. The king, however, captivates with his gentle, non-oppressive imposts — whose nature is the customary one-sixth share and the like. This is <s>śliṣṭa</s> (pun) with undivided words, since the words are construed in both senses without any splitting, remaining as they are.

This <s>rājā</s> means both the moon and the king. Now, the moon has ascended the <s>udaya</s> mountain. The king, however, has ascended to <s>udaya</s> (prosperity), that is, has attained sovereignty. The moon is <s>kāntimān</s> (radiant), luminous. The king is <s>kāntimān</s> (handsome). The moon has a <s>raktamaṇḍala</s> — a crimson disc,
Connected with the one who is the repository of faults, who moves on the path of the stars —

children.text: राज्ञा प्रदोषो मामित्यमप्रियं किं न बाधते ॥ ३१० ॥
children.translated_text: does not the evening, along with this unpleasant one, afflict me? || 310 ||

children.text: प्रदोषो रजनीमुखम्, प्रकृष्टोऽधिको दोषो लोभादिरस्येति प्रदोषश्च कश्चित् पुरुषो विवक्षितः । दोषा रात्रिराकर आश्रयस्तत्र दर्शनात् । यस्य दोषाकर इति तत्सन्निधौ दृष्टेः, दोषाकरेण चन्द्रेण, दोषाणां क्रौर्यादीनामाकरः स्थानं तेन नृपेण । नक्षत्रपथे व्योम्नि वतते नक्षत्रपथवर्तिना चन्द्रेण, क्षत्रस्य पन्थाः क्षत्रपथः क्षात्रो धर्मः शिष्टपालनदुष्टनिग्रहादिरूपः, न तथाऽक्षत्रपथस्तद्वर्तिना राजधर्मातिक्रमिणा नृपेण संबध्नन् सङ्गच्छमानः । मामित्थमनेन प्रकारेण अप्रियं न विद्यते प्रियाऽस्येति विरहिणं प्रदोषः क्षणदावतारः । किं कस्मात् न बाधते न तापयति ? बाधत एव । अप्रियं न प्रियमप्रियं द्वेष्यं किं न बाधते नापकरोति ? निगृह्णात्येव प्रदोषः प्रकृष्टदोषः पुरुषः कश्चित् । इदं भिन्नपदप्रायं श्लिष्टमुक्तेन विधिना प्रदोष इत्यादीनां भिन्नत्वाद् राज्ञा इत्यस्याभेदादिति ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Pradoṣa</s> is the twilight, the face of night; and a certain person is intended who has abundant faults such as greed and the like — '<s>pradoṣa</s>' meaning one of excessive fault. Night (<s>doṣā</s>) is the basis, the abode, because of being seen there — thus '<s>doṣākara</s>' (repository of night/faults), because of being perceived in its proximity; '<s>doṣākara</s>' also means the moon. And '<s>doṣākara</s>' as the repository, the locus, of faults such as cruelty and the like — meaning that king. Moving on the path of stars (<s>nakṣatrapatha</s>), the sky — by the moon; <s>kṣatrapatha</s> means the path of the <s>kṣatriya</s>, the royal <s>dharma</s> characterized by protecting the good and punishing the wicked — not on that path, that is, transgressing the royal <s>dharma</s> — by such a king. Connected with, associated with. 'Me, in this manner, this unpleasant' — one who has no beloved, a person in separation — the twilight, the advent of night. Why does it not afflict, not torment? It certainly does. 'Unpleasant' — not dear, hateful — why does it not harm, not injure? He certainly does oppress — the person of excessive fault. This is <s>śliṣṭa</s> (pun) predominantly with divided words, in the manner described, because words like '<s>pradoṣa</s>' and the like are divided, while '<s>rājñā</s>' (by the king) is undivided.

children.text: अलङ्कारान्तरगोचरः श्लेषोऽपि । स प्रागुक्त इति दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (pun) also operates within the domain of other <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments). Showing that such has already been stated, he says —
The <s>śleṣas</s> (puns) operating in the domain of <s>upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and the like
have already been shown earlier; now some additional ones are demonstrated. || 311 ||

children.text: उपमा रूपकमाक्षेपः व्यतिरेकश्चादिर्यस्य दीपकार्थान्तरन्यासादेः स गोचरो विषयो येषां ते श्लेषाः प्रागेवोपमाप्रस्तावादिषु दर्शिताः । ततः सम्प्रति नोच्यन्ते । तत्रोपमागोचरः श्लेषः शिशिरांशुप्रतिद्वन्द्वीत्यादिना

children.translated_text: The one attending <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) was shown through the verse beginning '<s>rājahaṃsopabhogārha</s>' ('worthy of enjoyment by the royal swan') —
The one in the domain of <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection) through the verse beginning '<s>amṛtātmani padmānām</s>' ('in the nectarine essence of lotuses') —
The one based on <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) through the verse beginning '<s>tvaṃ samudraśca durvārau</s>' ('you and the ocean, both irresistible') —
The one situated in <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) through the verse beginning '<s>hṛdyagandhavahā</s>' ('carrying a pleasing fragrance') —

children.text: । एवमन्येऽप्यर्थान्तरन्यासादिगोचरा द्रष्टव्याः । ये तु पूर्वं नोक्तास्ते अपरेऽन्ये केचन कियन्तो निदर्श्यन्ते प्रतिपाद्यन्त इति ॥
children.translated_text: Likewise, others operating in the domain of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) and the like should be noted. But those that were not stated previously — those additional, further ones, of a certain number — are now illustrated, expounded.

<s>Upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and what begins with these — <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), and the like — are the domains, the spheres, of those <s>śleṣas</s> (puns). These have already been shown earlier in the discussions on <s>upamā</s> and so forth. Therefore they are not discussed now. Among those, the <s>śleṣa</s> operating in the domain of <s>upamā</s> was shown through the verse beginning '<s>śiśirāṃśupratidvandvī</s>' ('rivaling the cool-rayed one') —
What are those? Showing them, he says —
There is one with an identical action; another with non-contradictory actions;
there is yet another with contradictory actions; and there is also a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) with restriction. || 312 ||

children.text: अभिन्ना एका क्रिया यत्र स तादृशः कश्चिदस्ति श्लेषः । अविरुद्धे सहभाविन्यौ क्रिये यस्मिन् स तद्रूपोऽपरोऽन्यः कश्चिदस्ति । विरुद्धे कर्मणी क्रिये यत्र स चान्यः कश्चिदस्ति । श्लेष इति सर्वत्र सम्बध्यते । नियमोऽवधारणमस्मिन्नस्तीति नियमवानपि विद्यते कश्चित् ॥
children.translated_text: Where the action is undifferentiated, single — such a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) exists. Where the two actions are non-contradictory, compatible — of that nature is another, a different one. Where the two actions are contradictory — yet another exists. '<s>Śleṣa</s>' (pun) is to be supplied everywhere. One in which there is <s>niyama</s> (restriction), determination — such a 'restricted' type also exists.
One whose expression has the form of negation of restriction; one that is non-contradictory; and one that is contradictory too —
the distinct nature of these will become clear only in the illustrative examples. || 313 ||

children.text: नियमस्याक्षेपो निषेधो रूपं स्वभावो यस्यां तथाविधोक्तिरभिधानं यत्र तादृशोऽप्यस्ति कश्चित् । नात्र विरोधोऽस्तीत्यविरोधी । सोऽप्यस्ति । विरोधोऽसङ्गतिरत्र विद्यत इति विरोधी । सोऽप्यस्ति । नामसङ्कीर्तनमात्रेण न ज्ञायन्त इत्याह—तेषां श्लेषाणामभिन्नक्रियादीनां निदर्शनेषु लक्ष्येष्वेव नाभिधानमात्रेण रूपस्य प्रतिनियतस्य लक्षणस्य व्यक्तिः प्रत्यवगमो भविष्यति । ततो यथाक्रमं निदर्श्यन्त इति ॥
children.translated_text: That in which the expression, the statement, has the form of the negation, the denial, of a restriction — such a type also exists. One in which there is no contradiction — that is the non-contradictory type. It too exists. One in which there is contradiction, incongruity — that is the contradictory type. It too exists. Since they are not understood merely by reciting their names, he says: the distinct nature, the clear comprehension, of the specific definition of these <s>śleṣas</s> (puns) beginning with the 'identical-action' type, will become apparent only in the illustrative examples, not merely through definitions. Therefore they are illustrated in due order.
Naturally sweet, affectionate, declaring intense passion —

children.text: दृशो दूत्यश्च कर्षन्ति कान्ताभिः प्रेषिताः प्रियम् ॥ ३१४ ॥
children.translated_text: both glances and messengers, dispatched by beloved women, attract the lover. || 314 ||

children.text: कान्ताभिर्नायिकाभिः वासकशय्याभिः प्रेषिताः प्रयुक्ता दृशो दृष्टयो दूत्यश्च निसृष्टार्थादय[ः] स्वभावेनैव मधुराः सुभगा उभय्योऽपि स्निग्धाः । प्रेमरसभाविता दृशः दूत्यस्त्वपरुषाः । रागं भावमुल्बणमुदीर्णमन्तर्गतमाकारविशेषेण शंसन्त्यः सूचयन्त्यो दृशः । दूत्यस्तु रागमुल्बणं नायिकानुरक्तिमधिकां चतुरमाचक्षाणाः कर्षन्ति वशीकुर्वन्ति प्रियं वल्लभम्, यत्र प्रेषिताः । अयमभिन्नक्रियः श्लेषः, कर्षणलक्षणयैकया क्रियया दृशां दूतीनां च सम्बन्धादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Dispatched, sent forth, by beloved women, heroines who have prepared the bed-chamber — glances and messengers (<s>dūtyas</s>), those entrusted with full authority and the like, are both naturally sweet, charming, by nature itself. Both are affectionate — the glances are imbued with the essence of love; the messengers, however, are gentle. Declaring, indicating, intense, surging passion within, through the particular expression of their form — these are the glances. The messengers, however, skillfully declare the intense passion, the heightened attachment of the heroine, and attract, bring under their control, the beloved, the lover, to the place where they have been sent. This is a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) with identical action, because both the glances and the messengers are connected by the single action characterized by attracting.
Sweet, passion-enhancing, tender — the songs of the <s>kokila</s> (Indian cuckoo);
they are listened to when intoxicated, and dark-eyed women are embraced. || 315 ||

children.text: असितेक्षणाः स्त्रियः कोकिलानां गिरश्च वाचः । मधुराः मनोहराः द्वय्योऽपि । रागं रक्तिभावं वर्धयन्ति रागवर्धिन्यः उभय्योऽपि । कोमलाः कोकिलागिरः श्रवणानुद्वेजनीयत्वात्, असितेक्षणास्तु सुखस्पर्शत्वात् । कोकिलागिरो मदेन समयकृतेन हर्षविशेषेण कलाः पुष्टाः । असितेक्षणास्तु मदेन मधुपानजनितेन कलाः विह्वलाः ।
कोकिलागिर आकर्ण्यन्ते श्रूयन्ते । असितेक्षणास्तु श्लिष्यन्ते आलिङ्ग्यन्ते ।
children.translated_text: The <s>kokila</s> songs are listened to, are heard. The dark-eyed women, however, are embraced, are held in an embrace.
This is a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) with non-contradictory actions, because listening and embracing are compatible, co-existing.

Dark-eyed women; and the songs, the voices, of <s>kokilas</s> (Indian cuckoos). Both are sweet, enchanting. Both enhance passion, increase amorous feeling — thus both are <s>rāgavardhinī</s> (passion-enhancing). The <s>kokila</s> songs are tender because they do not agitate the ears; the dark-eyed women are tender because of their pleasant touch. The <s>kokila</s> songs are enriched by intoxication — the particular joy produced by the season. The dark-eyed women, however, are intoxicated — languid with the intoxication born of drinking <s>madhu</s> (wine).
Displaying passion enhanced by the contact with wine,
the hot-rayed sun is overcome, while the passion-born one (<s>Aṅgaja</s>, the god of love) prevails. || 316 ||

children.text: एष घर्मांशुरादित्यः पराभवत्यस्तमेति । अङ्गजस्तु कामो विजृम्भते समुद्भवति । वारुण्या प्रतीच्या दिशा योगेन सङ्गमेन वर्धितमुपबृंहितं रागमरुणिमानम् आदर्शयन् धर्मांशुः पराभवतीति प्रकृतम् । अङ्गजस्तु वारुण्या मदिरया योगेन पानलक्षणेन वर्धितं रागं रतिभावमादर्शयन् विभ्रमैराविष्कुर्वन् विजृम्भत इति प्रक्रान्तम् । अयं विरुद्धक्रियः श्लेषः, पराभवविजृम्भणयोरस्तमयोदयरूपयोः परस्परविरोधात् इति ॥
children.translated_text: This <s>gharmāṃśu</s> (the hot-rayed one, the sun) sets, goes to disappearance. But <s>Aṅgaja</s> (the god of love) arises, comes forth. The primary meaning: the sun, displaying redness (<s>rāga</s>) that has been enhanced, nourished, by conjunction with the western (<s>vāruṇī</s>) direction, sets. But <s>Aṅgaja</s>, displaying passion (<s>rāga</s>), the sentiment of love, enhanced by the conjunction of wine (<s>vāruṇī</s>, i.e., liquor), in the sense of drinking, manifesting it through amorous transports, arises — this is the secondary meaning. This is a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) with contradictory actions (<s>viruddhakriya</s>), since setting and arising, being of the nature of decline and ascent, are mutually contradictory.
Sword-nature belongs to that weapon alone; crookedness belongs only to his bow;
and the quality of seeking belongs only to the arrows of this king. || 317 ||

children.text: अस्य नरेन्द्रस्य कस्यचिन्निस्त्रिंशत्वम् असौ खङ्ग एव वर्तते न म[न]सि निस्त्रिंशत्वम् । असित्वं क्रौर्यं चेति श्लिष्टम् । धनुष्येव वक्रता । न चेतसि वक्रता । नतत्वं शाठ्यं चेति श्लिष्टिः । शरेषु बाणेष्वेव मार्गणत्वं नात्मनि । मार्गणत्वं शरत्वं याचकत्वं चेति श्लिष्यते । अयं नियमवान् श्लेषः । असावेवेत्यवधारणप्रयोगादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Of this king, a certain one: 'sword-nature' (<s>nistriṃśatva</s>) resides in the sword alone, not in his mind. '<s>Asitva</s>' (sword-ness) and cruelty — thus the pun (<s>śleṣa</s>). Crookedness belongs to the bow alone, not to his heart. Curvature and duplicity — thus the pun. 'Seeking-nature' (<s>mārgaṇatva</s>) belongs to the arrows alone, not to himself. '<s>Mārgaṇatva</s>' means both 'being an arrow' and 'being a beggar' — thus the pun. This is a <s>śleṣa</s> with restriction (<s>niyamavān</s>), due to the use of the restrictive particle 'alone' (<s>eva</s>).
Thorns are found only on the stalks of lotuses, while you protect;
or rather, they are also seen in the embraces of passionate couples! || 318 ||

children.text: देव ! त्वयि रक्षति जगतीं पद्मानां [एव] दण्डेषु नालेषु कण्टको दृश्यते, न राज्ये । कण्टकः कार्कश्यलक्षणः, पद्मदण्डेषु राजविपक्षश्चेति श्लिष्टत्वात् । अयं नियम आक्षिप्यते । अथवा कथम् नियम्यते ? यतो रागिणां वा मिथुनानि स्त्रीपुंसयुग्मलक्षणानि तेषामन्योन्यालिङ्गनेष्वपि विषये[षु] कण्टकः रागजनितपुलकरूपो दृश्यते । तत्कथमेवमवधार्यत इति नियमाक्षेपरूपोक्तिरयं श्लेष इति ॥
children.translated_text: O lord! While you protect the world, thorns (<s>kaṇṭaka</s>) are seen only on the stalks, the stems, of lotuses — not in the kingdom. '<s>Kaṇṭaka</s>' in the sense of roughness, and as lotus-stalk thorns and as enemies of the king — thus the punning quality. This restriction is then challenged. Or rather, how can it be restricted? Since thorns in the form of horripilation born of passion are also seen in the embraces of amorous couples (<s>rāgimithunas</s>), in their mutual embracing. How then can this be so definitively asserted? — thus, this <s>śleṣa</s> is an utterance in the form of a challenge to the restriction.
A mountain-bearer, of many ridges, radiant, of fixed rising,
skilled, a lord of creatures, a master, and a wielder of the spear — such was he. || 319 ||

children.text: स विवक्षितः कश्चिन्महीभृत्पर्वतः राजा च, भूरयो महान्तः कटकाः सानवो यस्य पर्वतस्य । भूरिर्विशालः कटकः स्कन्धावारः हस्ताभरणविशेषो वा यस्य स भूरिकटको राजा । तेजस्वी रविः प्रभावविशेषयुक्तश्च नियतः प्रतिदिनमुदयः प्रभावलक्षणो यस्य स नियतोदयो रविः, नियतः स्थिरः उदयो राज्यरूपो यस्य स नियतोदयो राजा । दक्षो नाम प्रजापतिर्विधाता कश्चित् । राजा च दक्षः शूरः प्रजानां लोकानां च
children.translated_text: He, the one intended, is both a mountain (<s>mahībhṛt</s>) and a king: for the mountain, one with many great ridges (<s>kaṭakas</s>), peaks; for the king, one with a vast army-camp (<s>kaṭaka</s>) or a special bracelet. Radiant (<s>tejasvī</s>): the sun; and one endowed with special power. 'Of fixed rising' (<s>niyatodaya</s>): for the sun, one whose rising occurs every day; for the king, one whose ascendancy, in the form of sovereignty, is firm and stable. <s>Dakṣa</s> is the name of a <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures), a creator. And the king too is <s>dakṣa</s> (skilled), and a lord

children.text: पतिः अधिपः स्वामी कार्त्तिकेयः प्रभुश्च, शक्तिः आयुधविशेषः तां धारयतीति शक्तिधरः स्कन्दः । शक्तिमुत्साहमन्त्रप्रभावरूपां धारयतीति शक्तिधरो राजा । आसीदभूत् । अयमविरोधी श्लेषः । महीभृद्भूरिकटकत्वादीनामुभयत्राप्यव्याहतेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: of his subjects and of the people. '<s>Svāmī</s>' (master): <s>Kārtikeya</s> (the divine general); and also a sovereign. '<s>Śaktidhara</s>' (wielder of the spear): <s>Skanda</s>, who bears the spear as his special weapon; and the king who bears <s>śakti</s> (power) in the form of energy, counsel, and authority. He was — he existed. This is a non-contradictory <s>śleṣa</s> (<s>avirodhī</s>), since qualities like being a mountain-bearer, having many ridges, and the like are unobstructed in both meanings.
Though <s>Acyuta</s> (unfallen), yet a destroyer of the bull; though a king, yet one whose decline is unknown;
though a god, yet one without wise men; though <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the auspicious), yet one without serpents — such was he born to be known. || 320 ||

children.text: अच्युतो विष्णुः, न्यायभ्रंशाभावात् । स्थिरश्च । तत्र यदाऽच्युतो विष्णुस्तदा वृषस्य वृषभस्य अरिष्टनाम्नस्तेनोच्छेदाद् अवृषोच्छेदित्वं विरुद्धम् । पक्षान्तरे तु अविरुद्धम्, वृषस्य धर्मस्य राज्ञा अनुच्छेदात् । राजा चन्द्रः, नृपश्च । तत्र चन्द्रस्य अविदितः क्षयोऽनेनेत्यविदितक्षयत्वं विरुद्धम्, दक्षशापेन कृष्णपक्षे क्षीयमाणत्वात् । पक्षान्तरे तु राज्यापचयाभावादव्याघातः । देवो गतिदेवो विबुधः । सम्मतिदेवश्च राजा । तत्र गतिदेवः कथमविबुधः, असुर इति विरुध्यते । सम्मतिदेवस्तु राजा, विबुधाः पण्डिता विगता यतः । न तथा अविबुधः बुधयुक्तः पण्डितमण्डलमण्डितास्थानमण्डपः । शङ्करस्त्रिलोचनः, शान्तिकरश्च । तत्र त्रिनेत्रः फणिधरनद्धजटाजूटः सारसनीकृतनागः कुण्डलीकृतपन्नगः कथमभुजङ्गवान् इति विरोधः । राजा तु धूर्तसंसर्गाभावाद् अभुजङ्गवानिति युज्यते । जज्ञे विदितः क्रियाविदित इति सर्वत्र सम्बन्धनीयम् । अयं विरोधी श्लेष उदाहृतः ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> means <s>Viṣṇu</s>, due to the absence of deviation from righteousness; and also 'steadfast.' When <s>Acyuta</s> means <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then being a destroyer of the bull (<s>Vṛṣa</s>), namely the demon <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, contradicts being '<s>avṛṣocchedi</s>' (non-destroyer of the bull). But in the other meaning, there is no contradiction, since the king does not destroy <s>vṛṣa</s> (righteousness). 'King' (<s>rājan</s>) means both the moon (<s>Candra</s>) and a ruler. For the moon, being '<s>aviditakṣaya</s>' (one whose decline is unknown) is contradictory, since he wanes in the dark fortnight due to the curse of <s>Dakṣa</s>. But in the other meaning, there is no obstruction, since the king's sovereignty does not decline. '<s>Deva</s>' (god) means a celestial being and also a king by convention. For a celestial being, how can he be '<s>avibudha</s>' (without wise ones), since that would make him a demon — this is contradictory. But the king is '<s>avibudha</s>' in the sense of being endowed with learned men (<s>budhas</s>), whose court-pavilion is adorned with a circle of scholars. <s>Śaṅkara</s> means the three-eyed one (<s>Trilocana</s>) and also one who creates peace. For the three-eyed god, whose matted locks are wound with serpent-kings, who has made snakes into earrings, how can he be 'without serpents' (<s>abhujaṅgavān</s>) — this is the contradiction. But the king, due to the absence of association with rogues (<s>dhūrtas</s>), is fittingly without serpents. '<s>Jajñe</s>' (was known) should be connected with all statements as a common verb. This has been illustrated as a contradictory <s>śleṣa</s> (<s>virodhī</s>).
|| Thus ends the section on <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). ||
Revealing <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive expression), he says —
The perception of the absence of qualities, class, action, and the like
for the very purpose of showing a distinction — that is regarded as <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive expression). || 321 ||
