children.text: गुणश्च जातिश्च क्रिया च आदिशब्देन द्रव्यपरिग्रहः । तेषां वैकल्यस्याभावस्य दर्शनं वचनं यत्तत् । किमर्थम् ? विशेषस्यातिशयस्य कस्यचित्कार्यविषयस्य दर्शनाय प्रतिपादनार्थमेव । अत एव विशेषपरत्वात् सा तल्लक्षणा विशेषोक्तिरिष्यते मनीषिभिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: Quality, class, and action — by the word 'and the like,' substance is included. The showing, the stating, of their absence, their deficiency — that is what is meant. For what purpose? For the very purpose of showing, of demonstrating, some distinction, some extraordinary result in the domain of effects. Precisely because of its being directed toward distinction, that figure of such definition is regarded by the wise as <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive expression).
Illustrating that, he says —

children.text: न कठोरं न वा तीक्ष्णमायुधं पुष्पधन्वनः ।
children.translated_text: The weapon of <s>Puṣpadhanus</s> (the flower-bowed god of love) is neither hard nor sharp;
yet the three worlds have been conquered by it. || 322 ||

children.text: पुष्पधन्वनः कामस्यायुधं कुसुम[म]न्यद्वा तादृशं न कठोरं न कठिनम् न च अतितीक्ष्णं न च निशातं यथान्यत्, आयुधमयोमयं तेजितं खड्गादि तथाप्येवमपीति विशेषविवक्षायाम् । यदाह—अमुना पुष्यधन्वना आयुधेन वा भुवनानां स्वर्गादीनां त्रयं कृत्स्नं जगत् जितमाक्रान्तमेव नाजितमपि आसीदभवत् ।
अहो चित्रम् !  इह काठिन्यतैक्ष्ण्यलक्षणस्यायुधत्वेन प्रसिद्धस्य निषेधेनानङ्गास्त्रस्य जगज्जैत्रस्य विशेषः कोऽप्याविष्कृतो जगज्जयकार्यविषयः । तादृशमपीदं जगद्विजयसमर्थमहो यथेदं प्रतिविशिष्टमिति ॥
children.translated_text: How wondrous! Here, by negating what is well-known as constituting weapon-nature — namely hardness and sharpness — some extraordinary distinction of the weapon of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love), the conqueror of the world, has been revealed, a distinction related to the effect of world-conquest. Even such a weapon, which is capable of conquering the world — how supremely distinguished it is!

The weapon of <s>Puṣpadhanus</s> (the flower-bowed one, the god of love) — a flower or something of that kind — is not hard, not rigid; and not very sharp, not honed like other weapons made of iron, such as sharpened swords and the like. Even so — when the intent is to express a distinction — as he says: by this <s>Puṣpadhanus</s>, or by this weapon, the three worlds — heaven and the rest, the entire universe — have been conquered, subdued — not unconquered — they were so.
She is not a celestial maiden, nor born of the <s>Gandharva</s> clan;
yet she is capable of disrupting the penance of even <s>Vedhas</s> (the Creator). || 323 ||

children.text: इयं देवानां कन्यका योषिन्न भवति । सम्भवत्यस्मादिति सम्भवः । गन्धर्वाणां देवविशेषाणां कुलं वंशः सम्भवः, तत्र वा सम्भूतिरस्या इति गन्धर्वकुलसम्भवा न भवति । सा हि स्त्रीजातिरत्यन्ताभिरूपा । तथापि पूर्ववत् विशेषविवक्षायाम् । यदाह—एषा स्त्री या न तज्जातिः । वेधसोऽपि येन सृष्टा, यो वा वीतरागः प्रागेवान्यस्य । तपसो विषयसंयमस्य भङ्गं निवृत्तिं विधातुं कर्तृमलं समर्था । किमिदं रूप चातुर्यम् । इह देवजात्यादे रूपोत्कर्षवत्त्वनिवृत्त्या विशेषः, मानुष्यप्येवंविधा या प्रजापतिमपि रागपरवशं करोतीति दर्शितः ॥
children.translated_text: This woman is not a daughter of the gods, not a divine maiden. '<s>Sambhava</s>' means that from which one is born. The clan, the lineage of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, a special class of celestial beings, is their <s>kula</s>; she is not one born therein — not a <s>gandharvakula-sambhavā</s>. For that female species is of supremely beautiful form. Even so — as before, when the intent is to express a distinction — as he says: this woman, who is not of that class, is capable of disrupting, of destroying, the penance (<s>tapas</s>), the sense-restraint, of even <s>Vedhas</s> (the Creator <s>Brahmā</s>), by whom she was created, or who is already free from passion, let alone anyone else. What manner of beauty and charm is this! Here, by the cessation of belonging to classes such as divine and the like that possess excellence of beauty, the distinction is shown — that even though human, such a woman as this renders even <s>Prajāpati</s> (the lord of creatures) subject to passion.
No brow was knit, no lip quivered,

children.text: न च रक्ताभवद् दृष्टिर्जितं च द्विषतां कुलम् ॥ ३२४ ॥
children.translated_text: no glance turned red — yet the clan of enemies was conquered. || 324 ||

children.text: केनचिद् धीरेण भ्रूकुटिर्भ्रूभङ्गः कोपजन्मा न बद्धा न रचिता । दशनच्छदश्च अधरो न स्फुरितः कोपान्न कम्पि । दृष्टिश्च रक्ता रोषारुणा नाभवत् । तथापि च द्विषतां कुलम् अरिवर्गः जितं भग्नम् । चित्रमेतत् । अत्र भ्रुकुटीबद्धदशनच्छदस्फुरणादेः क्रियाया विगमेन निर्विकाररिपुविजयलक्षणो विशेषो दर्शित इति ॥
children.translated_text: By a certain resolute person: the brow-furrow, the knitting of the brows born of anger, was not formed, was not fashioned. And the lip (<s>daśanacchada</s>) did not quiver, did not tremble with anger. And the glance did not become red, reddened with rage. Yet even so, the clan of enemies, the hostile party, was conquered, defeated. This is extraordinary. Here, by the removal of the action of knitting brows, quivering of lips, and the like, the distinction characterized by conquering enemies without agitation has been shown.

children.text: न रथा न च मातङ्गा न हया न च पत्तयः ।
children.translated_text: No chariots, no elephants, no horses, no foot-soldiers —
yet by the sidelong glance of women alone, the three worlds are conquered. || 325 ||

children.text: रथाः स्यन्दना न सन्ति । न मातङ्गा हस्तिनः सन्ति । न च हया अश्वाः । नापि पत्तयः पदातयः । चतुरङ्गमनीकमिदं जयोपकरणम् । तथापि स्त्रीणामपाङ्गदृष्ट्या कटाक्षेणैव केवलं जगतां त्रयं त्रिभुवनं जीयते वशीक्रियते । अत्र रथादिलक्षणद्रव्याभावेन जगत्त्रयविजयलक्षणो विशेषः स्त्रीकटाक्षस्याविष्कृत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Chariots are not present. No elephants are present. No horses either. Nor foot-soldiers. This is the four-limbed army, the instrument of conquest. Yet even so, by the sidelong glance, the side-look alone, of women, the three worlds, the triple universe, are conquered, brought under control. Here, by the absence of substances such as chariots and the like, the distinction characterized by the conquest of the three worlds by women's sidelong glances has been revealed.
Showing another variety of <s>viśeṣokti</s>, he says —

children.text: एकचक्रो रथो यन्ता विकलो विषमा हयाः ।
children.translated_text: One-wheeled is the chariot, the charioteer is maimed, the horses are mismatched —
yet the radiant sun still conquers the three worlds! || 326 ||

children.text: एकं चक्रमस्येत्येकचक्रो रथः । कथं वहति ? यन्ता सारथिश्चारुणलक्षणः अङ्गविकलः । कथं कर्मण्य ? हया रथ्याश्च विषमाः सप्त । कथं धौरेयाः ? तथाप्यर्कः तेजस्वी प्रतापविशेषयुक्तो यतस्तस्मात् जगतां त्रयमाक्रामत्यभिभवति । तेजस्तत्रनिमित्तमिति ॥
children.translated_text: The chariot has one wheel — thus 'one-wheeled.' How can it carry? The charioteer, characterized as <s>Aruṇa</s>, is maimed in body. How can he be effective? And the horses, the steeds, are mismatched — seven of them. How can they be yoke-worthy? Yet even so, the sun (<s>arka</s>), radiant, endowed with special brilliance, therefore conquers, overwhelms, the three worlds. Radiance is the cause therein.

body.translated_text: What kind of <s>viśeṣokti</s> is this? He says —

children.translated_text: This very one is a <s>viśeṣokti</s> with a cause (<s>hetuviśeṣokti</s>), because of the qualifier 'radiant.'
This very method should be followed in the construction of other varieties as well. || 327 ||

body.text: सैषा अनन्तरोक्ता तादृशी हेतुविशेषोक्तिर्नाम विज्ञायते । कुतः ? तेजस्वीत्यर्क
body.translated_text: This very one just stated, of such a nature, is known as <s>hetuviśeṣokti</s> (distinctive expression with a cause). Why? Because of the qualifier of the sun

body.text: स्य विशेषणाद्धेतुरूपात् । तेजस्वित्वात् जगत्त्रयमाक्रामतीति । इमामवान्तरभेदविकल्पनादिशमतिदिशन्नाह- अयमित्यादि । अयमेवानन्तरोक्तः क्रमो न्यायः हेत्वपेक्षया हेतुविशेषोक्तिरित्येवंजातीयः अन्येषामपि भेदानां विशेषोक्तिविकल्पानां कल्पने प्रयोगेऽनुगन्तव्यः । ते चैवं कल्पनीयाः—
body.translated_text: which is in the form of a cause — 'radiant.' Because of being radiant, he conquers the three worlds. Extending this principle of sub-variety classification, he says: 'this very' and so forth. This very method, the principle stated just now, of the type 'since it is a <s>hetuviśeṣokti</s>' — should be followed, traced, in the construction, the application, of other varieties as well, other sub-types of <s>viśeṣokti</s>. And they are to be constructed thus —

body.text: न विषं विषमं किञ्चिंन्न च पाशोऽस्ति तादृशः ।
body.translated_text: No poison is so potent, no noose is of such kind —
yet the glances of doe-eyed women stupefy and bind the world.

body.text: न शस्त्रं निशितं किञ्चित्तादृशं नापि चामृतम् ।
body.translated_text: No sharp weapon exists of such kind, nor such nectar either —

body.text: स्त्रीणां कोपः प्रसादश्च हन्ति जीवयति क्षणम् ॥
body.translated_text: women's anger and favor slay and revive in an instant.

body.text: न किञ्चिन्मार्दवं तन्वि ! स्तनयोर्न च नम्रता ।
body.translated_text: O slender one! There is no softness in your breasts, nor any bending —
yet even so, this person is exceedingly enamored by them both.
By this method, other varieties too may be inferred.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinctive expression). ||

children.translated_text: Setting forth <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application), he says —
When the mention of someone is made by equating him with things
that are eminent in the desired quality, for the purpose of praise or blame — that is regarded as <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application). || 328 ||

children.text: विवक्षितः प्रतिपादयितुमिष्टः कश्चिद्नुणो धर्मः साधुरसाधुर्वा तेनोत्कृष्टैरधिमात्रैः प्रसिद्धैः कैश्चिद्वस्तुभिः सह समीकृत्य वस्तुतोऽसाम्येऽपि तथाभावमारोप्य कस्यचिदर्थस्य पुरुषादेः कीर्तनमाख्यानम् । किमर्थम् ? स्तुतिः प्रशंसा निन्दा जुगुप्सा चार्थः प्रयोजनं यस्मिन् कीर्तने तत्तथा समीकृतस्य स्तुत्यर्थं निन्दार्थं वा, सा तल्लक्षणा तुल्ययोगिता स्मृता । तेन गुणेन तादृशां तुल्ययोगिताप्रतिपादनात्, तादर्थ्येन तुल्ययोगिता तथाविधोक्तिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: The desired quality — some attribute, whether good or bad, that one wishes to convey — when equating, identifying, with certain things that are eminent, supreme, well-known in that quality, even though there is no real equality — imposing such equivalence; the mention, the description, of some thing, such as a person: for what purpose? Praise, commendation, or blame, reproach, being the purpose of that mention — that figure of such definition is known as <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application). Because it conveys the equal application of those who possess that quality, and being for that purpose, <s>tulyayogitā</s> is an utterance of such a nature.
Illustrating that, he says —
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>), and you as well —
all bear the designation '<s>Lokapāla</s>' (guardian of the world), which pertains to no other domain. || 329 ||

children.text: यमो दक्षिणस्या दिशः पतिः । कुवेर उतरस्याः । [वरुणः पश्चिमायाः] सहस्राक्षः शक्रः प्राच्याः । भवानपि त्वं च । एते[भ्योऽन्ये] नास्या विषयः । इत्यनन्यविषयां लोकपाल इत्येवंरूपां श्रुतिं शब्दं बिभ्रति वहन्ति, सर्वैस्तैर्लोकरक्षणात् । अत्र लोकपालत्वेन विवक्षितेन गुणेन उत्कृष्टैर्यमादिभिः समीकृत्य राज्ञः कस्यचित् कीर्तनस्मृत्यर्थमिति योजनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> is the lord of the southern direction. <s>Kubera</s> of the northern. <s>Varuṇa</s> of the western. The thousand-eyed one, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), of the eastern. And you too. This designation has no other domain — thus the epithet '<s>Lokapāla</s>' (guardian of the world), a title of such form, is borne, carried, by all of them, since all of them protect the world. Here, by equating a certain king with <s>Yama</s> and the others, who are eminent in the desired quality of being guardians of the world, the mention is for the purpose of praise — thus it should be construed.
The unions of doe-eyed women and the flashings of lightning
do not last even two moments, even though they themselves are intensely begun. || 330 ||

children.text: मृगाक्षीणां सङ्गतानि प्रेमाणि त[डि]तां विद्युतां विलसितानि च यथायोगं घनैर्मेघैरारब्धानि घनं निरन्तरमारब्धान्यपि । किं पुनरन्यानि ? स्वयमात्मना प्रकृतिचापल्यात्, न तु कारणवैगुण्येन घनारब्धत्वात् क्षणद्वयमपि द्वाव

पि क्षणौ न तिष्ठन्ति । किं पुनश्चिरम् ? यदि परमेकं क्षणं तिष्ठन्ति । इह विवक्षितेन गुणेन क्षणमात्रास्थायित्वेनोत्कृष्टैः प्रतीतैस्तड़िद्विलसितैः समीकृत्य स्त्रीप्रेम्णामतिचपलतया निन्दार्थं कीर्तनमिति लक्षणं योजनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: even two moments. How much less for a long time? At most, they last for one moment. Here, by equating, through the desired quality of lasting only a moment, the loves of women with the well-known flashings of lightning that are eminent in that quality, the mention is for the purpose of blame, due to the extreme fickleness of women's love — thus the definition should be applied.

The unions, the loves, of doe-eyed women, and the flashings of lightning — each respectively — though begun, initiated, by the clouds, or begun intensely, densely. How much less others? By their own nature, due to their innate fickleness, not through any deficiency of cause, since they are intensely begun — they do not last
|| Thus ends the section on <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application). ||
Demonstrating <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), he says —
Where there is the perception of the conjunction of contradictory entities,
for the very purpose of establishing the contradiction — that is known as <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), as follows: || 331 ||

children.text: विरुद्धानामन्योन्यप्रतिद्रन्द्विनां पदार्थानां क्रियागुणादीनां संसर्गस्य सन्निधेः दर्शनमवगमो यत्रोक्तिप्रकारे । किमर्थम् ? विरोधस्य विप्रतिषेधस्य साधनाय सविशेषं प्रत्यायनार्थमेव । अत एव विरोधप्रधानत्वात् स उक्तिविशेषः विरोध इति स्मृतः कथ्यते कविभिः । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Where in a mode of expression there is the perception, the apprehension, of the conjunction, the proximity, of mutually opposed things — actions, qualities, and the like — that are antagonistic to one another. For what purpose? Solely for the establishment, the particular demonstration, of opposition, of contradiction. Precisely because opposition is predominant, that particular mode of expression is known as <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), declared by poets. He illustrates with 'as follows' —
The cooing of the <s>rājahaṃsas</s> (royal geese), sweet with seasonal joy, increases,
while the cry of the peacocks, having lost its excellence, diminishes. || 332 ||

children.text: अरुणचरणचञ्चवो हंसविशेषा राजहंसाः । तेषां कूजितम् निनदः मदेन सामयिकेन हर्षोत्कर्षेण मञ्जुलं मधुरं वर्धते विजृम्भते । मयूराणां च रुतं कूजितं पुनरुत्क्रान्तमपगतं सौष्ठवमुत्कर्षो यतः, तत् क्षीयते निवर्तते । वृद्धिक्षययोः क्रियापदार्थयोः विरुद्धयोर्मिथः संसर्गस्यैकत्र सन्निधेर्दर्शनमिति लक्षणं योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Rājahaṃsas</s> are a special variety of geese with reddish feet and beaks. Their cooing, their call, sweet and melodious with seasonal excitement, with the peak of delight, increases, expands. And the cry, the call, of the peacocks — from which excellence, distinction, has departed, has gone — that diminishes, ceases. The definition should be applied thus: the perception of the conjunction, the proximity in one place, of the mutually opposed action-categories of increase and decrease. ||
By the rain-clouds of the monsoon, the sky becomes overcast,
while the minds of people, seized by passion, become colored with love. || 333 ||

children.text: जलधरैः प्रावृषि भवैः कारणैः अम्बरमाकाशं दुर्दिनायते भिन्नाङ्गं जायते । जगतां मनः पुनस्तै रेव रागेण रतिभावेनाक्रान्तं विषयीकृतं रक्तं जायते । अत्र दुर्दिनत्वरक्तत्वयोर्विरागरागरूपयोः गुणपदार्थयोः विरोधप्रतिपत्तिरिति लक्षणं योज्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: By the rain-clouds, those born of the monsoon season, as causes, the sky becomes overcast, becomes gloomy. The minds of people, however, seized by passion, by the feeling of love, made their object, become colored, become impassioned, by those very same clouds. Here, the definition should be applied as the perception of the opposition between the quality-categories of gloom and passion, which have the form of dispassion and passion respectively. ||
With slender waist, broad hips, red lips, dark eyes,

children.text: नतनाभि वपुः स्त्रीणां कं न हन्त्युन्नतस्तनम् ॥ ३३४ ॥
children.translated_text: sunken navel, and raised breasts — the body of women, whom does it not slay? || 334 ||

children.text: तनु कृशं मध्यम् । पृथुर्महीयसी श्रोणिः नितम्बो रक्तश्चौष्ठोऽधरः । असितं कृष्णमीक्षणमक्षि । नता निम्ना नाभिः । उन्नतौ स्तनौ यत्र तादृशं स्त्रीणां वपुः शरीरं कं नाम नरं [न] हन्ति चक्षुःप्रीतिमनःसङ्गादिक्रमेण दशमीं दशां कं न नयति ?  सर्वमेतादृशं जनं हन्ति । अत्र तनुमध्यपृथुश्रोणिप्रभृतीनां शरीरावयवद्रव्याणां परस्परविरोधिनां संसर्गदर्शनमिति लक्षणं योजनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Slender, thin is the waist. Broad, expansive is the hip, the buttock. Red is the lip, the lower lip. Dark, black is the eye, the glance. Sunken, depressed is the navel. Raised are the breasts — such a body of women, what man does it not slay? Through the sequence of visual delight, mental attachment, and so forth, to whom does it not bring the tenth state [of love's consummation]? It slays every such person. Here, the definition should be applied as the perception of the conjunction of the mutually contradictory bodily part-substances such as slender waist, broad hips, and the like. ||
With arms like lotus stalks, thighs like plantain stems, face like a lotus, eyes like water-lilies —

children.text: अपि ते रूपमस्माकं तन्वि ! तापाय कल्पते ॥ ३३५ ॥
children.translated_text: even such a form of yours, O slender one, serves to cause us burning! || 335 ||

children.text: मृणालवद्बाहू रम्भा कदली तद्वदूरू पद्ममिव मुखमुत्पलवदीक्षणे यत्र तत्तादृशमत्यन्तशीतवस्तुसरूपमपि रूपं ते तव सम्बन्धि तन्वि ! तापाय तप्त्यर्थमस्माकं कल्पते
भवति । किमिदं विरुद्धम् ? अत्र शीतगुणस्य तद्वतो वा द्रव्यस्य बाहुप्रभृतेः तत्समुदायस्य वा रूपस्य शरीरद्रव्यस्य तापेनोष्णताकारिकर्मणा सह विरोध इति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: to cause us burning. What is this contradiction? Here, the contradiction should be seen between the substance of the arms and the like, possessing the quality of coldness, or of the aggregate of such substances, that is, the bodily form, and the action of burning, which produces the effect of heat. ||

Arms like lotus stalks (<s>mṛṇāla</s>); thighs like plantain (<s>rambhā</s>, banana) stems; a face like a lotus; eyes like water-lilies (<s>utpala</s>) — even though such a form of yours, O slender one, resembles exceedingly cool substances, it serves
The pollen of mango and <s>campaka</s> (magnolia) trees, stirred up by garden breezes,
makes the eyes of travelers weep, even without touching them. || 336 ||

children.text: उद्यानेषु मारुतैरुद्धूताश्चूतानां चम्पकानां च रेणवः पौष्पाः परागाः । पान्थानां विरहिणां लोचनमस्पृशन्तोऽपि दूर एव दृश्यमाना उदश्रयन्ति । उदस्रवन्तीत्यपि पठ्यते । उभयत्रापि रोदयन्तीत्यर्थः । तच्च विरुद्धम् । स्पृशतामेव रेणूनां नयनजलोद्गमनिमित्तत्वात् । कथमस्पृशन्त उदश्रयन्ति ? अत्र स्पर्शनिषेधोदश्रयणयोः क्रिययोर्विरोध इति द्रष्टव्यम् । कूजितमित्यादेः [
children.translated_text: In the gardens, stirred up by breezes, the pollen, the flower-dust, of mango and <s>campaka</s> (magnolia) trees — of travelers, those in separation — even without touching their eyes, merely being seen from a distance, makes them weep. Some read '<s>udasravanti</s>' (make them shed tears) as well. In both readings, the meaning is 'makes them weep.' And that is contradictory, since only pollen that touches causes tears to flow. How can they, without touching, make the eyes weep? Here, the contradiction should be seen between the two actions of 'not touching' and 'making weep.' What is the difference between the verse beginning with 'The cooing' [

children.text: ] अस्य च को विशेषः । उभयत्रापि क्रियाविरोधात् । तत्र भिन्नाधिकरणयोः क्रिययोर्विरोधः । इह त्वभिन्नाधिकरण्योरिति महान् विशेषः । अन्यत्राप्येवंप्रकारत्वाद्विशेषस्थितेरिति ॥
children.translated_text: ] and this one, since in both there is a contradiction of actions? There, the contradiction is between actions in different substrates. Here, however, the actions are in the same substrate — this is a great difference. In other cases too, the difference is established by such variations in manner. ||
Your gaze, though devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, yet reaching the ear (<s>Karṇa</s>) —
in whom does it inspire trust, O sweet-spoken one? || 337 ||

children.text: कलभाषिणि ! ते दृष्टिः कस्य नाम विश्वसनीयत्वम् विस्रब्धतां याति ? न कस्यचित् । कुतः ? यतः कृष्णे नारायणे कृष्णायां द्रौपद्यां वा अर्जुने धनञ्जये चानुरक्ता सती कर्णं तद्विपक्षमङ्गराजमवलम्बते भजते, तस्माद्विरुद्धपक्षपातिनी कथमियं विश्वास्वा खलेति शब्दच्छलेन विरोधः प्रतीयते । वस्तुतस्तु दृष्टिः कृष्णा श्यामा क्वचिदर्जुना धवला अनुरक्ता ताम्रा च स्निग्धा वा कर्णं च श्रुतिपथमायातत्वादवलम्बत इत्यविरोधः । श्लेषानुविद्धोऽयमीदृशो विरोधः प्रतिपत्तव्य इति ॥
children.translated_text: O sweet-spoken one! Your gaze — for whom does it attain trustworthiness, reliability? For no one. Why? Because, being devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that is, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, or to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), and to <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>, it yet reaches <s>Karṇa</s>, their adversary, the king of <s>Aṅga</s>. Therefore, since it favors the opposing side, how can this be trusted? She is treacherous! — thus the contradiction is perceived through the device of verbal ambiguity (<s>śleṣa</s>). In reality, however, the gaze (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is dark (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>, black) in one place and white (<s>arjunā</s>, fair) in another, and is devoted, reddish, or affectionate; and it reaches the ear (<s>karṇa</s>), since it extends to the path of hearing — thus there is no contradiction. This type of <s>virodha</s>, pervaded by <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), should be understood as being of such a kind. ||
He summarizes <s>virodha</s> —
Thus this ornament extends in many varieties.

children.text: इति कथितेन क्रमेणायं विरोधोऽलङ्कारोऽनेको विचित्रः प्रकारो विकल्पोऽस्येति अनेकप्रकारः प्रतायते प्रसरति प्रतीयते लक्ष्यते वा ।
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner described, this ornament of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), having many, varied types, varieties — is of many varieties; it extends, spreads, is perceived, or is discerned.
Though dual, she is non-dual; though upward-facing, her face is bowed;
though hard, it is soft to the touch — such is the weight of the breasts of doe-eyed women. || Thus.
Another type too is illustrated —
|| Thus ends the section on <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). ||
Showing <s>aprastutastotra</s> (praise of the irrelevant), he says —
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is praise that is directed at what has not been introduced. || 338 ||

children.text: अप्रक्रान्ते तु अप्रकृत एव बहिस्तत्त्वेन कस्मिंश्चिद्वस्तुनि बुद्धिस्थे विषये या स्तुतिः संराधनमित्यनूद्य सा अप्रस्तुतप्रशंसा स्यादिति विधीयते, यदुद्देशेऽप्रस्तुतस्तोत्रमुक्तम् । अप्रक्रान्तेप्सितस्तुतिरिति पाठेऽप्रक्रान्तस्येप्सितस्येष्टस्य वस्तुनः कस्यचिदप्रक्रान्ता वा तद्विषयत्वात् । स्तुतिरिति
children.translated_text: Praise, that is, laudation, directed at what has not been introduced, that is, at what is not the current subject, at some object that is external in its essence yet present in the mind — such, having been stated, is ordained as <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, which was designated as <s>aprastutastotra</s> (praise of the irrelevant) in the summary. In the reading '<s>aprakrāntepsitastutiḥ</s>' — it is praise of some desired object that has not been introduced, or praise that is itself not introduced, because it pertains to that subject.
The rest is to be explained in the same manner. ||
Illustrating that, he says —
Happily live the deer in the forests, serving no other,
with water easily obtained without effort, with grass, <s>darbha</s> shoots, and the like. || 339 ||

children.text: जलैर्दर्भाङ्कुरैस्तृणोद्गमैः । आदिशब्देन तरुपल्लवादिभिरर्थैरुपकरणैर्वा अयत्नेन सेवापरिक्लेशादि[राहित्येन] सुलभैः [सुख]प्राप्यैरकृच्छ्राधिगतैरमृतायमानैरपरमन्यं कञ्चिदसेवमानाः परचित्ताराधनदुःखानभिज्ञाः स्वाधीनवृत्तयः सुखं निराकुलं [हरिणाः] वनेषु जीवन्ति । अपि नाम तादृशी वृत्तिरस्माकमपि स्यात् ? प्रतिपक्षपातः खलु प्रजायते । तादृशीं कल्याणीं वृत्तिं कल्पयतो हरिणेषु ईर्ष्या लक्ष्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: With water, with <s>darbha</s> shoots, with sproutings of grass — by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), with things such as tree-leaves and the like as resources — easily obtained without effort, without the hardship of service and the like, obtained without difficulty, as if they were nectar; serving no other, ignorant of the suffering of pleasing another's mind, living by their own free will — the deer live happily, free from disturbance, in the forests. 'If only such a livelihood were ours too!' — thus a contrasting sentiment is born. The jealousy toward the deer is discernible in one who imagines such a blessed livelihood. ||
It is this very irrelevant life of the deer that is praised here,
by a proud person who is weary of the hardship of attending upon a king. || 340 ||

children.text: सेयमनन्तरोक्ता मृगाणां वृत्तिरयत्नसुलभजलदर्भाङ्कुररूपा जीविका, वर्तन्ते जीवन्त्यनयेति कृत्वा । अप्रस्तुता अप्रक्रान्तैव, न प्रस्तुतापि तादृशप्रकरणाभावात् । प्रशस्यते संराध्यते अत्र प्रयोगे केनचिद् राज्ञोऽनुवर्तनम् सेवा तदेव क्लेशः दुःखरूपत्वात् । ततो निर्विण्णेनातिविरक्तेन मनस्विनोदात्तेन केनचित्ततोऽप्रस्तुतापीयमीदृग्विषया [स्तुतिः] काव्यशोभाकरत्वादलङ्कारः । अयमपरोऽत्र उदाह्नियते—

children.translated_text: Happy are those great souls who are pervaded by contentment,
free from possessions, from the hardships that are mere semblances of happiness. ||
Thus, in this manner, through what is not the current subject, renunciation is praised,
by one who is under the sway of weariness from the hardship of earning wealth and the like. ||

children.text: समासोक्तेरियं कथं भेद्यते, उभयत्राप्यन्यदभिप्रेत्यावान्तराभिधानात् ? तत्र सदृशम एवार्थान्तरमभिधीयते । इह तु विसदृशमिति महान् भेदः । विसदृशात् कथमर्थान्तर-
children.translated_text: How is this distinguished from <s>samāsoktī</s> (condensed expression), since in both cases something else is stated while intending another meaning? There, only a similar other meaning is expressed. Here, however, a dissimilar one — this is the great difference. If one asks: how can the understanding of another meaning arise from what is dissimilar?
Then: how does it arise even from what is similar? If one says 'from the context, the subject matter, and so forth' —

children.text: तुल संयोगो विप्रयोगश्च साहचर्यं विरोधिता । अर्थः प्रकरणं लिङ्गं शब्दस्यान्यस्य सन्निधिः ॥ सामर्थ्यमौचिती देशः कालो व्यक्तिः स्वरादयः । शब्दार्थस्यानवच्छेदे विशेषस्मृतिहेतवः ॥ —वाक्यपदीये
चेदिहाप्येवमस्तु । तत्र तादृशी प्रतीतिरिहेदृशीति न किञ्चिद्विरुध्यते । अन्ये त्विह प्रशस्यमेवाभिधीयते । तत्र तु निन्द्यमपीति विशेषं व्याचक्षते । तथैकान्तिको भेदोऽनयोर्निदशितः स्यादिति ॥
children.translated_text: then let it be so here as well. There the understanding is of such a kind; here it is of a different kind — there is no contradiction whatsoever. Others, however, explain the distinction thus: here only what is praiseworthy is stated, whereas there even what is blameworthy may be — thus a definitive difference between the two has been shown. ||

This, the livelihood of the deer as just described — the means of living characterized by water, <s>darbha</s> shoots, and the like, easily obtained without effort — they live, they subsist, by means of this. Though irrelevant, not introduced as the current subject, not being the topic at hand since there is no such context — it is praised, lauded, here in this composition, by some proud, noble person who is weary, deeply disenchanted, with the attendance upon a king, the service which is itself hardship due to its painful nature. Thus, although irrelevant, this praise directed at such a subject is an ornament, because it enhances poetic beauty. Here is another illustration —
|| Thus ends <s>aprastutastotra</s> (praise of the irrelevant). ||
Taking up <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), he says —
If one praises while appearing to blame, that is considered <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise);

children.text: दोषाभासा गुणा एव लभन्ते ह्यत्र सन्निधिम् ॥ ३४१ ॥
children.translated_text: for here only apparent faults, which are actually virtues, find their place. || 341 ||

children.text: निन्दन्निव दोषमाचक्षाण इव स्तौति गुणं भाषते यदि चेत्, असावेवंलक्षणा व्याजस्तुतिर्मता इष्टा । कथमत्र गुणाः प्रतीयन्ते ? यतस्तुतिरियं गुणाविष्क्रियालक्षणा स्यादिति ब्रवीति । हिर्यस्मादर्थे । यदत्रोक्तिविशेषे दोषवदाभासन्ते प्रतिभान्ति तादृशपदोपादानादेर्दोषाभासा गुणा एव शौर्यादयो न दोषोऽपि कश्चित् । अत एव लेश
स्तुतेरियं भिद्यते । तत्र हि दोषे गुणः कश्चिदेव प्रती[य]ते । यदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: (trace) is distinguished from this form of praise. For there, some virtue is perceived amidst a fault. As it was said —
'An apparent fault is actually some merit: his skill in flattery has been shown.'

children.text: इति । सन्निधिमवस्थानं लभन्ते प्रतीयन्त इति यावत् । अत्र व्याजस्तुतौ । ततः स्तुतिरेवेयम् सर्वथा [न] निन्दा काचिदपीति
children.translated_text: Thus they find their place, their standing — that is, they are perceived — here in <s>vyājastuti</s>. Therefore this is praise entirely, [not] any blame whatsoever —

If one who appears to be stating faults, who seems to be declaring defects, actually praises, states virtues — if so, such is the definition of <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), which is approved. How are virtues perceived here? Since this is praise, characterized by the revelation of merits — thus he explains. The word '<s>hi</s>' means 'because.' That which in this particular mode of expression appears as if it were faults, seems so due to the use of such words and the like — these apparent faults are actually virtues alone, such as valor and the like, not any fault whatsoever. Precisely for this reason, <s>leśa</s>
Illustrating that, he says —
Even by <s>Rāma</s>, a mere ascetic, was this earth conquered;

children.text: त्वया राज्ञापि सैवेयं जिता मा भून्मदस्तव ॥ ३४२ ॥
children.translated_text: and by you, a king, this very same [earth] has been conquered — let there be no pride in you! || 342 ||

children.text: रामेण दाशरथिना भार्गवेण वा तापसेन चतुरङ्गबलहीनेन तपस्विनापि । अ[नादरं] सूचयत्यपिशब्दः । कथञ्चिदनुगृहीतमुनिरूपेण जन्मान्तरोपात्ततपःप्रभावयोगाद्वा । तापसेनेति श्लिष्टम् । अत्र एवेयं श्लेषानुगतैव प्रवर्तते । यद्वक्ष्यतिइति श्लेषानुविद्धानामित्यादि
children.translated_text: By <s>Rāma</s> — either the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> or <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) — even though a mere ascetic, lacking a four-fold army, a renunciant. The word '<s>api</s>' (even) suggests contempt. Having somehow been favored by an ascetic form, through the power of austerities acquired in previous births, or through such association. The word '<s>tāpasena</s>' is used with double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>). Here, this very <s>vyājastuti</s> operates pervaded by <s>śleṣa</s>. As he will state: 'thus of those pervaded by <s>śleṣa</s>' and so forth —

children.text: । इयं भूतधारिणी पृथिवी जिता आक्रान्ता । त्वया तु चतुरङ्गबलपरिवारिणा राज्ञा नराविपेनापि सता । नातःपरमिहाधिकं पदम् अस्तीत्यपिशब्देन सूचयति । सैवेयं जिता तापसेन जिता एव । नान्या तदहमजयं पृथिवीमिति मदोऽहङ्कारस्तव मा भूत् । कोऽत्र विशेष इति चेत्-निन्दनेन च । महानुभावेन जितसमस्तमहीमण्डलेन सकलनरेन्द्रचूड़ामणिना गुणारामेण रामेण समीकृत्य परया स्तुत्या संयोजितो राजा कश्चिदिति व्याजस्तुतिरीदृशी सुतरां रमणीयेति ॥
children.translated_text: This earth, the bearer of beings, was conquered, was subdued. But by you, even though a king, an overlord, surrounded by a four-fold army. The word '<s>api</s>' suggests 'there is no higher station than this.' This very same earth was conquered — the very one conquered by the ascetic. Not some other. Therefore let there be no pride, no arrogance, in you that 'I have conquered the earth.' What is the distinction here, one may ask — it lies in the implicit censure and praise. A certain king has been joined with the highest praise by being equated with the great-souled <s>Rāma</s>, conqueror of the entire earth, the crest-jewel of all sovereigns, the garden of virtues — thus is <s>vyājastuti</s> of this kind supremely delightful. ||
<s>Śrī</s> (prosperity/the goddess) is enjoyed by you, having been snatched from an ancient man;
O king, does this befit you, a descendant of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage? || 343 ||

children.text: पुराणाज्जीर्णादकिंञ्चित्करात् पुंसः पुरुषात् कुतश्चित्, पुराणाच्च पुंसो विष्णोरिति श्लिष्टम् । आच्छिद्यावहृत्य श्रीरभ्युदयो राज्यश्रीश्च देवतेति श्लिष्टम् । त्वया परिभुज्यते निषेव्यते । तदिदमीदृशं कर्म परदाराच्छेदरूपं तवेक्ष्वाकुवंश्यस्य तद्भवस्य मनुकुलजन्मनः । इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्त्येत्यपि पठ्यते । तत्रेक्ष्वाकूणां ते वा वंशोऽस्येत्यन्यपदार्थः । यदुपज्ञेयं वर्णाश्रमाचारस्थितिलक्षणा लोकयात्रा प्रवर्तते । किं युज्यते ? नैवेदं युक्तं तवेदृशवंशसम्भवस्येत्यर्थः । राजन्नित्यामन्त्र्यते । इह पुराणादकिञ्चित्करात्पुंसः श्रीः सम्पत् आच्छिद्यते इति निन्द्यत एव । पुराणात् पुंसो विष्णोः श्रीः विभूतिर्देवतेति च श्लिष्टा । आच्छिद्यते । तामपि पुरुषोत्तमा[दा]क्रम्याकृष्यत इति वीर्योत्कर्षाविष्कृतेः स्तूयत एव कश्चिन्नृपतिः । तदियं सर्वथा श्लेषमुपजीवतीति ॥
children.translated_text: From an ancient, decrepit, worthless man, from some person — and from the ancient Man (<s>Puruṣa</s>), that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>). Having snatched, having seized, <s>Śrī</s> — prosperity, royal fortune, and also the goddess (<s>Śrī</s>) — this is the double meaning. It is enjoyed, is served, by you. This action of such a kind, resembling the seizure of another's wife, befits you, a descendant of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, born of the family of <s>Manu</s>? Some read '<s>Ikṣvākuvaṃśya</s>' as well, where the meaning is 'one whose lineage belongs to the <s>Ikṣvākus</s>' or 'your lineage.' From whose founding the conduct of the world, characterized by the observance of <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage) duties, proceeds. Does it befit? This is indeed not fitting for one born of such a lineage — that is the meaning. He is addressed as 'O king.' Here, that <s>Śrī</s>, wealth, is snatched from an ancient, worthless man — this is indeed being blamed. But from the ancient Man, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, the divine glory — this is the double meaning. It is snatched — that too is seized, drawn from the supreme being — and since this reveals the excellence of valor, a certain king is actually being praised. Thus this entirely depends on <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). ||
Your wife, the earth, is entwined with the coils of a serpent;
whence does your pride ascend to the highest peak? || 344 ||

children.text: कलत्रमिव कलत्रं मेदिनी, पालनादिना । मेदिनी पृथिवी जघन्यजातीया च स्त्री । भुजङ्गशब्देनात्र श्लेषः, फणधरो धूर्तश्च विवक्षित इति श्लिष्टम् । तस्य भोगः यथाक्रमं कामः संभोगश्चेति पुनः श्लिष्टम् । तत्र संसक्ता व्यवस्थिता तेन सा ध्रियते इति श्रुतेः । निरता चेत्युभयत्र योज्यम् । यत एवं तत् कुतः
children.translated_text: like a wife, the earth is your consort, through protection and the like. The earth — both the ground and a woman of low birth. By the word '<s>bhujaṅga</s>' (serpent) there is double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>) here: both the hooded serpent and a rogue are intended. His '<s>bhoga</s>' — enjoyment and the serpent's coil respectively — this is again a double meaning. She is attached to, established in, that; she is sustained by him — as the scripture says. And she is devoted — this should be applied in both senses. Since it is thus,

children.text: कस्मादुत्कर्षादहंकारः अहमत्राधिक इत्यभिमानः तव परां कोटिमधिमात्रतामारोहति ?  न युक्तमित्यमहङ्कर्तुं तवेति । निन्देव स्तुतिरियमखिलमहीतलाधि[पत्य]वर्णनलक्षणा अत्र लक्ष्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: whence, from what exalted position, does your pride — the conceit 'I am superior here' — ascend to the highest peak, to the utmost degree? It is not fitting — you should not be so proud. This is indeed censure-like praise, characterized by the description of sovereignty over the entire earth, that is discernible here. ||
Your wife —

children.text: अपरे अप्येवं श्लेषानुगता विकल्पा द्रष्टव्या इति निगमयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Concluding that other varieties following <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) should likewise be observed, he says —
Thus, of those interwoven with <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) and of others too, let it be observed
that the varieties of <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) are of limitless expanse. || 345 ||

children.text: इति कथितेन पथा श्लेषेणोक्त[रू]पेणानुविद्धानां युक्तानां व्याजस्तुतेः प्रकाराणां विकल्पानामन्येषां च शेषाणामपि प्रविस्तरः प्रपञ्चोऽपर्यन्तः अपरिमितः प्रयोगेषु लक्ष्यतां द्रष्टव्यः । इह तु दिङ्मात्रं दर्शितम् । विकल्पाः केचिदपरे निदर्श्यन्ते—

children.translated_text: The serpent supports the entire earth though fallen from his own station;
O king, having obtained sovereignty, what do you pride yourself on?
This world's minds have been captivated by you through the power of illusion;
resounding with your fame, following the deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — what do you seek to remedy?
The ear holds a blue lotus playfully, O doe-eyed one;

children.text: विक्रमेण भवानेतन्महता किं तव स्मयः ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: you, sir, do this with great effort — what is your pride in that? — Thus.

Thus, by the path described, the full expanse, the elaboration, of the varieties of <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) — those interwoven with, connected to, <s>śleṣa</s> (punning) in the form described, and of the remaining others as well — is limitless, immeasurable; it should be observed in actual usages. Here, however, only a mere indication has been shown. Some further additional varieties are illustrated —
|| Thus ends the section on <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise). ||
Introducing <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification), he says —
If, by something engaged in another matter, some result similar to that
is exemplified, whether good or bad — that would be <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification). || 346 ||

children.text: अर्थान्तरे निदर्श्यापेक्षया अन्यस्मिन् क्वचिदुचिते कार्ये प्रवृत्तेन तत्साधयता केनचिद्वस्तुना हेतुभूतेन कर्तृभूतेन तेनार्थान्तरेण सदृशं तुल्यं फलं किञ्चित् सदिष्टमसद् अनिष्टं वा निदर्श्येत प्रतिपाद्येत यदि, तदेवंलक्षणं निदर्शनं स्यादिति विधीयते । अर्थान्तरस्य वृत्तेनेत्यपि पाठः । तत्रार्थान्तरस्य कस्याचिद्वृत्तेन कर्मणा सदृशमिति व्याख्येयम् । शेषं समानम् ॥
children.translated_text: By something, some entity that serves as a cause or agent, engaged in another matter — another appropriate activity relative to what is to be exemplified — if some result, good (desirable) or bad (undesirable), similar, equal to that, is exemplified, is demonstrated — then that, having such a definition, is prescribed as <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification). There is also the reading '<s>arthāntarasya vṛttena</s>' — in which case it should be explained: similar to the action, the deed, of some other matter. The rest is the same.
Illustrating, he says —
The sun, even as it rises, bestows splendor upon the lotuses,
demonstrating that the fruit of prosperity is the benefiting of friends. || 347 ||

children.text: सविता रविरुदयन्नेवोदयमासादयन्नेव पद्मेषु श्रियं विकाशरूपामर्पयति निधत्ते । उदयपूर्वकेण पद्मविकाशेनार्थान्तरेण सदृशं फलं निदर्शयति-सुहृदामाश्रितान मनुग्रहमुपकारं नाम फल
कार्यमृद्धीनामभ्युदयानां विभावयितुं दर्शयितुमिति सत्फलमिदं निदर्शितं सुहृदनुग्रहम्याभीक्ष्णत्वादि[ति] ॥
children.translated_text: the effect of prosperity, of success — to demonstrate, to show it. Thus this good result — the benefiting of friends — has been exemplified, because of its constant recurrence.

The sun (<s>Savitā</s>), even as it rises, even as it reaches its rising — bestows, places upon the lotuses the splendor in the form of blooming. Through the other matter of the lotus-blooming preceded by the sunrise, it exemplifies a similar result: the benefiting, the helping of friends and dependents — this is the fruit,
Showing an exemplification with a bad result, he says —
Touched by the rays of the moon, the host of darkness meets its destruction,
indicating the dire end of those who oppose the king. || 348 ||

children.text: चन्द्रस्यांशुभिः स्पृष्टा भिन्ना ध्वान्तस्य तमसो राजिः संघातः पराभवं निधनं याति पराभूयत इति यावत् । सद्यस्तत्क्षणम् । किं कुर्वती ? राजा चन्द्रो नृपतिश्चेति श्लिष्टम् । तेन विरुद्धानां केषाञ्चित् दुष्टो विपद्रूपोऽ[न्तोऽ]वसानं यस्य तद्भावस्तत्ताम् अनर्थनिष्ठतां सूचयन्तीति । राजविरोधहेतुकमसत्फलमेतद् दर्शितम् पराभवस्यानिष्टत्वात् ॥
children.translated_text: Touched, pierced by the rays of the moon, the host, the mass of darkness, meets its destruction, its ruin — that is, it is overcome. Instantly, at that very moment. What does it do? '<s>Rāja</s>' means both the moon and the king — this is a <s>śleṣa</s> (pun). By him, of certain adversaries, the dire, calamitous end, the conclusion characterized by misfortune, its state of culminating in disaster — is indicated. The bad result caused by opposing the king has been shown, since destruction is undesirable.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification). ||
Setting forth <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) and <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), he says —
<s>Sahokti</s> (co-expression) is the statement of the co-existence of qualities and actions;

children.text: अर्थानां यो विनिमयः परिवृत्तिस्तु सा यथा ॥ ३४९ ॥
children.translated_text: the mutual exchange of meanings is <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) — as follows. || 349 ||

children.text: गुणानां कर्मणां च सम्बन्धिनः सहभावस्य युगपत् सत्तायाः कथनं प्रतिपादनं यदित्यनूद्य सहोक्तिः सा विज्ञेयेति विधीयते । अर्थानां गुणक्रियादीनां विनिमयो व्यत्ययः इत्यनूद्य परिवृत्तिविधीयते । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: The statement, the presentation, of the co-existence, the simultaneous occurrence, of qualities and actions that are related — having been referred to thus, <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) is prescribed, should be known. The exchange, the transposition, of meanings — qualities, actions, and the like — having been referred to thus, <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is prescribed. He illustrates with 'as follows.'

children.text: सह दीर्घा मम श्वासैरिमाः संप्रति रात्रयः ।
children.translated_text: Long now are these nights along with my sighs,
and pale, together with my own limbs, are those moon-adorned nights. || 350 ||

children.text: संप्रति विरहातुरस्य मम श्वासैर्निश्वसितैः सह दीर्घा आयता इमा रात्रयो वर्तन्ते । ममैवाङ्गैरवयवैर्विरहविधुरैः सह पाण्डुराश्चन्द्रो भूषणमासामिति चन्द्रभूषणाः । पाण्डुरत्वे निमित्तमिदमुक्तम् । अत्र दै[र्घ्य]स्य पाण्डुरत्वस्य चोभयसम्बन्धिनः सहभाव उक्तः । निश्वासा रात्रयश्च दीर्घा अङ्गानि रात्रयश्च पाण्डुरा युगपद्भवन्तीति ॥
children.translated_text: Now, for me who is tormented by separation — together with my sighs, my exhalations — these nights are long, extended. Together with my own limbs, my body-parts that are distressed by separation — pale. The moon is their ornament, hence 'moon-adorned.' This states the reason for their paleness. Here, the co-existence of length and paleness, belonging to both, has been stated. The sighs and the nights are both long; the limbs and the nights are both pale — simultaneously.
The mango blossom increases along with the swooning of travelers,
and the <s>Malaya</s> breezes fall along with their life-breaths. || 351 ||

children.text: पान्थानां वियोगिनां मूर्च्छया मोहनतया सह[चूतस्य] मञ्जरी सहकारकलिका वर्धते । तेषां पान्थानामसुभिः प्राणैः समं सह मलयानिलाः दक्षिणमरुतः पतन्ति च । अत्र वर्धनयोः पतनयोश्च उभयाधारयोः क्रिययोः सहभावोऽमिहितः । सहजचित्रहेतुगर्भा चेयं सहोक्तिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: Along with the swooning, the stupefying power, of the travelers, those in separation — the blossom, the bud of the mango tree (<s>sahakāra</s>), increases, grows. Along with the life-breaths of those travelers, the <s>Malaya</s> breezes, the southern winds, fall. Here, the co-existence of two actions — increasing and falling — that have a dual basis, has been expressed. And this <s>sahokti</s> has an inherent naturally charming cause.
Charming with the songs of cuckoos, with fragrant forest breezes,
the days of spring increase along with the joys of people. || 352 ||

children.text: कोकिलानामालापैः सुभगा मनोहराः सुगन्धयो वनवायवो येषामिति सुगन्धिवनवायवः सुरभेर्वसन्तस्य वासरा दिवसा जनानामानन्दैः प्रीतिभिः सार्धं सह वृद्धिं यान्ति । वर्धन्त इति यावत् । अत्रोभयाधिकरणयोर्वर्धनक्रिययोः सहभावो दर्शितः । इयमभिन्न[क्रिया] । क्रियान्तरात्तु भिन्नक्रिया इत्यनयोर्भेदः प्रतिपत्तव्य इति ॥
children.translated_text: Charming through the songs of cuckoos; having fragrant forest breezes — such are the days of spring (<s>surabhi</s>), which increase, grow, along with the joys, the delights, of people. That is, they both grow. Here, the co-existence of the action of increasing, having a dual substrate, has been shown. This one involves identical action. The difference from one involving different actions should be understood — this is the distinction between the two.
He concludes <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression) —
Thus some examples of <s>sahokti</s> have been given here.

children.text: सहोक्तेरुदाहृतयः प्रयोगाः काश्चन कतिपये न सर्वा, दत्ता दर्शिताः अत्र शास्त्रे । शेषाः प्रयोगाः सुलक्षणीयाः ॥
children.translated_text: some few, not all, examples, usages, of <s>sahokti</s> have been given, shown, here in this treatise. The remaining usages are easily identifiable.
By the method stated,
|| Thus ends the section on <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression). ||
Illustrating <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), he says —
And of <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) too, a brief delineation of its nature is made. || 353 ||

children.text: संप्रति परिवृत्तेश्च परिवृत्तेरपि रूपस्य निरूपणं किञ्चित् संक्षिप्तं क्रियत इति ॥
children.translated_text: Now, of <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) too, a brief, concise delineation of its nature is made.
By your arm that deals weapon-blows to the kings,
their fame, white as the <s>kumuda</s> lotus, long accumulated, has been seized. || 354 ||

children.text: तव भुजेन भुजगराजभोगायमानेन शस्त्रैः कृपाणादिभिः प्रहारं ददता प्रयच्छता भूभुजां राज्ञाम् । पूजानुग्रहनिन्दा[घात]दानस्य दानत्वाभावात् न चतुर्थी । चिरं दीर्घमर्जितं सञ्चितं कुमुदवत् पाण्डुरं यशस्तेषां भूभुजां सम्बन्धि हृतं गृहीतम् । अत्र प्रहारेण कर्मणा यशोरूपो गुणो विनिर्मितः । इतीदृशी परिवृत्तिरनुगन्तव्या ।
children.translated_text: By your arm, extending like the body of the king of serpents, dealing, delivering, blows with weapons such as swords and the like — to the kings. Since giving in the sense of worship, favor, blame, or physical blow does not take the dative case [here, it means striking]. Their long-accumulated, amassed fame, white like the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus), belonging to those kings, has been seized, taken. Here, through the action of striking, the quality in the form of fame has been exchanged. Thus such a <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) should be followed.
The complete delight of the world, and the composure even of the wise,
doe-eyed women seize by a mere sidelong glance, casting it away.
This is another example.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange). ||
Revealing <s>āśīs</s> (benediction), he says —
<s>Āśīs</s> (benediction) is the prayer for a desired object, as follows:
May the supreme light, beyond the reach of speech and mind, protect you. || 355 ||

children.text: अभिलषिते वाञ्छिते वस्तुनि क्वचित् क्रियाविशेषे आशंसनं प्रार्थनमित्यनूद्य आशीर्नाम विज्ञायत इति विधीयते । यथेत्युदाहरति— परमं पारमार्थिकं सकलकल्पनामलविकलं ज्योतिः संवेदनं सर्वपदार्थतत्त्वप्रकाशकत्वात् वाचो मनसश्चाविकल्पत्वात् न गोचरो न विषय इत्यवाङ्मनसगोचरः । अवाङ्मनसगोचरमित्यपि पठ्यते । तत्र न विद्यते वाङ्मनसयोर्गोचरो विषयभावो ग्राहकत्वमस्येति व्याख्येयम् । वो युष्मान् पातु रक्षतु । अत्राभिलषितं रक्षणमाशस्यत इति ।
children.translated_text: In the desired, wished-for object, some particular action — the prayer, the entreaty for it — having been referred to thus, is prescribed to be known as <s>āśīs</s> (benediction). He illustrates with 'as follows': May the supreme, ultimate, free from the taint of all conceptual construction, light — awareness, because of its illuminating the reality of all objects — which is not the domain of speech and mind, because of its being beyond conceptual construction — that is, beyond the reach of speech and mind — protect you. There is also the reading '<s>avāṅmanasagocaram</s>,' in which case it should be explained: that in which the domain, the object-nature, the capacity for grasping, of speech and mind does not exist. Protect you — here, the desired thing, protection, is prayed for.
May the ocean of the virtues of <s>Lokavidnu</s> protect the world from calamity,
he who has conquered the two veils through the realization of the non-duality of selflessness.
This is another example.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>āśīs</s> (benediction). ||

children.text: यत्र तेनैव तदुपमीयते स तद्धर्मः तस्यान्यत्र क्वचिदवृत्तेरनन्वयनाम अलङ्कारः । यदाहुः—

children.translated_text: Where the same thing serves both as the standard and the subject of comparison,
from the desire to express incomparability — that, they call <s>ananvaya</s> (non-correlation).
With lips reddened by betel, with gleaming teeth,
with eyes like blue lotuses — your face is like your face alone.
Where a thing is compared with itself alone, that is the ornament called <s>ananvaya</s> (non-correlation), because of the absence of occurrence of its quality elsewhere. As they say —

children.text: यत्रोपमानेन सहाभेदः, भेदश्च स्तुतिपरः परिदीप्यते ससंदेहो नामासावलङ्कारः कल्पितः । यथोक्तम्—
उपमानेन तत्त्वं च भेदं च वदतः पुनः ।
children.translated_text: The speech of one who states both identity and difference with the standard of comparison,
being for the purpose of praise and being doubtful — the wise know it as <s>sasaṃdeha</s> (the doubtful).

children.text: किमयं शशी न स दिवापि राजते कुसुमायुधो न धनुरस्य कौसुमम् ।
children.translated_text: Is this the moon? No, for he shines even by day. Is this the god of love? No, his bow is not made of flowers.

children.text: इति विस्मयाद् विमृशतोऽपि मे मतिस्त्वयि वीक्षिते न लभतेऽर्थनिश्चयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, even as I examine with wonder, my mind upon seeing you does not attain certainty of the matter.

Where identity with the standard of comparison, and also difference for the purpose of praise, are illuminated together with doubt — that ornament has been devised and called <s>sasaṃdeha</s> (the doubtful). As stated —
A simile that establishes the identity of the subject of comparison with the standard,
which one utters — that is <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor), as follows:
Extending across the entire sky, the measuring-rod of the <s>cakravāka</s> bird,
the foot [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>] triumphs — a mirror of the moon-faces of the <s>Siddha</s> women's finger-nails. — Thus.
And another ornament is called <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor). As stated —
Anticipating the objection that all three of these have not been subsumed, he shows the subsumption and says —
<s>Ananvaya</s> (non-correlation) and <s>sasaṃdeha</s> (the doubtful) have been shown within <s>upamā</s> (simile) itself;
and <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) too has been shown within <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) itself. || 356 ||

children.text: अनन्वयश्च [स]संदेहश्च द्वावप्येतौ उपमासु उपमाविकल्पेषु एव दर्शितो अन्तर्भावितौ तल्लक्षणयोगात् । तथाहि, अनन्वयस्ताव[त्—

children.translated_text: Having surpassed the realm of the moon and the lotus, your face
became comparable to itself alone —

children.text: इत्यात्मनोपमितत्वात्, मुखस्योपमैव । न चाभेदे कथमुपमानोपमेयभाव इति शङ्कनीयम्, अनन्वयेऽतिप्रसङ्गात् । न ह्यनन्वय इति व्यपदेशान्तरमात्रेणोपमानोपमेयभावस्तत्र निवर्तते, प्रतीतिविरोधात् । अथाभेदेऽपि भेदकल्पनया तद्भावः, इहाप्येवमस्तु । अत एवासाधारणोपमेयमात्मनैवोपमितेरन्यस्यानपेक्षणादन्यत्वप्रदर्शनव्याजेन चन्द्रारविन्दाभ्यां वदनमुपमितमिति व्याचक्षते । तथा कथमसाधारणोपमेति चिन्त्यम् । ससंदेहोऽपि—
children.translated_text: is nothing but a simile, since the face is compared with itself. Nor should one object: 'how can there be a relation of standard and subject of comparison when there is identity?' — since that would lead to over-extension in the case of <s>ananvaya</s> itself. For the relation of standard and subject of comparison is not eliminated there merely by the different designation '<s>ananvaya</s>,' since that would contradict the actual perception. If the relation exists even in identity through an imagined distinction, let it be so here too. For precisely this reason, since the subject of comparison is unique and is compared with itself alone without reference to another, the commentators explain that by the pretext of showing otherness, the face has been compared with the moon and lotus. In that case, how it can be called an uncommon simile is worth pondering. <s>Sasaṃdeha</s> (the doubtful) too, in the verse —

children.text: किं पद्ममन्तर्भ्रान्तालि किं ते लोलेक्षणं मुखम् ।
children.translated_text: Is this a lotus with bees wandering inside? Or is it your face with restless eyes?
My mind is swinging like a pendulum —

children.text: इति संशयमुखेन व्यक्तं सादृश्यप्रतीतेः ससंशयोपमैव । न च मन्तव्यम्—
children.translated_text: since the perception of similarity is clearly through the medium of doubt, this is nothing but a <s>sasaṃśayopamā</s> (doubtful simile). Nor should one think, based on the verse —

children.text: किमयं शशी न स दिवापि राजते
children.translated_text: Is this the moon? No, for he shines even by day —

children.text: इति [स्तुति]परो भेदो न दर्शित इति । एवं नाम कान्तिसंपन्नं मुखं यत् पद्मं तद्व्यवसीयत इति स्तुतेरपि प्रतीतेः । प्रायश्चापरा अप्युपमाः स्तुतिगर्भाः, चन्द्रादिप्रतिविशिष्टवस्तुसादृश्योद्भावनात् । न चायं तत्र[ावश्यं] स्तुतिपरो भेदः कथ्यते, अन्यथापि प्रयोगदर्शनात् । तद् यथा—
children.translated_text: that a difference for the purpose of praise has not been shown. For the perception of praise is also present: the face is so resplendent that it is taken to be a lotus. And most other similes too are pregnant with praise, since they evoke similarity with distinguished objects like the moon and the like. Nor is the difference there necessarily described as being for the purpose of praise, since usages of a different kind are also observed. For example —

children.text: एषा किंशुकराजी राजति दावानलो ज्वलन् किमयम् ।
children.translated_text: Is this a row of <s>kiṃśuka</s> trees, or is this a blazing forest fire?
Or is this an untimely twilight, portending the destruction wrought by separation? — Thus.
This moon-face, reddened in its hue by passion,
roars against the moon whose rising blush is ready.

children.text: इति मुखस्य चन्द्रत्वेन रूपणात् । साम्यप्रतीतिगर्भात् रूपकेषु रूपकविकल्पेष्वेव दर्शितमन्तर्भावितम् । रूपकविकल्प
children.translated_text: Since the face is figuratively identified as the moon, and because <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) contains the perception of similarity within it, it has been shown, subsumed, within <s>rūpaka</s> itself, within the varieties of <s>rūpaka</s>. A certain variety of <s>rūpaka</s>

children.text: एव कश्चिदुपमारूपकाख्यः । यथा व्यतिरेकगर्मी रूपकविकल्पो व्यतिरेकरूपकमाख्यायते । तदेतत्त्रयं यथालक्षणमुपमारूपकसंगृहीतमिति न किञ्चित् [तिर]ष्क्रियते ॥
children.translated_text: is called <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor). Just as a variety of <s>rūpaka</s> pregnant with <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is called <s>vyatirekarūpaka</s> (contrast-metaphor). Thus this triad has been subsumed within <s>upamā</s> and <s>rūpaka</s> according to their definitions, and nothing has been excluded.

Both <s>ananvaya</s> and <s>sasaṃdeha</s> have been shown, subsumed, within <s>upamā</s> (simile) itself, within the varieties of <s>upamā</s>, because of their conforming to that definition. For indeed, <s>ananvaya</s> in the verse —
When something connected with the meaning of a <s>śliṣṭa</s> (punning expression), somewhat endowed with <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy),
is again connected with the meaning of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — that is <s>utprekṣāvayava</s> (component of fancy), as follows:
Since their rising and setting are alike, when the sun has set,

children.text: वासाय वासरः ल्कान्तो विशतीव तमोगुहाम् ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: the lovely day enters, as it were, the cave of darkness to rest. — Thus.
Others accept a separate ornament called <s>utprekṣāvayava</s> (component of poetic fancy). As stated —
Showing that this too is subsumed within <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) because it is a particular type thereof, he says —
That which is called <s>utprekṣāvayava</s> (component of fancy) is indeed a variety of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) itself.

children.text: यः परैरुत्प्रेक्षावयवः पृथगुक्तः असौ सोऽपि चायमुत्प्रेक्षाया भेदो विशेषः कश्चित् । ततस्तत्संगृहीत एवेति नासंग्रहः कश्चित् ।
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>utprekṣāvayava</s> by others as a separate figure — that too is indeed a certain variety, a particular type, of <s>utprekṣā</s>. Therefore it is subsumed within it, and there is no failure of subsumption.
He explains <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) —
The combination of various ornaments is termed <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). || 357 ||

children.text: नाना अनेकस्यालङ्कारस्य संसृष्टिः संसर्गः एकत्रोक्तौ सन्निधानं संसृष्टिस्तु निगद्यते विधीयते, यदुद्देशं संकीर्णमुक्तम् । तुशब्देनैतदाह—जात्यादीनामिव नास्याः पृथग्लक्षणम् । तेषामेव तु द्वयोर्बहूनां वा संसर्गलक्षणेयमिति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination), the conjunction, the co-presence in a single expression of many, of multiple ornaments — is termed, is prescribed as, <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>. This was referred to earlier as '<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>' (mixed). By the word '<s>tu</s>' (but) he indicates: unlike <s>jāti</s> (genre) and the like, this does not have a separate definition of its own. Rather, it is characterized by the conjunction of two or many of those very ornaments.

children.text: कथमनेकस्यालङ्कारस्य एकत्रोक्तौ अवस्थानमिति सापेक्षत्वनिरपेक्षत्वरूपं प्रकारद्वयं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Showing the two modes in which multiple ornaments can coexist in a single expression — namely, with dependence and without dependence — he says —
The state of being principal and subordinate parts, or the equal status of all —
Thus, in the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination), a twofold arrangement is to be observed. || 358 ||

children.text: अङ्गमुपकारकम् । अङ्गि च उपकार्यम् । तयोर्भावोऽङ्गाङ्गिभावः साध्यसाधनत्वम् । तेनावस्थानं सन्निधानम् । सर्वेषां ये तत्रोपात्ताः । समो कक्षा बलं येषां तेषां भावः समकक्षता अङ्गाङ्गिभावमन्तरेण स्वातन्त्र्येणावस्थानं चेति—एवंरूपा द्वयी द्विविधा गतिव्यवस्था [लक्षणीया] द्रष्टव्या । कुत्रालङ्कारे ? संसृष्ट्यलङ्कारे विषय इति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>aṅga</s> (subordinate) is that which serves as an instrument. The <s>aṅgin</s> (principal) is that which is served. Their relation is the <s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s> (principal-subordinate relationship), that is, the relation of end and means. Their standing, their presence, is in that relation. Among all those that have been employed therein. Those whose rank, strength, is equal — their state is <s>samakakṣatā</s> (equal standing), that is, their standing independently without the principal-subordinate relationship. Such a twofold, two-typed arrangement of procedure is to be observed, to be noted. In which <s>alaṅkāra</s>? In the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination), as the subject.
O innocent one! The lotuses challenge the beauty of your face;
for those that are furnished with treasury and army — what is difficult for them? || 359 ||

children.text: मुग्धे ! तव मुखस्य श्रियं शोभामरविन्दानि पद्मान्याक्षिपन्ति । त्वन्मुखसदृशानि इति यावत् । इयमुपमा । कथमेतदिति साध्यते—कोशः पद्मगर्भो धनसम्भारश्च, दण्डो नालं चतुरङ्गबलमिति च श्लिष्टम् । ताभ्यां समग्राणां पर्याप्तानामेषामरविन्दानां दुष्करम् असाध्यं कार्यं किमस्ति किञ्चित् ? सर्वमेव साध्यं यत्त्वन्मुखश्रियमप्याक्षिपन्ति इत्यङ्गाङ्गिभाव[ा]वस्थानवत्याः संसृष्टेरुदाहरणमेतत्, उपमायाः साध्यत्वेनाङ्गितयावस्थानात् ।

कोशेत्यादेश्चार्थान्तरन्यासस्य श्लेषानुविद्धस्य साधनत्वेनाङ्गतया स्थितेरित्यलङ्कारत्रयं संसृष्टमङ्गाङ्गिभूतं वर्णितम् । उपमा अर्थान्तरन्यास इत्यलङ्कारद्वयं वा । श्लेषस्त्वर्थान्तरन्यासात्मनैव अवस्थितः, न पृथक् संख्यायत इति ।
children.translated_text: And the <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) beginning with '<s>kośa</s>' and so forth, being permeated by <s>śleṣa</s> (pun), occupies the position of the subordinate as the means of establishing — thus a triad of <s>alaṅkāras</s> has been described as combined in the principal-subordinate relationship. Or, it is a pair of <s>alaṅkāras</s>: <s>upamā</s> and <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. For the <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) exists as the very essence of the <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> and is not counted separately.

O innocent one! Lotuses, water-lilies, challenge the beauty, the loveliness, of your face — meaning they rival your face. This is the <s>upamā</s> (simile). How is this established? <s>Kośa</s> means both the calyx of the lotus and a treasury of wealth; <s>daṇḍa</s> means both the stem and the four-limbed army — this is the <s>śliṣṭa</s> (pun). Being furnished, fully equipped, with both of these — for these lotuses, what is difficult, what is unaccomplishable? Everything is accomplishable, since they even challenge the beauty of your face. This is an example of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) that has the arrangement of the <s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s> (principal-subordinate relationship), because the <s>upamā</s> (simile) occupies the position of the principal as the thing to be established.

children.text: समकक्षा तु संसृष्टिः नोदाहृता । सा त्वेवं द्रष्टव्या—
children.translated_text: But the <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) of equal rank has not been illustrated. It should be seen as follows —
The bodies of women are elevated by breasts, their faces have rolling eyes,

children.text: वचांसि च मधूनीव कथयन्ति न विक्रियाम् ॥ इति ।
children.translated_text: and their words, like honey, declare not any passion. ||
This is a <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) of <s>jātyupamā</s> (generic simile), of the equal-rank type.
Darkness smears the limbs as it were; the sky rains collyrium as it were;
like the service of wicked men, one's vision has become fruitless. ||

children.text: इति भासशूद्रकस्वीकृतं श्लोकं समकक्षाया उदाहरणत्वेन पठन्ति ।
children.translated_text: Thus they cite a verse attributed to <s>Bhāsa</s> and <s>Śūdraka</s> as an example of the equal-rank type.

children.text: कोशदण्डेत्यादिना यद्यर्थान्तरन्यासोऽङ्गतयोपन्यस्तः किं तत्र श्लेषेण ? अथ श्लेषः, स एवास्तु किमर्थान्तरन्यासेन ? तदयं न श्लेषो नार्थान्तरन्यासः शुद्धः । न चैतद्द्वयरूपा संसृष्टिरङ्गाङ्गिभावाप्रतीतेरनयोस्तदुदाहरणं चेदमुपमाया एव । [तम्याः] त्वङ्गित्वेनावसायादस्य त्वङ्गताप्रतीतेरित्यत आह—
children.translated_text: If through '<s>kośadaṇḍa</s>' and so forth an <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) has been presented as subordinate, what role does the <s>śleṣa</s> (pun) play? Alternatively, if there is a <s>śleṣa</s>, let that alone suffice — what need of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>? This is neither a pure <s>śleṣa</s> nor a pure <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. Nor is this a <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> constituted by these two alone, since the principal-subordinate relationship between them is not perceived — and this is an example only of the <s>upamā</s>. [The upamā] occupies the principal position; but since the subordinate status of this [other figure] is not perceived — to this he says —

children.text: श्लेषः सर्वासु पुष्णाति प्रायो वक्रोक्तिषु श्रियम् ।
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (pun) nourishes beauty in almost all indirect expressions (<s>vakrokti</s>);
all literary expression is divided into two: <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) and <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect expression). || 360 ||

children.text: श्लेषोऽयमुक्तलक्षणः स्वभावोक्ति जात्यपरपर्यायां मुक्त्वा सर्वासूपमादिषु न कस्याञ्चिदेव, पदार्थस्वभावस्य यथावस्थानात् । अन्यथा तथा तथा परिकल्पनरूपासु वक्रासूक्तिषु श्रियं शोभां पुष्णात्यावहति प्रायो बाहुल्येन । क्वचिदप्रयोगादस्य प्राय इत्याह । तथा चालङ्कारा जातिवर्ज्याः सर्वे श्लेषानुगता एव प्रायः प्रागुदाहृता । जातौ वा क्वचित् प्रयोगात् प्राय इत्युक्तम् । तदयमप्यर्थान्तरन्यासः वक्रोक्तिस्वभावः श्लेषगर्भोऽङ्गतयोपन्यस्त इति । श्लेषैकदेशे एकोऽलङ्कारः । भेदविवक्षया वा अलङ्कारद्वयमिति द्रष्टव्यम्, यथोक्तं प्राक् । सर्वमिदमलङ्कारजातम् अनेनैव राशिद्वयेन व्यवहार लाघवार्थं संगृह्णन्नाह- वाङ्मयं सर्वमेतदलङ्कारजातं द्विधा, नान्यप्रकारावस्थामवतिष्ठते । कथम् ? स्वभावोक्तिर्जातिः पूर्वोक्तलक्षणा यथावस्थितविचित्रपदार्थपरिदीपनरूपा, वक्रोक्तिश्च वस्तुस्वभावस्य तथातथान्यथाभिधानस्वभावा पूर्वोक्तविचित्रप्रभेदा उपमादिरुक्तिश्चेत्यनेन रूपेण द्विधेति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (pun), having the definition stated above, except for <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) — also known as <s>jāti</s> (generic type) — in all other figures such as <s>upamā</s> and the rest, not in any particular one alone, since the natural state of the object of meaning is maintained as it is [in <s>svabhāvokti</s>]. In those indirect expressions (<s>vakrokti</s>), which take the form of conceiving things in various alternative ways, it nourishes, brings about, beauty — predominantly, for the most part. Because it is occasionally not employed, he says 'mostly.' And thus all <s>alaṅkāras</s>, excluding <s>jāti</s> (generic type), are mostly accompanied by <s>śleṣa</s>, as previously illustrated. Or, because of occasional employment even in <s>jāti</s>, he says 'mostly.' Therefore, this <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> too, being by nature <s>vakrokti</s>, is presented as subordinate with <s>śleṣa</s> embedded within it. <s>Śleṣa</s> constitutes a portion of a single <s>alaṅkāra</s>. Or, when one intends to express them as distinct, it may be viewed as a pair of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, as stated before. Summarizing all this assemblage of <s>alaṅkāras</s> under just these two categories for the sake of terminological economy, he says: all this literary expression, this entire class of <s>alaṅkāras</s>, is twofold — it does not exist in any other mode. How? <s>Svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) is <s>jāti</s> (generic type), having the definition previously stated, whose nature is the illumination of wonderfully varied objects as they actually are; and <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect expression), whose nature is the description of the essence of things in one way or another, otherwise, having the various varieties previously stated — <s>upamā</s> and the like as modes of expression. In this form, it is twofold — this is the basic meaning.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). ||
Elucidating <s>bhāvikatva</s> (the quality of aesthetic imagination), he says —
They call <s>bhāvikatva</s> (aesthetic imagination) a quality pertaining to extended compositions (<s>prabandha</s>);
it is the <s>bhāva</s> (intent) of the poet, which abides in poetry from its very inception. || 361 ||

children.text: प्रबन्धः पद्यगद्यमिश्रात्मकस्त्रिविधः सन्तानः प्रबध्यते विरच्यतेऽसाविति । स विषयो यस्य स प्रबन्धविषयः काव्यसमुदायगोचरः । नैकदेशाधिकरणं तं प्रबन्धविषयं गुणं वि
शेषम् । अनुवादोऽयं भाविकत्वमिति । भाविकं नाम स्वार्थिकत्वादस्य विधेः । प्राहुरामनन्ति सूरय इति विधिः । सोऽपि न ज्ञायते कीदृशोऽपौ प्रबन्धविषयो
children.translated_text: distinction. '<s>Bhāvikatva</s>' is a restatement, so called by virtue of the suffix conveying its own meaning. 'They declare' — the learned proclaim — this is the injunction. But that too is not understood — what kind of quality pertaining to extended composition is this, for which <s>bhāvikatva</s> is prescribed by way of restatement? Showing it from its source and its essential nature, he says '<s>bhāva</s>' and so forth.

children.text: गुणः यदनुवादेन भाविकत्वं विहितमिति तं प्रभवतः स्वरूपतश्च दर्शयन्नाह- भाव इत्यादि । कवेः प्रबन्धकर्तुरभिप्रायः प्रबन्धनिर्वाहकः प्रयत्नविशेषो विकल्पात्मकः । यदाह—काव्येषु प्रबन्धेषु साध्येषु साधनरूपेण आसिद्धि प्रथमतः प्रभृति प्रबन्धविषयां सिद्धिं समाप्तिमधिकृत्य यः स्थितः तत्त्वव्यापकः स तादृशो भावस्तावत् प्रभवस्तस्य गुणस्य । अत एवासौ प्रबन्धविषयः । प्रबन्धसाधकभावसन्ता[ना]नुवर्तित्वात्, न प्रादेशिकः । ततश्च सर्वालङ्कार[ा/?/श्रय]भूतोऽसावादिमध्यान्तेषु प्रबन्धमनुवर्तते । एवं प्रभवतस्तावदुक्तः असौ गुण इति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāva</s> (intent) of the poet, the maker of the composition, is the special effort that sustains the composition, of the nature of imaginative conception. As he says: in poetry, in compositions, from the very inception, that is, from the first stage onward, up to the completion (<s>siddhi</s>) pertaining to the entire composition — the <s>bhāva</s> that abides pervading the whole — such is first the source of that quality. And precisely for this reason it pertains to the extended composition, because it follows the continuity of the creative intent that accomplishes the composition, and is not local or partial. Consequently, being the ground of all <s>alaṅkāras</s>, it follows the composition at its beginning, middle, and end. Thus, from the standpoint of its source, this quality has been stated.

<s>Prabandha</s> (extended composition) is of three kinds — verse, prose, and mixed — that which is composed, fashioned. That is the domain of this quality, which pertains to the totality of the literary work. Not confined to a single section — this quality pertaining to the entire composition is a
Now, dividing it from the standpoint of its essential nature, he says —
The mutual helpfulness of all the episodes of the subject-matter;
the non-employment of purposeless qualifiers; the description at the right place — || 362 ||
The clear manifestation of even a profound subject through the skill of expression;
all this depends on <s>bhāva</s> (the poet's intent) — therefore the learned call it <s>bhāvika</s>. || 363 ||

children.text: वस्तुनः प्रबन्धार्थस्य समुदायस्य पर्वाण्येव यथा नगरवर्णनादयः । वस्तुनि च तानि पर्वाणीति वा । वस्तुपर्वणां काव्यार्थसंघातसन्धीनाम् अङ्गानि समुदायपर्वणामिव परस्परस्योपकारित्वमन्योन्याङ्गाङ्गिभावेन सापेक्षाणामवस्थानम् । न तु स्वतन्त्राणामयःशलाकानामिव परस्परासंघट्टनम् । तथाभावातिरेके प्रबन्धो नारभ्येत । ततश्च कथमस्य प्रबन्धविषयता गुणस्य ? प्रबन्धविषयं च यावत किञ्चिद् विशेष्यं सम्भवति तत्र यानि विशेषणानि तेषां विशेषणानामुपाधीनां व्यर्थानां ***विगतोऽर्थः प्रयोजनं प्रस्तुते क्वचिदुपयोगो येषां यतो वा तेषां प्रकृतानुपयोगिनां कार्ये विवक्षिते क्वचिदङ्गभावमभजताम् अक्रिया तादृशं कञ्चिदर्थमनपेक्ष्य विशेषणमित्येवाप्रयोगः । किं तु सार्थकानां प्रकृते क्वचिद् कथञ्चित् उपयोगिनामेव क्रिया कस्यचिद्वस्तुनो यात्रादेः [?] स्थाने समुपनतेऽवसरे प्राप्तकालं वर्णनम् । तादृशं हि वर्णनमतिशोभते । यदाह भारविः—

children.translated_text: 'Loquacity indeed shines forth at the right occasion.'

children.text: इति । न त्वप्राप्तावसरं वर्णयितव्यमित्येवं ज्ञेयम् । अत्र क्वचिदस्थाने वर्णनं तस्य सौभाग्योपहतत्वाद् गम्भीरस्यापि दुर्बोधस्य न केवलमविषयस्य वस्तुनः धर्मादिरूपस्यार्थस्य प्रस्तावोपनतस्य व्यक्तिः सुखप्रतिपत्तिः । कृताया उक्तेः प्रतिपादनस्य क्रमः प्रकारस्तादृशः करतलाम
children.translated_text: This means one should not describe something at an inappropriate time. Here, description at an improper place would impair the composition's appeal. The manifestation, the easy comprehension, of even a profound, difficult-to-understand — not merely an obscure — subject of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and the like, when it presents itself at the appropriate juncture — through the skill of expression, the manner of the exposition that has been made — that manner which is like a lamp on the palm of the hand,

children.text: लकवत् अर्थप्रकाशनकौशलस्वभावः तस्य वशात् सामर्थ्यात् । अत्र च सर्वत्र भाव एव सत्कवीनां प्रमाणम् । स हि सर्वमीदृशमुचितं विचिनोति, तद्विपर्ययं तु दुर्भगं न स्पृशति, यदाह—भावायत्तमिदं सर्वम् । इतीदमनन्तरोक्तं सर्वं वस्तु पूर्व[व]दुपकारादिलक्षणं विशेषचतुष्टयं भावे प्रबन्धव्यापिनि उचितानुचितविवेकवेधसि मनसि कवेरायत्तं प्रतिबद्धम्, तत्कार्यत्वादिति हेतोः । तत्सर्वमनन्तरोक्तं विदुर्विदन्ति तद्विदः कवयः ।
children.translated_text: whose nature is the skill of illuminating meaning — through the power of that. And in all this, the <s>bhāva</s> (intent) alone of good poets is the authority. For it selects all that is appropriate and does not touch the opposite, which is inauspicious. As he says: 'all this depends on <s>bhāva</s>.' Thus, all this that has just been stated — the fourfold distinction characterized by mutual helpfulness and the rest — depends on the <s>bhāva</s>, the mind of the poet that pervades the composition and discerns the appropriate from the inappropriate, being its effect. And all this just stated is known, understood, by the knowledgeable poets.

Of the subject-matter, that is, the aggregate meaning of the composition, the episodes are like the junctures, such as the description of the city and the like. And those episodes exist within the subject-matter. The mutual helpfulness of the episodes of the subject-matter, that is, the junctures of the poetic meaning — like the limbs of a body — their standing in mutual dependence through the principal-subordinate relationship. Not the mutual non-connection of independent ones, like iron bars. In the absence of such a relationship, the composition would not even begin. Then how does this quality pertain to the composition? Wherever any qualifiable entity pertaining to the composition exists, the qualifiers thereof — those qualifiers, those limiting conditions, that are purposeless — that is, those whose purpose, utility in the matter at hand, is absent, or from which [no purpose proceeds] — the non-employment of such qualifiers that are useless to the purpose at hand, that do not assume the role of a subordinate in the intended effect — that is, the non-use of such purposeless qualifiers. Rather, the employment only of those that are purposeful, that have some utility somewhere in the matter at hand. The description of some subject such as a journey and the like at the appropriate place, at the right occasion, when the proper time has come. For such description shines exceedingly. As <s>Bhāravi</s> says —

children.text: ननु जात्यादिकमपि भाविंकमेव, न हि तस्यापि विना भावेन अभिनिवृत्तिः । तत्किमिदमेव भाविकम् ? उच्यते- पद्येऽप्येवम् । तथापि यो भाव[ः] प्राबन्धिको विशिष्टः, तदायत्तमिह भाविकमभिप्रेतम् । अत एवोक्तम्—काव्येष्वासिद्धि यः स्थितः

इतिं, जात्यादिकं तु प्रादेशिकभावाधीनम् । न हि प्रबन्धानुवर्तिना एकेन भावेन जात्यादिकं जन्यते प्रतिदेशमन्योन्यभावाभिनिवर्त्यत्वात् तस्य । तस्मात् तदन्वर्थैस्तैस्तैरभिधानैर्यथोक्तेन विधिना व्यवह्रियते न भाविकमिति ॥
children.translated_text: — while <s>jāti</s> and the like depend on a local, particular <s>bhāva</s>. For <s>jāti</s> and the like are not produced by a single <s>bhāva</s> that follows the entire composition, since they are brought about at each particular place by mutually different aesthetic intents. Therefore, they are designated by their respective appropriate names in the manner described, and not as <s>bhāvika</s>.

But surely <s>jāti</s> (generic type) and the like are also <s>bhāvika</s> (dependent on aesthetic imagination), for without <s>bhāva</s> they too cannot be brought about. Then is this alone <s>bhāvika</s>? The answer: even in a single verse it is so. Nevertheless, the <s>bhāva</s> that is specific to extended compositions, that is distinctive — what depends on that is meant here as <s>bhāvika</s>. Hence it was said: 'which abides in poetry from its very inception' —
|| Thus ends the section on <s>bhāvika</s> (aesthetic imagination). ||

children.text: ये काव्यधर्माः शास्त्रान्तरे स[न्ध्य]ङ्गादि[शब्द]व्यवहृताः त इह तल्लक्षणयोगादलङ्कारेषु संगृहीता इतिं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Showing that the properties of poetry which are designated in other treatises by terms such as <s>sandhyaṅga</s> (juncture-elements) and the like are here subsumed under <s>alaṅkāras</s> because they fit the definition thereof, he says —

And that which in other treatises has been elaborated under the headings of <s>sandhyaṅga</s> (juncture-elements), <s>vṛttyaṅga</s> (elements of style), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (dramatic properties), and the like —
all this is accepted by us as being of the nature of <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) alone. || 364 ||

children.text: वक्तॄणां[?] वक्तव्यान्तरसमुच्चये सन्धयो—मुखं प्रतिमुखं गर्भोऽवमर्शो निर्वहणमिति पञ्चोक्ताः

। तत्र उपक्षेपः परिकरः परिन्यासो विलोभनं युक्तिः प्राप्तिः समाधानं विधानं परिभावना उद्भेदः करणं भेद इति मुखाङ्गानि । विलासः परिसर्पो विधूतं तापनं नर्म नर्भद्युतिः प्रगमनं विरोधः पर्युपासनं पुष्पं वज्रभुपन्यासो
children.translated_text: Among these, the elements of <s>mukha</s> (opening) are: <s>upakṣepa</s> (hint), <s>parikara</s> (preparation), <s>parinyāsa</s> (establishment), <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement), <s>yukti</s> (contrivance), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (contemplation), <s>udbheda</s> (emergence), <s>karaṇa</s> (action), and <s>bheda</s> (distinction). The elements of <s>pratimukha</s> (progression) are: <s>vilāsa</s> (charm), <s>parisarpa</s> (diffusion), <s>vidhūta</s> (shaking off), <s>tāpana</s> (tormenting), <s>narma</s> (jest), <s>narmadyuti</s> (gleam of jest), <s>pragamana</s> (advance), <s>virodha</s> (opposition), <s>paryupāsana</s> (attendance), <s>puṣpa</s> (flower), <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), <s>upanyāsa</s> (introduction),

children.text: वर्णसंहार इति प्रतिमुखाङ्गानि । अ[भू]ताहरणं मार्गो रूपमुदाहरणं क्रमः संग्रहोऽनुमानं [प्रार्थना]
children.translated_text: and <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion of the scene). The elements of <s>garbha</s> (development) are: <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication), <s>mārga</s> (path), <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), <s>krama</s> (order), <s>saṃgraha</s> (summary), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>prārthanā</s> (supplication),

children.text: आक्षिप्तकं तोटकमधिबलमु[द्वे]गः संभ्रम इति गर्भाङ्गानि । अवपात उत्पातः
children.translated_text: <s>ākṣiptaka</s> (provocation), <s>toṭaka</s> (cutting), <s>adhibala</s> (superior force), <s>udvega</s> (agitation), and <s>sambhrama</s> (haste). The elements of <s>avamarśa</s> (pause) are: <s>avapāta</s> (descent), <s>utpāta</s> (upheaval),

children.text: सम्फेटः विद्रवः शक्तिः व्यवसायः प्रसादो द्युतिः खेदो निषेधो विरोध आदानं छलनं प्ररोचनेत्यवमर्शाङ्गानि । सन्धिर्निरोधो ग्रथनं निर्णयः परिभाषणं द्युतिः प्रसाद आनन्दः समय उपगूहनं भाषणं पूर्वभावः काव्यसंहारः प्रशस्तिरिति निर्वहणाङ्गानि ।
children.translated_text: <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (clash), <s>vidrava</s> (flight), <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>vyavasāya</s> (determination), <s>prasāda</s> (grace), <s>dyuti</s> (brilliance), <s>kheda</s> (exhaustion), <s>niṣedha</s> (prohibition), <s>virodha</s> (opposition), <s>ādāna</s> (seizing), <s>chalana</s> (deception), and <s>prarocanā</s> (instigation). The elements of <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) are: <s>sandhi</s> (union), <s>nirodha</s> (restraint), <s>grathana</s> (weaving), <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (conversation), <s>dyuti</s> (brilliance), <s>prasāda</s> (grace), <s>ānanda</s> (joy), <s>samaya</s> (agreement), <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace), <s>bhāṣaṇa</s> (speech), <s>pūrvabhāva</s> (antecedent state), <s>kāvyasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion of the work), and <s>praśasti</s> (eulogy).

In the aggregation of other things to be stated: the <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) are stated as five — <s>mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>avamarśa</s> (pause), and <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion).

children.text: वृत्तयो—भारती सात्त्वती कैशिकी आरभटी चेति चतस्रः

। तासां प्रत्येकं चत्वार्यङ्गानि । तत्र भारत्याः प्ररोचना आंमुखं वीथी शिल्पकं चेत्यङ्गचतुष्टयम् । सात्वत्या उत्थापकः परिवर्तकः संलापकः संघात्यश्चेति । कैशिक्या [नर्म] नर्मस्फिञ्जो नर्मस्फोटो नर्मगर्भश्चेति । आरभट्याः संक्षिप्तकोऽवपातो वस्तूत्थापनं संफेटश्चेत्यङ्गचतुष्टयम् ।
children.translated_text: Each of these has four elements. Among them, the four elements of <s>Bhāratī</s> are: <s>prarocanā</s> (prologue), <s>āmukha</s> (introduction), <s>vīthī</s> (street-scene), and <s>śilpaka</s> (craft-play).
