Of <s>Sāttvavtī</s>: <s>utthāpaka</s> (arousal), <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal), <s>saṃlāpaka</s> (dialogue), and <s>saṃghātya</s> (concord). Of <s>Kaiśikī</s>: <s>narmasphiñja</s> (jest-tinged), <s>narmasphota</s> (jest-outburst), <s>narmagarbha</s> (jest-laden), [and a fourth]. Of <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>: <s>saṃkṣiptaka</s> (abridgment), <s>avapāta</s> (sudden occurrence), <s>vastūtthāpana</s> (raising the subject), and <s>saṃpheṭa</s> (conflict) — these are the four elements.
The <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) are four: <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Sāttvavtī</s>, <s>Kaiśikī</s>, and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>.

children.text: लक्षणानि—भूषणमक्षरसंघातः शोभा उदाहरणं हेतुः संशयः दृष्ठान्तः प्राप्तिः [अभि] प्रायो निदर्शनं निरुक्तकं सिद्धिः विशेषणं गुणातिपातोऽतिशयः तुल्यतर्कः पदोच्चयो दृष्टान्तमुपदिष्टं विचारो विपर्ययो भ्रंशोऽनुनयो माला दाक्षिण्यं गर्हणमर्थापत्तिः प्रसिद्धिः पृच्छा सारूप्यं मनोरथो लेशः संक्षोभो गुणकीर्तनमनुक्तसिद्धिः प्रियवचनमिति षट्त्रिंशदुक्तानि
children.translated_text: The <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (dramatic properties) are: <s>bhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment), <s>akṣarasaṃghāta</s> (arrangement of syllables), <s>śobhā</s> (beauty), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>abhiprāya</s> (intention), <s>nidarśana</s> (demonstration), <s>niruktaka</s> (etymological explanation), <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualification), <s>guṇātipāta</s> (excess of quality), <s>atiśaya</s> (surpassing), <s>tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning), <s>padoccaya</s> (accumulation of words), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction), <s>vicāra</s> (reflection), <s>viparyaya</s> (reversal), <s>bhraṃśa</s> (downfall), <s>anunaya</s> (conciliation), <s>mālā</s> (garland), <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (dexterity), <s>garhaṇa</s> (reproach), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>prasiddhi</s> (well-known fact), <s>pṛcchā</s> (question), <s>sārūpya</s> (similarity), <s>manoratha</s> (wish), <s>leśa</s> (trace), <s>saṃkṣobha</s> (disturbance), <s>guṇakīrtana</s> (praise of merits), <s>anuktasiddhi</s> (establishment of the unstated), and <s>priyavacana</s> (pleasant speech) — thirty-six have been stated.

children.text: एषां तु स्वरूपमिह विस्तरभयादनधिकाराच्च न निर्दिश्यते । तदागमान्तरादेवानुगन्तव्यम् । तदेतदादिर्यस्यान्यस्यापि तादृशस्य लास्याङ्गवीथ्यङ्गादेस्तत्तथा [व्या]वर्णितमधिकारे विस्तरेण अनेकधा चर्चितम् । आगमान्तरेऽन्यस्मिन् शास्त्रे भरतादौ । इदं च सर्वं न केवलं पूर्वोक्तम् । काव्यशोभाकरत्वेन तल्लक्षणयोगादलङ्करणाद् वा अलङ्कार इत्येव । न सन्ध्यङ्गादित्वेन काव्यार्थत्वेन वा पृथगलङ्कारात् । काव्यशोभाकरं हि तथा तादृशं कथमलङ्कारतामतिक्रामेत् ? इष्टमनुगतमस्माकं क्रियाकल्प [एतदिति स्वी]क्रियताम् । अतस्तादृशं सर्वमलङ्कारसंगृहीतमिति । नाससंग्रहः कश्चिदिहेति भावः । अत एव वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: Having condensed the infinite expanse of poetic embellishments —

children.text: इति । न च काव्यशरीरालङ्कारव्यतिरिक्तः कश्चित् काव्यधर्मः सम्भवति यस्ताभ्याम् असंगृहीतः स्यात् । तदिह यथालक्षणमाभ्यां संगृहीतमिति न किञ्चित् क्षीयते ॥
children.translated_text: Thus, there is no property of poetry other than the body and the ornaments of poetry that would remain unsubsumed by these two. Therefore, here, what has been subsumed by these two according to their definitions — nothing is lost. ||

The essential nature of these is not set forth here, out of fear of prolixity and because it does not fall within this treatise's scope. It should be sought from the other treatise itself. This and what begins with it — of other such things too, such as the <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (elements of graceful dance) and <s>vīthyaṅgas</s> (elements of the street-scene) and the like — has been thus elaborated in that treatise's sections, discussed at length in many ways, in another śāstra, the treatise beginning with <s>Bharata</s>. And all this is not merely what was stated earlier. Because of producing the beauty of poetry, because of fitting the definition of <s>alaṅkāra</s>, or because of embellishing — it is <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) indeed, not something separate from <s>alaṅkāra</s> by virtue of being <s>sandhyaṅga</s> and the like, or by virtue of being a component of poetic meaning. For how could that which produces the beauty of poetry in that manner transcend the status of <s>alaṅkāra</s>? What has been accepted, what has been followed by us in our method of practice — let it be accepted. Therefore, all such things are subsumed under <s>alaṅkāra</s>. There is nothing here that is not so subsumed — this is the purport. Hence he will say —

Having thus accomplished, as promised, the refinement of the seed-varieties of the limited number of ornaments indicated by the earlier masters — excluding the profusion of ornaments — he concludes by saying:

children.text: पन्थाः स एष विवृतः परिमाणवृत्त्या संक्षिप्य विस्तरमनन्तमलंक्रियाणाम् ।
children.translated_text: This is that very path, laid open by the method of delimitation, having condensed the infinite expanse of ornamentations;

children.text: वाचामतीत्य विषयं परिवर्तमानानभ्यास एव विवरीतुमलं विशेषान् ॥ ३६५ ॥
children.translated_text: practice alone, which operates beyond the domain of words, is capable of unfolding the particulars. || 365 ||

children.text: स इति प्रक्रान्तः एषोऽयं निगम्यमानः । स इति वा पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञातः एष प्रसाधितः । स एष पन्था लक्ष्यलक्षणविकल्परूपो मार्गः । कस्य ? अलंक्रियाणाम् । अलङ्काराणां जात्यादीनां सम्बन्धी विवृतः प्रतिसंस्कृतः । अस्माभिरिति गम्यते । गम्यमानार्थस्य च शब्दस्य प्रयोगं प्रति कामचार
इत्युक्तम् । जात्यादयोऽलङ्काराः सामान्यविशेषलक्ष्यलक्षणप्रभेदतः प्रतिपादिता इति यावत् । कथं पुनरनन्ता अलङ्काराः प्रतिपादयितुं शक्या इत्याशङ्का । यदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: in usage. The ornaments such as <s>jāti</s> and the rest have been expounded in terms of the divisions of general and particular, example and definition — such is the meaning. But here arises the doubt: how can infinite ornaments be expounded? As has been said —

children.text: ते चाद्यापि विकल्प्यन्ते कस्तान् कार्त्स्न्येन वक्ष्यति ।
children.translated_text: 'They are being variegated even today — who could describe them in their entirety?

children.text: किं तु बीजं विकल्पानां पूर्वाचार्यैः प्रदर्शितम् ।
children.translated_text: But the seed of the varieties has been shown by the earlier masters;
to refine that very seed is our present effort.' ||

children.text: तदेवानुसरन्नाह—परिमाणेत्यादि । अलंक्रियाणामलङ्काराणां विस्तरं प्रपञ्चं लक्ष्यलक्षणविकल्पात्मकम्, अनन्तमपरिमितं संक्षिप्य संगृह्य
children.translated_text: Following that very principle, he says: 'by delimitation' and so forth. Having condensed, having gathered, the expanse, the elaboration, of ornamentations — of the ornaments — which consists of the varieties of examples and definitions and is infinite, unlimited —
'The properties that produce the beauty of poetry are called ornaments' —

children.text: इति सकलविकल्पव्यापकेन सामान्यलक्षणेन सास्नादिमत्त्वेनेवानन्तं गोप्रभेदं निःशेषं संगृह्य । परिमाणस्य परिमितेर्वृत्त्या सद्भावेन पञ्चत्रिंशदलङ्काररूपेण परिमाणीकृत्य परि[माप्य] इति यावत् । विवृत इति प्रकृतम् । न चैतद् व्याहतमाशङ्कनीयम् । यद्यपरिमितोऽलङ्कारविस्तरः कथमिह परिमित उक्त इति ? योऽसावपरिमितोऽलङ्कार-
children.translated_text: thus, by means of the general definition that pervades all varieties — just as the property of having a dewlap and the like comprehensively gathers the infinite sub-varieties of cattle — by the existence, the presence, of delimitation, having measured and limited them in the form of thirty-five ornaments — such is the meaning. 'Laid open' is the main predicate. And this should not be suspected as contradictory — if the expanse of ornaments is unlimited, how can it be stated here as limited? That same expanse of ornaments which is unlimited and has remained unstated —

children.text: विस्तरोऽनुक्तो वर्तते स एवालङ्कारविस्तरः परिमित उक्तस्तज्जातीयत्वादित्यविरोधः । वस्तुतस्तु योऽनुक्तोऽलङ्कारविस्तरोऽपरिमितः सोऽन्य एव । यस्त्वयमुक्तः परिमितो विस्तरः सोऽप्यन्य एव । यदि पुनरेतावानलङ्कारविस्तरः, तदा अनन्ता अलङ्कारा इति विरुद्ध्येत, परिमितत्वादस्य विस्तरस्य । [अत्रो]क्तालङ्कारविस्तरस्याभ्यासानुसारेण तस्याप्य[नुक्ता]लङ्कारविस्तरस्यावगमसम्भवादनन्तोऽलङ्कारविस्तरोऽयं परिमाणवृत्त्या विवृत इत्युक्तम् । यदाह—वाचामित्यादि । ये विशेषालङ्कारा वाचां गिरां विषयं गोचरमतीत्यातिक्रम्य वर्तन्ते, तान् वाचां विषयमतीत्य परिवर्तमानान् वस्तुतो विद्यमानान् इह चानुक्तानिति यावत् । अभ्यासः यथोक्तालङ्कारानुसारी स्वयं काव्यप्रयोगविषयोऽभियोग एव यथावत् कवीनाम्, नान्यत् किञ्चित् विवरीतुं प्रयोगद्वारेण प्रकाशयितुमलं समर्थः । एतन्मार्गानुसारेण हि प्रयोगाभ्यासवतां कवीनां स्वयमेवोक्तिविशेषलक्षणास्तेऽलङ्काराः प्रयोगपथमुप[पद्य]न्ते । ततश्चायमेव मार्गस्तेषाम् अप्यवगमोपाय इत्यनेनैव ते संगृहीताः । अत्र एवोक्तम्- संक्षिप्य विस्तरमनन्तमलंक्रियाणां स एष पन्थाः प्रकाशित इति । तस्मादशेषालङ्कारविषयं परिज्ञानमिच्छ[द्भिर]य पन्था यथावदभ्यसनीय इति ॥
children.translated_text: that very expanse of ornaments is the one stated as limited, because of being of the same class — hence no contradiction. In reality, the unstated expanse of ornaments that is unlimited is one thing. But the stated, limited expanse is another thing entirely. If, however, one were to say 'this much alone is the expanse of ornaments,' then the statement 'ornaments are infinite' would be contradicted, because this expanse is limited. Since by following the practice of the stated expanse of ornaments, the comprehension of that unstated expanse is also possible, it was said 'this infinite expanse of ornaments has been laid open by the method of delimitation.' As he says: 'of words' and so forth. Those particular ornaments that exist beyond the domain of words, of speech — that operate beyond verbal expression, that actually exist but have not been stated here — practice alone, which follows the stated ornaments, which pertains to the domain of one's own poetic composition and exercise — that practice alone of poets, properly pursued, and nothing else, is capable of unfolding, of revealing through actual usage. For indeed, by following this path, for poets who have practiced through composition, those ornaments — characterized by special modes of expression — themselves come into the path of usage. Therefore, this very path is the means for comprehending even those [unstated ornaments], and by this path they are subsumed. Here itself it was said: 'having condensed the infinite expanse of ornamentations, this is the path that has been illuminated.' Therefore, those who desire complete knowledge of the entire domain of ornaments should properly practice this path. ||

'That' (<s>saḥ</s>) — the one that was commenced; 'this' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>) — this one now being concluded. Or: 'that' — the one previously promised; 'this' — the one now accomplished. This is that path (<s>panthāḥ</s>), the road in the form of the varieties of examples and definitions. Of what? Of ornamentations, of the ornaments such as <s>jāti</s> (genre) and the rest — it has been laid open, refined. 'By us' is understood. And it has been said that a word whose meaning is understood may be freely employed

body.translated_text: || Thus ends the second chapter on <s>arthālaṅkāra</s> (ornaments of meaning) in the <s>Ratnaśrī</s> commentary on <s>Daṇḍin</s>'s <s>Kāvyalakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics of Poetry). ||

children.translated_text: Third <s>Pariccheda</s> (<s>Duṣkara</s>)
The third chapter is named <s>Duṣkara</s> (the difficult). ||

Having thus delimited the ornaments of meaning, with the recapitulation of the definition of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) mentioned in passing, and wishing to undertake the chapter on <s>duṣkara</s> (the difficult) preceded by the elaboration of <s>yamaka</s> (chiming), he says —
The repetition of a group of phonemes, either contiguous or separated,
is <s>yamaka</s> (chiming); and it pertains to the beginning, middle, or end of the verse-quarters. || 1 ||

children.text: वर्णानां स्वरव्यञ्जनानां संहतेः समुदायस्य व्यावृत्तिरावृत्तिः पुनरुच्चारणम् । नैकस्य वर्णस्य, तस्या अनुप्रासत्वात् । यथोक्तम्— वर्णावृत्तिरनुप्रासः
इति । तत्प्रसङ्गेन आवृत्तिमेव सङ्घातगोचरां यमकं विदुः
children.translated_text: And in that connection: 'They know the repetition pertaining to a cluster as <s>yamaka</s>' —

children.text: इति कृतलक्षणं यमकम् । तदेवमनूद्य यमकं विधीयते । सा च व्यावृत्तिः [कीदृशी ?] वर्णान्तरेणाव्यपेतोऽव्यवहितः व्यपेतो व्यवहितश्चात्मा स्वरूपं यस्या इत्यव्यपेतव्यपेतात्मा । तथा वर्णान्तराव्यवहिता वर्णसंहतेरावृत्तिरव्यपेतयमकम् । या तु व्यवहिता तद् व्यपेतयमकमिति द्विधा यमकं तावद् विकल्प्यते । तच्चैतद् द्विविधं यमकं विषयनिरूपणायामादिश्च मध्यश्चान्तश्च गोचरो विषयोऽस्येत्यादिमध्यान्तगोचरं विज्ञेयम् । कस्य ? पादानां प्रत्येकं चतुर्णां श्लोकावयवानाम् । सापेक्षार्थे गमकत्वात् समासः ॥
children.translated_text: — thus <s>yamaka</s> whose definition has been established. Having thus recapitulated, <s>yamaka</s> is now expounded. And that repetition — of what kind? — whose nature (<s>ātman</s>) is either uninterrupted (<s>avyapeta</s>), that is, without any other phoneme intervening, or interrupted (<s>vyapeta</s>), that is, with another phoneme intervening — thus '<s>avyapetavyapetātmā</s>.' Accordingly, when the repetition of the phoneme-group is uninterrupted by other phonemes, it is <s>avyapeta-yamaka</s> (contiguous chiming). When it is interrupted, it is <s>vyapeta-yamaka</s> (separated chiming) — thus <s>yamaka</s> is first of all divided into two kinds. And this twofold <s>yamaka</s>, in the determination of its domain, pertains to the beginning, the middle, or the end — thus '<s>ādimadhyāntagocara</s>' — this should be understood. Of what? Of the verse-quarters (<s>pāda</s>), individually, of the four components of a verse. The compound is formed because of the indicative function of the dependent meaning. ||

Of phonemes — vowels and consonants — the repetition, the re-utterance, of a group, a cluster — not of a single phoneme, since that would be <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). As has been said: 'the repetition of a phoneme is <s>anuprāsa</s>' —

children.text: पादचतुष्टयस्यादिमध्यान्तभाविनो यावन्तः प्रकाराः सम्भवन्ति तान् दर्शयति—
children.translated_text: He shows the various possibilities of the <s>yamaka</s> occurring at the beginning, middle, and end of the four verse-quarters —
The varieties of one-quarter, two-quarter, three-quarter, and four-quarter <s>yamaka</s>s:
at the beginning, middle, end; middle-end; middle-beginning; beginning-end; or everywhere. || 2 ||

children.text: एकपादयमकस्य द्विपादयमकस्य त्रिपादयमकस्य चतुष्पादयमकस्य [च] विकल्पना विकल्पाः प्रभेदाः कथ्यन्ते भवन्तीति वा शेषः । पादस्यैकस्य पादद्वयस्य पादत्रयस्य पादचतुष्टयस्य वा आदितो वा मध्यतो वान्ततो वा । आदौ मध्येऽन्ते वेति त्रयो विकल्पास्तावत् । मध्यतोऽन्ततश्चादिमं वर्जयित्वेति चतुर्थो विकल्पः । मध्यत आदितश्चान्त्यं विहायेति पञ्चमः । आदितोऽन्ततश्च मध्यं त्यक्त्वेति षष्ठः ।

सर्वत आदौ मध्येऽन्ते चेति सप्तमो विकल्पः । सर्वत इत्यस्यान्ते श्रुतस्य तसः प्रत्येकं सम्बन्धात् । सप्तम्यर्थश्चायम् । तथा च प्रथमं विवृतमादौ मध्येऽन्ते वेति । अन्यत्राप्येवं योज्यम् । यदा च सर्वतो यमकं तदा पादाभ्यासादयो विकल्पा जायन्ते ॥
children.translated_text: Everywhere — at the beginning, middle, and end — this is the seventh variety. The syllable '<s>taḥ</s>' at the end of '<s>sarvataḥ</s>' (everywhere), being heard, relates to each individually. And this has the sense of the seventh case (locative). And thus, the first one has been explained as 'at the beginning, middle, or end.' The same applies elsewhere as well. And when there is <s>yamaka</s> everywhere, varieties such as repetition of entire quarters arise. ||

The varieties, the divisions, of one-quarter <s>yamaka</s>, two-quarter <s>yamaka</s>, three-quarter <s>yamaka</s>, and four-quarter <s>yamaka</s> are stated, or they exist — this is the remainder. Of one quarter, of two quarters, of three quarters, or of four quarters — at the beginning, or at the middle, or at the end. At the beginning, in the middle, or at the end — these are the first three varieties. At the middle and at the end, excluding the beginning — this is the fourth variety. At the middle and at the beginning, leaving out the end — this is the fifth. At the beginning and at the end, omitting the middle — this is the sixth.

children.text: एते सप्त विकल्पा मौलाः परस्परसङ्करभाजोऽनेकधा प्रसरन्तीति दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Showing that these seven fundamental varieties multiply in many ways through mutual combination, he says —
Exceedingly numerous are the sub-varieties of these, born from combination;
some among them are seen to be easy, and some difficult. || 3 ||

children.text: विकल्पानां सम्भेदः सङ्करो मिश्रत्वमुच्चावचप्रकारः योनिः प्रभवो येषां ते सम्भेदयोनयः । भेदाः प्रकाराः अत्यन्तबहवो भूयांसो भवन्ति । एकत्र श्लोके क्वचिदादियमकं क्वचिन्मध्ययमकं क्वचिदन्तयमकं क्वचिन्मध्यान्तयमकं क्वचिन्मध्यादियमकं क्वचिदाद्यन्तयमकं क्वचित् सर्वत्र इत्येवमेतेऽनेकधा प्रसरन्ति । ते चैते सुखेन क्रियन्ते प्रयुज्यन्त इति सुकराः, तद्विपरीताश्च दुष्करा इति द्विधा पुनः संगृह्यन्ते । तत्र ते सुकरेषु दुष्करेषु च केचन केचिद् भेदा न सर्वेऽतिप्रसङ्गाद् दृश्यन्ते उदाह्रियन्ते ॥
children.translated_text: varieties, those whose origin (<s>yoni</s>), whose source, is combination (<s>saṃbheda</s>), mixture, various modes — those are called '<s>saṃbhedayoni</s>' (born from combination). The sub-varieties, the types, are exceedingly numerous, abundant. In a single verse, somewhere there is <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning, somewhere at the middle, somewhere at the end, somewhere middle-and-end <s>yamaka</s>, somewhere middle-and-beginning, somewhere beginning-and-end, somewhere everywhere — thus these proliferate in many ways. And these are further classified in two ways: <s>sukara</s> (easy) — those that are easily made, easily employed — and the opposite, <s>duṣkara</s> (difficult). Among these, among both the easy and the difficult, some, certain sub-varieties — not all, to avoid prolixity — are seen, are illustrated. ||
Of those seven

children.text: मानेन मानेन सखि प्रणयोऽभूत् प्रिये जने ।
children.translated_text: O friend, let there be no intimacy born of pride with the beloved;
rather, embrace his neck, you who have been deceived, and make him bashful. || 4 ||

children.text: सखि ! प्रिये जने विषयेऽनेन सङ्गमसुखविरोधिना मानेन प्रातिकूल्येन सह प्रणयपरिचयो मा भूत् । तव मानो न कार्य इति यावत् । यदि न मानः कर्तव्यः किमिदानीं क्रियताम् ? येन खण्डिता वञ्चितासि तस्य कण्ठमाश्लिष्य तमेव प्रियं कृतव्यलीकं सत्रपं सलज्जं कुरु विनयवर्त्मना तमेव विलक्षं विधेहि । किं मानेनेति ? शब्दार्थप्रधानमेतद् यमकव्याख्यानं क्रियते, भावार्थचर्चायामतिविस्तरप्रसङ्गात् । इदं प्रथमपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: O friend! Let there be no intimacy (<s>praṇaya</s>), no familiarity, with the beloved, with this man, through this <s>māna</s> (pride/sulking) which opposes the happiness of union — through this hostility. Your sulking should not be pursued — such is the meaning. If sulking is not to be pursued, then what should be done now? Embracing the neck of the one by whom you have been deceived (<s>khaṇḍitā</s>), make that very beloved, who has committed an offense, bashful (<s>satrapa</s>), that is, ashamed — lead him to embarrassment through the path of graciousness. What use is sulking? This explanation of <s>yamaka</s> focuses on the meaning of the word and sense, since an extended discussion of the emotional import would lead to excessive prolixity. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first quarter. ||
By the thundering of clouds, the desire of women, whose pride has been shattered,

children.text: नुन्नमानं मनः स्त्रीणां सह रत्या विगाहते ॥ ५ ॥
children.translated_text: together with passion (<s>Rati</s>), <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) enters their minds. || 5 ||

children.text: मदनः कामः रत्या कलत्रेण सह स्त्रीणां मनो विगाहते प्रविशति । किविशिष्टम् ? हंसानां मदं नुदतां मेघानां नादेन नुन्नो निरस्तो मानोऽस्येति नुन्नमानं मानसं वा अवेहि । तस्मिन्नवकाशमसौ लभते । इदं द्वितीयपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), together with <s>Rati</s> (his consort), enters, penetrates, the minds of women. Of what kind [is the mind]? Of those whose pride (<s>māna</s>) has been shattered (<s>nunna</s>), dispelled, by the thundering of clouds — that is, whose minds have been humbled — understand it so. In that [state of humbled pride], he finds an opening. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the second quarter. ||

children.text: राजन्वत्यः प्रजा जाता भवन्तं प्राप्य साम्प्रतम् ।
children.translated_text: The subjects have become possessed of a king, O king, now that they have obtained you,
skilled in seizing the earth whose girdle is the four oceans. || 6 ||

children.text: चत्वारः पूर्वादयोऽम्भोधयः परिखे[वोप]योगादिसाधर्म्येण रसना मेखला यस्याः तस्या उर्व्या भुवः करो हस्तो बलिश्चेति श्लिष्टम् । तस्य ग्रहे उपादाने चतुरं भ[वन्तं] प्राप्य प्रजा जना राजन्वत्यः सौराज्ययोगात् जाता अभूवन् साम्प्रतमद्येति तृतीयपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: The four oceans beginning with the eastern serve as the girdle, the belt, of the earth — through the similarity of serving as a moat and the like — the <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is that <s>kara</s> (hand/tribute) means both the hand of the earth and the tribute. In the seizing, the acquiring, of that [earth] — skillfully — having obtained you, the subjects, the people, have become <s>rājanvati</s> (possessed of a king), due to enjoying good governance — this is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the third quarter. ||
The forest was entered by some, the abode of the gods by others —
your enemies, bereft of infantry, chariots, elephants, and horses, by your hostile [forces]. || 7 ||

children.text: अन्यैस्त्वत्कृपाणभ्रमोज्भ्कतप्राणैदिवौकसां सद्म स्वर्गमाक्रान्तमारूढम् । किंभूतैः ? पदातिभिः रथैर्नागैरश्वैश्च रहितैस्त्यक्तैः । [अत्रारण्यगमनं स्वर्गगमनं वा भुवि निःस]हायत्वात् । तेन वा [भवत्त]स्तेषामाच्छादनात् । इदं चतुर्थपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: By others, whose life-breaths were expelled by the whirling of your sword, the abode of the gods, heaven, was entered, ascended. Of what kind? Bereft of, that is, abandoned by, infantry, chariots, elephants, and horses. [The entry into the forest or heaven was] because of being without support on earth. Or because of their being overwhelmed by you. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the fourth quarter. ||
By your enemies (<s>ahita</s>), by some who were fleeing, the forest was entered, invaded — meaning they entered the wilderness, abandoning their homes.
O lotus-faced one! Speak sweetly — what is this that mimics
the playful movement of your eyes through the wandering of bees? || 8 ||

children.text: अम्भोजमिव वदनमस्या इत्यम्भोजवदना [तस्याः सम्बुद्धिः] । तव नेत्रयोर्विभ्रमं चञ्चलत्वं मधुरं रम्यं भ्रमरा[णां भ्रान्त्या चा]पलेन विडम्बयति अनुकरोति मधुर्वसन्तः किं न्विदं वद ब्रूहि इति कश्चिच्चाटुकारः प्रियामुपलालयति । प्रथमद्वितीयपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: She whose face is like a lotus — thus 'lotus-faced' (<s>ambhojavadanā</s>) — [this is the vocative]. What is this that mimics, imitates, the charming, delightful playful movement (<s>vibhrama</s>), the darting quality, of your two eyes, through the wandering (<s>bhrānti</s>), the flitting, of bees — speak, tell me, O sweetly! — this is <s>Madhu</s> (Spring) — thus some flatterer coaxes his beloved. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first and second quarters. ||

children.text: वारणो वा रणोद्दामो हसो वा स्मर ! दुर्धरः ।
children.translated_text: O <s>Smara</s> (god of love)! Is it a war-elephant, untamed in battle, or a horse, irresistible?
Since neither brings us to our end, how wondrous is your prowess! || 9 ||
O <s>Smara</s>! Since neither a war-elephant (<s>vāraṇa</s>) untamed in battle nor a horse (<s>haya</s>) irresistible in combat, capable of bringing us to destruction, exists [in your arsenal]

children.text: यतो यस्मा[त् नः अस्मान्] अन्तं नाशं नयतः प्रापयतस्तव रणे उद्दामः क्षमो वारणो वा हस्ती वा, हयोऽश्वो वा दुर्धरः सांग्रामिको नास्ति ।
तत्तस्मादहो विचित्रीयते विक्रमस्तव यद् विना रणोपकरणे[नास्मद्विधाः] आसादिताः त्वयेति प्रथमतृतीयपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: therefore — how wondrous! — your prowess is marveled at: that without any instrument of battle, one such as us has been overcome by you. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first and third quarters. ||
The earth is conquered by kings like you, who shine with valor in battle,
and is then led to contentment by a continuous stream of wealth. || 10 ||

children.text: त्वादृशैः शक्तिसम्पन्नैर्नृपैराजौ रणे तैक्ष्ण्येन शौर्येण राजितैर्दीप्तैर्वसुधा पृथिवी जीयते । पुनस्तदनु वसुनो धनस्य धारया सन्तानेन दीयमानया करणेन हेतुना वा तृप्तिमभिलाषपर्यन्तं नीयते च । न केवलं जीयत एव वसुधेत्यत्राप्युक्तम् । प्रथमचतुर्थपादादियमकमिदम् ॥
children.translated_text: By kings like you, endowed with power, shining, resplendent with valor, heroism, in battle, in war — the earth is conquered. Then afterward, by a stream, a continuous flow, of wealth (<s>vasu</s>) being bestowed — by that as the instrument or cause — the earth is led to contentment, to the fulfillment of desire. Not only is the earth conquered — this too has been stated. This is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first and fourth quarters. ||
The cry of the intoxicated cuckoo makes my mind
overwhelmed with the longing aroused by the mango's budding blossom. || 11 ||

children.text: सहकारस्य कलिका मञ्जरी उत्कलिका उत्कण्ठा उत्तरा प्रबला यस्य [तथा उत्कलि]कोत्तरं [तद्]बहुलं मम मन करोति । पर्युत्सुकयतीति यावत् । मत्तस्य कोकिलस्य निस्वनः शब्दोऽप्येषो[ऽत्यन्त]मधुरः मन्मनः उत्कलिकोत्तरं करोतीति प्रकृतम् । अत्र द्वितीयतृतीयपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: The bud (<s>kalikā</s>), the blossom, of the mango tree; <s>utkalikā</s> means longing, eager desire; '<s>uttara</s>' means predominant, intense — thus <s>utkalikottara</s> means 'overwhelmed with longing' — my mind is made such, that is, it is made intensely anxious. The cry, the sound, of the intoxicated cuckoo — even this, being extremely sweet — makes my mind overwhelmed with longing aroused by the mango blossom — this is the main statement. Here this is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the second and third quarters. ||
How can such a condition, in which the hope of finding you has been thwarted,
which destroys a woman's body, be endured by a woman? || 12 ||

children.text: तवोपलम्भे समागमे आशा मनोरथः तस्य विहतौ विघाते इह अस्यां सत्यां तादृशी अभिलाषचिन्तनानुस्मृतिगुणकीर्तनोद्वेगविलापोन्माद[मूर्च्छा]व्याधिजडताक्रमेण प्रवृद्धावस्था अङ्गं नाशयतीत्यङ्गनाशिनी दशमी । तादृशीमित्यपि पठ्यते । तत्राङ्गनां तादृशीं त्व[द]नुरागपरवशामिति व्याख्येयम् । [अङ्गनाम्] आरोढुमासादयितुं कथं नालं न समर्था ? आरोहत्येव । नात्र सन्देहः । तदनुकम्प्यतामङ्ग ! वराकी । किं स्त्रीवधपातकदोहदेनेति

children.translated_text: this is a <s>yamaka</s> (alliterative repetition) at the beginning of the second and fourth feet.

The hope, the longing, for obtaining you, for union — when that is frustrated, destroyed — in this situation, a state that has progressed through the sequence of desire, brooding, remembrance, praising of virtues, agitation, lamentation, madness, fainting, illness, and stupor, destroys the body — thus it is called the tenth stage, 'body-destroying' (<s>aṅganāśinī</s>). The reading '<s>tādṛśīm</s>' is also found, in which case it should be explained as: such a woman, one subjected to passion for you. How is the [tenth stage] not capable of reaching, of attaining, the woman? It certainly does reach her. There is no doubt about this. Therefore, have compassion, O dear one, on this wretched woman! Why this desire for the sin of killing a woman? —
Seizing the eyes, they attract — with one adorned by tender shoots —
the young trees attract young men, and bees, turning toward lotuses. || 13 ||

children.text: तरुणा वृक्षेण बालैः पल्लवैः शोभमानेन नेत्रे निगृह्य कृष्टान् विक्षिप्तमनसः तरुणान् यूनः अलिनो भ्रमरा नलिनेषून्मुखाः प्रवृत्ताः । नेत्रे चक्षुषी निगृह्य दर्शनसुभगतया गृहीत्वा कर्षयन्ति अभिमुखीकुर्वन्ति । उभयदर्शनवशव्याकुलास्तरुणा इति यावत् । अत्र तृतीयचतुर्थपादादियमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: By a young tree adorned with tender shoots, having seized the eyes — young men whose minds are distracted, drawn; and bees (<s>alinas</s>), turning toward lotuses, directed toward them. Having seized the eyes, captivating them by the beauty of their appearance, they attract, they draw toward themselves. The young men are agitated, pulled by the sight of both — such is the meaning. Here there is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the third and fourth feet.
Bright, in the lake where bright and intoxicated cranes wade,
this goose makes — with its cry it makes — me a morsel for Death. || 14 ||

children.text: सरस इदं [सारसं तत्र] सारसे जले, किंभूते ? विशतो विगाहमाना आमत्ताः सारसाः पक्षिणो यस्मिन् [तत्र] विशदामत्तसारसे व्यवस्थिता विशदा शुक्ला हंसीयं विरहिजनोद्वेजनीयत्वात् मधुरेणापि कुत्सितेनाविषह्येन रुतेन शब्देन हेतुना करणेन [वा] अन्तकस्य मृत्योरामिषं ग्रासं मां कुरुते, मां हन्तीति यावत् । प्रथमद्वितीयतृतीयपादादियमकं विकल्पितमिदम् ॥
children.translated_text: This is a lake (<s>sārasa</s>); in that lake-water — of what kind? Where cranes (<s>sārasas</s>), birds, wade, diving in — there, in such a lake abounding in intoxicated cranes, this bright, white goose, because it agitates those in separation, with its sweet yet detestable, unbearable cry, as cause or instrument, makes me a morsel, a prey, of Death (<s>Antaka</s>) — meaning, it kills me. This is an alliteration varied at the beginning of the first, second, and third feet.
Poison follows poison; the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, a cause of sorrow,
together with the digit of the moon, pure and spotless, follows desire. || 15 ||

children.text: मलयानिलो ममानन्दन पीडाहेतुः अपोढम् अपगतं मलम् अत इति अपोढमलया विशदया इन्दोः कलया सह मदनं कामं नाम विषमं विषम् आशुनाशकत्वात् । अन्वेति अनुसरति उपनयती[?]त्यर्थः । अन्वेत्यनुकरोतीति वा व्याख्येयम्, मलयानिलश्चन्द्रकला च तादृगत्यन्ततापकरत्वात् मदनायत्तौ इत्यर्थः । प्रथमद्वितीयचतुर्थपादादियमकमिदम् ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>Malaya</s> breeze, a cause of my suffering, not delight — together with the digit of the moon, whose impurity has been removed, that is, pure and lustrous — follows desire (<s>madana</s>, the god of love), which is a terrible poison, because of its power to destroy quickly. 'Follows' means accompanies, brings near — such is the meaning. Or it may be explained as 'imitates,' since the <s>Malaya</s> breeze and the moon's digit, being producers of intense burning like that, are subordinate to <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) — such is the meaning. This is an alliteration at the beginning of the first, second, and fourth feet.
O <s>Anaṅga</s> (god of love)! A proud woman, do not wish to bring me to the state of being your quiver!

children.text: हारिणी हारिणी शर्म तनुतां तनुतां वतः ॥ १६ ॥
children.translated_text: Let the charming one, the one who steals happiness, make slender — alas, she makes my body slender! || 16 ||

children.text: अनङ्ग ! तव निषङ्गत्वं तूणीरत्वं शरनिकरपूरयोगेन मा मां निनीषुर्नेतुम् इच्छन्ती मानिनी काचिद् विवक्षितास्त्री हारिणी मुक्तालतालंकृता, अनेना[हा]र्यं रूपमुक्तम् । स्वभावरूपगुणयोगाच्च मनोहरा मे मम तनुतां कृशत्वं प्राणसन्देहं यतः गच्छतः शर्म समागमसुखं जीवितं तनुतां करोतु । प्रसीद, आज्ञापयैनाम् । देव ! त्वमेवास्याः प्रभवसीति प्रथमतृतीय वतुर्थपादादियमकं विकल्पितम् ॥
children.translated_text: O <s>Anaṅga</s> (god of love)! A certain proud woman (<s>māninī</s>), the intended woman, desiring to lead me to the state of being your quiver (<s>niṣaṅga</s>) — filled with the multitude of your arrows — [should not do so]. She is charming (<s>hāriṇī</s>), adorned with a string of pearls — by this, her captivating beauty is expressed. And being captivating by her natural beauty and qualities — let her make slender, that is, cause the emaciation, the mortal danger, of me who am departing, and thus let her diminish the happiness of union, the joy of life. Be gracious, command her! O lord, you alone have power over her — this is an alliteration varied at the beginning of the first, third, and fourth feet.
By your face, conquering us — how has it not conquered? How indeed?
The lotus — how the lotus adorns it, with its petals, with its bees, O my beloved! || 17 ||

children.text: मम प्रिये मत्प्रिये ! तव मुखेनास्मानेवं मुखरान् जयता वशीकुर्वता अकथं न विद्यते कथास्येत्यवचनम्, विकासयोगेन दलानि प्रशस्तानि पत्राण्यस्मिंन् इति दलि । प्रबुद्धमिति यावत्, अतश्च मकरन्दलोलुपमधुप

योगात्, अलयोऽस्मिन् विद्यन्ते इति अलिमत् । एवं च गुणयोगात् कमुदकमाश्रयमलङ्कुर्वत् भूषयत् कमलं पद्मपर्यायमपि कथमवचनं [सत्] न जितं जितमेवेति कमलेन मुखमुपमितम् । अत्र द्वितीयतृतीयचतुर्थपादादियमकमाविष्कृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: because of the abundance of nectar-seeking bees, bees (<s>alis</s>) are found therein, thus it is '<s>alimat</s>' (possessing bees). And thus, due to these qualities, the lotus, which is also an ornament decorating the lake (<s>kamuda</s>), the lotus synonymous with <s>padma</s> too — how could it remain speechless, unconquered? It is indeed conquered — thus the face is compared to the lotus. Here an alliteration at the beginning of the second, third, and fourth feet has been revealed.

O my beloved! By your face, conquering us, the eloquent ones, subjugating us — the lotus, speechless (<s>akatha</s>) — how could it not be conquered, how could it remain undefeated? — it is indeed conquered. Because of the capacity for blooming, its petals (<s>dalas</s>) are excellent, and it is therefore blossoming — hence
My beloved woman is delightful, robed in pale pink,
fragrant like the <s>Vāruṇī</s> direction, a repository of sweetness, having become radiant with a sunset glow. || 18 ||

children.text: रमणी स्त्री काचित् अभिमता रमणीया मनोज्ञा मे मम । किंभूता ? पाटलपुष्पवदापाटलमरुणमंशुकं यस्याः सा । तथा सौरभस्य सुगन्धितायाः कृत्रिमस्य सहजस्य चास्पदं भूमिः । कथमिव तादृशी दृश्यते ? अरुणीभूता सौरी सूर्यसम्बन्धिनी भा दीप्तिर्यस्याः सा तथाभूता वारुणी पश्चिमा दिगिव रमणीयेति प्रकृतम् । पादचतुष्टयादियमकमुक्तम् ॥
children.translated_text: A certain beloved woman (<s>ramaṇī</s>) is delightful (<s>ramaṇīyā</s>) to me. Of what kind? Wearing a garment that is pale pink like the <s>pāṭala</s> flower. And a ground, a locus, of fragrance — both artificial and natural sweetness. How does she appear so? The primary meaning: she is delightful like the western (<s>vāruṇī</s>) direction that has become suffused with the reddish radiance connected with the sun. This is an alliteration at the beginning of all four feet.
Thus the initial <s>yamaka</s> (alliteration), uninterrupted, has been varied.
Now some varieties of the interrupted type are also described. || 19 ||

children.text: आदियमकमव्यपेतं विकल्प्योपसंहरति- इत्युक्तेन प्रकारेण पादानामेकशः द्विशः त्रिशः चतुर्णां च, आदौ आदिर्वा यमकमव्यपेतमव्यवहितं विकल्पितमनेकधा विभक्तम् । तस्य यमकस्य व्यपेतस्य व्यवहितस्यापि, न केवलमव्यपेतस्य विकल्पाः प्रभेदाः केचित् कतिपये, न सर्वे, वर्ण्यन्त उदाह्रियन्त इति ॥
children.translated_text: He summarizes the uninterrupted initial <s>yamaka</s>: in the manner stated, at the beginning of one, two, three, or all four feet, the initial <s>yamaka</s> — uninterrupted, contiguous — has been varied, divided in many ways. Of that <s>yamaka</s>, even when interrupted, separated — not only when uninterrupted — some varieties, some sub-types — not all — are described, illustrated.
With the sweet emergence of the mango, fragrant and delightful,
the sulking of the doe-eyed women will be made a mere residue of words. || 20 ||

children.text: एणदृशां स्त्रीणां नानाप्रियजनवैमुख्यं शब्द उपमानेत्यादिवाचकः शेषोऽवशिष्टः, अर्थस्य विगमात् यस्य तं शेषमसन्तं करिष्यति मधुर्वसन्तः । केन ? मधुरेण
मनोज्ञेन सुगन्धिना सुरभिणा सहकारस्योद्गमेनाङ्कुरेणैव । कुं बहुना ? स हि तादृशो मानविरुद्धरागमुपनयन् मानस्य शेषीकरणे करणत्वं प्रतिपद्यते । प्रथमद्वितीयपादादिवर्तिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: charming, fragrant emergence, the sprouting, of the mango tree alone. Why elaborate further? For indeed, that one, being such, by bringing about passion that is opposed to sulking, becomes instrumental in rendering the sulking merely nominal. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> occurring at the beginning of the first and second feet.

Of the doe-eyed women — their sulking (<s>māna</s>), the various aversions toward their beloved — the word is the designation such as 'comparison' and the like; the remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>), left over, since the substance has departed — that empty remainder, will be made by spring (<s>madhu</s>). By what means? By the sweet,
The excessively reddened hand of the women performs the sport of plucking the <s>vīṇā</s> strings;
or, with jealousy, it strikes the beloved with the lotus-ear-ornament. || 21 ||

children.text: रामाणामतिताम्रः करः पाणिः तन्त्रीणां वीणागुणानां ताडनं वादनमेव विभ्रमं लीलां करोति विधत्ते, कान्ते पत्यौ विषये श्रवणोत्पलेनावतंसकुवलयेन ताडनं प्रहारं वा सेर्ष्यमीर्ष्यया सह वर्तमानं सासूयं करोति इति प्रकृतम्, तादृशमेव हि कर्म तस्य योग्यम् । प्रथमतृतीयपादादिविषयं यमकमिदम् ॥
children.translated_text: The excessively reddened hand (<s>kara</s>) of the women performs, arranges, the sport, the play, of plucking, of playing, the strings (<s>tantrīs</s>), the cords of the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute). In the beloved, the husband, as the object — the striking with the ear-lotus, the ornamental blue lotus worn at the ear — jealous, accompanied by jealousy — it performs, the primary meaning being: such indeed is the proper action for that hand. This is a <s>yamaka</s> in the domain of the beginning of the first and third feet.
With the splendid display of its full plumage, the peahen dances along;
the garland of clouds, set in motion by the winds, releases all its waters. || 22 ||

children.text: मेघानामाली माला सकलाः सर्वाः न काश्चिदेव । अपो जलानि विमुञ्चति वर्षति, कलापस्य बर्हभारस्योल्लसनं विस्तारः । तेन सह वर्तते सकलापोल्लसनया कलापिन्या मयूराङ्गनया प्रमुदितया अनुनृत्यते वृष्ट्यनन्तरं नट्यते । प्रथमचतुर्थपादादिगोचरं व्यपेतयमकमेतत् ॥
children.translated_text: the garland (<s>ālī</s>) of clouds releases all (<s>sakalāḥ</s>) its waters, every drop, raining down. With the display, the spreading, of the full plumage (<s>kalāpa</s>), the burden of tail-feathers — along with this, the delighted peahen, the female peacock, dances in response after the rain. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> in the domain of the beginning of the first and fourth feet.
Set in motion by the winds, gently, gently swaying —
O passionate woman! Your mind, in which the quarrel of pride is already dissolving of its own accord —

children.text: कलिकामद्य नीपस्य दृष्ट्वा कां नु स्पृशेद् दशाम् ॥ २३ ॥
children.translated_text: upon seeing the bud of the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) tree today, what state would it reach? || 23 ||

children.text: हे कामिनि ! ते तव मनश्चित्तं स्वयमात्मनैव तादृश[द्रावक]वस्तुनो दर्शनम् अन्तरेण गलति वर्तमानो मान एव कलिर्वर्तते अर्थान्तरम् । अद्य प्रावृषि नीपस्य तरोः कलिकां साक्षादिवोत्कलिकां दृष्ट्वा कां कीदृशीं दशामवस्थां स्पृशेद् गच्छेद् इति न विद्मः । सुतरां रागवक्तव्यतां यास्यतीति भावः । नु वितर्के । द्वितीयतृतीयपादादिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: O passionate woman (<s>kāminī</s>)! Your mind, your heart — of its own accord, without the sight of any such melting object, the pride (<s>māna</s>) is already dissolving, falling away, and the quarrel (<s>kali</s>) persists as something else. Now today, in the rainy season, upon seeing the bud (<s>kalikā</s>) of the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) tree — as if directly seeing desire's urging — what state, what kind of condition, would it reach? We do not know. The implication is: it will become all the more overflowing with passion. '<s>Nu</s>' expresses conjecture. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the second and third feet.
Having ascended the moonstone terrace of the pleasure-hill,
this peacock, with the tips of his beautiful crest-plumes trembling, dances! || 24 ||

children.text: एष शिखावलो मयूरः चन्द्रकस्य बर्हस्यान्तोऽग्रभागः लसन्नाकम्पमानश्चारु शोभनः चन्द्रकान्तोऽस्येति लसच्चारुचन्द्रकान्तः आक्रीडशैलस्य क्रीडापर्वतस्य सम्बन्धिनीमिमां सन्निहितचन्द्रकान्तस्य मणेस्तद्रूपां वा स्थलीं भूमिमारुह्य नृत्यति । द्वितीयचतुर्थपादादिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: This peacock (<s>śikhāvala</s>): the tip, the end, of the crest-plume (<s>candraka</s>, the 'eye' of the peacock tail) is swaying, trembling beautifully — thus 'one with beautiful trembling crest-tips.' Having ascended this terrace, this ground, of the pleasure-hill (<s>ākrīḍaśaila</s>), which is characterized by moonstone, or is of the nature of that gem — he dances. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the second and fourth feet.
The earth, rescued from the mass of kings, is now sustained by your arm;
she who was lifted by the Boar, she who rests upon the great serpent. || 25 ||

children.text: वराहेण क्रोडवपुषा विष्णुना उद्धृता जलधेर्वरस्योत्तमस्याहेः शेषस्योपरिस्थिता च या असौ सर्वा उर्वी पृथिवी राजकाद् राजसमूहाद् उद्धृता विजित्य गृहीता, अद्य सम्प्रति ते भुजेन बाहुना सर्वाभिसारिणा ध्रियते यथान्यायं परिपाल्यते । तृतीयचतुर्थपादादिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: By <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar), by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in his boar form, she was lifted from the ocean; and she who rests upon the excellent serpent <s>Śeṣa</s> — that entire earth, rescued from the mass of kings, seized by conquering them, is now, at present, sustained, properly protected, by your arm, the all-conquering one. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the third and fourth feet.
By your hand that makes an end of enemies in battles,
the war-elephants, struck, streaming with blood, shine like evening clouds. || 26 ||

children.text: ते तव करेण भुजेन [रणेषु] द्विषतां शत्रूणामन्तं नाशं करोत्यन्तकरेण हता [जनित]क्षताः करेणवो द्विषतां हस्तिनः क्षरद्रक्तं रुधिरमेषामिति क्षरद्रक्ताः तथा सन्तः सन्ध्यानुरक्ता घनाः सान्ध्यघना इव सरागधरापयोधरा इव भान्ति । प्रथमद्वितीयतृतीयपादादिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: By your hand (<s>kara</s>), your arm — making an end (<s>antakara</s>), bringing destruction, of enemies in battles — the war-elephants of the enemies, struck, wounded, streaming with blood — thus 'streaming with blood' — appearing so, they shine like clouds at twilight, like evening clouds suffused with redness, like rain-bearing clouds tinted with the colors of sunset. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first, second, and third feet.
Like a row of trees on a mountain shattered by winds, the enemy army was shattered by warriors;
and the sky was as if departed, covered everywhere with dust. || 27 ||

children.text: परा शत्रुभूता चमूः सेना भटैः शूरैर्ध्वस्ता भग्ना । कथमिव ? अगे पर्वते [स्थितानां] तरूणां राजिः संघातो वातैरिव । अत्र च व्य[ति]करे [क्वापि] क्वचित् स्थानेऽनिर्दिष्टे परागैः पांशुभिः समरसंक्षोभप्रभवैस्ततं व्याप्तमम्बरमाकाशमिदं परागतं विद्रुतं लीनमिवाभूत् । एवमतितुमुलं

children.translated_text: was the battle. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first, third, and fourth feet.

The hostile (<s>parā</s>) army was shattered, broken, by warriors, by heroes. Like what? Like a row of trees on a mountain (<s>aga</s>), by winds. And in this tumult, in some unspecified place, the sky was covered, pervaded, with dust rising from the upheaval of battle — as if it too had departed (<s>parāgata</s>), had fled, had concealed itself. Thus exceedingly violent
May the blessed lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> protect you, of ever fresh cloud-like radiance,
he the destroyer of the <s>Dānava</s> clan, the slayer of the foremost elephant with rut-flow! || 28 ||

children.text: स त्रैलोक्यविख्यातः विष्णुर्भगवानिति पूजावचनम् । वो युष्मान् पातु अपायाद् रक्षतु सदा नित्यम् । नवस्य नूतनस्य जलगर्भस्य घनस्य मेघस्येव द्युतिर्दीप्तिः अस्येति नवघनद्युतिः । श्याम इति यावत् । दानवानामसुराणां कुलं ध्वंसयति इति दानवकुलध्वंसी । सह दानेन मदेन वर्तते सदानो मत्तः । वरश्चासौ दन्ती च सदानश्चासौ वरदन्ती च कुवलयापीडादिः तं हतवान् सदानवरदन्तिहा । द्वितीयतृतीयचतुर्थपादादिव्यपेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: He, renowned in the three worlds — '<s>Bhagavān</s>' is a term of reverence — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, may he protect you from harm, always, eternally. His radiance is like that of a fresh, new, water-bearing cloud — thus 'of fresh-cloud radiance.' Meaning: he is dark-complexioned. He destroys the clan of <s>Dānavas</s>, the demons — thus 'destroyer of the <s>Dānava</s> clan.' '<s>Sadāna</s>' means one who is constantly in rut, intoxicated; and '<s>varadantī</s>' is a foremost tusker such as <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> — he who slew such a one is '<s>sadānavaradantihā</s>.' This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the second, third, and fourth feet.
With hair like that of a bee at its tip, with a face that causes jealousy in the lotus,
you who make the lotus something not worth painting — among those who are prone to love-madness, like <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī)! || 29 ||

children.text: ते तव कं शिरः । समाः केशा अस्येति समकेशम् । कस्य ? अलेर्भ्रमरस्य अलिन इत्यर्थः । भृङ्गस्येव श्यामशिरोरुहं तव शोभतेतराम् । मुखं च ते कमलेन पद्मेन सहेर्ष्याकरम् । तत्साम्यात् कमलमिव मुखं विराजत इत्यर्थः । एवं वराङ्गी त्वं कमला लक्ष्मीरिवोन्मदिष्णुषु ये केचित् कामोन्मादशीलास्तेषु मध्ये कं नाम पुरुषम् अलेख्यमगणनीयमुन्मदिष्णुतया करोषि ? यस्तज्जां शोभामीदृशीं पश्यति तं सर्वमेवोन्मादयसि न किञ्चिन्मुञ्चसीत्यर्थः । पादचतुष्ट्यादिव्यपेतयमकमेकजातीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Your head (<s>ka</s>) — hair that is smooth like that of a bee (<s>ali</s>), at its tip. Your face, together with the lotus, causes jealousy — because of its similarity to the lotus, your face shines like a lotus. Thus, O beautiful-limbed one, you, like <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), among those who are prone to love-madness — what man do you make uncountable, negligible, through their madness? Whoever sees such beauty is maddened — you do not spare anyone, such is the meaning. This is a <s>yamaka</s> of one type at the beginning of all four feet, with interruption.
Accompanied by a lover with delight, adorned with magnificent gem-ornaments,
with intoxicated, wandering eyes, with ample hips — they are capable of [conquering]. || 30 ||

children.text: अदभ्रजघनाः स्त्रियो मदेन यौवनमधुपानादिसम्भूतेन । भ्रमन्त्यो दृशो नेत्राण्यासामिति मदभ्रमदृशः । उदारा महार्हा मणयः पद्मरागेन्द्रनीलादयः रत्नमेखलादिस्वभावा भूषणमलङ्कारो यासामिति उदारमणिभूषणाः सत्यः । मुदा प्रीत्या अन्वितं युक्तं रमणं वल्लभं कर्तृं क्षमाः शक्नुवन्ति । रमणमतितरां मोदयन्तीति यावत् । पादचतुष्टये पादादिव्यपेतयमकमेकजातीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: Women with ample hips (<s>adabhrajaghanāḥ</s>), with intoxication born of youth, wine-drinking, and the like — their eyes wander, roll, due to intoxication, thus they have 'intoxicated wandering eyes.' Adorned with magnificent, precious gems — rubies, sapphires, and the like, forming jeweled girdles and similar ornaments — thus 'adorned with magnificent gem-ornaments.' With delight (<s>mudā</s>), with joy, they are capable of making, of rendering, a lover (<s>ramaṇa</s>) accompanied, united. Meaning: they delight the lover exceedingly. This is a <s>yamaka</s> of one type with interruption at the beginning of all four feet.
By the cries of the cuckoos, nourished by others, my mind has been stolen;
and by your uttered words too, O messenger-woman, and by the gentle southern breezes too! || 31 ||

children.text: हे दूति ! अन्यपुष्टानां कोकिलानां सम्बन्धिभिरारुतैः शब्दैरुदितैः सम्पन्नैः मे मम मनो हृतं गृहीतम् । न केवलमेभिः । ते तवोदितैरालापैः पेशलैदक्षिणैर्मारुतैरपि
पवनैश्च हृतमिति प्रकृतम् । प्रथमतृतीययोर्द्वितीयचतुर्थयोश्च पादयोरादितो व्यपेतयमकम ॥
children.translated_text: the southern winds — it has been stolen — this is the primary meaning. This is an interrupted <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the first and third feet, and the second and fourth feet.

O messenger-woman (<s>dūtī</s>)! By the cries, the sounds, of the cuckoos (<s>anyapuṣṭas</s>, those nourished by others), that have arisen, that have been produced — my mind has been stolen, seized. Not only by these. By your uttered words too, your charming, courteous utterances, and by the breezes too,
Women, having conquered the modesty of young men, dwell upon their bodies;
slender-waisted, with moon-like faces beautified by flowing perspiration. || 32 ||

children.text: स्त्रियो यूनां तनुमङ्गमध्यासते अधिशेरते पुरुषायितयोगेन । किंभूताः ? सुरया मदिरया जिता उत्सा

रिता ह्रीस्त्रषा अस्यामिति सुराजितह्रियोऽत्यन्तमत्ताः । तनु क्षामं मध्यमुदरमासामिति तनुमध्याः, क्षरता स्वेदेन श्रमजलेन मुक्ताजालकेनैव सुष्ठु राजितमलंकृतं मुखमिन्दुकान्त्यादिना आसामिति क्षरत्स्वेदसुराजितमुखेन्दवः । द्वितीयतृतीययोः प्रथमचतुर्थयोश्च पादयोरादितो व्यतेतयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: their modesty overcome — thus '<s>surājitahriyaḥ</s>' means utterly intoxicated. '<s>Tanumadhyāḥ</s>' means having slender waists, thin in the middle, the abdomen. '<s>Kṣaratsveda-surājita-mukhendavaḥ</s>' means their moon-like faces are beautifully adorned by the flowing perspiration, the exertion-sweat, like a net of pearls, radiant with the luster of the moon and the like. In the second and third, and the first and fourth quarter-verses, there is <s>vyapeta-yamaka</s> (separated syllabic repetition) from the beginning. ||
Women mount upon the bodies of young men through the practice of <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top position). Of what kind? Conquered by <s>surā</s> (liquor), intoxicated,
Thus the variety of <s>vyapeta-yamaka</s> (separated syllabic repetition) has also been shown.
There also exists a variety whose nature is mixed — both separated and unseparated — as follows: || 33 ||

children.text: एवं विकल्प्य निगमयति—इत्युक्तेन विधिना व्यपेतस्य यमकस्य प्रभेदोऽपि विकल्पश्चैव प्रकृतो दर्शित उदाह्रितः । न केवलमव्यपेतमयमकविकल्प इति अपिशब्देनाचष्टे । अव्यपेतव्यपेतश्चात्मा स्वभावो व्यामिश्रो यस्य विकल्पस्य, प्रकरणाद् यमकसम्बन्धिनः, सोऽप्यस्ति, न केवलमुक्तः शुद्धः । अस्येति पाठे अस्य यमकस्य सम्बन्धी विद्यत इति गम्यते । कीदृशोऽसौ ? तद्यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Having thus distinguished, he concludes: in the manner stated, the variety, indeed the classification, of the separated <s>yamaka</s> has been shown, illustrated. Not only the unseparated <s>yamaka</s> variety — this is indicated by the word '<s>api</s>' (also). A variety whose nature (<s>ātmā</s>) is mixed, combining both unseparated and separated — of the <s>yamaka</s> type, as understood from the context — that too exists, not merely the pure type stated. In the reading '<s>asya</s>' (of this), it is understood that there exists [a variety] belonging to this <s>yamaka</s>. Of what kind is it? He illustrates with 'as follows' —
That friend is unable to behold the <s>sāla</s> tree with buds clinging to its branches,
nor the row of bees clinging to the <s>vakula</s> trees, nor even the lotus-ponds. || 34 ||

children.text: सा आली सखी काचिद् विवक्षिता विरहातुरा वीक्षितुं न अलं [न] शक्नोति, किम् ? आलम्बनमालम्बः सह तेन वर्तते सालम्बा आलम्बमानाः समन्ततोऽवरूढा इत्यर्थः । सालम्बाः कलिका यासां सालानां शाखानां ताः सालम्बकलिकासाला यस्य सालस्य तरुविशेषस्य सर्जस्य तमीक्षितुं विरहज्वरसम्भूतामनोरोचकत्वा[न्ना]लम् । सालम्बाः कलिका एव परिक्षेपसाधर्म्येण सालः प्राकारो यम्येत्यपि व्याख्यायते । न केवलमेवम् । आलीनाः श्लिष्टा वकुलाः केसरतरवः पुष्पसमृद्धियोगाद् यैरित्यालीनवकुलान् अलीन् भ्रमरानपि पूर्ववद्वीक्षितुं नालमिति प्रकृतम् । नालमस्यास्तीति

नालीकं पद्मम् । अन्येषां दृश्यत इति दीर्घत्वम् । तद्विद्यते आसामिति नालीकिनीः पद्मिनीरपि वीक्षितुं नालमिति प्रकृतम् । दुष्करं वराकी जीविष्यतीति काचिद् विरहिणीं सखीमुद्दिश्य कञ्चिदेवं वक्तीति प्रथमद्वितीययोस्तृतीयचतुर्थयोश्च पादयोरादितोऽव्यपेतव्यपेतं यमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Nālīka</s>' means lotus. In other readings, the lengthening is seen. Those which possess these — '<s>nālīkinīḥ</s>' means lotus-ponds — she is unable to behold them either. 'Poor thing, it will be hard for her to survive!' — thus someone says this about a friend who is in separation. In the first and second, and the third and fourth quarter-verses, from the beginning, there is mixed separated-unseparated <s>yamaka</s>. ||

That friend (<s>ālī</s>), a certain intended companion, afflicted by separation, is not able to behold — what? The <s>sāla</s> tree — '<s>sālamba</s>' means 'having support,' that is, clinging, rooted all around — whose buds (<s>kalikā</s>) are supported, clinging to the branches (<s>sālā</s>) of the <s>sāla</s>, a particular tree, the <s>sarja</s> — she cannot bear to behold it, due to the disgust born of the fever of separation. The supported buds, like an enclosure by way of similarity, are also explained as a wall (<s>sāla</s>, rampart). Not only this. The <s>vakulas</s> (<s>kesara</s> trees), with their abundance of blossoms by which bees have clung (<s>ālīna</s>) to them — nor even the bees (<s>alī</s>) — she is unable to behold them, as before. '<s>Nālī</s>' —
Unable to behold the time whose stars and constellations are invisible,
the time filled with great dark clouds whose thunder resounds loudly. || 35 ||

children.text: कालं समयं काला महान्तो घना अस्मिन्निति कालमहाघनम् । विपुलनीलजलदम् । तारस्य भावस्तारता उच्चैस्तरत्वम् । तया गाम्भीर्ययोगेन रम्यं कान्तं रसितं गर्हितं मेघसम्बन्धि यस्मिन्निति

तारतारम्यरसितं गम्भीरघनगर्जितगर्भम् । अनालक्ष्यास्तिरोहिताः, मेघपिहितत्वात् । तारा उज्ज्वलास्तारका नक्षत्राणि अस्मिन्निति अनालक्ष्यतारतारकं कालं विरहिणि जने कृतान्त[सदृश]मतिदुःसहत्वाद् वीक्षितुं का नाम स्त्री संयुक्ताऽपि प्रागेव वियुक्ता । अलं शक्नोति ? नैव काचित् । इति प्रावृष उत्कण्ठाकारित्वमुद्भावितम् । प्रथमचतुर्थयोर्द्वितीयतृतीययोरादितोऽव्यपेतव्यपेतयमकं नैकजातीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: combined with depth, the thunder (<s>rasita</s>), the rumbling of the clouds, is beautiful, pleasing — containing within it the deep rumbling of the clouds. The stars, being hidden, concealed by the clouds, are invisible — '<s>anālakṣya-tāra-tāraka</s>' means the bright stars and constellations are invisible in it. Such a time (<s>kāla</s>), like death for the person in separation, being utterly unbearable — what woman, whether united or especially separated, can bear to behold it? None at all. Thus the anguish-causing nature of the rainy season is expressed. In the first and fourth, and the second and third quarter-verses, from the beginning, there is mixed separated-unseparated <s>yamaka</s> of more than one kind. ||

'<s>Kāla</s>' means the season; '<s>kāla-mahā-ghana</s>' means one in which there are great, dense, dark clouds — [a time] with vast, dark rain-clouds. The quality of being '<s>tāra</s>' (loud), its loudness — with that,
Night, whose length depends on three <s>yāmas</s> (watches), brings us toward death;
that very night has been churned, that is, destroyed, by me, a fool, whose beloved suffers anguish of her life-breath. || 36 ||

children.text: यामानां त्रयं त्रयोः प्रहराः । तत्राधीन आयत्त आयामो दैर्घ्यं यस्यास्तया निशा रात्र्या वर्षायमाणया हेतुभूतया मरणमनुयामो गच्छामो वयं भवदर्थे । तन्नेदमस्मान् दुनोति । किं त्विदमतिकष्टम्- यामङ्गनामहं गतवानस्मि सेदानीमसूनामार्तिं पीडामायातीत्यस्वार्त्याया प्राणार्तिदुःखनिर्वेशा
निर्वेशस्तु पुमान् भोगे वेतने मूर्च्छनेऽपि च इति मेदिनी ॥

। मया अधिया तत्परित्यागात् दुर्बुद्धिनेदृशेन मया सा मथितैव हतैव । नात्र सन्देहः । न हि सा मद्विरहिता जीवति वराकी । स्वविरहदुःखनिमित्तत्वात् तन्मरणस्य मया मथितैवत्युक्तम् । एवं विपद्यमानेन मया सह सापि वराकी मथिताऽनया निशेति वा योज्यम् । एवं वियुक्तः कश्चित् कामी प्रियामनुशोचति । पादचतुष्टयादियमकं व्यपेतमव्यपेत[मेक]रूपम् ॥
children.translated_text: by me, of evil mind, due to my abandonment of her — by such a me, she has been churned, destroyed indeed. There is no doubt about this. For that poor woman does not survive separated from me. Since her death is caused by the suffering of separation from me, it is said 'churned by me indeed.' Thus, being ruined together with me — or it may be construed: that poor woman too has been churned by this night together with me. Thus a certain separated lover laments his beloved. The <s>yamaka</s> from the beginning of the four quarter-verses is separated and unseparated, of a single form. ||

Three watches (<s>yāma</s>) — three <s>praharas</s> (periods). The night whose length (<s>āyāma</s>), whose extension, depends upon those three watches, that night, as the raining season serves as the cause — we approach death, we go toward it, on your account. That does not torment us. But this is exceedingly painful: '<s>yāma</s>' — I went to that woman, and now she has arrived at the anguish, the suffering, of her life-breaths — '<s>asvārtyā</s>' means one submerged in the suffering and distress of her vital breaths,
He summarizes the varieties of <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of quarter-verses —
Thus has been shown the nature of the varieties of <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of quarter-verses;
in the same way, other <s>yamakas</s> too should be classified. || 37 ||

children.text: इत्युक्तेन प्रकारेण आदिश्चासौ पादश्च, अवयवे समुदायोपचारात् । तत्र यमकं पादादियमकमित्यर्थः । तस्य विकल्पः प्रभेदः । तस्याव्यपेतस्य व्यपेतस्य च गतिः स्वरूपमीदृश्येवंविधा दर्शितेति शेषः । आदिपादयमकवत् मध्यान्तपादयमकमनुगन्तव्यमित्यतिदिशति- एवमादिपादयमकविकल्पन्यायेनैव इतराणि मध्यान्तवर्तीन्यपि, न केवलं पूर्वाणि । यमकानि सुकराणि प्रभेद्यानि, स्वयमनुगन्तव्यानि, दिशस्तादृशो दर्शितत्वात् ।
children.translated_text: In the manner stated, '<s>ādi</s>' (beginning) refers to the quarter-verse — the term for the whole applied to the part. The <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the quarter-verse is '<s>pādādiyamaka</s>' — that is the meaning. Its variety, its classification — the nature of both the unseparated and the separated types — has been shown to be of such a form as described. Just as with the <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning, those occurring at the middle and end of the quarter-verse should also be understood — he extends the principle: by the very same method of classifying the <s>yamaka</s> varieties at the beginning of the quarter-verse, the others too, occurring at the middle and end, not only the previous ones. <s>Yamakas</s> that are easy [to compose] should be classified, should be understood on one's own, since the direction of such a kind has been shown.
And they should be classified thus —
O friend! Somehow conciliate that sweet-spoken beloved of yours,

children.text: आनय त्वरितं कुर्मः कर्म भूयो न तादृशाम् ॥
children.translated_text: and bring her quickly — let us not commit such a deed again. ||
the splendor of an ascetic, he always bestows [blessings].
Having attained, through the conquest of the senses,
When you rule, O master, the world rejoices in both worlds. ||
Having gone to another land, I am not able to earn wealth;

children.text: प्रिये विना विनाशं त्वामसवो यान्ति मे ध्रुवम् ॥
children.translated_text: O beloved, without you, my life-breaths surely go toward destruction. ||
O proud and wealthy one, abandon your pride! The thunder of dense clouds —
what will this season do to one whose splendor and livelihood depend on the beloved? ||
May the <s>Tathāgata</s> (the Buddha) grant such a boon
by which the unconquerable
sense-objects, those causes of various diseases, are conquered. ||
Those heroes who are skilled in statecraft, who conquer the existence born of vice,
those great souls who are devoted to the protection of their subjects — they are the valiant ones. ||
O king, of you whose kingdom is purified by truth, constantly, this [arm],
terrifying to enemies, becomes like a wish-fulfilling tree for you. ||
May the foot of Him who possesses the six supernatural powers, the destroyer of the six faults,
by whom the army famed for conquering the world was, though unconquered, conquered — protect you! ||
Thus the <s>yamaka</s> at the middle and end of two and four quarter-verses should be classified. ||

children.text: तान्यपि किं न विकल्प्यन्ते इति चेदाह—
children.translated_text: If one asks why those too are not fully classified, he says —
Out of fear of prolixity, the varieties are not desired to be stated in their entirety;
only some that are considered difficult are shown there. || 38 ||

children.text: भेदा यमकविकल्पाः सुकराः कार्त्स्नेन साकल्येन [न] लक्षिताः [यतः] पादमध्यान्तभाविनोऽपि आख्यातुं दर्शयितुं [न] ईप्सिता नेष्टा अस्माभिः । कुतः ? प्रपञ्चेति ग्रन्थविस्तरभयाद् हेतोः । मा भूदतिविस्तर इति संक्षिप्तकाव्यलक्षणप्रणयनप्रतिज्ञानात् । तस्मात् केचिदेव भेदाः प्रकाराः दर्शिताः । इदानीं तु तत्र यमकेषु दुष्करत्वेन दुष्करा इत्येवाभिमता इष्टा दुष्करा एव न सुकरा अपि भेदा मध्ययमकादिविकल्पाः केचन कियन्तो, न सर्वे प्रपञ्चभयात् निदर्श्यन्ते ॥
children.translated_text: The varieties, the <s>yamaka</s> classifications, that are easy — have not been characterized in their entirety, completely, [because] even those occurring at the beginning, middle, and end of the quarter-verse are not desired, not wished, by us to be stated, to be shown. Why? Due to the fear of prolixity, of excessive length of the treatise, as the reason. Lest there be excessive elaboration — since the promise was to compose a concise poetics. Therefore only some varieties, some types, have been shown. But now, among those <s>yamakas</s>, some — a certain number, not all — that are considered, regarded as, difficult, that are indeed difficult, not easy — the middle-<s>yamaka</s> and other varieties — are shown as examples, out of fear of prolixity. ||
O you of steadfast prosperity, you who are controlled in the senses! You, a practitioner, do not decline;
though free from deceit, you strive; for your sake, happiness does not approach decay. || 39 ||

children.text: स्थिरा अनपायिन्यः, तत्कारणानुष्ठानाविच्छेदात् । आयतिरुभयलोकाभ्युदयरूपा अस्येति स्थिरायते इत्यामन्त्रणमेतत् कस्यचित् । अन्यकार्यान्निरुद्धानि संवृतानि इद्रियाणि बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि चक्षुरादीनि कर्मेन्द्रियाणि पादादीनि वा येनेति यतेन्द्रियो भवान् यतेर्मुनेर्न हीयते नावकृष्यते यतेन्द्रियत्वादेव । न केवलमेतत् । न विद्यते माया परवञ्चना यस्य अमायस्तस्य भावोऽमायता [निःशाठ्यं] परोपकारिता च, तव इयते एतावते महते क्षयं नाशम् अयते अगच्छते स्थिराय सुखाय कामायेति चित्तानुग्रहाय नित्यसुखार्थमभूत् । सर्वत्र सम्पन्नो भवान् । न क्वचिदपि विपन्न इत्यर्थः ।

children.translated_text: This is middle-<s>yamaka</s> of a single form, unseparated in nature, across four quarter-verses — and precisely therefore difficult of such a kind.

'<s>Sthirāyate</s>' — 'steadfast,' meaning imperishable — due to the unbroken performance of their causes. One whose future prosperity, characterized by the welfare of both worlds, is such — '<s>sthirāyate</s>' is an address to a certain person. One whose sense organs — the cognitive faculties such as the eye and the like, or the motor faculties such as the feet and the like — are restrained, controlled, prevented from other activities — such a person, you, do not decline, are not diminished, from the state of an ascetic (<s>yati</s>), precisely because of being one who has controlled the senses. Not only this: one in whom there is no deceit (<s>māyā</s>), no deception of others — '<s>amāya</s>' — its state is sincerity and benevolence toward others. For you, of such magnitude, this does not approach decay, destruction — it has become [eternal], for the sake of lasting, steady happiness, for the gratification of the mind, for eternal bliss. You are accomplished in every way. You are not deficient in anything — that is the meaning.
beautified by wealth, your [virtues] are praised.
In assemblies, O king, by the mouths of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, unpolluted by liquor,

children.text: न भासुरा यान्ति सुरान्न ते गुणाः

children.translated_text: among subjects devoted in their affection, they have attained abundance. || 40 ||
Your radiant qualities do not [merely] reach the gods;

children.text: हे राजन्, सभासु परिषत्सु महीसुराणां ब्राह्मणानां मुखैः किभूतैः ? सुरया हतेति, न तथा असुराहतास्तेरमद्यदूषितैः पवित्रैः । वसुना धनेन यथाकामं प्रतिपादितेन राजितैः प्रीतियोगात् विकसितैः कर्तृभूतैः स्तुता वर्णितास्ते तव त्यागसत्त्वशौर्यादयो भासुराः, दोपासङ्करादुज्ज्वलाः परिशुद्धाः प्रजासु इह लोकेषु रागोऽनुरक्तिर्नृपविषय आत्मा स्वभावस्तत्प्रधानत्वाद् यासामिति रागात्मसु मन्त्रानुरक्तासु विषये राशितां प्रचयतामभिव्याप्तियोगेन गता मर्त्यलोकं सकल व्याप्य कीर्तिद्वारेण सुरान् देवान् न न यान्ति कि तु यान्तेव । स्वर्गेऽपि प्रसिद्धास्ते इत्यर्थः । चतुष्पादमध्ययमकमेकरूपं व्यपेतमिति ॥
children.translated_text: O king, in assemblies, in gatherings, by the mouths of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the earth-gods — of what kind? '<s>Asurāhata</s>' means not struck by liquor — that is, not polluted by wine, pure. Beautified, gladdened, by wealth (<s>vasu</s>) generously bestowed, serving as agents, your [virtues] — valor, courage, heroism, and the like — are praised, described, being radiant, brilliant due to the absence of any taint of fault, pure. Among the subjects, in these worlds — whose nature (<s>ātmā</s>) is devotion, attachment toward the king, predominantly so — among such devoted subjects, your qualities have attained abundance, the state of being heaped, pervading all. Having pervaded the entire mortal world through the gate of fame, they do not not reach — rather, they do reach — the gods, the celestials. You are famous even in heaven — that is the meaning. This is middle-<s>yamaka</s> of a single form, separated, across four quarter-verses. ||
a radiant ornament is to be worn here,
Your beloved, of good conduct, unwavering — she by whom
no fruit whatsoever is there for me from her who possesses beauty. || 41 ||
she who is intoxicated by the special delight of the festival of love —

children.text: हे सच्चरिताप्रमत्त इति सरोषं विरुद्धलक्षणमामन्त्रणम् । दुर्वृत्तप्रमत्तेति गम्यते । सहस्राक्षोऽन्ध इति यथा । असच्चरिते विप्रिये वा अप्रमत्ता अवहिता असच्चरिताप्रमत्त व्यलीकशील इति संबोध्यते । या तव प्रिया बल्लभा तया रतमेवोत्सवस्तत्र स एव वा आमोदविशेषः प्रीत्यतिशयः तेन मत्तया गर्वितया । अंशवोऽस्मिन् सन्तीत्यंशुमद् भासुरं [वि]भूषणं मेखलादिकं धार्यमङ्गे निवेश्यम् । तस्याः प्रसाधनं सफलं किमस्माकं तेन विफलेन भारमात्रेण ! कान्तिमत्तया विभूष[णोत्थया] मे मम न किञ्चित् फलं प्रयोजनमस्ति । एवमप्यहं तव द्वेष्येव । तव परवशस्य । इहेति वाचोयुक्तौ । इह वा प्रस्तावे, काचिदङ्गना प्रियं प्रस्तावे क्वचित् प्रसाधने नियुञ्जानं एवमीर्ष्यति । पादचतुष्टयान्तयमकमेकरूपव्यपेतमिति ॥
children.translated_text: 'O you of good conduct and unwavering nature' — this is an angry address with contradictory characterization. What is understood is 'O you of wicked conduct and dissolute nature.' Just as '<s>Sahasrākṣa</s>' (thousand-eyed) is used to mean 'blind.' 'O shameful one' — thus he is addressed as one unwavering in misconduct, deceitful in character. She who is your beloved, your darling — by her, intoxicated, proud, with the special delight, the excess of pleasure, that is the festival of love itself, or in it — a radiant ornament (<s>vibhūṣaṇa</s>), such as a girdle and the like, is to be worn, to be placed on the body. Her adornment is fruitful — what use is this fruitless [ornament] to us, a mere burden! No fruit, no purpose whatsoever, exists for me from the beauty arising from [her] ornament. 'Even so I am hateful to you, who are in another's power.' '<s>Iha</s>' is a mere expletive. Or, in this context, a certain woman, seeing her beloved engaged in adorning another on some occasion, expresses jealousy thus. This is end-<s>yamaka</s> of a single form, separated, across four quarter-verses. ||
for indeed, destitution and lordship are opposed;
Those like you, O lord, do not know the savor of bowing,

children.text: य एव दीनाः शिरसा नतेन ते

children.translated_text: and go about amply immersed in the savor of wretchedness. || 42 ||
those who are wretched bow their heads before you

children.text: हे नाथ स्वामिन् ! भवादृशास्त्वद्विधा महात्मानः नतेः परप्रणामस्य रसं स्वादं कीदृशोऽसाविति न जानते न विदन्ति । न नमन्तीति यावत् । किं कारणम् ? खलु यस्मात् सन्नोऽवसन्नो दुर्गतस्तस्य भावः सन्नता । इनस्य भाव इनता । सन्ततेनते दौर्गत्यैश्वर्ये नाम विरुद्धे परस्परव्याहते ।
children.translated_text: O lord, O master! Those like you, those great souls of your kind, do not know, do not understand, the savor, the taste, of bowing, of prostration before others. They do not bow — that is the sense. For what reason? Because indeed destitution (<s>sannata</s>) — the state of one who is lowly, fallen, unfortunate — and lordship (<s>inata</s>), the state of being a lord — are opposed, are mutually contradictory.

children.text: यदि सन्नः कथमिनः ? अथेनः कथं सन्नः ? तादृशश्चे[नो] नातिरसज्ञः [सन्नतायाः] इति भावः । त्वं चेनः तस्माद् भवादृशा नते रसं न जानत इति निगमनीयम् । के तर्हि नतिरसज्ञा इत्याह—य इत्यादि । य एव केचिद् दीना दुर्गतास्त एव ते तवेनस्य [सविध इति शेषः] नतेन सप्रणिपातेन शिरसा पूर्वोक्तेन दैन्येन कार्पण्येन तद्विधास्वाद्यत्वाद् रसेन लक्षिताः सन्तोऽल म[त्य]र्थं चरन्ति प्रवर्तन्ते । ऐश्वर्यं न क्वचिन्नमति । दारिद्रयमेव सर्वत्र प्रणिपतति इति पिण्डार्थः । चतुष्पादान्तयमकमेकरूपमव्यपेतात्मकमिति ॥
children.translated_text: If one is destitute, how can one be a lord? If one is a lord, how is one destitute? And if one is such a lord, then one is not a knower of the savor [of destitution and bowing] — such is the purport. And you are a lord; therefore those like you do not know the savor of bowing — this should be understood as the conclusion. Who then are the knowers of the savor of bowing? He says, beginning with 'those who' — those who are wretched, those who are unfortunate — those very ones, before you, the lord [— this is supplied] — with bowed heads, with prostration, as described earlier, marked by the savor of wretchedness, of poverty, being of such a kind that it can be savored — they go about, they engage, greatly. Lordship never bows anywhere; it is only poverty that prostrates everywhere — this is the summary meaning. This is end-<s>yamaka</s> of a single form, unseparated in nature, across four quarter-verses. ||
with her light glance, weighty; with her gait;
With her playful smile, pure; with her gentle speech;

children.text: सा हन्ति तेन गलितं मम जीवितेन ॥ ४३ ॥
children.translated_text: she slays — and thereby my life has slipped away. || 43 ||
with the display of her blossoming hips,

children.text: लीलास्मितेन विलासहसितेन शुचिना विशदेन मृदुना कोमलेनोदितेनालापेन लघुना लोलेन च व्यलोकितेन वीक्षितेन गुरुणा मन्थरेण गतेन गमनेन व्याजृम्भितेन विस्तीर्णेन जघनेन नितम्बेन च दर्शितेन सर्वेणैतेन मन्मथशस्त्रप्रकरायमाणेन सा काचिदङ्गना हन्ति । प्रदत्तेन घातेन मर्मावेधहेतुना गलितं विगतं मम जीवितेन । नान्यदिह किञ्चित् कारणमिति कश्चित् कामातुरो विरौति । चतुष्पादमध्यान्तयमकमेकरूपं व्यपेतम् ॥
children.translated_text: With a playful smile, a coquettish laugh; with a pure, clear, soft, gentle utterance that has arisen; with a light, wavering glance, a look; with a slow, unhurried gait, a walk; and with a prominently displayed, broad hip, a buttock — by all of this, which appears like a mass of <s>Manmatha's</s> (the god of love's) weapons, displayed by her, a certain woman slays. By the blow thus dealt, which is the cause of piercing the vital points, my life has departed, has ceased. There is no other cause here — thus a certain love-stricken man cries out. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> (alliteration) at the middle and end, of one type, interrupted.
whose honor expands in a world that bows down, he who brings his own nature —
He who is glorious, whose measure equals the path of the immortals,
whose eminence is incomparable — bow to him! || 44 ||
his immensity — he who is eternal, whose names are immeasurable,

children.text: श्रीमान् नित्यं लक्ष्म्या युक्तः । न क्वचिदेकत्र[स्थः] सर्वमयत्वादित्यमान् विभुरिति यावत् । स्थितिमान् सदा स्थित्यनुगतः नित्य [इत्यर्थः] । एवंभूतो य आत्मानं

स्वभावं भूमानं बहुतां विश्वरूपत्वात् । आनयति प्रापयति । किंभूतम् ? अमरवर्त्मना आकाशेन समानं तुल्यं मानं प्रमाणं यस्येत्यमरवर्त्मसमानमानम् आकाशवदप्रमाणम् । आनते भक्तिमति जगति जनेषु प्र[थ]मानो विजृम्भमाणो मानः पूजा यस्येत्यानतजगत्प्रथमानमानं जगत्पूज्यम् । आनते जगति [प्रथमानः] प्रादुर्भवन् मानोऽनुग्रहो य[स्य] इति [वा] योज्यम् । तमेवंविधं विष्णुमानमत हे जनाः
children.translated_text: his immensity (<s>bhūman</s>), his manifoldness, because of his universal form. He brings it forth. Of what kind? Whose measure (<s>māna</s>) equals that of the path of the immortals, that is, the sky — meaning immeasurable like the sky. In the world that bows down in devotion, whose expanding honor, worship, is thus — meaning worthy of the world's reverence. Or it should be construed: in the bowing world, whose grace manifests. Bow down to him, such a <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O people —
thus the remainder

children.text: । पुनः किंविशिष्टम् ? अमानान्यपरिमितानि नामानि यस्ये[त्य]माननामानं सर्वमयत्वादनन्ताभिधानम् । अप्रतिमानोऽनुपमः मानोऽभ्युन्नतिरस्येत्यप्रतिमानमानम् ।
children.translated_text: . Furthermore, of what distinction? Whose names are immeasurable (<s>amāna</s>), unlimited — meaning of infinite appellations because of being all-pervading. Incomparable (<s>apratimāna</s>), without equal; whose eminence, whose exaltation — thus '<s>apratimānamāna</s>'.

children.text: क्वचिदानमतेति पाठः । तत्र बलिबन्धने भुवं मितवन्तं भूमानंम् आनानां प्राणिनां [मतं] शरणतया इष्टमात्मानं परपुरुषं विष्णुम् । तमित्यर्थाद् य इत्युपात्तत्वात् । आनमत् हे जना इति व्याख्येयम् । शेषं समानम् । चतुष्पादमध्यान्तयमकमेकरूपमव्यपेतव्यपेतात्मकम् ॥
children.translated_text: In some readings '<s>ānamata</s>' appears. In that case: him who measured the earth at the binding of <s>Bali</s>, the immense one (<s>bhūman</s>); desired by living beings as a refuge, the supreme person (<s>parapuruṣa</s>), <s>Viṣṇu</s>. 'Him' is understood from the context since 'who' has been employed. 'Bow down, O people!' — thus it should be explained. The rest is the same. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> at the middle and end, of one type, of both interrupted and uninterrupted character.

<s>Śrīmān</s> — always endowed with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity). Not situated in any single place, because of being all-pervading — thus '<s>amān</s>' means the all-pervading one. '<s>Sthitimān</s>' — always accompanied by permanence, meaning eternal. Such a one brings, leads forth, his own nature (<s>ātman</s>),
she who is substantial, bearing much gold, him —
Delighting him who impels with his chest,
she regards even the elixir of life as worthless. || 45 ||
she whose girdle-bells imitate the calls of cranes,

children.text: सा काचिदभिमता स्त्री सारभूतमुत्कृष्टमुरुसारं सुवर्णं भूषणीकृतं धारयतीति मुरुसारधरा । उरुसारधरेति पाठे- उरुसारं स्त्रीजनोचितं गुणोत्कर्षं धारयतीति व्याख्येयम् । सहारसेन रणितेन वर्तन्त इति सारसा पक्षिणः

। सारसै रसद्भिरनुकृता तुल्या तत्समानशब्दत्वात् सारसकाञ्ची मेखला यस्या इति सारसानुकृतसारसकाञ्ची तमिष्टं कञ्चित् । पाठान्तरे- सारभूतं नागरकवृत्तसम्पन्नम् । सारयन्तं रसादुपरमयन्तम् । उरसा पयोधरभारेण परिरम्भेण रमयन्ती रन्तुं प्रयुञ्जाना आत्मना सुखयन्ती वा, रसायनमजरत्वादिसुखयोगमपि असारमल्पमेवेति मन्यते । सुरतसुखमेव भृशं बहु मन्यते । तथाविधो हि तदाभिमानो [जा]यते । चतुष्पादादिमध्ययमकमेकरूपं व्यवहितम् ॥
children.translated_text: Cranes — whose girdle-bells (<s>kāñcī</s>) imitate, equal, the cries of cranes, because of the similarity of sound — thus '<s>sārasānukṛtasārasakāñcī</s>.' Him, a certain beloved man. In the alternate reading: '<s>sārabhūta</s>' means endowed with the accomplishments of a refined urbane man. '<s>Sārayanta</s>' means causing him to withdraw from pleasure. Delighting him with her chest, with the weight of her breasts, with an embrace — enjoying, employing herself, or pleasing him — she considers even the elixir of immortality (<s>rasāyana</s>), with its pleasures of agelessness and the like, as worthless, as of little account. The pleasure of lovemaking alone she considers exceedingly important. For such indeed is the conviction that arises in that state. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning and middle, of one type, interrupted.

She — a certain beloved woman — '<s>urusāradharā</s>' means she bears excellent gold as ornament, and is thus 'bearing much gold.' In the reading '<s>urusāradharā</s>': she bears the excellence befitting a woman — this should be the explanation. '<s>Sārasas</s>' are birds that exist with their melodious cries,
fortune, make the blind ones wise in statecraft;
By the examination of right and wrong policy, by that unfailing —
attain the end of all policies, bring forth those who have gained attainment. || 46 ||
you who follow the vehicle of the <s>Jina</s>, who need not travel anywhere —

children.text: अनया न विद्यतेऽयो विगमो यस्या इति । अनयाऽनया स्थिरा आयतिरभ्युदयो यस्येत्यनयायते ! आनयने प्राप्तौ

। अन्धान[वलोकना]शक्तान् । विनय नयाभिज्ञान् नयानयसमर्थान् विधेहि । कथं ? नयस्य त्रिवर्गोपायस्यानयस्य तद्विपर्ययस्य चालोचन[ा/?/] विवेचना । तया नयानयालोचनया । अनया अपरोक्षया हेतुभूतया करणेन वा । अपि च यानयानहितोपायान् न अयासीः न प्राप्तवानसि तान्नयान् । आनयनमानयः प्राप्तिस्तमाश्रितान् प्राप्तियुक्तान् प्राप्तान् जनय कुरु । आनयेति यावत् । कथम् ? जिनस्य तथागतस्य यानं यान्ति प्राप्नुवन्ति स्मरन्त्यनेन हितमिति आगमः । तं याति यथावद् वेत्तीति जिनयानयास्त्वम् । अतश्च प्रज्ञाबलादेव हितप्राप्तेर्न क्वचिद् यानं यात्रापरिक्लेशं याति गच्छत्याचरतीति अयानयास्त्वं क्वचि
children.translated_text: The blind — those unable to see. Make them skilled in policy (<s>naya</s>), competent in discerning right and wrong policy. How? Through the examination, the discernment, of <s>naya</s> (right policy), the means to the triple goal, and <s>anaya</s> (wrong policy), its opposite. By means of that examination of right and wrong policy. By this, which is direct, serving as the cause, or as the instrument. Moreover, you have not sought — have not attained — the cessation, the end, of those policies that lead to beneficial means. Produce those who have attained, who are endowed with attainment — that is, bring them forth. How? You are one who follows the vehicle (<s>yāna</s>), the teaching, of the <s>Jina</s> (<s>Tathāgata</s>), through which the beneficial is remembered and attained. And thus, by the power of wisdom alone, since the beneficial is attained, you who need not travel (<s>ayānayā</s>) anywhere, not going anywhere,

children.text: दगच्छन् व्यवहित एव सर्वनयनिरन्तरं तथागतसमयम[भ्य]सन् सर्वान्नयान् प्राप्नुहीत्यर्थः । प्रथमतृतीययोः पादयोराद्यन्तयमकमेकरूपमव्यपेतव्यपेतं, द्वितीयचतुर्थयोरादिमध्ययमकमेकरूपमव्यपेतव्यपेतात्मकमिति ॥
children.translated_text: remaining undistracted, continuously practicing the doctrine of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — attain all policies — such is the meaning. In the first and third feet there is a <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning and end, of one type, of both interrupted and uninterrupted character; in the second and fourth feet, at the beginning and middle, of one type, of both interrupted and uninterrupted character.

'<s>Anayā</s>' — that from which there is no departure, that is, she is unfailing. '<s>Anayāyate</s>' — O you whose fortune, prosperity, is unfailing, imperishable! In the sense of attainment, of reaching.
the earth-born one was routed in the battle of unequaled weapon-power.
With the cry of the hero-bird stationed on the banner,
let the terrible enemy know an equal fate to the ram. || 47 ||
Before <s>Hari</s>, fierce like the sun,

children.text: भूमेरपत्यं भौमो नरकासुरः अवेजि विद्रुतः । केन ? रवेण नादेन । कस्य ? ध्वजे वर्तमानस्य वीरस्य विक्रान्तस्य वेः पक्षिणः । गरुत्मत इति यावत् । कुत्र ? अतुलमसमम् अस्त्राणां गौरवं भारो यत्रेत्यतुलास्त्रगौरवे संयति युद्धे । अत एव भैरवे भीमे यस्य ध्वजचिह्नस्येदृशो विक्रमस्तस्यैतस्य तु रोचिष्णो रवेः सूर्यस्येवोग्रस्य
तेजस्विनः पुरोऽग्रतो रिपुं भौममन्यं वा अवेर्मेषस्यतुल्यमवेत जानीतेति चतुष्पादाद्यन्तयोरेकरूपं व्यपेतयमकमव्यपेतं च ॥
children.translated_text: the mighty one — before him, the enemy <s>Bhauma</s> or another, equal to the ram (<s>Aries</s>) — let him know, let him recognize. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning and end, of one type, interrupted and also uninterrupted.

The son of Earth, <s>Bhaumā</s> (the demon <s>Naraka</s>), was routed, put to flight. By what? By the cry, the sound. Of whom? Of the hero-bird, the mighty bird stationed on the banner — that is, <s>Garuḍa</s>. Where? In the battle of unequaled, incomparable weapon-power, where the weight, the mass, of weapons is unmatched. And therefore, in this terrible, fearsome battle — his whose banner-emblem has such prowess — of this radiant one, like the fierce sun,
by me, she from whom cessation is unattainable, she who is free from disease —
