She who is afflicted by the sickness of separation, clinging to the art of illusion,
unite her with me, her of compassionate nature, O compassionate one! || 48 ||
her pain born of separation I shall dispel, her of immeasurable watches —

children.text: अमूं तामिष्टां काञ्चिद् रूपसम्पत्त्यादियोगात् अय इष्टफलं दैवमस्यास्तीति अयाम् । अर्श आदित्वादच् । गुणवतीम्, किंभूताम् ? मयामयार्तिं डुमिञ् प्रक्षेपणे येन मयः प्रक्षेपः परित्यागो विरह इति यावत् । मय एवामयो विकारस्तस्य स एव वा आर्तिः व्यथा यस्या इति मयामयार्तिं विरहव्याधिपीडिताम् । अतश्च मयामयालम्ब्यकलामयामयाः अविकारो दक्षस्तस्यापकृतस्तेनालम्ब्यो गृहीत इति व्यथाकरत्वात् सरोषमधिक्षिप्तः कलामयश्चन्द्र एव पीडाकरत्वादामयो रोगो यस्य इति मयामया- लम्ब्यकलामयामया । केन ? तेन निशा रात्र्या हेतुना अयातव्यो विरामोऽन्तो यमित्ययातव्यविरामयाऽनवसानया विरहवशात् । अतश्च[न]मानं मा भिदादिषितोङिति

भिदादिदर्शनादङ् [?] विद्यते येषामित्यमा अपरिमिता यामाः प्रहरा [अ]स्या इत्यमयामया । ततश्चातिदुःखहेतुत्वादधिक्षिप्यते अमयेति, निश्रीकया मा श्रीर्न विद्यतेऽस्या इति कृत्वा अमया [अमं] तद्विरहविकारं यातीत्यमया विरहदुःखपीडितेन सह अमय संगमय
children.translated_text: whose watches (<s>yāmas</s>) are immeasurable (<s>amā</s>), unlimited — thus '<s>amayāmayā</s>.' Therefore, because of being the cause of extreme suffering, it is rebuked as '<s>amayā</s>' — devoid of fortune, '<s>mā</s>' meaning <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) being absent. '<s>Amayā</s>' — she who goes (<s>yāti</s>) to that state of separation — afflicted by the pain of separation, together with [me],

children.text: हे करुणामय ! सानुक्रोशमये मित्रेति कश्चित् सुहृदामन्त्र्यते । चतुष्पादाद्यन्तयमकमेकरूपमव्यपेतव्यपेतमिति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>amaya</s>' — unite, bring together — O compassionate one (<s>karuṇāmaya</s>)! O one whose nature is compassion, O friend — thus a certain person addresses a companion. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning and end, of one type, interrupted and uninterrupted.

That beloved woman — because of the conjunction of beauty and the like, she whose fortune, whose auspicious destiny, exists. '<s>Ayām</s>' means 'endowed with good fortune,' with the suffix '<s>ac</s>' by the rule of '<s>arśa ādi</s>.' A virtuous woman — of what character? '<s>Mayāmayārtim</s>' — '<s>maya</s>' from the root '<s>ḍumiñ</s>' meaning 'to throw' — separation, as it were; '<s>maya</s>' itself is '<s>āmaya</s>' (disease), or the affliction born of that — thus she is 'one whose pain is the disease of separation,' afflicted by the sickness of separation. Therefore, '<s>mayāmayālambyakalāmayāmayāḥ</s>': the one free from agitation, the skillful one, whose skill has been grasped — that is, the moon (<s>kalāmaya</s>), which causes pain, being thus an <s>āmaya</s> (disease) — has been angrily rebuked because of its capacity to cause suffering. By what? By the night, as the cause — whose cessation, whose end, is unreachable, that is, unending because of separation. And thus
and the freedom from desire of those whose foremost regard has been obtained without effort.
Your impartial nature conquers the dispassion of those who are intoxicated by opinion,
without distress — your equanimity, not crookedness, prevails. || 49 ||
Your impartial nature goes forth, contrary to the reverse of the highest,

children.text: ते तव अताम्यतो दुश्चरिताभावात् प्रज्ञाकौशलाद् वार्थसिद्धिं [आप्नुवतः] सम्बन्धिन्यां मतौ बुद्धौ विषये समता रागद्वेषादिवैषम्याभावादेकान्तोचिता

दक्षिणतैव प्रवर्तते । यदाह- न वामतेति, न दुष्टता काचित् । किंविशिष्टा ? उत्तमताया प्रधान[त्व]स्य विलोमतां प्रातिकूल्यमधमताम् अयती अगच्छन्ती, किंतु अतापेनाकृच्छ्रेण लब्धा प्राप्ता अग्रिमताया अनुलोमता आनुगुण्यं ययेत्यतापलब्धाग्रिमतानुलोमता अ[क्लेशेन सर्वराजपुरोवर्तित्वं त]वेति यावत् । आरमतां तपस्विनामकामतामलुब्धतां मतां प्रशस्तां धुनाना जयन्ती तदुपमितेति यावत् । समता प्रवर्तत इति निगमनीयम् । चतुष्पादादिमध्यान्तयमकं व्यपेतमेकरूपमिति ॥
children.translated_text: prevails as nothing but righteous conduct. As stated: 'not crookedness' — no wickedness whatsoever. Of what distinction? Not going toward the reverse, the contrariness, the baseness, of the highest, of preeminence; rather, the conformity with primacy, obtained without distress, without hardship — thus '<s>atāpalabdhāgrimatānulomatā</s>,' meaning effortless attainment of the position of being foremost among all kings. Conquering, surpassing, the commendable freedom from desire, the non-greed, of ascetics. It should be concluded: equanimity prevails. This is a four-footed <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning, middle, and end, interrupted, of one type.

In your wisdom (<s>mati</s>), in the domain of your intellect — for you who do not suffer because of the absence of misdeeds, because of the skill of wisdom, [or for you who attain the accomplishment of goals] — equanimity (<s>samatā</s>), the absence of the inequality of passion, hatred, and the like, entirely fitting,
whose conversation-cry is dark, whose dark clouds belong to the dark season,
O <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death) of <s>Kāla</s> (Mahākāla/Śiva), whose throat is dark, whose monkey-face is dark,
may the <s>Kāla</s> (Time) of dark strife proceed, the dark time of the dark <s>kalā</s> (phase). || 50 ||
whose dark spots are white-dark, the woman cast out in the dark season —

children.text: कालकालो महाकालः शङ्करः तम्य गलः कण्ठः कलिरेव कालः । कालमुखो गोलाङ्गलः । कालकालगलश्च कालश्च कालमुखश्च तेषां कालकं कृष्णत्वम् । तदालाति गृह्णातीति मूलविभुजादिदर्शनात् कः । कालकालगलकालकालमुखकालकालः । कालं कायन्ति शब्दायन्ते इति कालका मयूराः तेषामिदं कालकं, कालकं च तदालपनं कं रुतं चेति कालकालपनकम् । अलीनां समूह आलः । आलवत् कालाः कृष्णा घना मेघा यस्मिन् काले स आलकालघनकालः । स चासौ कालकालपनकालकालघनकालकालश्चेति विशेषणसमासः । तद्वत् कालः कृष्ण इति विष्णोरामन्त्रणमिदम् । कमुदकमालवन्तीति [? आलान्तीति] कालाः । पूर्ववत् कः । काल एव कालकाः स्वार्थे कः । कालकैर्मेघैः । तदुपजीविभिः परिवारभूतैरालसति भातीति कालकालसि समुद्रे, क्विवन्तस्य सप्तम्यन्तस्य रूपम् । तत्र तका[? उत्का] विष्णुविरहात् कृच्छ्रजीवितात् लकालोका[?] ललनिका स्त्रीः लक्ष्मीरिति यावत् । किंविशिष्टा ? अलकानामालिः
इतः परं षट्पञ्चाशत्तमश्लोकस्यान्तिमभागपर्यन्तं टीका लिपिकरप्रमादाद् भ्रष्टा ।

children.translated_text: '<s>Kālakāla</s>' is <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>; his throat (<s>gala</s>) — the quarrel (<s>kali</s>) itself is '<s>kāla</s>.' '<s>Kālamukha</s>' is the langur monkey. The darkness of the throat of <s>Kālakāla</s>, the darkness of <s>Kālamukha</s> — their blackness is '<s>kālaka</s>.' One who grasps that, from the observation of the root '<s>vibhuj</s>' and the like — is '<s>ka</s>.' Thus '<s>kālakālagalakālakālamukha-kālakāla</s>.' '<s>Kālakā</s>' means peacocks, those that cry at the time [of rain]; their sound is '<s>kālaka</s>,' and the conversation of that sound, its cry — is '<s>kālakālapanaka</s>.' A mass of bees is '<s>āla</s>.' Where the clouds are dark like the mass of bees, that season is '<s>ālakālaghanakāla</s>.' And that combined compound is a qualifying compound. Similarly, '<s>kāla</s>' meaning dark — this is an address to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Water possessing '<s>ka</s>' (joy) is '<s>kālā</s>.' As before, '<s>ka</s>' is the suffix. '<s>Kālaka</s>' means the clouds; in the ocean that shines with those clouds and the beings dependent upon them — that is the locative form of a '<s>kvi</s>'-ending word. There, afflicted by separation from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, living with difficulty — '<s>lalanīkā</s>' means a woman, that is, <s>Lakṣmī</s>. Of what quality? Whose row of curls
The definition of <s>sandaṣṭa yamaka</s> (bitten alliteration), though included under what has been stated, is described distinctly —
The location of <s>sandaṣṭa yamaka</s> (bitten alliteration) is the end and beginning of two feet;
though included under what has been stated, it is here proclaimed independently. || 51 ||
He illustrates that —
a sinful pride — was joined with the sentiment of anger.
Though possessed of passion, the helpless woman, by her pride —
even though tormented, was not led to the torment of me. || 52 ||
She who had not united her self with <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), though tormented —
He states the definition of <s>samudga yamaka</s> (box alliteration) —
<s>Samudga</s> (box alliteration) is the repetition of half-verses; its varieties are considered to be three.
The repetition of whole feet too is of multiple types — it is manifested through examples. || 53 ||
He illustrates the interrupted <s>samudga</s> —
He should not be slighted by you, whose patience is vast, he who possesses steadfast strength;
he should not be disregarded by you, whose patience is vast — he who possesses steadfast strength. || 54 ||
He illustrates the uninterrupted <s>samudga</s> —
they were not conquered by those who did not meet with wise policy.
Men were conquered, having met with conciliation,
destroyed by the fire of affliction to prosperity. || 55 ||
Destroyed indeed by the fire of worldly existence,
He illustrates the mixed interrupted-uninterrupted <s>samudga</s> —
flocks of those whose dense cloud-gathering dispels speech.
The charming flocks of those who carry the <s>kalā</s> (art) arrive,
the charming sounds of the peacocks cease. || 56 ||
The flocks with dense cloud-gathering that dispels speech,
Thus: 'the flocks whose dense cloud-gathering dispels speech' means of the swans — this is the import. 'The sounds cease' — thus three varieties of <s>samudga</s> have been illustrated.

children.text: यमिति । वृन्दानिलापोढघनागमानां हंसानामिति यावत् । आरुतयो निनदा अपयन्ति विरमन्ति चेति समुद्गस्य त्रयो भेदा निदर्शिताः ॥

children.translated_text: he says —
Regarding <s>pādābhyāsa</s> (foot-repetition),
by me, bowing, with conquered pride that had become her nature, with a mind won over —
By me, the slow one, whose pride had become her nature, whose mind was devoid of mercy —
the lord of my life was embraced. || 57 ||
with the pair of breasts spread upon the chest,

children.text: दयया अनुग्रहेण वर्जितं विरहितं मानसं चित्तं यस्य तादृश आत्मा आवर्जितः स्वीकृतश्च मानो गर्वः तेन सात्मा स्वभावीभूतोऽभ्यासाद् यस्याः तयैवंभूतया मया मन्दया जडया[नमन्] प्रणिपतन् जीवितेश्वरः प्रियः न समालिङ्ग्यत न परिष्वक्त इत्यनुशोचति काचित् । कथम् ? उपास्तीर्णं निवेशितं भरन्यस्तपयोधरद्वयं यस्मिन् समालिङ्गन इति क्रियाविशेषणम् । कुत्रेत्यपेक्षायामुरसीति योज्यम्, असमस्तत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: She whose mind was devoid of mercy, compassion, was of such a nature; and whose pride had been won over, made one's own — that pride having become habitual through practice. By such a woman, by me, the slow one, the foolish one — the lord of my life, the beloved, bowing, was not embraced, was not enfolded — thus a certain woman laments. How? With the pair of breasts spread, deposited, the burden placed upon the chest — this qualifies the act of embracing. In response to the question 'where?' — 'upon the chest' should be supplied, since it is not compounded.
with your qualities, rising, pure as a lotus-stalk.
Among assemblies of gods, the power adorned
enjoying the wealth of cities, enter and sport! || 58 ||
He, radiant among the powerless gods, adorned,

children.text: तव गुणैर्मृणालवन्निर्मलैः परिशुद्धैः सुराणां सभा देवपर्षदारोहि कीर्तिद्वारेण प्राप्ता । किंभूता ? [अबला] बलनाम्नोऽसुरस्य शक्रनिरस्तस्य तत्रासम्भवात्, न विद्यते बलोऽस्यामिति कृत्वा । वसत्यस्यामित्युषिता गत्यर्थानाप्यादाधारे(?) च इत्याधारे क्तः । विभोः शक्रस्य उषिता वासाधारः विभूषिता शक्राध्यासिता । धर्मार्थकाममयैर्गुणैर्व्याप्तभुवनः स त्वमिदानीं पुरां वरभवनयुजां नगराणां भासुराणां विभूतिभिर्भ्राजिष्णूनां सम्पदोऽभ्युदयान् सुखानि निर्विश अनुभव । अबलाः स्त्रियः विभूषिताः विहारयन् भ्रमयन् [रमय]न्निति । कृतकृत्यस्य कामोपभोगो दर्शित इति ॥
children.translated_text: By your qualities, spotless like lotus fibers, the assembly of the gods, the divine court, has been reached through the door of fame. Of what kind? Since the <s>Asura</s> named <s>Bala</s>, who was vanquished by <s>Śakra</s>, cannot exist there — thus it is '<s>abalā</s>' (without <s>Bala</s>). Of the lord <s>Śakra</s> — it is the dwelling-place, adorned by <s>Śakra</s>. You, whose worlds are pervaded by qualities consisting of <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) — now enjoy the splendors, the prosperities, the pleasures, of the cities, the resplendent towns with fine palaces. Entertaining and delighting the adorned women — thus the enjoyment of pleasures by one who has accomplished his duty has been shown. ||
and the pair of breasts — which man do they not slay, except you?
Sweet words, the slender-waisted woman,
to find another free of blemish and embodied. || 59 ||
In the enumeration where you are foremost, the ring finger does not proceed [further]

children.text: कलं मधुरम् । उक्तं वचनम् । स्तनद्वयी पयोधरयुगलं च तनोः शरीरस्य सम्बन्धिनो मध्यस्य नामिका आवर्तिका स्त्रीणामित्यर्थात् । कं नाम नरं न हन्ति ? किं तु सर्वमेव हन्ति । अभिलाषादिकामावस्थाः क्रमेण दशमीं नयन्तीति कृत्वा हन्तीत्युच्यते । त्वदृते त्वामन्तरेण । त्वमेव केवलमनेन [न] हन्यसे जितेन्द्रियत्वात् । तनुमद्ध्यनामिकेत्यत्र तनुत्वमाने हिशब्दो यस्मादर्थे । यत एवम्, अतः कारणात् भवान् मुखमादिः गुणैरग्रनीतत्वात्
, यस्मिन् गणने सत्पुरूषसंख्यायां तस्मिन् भवन्मुखे गणने क्रियमाणे कलङ्कमुक्तं निर्दोषं तनुमत्, भूतं
children.translated_text: in the enumeration, in the count of worthy persons — when such counting is performed beginning with you, one who is free of blemish, faultless, and embodied,

children.text: सकलनिष्कलपरिमाणव्यतिरिक्तं भूतं पुरुषं व्याप्यभूतम् । अनामिका कनिष्ठानन्तराङ्गुलिर्न याति न गच्छति । [त्वां प्रथमं कनिष्ठिकायां गुणवत्त्वया गणयित्वा [स्थितस्य] त्वमिव निष्कलङ्को द्वितीयायामनांमिकायां गणयितव्यो
children.translated_text: a real being distinct from total and partial measures — the ring finger (<s>anāmikā</s>), the finger next to the little one, does not proceed, does not advance — [meaning, having counted you first on the little finger, there is no one as blemish-free as you to count on the second, the ring finger —
there is no such person] — such is the meaning. ||

'<s>Kala</s>' means sweet. '<s>Ukta</s>' means speech, utterance. The pair of breasts (<s>stanadvayī</s>) and the slender waist (<s>madhya</s>) belonging to the body — the <s>nāmikā</s> (she who bends), referring to women — which man (<s>ka</s>) do they not slay? Rather, they slay everyone. It is said they 'slay' because the stages of desire beginning with longing lead progressively to the tenth (death). '<s>Tvadṛte</s>' means 'except for you.' You alone are not slain by these, because of having conquered your senses. In '<s>tanumaddhyanāmikā</s>' — the word '<s>hi</s>' is in the causal sense. Since this is so, therefore you are foremost (<s>mukha</s>, the head), being led by your qualities,
in battle, O one equal to the Unborn (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), armed and ready for war;
Your soldiers spread your fame in the directions and dust
with their sharpened weapons, the valiant ones, destroying the enemy's clan. || 60 ||
and they spread the diminishment of the vigor and pride of the enemies

children.text: अजोपम विष्णुतुल्य ! ते तव सैनिकाः सेनाचरा नराः शितमायुधमेषामिति शितायुधाः तीक्ष्णहेतयः । दंशिता वर्मिताः । तरस्विनः शूराः सन्तः यशश्च कीर्ति च ते रजश्च पार्थिवं दिक्षु वितन्वते विस्तारयन्ति । युधा रणेन तुमुलेन । द्विषां च कुलं [वि]तनु प्रहारशतजर्जरत्वाद् विगतशरीरम् । न विद्यते तेजोऽस्येत्यतेजः निष्प्रभावम् । विगतो मदोऽस्मादित्यपमदं वीतगर्वं कुर्वन्तीति ॥
children.translated_text: O one equal to the Unborn (<s>Viṣṇu</s>)! Your soldiers, the warriors of your army, bearing sharpened weapons, keen-edged arms — armored, clad in armor — valiant, heroic — they spread your fame and the dust of the earth in the directions, in battle, in fierce combat. And they render the clan of the enemies (<s>dviṣas</s>) — their bodies emaciated from being shattered by hundreds of blows — devoid of vigor, without power — and stripped of pride, humbled. ||
swelling with pride, remembering [that he alone bears the earth];
The serpent-king (<s>Śeṣa</s>) bears the circle of the earth upon his hood, together with your arm,

children.text: भुजङ्गमो मा स्म रतो मदं चितम् ॥ ६१ ॥
children.translated_text: let him not, elated with pride, harbor arrogance. || 61 ||
hear this one [word of advice]: knowing your arm to be a fellow earth-bearer,

children.text: ते तव भुजेन अमा सह भूमेर्वलयं महीमण्डलं बिभर्ति धारयति भुजङ्गमः शेषो नागराजः । नक एव ते भुजः । [अतः] स्वमात्मीयं भुजं बाहुं भुवं पृथिवीं धारयति वहतीति भूधरमवेत्य ज्ञात्वा मम भुजो स्वयं धारयतीति मदमहङ्कारं चितमुपचितमुदीर्णं [रतः] अभिनिविष्टः सन् मा स्म गमस्त्वं मा गच्छतु भवान् । इतीदमेकं प्रधानमुक्तं वचनम् । अञ्चितं हितं शृणु गृहाण । मत् मत्तः सकाशात् स्मरतः जानतः । प्राप्तज्ञानः एवमुदास्ते भवान् यदि न विरुद्धं [व्यवहरति], तदा सुतरां शोभते विनयालङ्कतगुणत्वादितीदमेकं मद्वचनं सर्वगुणभूषणं ग्राह्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Together with your arm, the serpent (<s>bhujaṅgama</s>), <s>Śeṣa</s> the serpent-king, bears, sustains, the circle of the earth, the terrestrial sphere. Not your arm alone. Therefore, knowing, understanding, that your arm — which sustains, carries the earth — is his own fellow earth-bearer, let him not harbor, let him not indulge in, pride (<s>mada</s>), that is, the arrogance of thinking 'My arm alone bears it' — let him not proceed with such elation. Hear, accept, this one principal word of advice, beneficial, from me who knows. If he, having gained this knowledge, does not act contrarily, he will be all the more resplendent, being adorned with the quality of humility — this one word of mine, an ornament of all virtues, should be heeded. ||
does it not destroy your happiness?
The fire of love, intensified by your pride (<s>māna</s>) —
it has spread equally from that [pride] — in the domain of passion, instantly! || 62 ||
O lotus-eyed one, everywhere, in an instant,

children.text: हे तामरसेक्षणे पद्माक्षि ! न विद्यते रसः कामादरो यस्या इत्यरसेऽरसिके ! प्रियसङ्गमसुखवैमुख्यादेवमामन्त्रिता सरोषम् । स्मरः काम एव अनलः तापकारित्वात् । स्मरानलो यो मानेन प्रियसङ्गमविरोधेन गर्वेण वर्धितो दीपितः, सोऽयं क्षणेनैकेन समं सह नाधिकेन कालेन ततो विस्तृतः क्षणमात्रेण विजृम्भितः ते तव निर्वृतिं सुखतां प्रति विशिष्टायासं प्रयोगसम्भवं समन्ततः सर्वथा किं नापाकरोति न हन्ति ? अपाकरोत्येव । तस्मात् संगम्यतां प्रियम् । किमनेन दग्धमानेनेति ॥
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one (<s>tāmarasekṣaṇe</s>)! O you devoid of passion (<s>arase</s>)! — thus she is addressed angrily, due to her aversion to the happiness of union with the beloved. The fire of love (<s>smara</s>) — tormenting by nature — is the fire of desire. This fire of love, which has been intensified, inflamed, by <s>māna</s> (pride), by the hostility toward union with the beloved, by haughtiness — this one, in a single instant, equally, and not more time than that, having spread from that [pride], having expanded in a mere instant — does it not utterly destroy, does it not annihilate, your happiness, the comfort of pleasure, the effort born of enjoyment? It certainly does. Therefore, unite with your beloved. What use is this accursed pride? ||
because of your might, O nameless one — beyond new <s>soma</s> offerings —
Because of your splendor, O humbler — of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) —
any interruption of the <s>soma</s> sacrifice in your domain as lord of the world? || 63 ||
because of your power, was there indeed never, at all,

children.text: प्रभा अस्यास्तीति प्रभावतो दीप्तिमतः गुणोत्कर्षात् । वासवस्य शक्रस्य । नामयतीति हे नामन जेतः ! प्रभावतः प्रभावात् शक्तिविशेषप्रभावेण शक्रतुल्येति यावत् । नमनं नामः स न विद्यतेऽस्येति हे अनाम ! परप्रणिपातानभिज्ञ ! सर्वातिरेकात् । यत एवं

गुणयुक्तो भवान्, अतः कारणात् त्वयि पिष्टपस्य जगतः प्रभौ स्वामिनि सति सवस्य यागस्य नवः प्रत्यग्र आसवः सोमो विलक्षणः पानविशेषः अस्मिन्निति नवासवस्य सोमयागस्येति यावत् । विच्छित्तिर्विघातः । नाम सर्वथा वाचोयुक्तौ वा । न वा नैवासीदभूत् । सर्वदा धर्मक्रिया प्रवर्तत इति कश्चिन्नरपतिः स्तूयते ॥
children.translated_text: endowed with virtues, therefore, in you as the lord of the world (<s>piṣṭapa</s>) — of the <s>soma</s> sacrifice (<s>savasya</s>) — fresh, new <s>āsava</s> (soma), the extraordinary <s>soma</s> libation — thus 'of the fresh-<s>soma</s> sacrifice' — was there disruption, obstruction? '<s>Nāma</s>' means 'in every way' or is a mere expletive. Or not — there never was any. Righteous actions always proceed — thus a certain king is praised. ||

'<s>Prabhāvataḥ</s>' — because of being radiant, resplendent, because of the excellence of qualities. Of <s>Vāsava</s>, of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). O '<s>nāman</s>' — O conqueror, one who makes others bow! '<s>Prabhāvataḥ</s>' — because of might, by the special power of capacity — meaning equal to <s>Śakra</s>. '<s>Anāma</s>' — O one who has no bowing, no subjugation! One to whom no one else's prostration is familiar — because of surpassing all. Since you are thus
having created clouds of dust from the battlefields, filling the sky —
Supreme, beyond the series of battles, powerful, blocking —
surpassing the series of the enemy's powerful war-elephants. || 64 ||
through the succession of his powerful war-elephants,

children.text: परमुत्कृष्टम् । गुणयोगात् परं शक्र परायाः त्वं युद्धरसेनातिगतवानसि । किंभूतम् ? बलं सामर्थ्यं वारयतीति बलवाः । वारयतेः क्विबन्तस्य रूपम् । कस्य ? रणानां परसमराणां परयुद्धाभिभावीति (?) कुर्वन् । बलवारणानां सेनागजानां बलं प्राणं वाति गच्छतीति बलवः । आतोऽप्रादेः कः । सप्राणः आरणः शब्दो येषामिति बलवारणानां गम्भीरोदीर्णगर्जितानां सम्बन्धिन्याः परम्परायाः परिपाट्या घटायाः सत्त्वादियोगात् प्रकृष्टायाः सकाशात् धूलीः स्थलीः पांशुप्रकरान् तत्प्रेरणाय विधाय कृत्वा पराया इति परम्पराया इति बाह्यधूली स्थलीविकारेति । लुग्लोपलक्षणा पञ्चमी । व्योमाकाशं रुन्धन्नावृण्वन् पराया इति प्रकृतम् ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Param</s>' means supreme, because of the conjunction of virtues; O one surpassing (<s>param</s>) <s>Śakra</s> — you have surpassed the series of battles by your martial prowess. Of what kind? '<s>Balavān</s>' — one who wards off strength, might. This is the form of a <s>kvip</s>-suffix derivative of the root '<s>vārayati</s>' (to ward off). Whose? Of the battles, of the enemy's combats — one who overwhelms the enemy's warfare. Of the army-elephants (<s>balavāraṇas</s>) — whose life-breath (<s>bala</s>) departs (<s>vāti</s>), thus '<s>balava</s>' — the '<s>ka</s>' suffix from the root '<s>at</s>.' Having life-breath; '<s>āraṇa</s>' means sound — thus '<s>balavāraṇas</s>' are those with deep, mighty roaring. By the succession, the series, the array of these — because of its excellent qualities — having created, produced, clouds of dust, masses of earth-particles, to drive them forward — '<s>parāyāḥ</s>' stands for '<s>paramparāyāḥ</s>' — the fifth case used in the sense of the ablative indicator of separation. Filling, covering the sky — '<s>parāyāḥ</s>' is the main predicate. ||
of those of your kind, unsettled in mind;
I do not believe the words of you, O shameless one, false —
of those of your kind, of harmful intent. || 65 ||
of those of your kind, of evil disposition;

children.text: हे अलज्ज ! भवद्विधानां युष्मादृशानाम् । असमाहितानां विक्षिप्तचेतसां भवे संसारे द्वौ प्रकारौ अहङ्कारममकारौ रागद्वेषौ वा येषामिति भवद्विधानाम् । अत एव यथा आत्मा न वञ्चनीय[ः/?/] तथा परोऽपीति समप्रवृत्त्यभावादसमाहितानाम् । असमाश्च तेऽहिताश्चेति विग्रहः । अत एव न विद्यते हितं श्रेयो धर्मो येषामिति अहितानां वाचं मिथ्या भवत् वितथं जायमानं विधानमनुष्ठानमन्यथा विधायान्यथाकरणाद् यस्यामिति मिथ्याभवद्विधानाम् । अत एवासमस्यातुलस्य महतः अहेः सर्पस्येव तानो गतिः कौटिल्यादियोगात् यम्यामित्यसमाहितानां गिरो न श्रद्दधे न

children.translated_text: accept, the words — thus someone angrily rebukes someone. ||

O shameless one! Of those of your kind, of people like you. Of the unsettled, of those whose minds are distracted — of those who have two modes in worldly existence, namely ego and possessiveness, or attachment and aversion — thus '<s>bhavadvidhāna</s>.' And precisely therefore, since they do not act with equal regard toward themselves and others — '<s>asamāhitānām</s>' (unsettled). '<s>Asamāḥ</s>' (unequal) and '<s>ahitāḥ</s>' (harmful) — thus the analysis. And precisely therefore, '<s>ahitānām</s>' — those who have no welfare, no virtue. The words — the conduct '<s>vidhāna</s>' that arises falsely (<s>mithyā</s>), that is born deceitfully, arranging things one way while acting another way — thus '<s>mithyābhavadvidhānām</s>.' And precisely therefore, of the unsettled one — whose course is like that of a great serpent (<s>ahi</s>), because of crookedness — I do not believe, I do not
O one armored, of esteemed honor, not of <s>Rājasa</s> nature, with a royal army —
O one armored, of esteemed honor, not of <s>Rājasa</s> (impure) [nature], with a royal army —
O armored one, of true honor, you do not merely rule [in name]. || 66 ||
O one who has destroyed the enemy's glory, of esteemed honor, with a royal army —

children.text: अहितानामुमाभिख्या अहितोमा । सन्ना नि[र]स्ता अहितोमा यत इति हे सन्नाहितोम निरस्तशत्रुशोभ ! आनमतीत्यानमः कर्तर्यच । राज्ञः सेना राजसेना । आनमा आनता राजसेना यस्मिन्निति हे आनमराजसेन ! न नमतीत्यनमः हे अनम ! रजसो विकारो राजसो दुष्टः । न राजसोऽराजसः सात्त्विकः । हे अराजस ! इन स्वामिन् ! हिता उमा गौरी यस्य स हितोमः । न विद्यते मा श्रीरस्येत्यमः । न अमोऽनमः सश्रीकः । राजा चन्द्रः । स [ललाटभूषा] यस्येति अनमराजा, हितोमश्चासौ अनमराजा च हितोमानमराजा शङ्करः । तेन सेनः सनाथः तद्युक्तोऽहितमानमराजसेनः । [तस्य सम्बुद्धिः] । सन्नाहितो दंशितः मानमाहितः आगतः प्राप्तः सन्ना सत्पुरुषः स न भवन् त्वं मा न राजसे, एवं चानेकगुणयुक्तस्त्वमतितरां राजस इत्यर्थः । अत्र हेतुफलभावो यथायथं योजनीयः । यतः सन्नाहितः, तस्मादानमराज
सेनः सन्नाहितोमश्च, यतश्च मानमाहितः, तस्मादनमः । यतश्च हितोमानमराजसेनः, तस्मादसन्ना अराजसश्च । यतश्चैतदेवं अतो राजसे वा नेति ॥
children.translated_text: and because all this is so, therefore he rules, or rather, he does not merely rule [in name alone]. ||

'<s>Ahitomā</s>' — the glory of the enemies; '<s>sannā</s>' means destroyed, cast down — O one who has destroyed the enemy's glory! '<s>Ānamaḥ</s>' means one who makes others bow — agent form with the suffix '<s>ac</s>.' The army of the king is '<s>rājasena</s>.' '<s>Ānamā</s>' means bowed, submissive — that whose royal army is bowed to — O one whose royal army makes others bow! '<s>Anama</s>' means one who does not bow. '<s>Arājasa</s>' means not of <s>Rajasic</s> (impure) quality — <s>Sāttvika</s> (pure). O non-Rajasic one! O lord! '<s>Hitomā</s>' — one whose <s>Umā</s> (<s>Gaurī</s>) is propitious. '<s>Anama</s>' — one who is not without <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), possessing <s>Śrī</s>. '<s>Rāja</s>' means the moon, who is the forehead-ornament — thus '<s>hitomānamarājā</s>' is <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). By him, '<s>sena</s>' means protected, accompanied by him — '<s>ahitamānamarājasena</s>.' [This is] his vocative. 'Armored' (<s>sannāhita</s>); honor (<s>māna</s>) that is '<s>āhita</s>' (established, attained); a worthy person (<s>sannā</s>, <s>sat</s>) — you do not merely rule, rather, being endowed with such manifold qualities, you rule supremely — such is the meaning. Here the relation of cause and effect should be applied as appropriate: because armored, therefore his royal army makes others bow and the enemy's glory is destroyed; because his honor is established, therefore he does not bow; because he is protected by <s>Śiva</s>, therefore he is not <s>Rājasic</s>, and [his enemies are] destroyed;
The repetition of a verse-quarter — once, twice, or thrice — has been illustrated thus;

children.text: श्लोकद्वयं तु युक्तार्थं श्लोकाभ्यासः स्मृतो यथा ॥ ६७ ॥
children.translated_text: but two verses with connected meaning are called <s>ślokābhyāsa</s> (verse-repetition), as follows: || 67 ||

children.text: सकृदेकवारं द्विः वारद्वयं त्रिः वारत्रयं च पादस्य सम्बन्धी योऽम्यासः स एवम् उक्तेन प्रकारेण दर्शितः समुदाहृतः । श्लोकयोर्द्वयं द्वौ श्लोकौ युक्तोऽर्थोऽभिधेयं येनेति युक्तार्थमपृथगर्थयुक्तम्, इत्यनूद्य श्लोकाभ्यासः स्मृतो विज्ञायते इति विधीयते यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Once, that is, one time; twice, two times; and thrice, three times — the repetition pertaining to the verse-quarter has been illustrated, exemplified, in the manner described. Two verses, a pair of verses, with connected meaning — that is, having an undivided sense — having stated this resumptively, '<s>ślokābhyāsa</s>' (verse-repetition) is recognized, is known — this is prescribed. 'As follows' — he illustrates: ||
By you, the leader, whose arm is round and powerful,
the rescuer of allies — this earth, fearless, has taken refuge in you, the peerless one. || 68 ||

children.text: भवता त्वया, विनयति जगत् सनातने मार्गे निवेशयतीति [तेन] विनायकेन विनेत्रा । वृत्तो वर्तुल उपचितः पीनो बाहु

रस्येति वृत्तोपचितबाहुना । सुष्ठु अमित्राण्युद्धरतीति स्वमित्रोद्धारिणा इयं पृथ्वी भूमिरभीता स्वपरचक्रोपद्रवाभावात् निर्भया, अतुला विपक्षैस्तुलयितुमशक्यत्वाद् अपरोपमा, आश्रिता अधिष्ठिता वर्तत इति कश्चिद् राजा स्तूयत इत्यनेनार्थेन तावदेकः श्लोकः ॥
children.translated_text: thus 'one with a round, powerful arm.' '<s>Svamitroddhāriṇā</s>' — one who rescues his allies, who uplifts them. This earth is fearless (<s>abhītā</s>), free from the disturbance of hostile and friendly armies — without terror. '<s>Atulā</s>' — incomparable, incapable of being equaled by opponents. She has taken refuge, has been established [under your rule] — thus a certain king is praised — with this meaning, one verse [is complete]. ||
By you — '<s>vināyaka</s>' means one who leads the world onto the eternal path, thus a guide. Whose arm is round (<s>vṛtta</s>) and powerful (<s>upacita</s>), well-developed —

children.text: तव तावदीदृशोऽभ्युदयः, त्वद्विपक्षस्य का गतिरित्ययमेव श्लोकोऽर्थान्तरेणाभ्यस्यते—
children.translated_text: Such is your prosperity; what then is the fate of your adversary? This very verse is now repeated with a different meaning —
By you, the leaderless one, whose arm lies stiff upon the funeral pyre,
the one who has abandoned his own allies — this earth, approaching <s>Yama</s>, has taken refuge in incomparable [death]. || 69 ||

children.text: विगतो नायकोऽस्मादिति विनायकेन नेतृशून्येन त्वयि रुष्टे परित्रायकस्याभावात् । भवता सता । चितायाः समीप उपचितम् । वृत्त उपरतो निर्जीवः [स्वपक्ष]समुदायोपरमात् उपचितो बाहुरस्येति वृत्तोपचितबाहुना । अत एव सुहृत्परित्यागात् स्वानि मित्राणि उज्जहातीति स्वमित्रोद्धा, [उत्पूर्वकस्य ओहाक् त्यागे इत्यस्य] क्विबन्तस्य तृतीयैकवचनान्तस्य रूपम् । अरिणा त्वया विपक्षेण । अभीता अभिमुखमागता । पृथ्वी महती यमस्य तुलां उपमालक्षणाम् । आश्रिता प्राप्ता ।
त्वदरातेः पुनरीदृशी गतिः । अनेनार्थान्तरेण स एव श्लोक अभ्यस्त इति श्लोकाभ्यासोऽयमीदृशः ॥
children.translated_text: Such is the fate of your enemy. By this different meaning, that very verse has been repeated — thus this is a <s>ślokābhyāsa</s> (verse-repetition) of this kind. ||

'<s>Vināyaka</s>' — one from whom the leader has departed, thus 'leaderless,' without a protector, since when you are angered there is no one to save him. '<s>Bhavata</s>' — by existing [i.e., because you exist]. '<s>Upacita</s>' means near the funeral pyre; '<s>vṛtta</s>' means ceased, lifeless — dead from the cessation of his entire faction — whose arm is stiff near the pyre — thus 'one with a ceased arm near the pyre.' And precisely therefore, from the abandonment of friends — he abandons his own allies — '<s>svamitroddhā</s>' is the form of the <s>kvip</s>-suffix derivative of the root '<s>ujjahāti</s>' (to abandon) with the prefix '<s>ut</s>,' in the instrumental singular. By the enemy, by you the adversary. '<s>Abhītā</s>' — having come face to face, approached. The earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>), great, has taken refuge in, has attained, the scale (<s>tulā</s>), the measure of comparison, of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death).
That which has four quarters of identical form is called <s>mahāyamaka</s> (great chiming);
even therein, repetition is observed — that is the supreme feat of <s>yamaka</s> craft. || 70 ||

children.text: एकः समान आकारः स्वरूपं येषामित्येकाकारः, सर्वतो यमकयोगात् चत्वारः पादा यस्य यत्रेति वा । एकाकारचतुष्पादं यत्, तदीदृशं महच्च यत् तद् यमकं च, सर्वयमकप्रधानत्वात्, महायमकमित्याह्वयः संज्ञा अस्येति महायमकाह्वयं वेदितव्यम् । एकाकारचतुष्पादत्वं प्रत्येकं सर्वतो यमकयोगाद् विनाभ्यासादपि सम्भवतीत्याह—तस्यापीत्यादि । तस्यापि महायमकस्यापि न केवलं समूहादेरभ्यासः त्रिपादावृत्तिर्दृश्यते । अत एवेयमीदृशी परा सर्वयमकक्रियाप्रधानत्वात् । यमकस्य क्रिया प्रयोगः । अत एवेदं
त्रिपादाभ्यासाद् भिद्यते । तत्र प्रत्येकं पादेषु सर्वतो यमकाभावात् केवलं पादयमकमात्रं त्रिरभ्यस्यते ॥
children.translated_text: It is distinguished by the repetition across three feet. There, since there is no <s>yamaka</s> in every position within each foot individually, only the foot-<s>yamaka</s> alone is repeated three times.

'<s>Ekākāra</s>' (of identical form) — those whose form, whose appearance, is one and the same — because of <s>yamaka</s> in every position. That which has four quarters of identical form — such a great and marvelous <s>yamaka</s> — since it is preeminent among all <s>yamakas</s>, its designation is '<s>mahāyamaka</s>' (great chiming) — this should be understood. The four-quarter identical form can occur even without repetition, through <s>yamaka</s> in every position of each quarter — he says: 'even therein' and so forth. Even of this <s>mahāyamaka</s> — not merely of a group and the like — repetition, that is, three-quarter recurrence, is observed. For this very reason, this is such a supreme, preeminent feat of <s>yamaka</s> craft, because of its primacy among all <s>yamaka</s> techniques. And for this very reason, this
Illustrating that, he says —
'<s>Samānayāsamānayā samānayā sa mānayā</s>,'
'<s>samānayāsamāna yā samānayāsamānayā</s>.' || 71 ||

children.text: यासः प्रयासः खेदः । मानश्च प्रियविषयं प्रातिकूल्यम् । यासमानौ तुल्यौ, यदा समाना, तदायासोऽपीति समकालत्वात् । यथा चायासस्तापयति तथा मानोऽपि प्रियसङ्गमसुखविरहादिति । यस्याः तया समानयासमानया । सह मानेनार्हणेन गुणयोगाद् वर्तत इति समानया मान्यया अनया कयाचिदिष्टया । स त्वम् । असम गुणोत्कर्षादनुपम ! [मा] मां समानय संगमयेति कञ्चित् सुहृदमभ्यर्थयति कश्चित् कामी । पुनः सा विशिष्यते—या प्रणयिनी सह मया श्रिया वर्तत इति समा कान्तिमती । अनयस्याकार्यस्यासौ निषेधः तस्य मानं प्रमाणमनुभवं यातीति अनयासमानया । अकार्यपरिहारज्ञतया अनयासमानयेति निगमनीयम् ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Yāsa</s>' means exertion, fatigue. And '<s>māna</s>' means aversion directed toward a beloved. When exertion and pride are equal (<s>samāna</s>), then fatigue too is present, due to their simultaneity. And just as exertion causes torment, so does pride, through the absence of the happiness of union with the beloved. By her who has equal exertion and pride — '<s>samānayāsamānayā</s>.' With honor (<s>māna</s>), that is, with esteem due to her possession of qualities — thus '<s>samānayā</s>' means 'honorable,' by this particular beloved woman. 'You' (<s>sa</s>). O incomparable one (<s>asama</s>), due to the excellence of your qualities! Unite me — a certain lover entreats some friend. She is further qualified: she who, the beloved one, has beauty (<s>samā</s>, radiant) together with my fortune (<s>śrī</s>). Her honoring of the standard (<s>māna</s>), the authority, of what is improper (<s>anaya</s>), its prohibition — she attains the experience of it — thus '<s>anayāsamānayā</s>.' The conclusion should be: she who knows how to avoid improper conduct — '<s>anayāsamānayā</s>.'
'Their varieties are exceedingly numerous, and are sources of combination.'

Showing a mere indication, an easily comprehensible form, therein, he says —
to protect the earth, of undiminished valor,
Bearing the likeness of <s>Dharādhara</s> (the earth-supporter, Śeṣa), the arms of the protectors of the earth,
irresistible in force, shouldering the yoke of honor. || 72 ||
methodically they endure — having swiftly destroyed their enemies,

children.text: धरां धारयतीति धराधरः शेषो भुजगराजः, तस्याकारं सादृश्यं धारयन्तीति धराधराकारधराः । धराभुजां राज्ञां भुजा बाहवः । अहीनः पर्याप्तो विक्रमः शौर्यम् एषामित्यहीनविक्रमाः । सहसा त्वरितमकालक्षेपेण हता अरयोऽमीभिरिति हतारयः । रयेण वेगेन रंहसा उद्धुरा दुर्धराः । मान एव धूः कृत्यम् । मानधुरामवलम्बत इति मानधुरावलम्बिनः । महीं पृथिवीं पातुं रक्षितुं सहन्ते कल्पन्ते तादृशगुणयोगात् । क्रमात शास्त्रविहितेन क्रमेण न्यायेनेति यावत् । इह संदष्टयमकमादिमध्ययमकव्यपेतं मध्ययमकं व्यपेतमिति संभिन्नमुदाहृतम ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharādhara</s>' is <s>Śeṣa</s>, the king of serpents, who supports the earth. Those who bear the likeness, the semblance, of him — thus '<s>dharādharākāradharāḥ</s>.' The arms, the limbs, of the protectors of the earth (<s>dharābhujām</s>), of kings. '<s>Ahīna</s>' means sufficient, ample; their valor, their heroism — thus 'of undiminished valor.' Swiftly, quickly, without delay, the enemies have been destroyed by them — thus 'having destroyed enemies.' Irresistible (<s>uddhurā</s>) by their force, their speed, their momentum. Honor itself is their yoke, their duty — they bear the yoke of honor, they shoulder it — thus 'shouldering the yoke of honor.' They are capable of protecting, of guarding, the earth, due to possessing such qualities. Methodically — by the procedure prescribed by the treatises, by proper order. Here, interlocked <s>yamaka</s> — initial-middle <s>yamaka</s>, separated, and middle <s>yamaka</s>, separated — has been illustrated in a combined form.
Repetition in reverse order, in the domain of the foot, half-verse, and whole verse —
this <s>yamaka</s> is known as <s>pratiloma</s> (reverse), due to its reverse nature. || 73 ||

children.text: आवृत्तिरभ्यासः । कथं ? प्रातिलोम्येन प्रतीपतया लक्षिता, नानुलोम्येन, किंविषया ? पादश्चार्धश्च प्रकरणात् श्लोकस्य, श्लोकश्च [तेषां] समुदायः गोचरो विषयो यस्या इति पादार्धश्लोकगोचरा । पादगोचरा, अर्धविषया, श्लोकाश्रया चेति त्रिविधमनूद्य प्रतिलोमं नाम यमकं स्मृतमिति विधीयते । कुतः ? प्रतिलोमत्वात् तस्या इति गम्यते । प्रतिलोमेति कृत्वा । यत् त्वनुलोम्ना स पादाभ्यासादिरिति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: Repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) means recurrence. How? Characterized by reverse order (<s>prātilomya</s>), in the backward direction, not in the forward direction. What is its domain? The foot, the half-verse — contextually, of the verse — and the verse: the aggregate of these is its domain, its field — thus 'in the domain of foot, half-verse, and verse.' Having stated three types — foot-domain, half-verse-domain, and verse-domain — the <s>yamaka</s> called <s>pratiloma</s> (reverse) is ordained as being known. Why? Because of its reverse nature — this is understood. It is called <s>pratiloma</s>. As for what occurs in forward order, that is the foot-repetition type and the like — such is the implication.
Illustrating that, he says —

children.text: यामताश कृतायासा सा याता कृशता मया ।
children.translated_text: '<s>Yāmatāśa kṛtāyāsā sā yātā kṛśatā mayā</s>.'
'<s>Ramaṇārakatā te'stu stute tākaraṇāmara</s>.' || 74 ||

children.text: कृशस्य भावः कृशता । कृतो जनित आयासः श्रमो ययेति कृतायासा । या कृशता दौर्बल्यम् । सा याता प्राप्ता मया अमता प्रतिकूलतां [गता] आशा, अर्थात्

सुरतमनोरथो यस्येति हे अमताश मत्सङ्गमासहिष्णो ! हे रमण ! अकरणेनाकृतिमत्त्वेन अमर ! अकरणामर सत्यदेव ! यद्वा अकरणे अविहिते प्रमत्त ! अमर देव ! तव स्तुतम् । तदितः प्राप्तः हे स्तुतेत वर्णनेन प्राप्त ! ते तव अरकता गमनमेवास्तु । किमागमनेन, इयर्ति गच्छतीत्यरको [गन्ता] ततो भावप्रत्ययस्तल् विधीयते । समयमतिक्रम्यागतः कश्चित् प्रियः कयाचित्तु सरोषमित्थमधिक्षिप्यते । इदं पादप्रतिलोमयमकम् । प्रथमस्य तृतीयस्य च पादस्य [क्रमशः] प्रातिलोम्येन पाठे श्लोकनिष्पत्तिः ॥
children.translated_text: whose longing for lovemaking is frustrated — thus 'O <s>amatāśa</s>,' O you who cannot bear separation from me! O lover (<s>ramaṇa</s>)! By non-action, by your having a bodiless form — O immortal (<s>amara</s>), O <s>akaraṇāmara</s>, O eternally real one! Or, O one who is heedless of what should not be done! O god (<s>amara</s>)! Your praised fame — from that, O you who are attained through praise! May your departure (<s>arakatā</s>) alone be yours. What use is your coming? — <s>araka</s> meaning 'one who goes.' A certain lover who has arrived past the appointed time is thus rebuked angrily by some beloved woman. This is foot-reverse <s>yamaka</s>. When the first and third feet are read in reverse order, the verse is produced.

Emaciation (<s>kṛśatā</s>) is the state of being thin. One who has undergone exertion (<s>āyāsa</s>), fatigue — thus '<s>kṛtāyāsā</s>.' The emaciation, the weakness — has come (<s>yātā</s>) upon me (<s>mayā</s>). '<s>Amatā</s>' means one whose hope has become adverse,

children.text: नादिनोऽमदनाधीः स्वा न मे काचन कामिता ।
children.translated_text: '<s>Nādino'madanādhīḥ svā na me kācana kāmitā</s>.'

children.text: तामिका न च कामेन स्वाधीना दमनोदिना ॥ ७५ ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāmikā na ca kāmena svādhīnā damanodinā</s>.' || 75 ||

children.text: नादो नाम तत्त्वविशेषः शैवसमयप्रसिद्धः स विद्यतेऽस्येति नादिनो मे मम स्वा स्वकीया धीः । न विद्यते मदनः कामोऽस्यामिति अमदना ततश्च स्वाधीना सदृशवर्तिनी भवतु । एवं किमतः ? ततश्च मे मम न काचन न काचित् कामिता विषयाभिलाषः । कामेन दमं नुदतीति तेन दमनोदिना प्रशमप्रत्यनीकेन हेतुना ते तदभावादेव तामिका न भवितुमर्हति । कामनिमित्तः सन्तापो नास्तीत्यर्थः । इदमर्धप्रतिलोमयमकम् । अत्रार्धान्तरमारभ्य प्रातिलोम्येन पाठे श्लोकनिष्पत्तिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Nāda</s>' is a particular metaphysical principle well-known in the <s>Śaiva</s> tradition; it exists in him, hence '<s>nādina</s>' — my own (<s>svā</s>) intellect (<s>dhī</s>). It is '<s>amadanā</s>' — one in which desire (<s>madana</s>, love) does not exist — and therefore self-governed (<s>svādhīnā</s>), acting in accordance with its own nature. So what of it? Consequently, I have no desire whatsoever (<s>kāmitā</s>), no longing for objects. Since desire is absent (<s>damanodina</s>) — desire drives away (<s>nudati</s>) self-restraint (<s>dama</s>) — by that which is opposed to tranquility, as the cause; because of the very absence of that, darkness (<s>tāmikā</s>) should not exist. The meaning is: there is no suffering caused by desire. This is half-verse reverse <s>yamaka</s>. Here, when read from the other half-verse in reverse, the verse is produced.
'<s>Yānamānayamārāvikāśonānājanāsanā</s>.'
'<s>Yāmudāraśatādhīnāmāyāmāyamanādi sā</s>.' || 76 ||

children.text: मानमवलेपं यातीति मानयः दृष्टः त्रैलोक्यं विजग्राह । मानयश्चासौ मारश्चेति मानयमारः । तमवितुं रक्षितुं साधनभावेन तत्सामर्थ्यानुग्रहात्, शीलं यस्या इति मानयमारावी । स चासौ कशा प्रतोदश्चेति मानयमाराविकशा या काचिद् भवेत् तस्या ऊना हीना असमाना या न भवति किं तु समानैव तद्वत् कामसाधनत्वात् । यदाह— आनेत्यादि । अन.........सत्यानाः कर्तर्यत् समर्था इन्द्रियजयादियोगात् । जनाः, तेषामसनं क्षेपोऽतितरां यत्रेति अनाजनासना । मुनीनामपि रागजननी अत एवोदाराणां महतां शते बहुत्वोपलक्षणम् । अधीना यस्मात् सेवनात् यामायाम जितवानस्मि । सा अनादि नदिता भणिता । नान्या । किम् ? आयम् आगमनम् । आगच्छति, आहुतेति यावत् । कश्चिदितिवृत्तमात्मनः कञ्चित् कथयति । आनुलोम्येन तावदयं श्लोकः ॥
children.translated_text: She goes to pride (<s>māna</s>), arrogance — thus '<s>mānaya</s>' — seen thus, she has conquered the three worlds. She is both '<s>mānaya</s>' and '<s>māra</s>' (the destroyer) — thus '<s>mānayamāra</s>.' Her nature is to serve as a means to protect that, through the bestowal of its power — thus '<s>mānayamārāvī</s>.' She who is like a whip (<s>kaśā</s>) of <s>Mānayamāra</s> — any such woman — she is not inferior (<s>ūnā</s>), not unequal, but rather equal to that, because of being similarly an instrument of desire. As he says, beginning with '<s>āna</s>' and so forth: ... those capable through the mastery of the senses and the like. Of those people, '<s>asana</s>' means the casting, the utter agitation — thus '<s>anājanāsanā</s>.' Even of sages she generates passion; therefore, among the hundred (as a figure for many) great ones. She from whose service I have attained, conquered — that <s>āyāma</s> (control). She (<s>sā</s>) is <s>anādi</s> (the one proclaimed, spoken of). No other. What? The arrival (<s>āyam</s>). She comes, she is summoned — such is the meaning. Someone narrates his own story to someone. In the forward direction, thus is this verse.
In reverse, this very verse is read as —
'<s>Sā dināmayamāyāmā nādhītā śaradāmuyā</s>.'
'<s>Nāsanājanānā śokavirāmāya na mānayā</s>.' || 77 ||

children.text: सा काचिदभिमता स्त्री दिनमेवामयो विकारोऽत्यन्तरुक्षत्वात् दिनामयम् अधीता अधीगता प्राप्ता न न भवति किं तु अधीतैवात्यन्तसौकुमार्यात् । अत एवायः आगतः अनुभाव्यः आमः पीडा ययेति आयामा । केन ? अमुया प्रत्यक्षवर्तिन्या शरदा अतिदीप्रदिवाकरया हेतुना, अत एव च न जननमजननम् । आसनस्यावस्थानस्याजननमकरणं यया इति आसनाजनना सुखासिकामलभमाना शोकस्य त्वद्विरहसम्भवस्य विरामाय विनोदाय शोकाभिभवार्थं मानमहङ्कारं शोकमभिभवामि इत्येवं रूपं यातीति मानया भवति । त्वद्वियोगसम्भवं शोकमभिभवितुं न शक्नोति इत्यर्थः । श्लोकप्रतिलोमयमकम् ॥
children.translated_text: She, a certain beloved woman — the day itself is the affliction (<s>āmaya</s>), the disturbance, due to its extreme harshness — '<s>dinā-maya</s>.' She is attained (<s>adhītā</s>), reached, not not so, but indeed attained, due to her extreme delicacy. Therefore the suffering (<s>āyāma</s>) that has come, that is to be experienced, is prolonged. By what cause? By this autumn (<s>śarad</s>), present before one's eyes, with its excessively blazing sun. And therefore there is no birth (<s>ajanana</s>), no production, of a resting position — '<s>āsanājanānā</s>' — she who does not obtain comfortable repose. She becomes '<s>mānayā</s>' — she goes to pride in the form of 'I shall overcome grief' — for the purpose of allaying (<s>virāma</s>), of dispelling, the grief born of separation from you, for the sake of overcoming the grief. She is unable to overcome the grief born of separation from you — such is the meaning. This is whole-verse reverse <s>yamaka</s>.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>yamaka</s> (alliterative repetition). ||
If the identity of syllables between the two half-verses is in alternating positions,
the experts call that <s>gomūtrikā</s> (cow-urine pattern) — a difficult form, as follows: || 78 ||

children.text: अर्धयोः श्लोकसम्बन्धिनोरभिव्यक्त्यर्थः उपर्यधोभावेन लिखितयोः सम्बन्धिनां वर्णानां निरन्तराणामेकरूपत्वं सारूप्यं तेषामेव वर्णानां समुत्थानात् । एकैकमक्षरमन्तरं व्यवधानमस्मिन्नित्येकान्तरम् एकैकवर्णव्यवधानं यदि भवति निरन्तरपाठवदर्धयोरौत्तराधर्येण एकैकवर्णान्तरपाठे स एव श्लोको यदि
निष्पद्यत इत्यर्थः । तदीदृशं दुष्करं गोमूत्रिकेति अभिधानेन प्राहुः व्यवहरन्ति तद्विदो गोमूत्रिकाबन्धवादिनः । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: when read with alternating single syllables in upper-and-lower order, the same verse is produced — such is the meaning. That which is of this kind, which is difficult, is called '<s>gomūtrikā</s>' by that designation — they use this term, say the experts, those who speak of the <s>gomūtrikā</s> pattern. He gives an example with '<s>yathā</s>' (as follows):

Of the two half-verses belonging to the verse, written one above the other for the purpose of display — the identity, the sameness, of the contiguous syllables, arising from the very same syllables being produced. '<s>Ekāntara</s>' means having one syllable as the interval, the gap — if in the reading with alternating single-syllable intervals, just as in the continuous reading, the two half-verses,
'<s>Madano madirākṣīṇām apāṅgāstro jayed ayam</s>.'
'<s>Madeno yadi tat kṣīṇam anaṅgāy āñjaliṃ dade</s>.' || 79 ||

children.text: मदिराक्षीणां स्त्रीणाम् । अपाङ्गं कटाक्ष एवास्त्रमायुधं रागसाधनत्वाद् यस्येति अपाङ्गास्त्रः देवदत्तस्य गुरुकुलमिति यथा । मदनः कामः । अयं लोकविख्यातः ।

जयेद् जगद्वशीकुर्यात् । न क्वचित्प्रतिहतशक्तिर्य[दि] यस्मात् इष्टविषयप्रापणात् । मम एनः पापम् अर्थात् तत्प्राप्तिविघ्नभूतम् । क्षीणम् अस्तंगतम् ततः पूर्णमनोरथत्वात् अहमनङ्गाय तस्मै कृपाद्यपपत्तये । तादर्थ्ये क्रियासम्बन्धे वा चतुर्थी । अञ्जलिं प्रणामकरसम्पुटं दधेः रचयामि तमाराधयामीति कश्चित् कामी [काचित्] कामिनी वा ब्रवीति ॥
children.translated_text: He would conquer, would subjugate the world. His power is never obstructed, since he brings one to the desired object. My sin (<s>enas</s>), which was an obstacle to attaining that — has been destroyed (<s>kṣīṇam</s>), has perished. Therefore, since my desire is now fulfilled, I offer to <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love), to him, for the sake of showing gratitude. The dative case is used to express purpose or connection with the action. I make an <s>añjali</s> (respectful salutation with joined palms) — I fashion it, I worship him — thus says some lover, whether male or female.

Of the women with intoxicating eyes (<s>madirākṣīs</s>). The sidelong glance is the weapon (<s>astra</s>) — it is the armament for accomplishing passion — thus '<s>apāṅgāstra</s>,' like 'Devadatta's teacher's household.' <s>Madana</s> (the god of love). This one renowned in the world.
They call it <s>ardhabhrama</s> (half-rotation) if the verse-half rotates;
and if there is rotation in all directions, that is called the desired <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (all-auspicious). || 80 ||

children.text: औत्तराधर्येण चतुर्षु पादेष्वभिव्यक्त्यर्थं लिखितेषु प्रथममक्षरमारभ्य औत्तराधर्येण द्विराद्यन्ततः क्रमेण पाठे अर्ध निष्पद्यते, पुनस्तथैव परिशिष्टस्य पाठे अपरार्धनिष्पत्तिरिति श्लोकस्य द्वाभ्यां भ्रमणं श्लोकार्धभ्रमणं यदि भवेत् तादृशमर्धभ्रमं नाम दुष्करमाहुरामनन्ति तद्विदः ।
children.translated_text: When the four feet are written one beneath the other for the purpose of display, beginning from the first syllable, in upper-and-lower order, reading forward and backward twice in sequence — one half is produced; then in the same way, from the reading of the remaining portion, the other half is produced — thus, when the verse undergoes rotation by means of two such movements, that is called <s>ardhabhrama</s> (half-rotation), a difficult form, according to the experts.

children.text: सर्वतोऽनुलोमप्रतिलोमतः पूर्ववदौत्तराधर्येण च यदि भ्रमणं श्लोकस्य भवेत् तादृशं सर्वतोभद्रं नाम दुष्करमिष्टं तज्ज्ञैरिति ॥
children.translated_text: If there is rotation of the verse in all directions — forward, backward, as before, and also in upper-and-lower order — such is called <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (all-auspicious), a difficult form desired by the connoisseurs.
He illustrates both —
'O <s>Manobhava</s> (god of love)! Your army, a proud woman, is not for rising —'
'Through fear, immeasurable — or let us not, we who are sinful. O you who are near!' || 81 ||

children.text: हे मनोभव ! अत एव सर्वेषां चित्ताधिष्ठानतया हे नत ! प्रत्यासन्न ! देवान्तरवद् यो [न] परोक्षः, मानिनी काचिदिष्टा तव अनीकं सेना जगद्विजयप्रयुक्तत्वात् । [अन्या] सेना कुतश्चित् सभयापि । इयं त्वकुतोभया काचित् सेना इत्याह—भयादित्यादि । [सा] अमः पीडा । अमेयोऽप्रमाणोऽमो यस्या इति अमेयामा [भवतु] मा वा [भूत् । कुतः ?] भयात् [त्वदुत्थात्] कारणान्तरात् मा वा न भवति । सेयमीदृशी तवोदयाय जगद्वि[जय]लक्षणाय न न भवति, किं तु भवत्येव । केचन वयमत्र एनोमयाः पापस्वभावाः । अनुदयभाजस्तिष्ठामः, तत्प्रसादाप्रतिलम्भात्, प्रत्युत निर्दयभावनात् । तदियं प्रसीदतु तव सेनेति अर्धभ्रमम् ॥
children.translated_text: O <s>Manobhava</s> (born of the mind)! Precisely because of being established in everyone's consciousness — O you who are near (<s>nata</s>), not remote like other gods! A certain beloved proud woman (<s>māninī</s>) is your army, since it is employed for the conquest of the world. Other armies may be fearful from some quarter. But this one is fearless from all quarters — an army of such kind, he says: 'from fear' and so forth. She is '<s>ameyāmā</s>' — one whose suffering is immeasurable — let her be so, or let her not be. From what cause? From fear arising from you, or from some other cause — let it be or not. This army of such a kind is not not (<s>na na</s>) for your rising, for the conquest characterized by world-conquest — rather, it certainly is. Some of us here are sinful in nature (<s>enomayāḥ</s>). We remain without fortune, without obtaining her grace, but rather receiving only her cruelty. Let this your army be gracious — this is the <s>ardhabhrama</s> (half-rotation).
'<s>mārānāyāyānā rāmā</s>.'
'<s>Sāmāyāmā māyā māsā</s>,'
'<s>māyārāmā mārāyāmā</s>.' || 82 ||
'<s>Yānāvārārāvānāyā</s>,'

children.text: सा काचिदिष्टा रामा स्त्री मासा चन्द्रेण अमा सह माराय नाशार्थम् अस्माकमुपस्थितेति शेषः । कीदृशीति सा विशेष्यते । या रामा अमस्य पीडाया आयामो दीर्घता यस्य इत्यमायामा पीडावती मा न भवति । अदुःखनिमित्तं तप्यत इत्यर्थः । तदेव कुतः ? मारस्या कामस्य आनायो जालं जगद्बन्धनं किमपि तत् । अयानमगमनमपतनं यस्या इति मारानायायाना । यतोऽस्याः सुमन्दो रागः, तस्माद् अस्मद् दुःखेन [न] तप्यत इत्यर्थः । सा कीदृशीति पुनर्विशिष्यते [यानं पादयुगम् आवृणोतीति यानावारः, तस्य आरावः शब्दो वर्तते यत्र सा] यानावारारावा, अत एव आनं प्राणमायातीति आनाया बलीयसी माया परव्यामोहो फलोपायश्च आरामः क्रीडाभूमिरस्या इति मायारामा या ईदृशी सा माराय अस्माकमिति [योज]नीयम् । इदं सर्वतोभद्रम् ॥
children.translated_text: She (<s>sā</s>), a certain beloved woman (<s>rāmā</s>), together with the moon (<s>māsa</s>), in conjunction with the new-moon (<s>amā</s>), has arrived for our destruction (<s>māra</s>) — this is the remainder. Of what kind is she? She is further qualified: she, the beloved woman, whose prolonged suffering (<s>āyāma</s>) of pain (<s>ama</s>) is not absent — she suffers not without cause. And why is that? Because of some net (<s>ānāya</s>, snare) of <s>Māra</s> (the god of desire), some bond for the world — she is '<s>mārānāyāyānā</s>' — one who does not fall into it. Since her passion is very feeble, therefore she is not tormented by our suffering — such is the meaning. She is further qualified: one at whose footsteps (<s>yāna</s>) the sound of adornments (<s>ārāva</s>) resounds — thus '<s>yānāvārārāvā</s>.' Therefore she is strong — '<s>ānāyā</s>.' Illusion (<s>māyā</s>), the capacity to bewitch others and the means to an end, is her pleasure-ground (<s>ārāma</s>) — thus '<s>māyārāmā</s>.' She who is of such a kind — she is for our destruction — this should be construed. This is the <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (all-auspicious pattern).
Showing the difficult form characterized by the restriction of vowels, places of articulation, and consonants, he says —
The restriction of vowels, places of articulation, and consonants — that which is a difficult form among them —
is the desired one, starting from four; the other, starting from five, is shown as easy. || 83 ||

children.text: स्वरः अकारादिः । स्थानं च यद्भवो वर्णः कण्ठादिः । वर्णश्च व्यञ्जनं ककारादिः [तेषां] स्वरस्थानवर्णानां नियमः व्यवस्था इयत्ता, योऽसौ नियमो दुष्करेषु वर्णेषु मध्ये इष्टस्तज्ज्ञैः सोऽपि दुष्कर इत्यर्थः । एष च नियमः चतुर्भ्यः प्रत्येकस्वरस्थानवर्णेभ्यः प्रभृति आरभ्य चतुर्षूपादाय [क्रमशो न्यूनतया] एकं स्वरं स्थानं वर्णं वा यावद् दर्श्यते उदाह्रियते । तादृशस्य दुष्करत्वात् । न पञ्चप्रभृति, तस्य सुकरत्वात् । यदाह परः,—पञ्चप्रभृतिनियमः स्वरस्थानवर्णकृतः सुकरमुखेन क्रियते । तस्मान्नासौ निर्दिश्यते दुष्कर इति ॥
children.translated_text: Vowel (<s>svara</s>) means '<s>a</s>' and the like. Place of articulation (<s>sthāna</s>) means the throat and the like, where the consonant is produced. Consonant (<s>varṇa</s>) means '<s>ka</s>' and the like. The restriction, the regulation, the limitation, of vowels, places of articulation, and consonants — this restriction, among the difficult compositions, is desired by the experts — meaning it too is difficult. And this restriction is shown, illustrated, starting from four individual vowels, places of articulation, or consonants — that is, employing four and reducing further to one vowel, one place, or one consonant. Because of the difficulty of such a kind. Not starting from five, since that is easy. As he says: 'the other' — the restriction of vowels, places of articulation, and consonants starting from five is performed with ease. Therefore it is not designated as a difficult form.
'<s>gītīr ītīḥ prītīr bhītīḥ</s>.'
'<s>Āmnāyānām āhāntyā vāk</s>,'
'<s>dhe ye cec che deśe kṣeme</s>.' || 84 ||
'<s>Bhogo rogo modo moho</s>,'

children.text: आम्नायानां वेदानाम्, अन्ते भवा अन्त्या वागुपनिषदिति यावत् । सा गीतीर्गानानि विलासिनां सुखाभिमता ईतीरुपद्रवान् मृगाणामिव दुःखानुबन्धित्वाद् आहोपादिशदिति । प्रीतीश्च संसारे प्राकृतजनसुलभाः चित्तोद्धर्षात् । भीतीः त्रासाद् भयानुबन्धित्वाच्चाह । भोगश्च रूपादिविषयानुभवः । रोगो व्याधिर्विविधदुःखात्मकः

संसाराक्षेपकत्वात् । [तत्र] च वधबन्धनादिव्यसनहेतुत्वात् । तत्रैवं रोगभूते विषयभोगे मोदः सुखितोऽहं सर्वथेति हर्षो मोहोऽज्ञानम्, दुःखसुखविपर्यासप्रवृत्तत्वादित्यप्याह सा । यत एवं सर्वमुपद्रुतं संसारचक्रम्, तस्माद् देशे स्थाने क्षेमे सर्वोपद्रवरहिते शान्ते मोक्ष इति यावत् । धानं धा भिदादिदर्शनादाह [?] धारणे चित्तस्य इच्छा च छन्दश्च इच्छे
children.translated_text: because it casts one into <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). And because it is the cause of calamities such as death and bondage. In such enjoyment, which is in truth a disease, delight (<s>moda</s>) — the elation of thinking 'I am happy in every way' — is delusion (<s>moha</s>), ignorance, because it proceeds from the reversal of pain and pleasure — thus she also declared. Since all this, the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is afflicted, therefore in a place (<s>deśa</s>) that is secure (<s>kṣema</s>), free from all afflictions, peaceful — meaning <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). '<s>Dhāna</s>' means holding, sustaining; the desire and the will of the mind to hold —

children.text: अत्रेच्छाया द्धैविध्यं स्वीकृत्य द्विवचनमिति टीकाकर्तुरभिप्रायः प्रतिभाति ।

धे ये धातव्ये कार्ये । श्रेयोऽर्थिभिर्मोक्ष एवं शरण्यतया चित्तेन धारयितव्यः । तत्रैव च छन्दोऽभिधातव्यः न संसार इत्यप्याह सा वागिति । आकारस्य ईकारस्य ओकारस्य एकारस्यैव च प्रयोगात् चतुःस्वरोऽयं श्लोक इति ॥
children.translated_text: in the task that is to be sustained. <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) is to be held by the mind with the conviction of its being the refuge, by those who seek the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>). And the desire (<s>chandas</s>) should be directed toward that alone, not toward <s>saṃsāra</s> — thus that voice also declared. Because of the employment of only the vowels ā, ī, o, and e, this verse uses four vowels.

Of the <s>āmnāyas</s>, the <s>Vedas</s> — the final utterance that arises at the end is the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. That [voice of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>] declared that songs (<s>gītīs</s>), the musical compositions dear to pleasure-seekers, are calamities (<s>ītīs</s>), because like deer they are bound by suffering. And pleasures (<s>prītīs</s>) in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), easily accessible to ordinary people, arise from the agitation of the mind. And fears (<s>bhītīs</s>), from terror, because they are accompanied by dread — she declared. And enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) is the experience of sense-objects such as form and the like. Disease (<s>roga</s>) is affliction, consisting of various sufferings,
possessing supreme wisdom,
Devoted to the vow of conquering the earth and maintaining its stable governance,
in battle, the <s>Kurus</s>, the clan of their enemies. || 85 ||
they greatly restrained and mightily shook

children.text: क्षितेः पृथिव्या विजितिर्विजययोगः, स्थितेश्च तद्व्यवस्थाया यथावत् परिपालनरूपायाः क्षेमस्य च विहितिर्विधानं सम्पादनम् । एतदुभयमवश्यकर्तव्यतया व्रतं नियमः, तत्र रतिस्तत्परता येषामिति क्षितिविजिति[स्थिति]विहितिव्रतरतयः । कुरव इति वक्ष्यति । एतच्च प्रज्ञामन्तरेण न भवतीत्याह— परा शोभापरा गुणदोषविवेकसमर्था गतिः प्रज्ञा येषामिति परगतयः । एवं च शक्तिसम्पन्नरिपुविजयचतुरा इत्या

चष्टे, कुरवो राजानो यथोक्तगुणा युधि समरे स्वमात्मीयम् अरीणां कुलम् । उरु भृशं क्रियाविशेषणम् । रुरुधुरावृतवन्तः............वशमानयन् । दुधुवुश्च अभिभवादकम्पयन् । गुरु बलवत् । इदमपि क्रियाविशेषणम् । गुरु वा अरिकुलं शक्तियोगात् । अयमिकाराकारोकारमात्रप्रयोगात् त्रिस्वरः श्लोक इति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Uru</s>' (greatly) is an adverb modifying the action. '<s>Rurudhus</s>' — they restrained, enclosed... brought under their control. And '<s>dudhuvuḥ</s>' — they shook, overwhelmed them. '<s>Guru</s>' (mightily) — powerfully; this too is an adverb. Or '<s>guru</s>' qualifies the enemy clan as formidable, due to its strength. Because this verse employs only the vowels i, a, and u, it is a three-vowel verse.

The conquest (<s>vijiti</s>) of the earth (<s>kṣiti</s>); and the arrangement (<s>vihiti</s>), the accomplishment, of the welfare (<s>kṣema</s>) of its stable governance (<s>sthiti</s>), characterized by proper maintenance. Both of these being the vow (<s>vrata</s>), the obligation that must be carried out — devotion (<s>rati</s>) to that: thus '<s>kṣitivijitisthitivihitivrataratayaḥ</s>' (those devoted to the vow of conquering and governing the earth). '<s>Kuravas</s>' (the <s>Kurus</s>) — as will be stated. And this cannot be achieved without wisdom — hence he says: those whose wisdom (<s>gati</s>) is supreme (<s>parā</s>), that is, excellent, capable of discriminating between merits and faults — thus '<s>paragatayas</s>' (possessing supreme wisdom). And thus he declares them to be powerful, skilled at conquering enemies endowed with strength. The <s>Kuru</s> kings, possessing the qualities described, in battle, their own, that is, belonging to themselves — the clan of enemies.
Prosperity and radiance, modesty and fame, wisdom and conduct, speech and affection —

children.text: एधेते द्वे द्वे ते ये नेमे देवेशे ॥ ८६ ॥
children.translated_text: these flourish in pairs in him who is not like this lord of the gods. || 86 ||

children.text: ये द्वे देवानामीशे देवेशे सुरपतावपि न स्त इमे ते द्वे द्वे च वस्तुनी एधेते वृद्धिं गच्छतः । के ते इति विशेषेण दर्शयति— श्रीश्च विभूतिः दीप्तिश्च तद्भाविनी द्युतिराज्ञा वा श्रीदीप्ती । ह्रीश्च त्रपा [आकार]संकोचलक्षणा ततः कीर्तिश्च यशः सर्वत्र गुणख्यातिरूपा ह्रीकीर्ती । धीश्च प्रज्ञा हेयोपादेयविवेकस्वभावा तदनुसारिणी च नीतिः सम्यक्प्रयोगरूपा त्रिवर्गानुबन्धिनी धीनीती, गीश्च वाक् मधुरा लोक
संग्राहिका प्रीतिश्च तदनुवृत्ता गीःप्रीती, इतीमे द्वे द्वे सम्बन्धिन्यौ एधेते । नान्ये ये केचित् । इतीकारस्यैकारस्य च प्रयुक्तेर्द्विस्वरोऽयं श्लोकः ॥
children.translated_text: and <s>prīti</s> (affection) that follows it — '<s>gīḥprītī</s>.' These, in pairs, related to each other, flourish — and not in any others. Because only the vowels ī and e are employed, this is a two-vowel verse.

Those two [qualities] that do not flourish even in the lord of the gods (<s>deveśa</s>), the king of the celestials — these, in pairs, flourish, grow. What are they? He shows specifically: <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) and <s>dīpti</s> (radiance), which is the brilliance attendant upon it, or the radiance of command — '<s>śrīdīptī</s>.' <s>Hrī</s> (modesty), bashfulness, characterized by restraint of behavior, and from that <s>kīrti</s> (fame), renown, the spread of one's virtuous reputation everywhere — '<s>hrīkīrtī</s>.' <s>Dhī</s> (wisdom), intelligence, whose nature is the discrimination of what is to be rejected and accepted, and <s>nīti</s> (conduct), the proper application that follows wisdom, connected with the three goals of life — '<s>dhīnītī</s>.' <s>Gīḥ</s> (speech), sweet utterance that wins over the people,
<s>Mārā nāyā yānā rāmā</s> |
<s>Sāmā yāmā māyā māsā</s>
<s>Māyā rāmā mārā yāmā</s> || 87 ||
<s>Yānā vārā rāvā nāyā</s>

children.text: सर्वतोभद्रं पूर्वोक्तमेकस्वरोदाहरणमपि कल्पते इति पुनरुदाहृतम् । एकस्वरोदाहरणमात्रमिह विवक्षितम् । तच्च पूर्वसिद्धमेव सम्भवतीति किमपूर्वेणेदृशेनाहोपुरुषिकामात्रणेति भावः । पूर्वत्र्याख्यात एवार्थोऽनुसर्तव्यः । एवं स्वरनियमश्चतुर्विधो दर्शितः ।
children.translated_text: The <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (universally auspicious palindrome), described earlier, also serves as an example of the single-vowel type — hence it has been cited again. Only the illustration of the single-vowel type is intended here. And since that is already established from before, what need is there for something unprecedented, a mere display of bravado? — this is the purport. The meaning already explained in the previous context should be followed. Thus, the vowel-restriction (<s>svaraniyama</s>) has been shown to be of four kinds.
Showing the place-of-articulation restriction (<s>sthānaniyama</s>), he says —
O beautiful woman! Just once, cast your gaze upon the sky,
which is adorned with hosts of stars and free of clouds, delighting the eyes. || 88 ||

children.text: नक्षत्राणां गणैः शालिनि सम्बन्धिते विराजमाने वा नक्षत्रगणशालिनि, न विद्यन्ते [घना अ]स्मिन्नित्यघने मेघमलविकले अत एव नयनानामानन्दं प्रीतिं जनयतीति नयनानन्दजनने गगनेऽन्तरीक्षे दृष्टिर्दीयतां प्रयुज्यताम् । सकृत् एकवारमपि । तावतैव मदनपरवशायास्तस्याः प्राप्तेः । नाधिकं प्रार्थ्यते, सकृद् वा दर्शनेन गगनमनुगृह्यताम् । अन्यथै विफला अस्य शोभेति कश्चिच्चाटुकारः कामी कान्तामुपलालयति । अङ्गनेति प्रियामन्त्रणम् । कण्ट्यतालव्यदन्त्यमूर्धन्यमात्रप्रयोगात् चतुस्थानोऽयं श्लोक इति ॥
children.translated_text: Adorned with, that is, endowed with, hosts, groups, of stars — thus '<s>nakṣatragaṇaśālin</s>' (adorned with hosts of stars); in which there are no dense [clouds] — thus '<s>aghana</s>' (free of clouds), devoid of clouds and impurity — and therefore delighting the eyes, producing joy for the eyes — upon that sky, the firmament, let your gaze (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) be cast, be directed. Even once, even a single time. For by that alone, she who is overpowered by <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) would be won over. Nothing more is asked; or, even once, let the sky be graced by your glance. Otherwise, its beauty would be fruitless — thus some flatterer, a lover, coaxes his beloved. '<s>Aṅgane</s>' is an affectionate address to the beloved. Because only guttural, palatal, dental, and retroflex sounds are employed, this is a four-place-of-articulation verse.
O full-breasted one! Your face, dark with curling locks like the hue of bees,
with lotus-like eyes and moon-like radiance — whom does it not slay? || 89 ||

children.text: अलकः केशविन्यासविशेष एव चञ्चलत्वादिना लता । अलिवन्नीला अलकलता यस्मिन्निति अलिनीलालकलतम् । नलिनस्येव च्छाया शोभा अनयोरिति नलिनच्छाये सरोजतुल्ये नयने अस्मिन्निति नलिनच्छायनयनं शशिन इव कान्तिरस्येति तदीदृशमिति मनोहरं ते तवाननं कं न हन्ति कं नाम कामिनं दशमीं दशां न नयति ? सर्वमेव रागिणं हन्तीत्यर्थः । घनस्तनीति प्रियामन्त्रणम् । कण्ठ्यतालव्यदन्त्यमात्रप्रयोगात् त्रिस्थानोऽयं श्लोक इति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>alaka</s> (curl of hair), a particular arrangement of locks, is itself a creeper (<s>latā</s>) due to its curliness. Dark like a bee — the curl-creeper of which this is the quality — thus '<s>alinīlālakalatam</s>' (having curl-creepers dark as bees). With eyes whose beauty (<s>chāyā</s>) is like that of a lotus — thus '<s>nalinacchāyanayanam</s>' (with lotus-like eyes). Having radiance like that of the moon — thus such; your face, captivating — whom does it not slay, what lover does it not bring to the extremity of the tenth state? It slays every passionate person — that is the meaning. '<s>Ghanastani</s>' (O full-breasted one) is an affectionate address to the beloved. Because only guttural, palatal, and dental sounds are employed, this is a three-place-of-articulation verse.
O ever-sinless one, O ever-blissful one, O you who consort with women of bowed limbs —
your virtuous wife is afflicted with manifold distress from the assault of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love). || 90 ||

children.text: हे सदानघ ! सर्वदा निष्पाप ! अत एव विप्रतीसाराभावात् सन् विद्यमानः शोभनो वा आनन्दः प्रमोदोऽस्येति सदानन्द ! नताङ्गानां स्त्रीणां सङ्गः संभोगलक्षणः, तेन सङ्गतः अन्यस्त्रीसंभोगप्रसक्तः । हे नताङ्गासङ्गसंगत ! सती चासावङ्गना

चेति सदङ्गना तवेत्यर्थात् । अनङ्गेन कामेन लङ्घनमभिभवः ततो लग्नः सक्तः उत्पन्नः नानानेकप्रकारः आतङ्कः पीडा यस्या इति अनङ्गलङ्घनालग्ननानातङ्का वर्तते । अनङ्गेन वा लङ्घनं तत आलग्नो नानातङ्को यस्याः सेयमनुकम्प्यतामिति कञ्चित् कामिनं विषयान्तरप्रसक्तं निजबधूनिमित्तं सानुनयं काचिदेवमाह । कश्चिद् वा । कण्ठ्यदन्त्यमात्रप्रयुक्तो द्विस्थानोऽयं श्लोक इति ॥
children.translated_text: she who is both virtuous (<s>satī</s>) and a woman (<s>aṅganā</s>) — yours, by implication. By the assault of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), she has been overwhelmed; from that she is attached; and manifold, of many kinds, is the distress, the suffering, that has arisen in her — thus she is '<s>anaṅgalaṅghanālagnanānātaṅkā</s>' (afflicted with manifold distress from the assault of love). Or, by <s>Anaṅga</s> there is assault; from that has arisen manifold distress in her — let her be pitied. Thus some woman, with conciliatory words, addresses a certain lover who is attached to other objects, on behalf of his own wife. Or some [friend says this]. Because only guttural and dental sounds are employed, this is a two-place-of-articulation verse.

O <s>sadānagha</s> (ever-sinless one)! Always without sin — and therefore, due to the absence of remorse, possessing true joy — O <s>sadānanda</s> (ever-blissful one)! <s>Natāṅga</s> (women of bowed limbs) — the union, the sexual enjoyment, with women — through that, you are engaged, attached to the enjoyment of other women. O you who consort with women of bowed limbs (<s>natāṅgāsaṅgasaṅgata</s>)! Your virtuous wife (<s>sadaṅganā</s>) —
<s>Agāgāṅgāṅgakākākagāhakāghakakākahā</s> |
<s>Ahāhāṅgakhagāṅkāgakaṅkāgakhagakākakaḥ</s> || 91 ||

children.text: अकति कुटिलं गच्छतीत्यकम् । कर्तर्यच् । अक कुटिलायां गताविति धातुः । आ समन्तात् कायति शब्दायते इति आकम् । आतः प्रादिभ्य इति कः । अकं च तदाकं चेति अकाकम् । गङ्गाया इदं गाङ्गम् । गाङ्गं च तत् कमुदकं च गाङ्गकम् । गाङ्गकं च तत् अकाकं चेति गाङ्गकाकाकम् । तत्र तस्य वा गाहकः प्रवेष्टा हे गाङ्गकाकाकगाहक ! अत एव अघान्येवाघकानि कुत्सितत्वात् तानि मलिनत्वादिना काकाः तान् हन्तीति अघककाकहा कृतगङ्गास्नानत्वात् निष्पापस्त्वम् । ततश्च गां स्वर्गम् अगाः प्राप्तवानसि न सन्देहः । एवंविधस्य स्वर्गगमनमवश्यम्भावीति भविष्यत्यति भूतमुपचर्य अगास्त्वमिति भूतप्रयोगः कृतः, यथा अजितेऽपि बले जयकारणसाकल्यात् जितव्यपदेशः जितमिदं मया बलम् । कियदेतदिति प्रतिपत्तव्यम् । एवं पुण्यमयस्य तव शोकोऽपि न संभवति इत्यामन्त्रणद्वारेण सूचयति हाहेत्येवंरूपः प्रलापः शोकसंभवः । हाहा तमङ्गति......यातीति हाहाङ्गः । अगि गत्यर्थो धातुः । न हाहाङ्गोऽहाहाङ्गः । हेऽहाहाङ्ग विशोक ! एवं गुणयोगात् आ म्वर्गं प्रसिद्धस्त्वमिति संबोधनमुखेनाभिधत्ते । खग आदित्यः । सोऽङ्कश्चिह्नं तत्र गतेरस्येति खगाङ्कः स चासावगः पर्वतश्चेति खगाङ्कागः सुमेरुरिति यावत्, स च स्वर्ग एव, देवानां [तत्र] अवस्थानात् ! तं कङ्कति कीर्तिद्वारेण दच्छति इति व्याप्यादण्

children.translated_text: O <s>khagāṅkāgakaṅka</s>! And thus, because of your benevolent nature, association with the wicked too

children.text: तव नास्तीति कथयति अगन्ति कुटिलं गच्छन्ति अदान्तत्वादिति अगानि । कतर्यच् । अगानि च तानि खानि इन्द्रियाणि च इत्यगखानि तानि गच्छन्ति इति अगखगाः अदान्तेन्द्रियाः खला इति यावत् । त एव कुत्सितत्वादगखगकाः । तेषु अककः अलोलः अलुब्धः निरपेक्षः, तत्संसर्गद्वेषात् । हे अगखगकाकाक इति कश्चित् पुरुषः स्तुतः । कण्ठ्यमात्रप्रयोगादेकस्थानोऽयं श्लोकः ॥ ९१ ॥
children.translated_text: does not exist for you — he declares: '<s>aganti</s>' means they go crookedly, due to lack of self-control — thus '<s>agāni</s>,' by the <s>ac</s> suffix in the agent sense. Those '<s>agāni</s>' which are also '<s>khāni</s>' (sense-openings), that is, sense-organs — thus '<s>agakhāni</s>'; those who go with them are '<s>agakhagāḥ</s>' — those of uncontrolled senses, wicked persons. Those very ones, being contemptible, are '<s>agakhagakāḥ</s>.' Among them, one who is '<s>akaka</s>' — unswayed, uncovetous, indifferent — due to aversion to association with them. O <s>agakhagakākaka</s>! — thus some person is praised. Because only guttural sounds are employed, this is a one-place-of-articulation verse. || 91 ||

'<s>Aka</s>' — one who goes crookedly, from the root '<s>ak</s>' meaning 'to go crookedly' — the <s>ac</s> suffix in the agent sense. '<s>Āka</s>' — one who sounds forth all around, from '<s>ā</s>' + '<s>kai</s>' (to sound). '<s>Akāka</s>' — that which is both <s>aka</s> (crooked) and <s>āka</s> (sounding). '<s>Gāṅga</s>' — pertaining to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. '<s>Gāṅgaka</s>' — <s>Gaṅgā</s>-water. '<s>Gāṅgakākāka</s>' — that which is both <s>gāṅgaka</s> (Gaṅgā-water) and <s>akāka</s> (crooked-sounding). The '<s>gāhaka</s>' (one who plunges) into that — O you who plunge into the crooked-sounding Gaṅgā-water! And therefore, '<s>agha</s>' (sins) — those sins themselves are '<s>aghaka</s>' due to their contemptible nature — and those which are crows (<s>kāka</s>) due to their impurity — he who slays them — '<s>aghakakākahā</s>': you are one who has destroyed sinful impurities through having bathed in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. And therefore you have gone to heaven (<s>gām agāḥ</s>) — there is no doubt. For such a person, attainment of heaven is inevitable — using the past tense figuratively for the future, as when one says 'this army is conquered by me' even before the battle, due to the completeness of the causes of victory. This should be understood. And thus your grief too is impossible, since you are made of merit — he indicates through the address that lamentation of the form '<s>hāhā</s>' is born of grief. '<s>Hāhāṅga</s>' — one who goes to <s>hāhā</s>... '<s>Ahāhāṅga</s>' means one who does not go to lamentation — O you without grief! Thus, through the door of address, because of such virtue, your fame reaches up to heaven — he declares. '<s>Khaga</s>' means the sun. That is the mark (<s>aṅka</s>), and one who goes there — '<s>khagāṅka</s>'; and that is also a mountain (<s>aga</s>) — '<s>khagāṅkāga</s>' means <s>Sumeru</s>, which is indeed heaven, because the gods reside there. He who celebrates it (<s>kaṅkati</s>) through the door of fame —

children.text: एवं स्थाननियमश्चतुर्धा दर्शितः । संप्रति वर्णनियमं दर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Thus the place-of-articulation restriction (<s>sthānaniyama</s>) has been shown in four varieties. Now, showing the consonant-restriction (<s>varṇaniyama</s>), he says —
Hey, hey! O you crying, trembling deer — the tearing of your haunch is a sin that has befallen you!

children.text: किं केकाकाकुकः काको मामा गामा ममामम ॥ ९२ ॥
children.translated_text: Does the crow become a peacock with its call? Do not come, do not come near me, O possessionless one! || 92 ||

children.text: रे रे इत्यनादरे भर्त्सने वा । त्रासा[दिपर]वशतया भृशमभीक्ष्णं वा रौतीति रोरुः । रौतेर्यङन्तात् क्विपि रूपम्, रोरुश्चासौ रुरुश्च मृगविशेषः रोरुरुरुः । तस्य

ऊरुः क्रोडदेशः तस्य रुग् विदारणमेवागः पापं तद् गच्छतीति रोरुरुरूगागोगः । पर्वतदेशवर्तनात् तरुमूलगतगोपनघातुकेन केनचित् गोपेन दुरितमिदमाचरितमिति सविशेषं दर्शयति— अगस्य पर्वतस्याङ्गमेकदेशः । तद्गतः तत्रावस्थानात् अगाङ्गगः । अगेषु तरुषु व्यवस्थिता गावोऽस्य इत्यगगुः । त्वमेवं प्रत्यक्षपापः । मा मा सावेगे वारणे आम्रेडितप्रयोगः । मागाः मा आगच्छ । [मम मादृशस्य पुण्यात्मनः सविध इति शेषः ।] नेदृशः पापीजनोऽस्मदन्तिकमागन्तुमर्हति । अममो निष्परिग्रहः । मा अमम परिग्रहक्लेशोपहत इति तस्यामन्त्रणम् । अनेन मृगवधपातकनिमित्तं सूचितम्, परिग्रहोपहतानामेवेदृशदुश्चरितसम्भवात् । निष्परिग्रहाणां तु निष्पापत्वात् । यदि नाम एवं तथापि किं न युष्मत्समीपमुपगच्छेयमित्याशङ्क्य तदसम्भवं प्रतिवस्तुना दर्शयति । केका मयूरध्वनिर्मधुरः । तस्य सैव वा काकुः भङ्गः । तत्रैव सहजतया प्रतिनियमात् । तया कायति शब्दायत इति केकाकाकुकः । काको वायसः किं सम्भवति ? नैव । तद्वत् त्वद्विधपापजनसंसर्गोऽस्मद्विधानां श्रेयोऽर्थिनां न सम्भवतीति कश्चिन्मुनिः कृतमृगवधपातकं गोपालकमरण्यचरमात्मसमीपसर्पन्तमित्थमभिधत्ते ।
children.translated_text: the thigh (<s>ūru</s>), the flank region — the tearing (<s>ruk</s>) of that is itself a sin (<s>āgas</s>), and it goes to that — thus '<s>roru-rurū-ruk-āgaḥ-gaḥ</s>.' Since it was committed by a cowherd dwelling in a mountainous region, hiding at the foot of a tree — he shows this specifically: the limb (<s>aṅga</s>), a portion, of the mountain (<s>aga</s>); dwelling there — thus '<s>agāṅgagaḥ</s>.' One who has cattle (<s>gāvas</s>) stationed among trees (<s>aga</s>) — thus '<s>agaguḥ</s>.' You who have thus committed a manifest sin — '<s>mā mā</s>' is a reduplicated expression of alarm or prohibition. Do not come, do not approach — [near me, one of pure soul, is the remainder.] Such a sinful person is not fit to approach our vicinity. '<s>Amama</s>' means possessionless, without possessions. 'Do not, O possessionless one, be afflicted by the distress of possessions' — thus is the address to him. By this, the sin of killing a deer is indicated, since such misdeeds occur only among those afflicted by possessions. Those without possessions are sinless. If one objects, 'even so, why should I not approach your vicinity?' — anticipating this, he shows its impossibility by a counter-example. '<s>Kekā</s>' is the sweet cry of the peacock. That itself is the modulation, the inflection, of its voice — since it is naturally fixed there by inherent constraint. One who sounds with that '<s>kekā</s>' cry — '<s>kekākākukaḥ</s>.' Can the crow (<s>kāka</s>) become like that? Never. Likewise, the association of sinful persons like you with seekers of the highest good like us is impossible — thus a certain sage addresses a cowherd who has committed the sin of killing a deer, a forest-dweller who approaches his vicinity.
Because only the consonants r, g, k, and m are employed, this is a four-consonant verse.

'<s>Re re</s>' — in the sense of disrespect or reproach. '<s>Roruḥ</s>' — one who cries out repeatedly or intensely due to being overpowered by fear. This is the <s>kvip</s> form from the intensive (<s>yaṅanta</s>) of the root '<s>ru</s>' (to cry). He is both <s>roru</s> (crying repeatedly) and a <s>ruru</s> (a particular deer) — thus '<s>roru-ruruḥ</s>.' Of that deer,
The god who delights the gods, who drives away the reviler of the <s>Vedas</s>,
shook heaven with his roar as he tore apart the foe of the gods. || 93 ||

children.text: देवानां नन्दनः प्रीतिकरः तद्योगक्षेमाचरणपरत्वात् । वेदनिन्दिनः धर्माधिक्षेपकस्य लोकस्य नोदनो निषेद्धा [त्रयी]प्रवर्तनात् । देवो विष्णुः । तस्यैव तादृशत्वात्, वक्ष्यमाणविशेषयोगाच्च । दानवानसुरान् नन्दयति वर्धयति तद्योगक्षेमाचरणादिति दानवनन्दिनोऽसुरेश्वरस्य हिरण्यकशिपोः, अन्यस्य वा कैटभादेः दानेऽवखण्डने विदारणे नादेन दर्पोन्मुक्तेन सिंहनादेन [स्तम्भ]भङ्गसम्भवेन वा नादेन शब्देन तुमुलेन हेतुना दिवं स्वर्गलोकं दुदाव । किमिदमित्युपजातशङ्कमकरोदित्यर्थः । दकारवकारनकारमात्रात्मत्वात् त्रिवर्णोऽयं श्लोकः ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Nandana</s>' (delighting) — one who gives joy to the gods, because of his dedication to their welfare. '<s>Nodana</s>' (driver away) — the suppressor of the reviler of the <s>Vedas</s>, of one who scorns <s>dharma</s>, by establishing the path of the <s>Vedas</s>. The god is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because he alone is of such a nature, and because of the particular qualities about to be described. '<s>Dānavanandin</s>' (one who delights the <s>Dānavas</s>), meaning the lord of the <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, or some other such as <s>Kaiṭabha</s> — in the tearing apart (<s>dāna</s>), the splitting, of that foe, with a roar (<s>nāda</s>) — a lion's roar released with pride, or the sound arising from the breaking of the pillar — with that resounding, tumultuous sound as the cause, he shook (<s>dudāva</s>) heaven, the celestial world. He caused heaven to tremble with wonder — that is the meaning. Because this consists only of the consonants d, v, and n, this is a three-consonant verse.
The wise one, the essence among gods, demons, and enemies, together with the cranes,

children.text: ससार सरसीः सीरी ससूरूः स सुरारसी ॥ ९४ ॥
children.translated_text: the plowman, with his father-in-law, the destroyer of the demons' pride, traversed the lakes. || 94 ||

children.text: स प्रसिद्धः सीरी बलभद्रः सूरिः सर्वविद्याकोविदः सुराश्चासुराश्च तानासर्तुं व्याप्तुमप्रतिहतत्वात् शीलमस्येति सुरासुरासारी । [तादृशः] सारः सामर्थ्यमस्येति सुरासुरासारिसारः । नयसम्पन्नो विक्रमसम्पन्नश्चेत्युक्तं भवति । शोभनाभ्यामूरुभ्यां वर्तत इति ससूरूः । सौरूप्यमनेनोपलक्षितम् । सुरारसी मदिरास्वादी । तथा [च बलभद्रः] प्रसिद्धः । सरसीः क्रीडादीर्घिकाः ससार वारिविहारयोगेन निर्विवेश । किंविशिष्टाः ? आरसिभिर्मुखरैः सारसैः पक्षिविशेषैः सह वर्तत इति सारसिसारसाः । अनेन विलासित्वमस्योद्भावितम् । रेफसकारमात्रस्वभावतया द्विवर्णोऽयं श्लोकः ।
children.translated_text: He is the famous <s>Sīrī</s> (<s>Balabhadra</s>), a sage (<s>sūri</s>), learned in all sciences; whose disposition (<s>śīla</s>) is to pervade gods and demons alike without obstruction — thus '<s>surāsurāsārī</s>.' [Such a one] whose strength, whose capability, is such — thus '<s>surāsurāsārisāra</s>.' It is said that he is endowed with statecraft and valor. '<s>Sasūrū</s>' means one who exists with beautiful thighs — by this, handsomeness is indicated. '<s>Surārasī</s>' means a connoisseur of liquor — and thus [<s>Balabhadra</s>] is well known.
