He entered pleasure-ponds (<s>sarasī</s>) by way of water-sports. Of what kind? Those frequented by vocal <s>sārasas</s> (cranes), a particular type of bird, that is, '<s>sārasīsārasāḥ</s>.' By this, his pleasure-loving nature is evoked. This verse consists of only two consonants, being composed solely of the sounds <s>ra</s> and <s>sa</s>.
Surely our faces have been overwhelmed by this man,
by his face — and the lord, not a sinless man, wishes to send us, his followers, to fight this no lesser foe. || 95 ||

children.text: नूनं निश्चितमेतत् । किं तत् ? नोऽस्माकमाननानि मुखानि न [न] नुन्नानि किं तु नुन्नान्यभिभूतान्येव । केन ? अनेन पुरुषेण, येन सार्धं योद्धव्यम् । केन ? अनेनात्मीयेन मुखेन मातेण्डमण्डलेनेव तेजस्विना मुखेन । आस्तां तावद् युद्धम्, मुखमप्यस्यावलोकयितुमस्मन्मुखानि न शक्नुवन्ति । काऽप्ययमतिमानुषः पुरुषः । तादृशेन सह [यो] योद्धुमस्मान् नियुङ्क्तेऽसौ प्रभुरपरीक्षकोऽस्माकमिति कथयति । एतेन पूर्वोक्तेनानूनेनापि

केना[प्य]तिबलीयसा योद्धुमित्यर्थात् । निनीः.......... नियोक्तुमिच्छुः । अनान् प्राणिनः प्राणोऽनुजीविनोऽस्मान् नयतेः सन्नन्तात् क्विपि रूपम् । इनोऽस्माकं प्रभुः । ना पुरुषोऽयं नानेनाः एनः पापं न विद्यतेऽस्येत्यनेनाः न भवतीति किं तु सपाप एव । ननु वितर्क निश्चये वा, यदेनेनातिमानुषप्रभावेणास्मान् धातयितुमिच्छति । स्वयमप्यत्र योद्धुं प्राप्तः । इति केनचित् अतिबलीयसा योद्धुं नियुक्ताः प्रभुना अनुजीविनो वितर्कयन्ति । अयं नकारमात्रनिबन्धत्वादेकवर्णः श्लोकः ॥
children.translated_text: by some exceedingly powerful opponent — to fight, that is the meaning. '<s>Nīnīḥ</s>' ... wishing to command. '<s>Anān</s>' means living beings, life-breaths — us, his dependents — this is the form from the root <s>nay</s> with the <s>kvip</s> suffix after the <s>san</s> ending. '<s>Ina</s>' means our lord. This man (<s>nā</s>) is not sinless (<s>anenāḥ</s>) — '<s>enas</s>' (sin) does not not exist in him — he is not free from sin, but rather is sinful indeed. '<s>Nanu</s>' expresses deliberation or certainty: that he, with his superhuman power, wishes to destroy us. He himself too has come here to fight. Thus the dependents, commanded by their lord to fight against an exceedingly powerful foe, deliberate. This verse is a single-consonant verse, being composed solely of the letter <s>na</s>. ||

'<s>Nūnam</s>' means 'certainly, this is established.' What is established? Our (<s>naḥ</s>) faces (<s>ānanāni</s>) have indeed been overwhelmed (<s>nunnāni</s>). By whom? By this man, against whom we must fight. By what? By this face of his, resplendent like the orb of the sun. Let alone battle — our faces cannot even bear to look upon his face. This is some superhuman person. That master who commands us to fight against such a one is an undiscerning judge of our capacity — thus they say. By this [adversary], the aforementioned one, who is no lesser [in power],
He concludes the difficult path —
Thus, even the difficult path has been shown, its procedure somewhat demonstrated.

children.text: इत्युक्तेन विधिना दुष्करमार्गो दुष्करोऽपि काव्यप्रकारः । न केवलं सुकर इत्यपि शब्दः । किञ्चिद् ईषत् संक्षेपतः, तथा प्रतिज्ञानात् । क्रियाविशेषणमेतत् । आदर्शित उक्तः क्रमः स्वभावोऽस्येत्यादर्शितक्रमः प्रतिपादित इति दुष्करमार्गेऽपि
कश्चिदादर्शितः क्रम इत्यपि पाठः । तत्र दुष्करमार्ग विषयेऽपि क्रमः प्रकारः कश्चित् कोऽपि संक्षिप्तः आदर्शित इति योज्यम् ।
children.translated_text: there is also the reading 'some procedure has been demonstrated.' There, even in the domain of the difficult path, some procedure, some method, in concise form, has been demonstrated — this should be construed thus.

In the manner stated, the difficult path (<s>duṣkaramārga</s>), even though a difficult type of poetry — not merely the easy kind, as indicated by the word '<s>api</s>' (even) — somewhat, briefly, in concise form, as was promised. This is an adverb modifying the action. Its procedure, its nature, has been shown — thus 'having its procedure demonstrated' means it has been set forth. Even in the difficult path,
|| Thus ends the section on <s>citra</s> (the artistic). ||
Connecting the <s>prahelikās</s> (riddles), he says —
The nature of the types of <s>prahelikā</s> (riddle) is now set forth once again. || 96 ||

children.text: पुनः अथ प्रहेलिकानां तद्रूपाणां वा प्रकाराणां विकल्पानां गतिः स्वरूपं लक्षणं लक्ष्यं च, उद्दिश्यते प्रतिपाद्यते ॥
children.translated_text: 'Again' — that is, now: the nature, the essential characteristic, the definition and the exemplified, of the <s>prahelikās</s> (riddles), or of the types of such form, the varieties — is set forth, is demonstrated. ||
If one asks where such things are useful, he says —
In the diversions of playful gatherings, in secret counsel amidst a crowd of connoisseurs,
and also for bewildering others, <s>prahelikās</s> (riddles) are useful. || 97 ||

children.text: गोष्ठीनामनेकविधत्वात् क्रीडारूपाः प्रीतिस्वभावा रसवत्यो या गोष्ठ्यः समवायाः काव्यालापरूपा विदग्धानां ता एव सुखेन कालप्रेरणारूपत्वाद् विनोदाः तेषु क्रीडागोष्ठीविनोदेषु । तज्ज्ञैः प्रहेलिकावेदिभिः सह आकीर्णे जनसंबाधे स्थाने क्वचिन्मन्त्रणे गुप्तभाषणे तद्विदामेव तत्र गूढार्थानां प्रहेलिकानां रहस्यभूतार्थप्रतिपत्तिः । इतरेषां तत्र सन्निहितानामपि किमिदमुच्यत इति तदनवगमात् आकीर्णेऽपि मन्त्रणं प्रहेलिकाभिः साध्यते । [सामर्थ्यं चेद्] ज्ञायतां किमस्माभिरुच्यत इति व्यामोहने तत्त्वानिश्चयादाकुलीकरणे, नर्मरूपे वापि विषये । चैवेत्यपि पाठः । सहोपयोगेन प्रयोजनेन वर्तत इति सोपयोगा उपकारिण्यः । ततस्ता अप्यलङ्कारवत्

children.translated_text: should be considered in the treatise on poetics. And thus what was said by <s>Bhāmaha</s> —
Profound in the meanings of various verbal roots, bearing the designation of <s>yamaka</s>,
that <s>prahelikā</s> has been declared, in the response of <s>Rāmaśarman</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>. ||
If even these poems are, like treatises, comprehensible only through commentary,
they are a festival for the wise alone — alas, the dull-witted are slain! ||
— that has been set aside. Because of their utility, <s>prahelikās</s> must necessarily be discussed, just like ornaments. ||

Since gatherings are of many kinds, those that are of a playful nature, whose character is delight, that are full of aesthetic flavor — the assemblies of the cultivated, consisting of poetic conversation — those very ones, being a means of pleasantly passing time, are diversions. In such playful gatherings and diversions. In a place that is crowded (<s>ākīrṇa</s>), thronged with people, in secret counsel, in confidential speech, with connoisseurs, those who understand riddles — the apprehension of the meaning that constitutes the secret of riddles with hidden meanings is possible only for those who understand them. Even though others are present there, since they cannot grasp 'what is being said' — secret counsel in a crowd is accomplished through <s>prahelikās</s>. [And if the capacity is there,] in bewildering — 'understand what we are saying!' — in causing confusion through the non-determination of the true meaning, or in a subject of playful nature too. There is also the reading '<s>caiva</s>.' '<s>Sopayogā</s>' — having utility, purpose — they are useful, beneficial. Therefore they too, like ornaments,
Defining them, he says —
They call '<s>samāgatā</s>' (the conjoined) one whose meaning is hidden through the junction of words;
where deception is effected through a word established in a different sense, that is '<s>vañcitā</s>' (the deceptive). || 98 ||

children.text: पदयोः सुप्तिङन्तयोः सन्धिना पदघटनेन तादृशेन हेतुना गूढो दुर्बोधः [कृच्छ्रगम्यो]ऽर्थो विवक्षितमभिधेयं यस्या इति गूढार्थप्रहेलिकां समागतामाहुस्तद्विदः । गोपितार्थसमागतपदप्रधानत्वात् समागतेति तादृशी व्यवह्रियते यत्र प्रहेलिकायाम् अन्यत्र वा अर्थान्तरे ॥
children.translated_text: Through the junction (<s>sandhi</s>), the joining, of words (<s>pada</s>) — declined or conjugated forms — such a cause makes the meaning hidden, difficult to understand, [hard to grasp] — the intended signification of which is so — the connoisseurs call such a <s>prahelikā</s> with hidden meaning '<s>samāgatā</s>' (the conjoined). Because the conjunction of words with concealed meaning is primary, it is designated as '<s>samāgatā</s>.' Where, in the <s>prahelikā</s> or elsewhere,

children.text: रूढेन प्रसिद्धेनार्थान्तरप्रयुक्तेन शब्देन वाचकेन वञ्चना वञ्चनं वा । विवक्षिंताद् अर्थादन्यत्र बुद्ध्युत्पादात् विप्रलम्भो जायते यत्र सा तत्परत्वाद् वञ्चिता नाम विज्ञायते ॥
children.translated_text: through a word, a signifier, that is established (<s>rūḍha</s>), well-known, employed for a different meaning — the deception, the deceiving. Since an understanding is produced regarding a meaning other than the intended one, bewilderment arises — where this happens, that, because of its primary function [of deception], is known as '<s>vañcitā</s>' (the deceptive). ||
That which causes confusion through the employment of transposed or greatly separated words,

children.text: सा स्यात् प्रमुषिता यस्यां दुर्बोधार्था पदावली ॥ ९९ ॥
children.translated_text: that is '<s>pramuṣitā</s>' (the plundered), in which the sequence of words has a meaning difficult to grasp. || 99 ||

children.text: अतिव्यवहितानामत्यन्तविप्रकृष्टानाम् । यथा मोहो जायते । पदानां प्रयोगोऽभिधानमतिव्यवहितो वा । अतिव्यवहितः प्रयोगतः स्यात् । अत्यन्तव्यवहितपदयोजनाहेतोर्मोहः । सोऽर्थानिश्चयं विपरीतार्थप्रतिपत्तिं [च] करोति जनयतीति मोहकारिणी या सा व्यवहितपदप्रधानत्वाद् व्युत्क्रान्ता नाम प्रहेलिका वेदितव्या ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Ativyavahita</s>' means exceedingly far apart, greatly separated. Such that confusion arises. The employment, the expression, of words is greatly separated. It may result from greatly separated employment. Due to the cause of exceedingly separated word-arrangement, confusion arises. That confusion produces the non-determination of meaning and the apprehension of a contrary meaning — thus it is 'confusion-causing.' That which is so, because of the predominance of separated words, should be known as the <s>prahelikā</s> called '<s>vyutkrāntā</s>' (the transposed). ||

children.text: यस्याः प्रहेलिकायाः सम्बन्धिनी पदानामावली समुदायः दुर्बोधः कृच्छ्रगम्यः अर्थोऽभिधेयं यस्या इति दुर्बोधार्था सा प्रहेलिका अपहृतार्थत्वात् प्रमुषिंता नाम स्यात् ॥
children.translated_text: Of the <s>prahelikā</s> in which the sequence, the assemblage, of words has a meaning that is difficult to understand, hard to grasp — the intended signification of which is difficult — that <s>prahelikā</s>, because its meaning has been plundered, is called '<s>pramuṣitā</s>' (the plundered). ||
'<s>Samānarūpā</s>' (the homonymous) is one composed with words whose meanings are secondarily imposed;
'<s>paruṣā</s>' (the harsh) is one whose words are shaped by mere grammatical rule. || 100 ||

children.text: या गौणार्था मुख्यादभिधेयादन्यस्मिन्नभिंधेये आरोपितैरव्याप्तैः पदैः शब्दैः ग्रथिता विरचिता सा तादृशार्थान्तरप्रतिपादनपरत्वात् समानरूपा नाम स्मर्यते ॥
children.translated_text: That which is composed, constructed, with words that are imposed (<s>āropita</s>), not directly applicable, upon a signified meaning other than the primary — '<s>gauṇārtha</s>' (secondary meaning) — that, because of being primarily devoted to conveying such another meaning, is known as '<s>samānarūpā</s>' (the homonymous). ||

children.text: लक्षणस्य शब्दानुशासनस्यास्तित्वं सद्भावमात्रं प्रयोगप्रभृतिव्यवच्छेदात् । तेन व्युत्पादिताः संस्कृताः श्रुतयः पदानि अप्रहताः यस्यां सा प्रयोगप्रतीती रसविरहात् परुषा नाम स्यात् ॥
children.translated_text: Where the mere existence, the bare presence, of <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (grammar, the science of language) — to the exclusion of practical usage and the like — and by that, the words (<s>śruti</s>) are cultivated, refined, yet lacking impact — in such a <s>prahelikā</s>, devoid of aesthetic savor due to its [overly] grammatical nature, that is called '<s>paruṣā</s>' (the harsh). ||
'<s>Saṅkhyātā</s>' (the enumerated) is one where enumeration is the cause of confusion;

children.text: अन्यथा भासते यत्र वाक्यार्थः सा प्रकल्पिता ॥ १०१ ॥
children.translated_text: where the sentence-meaning appears otherwise, that is '<s>prakalpitā</s>' (the contrived). || 101 ||

children.text: कारणं साक्षादनुक्तस्य विवक्षितस्यार्थस्य संख्यामुखेन समुन्नयनात्, संख्याता नाम सा भवेत् ॥
children.translated_text: since the intended meaning, not directly stated, is elicited through the device of number — that is called '<s>saṅkhyātā</s>' (the enumerated). ||
Where, in the <s>prahelikā</s>, enumeration — unity, duality, and so forth — is the cause of confusion, of the non-apprehension of the true meaning,

children.text: यत्र प्रहेलिकायां वाच्यस्य पदसमुदायस्यार्थोऽभिधेयमन्यथा अवस्थितः, अन्यथा तद्विपर्ययेणावभासते प्रतिभाति सा प्रहेलिका प्रकल्पिता नाम, अन्यथार्थकल्पनपरत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Where, in the <s>prahelikā</s>, the meaning of the group of words, the signified, which stands in one way, appears otherwise, in its contrary form — that <s>prahelikā</s> is called '<s>prakalpitā</s>' (the contrived), because of being primarily devoted to contriving the meaning differently. ||
'<s>Nāmāntaritā</s>' (the name-concealed) is one in which there is multiple-meaning construction upon a name;
'<s>nibhṛtā</s>' (the concealed) is one with a concealed other meaning, expressed through language touching upon a common property. || 102 ||

children.text: यस्याः प्रहेलिकायाः सम्बन्धिनो नानार्थस्यानेकस्याभिधेयस्य कल्पना उद्भावनं भवति । कुत्र ? नाम्नि क्वचित् संज्ञायां विषये [सा] प्रहेलिका नाम्ना व्यवहितार्थत्वात् नामान्तरिता नाम स्यात् ॥
children.translated_text: Of the <s>prahelikā</s> in which there occurs the construction, the evocation, of multiple meanings (<s>nānārtha</s>) — of many significations. Where? Upon a name, upon some designation as the subject — that <s>prahelikā</s>, because its meaning is concealed by a name, is called '<s>nāmāntaritā</s>' (the name-concealed). ||

children.text: या दर्शितान्यार्था । [निभृतो निगूढः] निभृतो व्यवस्थितो वान्यार्थोऽभिधेयं यस्यामिति निभृतान्यार्था अभिधेयान्तरात् । कथम् ? तुल्यं समानमुभयत्र वृत्तेः, धर्ममर्थरूपं तन्निमित्तीकृत्य प्रवृत्तेः, स्पृशतीति तुल्यधर्मस्पृक् । तुल्यो वा विवक्षितेनार्थेन सदृशो धर्मो गुणोऽस्येति तुल्यधर्माणमर्थं स्पृशतीति तुल्यधर्मस्पृक् । तया तुल्यधर्मस्पृशा गिरा शब्देन हेतुना तादृशी गीः प्रयुज्यते या विवक्षितसदृशमर्थान्तरमभिदधाना । तत्रैव विवक्षितेऽर्थे निष्ठा अस्येति । यद्वा तुल्यधर्मस्पृशा गिरा कारणेन निभृतः अप्रकटोऽन्यो गृहीतार्थापेक्षया अर्थोऽभिधेयं यस्यामितिं योज्यम् । सा तादृशी प्रहेलिका निभृता आख्यायते ॥
children.translated_text: That whose other meaning has been shown: '<s>nibhṛta</s>' means hidden, or '<s>nibhṛta</s>' means established — that whose other meaning, signification, is hidden or established — '<s>nibhṛtānyārthā</s>' — from another signification. How so? Through language that touches upon (<s>spṛśat</s>) a common property (<s>tulyadharma</s>) — since the usage is the same in both cases, proceeding by taking as its basis the form of meaning that is a property, it touches. Or: whose property, quality, is similar to the intended meaning — touching upon a meaning having a similar property. Through such language, a word that serves as the cause — such a word is employed that denotes another meaning similar to the intended one. Therein lies the commitment to the intended meaning. Or: through language touching upon a common property, the other meaning, another signification in relation to the grasped meaning, is hidden (<s>nibhṛta</s>), non-manifest — in which this is the case, it should be construed. Such a <s>prahelikā</s> is called '<s>nibhṛtā</s>' (the concealed). ||
'<s>Saṃmūḍhā</s>' (the bewildering) is one achieved through a synonym presented alongside an equivalent word;
that which, though its meaning is directly stated, serves to cause bewilderment. || 103 ||

children.text: उपन्यस्तेन तदर्थानुसारेण कल्पितेन शब्दस्य विवक्षितत्वावाचकत्वेन प्रसिद्धस्य तदर्थप्रकाशनात् पर्यायेण शब्दान्तरेण साधिता उपन्यस्तशब्दपर्यायसाधिता । उपन्यस्तपर्यायार्थप्रसाधितेत्यपि पाठः । तत्र उपन्यस्तार्थानुगमकल्पितस्य तदर्थप्रकाशनात् पर्यायस्य शब्दान्तरस्यार्थे प्रसाधिता उपन्यस्तपर्यायार्थप्रसाधिता इति व्याख्येयम् । सा तादृशी समानशब्दा नाम प्रहेलिका ।
children.translated_text: Through a synonym (<s>paryāya</s>), another word, that illuminates the meaning of the word presented (<s>upanyasta</s>), arranged in accordance with its meaning — presented as a non-denoting equivalent of the intended word, illuminating its meaning — the <s>prahelikā</s> is achieved, is '<s>upanyastaśabdaparyāyasādhitā</s>.' There is also the reading '<s>upanyastaparyāyārthaprasādhitā</s>,' where the meaning should be explained as: achieved through the synonym's meaning that illuminates the meaning of the presented word. Such a <s>prahelikā</s> is known as '<s>samānaśabdā</s>' (the synonym-based).

children.text: साक्षात् वाचकव्यापारेण अर्थो निर्दिष्टः प्रतिपादितोऽस्याम् इति निर्दिष्टार्थापि । अतिशये अपिशब्दः । मूढये तत्त्वार्थाप्रतिपत्तये स्यात् । साध्यसंमोहकरत्वात् संमूढा नाम प्रहेलिका ज्ञेया ॥
अत्र श्लोकव्याख्यायां द्वेधा गूढये इति पाठ उदाहरणविरोधात् त्यक्तः ।

children.translated_text: Though its meaning has been directly stated, indicated through the function of denotative words — '<s>nirdiṣṭārthā</s>' — even so (the word '<s>api</s>' indicates emphasis), it serves to cause bewilderment, the non-apprehension of the true meaning. Because it produces confusion about what needs to be understood, the <s>prahelikā</s> should be known as '<s>saṃmūḍhā</s>' (the bewildering). ||
'<s>Pārihārikī</s>' (the circumlocutory) is one whose name involves a garland of connections;
'<s>ekacchannā</s>' (the one-concealed) is one where, having revealed what is dependent, the support is concealed. || 104 ||

children.text: योगानां सम्बन्धानां माला बाहुल्यं सा आत्मा तन्निमित्तत्वाद् यस्य तद् योगमालात्मकं नाम संज्ञानं प्रसिद्धं यस्याः
सम्बन्धि तत्समयत्वात् सा प्रहेलिका प्रसिद्धनामपरिहारयोगात् पारिहारिकी नाम स्यात् ।
children.translated_text: related to it, because of its being of that convention — that <s>prahelikā</s>, because of the connection with circumventing the well-known name, is called '<s>pārihārikī</s>' (the circumlocutory).

A garland (<s>mālā</s>), an abundance, of connections (<s>yoga</s>) — that being the essential basis, the cause — the name that is the well-known designation, '<s>yogamālātmaka</s>,' of the <s>prahelikā</s>

children.text: यस्या[माश्रित]माधेयं व्यज्य प्रकाश्य साक्षादभिधानात् आश्रयस्य आधारस्य गोपनं निगूहनं तद्वाचकस्य प्रयोगात् सा भवेदेकच्छन्ना नाम प्रहेलिका, एकस्याश्रितस्यैव छन्नत्वात् ॥
children.translated_text: Where, having revealed, having made manifest through direct statement, what is dependent (<s>āśrita</s>), the superimposed — there is the concealment, the hiding, of the support (<s>āśraya</s>), the substratum, through the employment of its denoting word — that is the <s>prahelikā</s> called '<s>ekacchannā</s>' (the one-concealed), since only one element — the dependent — is concealed. ||
That is '<s>ubhayacchannā</s>' (the both-concealed), in which both are hidden;
that is '<s>saṅkīrṇā</s>' (the mixed), in which there is an intermingling of various characteristics. || 105 ||

children.text: यस्यामुभयस्याश्रितस्य [आश्रयस्य] च गोपनमावरणम्, उभयच्छन्ना नाम सा प्रहेलिका स्यात् ।
children.translated_text: Where there is the concealment, the veiling, of both — the dependent and the support — that <s>prahelikā</s> is called '<s>ubhayacchannā</s>' (the both-concealed).

children.text: यस्यां नानालक्षणस्य समागतादिरूपस्यानेकस्य संकरः संभेदः स्यात्, सा सङ्कीर्णा नाम प्रहेलिका भवेत् ॥
children.translated_text: Where there is the intermingling, the blending, of many characteristics, of the forms of <s>samāgatā</s> and the like — that <s>prahelikā</s> is called '<s>saṅkīrṇā</s>' (the mixed). ||
These sixteen <s>prahelikās</s> (riddles) have been set forth by the earlier teachers;
and fourteen others, defective <s>prahelikās</s>, have been taught by them. || 106 ||

children.text: एता यथोक्तलक्षणाः षोडश प्रहेलिका निर्दिष्टा उक्ताः पूर्वैराचार्यै रामशर्मादिभिः । तल्लक्षणविरोधात् दुष्टाः हेयाश्च ताः प्रहेलिकाश्चेति दुष्टप्रहेलिकाः । न केवलमदुष्टाः । अत एव समागतादिविलक्षणत्वाद् अन्याश्चतुर्दश तैः पूर्वाचार्यैरधीता निर्दिष्टा इति ॥
children.translated_text: These sixteen <s>prahelikās</s>, having the characteristics as stated, have been set forth, declared, by the earlier teachers such as <s>Rāmaśarman</s> and others. Because they contradict the proper characteristics, they are defective and to be rejected — '<s>duṣṭaprahelikāḥ</s>' (defective riddles). Not merely the non-defective ones. And precisely because they differ from the characteristics of <s>samāgatā</s> and the like, fourteen others have been taught, declared, by those earlier teachers. ||
If one asks why those are not stated here, he says —
We, however, considering the faults to be innumerable,
shall describe only the good ones; those defective ones are without [valid] characteristics. || 107 ||

children.text: वयं पुनः । विशेषविवक्षायां पुनः शब्दः । दोषाः प्रहेलिकासम्भविनः हेयाः प्रहेलिका[श्च] अपरिसंख्येयाः । न लक्षणतो न लक्ष्यतश्च गुणवदादरेणाप्रतिपाद्यान् मन्यमानाः पश्यन्तः साध्वीरेव प्रहेलिका अभिधास्यामः ।
children.translated_text: We, however — the word '<s>punaḥ</s>' (however) indicates a special intention. The faults that can occur in <s>prahelikās</s>, the defective ones and the <s>prahelikās</s> [themselves], are innumerable — they are not to be set forth with the same care as the meritorious, either by definition or by example. Considering, seeing, this, we shall describe only the good <s>prahelikās</s>.

children.text: नन्वेवमपार्थादयोऽपि दोषा अपरिसंख्येयाः स्युः, विशेषहेत्वभावात् ? नैतदेवम् । अपार्थादयो हि दोषाः क्वचिद् गुणा अपि । यद्वक्ष्यति—

children.translated_text: That of the speech of the intoxicated, the mad, and children becomes faulty elsewhere —

children.text: इत्यादि । ततस्ते चिन्तनीयाः । प्रहेलिकादोषास्तु न क्वचिद् गुणा अपि, यतोऽपार्थादिवन्निरूपणीयाः स्युः । अतश्च अपार्थादयो वक्तव्या यतः सर्वकाव्यसम्भविनस्ते दोषाः । प्रहेलिकादोषास्तु प्रादेशिका इत्याशयवता उक्तम्— दोषानित्यादि । यद्वा, प्रहेलिकादोषा अपरापरदोषसम्भवेन चतुर्दशेति इयत्तया अपरिसंख्येयाः । ततश्चातिप्रसङ्गान्नोच्यन्ते इत्यभिप्रायेणोक्तम्— दोषानित्यादि । अपार्थादयस्तु सर्वकाव्यदोषाः परिसंख्या[ताः] । तथैव न तद्वचनेऽतिप्रसङ्ग इति चाकूतम् । अत एवाभिधास्यति—
children.translated_text: and so forth. Therefore, these must be considered. The faults of <s>prahelikā</s> (riddles), however, are never virtues anywhere, since they would need to be examined just like <s>apārtha</s> (meaninglessness) and the like. And therefore, <s>apārtha</s> and similar faults are to be discussed, since those faults can occur in all poetry. But the faults of <s>prahelikā</s> are provincial — with this intent it was said: 'faults' and so forth. Alternatively, the faults of <s>prahelikā</s>, through the possibility of ever-new faults, are innumerable even by the count of fourteen. And therefore, because of the danger of over-extension, they are not stated — with this intent it was said: 'faults' and so forth. The faults such as <s>apārtha</s> and the like, being faults of all poetry, are enumerable. Accordingly, there is no over-extension in stating them — such is the intention. For this very reason, he will state —

But then, would not faults like meaninglessness and the like also be innumerable, since there is no distinguishing ground? This is not so. For faults like meaninglessness and the like are, in some contexts, actually virtues. As he will state —
'The faults are only ten' —

children.text: इति । कथं तर्हि दुष्टप्रहेलिका ज्ञायन्ते यथा
वर्ज्येरन् । न हि दुष्टतया अज्ञातानां परिहारः संभवतीत्याशङ्क्य तत्प्रत्युपायमाह— याः प्रहेलिकाः । तुशब्दः
children.translated_text: they may be avoided? For the avoidance of things unknown as faulty is not possible — anticipating this doubt, he states the remedy: 'those <s>prahelikās</s>, however.' The word '<s>tu</s>' indicates

children.text: अर्थान्तरविवक्षायाम् । यथोक्तलक्षणविरहात् न विद्यते लक्षणमासामित्यलक्षणाः, ताः स्वयमेव दुष्टा ज्ञायन्ते । प्रतिनियतलक्षणव्युत्पत्तेः, अतल्लक्षणानां तदाभासताप्रतिपत्तेः । किं तासां प्रपञ्चप्रयासेनेति ?
children.translated_text: a different sense. Those that lack the defining characteristics as stated — those whose definition does not exist — such characterless ones are themselves known to be faulty. Because of the derivation from the specific established definitions, those that lack such definitions are understood as mere semblances thereof. What need is there for the elaborate labor of detailing them?
How then are faulty <s>prahelikās</s> to be recognized, so that
My heart, you are not one who knows the taste of offense — why then are you angry?
Enough with these misplaced tears, O red-eyed one! || 108 ||

children.text: हे मम चेतः, आगसोऽपराधस्य व्यलीकस्य रसं स्वादमाचरणरूपम् अभिजानातीत्यागोरसाभिज्ञं कृतदोषं न भवति । ततो निरागसे मह्यं कस्मात् कारणात् प्रकृप्यसि ? न किञ्चित् कारणम् । ततश्चायमकारणः कोपो न कार्य इति वारयति । व्यलीकलक्षणकोपस्थानाभावादस्थाने अकाण्डे रुदितैरश्रुपातै कोपमयैः एतैरिति प्रत्यक्षनिर्देशः । अलं वारणे । मा रोदीरित्यर्थः । आलोहितेक्षणे इति प्रियामन्त्रणम् । मे आगोरसाभिज्ञमित्यनयोः पादयोः मयागोरसाभिज्ञमिति अयादेशेन सन्धिना विवक्षितार्थस्य गूढार्थत्वात् समागतेयमुदाहृतेति ॥
children.translated_text: O my heart! '<s>Āgorasābhijña</s>' means one who knows the taste, the savor, that is, the experience, of offense (<s>āgas</s>), wrongdoing — it is not so, it has not committed a fault. Therefore, why are you angry with me, who am without offense? There is no reason. And therefore this causeless anger should not be indulged — thus he restrains her. 'Misplaced' — because of the absence of the ground for anger characterized by wrongdoing — at an inappropriate, untimely occasion. With these tears, these weepings, filled with anger — 'these' is a demonstrative reference. '<s>Alam</s>' in the sense of prohibition — meaning: do not weep. '<s>Ālohitekṣaṇe</s>' (O red-eyed one) is an address to the beloved. In the two verse-quarters '<s>me āgorasābhijñam</s>,' through the euphonic combination (<s>sandhi</s>) yielding '<s>mayāgorasābhijñam</s>,' the intended meaning becomes hidden — therefore this is illustrated as a <s>samāgatā</s> (convergent) [type of <s>prahelikā</s>]. ||
As your delight increases in serving the hunchback woman,
it does not so increase when you enjoy women who rival the celestial maidens. || 109 ||

children.text: कुब्जा स्त्रियमासेवमानस्य निर्विशतः ते तव रतिः प्रमोदो वर्द्धते । यथा एवं तथा अमरस्त्रीविडम्बिनीर्दिव्याङ्गनासमाना नारीनिर्विशतः सेवमानस्य रतिर्न वर्धते । तत्रैव तवाधिकारादित्यर्थः । अत्र कुब्जा [इत्यनेन] कन्याकुब्जा विवक्षिता यथा सत्यभामा भामेति । तद्नतिस्तद्गतौ वा । पुरुषः कुब्जाशब्देन भग्नपृष्ठदेशायां योषिति रूढेन तत्र प्रतीतिजननात् वञ्च्यत इति वञ्चितेयं निदर्शिता ॥
children.translated_text: Of one who serves, who frequents, a hunchback (<s>kubjā</s>) woman — of one who enjoys — your delight, your pleasure, increases. Just as it does so, in the same manner, of one who enjoys women rivaling the celestial maidens, divine beauties — the delight does not increase. Because your predilection lies there alone — such is the meaning. Here, by '<s>kubjā</s>' is intended <s>Kānyakubjā</s> (the city Kanauj), just as <s>Satyabhāmā</s> is called '<s>Bhāmā</s>.' The intended meaning refers to devotion or residence there. A man is deceived by the word '<s>kubjā</s>,' which is established in common usage as referring to a hunchbacked woman, because it generates that understanding — thus this is illustrated as a <s>vañcitā</s> (deceptive) [type]. ||
The swan kisses the face of the lotus-plant, on the stalk with its rough thorns,
making a sweet sound with its beak, scratching the limbs. || 110 ||

children.text: अत्र पद्मिन्या मुखं कमलरूपं तुण्डेन चञ्च्वा चुम्बति हंसः, वल्गु मनोहरं यथा भवति तथा रवं रुतं कुर्वन् कर्कशः कण्टकोऽस्मिन्निति कर्कशकण्टके पद्मिन्या दण्डे नाले अङ्गानि अवयवान् घदृयन् कण्डूयमान इत्ययमत्रार्थो विवक्षितः । तत्र च दण्डे चुम्बतीत्यादिव्यवहितपदप्रयोगान्मोहो जायत इति व्युत्क्रान्ता इयमुदाहृता ॥
children.translated_text: Here, the intended meaning is: the swan (<s>haṃsa</s>) kisses the face, the lotus-flower, of the lotus-plant (<s>padminī</s>) with its beak; making a sound that is sweet, charming; scratching the limbs, the parts, on the stalk, the stem, of the lotus-plant, which has rough thorns. The confusion arises from the employment of words in a disjointed order, such as 'on the stalk, kisses' — thus this is illustrated as a <s>vyutkrāntā</s> (transposed) [type]. ||

children.text: खातयः कनि काले ते स्फातयः स्फीतवल्गवः ।
children.translated_text: O maiden! On your beautiful, moon-like foot,
the anklets, plentiful and of rich, sweet sound, become manifest right now. || 111 ||

children.text: हे कनि कन्ये ! ते तव काले पादे चन्द्रे मनोज्ञे चन्द्रे वा हे कमनीये प्रिया

मन्त्रणमेतत् । खातयः किंङ्किणिकाः नू पुरादिरूपा स्फातयः स्फीताः पर्याप्तशोभाः स्फीतवल्गवः मधुरघनारसाः साक्षाद्भवन्ति । प्रत्यक्षतामुपयान्ति । तन्निनदग्रहणादाकर्णान्तचक्षुषा वा गृह्यन्त इत्यर्थः । अत्रेदृशमनोज्ञवस्तुसाक्षात्करणे मम वायवः प्राणाः । रागाभिभवात् चारिणोऽनवस्थायिनः । यान्तीत्यर्थः । एवं दुर्बोधार्थपदप्रयोगात् प्रमुषितेयं लक्षितेति ॥
children.translated_text: the beloved. The anklets (<s>khātayaḥ</s>), the <s>kiṅkiṇikās</s> in the form of anklet-bells (<s>nūpura</s>) and the like, are plentiful (<s>sphātayaḥ</s>), of ample beauty, and of rich, sweet sound — they become manifest directly, they come into perception. They are apprehended through the grasping of that tinkling sound, or through the eye that extends to the ear. Here, upon perceiving such a charming thing directly, my life-breaths (<s>vāyavaḥ</s>) are departing (<s>cāriṇaḥ</s>), becoming unsteady — because of being overwhelmed by passion. They depart — such is the meaning. Thus, through the employment of words whose meanings are difficult to comprehend, this is illustrated as a <s>pramuṣitā</s> (robbed [of meaning]) [type]. ||
O maiden (<s>kani</s>)! On your foot (<s>kāle</s>), which is beautiful, moon-like (<s>candre</s>) — or: O charming one — this is an address to
In this garden, I saw a creeper with five shoots,
on each shoot of which there is a fresh cluster of blossoms. || 112 ||

children.text: वल्लरीति स्त्रीत्वसाधर्म्येण काचिद् योषिद् विवक्षिता । पल्लवशब्देन च तत्साम्यादङ्गुलयः कुसुममञ्जरीति च तत्सादृश्यात् नखाः । शेषं सुगमम् । एवं गौणार्थप्रयुक्तैर्वल्लरीत्यादि शब्दैः साधितेयं समानरूपा निरूपितेति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Vallarī</s>' (creeper) — by the analogy of femininity, some woman is intended. By the word '<s>pallava</s>' (shoot), because of the similarity, the fingers [are meant]; and by '<s>kusumamañjarī</s>' (cluster of blossoms), because of the resemblance, the nails [are meant]. The rest is easy to understand. Thus, through words like '<s>vallarī</s>' and the like employed in their secondary, figurative senses, this is illustrated as a <s>samānarūpā</s> (homologous) [type], established through secondary meaning. ||
The topers wander freely in the liquor-house,

children.text: मज्जन्त इव मत्तास्ते सौरे सरसि संप्रति ॥ ११३ ॥
children.translated_text: with their teeth gleaming — as if plunging, intoxicated, in the sun's lake. || 113 ||

children.text: सुरां कुर्वन्तीति तत्करोति तदाचष्ट इति णिजन्तात् सुरयतीति कर्तर्यचि विहिते सुराः शौण्डिकाः । मत्तास्ते केचित् विवक्षिताः । सुराया आलये मदिरामन्दिरे सम्प्रति स्वैरं यथेष्टं भ्रमन्ति । दशनार्चिषा दन्तप्रभया परितः स्फुरन्त्या लक्षिताः । सुराया इदं सौरे मद्यसरसि ह्रदे मज्जन्त इव लक्ष्यमाणाः । सुरा इत्यस्य शौण्डिकेषु सुरासम्बन्धिनि च सौर इत्यस्याप्रसिद्धेः । लक्षणस्य च तादृशस्य सम्भवात् परुषेयम् आविष्कृतेति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Surāḥ</s>' — those who make <s>surā</s> (liquor), that is, drunkards, from the causative '<s>surayati</s>,' the agent form with the suffix '<s>ac</s>.' Certain intoxicated ones are intended. They wander freely, as they please, in the <s>surā-ālaya</s>, the liquor-house. Marked, identified, by the radiance of their teeth (<s>daśanārcis</s>), gleaming all around. They appear as if plunging in the <s>saura</s> (solar) lake, the pond of wine. Because '<s>surā</s>' in the sense of drunkards and '<s>saura</s>' in the sense of relating to wine are uncommon. And since such a definition is possible — this is illustrated as a <s>paruṣā</s> (harsh/rough) [type], being revealed [through uncommon usage]. ||
There is a certain city, with the nasal [phoneme] in the middle, adorned with the four <s>varṇas</s>,
in which there are kings designated by the eight <s>varṇas</s>. || 114 ||

children.text: नासिक्यो वर्णो ञकारोऽत्र विवक्षितः । मध्ये मध्यो वा यस्याः सा नासिक्यमध्या । परित आद्यन्ततः । चतुर्भिर्वर्णैः विभूषिता अस्ति वर्तते पुरी काचित् ।

यस्यां पुर्यामष्टौ वर्णा आह्वयः संज्ञा येषामित्यष्टवर्णाह्वया नृपा राजानः सन्ति । अत्र काञ्ची पुरी पल्लवाश्च तस्यां नृपा इति परमार्थः । चतुरादिसंख्योपादानं तु तद्विवक्षितार्थव्यामोहकरमिति संख्यातेयमाख्यातेति ॥
children.translated_text: In which city there are kings whose designation (<s>āhvaya</s>) consists of eight phonemes. Here, the actual meaning is: the city is <s>Kāñcī</s>, and the <s>Pallavas</s> are the kings therein. The use of numbers like four and the like is to cause confusion about the intended meaning — thus this is illustrated as a <s>saṅkhyātā</s> (numerical) [type]. ||

The nasal phoneme — the <s>ña</s>-sound is intended here. That which has this as its middle, or in the middle — thus '<s>nāsikyamadhyā</s>' (with the nasal in the middle). Around — at the beginning and end. Adorned with four phonemes — there exists a certain city.

children.text: गिरा स्खलन्त्या नम्रेण शिरसा दीनया दृशा ।
children.translated_text: With faltering speech, with bowed head, with a pitiable gaze,
standing even trembling — O elder, you do not pity me! || 115 ||

children.text: स्खलन्त्या दौर्गत्योपहतस्येश्वरेषु प्रतिभाक्षयगृहीतस्य व्याकुलवचनत्वाद्, रागादेशाच्चेति द्वैधम् । नम्रेण शिरसा दुर्विधस्य पराराधनपरत्वात् रागरसाच्चेति अपरं द्वैधम् । दीनया दृशा दरिद्रेण निरानन्दत्वात्

अभिमतरागविषयासिद्धेश्चेत्यपरं द्वैधम् । सोत्कम्पमत्यन्तं क्षीणत्वात् कामावेशाच्चेति इदमपि द्विधा । वृद्धा शब्दस्य जरतीवाचिनः संबोधने वृद्धे इति । [तथैव] वृद्धाशब्दस्य लक्ष्मीवचनस्य इत्यपरं द्वैधम् । एवं तिष्ठन्तमनुकम्पाभाजनमपि किं मां नानुकम्पसे ? अत्र कश्चिद् दरिद्रो लक्ष्मीं लभताम् इति विवक्षितो वाक्यार्थः । वृद्धां काञ्चित् योषितमाभाषते कश्चित् कामीति अन्यस्त्वर्थः प्रतिभाति । तदियं प्रकल्पिता निदर्शितेति ॥
children.translated_text: or because of failure to obtain the desired object of passion — thus another double meaning. 'Trembling' — because of being extremely emaciated; or because of the onslaught of desire — this too is twofold. '<s>Vṛddhe</s>' — the vocative of the word '<s>vṛddhā</s>' meaning an old woman. Likewise, '<s>vṛddhā</s>' in the sense of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) — thus another double meaning. Thus, standing even so, deserving of pity — why do you not pity me? Here, the intended sentence-meaning is that a poor man should obtain <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth). But another meaning appears: some lover addresses some old woman. Thus this is illustrated as a <s>prakalpitā</s> (constructed) [type]. ||

'Faltering' — because of being afflicted by misfortune, losing eloquence before the powerful, with confused speech; or because of the instruction of passion — thus there is a double meaning. 'With bowed head' — because of being devoted to serving others, being wretched; or because of the passion of desire — thus another double meaning. 'With pitiable gaze' — pitiable because of being poor, joyless;
In the beginning, 'king' — O restless-eyed one! — some sovereign is celebrated,
and as 'eternal' — yet he is neither a king nor eternal. || 116 ||

children.text: हे अधीराक्षि ! कोऽपि कश्चिदनिर्धारितरूपविशेषः पार्थिवः पृथिवीपतिः वृक्षश्च इति श्लिष्टम् । आदौ प्रथमतो राजेत्येवं गीयते कीर्त्त्यते । सनातनश्च गीयते । सनातनश्च शाश्वतः, विष्णुर्वा । न विद्यतेऽतनः शब्दोऽस्मिन्निति अतनः स पार्थिवः । आदौ राजेति यो गीयते, न अतनः किं तु तनः शब्दसहित एवेतिं त्रैविध्यम् । यद्वा न तन अतनः । न तथा नातनः । सह तेन वर्तत इति सनातनश्च कोऽपि पार्थिवो गीयते । स एवार्थः । व्युत्त्पत्तिमात्रेण भिद्यते । असौ पूर्वोक्तः । आदौ राजा सनातनश्च नैव राजा महीपतिराद्यः । नापि सनातनः शाश्वतो विष्णुर्वा भवति । राजातन इति वृक्षविशेषस्य नाम, यस्य क्षीरीति प्रसिद्धिः । तत्रेयं नानार्थकल्पनेति नामान्तरितेयमुदीरिता ॥
children.translated_text: O restless-eyed one! Some, that is, some unspecified, sovereign (<s>pārthiva</s>) — which also means 'tree' through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). At first, he is celebrated as 'king' (<s>rāja</s>). And as '<s>sanātana</s>' (eternal), everlasting — or as <s>Viṣṇu</s>. '<s>Atanaḥ</s>' means one in whom there is no sound — that sovereign. He who is celebrated at first as 'king' is not '<s>atana</s>' (without sound) but rather '<s>tana</s>' (with sound), accompanied by sound — thus there is a threefold [reading]. Or: '<s>na tana</s>' means '<s>atanaḥ</s>'; '<s>na tathā</s>' means '<s>nātanaḥ</s>'; existing together with that is '<s>sanātanaḥ</s>' — and some sovereign is celebrated. The meaning is the same. It differs only in the etymological derivation. The aforementioned [sovereign] — at first a king and eternal — is neither a king, a lord of the earth, the first [king]; nor eternal, everlasting, or <s>Viṣṇu</s>. '<s>Rājātana</s>' is the name of a particular tree, known popularly as a 'milk-tree' (<s>kṣīrī</s>). This involves the fabrication of manifold meanings — thus this is illustrated as a <s>nāmāntaritā</s> (disguised by name) [type]. ||

children.text: हृतद्रव्यं जनं त्यक्त्वा धनवन्तं व्रजन्ति काः ।
children.translated_text: Who are they that abandon a man whose wealth has been taken and go to the wealthy one?
Courtesans, who have attracted people through hundreds of various charms, are not hard to resist! || 117 ||

children.text: हृतं द्रव्यमस्मादिति हृतद्रव्यं निर्धनं नरं त्यक्त्वा धनवन्तं नरं का व्रजन्ति ? नाना अनेकप्रकाराणां भङ्गीनां श्रृङ्गारचेष्टालक्षणानां शतैः । बहुत्वोपलक्षणमे[तत्] । आकृष्टा वशीकृता लोकाः पुरुषा याभिरिति नानाभङ्गि[शता]कृष्टलोकाः दुर्धरा दुर्वारा अनाय[त्त]त्वात् । वेश्या गणिका एवंविधा भवेयुरिति उत्तरमाशङ्क्य निषेधति—एवंविधाः सत्योऽपि न वेश्याः किं तु श्रिय इत्यत्रोत्तरम् । अतो नानाभङ्गिशताकृष्टलोका इत्यादेः तुल्यधर्मस्पृशो गिरः श्रिय इत्यस्मिन्नर्थे निभृतत्वाद् व्यवस्थानात् तया वा श्रिय इत्यस्यार्थस्य निभृतत्वान्निगूढत्वात् निभृतेयमुदाहृता ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Hṛtadravya</s>' — one from whom wealth has been taken, that is, an impoverished man — abandoning him, who goes to the wealthy man? Various, of many kinds — through hundreds of <s>bhaṅgīs</s> (charming gestures) characterized by amorous maneuvers — this is an indication of numerousness. Those by whom people, men, have been attracted, captivated — thus '<s>nānābhaṅgiśatākṛṣṭalokāḥ</s>' — they are irresistible, uncontrollable, because of their independence. One might suspect that courtesans (<s>veśyā</s>) would be of this kind — he negates: even though such, they are not courtesans but rather <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) — this is the answer here. Therefore, because the words '<s>nānābhaṅgiśatākṛṣṭalokā</s>' and the like, which describe qualities shared [with courtesans], have their meaning of '<s>Śrī</s>' (Fortune) concealed, hidden — this is illustrated as a <s>nibhṛtā</s> (concealed) [type]. ||
He whose name signifies 'surpassed finest hair,' and who has a name meaning 'groundless' —
that one, O sweet-voiced one, makes me exceedingly passionate. || 118 ||

children.text: केशस्याख्या संज्ञा यस्य स प्रकृष्टकेशाख्यः प्रवालः येनेति जितप्रकृष्टकेशाख्यः प्रवालोपम [इत्यर्थः] । न विद्यते भूमिरस्येति अभूमिः । तेन अर्थतः समानः आह्वयः संज्ञा यस्या असौ अभूमिसाह्वयः अधरः तव यः । असौ अयं मामुत्कमुन्मनसमधिकमत्यर्थं करोति । एवं कल्पितप्रसिद्धशब्दपर्यायसाधितेयं समानशब्दा निदर्शितेति ॥
children.translated_text: hair (<s>keśa</s>) the name (<s>ākhyā</s>) is what is designated — thus '<s>prakṛṣṭakeśākhya</s>' means '<s>pravāla</s>' (coral/young shoot) — the meaning is: comparable to a fine young shoot. '<s>Abhūmi</s>' — one who has no ground. By that, the one whose name (<s>āhvaya</s>) is essentially the same — 'that which has no ground' — that is, your lip (<s>adhara</s>). That one makes me passionate (<s>utka</s>), longful, exceedingly so. Thus, this is illustrated as a <s>samānaśabdā</s> (synonymous) [type], established through devised synonyms of well-known words. ||
O sweet-voiced one (<s>kalabhāṣiṇi</s>)! '<s>Jita</s>' means compared to, surpassed; of the finest
The two lovers, turning away from each other in anger, lay down on the bed;
and lying thus, out of passion, they freely kissed each other's faces. || 119 ||

children.text: कामी च कामिनी च कामिनौ स्त्रीपुंसौ रुषा प्रण्यकलहेन हेतुना परावृत्य पराङ्मुखीभूः[य] शयनीये तल्पे शयितौ । तथैव परावृत्त्यैव मुखमन्योन्यस्य स्वैरं यथेष्टं रागादचुम्बताम् चुम्बितवन्तौ इति मोहो जायते । कथं नाम परावृत्य शयितौ स्वैरं मुखं चुम्बत इति ? यथा पूर्वं संमुखं शयितौ तथैव पुनः संविष्टौ रागपरवशतया स्वैरं मुखमचुम्बतामिति तु परमार्थः । इयमेव साक्षान्निर्दिष्टार्थापि संमोहकारिणीति संमूढा दर्शिता ॥
children.translated_text: The male lover and the female lover — the two lovers, man and woman — having turned away, having become back-to-back, due to anger, due to a lovers' quarrel, lay down on the bed. And in the same way, while turned away, they freely, as they pleased, kissed each other's faces out of passion. Confusion arises — how can those who lay down turned away freely kiss each other's faces? [The actual meaning is:] just as they first lay facing each other, in the same way again, they lay together, and being overpowered by passion, freely kissed each other's faces — such is the true meaning. This one, even though its meaning is directly stated, causes confusion — thus it is shown as a <s>saṃmūḍhā</s> (confounding) [type]. ||
The people, struck by the rays of the preceptor of <s>Karṇa</s>'s enemy who was born from <s>Indra</s>,
rejoice at the sky pervaded by clouds that bear the enemy of fire's cold. || 120 ||

children.text: विना पक्षिणा गरुडेन । सामर्थ्यात् तेन किल देवराजमभिभूय कदाचिद—मृतमाहृतम् । [जितम्] विजितम् आत्मसात् कृतम् [अन्नमाहारो] यस्य स विजितान्नः अभृतभोजी । स चार्थादिन्द्रः । भवत्यस्मादिति भवः । विजितान्नो भवो जन्महेतुर्जनकः । यस्य यस्माद् वा भवो भवनं जन्म यस्य स विजितान्नभव अर्जुनः तं द्वेष्टी[ति] विजितान्नभवद्वेषी कर्णः । तस्य गुरुरादित्यः । तस्य पादैः किरणैः हतस्ततः । तादृशी जनो व्योम गगनमभिनन्दति । प्रीतिनिर्भ रेणान्तःकरणेन गृह्णाति । किंविशिष्टम् ? हिममपहन्तीति हिमापहः अग्निः । तस्यामित्रम् उदकम् । तद् धारयन्तीति हिमापहामित्रधरा मेघाः । तैर्व्याप्तम् । अत्र विजयसम्बन्धाद् विजितमित्यमृतस्य भानं निवृत्तम् । तत्सम्बन्धाच्च विजितान्न इतीन्द्रस्य । तस्माद् जन्मयोगाद् विजितान्नभव इत्यर्जुनस्य । तद्वैरयोगाच्च विजितान्नभवद्वेषीति कर्णस्य । तज्जन्मयोगाच्च विजितान्नभवद्वेषिगुरुरित्या[दित्य]स्य ।
children.translated_text: Without <s>Garuḍa</s>, the bird — by his power, having once overcome the king of gods, the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) was carried off. '<s>Vijitānna</s>' — one who has conquered food, that is, appropriated nourishment — thus one who lives on the food of others. And that is essentially <s>Indra</s>. '<s>Bhava</s>' — born from him. '<s>Vijitānnabhava</s>' — one whose birth, whose origin, is from <s>Indra</s> whose food was conquered — that is, <s>Arjuna</s>. His enemy (<s>dveṣī</s>) — '<s>vijitānnabhavadveṣī</s>' — is <s>Karṇa</s>. His preceptor (<s>guru</s>) is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). By his rays (<s>pāda</s>), struck — therefore. Such people rejoice at the sky. They embrace it with hearts overflowing with delight. Of what kind? '<s>Himāpaha</s>' — that which destroys cold — fire. Its enemy (<s>amitra</s>) is water. Those that bear it — '<s>himāpahāmitradhara</s>' — clouds. Pervaded by those clouds. Here, because of the connection with conquest, the sense of '<s>vijita</s>' as '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar) has been prevented. Because of that connection, '<s>vijitānna</s>' refers to <s>Indra</s>. Because of his birth-connection, '<s>vijitānnabhava</s>' is <s>Arjuna</s>. Because of the enmity-connection, '<s>vijitānnabhavadveṣī</s>' is <s>Karṇa</s>. Because of the birth-connection to him, '<s>vijitānnabhavadveṣiguru</s>' is <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun).

children.text: हिमोपघातयोगेन हिमापह इत्यग्नेः । तदमित्रतायोगाच्च हिमापहामित्रमित्युदकस्य । तद्धारणसम्बन्धाच्च हिमापहामित्रधरा इति मेघानाम् । एवं सम्बन्धपारिहारिकीयमुदाहृता ॥
children.translated_text: Through the connection with damage by frost — '<s>himāpaha</s>' (remover of frost) designates fire. Through the connection of enmity with that — '<s>himāpahāmitra</s>' (enemy of the frost-remover) designates water. And through the connection of bearing that — '<s>himāpahāmitradhara</s>' (bearer of the enemy of the frost-remover) designates clouds. Thus the relational-eliminative type has been illustrated.

children.text: न स्पृशत्यायुधं जातु न स्त्रीणां स्तनमण्डलम् ।
children.translated_text: The hand of some non-human being never touches a weapon, nor the rounded breasts of women;
yet it is certainly not without fruit. || 121 ||

children.text: अमनुष्यस्य कस्याप्यनिर्धारितरूपविशेषस्य हस्तः जातु कदाचिदपि आयुधं न स्पृशति गृह्णाति । न च स्त्रीणां स्तनमण्डलं पयोधरभारं स्पृशति । अयमेवं फलभूतकर्मरहितो हस्तो नाफलः सफलः किल । नान्यादृशं साफल्यमस्यास्मभ्यं रोचत इति किलशब्देन सूचयति । अत्राश्रितो हस्तः अभिव्यक्तो वाचकप्रयोगात् । आश्रयस्तु गोपितः, गन्धर्वहस्त इति साक्षादनभिधानात् । गन्धर्वहस्त इति चाभिधानमेरण्डस्य । तदियमेकच्छन्ना दर्शितेति ॥
children.translated_text: The hand of some non-human being whose specific form has not been determined — never, not even once, does it touch, grasp, a weapon. Nor does it touch the rounded breasts, the mass of bosoms, of women. This hand, devoid of such fruit-bearing actions, is 'certainly not without fruit' — it is fruitful. By the word '<s>kila</s>' (certainly) it is hinted: another kind of fruitfulness is not to our liking. Here the dependent element, the hand, is made explicit through the use of the denoting word. But the substrate is concealed, since '<s>gandharva-hasta</s>' (gandharva's hand) is not directly stated. And '<s>gandharva-hasta</s>' is a designation of the castor-oil plant (<s>eraṇḍa</s>). Thus this has been shown as the one-concealed type.

children.text: केन कः सह सम्भूय सर्वकार्येषु सन्निधिम् ।
children.translated_text: Having joined with what, what thing attains proximity in all activities,

children.text: लब्ध्वा भोजनकाले तु यदि दृष्टो निरस्यते ॥ १२२ ॥
children.translated_text: yet at mealtime, if seen, is cast away? || 122 ||

children.text: केन शिरसा सह सम्भूय संगत्य सर्वेषु कार्यादिषु स्नाना[धि]वासनादिषु सन्निधिमुपस्थानं लब्ध्वा प्राप्य भोजनकाले अन्नगतो यदि कथञ्चिद् दृष्टः स्यात्, तदा कः तादृशो नि[र]स्यते ? केशः । तस्य तादृशत्वात् । अत्र केन क इति सामान्यपद

प्रयोगादाश्रयः शिरोलक्षणः आश्रितश्च केशः । तौ च्छन्नौ इत्युभयच्छन्नेयमुदाहृता । केनेश इति [पाठे] केन ककारेण ईशशब्दः सम्भूय, शेषं पूर्ववत् । केन ब्रह्मणा ईशः शङ्कर इति चार्थान्तरं वाच्यम् । तन्महाप्रयोगादुभय[गो]पनं प्रागिवेति व्याख्येयम् ॥
children.translated_text: the substrate, characterized as the head, and the dependent, the hair, are concealed. Since both are concealed, this has been illustrated as the both-concealed type. In the reading '<s>keneśa</s>,' the word '<s>īśa</s>' (lord) joins with the letter '<s>ka</s>' — the rest is as before. An additional meaning should be stated: by which <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śaṅkara</s>)... — the concealment of both through that grand usage should be explained as before.

Having joined together with the head, having associated with it, having attained proximity, presence, in all activities such as bathing, perfuming, and the like — at mealtime, if somehow seen when it has gotten into the food, then what such thing is cast away? A hair (<s>keśa</s>). Because it has precisely that character. Here, through the use of the general words '<s>kena</s>' (by what) and '<s>ka</s>' (what),

children.text: सहया सगजा सेना सभटेयं न चेज्जिता ।
children.translated_text: If this army with horses, elephants, and foot-soldiers is not conquered,
then this son of ours would be one without a mother, a fool — though a knower of letters! || 123 ||

children.text: वर्तत इति सहया सगजा सभटेयं चेद् या न जिता नाक्रान्ता तदा नोऽस्माकं सुतः अमातृकः अजननीकः । अ[न]क्षरज्ञश्च मूढः स्यादिति [आपाततो]ऽयमर्थः । तत्त्वार्थस्तु हश्च यश्च ताभ्यां वर्णाभ्यां सह वर्तत इति । सह यो गश्च जश्च वर्णः, ताभ्यां सह सगजा । इश्च नश्च वर्णः । ताभ्यां युक्ता सेना, भकारटकाराभ्यां योगात् सभटा । एवंविधा च सिद्धा मातृका सा इयं चेन्न जिता सम्यगध्ययनयोगेन यदि न वशीकृता स्यात्, तदा अयं नः सुतः । न विद्यते मातृका वर्णसमाम्नायः । अनधीतत्वादस्येति अमातृकः अत एव शास्त्रापरिज्ञानात् मूढो मूर्खः हेयोपादेयज्ञानविकलः स्यात् । न क्षरति न नश्यतीत्यक्षरं वेदं जानातीत्यक्षरज्ञस्तु वेदमात्रपाठकस्तु स्यात् । न मातृकाध्ययनेनापि वेदपाठसम्भवात् । अक्षरज्ञश्चेत्यपि पाठः । तत्र मूर्खतया नश्वरपदार्थस्वभावापरिज्ञानादक्षरं सर्वं नित्यं जानीयादित्यक्षरज्ञश्च नित्यग्रहगुप्तश्च भवेत् ॥
children.translated_text: it exists thus — if this army with horses, elephants, and soldiers, if it is not conquered, not subdued, then our son would be without a mother (<s>amātṛka</s>), without a parent, and unknowing of letters, a fool — this is the apparent meaning. But the real meaning is: '<s>ha</s>' and '<s>ya</s>' — with those two letters it exists, thus '<s>sahaya</s>.' '<s>Sa</s>' (the letter) together with '<s>ga</s>' and '<s>ja</s>' — '<s>sagajā</s>.' '<s>I</s>' and '<s>na</s>' are the letters — joined with those, '<s>senā</s>.' Joined with '<s>bha</s>' and '<s>ṭa</s>' — '<s>sabhaṭā</s>.' Such a completed alphabet (<s>mātṛkā</s>) — if this is not conquered, not mastered through proper study, then this son of ours — for whom the alphabet, the letter-sequence, does not exist, who has not studied it — is '<s>amātṛka</s>' (without alphabet); and therefore, due to ignorance of the scriptures, he would be a fool, ignorant, deficient in the knowledge of what is to be accepted and rejected. '<s>Akṣarajña</s>' (knower of letters) means merely one who recites the <s>Vedas</s>, but is not [truly learned], since <s>Vedic</s> recitation is possible even without studying the alphabet. In the reading '<s>akṣarajñaś ca</s>,' because of his foolishness and ignorance of the nature of perishable objects, he would know everything as imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), eternal — thus '<s>akṣarajña</s>' means one who is forever in the grip of error.
Together with horses (<s>haya</s>), with elephants (<s>gaja</s>), and with foot-soldiers (<s>bhaṭa</s>) —
He shows what kind of mixture this is —
This one combines the concealed-by-name, the mixed, and the deceptive forms;
in this manner, the sequence of mixtures in the other types too should be inferred. || 124 ||

children.text: सेयं प्रक्रान्ता प्रहेलिका तल्लक्षणयोगान्नामान्तरितया मिश्रेण संसृष्टेन वञ्चिताया रूपेण योगः सम्बन्धोऽस्यास्तीति नामान्तरितामिश्रवञ्चितारूपयोगिनी । मातृकेत्यस्मिन्नाम्नि सहयेत्यादिनानेकार्थकल्पनादमातृकाशब्देनाजननी, मूढेनानधीतसिद्धमातृकाप्रतीतिविप्रलम्भात्, अक्षरज्ञशब्देन च वर्णज्ञप्रसिद्धेन वेदवेदिन्यविनश्वरज्ञेवानिश्चयवञ्चनात् ।
children.translated_text: This riddle that has been set forth, because of conforming to the definitions — combines with the forms of the name-concealed, the mixed (<s>saṃsṛṣṭa</s>), and the deceptive (<s>vañcitā</s>). In the name '<s>mātṛkā</s>' (alphabet/mother), through the construction of multiple meanings beginning with '<s>sahaya</s>' and the like, by the word '<s>amātṛkā</s>' meaning 'without a mother,' there is deception through the assumption of a different meaning; by '<s>mūḍha</s>' (fool) there is the deception of not perceiving the established meaning of '<s>mātṛkā</s>' (alphabet); and by the word '<s>akṣarajña</s>' (knower of letters), well-known as meaning 'one who knows the letters,' the deception is the uncertainty of whether it means 'knower of the <s>Vedas</s>' or 'knower of the imperishable.'

children.text: संकरशेषमतिदिशन् प्रस्तावमिमं निगमयति— एवमेव यथोक्तसंकरानुसारेण इतरासामपि

children.translated_text: of the other types too — the name-concealed, the deceptive, and those distinct from these — not only of these two alone —

children.text: संकरस्य संसर्गस्य क्रमः प्रकार उन्नेयोऽभ्यूह्यः । स चैव मुन्नीयताम्—
children.translated_text: the sequence, the manner, of mixture, of combination, should be inferred, should be deduced. And let it be so inferred —
Extending the remaining types of mixture and concluding this topic — in this very manner, following the principle of the mixtures stated,
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are addicted to liquor-drinking, who eat the food of <s>Śūdras</s>,
having abandoned the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, who fight and have [resorted to sin] —
this is a mixture of the two that have come together [the transposed type].
On this vast mountain, a mountain was seen, not one with waterfalls clinging to it,
one called [sun-flesh-branch?] that would swing at every moment —
this is a mixture of the identical-form and the different-word types.
The beloved of the husband of <s>Lakṣmī</s> has gone to the wife of the bearer of <s>Gaṅgā</s>;
why is there distress for me, O bearer of the moon, at your rising?
This is a mixture of the eliminative and the constructive types.
|| Thus ends the section on <s>prahelikā</s> (riddles). ||

children.text: एवं शब्दालङ्कारस्वभावाः काव्यगुणा यथावत् प्रतिपादि[ताः] । दोषा अपि केचिदसाधारणवैदर्भमार्गसम्भविनः श्लेषादयः । संप्रति सर्वमार्गसाधारणानुपदर्शयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: Thus the poetic qualities that are of the nature of <s>śabdālaṅkāra</s> (ornaments of sound) have been properly set forth. Some faults too are specific to the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style, beginning with <s>śleṣa</s> and the like. Now, presenting the faults common to all styles, he says —
<s>Apārtha</s> (meaningless), <s>vyartha</s> (contradictory), <s>ekārtha</s> (redundant), <s>sasaṃśaya</s> (ambiguous), <s>apakrama</s> (disordered),
<s>śabdahīna</s> (grammatically deficient), <s>yatibhraṣṭa</s> (with broken caesura), <s>bhinnavṛtta</s> (with broken meter), <s>visandhika</s> (with faulty juncture), || 125 ||
and contradicting place, time, craft, common practice, logic, and scripture —

children.text: इति दोषा दशैवैते वर्ज्याः काव्येषु सूरिभिः ॥ १२६ ॥
children.translated_text: these are the ten faults alone, to be avoided in poetry by the wise. || 126 ||

children.text: अपगतोऽर्थः अभिधेयो वाक्यसम्बन्धि यत इत्यपार्थम् । विरुद्धः पूर्वापराहतः अर्थोऽभिधेयो यस्मिन्निति व्यर्थम् । एकः स एव प्रतिपादितोऽर्थोऽभिधेयः पुनर्यस्मिन् प्रतिपाद्यते तदेकार्थम् । संशयोऽर्थविषयः, किमयमर्थोऽयं वेत्युभयार्थावलम्बी प्रत्ययः, तेन [स]ह वर्तते तज्जनकत्वादिति ससंशयम् । अपगतः क्रमो यथोद्देशं प्रत्याम्नायत इत्यपक्रमम् । शब्देन शब्दविद्याप्रसिद्धेन पदेन हीनं रहितं तद्विपक्षयोगादिति शब्दहीनम् । यतेः छन्दःशास्त्रविहितात् विगमात् भ्रष्टमपगतमिति यतिभ्रष्टम् । भिन्नं
छन्दोविचितिविद्यारूढं वृत्तं पद्यं जातेरपि विरोधसम्भवात् यस्मिन्निति भिन्नवृत्तम् । विगतः सन्धिः शब्दशास्त्रप्रसिद्धो यणादेशादिर्यस्मिन्नितिं विसन्धिकम् ॥
children.translated_text: that in which the meter (<s>vṛtta</s>), the verse established by the science of prosodic analysis, is broken — since violation can occur even in <s>jāti</s> (genre-meters). <s>Visandhika</s> (with faulty juncture) — that in which the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture), established in the science of grammar, such as the substitution of <s>yaṇ</s> and the like, is absent.

<s>Apārtha</s> (meaningless) — that from which the meaning, the signified, relating to the sentence, has departed. <s>Vyartha</s> (contradictory) — that in which the meaning, the signified, is contradicted, self-defeating between the preceding and following parts. <s>Ekārtha</s> (redundant) — that in which one and the same meaning, already conveyed, is conveyed again. <s>Sasaṃśaya</s> (ambiguous) — doubt regarding the meaning, a cognition hanging on both meanings, 'is this the meaning or that?' — that which coexists with it, being its generator. <s>Apakrama</s> (disordered) — that in which the sequence has departed from the order of enumeration in the corresponding assignment. <s>Śabdahīna</s> (grammatically deficient) — devoid of, lacking, a word, a verbal expression established in the science of grammar, due to the conjunction with its opposite. <s>Yatibhraṣṭa</s> (with broken caesura) — fallen, departed from the caesura (<s>yati</s>) prescribed by the science of prosody. <s>Bhinnavṛtta</s> (with broken meter) —

children.text: देशः पर्वतादिः । कालो दिवसादिः । कला नृत्यगीतादिविद्याः । लोकश्च सत्त्वलोको भाजनलोको वा चित्रप्रचारः । न्यायश्चान्वीक्षिकी । आगमश्च वेदादिः । देशकालकलालोकन्यायागमाः । तैर्विरोधो बाधा विद्यतेऽस्मिन्निति देशकालकलालोकन्यायागमविरोधि च तत्तद्व्यवस्थातिक्रमात् । विरोधीत्येतद्देशादिभिः प्रत्येकं सम्बन्धनीयम् । चकार उक्तसमुच्चये । इत्येते अनन्तरोद्दिष्टा दशैव । अन्यूनानतिरिक्ता दोषा गुणविपक्षत्वाद् वर्ज्याः शास्त्रचक्षुषा दृष्ट्वा परिहर्तव्याः । सूरिभिः प्रतिपत्तृभिः । कुत्र ? काव्येषु पूर्वोक्तरूपेषु । काव्यविशेषदोषाणामपि क्वचित् केषाञ्चित् प्रतिनियमात् । तत्सम्भवित्वात् काव्यदोषास्ते, यथा हेतुसम्भ[वि]नो

ऽसिद्धादयो हेतुदोषाः । यथा चाराञ्जिकादयो धान्यसम्भविनो धान्यदोषा उच्यन्ते लोके । अत्रापार्थादयो यदा भावप्रधानाः, तदा अपार्थत्वादयो दूषणानीति भावसाधनेन दोषाः । दूषयन्ति वा काव्यव्यपदेशमात्रेण क्वचिद् वा अपवादविषये काव्यमेवेति तत्त्वात् अन्यत्रेति दोषाः । यद्वक्षति—
children.translated_text: are called faults of the reason; just as <s>ārāñjikā</s> and the like, arising in grain, are called faults of grain in common parlance. Here, when <s>apārtha</s> (meaningless) and the like are primarily concerned with the state of affairs (<s>bhāva</s>), the conditions of meaninglessness and so forth are the defects — thus the faults are established through their real nature. Or they vitiate the mere designation of poetry, or in some cases, in the domain of exception, the poetry itself — because of its being precisely that — elsewhere they are faults. As he will state —
'Other than the speech of the intoxicated, the mad, and children, it is faulty' —

children.text: इत्यादि । तद्योगात् काव्यं दुष्टमिति ज्ञेयम् । यदा तु धर्मप्रधानाः, तदा अपार्थादयो दुष्यन्ति हेया भवन्तीति दोषाः । तदाभासत्वाच्च काव्येषु दोषाः । यथा दृष्टान्ताभासा दृष्टान्तेषु, शब्दाभासाः शब्देष्विति सर्वथा काव्यदोषास्ते वर्जनीया स्मृतिमतेति ॥
children.translated_text: and so forth. Because of its conjunction with these, the poetry should be known as faulty. But when they are primarily concerned with the property (<s>dharma</s>), then <s>apārtha</s> and the like are vitiated, become objectionable — thus they are faults. And because of being mere semblances thereof in poetry, they are faults — just as fallacious examples (<s>dṛṣṭāntābhāsas</s>) are faults among examples, and pseudo-words (<s>śabdābhāsas</s>) are faults among words. In every way, these poetic faults are to be avoided by the mindful.

'<s>Deśa</s>' (place) refers to mountains and the like. '<s>Kāla</s>' (time) refers to day and the like. '<s>Kalā</s>' (craft) refers to arts such as dance, song, and the like. '<s>Loka</s>' (common practice) refers to the world of beings or the world of objects, that is, the varied course of things. '<s>Nyāya</s>' (logic) refers to the science of reasoning (<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>). '<s>Āgama</s>' (scripture) refers to the <s>Vedas</s> and the like. Contradiction, obstruction with place, time, craft, common practice, logic, and scripture — that which has such contradiction, due to transgressing the respective established conventions. 'Contradicting' should be connected separately with each — place, time, and so forth. The particle '<s>ca</s>' (and) indicates the collection of those stated. 'These' — those just enumerated — are ten alone, neither fewer nor more, faults, to be avoided — detected through the eye of the treatise and eliminated — by the wise, the discerning. Where? In poetry of the form previously described. Because even the faults specific to particular types of poetry are, in some cases, restricted to certain types. Because they can arise therein, they are poetic faults — just as <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished) and the like, arising from the reason (<s>hetu</s>),
that which is deficient in thesis, reason, or example, and that which is flawed, is described
briefly, according to proper method, for the understanding of their essential meaning. ||

children.text: इत्यादिना विस्तरेण प्रतिज्ञाहान्यादयो दोषाः काव्यलक्षणान्तरे दर्शिताः । ते किमिह नोच्यन्त इति चेदाह—
children.translated_text: By this and other such statements, the faults of thesis-failure (<s>pratijñāhāni</s>) and the like have been shown at length in another treatise on poetics. If asked: why are they not discussed here? — he says —
Now,
The question whether the failure of thesis, reason, and example is a fault or not —
that inquiry is mostly harsh; what fruit is there in adopting it? || 127 ||

children.text: प्रतिज्ञा साध्यनिर्देशः, विधिरूपो निषेधलक्षणो वा । साध्यस्य सर्वस्य सदसत्त्वाभ्यां व्याप्तेः । स च प्रमाणान्तराव्याहतः । प्रमाणान्तरनिरस्तस्याहेतुगोचरत्वात् । यथोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: The thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) is the statement of what is to be proved — whether in the form of an affirmation or a negation. Since everything to be proved is covered by the two possibilities of existence and non-existence. And this thesis is one not contradicted by other means of knowledge. Since what has been refuted by other means of knowledge is not within the scope of a reason. As stated —
'In a doubtful matter, from the statement of a reason, a reason standing alone is without support' —
Thus. Similarly,
'One who is endowed with reasons as protection is never slain' —

children.text: इत्यादिः । अन्यत्र तद्विस्तरः । हेतुः, तस्या एवंरूपायाः प्रतिज्ञाया साधनभूतोऽर्थः त्रिरूपोऽन्यो वा । तस्यापि तल्लक्षणशास्त्रे विस्तरः । दृष्टान्तः साध्यसाधनयोः सम्बन्धप्रतिपत्तिविषयभूतोऽर्थः कश्चित् । स च साधर्म्यदृष्टान्तो वैधर्म्यदृष्टान्तश्चेत्यादिना अन्यत्र निर्णीतः । तेषां त्रयाणां हानिर्यथा[क्रमं] प्रतिज्ञाहेतुदृष्टान्तहानिः । [द्वन्द्वात् परं श्रूयमाणस्य] प्रत्येकमभिसम्बन्धात् प्रतिज्ञाहानिः हेतुहानिः दृष्टान्तहानिश्चेति त्रिविधो भवति । तत्र प्रतिज्ञाहानिः- तयैव प्रतिज्ञया हेतुना सिद्धान्तेन सर्वागमैः प्रसिद्धधर्मतया प्रत्यक्षेण च बाधेत्यनेकधा । यथोक्तं भामहेन—
children.translated_text: and so forth. The details of this are found elsewhere. The reason (<s>hetu</s>) is the entity that serves as the means of establishing such a thesis, having the triple character, or of another kind. Its details too are found in the treatise on that topic. The example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is some entity that serves as the object for understanding the connection between what is to be proved and its means of proof. And this is determined elsewhere as the example by similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and by dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), and so forth. The failure of those three — the thesis-failure, reason-failure, and example-failure — respectively. From the compound being distributive, the singular relates to each: thesis-failure, reason-failure, and example-failure — thus it is of three kinds. Among these, thesis-failure is: contradiction by that very thesis itself, by the reason, by established doctrine, by all scriptures, by well-known properties, and by direct perception — in these many ways. As stated by <s>Bhāmaha</s> —
'That which contradicts its own meaning, the reason, established doctrine, all scriptures,
well-known properties, and which is contradicted by direct perception — is faulty.' ||
Thus. Reason-failure is characterized by unestablishedness and the like. As stated —
'The reason should be known as having triple character; a pseudo-reason is the reverse of that.' ||

children.text: इति । तस्यान्यत्र विस्तरः । दृष्टान्तहानिः साध्यधर्मविरहादिरूपात् । तदुक्तम्—
children.translated_text: The details of that are found elsewhere. Example-failure arises from the absence of the property to be proved, and so forth. As stated —
'An example is said to be established by the properties of what is to be proved and its means of proof;
its reverse, or its semblance, or its non-occurrence — [constitutes example-failure].' ||

children.text: इति । तद्विस्तरोऽप्यन्यत्रैव । सेयं त्रिविधा हानिः प्रत्येकमनेकशो नाना काव्येषु दोषः । वैगुण्यं वा दोषो वेति सदसत्पक्षविकल्पनम् । विचारोऽयं [वि]गृह्य परीक्षा[या] इह कथञ्चित् प्रस्तुतत्वेऽपि [मुख्यतस्तस्याः] तर्कशास्त्र[गोचर]त्वात् कर्कशप्रायः कर्कशभागः अतिगम्भीरत्वादिहानधिकाराच्च, प्रायो भूयान् यस्मिन्निति कृत्वा । तेन वा प्रायो बहुलः । प्रायेण भूम्ना वा कर्कशः कर्कशप्रायः । राजदन्तादिषु दर्शनात् पूर्वनिपातः । कर्कशप्रायः कठिनभूयिष्ठः अरञ्जक इति यावत् । इह च कोमलप्रायः काव्यप्रतिनियतः गुणदोषविषयो विचारोऽधिकृतः । तस्मात् तेन कर्कशप्रायेण विचारेण आलीढेन अनुष्ठानमुखेनादृतेन किं फलम् ? काव्यप्रतिनियतगुणदोषनिर्णयरूपं प्रयोजनं किमस्ति ? नैवेत्याशय । तथा चाह—
children.translated_text: The details of that too are found elsewhere only. This threefold failure, being various in each category, is in multiple ways a fault in poetry. Or, 'is it a deficiency or a fault?' — this is an exploration of both possible positions. This inquiry, this examination through analytical critique, though somehow relevant here, is [principally] within the domain of the science of logic (<s>tarkaśāstra</s>) and is therefore mostly harsh, mostly difficult, because of its extreme profundity and because it does not properly belong here. '<s>Prāya</s>' means that which is preponderant. Or by that, it is mostly so. Or, for the most part, predominantly harsh — thus '<s>karkaśaprāya</s>.' The prior position [of the modifier] is observed as in '<s>rājadanta</s>' and similar compounds. '<s>Karkaśaprāya</s>' means consisting mostly of hard material, unappealing. Here, however, the inquiry regarding qualities and faults that is relevant to poetry is of a gentle nature. Therefore, by adopting, by following, by adhering to that harsh inquiry — what fruit, what purpose in the form of determining the qualities and faults specific to poetry, is there? None at all — this is the intention. And accordingly he says —

children.text: काव्यलक्षणे काव्यप्रतिनियता दोषा गुणाश्च विचार्यन्ते । न शास्त्रान्तरसाधारणा अपि, सर्वशास्त्रसमुच्चयप्रसङ्गात् । ततश्च अत्रैव सर्वगुणदोषव्युत्पत्तौ शास्त्रान्तराणि व्यर्थानि स्युः, तावन्मात्रफलत्वाद् विद्यास्थानानाम् । तत्रैतत्प्रतिनियतव्युत्पत्तेरन्यतः सिद्धेरिदमपि व्यर्थं स्यात्, सर्वत्र प्रतिनियमाभावात् । न चैवम्, गुणदोषव्युत्पत्तीनां प्रतिशास्त्रं नियमदर्शनात् । अथ काव्याङ्गत्वात् प्रतिज्ञाभेदादिकं विद्यान्तरमपि संक्षिप्तमिहाभिधानीयम् । तत् किं छन्दोविचित्यादिकं तत्र नाभिमतम् ? तस्यापि काव्याङ्गत्वेन निमित्तस्य समानत्वात् । न च यत्किञ्चिदिह दर्शितम् इत्येतावता शास्त्रान्तरे सम्यग्ज्ञानं सम्पद्यते, पुनस्तच्छास्त्रादेव यथावदवगमव्यपेक्षणात् ज्ञानानां [च] प्रतिशास्त्रं नियतत्वात् । ततस्तत एव तत्तज्ज्ञानमपेक्षणीयम् । यत् पुनः काव्यलक्षणस्यास्य प्रमाणलक्षणीकरणम्, तदाहोपुरुषिकामात्रमिति सूक्तमिदं तेनालीढेन किं फलमिति ॥
children.translated_text: In the treatise on poetics, faults and merits that are specific to poetry are to be examined — not those common to other disciplines as well, since that would lead to the undesirable consequence of accumulating all sciences. And if all merits and faults were to be learned here alone, the other sciences would become useless, since the fields of knowledge have precisely that as their purpose. And if the knowledge specific to this field is obtainable from elsewhere, this too would be useless, since there would be no exclusive domain anywhere. But this is not the case, since the determination of merits and faults is observed to be specific to each discipline. Now, if because [logic and the like] are ancillary to poetry, a different branch of knowledge such as the analysis of propositions and their divisions should also be briefly discussed here — then why is the examination of meter and the like not considered relevant there? Since the same ground — namely, being ancillary to poetry — applies to that as well. And merely because something has been shown here in some measure, complete knowledge of the other science is not achieved, since one must still look to that very science for proper understanding, and since knowledge is determined by each specific discipline. Therefore that particular knowledge is to be sought from that very science. As for this treatise on poetics attempting to characterize the means of valid knowledge — that is mere bravado, it has been well said: 'What is the use of that which has been licked [i.e., superficially treated]?' ||

children.text: एषां यथोद्देशं सनिर्देशं सापवादं [विवरणं] कर्तुं प्रक्रमते—
children.translated_text: He proceeds to explain these [faults] in order, with definitions and exceptions —
That which is devoid of sentence-meaning is considered <s>apārtha</s> (meaningless);
it constitutes a fault when found outside the speech of the intoxicated, the insane, or children. || 128 ||

children.text: समुदायार्थ इत्यारभ्य श्लोकत्रितयटाकायां मातृकास्थक्रमः असंलग्न इति कृत्वा अर्थपर्यालोचनेन शोभनतरः क्रमः स्वीकृतः ॥
समुदायस्य प्रकरणात् पदसम्बन्धिनो वाक्यस्य अर्थोऽभिधेयम् अङ्गाङ्गिभूतक्रियाकारकसम्बन्धविशेषलक्षणं सांव्यवहारिकम् । तेन शून्यं रहितम् । न पदार्थ
children.translated_text: The meaning of the aggregate, as understood from the context — of the sentence constituted by words — is the signification characterized by the special relation of action, agent-factors (<s>kāraka</s>), and the like, serving as principal and subordinate, in conventional usage. Devoid of that, lacking it. Not merely by the word-meaning

children.text: मात्रेण, तस्य क्वचिदप्यव्यभिचारात् । दशदाडिमानि षडपूपा इत्यादावपि पदार्थप्रत्ययोदयात् । यत् इत्यनूद्य तत् समुदायार्थशून्यम् अपार्थम् । इह दोषप्रस्तावे । अपार्थमिति वा अपार्थं नाम इष्यते स्मर्यत इति विधिः । तदपार्थं दुष्यति काव्यदोषो भवति इत्युत्सर्गः । तस्यापवादमाह- मत्तेत्यादि । मत्ता मदिरामदादियोगात् । उन्मत्ता वायुक्षोभादिचित्तविक्षेपात् । बालाः हेयोपादेयज्ञानविकलाः अव्युत्पन्नाः तथा बालकल्पाः शक्तिविकला वृद्धा असंबद्धभाषिणः । तेषां तथाविधाया एवोक्तेरुचितत्वात् । सैव तेषां सूक्तिरिति । [अतः] तेषामुक्तेरन्यत्र सुभाषितविषये [तदिदमपार्थं] दुष्यति दुष्टं जायते ॥
children.translated_text: alone, since that is invariably present. Even in expressions like 'ten pomegranates, six cakes,' there arises an apprehension of word-meaning. Having stated this with 'that which,' that which is devoid of sentence-meaning is <s>apārtha</s> (meaningless) — here in the context of faults. Or: '<s>apārtha</s>' is the designation — it is approved, it is recognized — this is the rule. That <s>apārtha</s> constitutes a poetic fault — this is the general principle. He states the exception: 'of the intoxicated' and so forth. '<s>Matta</s>' means those affected by the intoxication of liquor and the like. '<s>Unmatta</s>' means those whose minds are deranged by disturbances of wind and the like. '<s>Bāla</s>' means children, those lacking the knowledge of what is to be accepted and rejected, the uninstructed, and also the childlike — the aged whose faculties have deteriorated, who speak incoherently. Since such speech is fitting precisely for them — that alone is their eloquence. [Therefore] outside the speech of such persons, in the domain of good poetry, [this <s>apārtha</s>] constitutes a fault, becomes defective. ||
He illustrates that —
The ocean is drunk by the gods; I am afflicted by old age;
these clouds thunder; <s>Airāvaṇa</s> is dear to <s>Hari</s>. || 129 ||

children.text: न ह्यत्र समुद्रः पीयत इत्यादेः पदसमुदायस्य कश्चिदेकोऽर्थो गृह्यते यः काव्यार्थः स्यात् । अवयवार्था एवान[न्विताः] शलाकाकल्पाः प्रतिभान्ति । तदीदृशमपार्थं विज्ञेयम् ॥
children.translated_text: For here, of the word-aggregate 'the ocean is drunk' and so forth, no single unified meaning is grasped that would constitute a poetic meaning. The individual word-meanings alone, unconnected, appear like isolated sticks. Such <s>apārtha</s> (meaninglessness) should be understood. ||
Concluding by way of exception that this [fault] is, as a general rule, impossible [in actual poetry], he says —
This speech of those whose minds are unsettled is not blameworthy;
elsewhere, what poet would ever employ such a thing? || 130 ||

children.text: इदमनन्तरोक्तमपार्थमभिधानं वचनम् अस्वस्थं चित्तमन्तः[करणं] येषामित्यस्वस्थचित्तानां मत्तोन्मत्तादीनां [अभिधानमनिन्दितं] स्यात् । अन्यत्र तु निन्दितम् । अथवा इतर[त्र] स्वस्थेषु विषये तत्कर्तृत्वकल्पनात् । एवमिदमनन्तरोक्तमपार्थमादिर्यस्य दशदाडिमादेस्तदेवमादिकमसम्बद्धं [वाक्यजातं] को नाम कविरकुशलोऽपि, प्रागेव निपुणः । प्रयुञ्जीत रचयेत् ? नैव [कश्चित् प्रयुङ्क्ते ] । मूलहानेरतिस्थूलत्वाच्च नात्र भ्रान्तिः सम्भाव्य[त] इति भावः । वाक्यविकारत्वात् तु इदमपि कथञ्चित् काव्ये सम्भवेदिति सम्भवमात्रकल्पनया स्वस्थेष्वपि दर्शितमिति ॥
children.translated_text: This just-described meaningless speech, utterance, would be unblameworthy [only] for those whose minds (<s>citta</s>), whose inner faculties, are unsettled — the intoxicated, the insane, and the like. Elsewhere, however, it is blameworthy. Or: in the domain of those who are of sound mind, the very imagining of its authorship [would be absurd]. What poet, even an unskilled one, let alone an accomplished one, would compose such meaningless [verse] as the one just cited and [others] beginning with 'ten pomegranates' — such incoherent [collections of sentences]? None at all. Since the loss of the fundamental [principle of poetry] is too gross, error here is not even to be imagined — such is the purport. Yet, since it is a distortion of the sentence, even this might somehow occur in poetry — with just the possibility being imagined, it has been illustrated even for those of sound mind. ||
In a single sentence or in a larger composition, that which is defeated by what precedes or follows,
through contradictory meaning, is called <s>vyartha</s> (self-contradictory) and is listed among the faults. || 131 ||

children.text: एकं च तद् वाक्यं च इत्येकं वाक्यं पद्यात्मकं गद्य[मयं] वा [तत्र] प्रबन्धे वा सर्गबन्धादिके यत्र क्वचिदादौ मध्ये अन्ते वा पूर्वापराभ्यां पराहतं पूर्वापरविरुद्धं वचनं व्यर्थमिति व्यर्थं नाम पठ्यते ज्ञायते अत्र दोषेषु प्रकरणात् काव्यसम्बद्धेषु मध्ये । अयमपि काव्यदोष इति यावत् । कुतः ? विरुद्धः प्रतिषिद्धः अर्थोऽभिधेयम् यस्मिन् तस्य भावः । तया हेतुभूतया । न तु विगतार्थतया, अपार्थमित्येव तस्य संग्रहादिति ॥
children.translated_text: A single sentence (<s>ekavākya</s>), whether in verse or in prose — therein, or in a composition (<s>prabandha</s>), such as a canto-structured work and the like — wherever, at the beginning, middle, or end, a statement that is defeated, contradicted, by what precedes and follows is called <s>vyartha</s> (self-contradictory) — is known as <s>vyartha</s> in this context of faults, among those connected with poetry. This too is a poetic fault — that is the sense. Why? Because its meaning, its signification, is contradicted, prohibited — its quality is such. Due to that, which serves as the reason. Not, however, due to being devoid of meaning, since that would already be subsumed under <s>apārtha</s>. ||
Destroy the entire clan of enemies! Conquer this earth!

children.text: न हि ते कोऽपि विद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानुकम्पिनः ॥ १३२ ॥
children.translated_text: For no one is your adversary, O you who have compassion for all beings! || 132 ||

children.text: शत्रूणां कुलं कृत्स्नं सर्वं जहि नाशय राजन् ! ततो निःसपत्नं विश्वम्भरां महीमिमां जय आत्मसात् कुरु । ते तव कोऽपि कश्चिद् विद्वेष्टा शत्रुर्न विद्यते । कुतः सर्वभूतानुकम्पिनः सर्वभूतहितैषित्वात् । अन्तर्भावितहेत्वर्थं विशेषणमिदम् । अत्र शत्रुः पूर्वं विहित एव पश्चात् तत्पर्यायेण निषिद्धः । पूर्वापराहतमीदृशं व्यर्थमेकवाक्यविषयमवगन्तव्यम् । प्रबन्धविषयं तु तत्र संभवेदिति ॥
children.translated_text: O king! Destroy, annihilate, the entire, whole clan of enemies! Then, with no rivals, conquer this earth, make it your own! No one, no person, is your adversary, your enemy. Why? Because of your compassion for all beings, because of your wishing well to all beings. This qualifier contains within it the meaning of a reason. Here, the enemy is first prescribed and then subsequently denied by its synonym. Such self-contradiction, pertaining to a single sentence, should be understood as <s>vyartha</s>. In a composition, however, it could also occur. ||
Showing the exception to this, he says —
There is a certain condition of a mind attached with passion,
in which even speech of contradictory meaning would be considered acceptable. || 133 ||

children.text: यस्यामवस्थायां वक्तुः सम्बन्धिन्यां विषये । विरुद्धोऽर्थो यस्यामिति विरुद्धार्था पूर्वापराहताभिधेया अपि, न केवलमितरा । भारती वचनम् अभिमता अदुष्टा । तदा तथोचितत्वात् । चेतसः तादृशी क्वचित् समवस्था दशा अस्तिं विद्यते । कस्य ? सहाभिषङ्गेण [आसक्त्या] क्वचिद् विषये स्त्र्यादौ वर्तते इति साभिषङ्गस्य अतिरक्तचेतसः सम्बन्धिनी कुतश्चित् मनोवस्थाविशेषाद् व्यर्थमप्यनिन्द्यमित्यर्थः ॥
children.translated_text: In a condition pertaining to the speaker, in the relevant situation: even that whose meaning is contradictory — whose signification defeats what precedes and follows — not merely the other kind — such speech (<s>bhāratī</s>), utterance, would be accepted, would not be faulty. Because it is appropriate in such a condition. There exists some such state, some condition, of the mind. Of whose mind? Of one who has attachment (<s>abhiṣaṅga</s>), passionate fixation, toward some object such as a woman and the like — of one whose mind is excessively colored — from some particular mental state born of some cause, even <s>vyartha</s> is not blameworthy — that is the meaning. ||
He illustrates that —
How can the desire for another's wife befit me, a virtuous man?

children.text: पिबामि तरलं तस्याः कदा नु दशनच्छदम् ॥ १३४ ॥
children.translated_text: When shall I drink the tremulous lower lip of hers? || 134 ||

children.text: परम्य दारेषु कलत्रे । अभिलाषः सङ्गमेच्छा । लोकशा[स्त्रविरुद्धो]ऽयं

मे ममार्यस्य न्यायव्य[व]हारिणः सतः कथं नाम युज्यते संगच्छते ? नैवायं मम युज्यत इत्यर्थः । इत्थं कथञ्चित् प्रतिसंख्यानात् लब्धस्य विवेकस्य विपर्ययः पुनरभिषङ्गपरवशोऽनुपतितः । तस्याः परयोषितः कस्या[श]चिदिष्टाया दशनच्छदमधरं तरलमुज्ज्वलं कदा नु पिबामि ? कतरत् तादृशं पुण्यदिनं भवेत् ! नु प्रार्थनायाम् । ईदृशं पूर्वापराहतमपिं अत्यासक्त्याद्यवस्थानुगृहीतं न दुष्यति, तादृशस्यैव तदोचितत्वादिति ॥
children.translated_text: this desire of mine — how does it befit, how does it accord with — me, a virtuous man, one who conducts himself according to propriety? It does not befit me at all — that is the meaning. Thus, when some discrimination has been gained through some reflection, its reversal, again overwhelmed by passionate attachment, follows immediately. Of hers, some desired woman who belongs to another — when shall I drink her tremulous, lustrous lower lip? What blessed day would that be! The particle '<s>nu</s>' expresses longing. Such self-contradiction, though present, is not faulty when graced by a state of extreme attachment and the like, since it is precisely fitting for one in such a state. ||
For another's wife, another's spouse — the desire, the wish for union. Contradicting both worldly convention and scripture,
If what was said before is stated again without distinction,

children.text: अर्थतः शब्दतो वापि तदेकार्थं मतं यथा ॥ १३५ ॥
children.translated_text: whether in meaning or in words, that is considered <s>ekārtha</s> (tautology), as follows: || 135 ||

children.text: पूर्वोक्तं प्रथमं प्रयुक्तं शब्दार्थरूपं किञ्चित् भूयः पुनरपि यदि कथञ्चित् प्रमादात् कीर्त्यते प्रयुज्यते । कथम् ? अविशेषेण पूर्वोक्तमप्यर्थविशेषमनपेक्ष्य तावत्येवार्थे । यदि तु विशेषापेक्षा स्यात्, तदा नैकार्थमिति भावः । तदीदृशमेकार्थम् । अतः एकः पूर्वापरकालभाव्यर्थः अविशिष्टः अस्मिन्निति कृत्वा । कथम् ? अर्थतः अभिधेयेन पूर्वप्रतिपादितस्यैवार्थस्य अविशेषेण पुनः प्रतिपादनात् । शब्दतो वाचकेन वा हेतुना तावत्येव चार्थे पुनः शब्दप्रयोगात् । न पुनरर्थपौनरुक्त्यमनपेक्ष्य शब्दपौनरुक्त्यं स्वतन्त्रं दर्शयितुं शक्यम्, अर्थ[तो भिन्नस्य] एव शब्दस्य यमकादौ अपुनरुक्तेः । यत्र त्वर्थाभेदः तत्र तद्द्वारकं शब्दपौनरुक्त्यम् । अपीत्युभयथा दर्शितम् । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Something stated previously, first employed in the form of word and meaning, if somehow through carelessness it is stated, employed, again (<s>bhūyaḥ</s>). How? Without distinction — even though previously stated, without regard to a particular distinction of meaning, in exactly that same extent of meaning.
