But if there were regard for a distinction, then it would not be tautology — such is the purport. Such is <s>ekārtha</s> (tautology). Hence: the meaning existing at the earlier and later times is undifferentiated in it — thus it is called so. How? In meaning — through conveying the same previously established meaning again without distinction. Or in words — through employing the same word again for exactly the same meaning. However, verbal repetition cannot be shown independently without regard to repetition of meaning, since a word that is [semantically] different does not constitute repetition in <s>yamaka</s> and the like. But where there is no difference in meaning, there verbal repetition operates through that medium. The word '<s>api</s>' shows both ways. He illustrates with 'as follows' —
Yearning, they agitate the young woman — those dark as her locks,
rain-clouds possessing lightning, deep-sounding, with thunder. || 136 ||

children.text: बालां स्त्रियं काञ्चित् । उत्काम् उत्कण्ठिताम् । उन्मनयन्ति उत्कण्ठयन्ति । उत्कण्ठतामात्रापेक्षायाम् इदमेकार्थम्, विशेषापेक्षा[राहित्ये]नेति द्रष्टव्यम् । एते प्रत्यक्ष
वातनः । तस्या बालाया अलकानामिव त्विट् प्रभा येषामिति तदलकत्विषः । अम्भोधरास्तडित्वन्त इति अन्यतरेण मेघमात्रप्रतिपादनादेकार्थम् । रूपविशेषविवक्षायां तु अनेकार्थत्वं स्यात् । यथाह भारविः—
children.translated_text: clouds. Having the luster of her locks (<s>alaka</s>) — whose radiance resembles that of her tresses. '<s>Ambhodharāḥ</s>' (rain-clouds) and '<s>taḍitvantaḥ</s>' (possessing lightning) — since by either one alone, merely 'cloud' is conveyed, this is tautological. If, however, a distinction of visual form is intended, then it would not be tautological. As <s>Bhāravi</s> says —
matted locks, like a rain-cloud possessed of lightning.
Bearing a dark-blue luster, with tawny

children.text: इति । गम्भीराः स्तनयित्नव इत्येकेनैव स्तननयोग्यस्य प्रतिपादनादुभयमेवार्थमविशेषविवक्षायामिति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus. '<s>Gambhīrāḥ</s> <s>stanayitnavaḥ</s>' (deep-sounding thunderbolts) — since by this one expression alone, that which is capable of thundering is conveyed, both terms express the same meaning without any intended distinction — thus it is tautological. ||

A certain young woman (<s>bālā</s>). Yearning (<s>utkā</s>), filled with longing. They agitate, they intensify her longing. If only the general sense of longing is intended, this is tautological, since there is no regard for distinction — this should be observed. These, directly visible,
Here too, teaching the exception, he says —
If some heightening of compassion and the like is to be expressed,
it is not a fault even if repeated; rather, this is an ornament. || 137 ||

children.text: अनुकम्पा अनुक्रोश आदिर्यस्य विस्मयहर्षादेस्तस्य तद्रूपो वा अतिशयो विशेषः अनुकम्पाद्यतिशयः,

नानुकम्पादिमात्रम् । कश्चिद् अन्यतमो यदि विवक्ष्यते प्रका[शयितुमि]ष्यते तदा पुनरुक्तोऽपि वाक्येऽर्थतः शब्दतोऽपि वा न दोषः । एकार्थलक्षणेऽभिहिते विकारो नास्ति । गुणोऽपि न तादृशः कश्चिदिति चेदाह—प्रत्युतेति । विशेषविवक्षायां निपातसमुदाय एको वा निपातः । यदाह—इयं पुनरुक्तिरलंकृतिः काव्यशोभाकरत्वाज्जायते तादृशि विषये इति ॥
children.translated_text: not mere compassion and the like alone. If any particular one is to be expressed, to be made manifest, then even though repeated in the sentence, whether in meaning or in words, it is not a fault. No change occurs in the definition of <s>ekārtha</s> as stated. And if one objects that there is also no such merit, he says: 'rather' (<s>pratyuta</s>). The particle-compound indicates the special intention. He says: this repetition, in such a context, becomes an ornament (<s>alaṅkṛti</s>), because it enhances poetic beauty. ||
Compassion (<s>anukampā</s>), pity — that which is the beginning of wonder, joy, and the like — its heightening, its special degree, is '<s>anukampādyatiśaya</s>,'
He illustrates that —
She is slain, that woman of beautiful form, by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), that causeless enemy;
she is slain, she of beautiful limbs; she is slain, she of sweet speech! || 138 ||

children.text: सा काचिदिष्टा वरारोह स्त्री मुख्या हन्यते पीड्यते । चारु सर्वमङ्गमस्या इति चारुसर्वाङ्गी । हन्यते मञ्जुभाषिणी मधुरालापिनी हन्यते स्मरेण कामेन अकाण्डवैरिणा निर्निमित्तशत्रुणेति । ईदृशं पुनरुक्तमपि काव्यभूषणमवस्थाविशेषयोगात् । आह च—
विस्मये च विषादे च कोपे दैन्ये च वारणे ।
children.translated_text: In wonder, in grief, in anger, in wretchedness, in prohibition,

children.text: प्रसादे चैव हर्षे च पदमेकं द्विरुच्यते ॥
children.translated_text: in grace, and in joy — a single word may be uttered twice. ||
Thus. ||

She, some desired woman of excellent form (<s>varāroha</s>), a noble lady, is slain, is tormented. She of beautiful limbs in every part — '<s>cārusarvāṅgī</s>.' She is slain. She of sweet speech (<s>mañjubhāṣiṇī</s>), she of melodious conversation — she is slain — by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love, <s>Kāma</s>), the causeless enemy, the foe without provocation. Such repetition, though present, is a poetic ornament due to the appropriateness of the particular emotional state. And it is said —
If words employed for the purpose of determination produce doubt,

children.text: वचांसि दोष एवासौ ससंशय इति स्मृतः ॥ १३९ ॥
children.translated_text: that fault is known as <s>sasaṃśaya</s> (the doubtful). || 139 ||

children.text: वचांसि शब्दाः प्रयुक्तानि प्रकाशितानि । किमर्थम् ? निर्णयार्थम् । निर्णयो निश्चयः, प्रकरणात् काव्यार्थविषयः संशयविपर्यासविरोधी प्रत्ययः । अर्थः प्रजोजनम्, साध्यत्वाद् यस्मिन् प्रयोगे इति क्रियाविशेषणम् । तच्च स्वभावतो नपुंसकम् द्वितीयैकवचनान्तं च स्मर्यते । न तु संशयार्थम्, तदानीं दोषात् । यद् वक्ष्यति—ईदृशं संशयाय
इत्यादि । संशयनिश्चयविपर्ययमर्थद्वयावगाहि ज्ञानं यदि जनयन्ति, असौ तादृशः संशय इति ससंशयो नाम दोष एव काव्ये । न गुणोऽपि तत्र विषये । अन्यत्र तु भवेत् । स्मृतो विज्ञायते ॥
children.translated_text: and so forth. If they produce knowledge that encompasses two meanings in the manner of doubt, certainty, and contrary understanding — such is called <s>sasaṃśaya</s> (the doubtful), a fault indeed in poetry. Not a merit in that context. Elsewhere, however, it could be one. It is known, it is recognized. ||

Words (<s>vacāṃsi</s>), verbal expressions, that are employed, made manifest — for what purpose? For the purpose of determination (<s>nirṇaya</s>). Determination means certainty — in the context of the discussion, a cognition regarding the poetic meaning that is opposed to doubt, contrary understanding, and contradiction. 'Purpose' (<s>artha</s>) means the goal, since it is the object to be achieved — this is an adverb qualifying the action. And by its nature, it is neuter and in the accusative singular — this is to be noted. Not for the purpose of creating doubt, since that would already be a fault. As he will state: 'such as this, for the sake of doubt' —
O friend, you whose eyes are playfully restless with the savor of gazing upon the beloved of your heart's desire,
that distant figure — is it your mother? She could not bear to see such [behavior]. || 140 ||

children.text: मनोरथस्य हृदयाभिलाषस्य प्रियो दयितः कश्चित् । तदेकालम्बनत्वात् तस्य आलोकनमालोकः । तत्र रसः । तेन लीले चपले ईक्षणे नेत्रे यस्या इति मनोरथप्रियालोकरसलीलेक्षणे सखीति सम्बोधनम् । यद् वा मनोरथप्रिय इष्टः । आलोकः प्रकाशो बाह्यः । तद्वदरसलोलेक्षणत्वं न संवृत्तम् [?] आत्मानमन्तस्तिष्ठन्तं नेच्छसि । किं तु यथेष्टं बहिरालोके भ्रमितुं वाच्छसीति अभिप्रायेण

एवमामन्त्र्यते । अत एव अत्रापि संशयः, कतमोऽर्थोऽत्राभिप्रेत इत्यनिश्चयात् । यदि नामैवम्, ततः किंमित्याह—आरादिति । ईदृशमेवंविधं तव स्वातन्त्र्यं मनोरथप्रियालोकरसलोलत्वम् । असौ तव माता आराद् वृत्तिरस्या इत्याराद्वृत्तिः । द्रष्टुं न क्षमा । अत्राप्याराच्छब्दस्य दूरान्तिकवृत्तित्वात्, असावित्यस्य च परोक्षापरोक्षयोर्वृत्तेः संशय्यते । किमसौ माता दूरवृत्तिरीदृशं द्रष्टुं न क्षमा न शक्नोति परोक्षत्वात्, किं वा असौ इयं माता आराद्वृत्तिरासन्नवर्तिनी ईदृशं द्रष्टुं न क्षमा न सहते । ईदृशं दृष्ट्वा सुतरां कुप्यतीति
children.translated_text: She is thus addressed. Therefore, here too there is doubt, due to the uncertainty as to which meaning is intended. If so, what then? He says: '<s>ārāt</s>' and so forth. Such is your freedom, your fickleness of heart that delights in gazing at other objects of desire. That mother of yours — '<s>ārādvṛtti</s>' means one whose conduct is 'from afar.' She is not able to see such a thing. Here too, since the word '<s>ārāt</s>' functions both as 'far' and 'near,' and since the pronoun '<s>asau</s>' operates in both the visible and the remote, doubt arises. Is that mother of distant conduct unable to see such a thing, being out of sight? Or is that very mother of near conduct, who is close by, unable to bear seeing such a thing? Upon seeing such conduct, she would become all the more angry —
this is a certain uncertainty. Thus, such doubt should be perceived.

The beloved, a certain dear one, of her heart's desire (<s>manoratha</s>). Because he is the sole object of her focus — his seeing, his gazing, is '<s>āloka</s>.' The savor (<s>rasa</s>) in that. By which her eyes (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) are playfully restless (<s>lola</s>) — thus 'O you whose eyes are playfully restless with the savor of gazing upon the beloved of your heart's desire, O friend!' — this is an address. Or: the beloved of her desire is dear (<s>priya</s>). '<s>Āloka</s>' means external radiance. Thus, the state of having eyes restless with the savor of external display has not been concealed [?] — you do not wish your inner self to remain hidden. Rather, you wish to wander freely in the external gaze — with this intent
Here too he states the exception —
If such an expression is employed at any time for the very purpose of doubt,
it would be an ornament itself, not a fault — in that case, as follows: || 141 ||

children.text: ईदृशमेवंविधं ससंशयं वचनं यन्निश्चयार्थ[निगूहनेन] संशयायैव काव्यार्थसन्दे[होत्पादना]र्थमेव, तथेष्टत्वात् । जातु कदाचित्, न सर्वथा । तादृशे प्रस्तावे यदि प्रयुज्यते तदा असौ संशयः अदोषो जातः अलङ्कारो गुण एव स्यात् काव्यस्य । न दोषः स्यात् । तत्र तादृशि संशये विषये तस्यैव तत्र विधेयत्वात् । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: Such an expression containing doubt — which, by concealing the intended definite meaning, is for the very purpose of doubt, for the production of uncertainty about the poetic meaning, since that is desired. At any time (<s>jātu</s>), occasionally, not always. If, in such a context, it is employed, then that doubt, having arisen without fault, would be an ornament, a virtue indeed, of the poetry. It would not be a fault. In that case, in the case of such doubt, since it alone is to be the subject therein. He gives an example with '<s>yathā</s>' (as follows):
I see that blameless woman overwhelmed by the affliction born of desire;
devoured by cruel time itself — what use is our hope in you? || 142 ||

children.text: तां काञ्चिदिष्टाम् अनिन्दितां स्त्रियम् । अनङ्गात् कामात् जातः अनङ्गजः स च सा वा आतङ्कः पीडा । अङ्गात् शरीरात् जातः बाह्यभूतसंभूतत्वात् अनङ्गजः स च सा वा आतङ्क सन्तापश्चेतिं द्वैधम् । मदनेन लङ्घितामभिभूतां सतीं कालेन मृत्युनैव कठोरेण अस्थानप्रहारित्वात् । कालेनैव कठोरेण ग्रीष्मेण कालावर्षिकाग्रस्तां मृणालिकामिव कवलिताम्, पश्यामि अवैमि । नात्र सन्देहः इत्यपरं द्वैधम् । ततश्च त्वयि आशया अभिलाषेण नोऽस्माकं किं प्रयोजनम् ? न किञ्चित् । यदि सा अस्तिं तदथें त्वामभिलषामि किमिदानीं त्वयेति । किं नस्तदाशयेति पाठे—तत्र किमिंदानीं नः अस्माकं तस्यामाशया प्रत्याशया ? गता दूरमस्माकमसाविति व्याख्येयम् ॥
children.translated_text: That certain beloved, blameless woman. Born from <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love, desire) — thus '<s>anaṅgaja</s>' — and that which is the affliction, the suffering. Or: born from the body (<s>aṅga</s>), being produced from external elements — '<s>anaṅgaja</s>' — and that which is the illness, the torment — thus the double meaning. Overwhelmed by <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) — devoured by time, by death itself, cruel, because of striking at an inappropriate moment. Or: devoured by cruel time itself, by summer, seized like a lotus-fiber by the dry season — I see, I perceive. There is no doubt about this — this is another double meaning. And therefore, what purpose is served by our hope, our desire, for you? None at all. If she exists, then for her sake I desire you — but what use is there now for you? In the reading '<s>kiṃ nas tadāśaye</s>' — what is the point now of our hope, our expectation, regarding her? She has gone far from us — this is how it should be explained.
He elucidates that —
Is she afflicted by desire, or tormented by heat? — such uncertainty-producing speech,
a messenger-woman speaks playfully, in order to agitate a young man. || 143 ||

children.text: उक्तेन प्रकारेण कामेन आर्ता घर्मेण तप्ता क्षपिता वा
इत्येवमनिश्चयकरं संशयजनकं वा वाक्यं दूती काचित् आह ब्रवीति । नर्मणा परिहासेन हेतुना इत्युक्तेन विधिना । किमसौ मद्वियोगात् कामार्ता घर्मतप्ता वा केवलमित्यनिश्चयलाभात्
children.translated_text: thus, such uncertainty-producing, doubt-generating speech a certain messenger-woman (<s>dūtī</s>) speaks, utters. Playfully (<s>narmaṇā</s>), by way of jest, as the cause, in the manner described. 'Is she afflicted by my separation, by desire, or merely tormented by heat?' — from the attainment of such uncertainty,

children.text: युवानं कञ्चित् कामेन आकुलीकर्तुं विधुरयितुम् । ततश्च संशय एवात्राभिधेयत्वादलङ्कारः ॥
children.translated_text: in order to agitate, to distress, a certain young man with desire. Therefore, since doubt itself is the intended subject here, it is an ornament.
In the manner stated: afflicted by desire (<s>kāma</s>), or tormented, consumed, by heat (<s>gharma</s>) —
If the elaboration of meanings is not made in conformity with the order of their enumeration,
the wise call that fault by the name <s>apakrama</s> (wrong sequence). || 144 ||

children.text: अर्थानां यथोद्दिष्टानां केषाञ्चिदुद्देशः प्रथमोपक्षेपः तस्यानुगुणस्तत्र क्रमानुसारित्वात् अनुदेशः
प्रत्याम्नायश्चेत् न कृतः स्यात् प्रमादात्, तादृशं विशेषमन्तरेणेति भावः । अपक्रम इति अभिधानं संज्ञा यस्येत्यपक्रमाभिधानम् । अपक्रमं नाम दोषं तं यथोक्तमाचक्षते कथयन्ति कवयः । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: if such an elaboration has not been made, through inadvertence, without any such particular reason — this is the implication. That which bears the designation <s>apakrama</s> (wrong sequence) — '<s>apakramābhidhāna</s>' — poets declare it to be a fault of such a kind as described. He gives an example with '<s>yathā</s>':

Of certain meanings that have been enumerated — the first mention being their enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>) — the elaboration (<s>anudeśa</s>) that is in conformity with that, following the same sequence —
The causes of the sustenance, creation, and destruction of the worlds, the unborn ones —
<s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) — may they protect you! || 145 ||

children.text: जगतां लोकानां स्थितिः प्रबन्धानुवृत्तिः । निर्माणमुत्पादः । संहारो नाशस्तेषां हेतवः, तत्कर्तृत्वात् न जाता अकृतका इत्यजाः नित्याः । के ते ? शम्भुश्च शङ्करः, नारायणश्च विष्णुः । अम्भोजयोनिश्च ब्रह्मा । शम्भुनारायणाम्भोजयोनयः । वो युष्मान् पालयन्तु रक्षन्तु । अत्र जगतां स्थितिहेतुर्नारायणः, निर्माणहेतुरम्भोजयोनिः संहारहेतुः शम्भुरित्यागमात् न यथोद्देशमनुदेशः कृत इत्यपक्रमनामायं काव्यदोष इति ॥
children.translated_text: Of the worlds: sustenance (<s>sthiti</s>) means continued existence. Creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) means production. Destruction (<s>saṃhāra</s>) means annihilation — they are the causes of these, being the agents thereof. Unborn (<s>ajāḥ</s>), uncreated, eternal. Who are they? <s>Śambhu</s>, that is, <s>Śaṅkara</s>; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and the lotus-born (<s>Ambhojayoni</s>), that is, <s>Brahmā</s>. May they protect you. Here, the cause of sustenance is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the cause of creation is the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, and the cause of destruction is <s>Śambhu</s> — thus, according to scriptural tradition, the elaboration has not been made in the same order as the enumeration — this is the poetic fault called <s>apakrama</s> (wrong sequence).
Here too he states the exception —
If some effort, some cause for understanding the connection, has been made,
then even the transgression of sequence is not considered a fault by the wise, as follows: || 146 ||

children.text: यत्नेन प्रतियत्नेन यथावस्थानातिक्रमेणान्यथा सम्बन्धयोजनमनुदेशः तस्य विज्ञानमवगमः । तस्य हेतुः कारणं कोऽपि कश्चित् तादृशः येन तत्र सम्बन्धो विज्ञायते । न यथोद्देशम् । यदि कृतः स्याद् यत्नः । सम्बन्धनिर्ज्ञानहेतुरित्यपि पठ्यते । तत्र सम्बन्धस्यायथोद्देशमनुदेशस्य निर्ज्ञाने हेतुः कारणभूतो यदि यत्नः कोऽपि
कृतः स्यादिति व्याख्येयम् । तदा क्रमस्य यथोद्देशमनुदेशस्य लङ्घनमतिक्रममपि न केवलमलङ्घनम् । न दोषमाहुः स्मरन्ति सूरयः कवयः । यथेत्युदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: that serves as the reason for discerning the connection of the elaboration not made in the order of enumeration has been made. Then the transgression of sequence — the violation of the elaboration following the order of enumeration — even that, not merely its observance, is not considered a fault, is not deemed so, by the wise, the poets. He gives an example with '<s>yathā</s>':

By effort, by counter-effort — the connection, the conjunction, made otherwise, not in the order of enumeration, by transgressing the proper position — the elaboration: its understanding, its comprehension. Its cause, its reason — some such thing by which the connection is understood there. Not in the order of enumeration. If such an effort has been made. There is also the reading '<s>sambandhanirjñātahetu</s>,' where it should be explained as: if some cause
Separation from kin, death, and exile from one's country — among these three,
the first and last are prolonged sufferings; the middle one is a momentary fever. || 147 ||

children.text: बन्धूनां त्यागो विरहो विरहो बन्धुत्यागः । तनोः शरीरस्य त्यागो मरणम् । देशस्य आत्मीयस्य त्यागो देशत्याग इति त्रिषु एतेषु बन्धुत्यागादिषु दुःखेषु । आदिश्चान्तश्च इत्याद्यन्तौ

बन्धुत्यागदेशत्यागौ आयतौ दीर्घौ च तौ क्लेशौ संबाधौ । आयतो क्लेशो दुःखमनयोरित्यायतक्लेशौ यावज्जीवमनुबन्धात् । मध्यमस्तनुत्यागः क्षणिकः क्षणमात्रभावी चासौ ज्वरस्तापश्चेति क्षणिकज्वरः शरीराभावे नानुबन्धात् । अत्रायतक्लेशत्वं बन्धुत्यागदेशत्यागयोः । एवं न तनुत्यागस्य । क्षणिकज्वरत्वं च तनुत्यागस्यैव नेतरयोरिति यत्नसम्बन्धः । सम्बन्धनिर्ज्ञातहेतुरीदृशो द्रष्टव्यः । यदि पुनः त्रयाणामप्येकरूपत्वं तदा क्रमलङ्घनं दोष एव स्यात्, विशेषस्य तादृशस्याभावादिति ॥
children.translated_text: separation from kin and exile from country — are prolonged, long-lasting sufferings, afflictions. Their suffering, their pain, is prolonged, enduring, due to continuing as long as one lives — thus 'of prolonged suffering.' The middle one — death — is momentary, lasting only an instant, and is a fever, a torment — thus 'momentary fever,' since in the absence of the body, there is no continued suffering. Here, the quality of prolonged suffering belongs to separation from kin and exile from country, but not to death. And the quality of momentary fever belongs to death alone, not to the other two — this is the effort-based connection. A cause for discerning the connection of this kind should be perceived. If, however, the character of all three were the same, then the transgression of sequence would indeed be a fault, since there would be no such distinguishing feature.

The separation from kin — the absence of relatives — is the first. The death of the body — the departure from the body — is the second. Exile from one's own country is the third — among these three, these sufferings beginning with separation from kin. The first and last —
That which is devoid of correct language, whose path of exemplary usage and grammatical rule is imperceptible —
a word-usage favored by the unlearned; but that which is favored by the learned is not faulty. || 148 ||

children.text: पदस्य सुबन्तस्य तिङन्तस्य वा प्रयोगो व्यवहारः पदप्रयोगः, लक्ष्यते [यत्] तदिति लक्ष्यमुदाहरणम् । लक्षणं शब्दशासनम्, लक्ष्यते अनेन शब्दरूपमिति कृत्वा । तयोः ते एव वा पद्धतिः मार्गः, ततो व्यवहारप्रवृत्तेः । अनालक्ष्या अदृश्या, अभावात् । लक्ष्यलक्षणपद्धतिर्यस्मिन् स तादृश अशिष्टैरनाप्तैः स्वीकृतः । इत्यनूद्य शब्दहीनं तद्विज्ञेयमिति विधीयते । यः पुनरेवंभूतोऽपि पदप्रयोगः शिष्टैरिष्यते शास्त्रे काव्ये वा, क्वचित् प्रयुक्तत्वात् । स शिष्टैः शास्त्रकारैस्तत्प्रज्ञैर्वा इष्टस्तु आप्तप्रयुक्तः पुनः न दुष्यति, तेषां सर्वथेह प्रमाणत्वात् । अनन्तो हि शब्दराशिः । तत्र कश्चिच्छब्दः शब्दानुशासनाद् गृह्यते । कश्चिदाप्तप्रयोगात् तत्कल्पात् । शब्दानुशासनमपि आप्तोपदेश इति न कश्चिदनयोर्विशेषः अत एवोक्तम् — शिष्टेष्टस्तु न दुष्यतीति ॥
children.translated_text: The employment, the use, of a word — whether a declined noun or a conjugated verb — is 'word-usage' (<s>padaprayoga</s>). '<s>Lakṣya</s>' (exemplary usage) is that which is observed, namely authoritative examples. '<s>Lakṣaṇa</s>' (grammatical rule) is the science of language, since the form of the word is known through it. Their path, or indeed those themselves constituting the path, since usage proceeds from them. When this path is imperceptible, invisible, due to its absence — when the word-usage lacks observable exemplary usage and grammatical rule — it is favored by the unlearned, the unauthorized — having stated this by way of introduction, it is ordained that such should be understood as '<s>śabdahīna</s>' (devoid of correct language). But a word-usage that, even though being of such a nature, is favored by the learned, in either a treatise or a poem, because it has been employed somewhere — such a usage favored by the learned, employed by authorities — is not faulty, since they are in all respects authoritative here. For the mass of words is infinite. Of these, some words are grasped from the science of grammar. Others from authoritative usage, which is equivalent to that. And the science of grammar itself is also the teaching of authorities — thus there is no difference between these two. Therefore it was said: 'that which is favored by the learned is not faulty.'
He illustrates that —
Your arm protects the earth girdled by oceans,
O great king — no inquiry [is needed] — 'it does not exist' is not the aesthetic savor of these words. || 149 ||

children.text: अवतिरतङानः तङा प्रयुक्तः । बाहुभिरित्यपेक्षा भवत इति षष्ठीस्थाने चतुर्थी प्रयुत्ता । अर्णवशक्वरी मेखला रत्नयोगादिना यस्या इत्यर्णवश्क्वरी नदृतः
children.translated_text: '<s>Avati</s>' — the root '<s>av</s>' (to protect) has been conjugated with the '<s>taṅ</s>' termination. '<s>Bhavate</s>' — a dative case has been used in place of the genitive. '<s>Arṇavaśakvarī</s>' means one whose girdle consists of oceans, due to the connection with jewels and the like —

children.text: इति कपा भवितव्यम् । महाराजन्नित्यत्रापि सख्यहोराज्ञां टच्
children.translated_text: the form should be '<s>arṇavaśakvarī</s>' with the nominal affix. In '<s>mahārājan</s>' too, the vocative form with the '<s>ṭac</s>' affix

children.text: इति टचा भाव्यम् । तदिदं सर्वं शास्त्रशिष्टप्रयोगप्रतिकूलमिति शब्दहीनम् । नन्वनुप्रासादिः शब्दरसोऽत्र विद्यते काव्यगुणः । तन्नेदमेकान्तहेयमिति चेदाह— इत्येवं दुष्टानां शब्दानां न च रसोऽनुप्रासादिरपि जिज्ञासितावेव स्थितो ग्राह्यः । अश्रद्धाश्रयतया तस्या व्युपहतत्वात् । शुद्धायां हि भूमौ न्यस्तः पुष्पप्रकरः शोभते । यः पुनरपूतायां भुवि निक्षिप्यते कुसुमनिकरः स निष्फल एव । तथा शुद्धायां शब्दपद्धतौ रसः अनुप्रासादिः शोभते नान्यथा । यत्र पुनरयं रसो दर्शितः, तद् रसप्रयोगेऽपि शब्दहीनत्वात् हेयमिति ख्यापयितुम् । महाराजन् न जिज्ञासा नास्तीत्यासां गिरां रसः इत्यपि पाठः । तत्रासां गिरां रसो नास्तीति ईदृशी जिज्ञासा न विद्यते, हेयत्वादीदृशस्य रसस्येति व्याख्येयम् । शेषं समानमिति ॥
children.translated_text: should be applied. All this is contrary to the usage sanctioned by grammatical treatises and learned practice — thus it is '<s>śabdahīna</s>' (devoid of correct language). But here there is the aesthetic savor of alliteration and the like — that being a poetic virtue, this is not entirely to be rejected — if one says so, he replies: thus, the aesthetic savor, even the alliteration and the like, of words that are faulty in this manner, is not at all to be accepted as worthy of inquiry, as established. Because that savor is vitiated by being grounded in untrustworthiness. For a heap of flowers placed on clean ground is beautiful. But a cluster of flowers thrown on impure ground is fruitless indeed. Similarly, aesthetic savor such as alliteration shines on a pure foundation of correct language, but not otherwise. Where, however, this aesthetic savor has been demonstrated, even in the application of savor, because of being '<s>śabdahīna</s>' (devoid of correct language), it is to be rejected — this is being declared. The reading '<s>mahārājan na jijñāsā nāstītyāsāṃ girāṃ rasaḥ</s>' is also found. There, the meaning should be explained as: the inquiry 'is there no savor in these words?' does not exist — because such savor is to be rejected. The rest is the same.
Teaching that sometimes there may be a false impression of '<s>śabdahīna</s>' even in what is not actually devoid of correct language, he says —
Approaching from the southern mountain, the wind makes the mango trees
beautiful with their gracefully swaying coral-like young shoots. || 150 ||

children.text: दक्षिणाद्रेर्मलयपर्वतादुपसरन आगच्छन मारुतः चूतपादपान् सहकारतरून् ललितं सलीलमाधूतैराकम्पितैः प्रवालैरङ्कुरैः पल्लवोद्गमैः शोभन्ते इति ललिताधूतप्रवालाङ्कुरशोभिनः । स तत् कुरुते विधत्ते । अत्र किल दक्षिणाद्रेरुपसरणे भावात् पञ्चमी न युज्यते, अपायलक्षणत्वात् तस्याः । उपसरणापेक्षया त्वाधारेण व्याप्येन वा दक्षिणानिलेन भाव्यम् । ततश्च सप्तमी द्वितीया वा युज्यते । नैवं कृतम् । अतः शब्दहीनमेवंविधमिति कुधियो मन्यन्ते । न चैतदेवम् । उपसरणं हि तत आगमनमिति विश्लेषयोगाद् दक्षिणाद्रिमामृश्योपसर[त्ययमि]ति ल्यब्लोपलक्षणा पञ्चम्येव युज्यते ॥
children.translated_text: Approaching from, coming from, the southern mountain (<s>dakṣiṇādri</s>), the <s>Malaya</s> mountain — the wind makes the mango trees (<s>cūtapādapas</s>) beautiful, adorned with gracefully (<s>lalita</s>), playfully, shaken (<s>ādhūta</s>), swaying coral-like young shoots (<s>pravālāṅkuras</s>), tender sprouts — thus '<s>lalitādhūtapravālāṅkuraśobhinaḥ</s>.' He makes them so, he produces this effect. Here, indeed, since there is a relationship of origin (<s>bhāva</s>) in approaching from the southern mountain, the ablative case seems inappropriate, since that case denotes separation (<s>apāya</s>). In relation to approaching, the southern wind should be understood either as the substratum or as the thing pervaded. Therefore either the locative or the accusative would be appropriate. That has not been done. Hence those of poor intellect think that this kind of usage is '<s>śabdahīna</s>.' But this is not so. For 'approaching' (<s>upasaraṇa</s>) means 'coming from there' — and due to the connection with separation, the ablative qualified by the <s>lyap</s>-elision — 'having touched the <s>Dakṣiṇādri</s>, he approaches' — the ablative alone is appropriate.
he says —
Having considered this in mind,
For those whose minds are lazy in perceiving the greatness of the grammatical science and the like,
such usage appears like incorrect speech, but it does not abandon its beauty. || 151 ||

children.text: इत्येवंविधं लक्ष्यम् । अपभाषणवत् शब्द[हीन]मिवाभाति प्रतिभासते । केषाम् ? शास्त्रं शब्दलक्षणादिकम् । तस्य माहात्म्यं प्रभावः । एवंविधलक्ष्यसंग्राहकत्वम् । तस्य दर्शनमभ्यासः तत्रालसं मन्दं चेतो येषामिति [शास्त्रमाहात्म्यदर्शनालसचेत]साम् शास्त्रमाहात्म्यदर्शनेन नेदृशी भ्रान्तिरुपजायते, तस्याज्ञ[त्वा]पनोदित्वात् । यथोक्तम्—
children.translated_text: Such is the exemplary usage. It appears, it seems, like incorrect speech (<s>apabhāṣaṇa</s>), like language devoid of correct usage. To whom? The science of grammar and the like — its greatness, its power, consisting in its capacity to encompass such exemplary usage. The study, the practice, of perceiving that — those whose minds are lazy, sluggish, in that regard — for those whose minds are lazy in perceiving the greatness of the grammatical science. Through the perception of the greatness of the science, such a false impression does not arise, since that removes the ignorance. As it is said —
'The science is that which removes delusion.'

children.text: इति । न चेदृशं सौभाग्यं साधुतामुज्झति त्यजति । सुभगेनेवेदृशं सदृशः । यथोक्तं प्रागस्माभिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: Thus. And such beauty, such correctness, is not abandoned, not relinquished, by such usage. It is as if it were beautiful — it is exactly like correct usage. As we have stated earlier.
In verses, they know the word-break at a fixed position as the caesura (<s>yati</s>);
that which is devoid of it is called '<s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>' (broken caesura) — offensive to the ear — as follows: || 152 ||

children.text: श्लोकेषु पद्येषु विषये पदस्य सुपतिङन्तस्य छेदो विरामः छन्दःशास्त्रप्रसिद्धः पदच्छेदः । नियतं तद्धि व्यवस्थानं चतुर्थवर्णादिलक्षणं यस्मिन्निति नियतस्थानम् । तन्नियतस्थानं पदच्छेदम् । अनुवादोऽयम् । यति विदुः स्मरन्ति तद्विद इति विधिः । तस्या यतेरपेतमपगतं तदपेतं यतिभ्रष्टम् । श्रवणं कर्णमुद्वेजयतीति श्रवणोद्वेजनम् । अनश्च हेयम् । श्रुतिसुभगं हि लक्षणानुगतं काव्यमुपादीयते । यथेति [यतिभ्रष्टम्] उदाहरति ॥
children.translated_text: In verses, in metrical compositions, the break (<s>cheda</s>), the pause, of a word — whether a declined noun or a conjugated verb — well-known from the science of prosody (<s>chandaḥśāstra</s>) — is called the word-break (<s>padaccheda</s>). That which has a fixed position — characterized as occurring after the fourth syllable and so forth — at which this break occurs — thus 'of fixed position.' That word-break of fixed position — this is the statement of what is already accepted. They know it as the caesura (<s>yati</s>), they remember it — so declare the experts: this is the prescription. That which is devoid of, departed from, that caesura — is called '<s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>' (broken caesura). It offends the ear (<s>śravaṇa</s>), causes discomfort — thus '<s>śravaṇodvejana</s>' (offensive to the ear). And therefore it is to be rejected. For poetry that follows the rules of prosody and is pleasing to the ear is to be adopted. He gives an example with '<s>yathā</s>': [of broken caesura] —
sees here the unforced aesthetic savor* — with the learned — beginning with 'having approached' — this is faulty.
The king of the solar dynasty observes the arts of women's song* — [caesura break marked with *] —
the king bears the earth in subjection* — 'thus is the usage' — and there exists indeed such correct employment. || 153 ||
Seeing with scripture alone what should and should not be done, flawlessly* — [caesura break] —

children.text: शिष्टैरमा सह । संगीतविधिं प्रेक्षणकम् । अक्लिष्टा यथागमं प्रयुक्ता रसाः शृङ्गारवीरादयोऽस्मिन्निति अक्लिष्टरसं स्त्रीणां सम्बन्धिनम्, तत्प्रयुक्तत्वात् । अयं विवक्षितः कश्चिदादित्यवंश्यः सूर्यान्वयसम्भूतः । नरेन्द्रः पश्यतीह प्रस्तावे । इह वाचोयुक्तौ [वा] । अत्र मन्दाक्रान्तायां समुद्रर्तुलोकैः [४।६।७] यतिविधानम् ।

तद्व्यतिक्रमात् इत्यादि ईदृशं दुष्टं हेयम् ॥ अत्रापवादमाह—कार्येत्यादि । कार्याणि त्रिवर्गानुबन्धीनि कर्माणि स्वस्वकार्याणि । तद्विपरीतानि [अकार्याणि] आगमेनैव उत्पत्यादिना तत्प्रतिपादकेन पश्यन् यथार्हमनुतिष्ठन् । वश्यां विधेयामुर्वीमवति रक्षति नृप इति, एवंविधप्रयोगः शिष्टानामस्ति । न च नास्त्येव । तस्मादीदृशः साधुरेव ॥
children.translated_text: Through the transgression of that — such a verse is faulty and should be rejected. Here he states the exception, beginning with '<s>kārya</s>' and so forth. <s>Kāryas</s> (duties) are actions connected with the three aims of life, one's own respective duties. And their opposites [improper actions] — seeing them through scripture (<s>āgama</s>) alone, through revelation and the like that demonstrate them, and carrying them out as appropriate. A king protects the obedient, governable earth — such a usage exists among the learned. It is not the case that it does not exist at all. Therefore, such a construction is entirely proper.

with the learned, together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>. A musical performance, a spectacle. In which the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and <s>vīra</s> (the heroic) and the like have been employed naturally, in accordance with tradition — thus '<s>akliṣṭarasa</s>' (with unforced sentiments), pertaining to women, since it is performed by them. This one intended is a certain descendant of the solar dynasty (<s>Ādityavaṃśya</s>), born of the lineage of the sun — a king, who watches at this occasion. '<s>Iha</s>' can also mean 'as is fitting.' In the <s>mandākrāntā</s> (slowly advancing) meter, the <s>yati</s> (caesura) is prescribed at positions [4, 6, 7] — after <s>samudra</s>, <s>ṛtu</s>, and <s>loka</s>.

children.text: ननु नियतस्थानपदच्छेदो यतिरिति हेतुपदैकदेशच्छेदः । तत् कथं न यतिभ्रष्टमित्यत आह—
children.translated_text: But if <s>yati</s> (caesura) is defined as the word-break at a fixed position, then the break occurs within one part of the word '<s>hetu</s>.' How then is it not a caesura-fault? To this he says —

children.text: लुप्ते यदान्ते शिष्टस्य पदत्वं निश्चितं यथा ।
children.translated_text: Just as when the ending [of a word] is elided, the word-status of the remainder is established,
so too that which ends with a <s>sandhi</s> (euphonic combination) modification is described as still being a word. || 154 ||

children.text: पदस्यान्ते यथासम्भवं विभक्त्यादिरूपे लुप्ते सति शिष्टस्य व्यवस्थितस्य भागस्य पदत्वं निश्चितम् ।

पठत्यादेः शब्दविद्यायाम् । तथा तद्वत् । सन्धिः संहिता । [तत्र] यणादेः विकारोऽन्यथात्वमन्तोऽवसानं यस्य तत्सम्बन्धि[वि]कारान्तमतद्नुणसंविज्ञानात् सन्धिविकारमपहृत्य शिष्टं प्रकृतिरूपं पदमेवेति वर्ण्यते स्मर्यते शिष्टैः । ततः कार्याकार्येत्यादौ चतुर्थादिना वर्णेण पदच्छेदो यतिर्न विरुध्यत इति ॥
children.translated_text: as taught by '<s>paṭhati</s>' and the like in the science of grammar. Similarly, in the same way. <s>Sandhi</s> is euphonic combination. [Therein,] a modification (<s>vikāra</s>) such as <s>yaṇ</s> (semivowel substitution) and the like — the alteration, the transformation — is at the end of what is related to it. That which ends with a <s>sandhi</s> modification — by the recognition of the original form through removing the <s>sandhi</s> modification — the remainder in its original form is described, is remembered by the learned, as a word indeed. Therefore, in '<s>kāryākārya</s>' and the like, the word-break (<s>yati</s>) at the fourth syllable and so forth is not violated.
When, at the end of a word, the case-ending or the like is elided as applicable, the word-status of the remaining, established portion is certain —

children.text: ईदृशमपि यदि श्रवणानुद्वेजनं तदा ग्राह्यमन्यथा हेयमिति पुनर्विशेषं दर्शयन्नाह-
children.translated_text: Showing a further qualification — that even such a construction, if it is not harsh to the ear, is acceptable, but otherwise it should be rejected — he says —

children.text: तथापि कटु कर्णानां कवयो न प्रयुञ्जते ।
children.translated_text: Even so, poets do not employ that which is harsh to the ears;
the army of that king, with banners like upraised clouds — this kind of expression [is faulty]. || 155 ||

children.text: यद्यपि स[न्धिवि]कारान्तं पदं स्मृतम्, तथापि एवमपि कर्णानां कटु श्रवणोद्वेजनं न प्रयुञ्जते कवयो रसज्ञाः । तादृशं वर्जनीयमित्यर्थः । कतरत् तदित्युदाहरतितस्य राज्ञः कस्यचित् । ध्वजिनी सेना केतुभिर्ध्वजैरुच्छ्रितैः उदस्ता उत्क्षिप्ता जलदा यथा इति केतूदस्तजलदा इत्यदः ईदृशं कर्णकटु वर्ज्यमत्र । यद्यपि तुशब्दे अकोऽकि दीर्घेण परेणापाकृते के इत्य[त्र] पदत्वं स्यात्, तथापि श्रवणोद्वेजनमीदृशमिति न प्रयोक्तव्यम् । अत्र च श्रुतिरेव कवीनां प्रमाणमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Even though a word ending with a <s>sandhi</s> modification is accepted, even so, that which is harsh to the ears, offensive to hearing, is not employed by poets, those who are connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s>. Such an expression should be avoided — that is the meaning. What is it? He illustrates: 'of that king, some [particular one], the army (<s>dhvajinī</s>) — with banners (<s>ketus</s>) that are like upraised clouds' — '<s>ketūdastajaladā</s>' — this kind of expression is harsh to the ears and should be avoided. For even though by the rule of vowel lengthening where '<s>a</s>' follows '<s>a</s>,' when the <s>tu</s> ending is displaced, the word-status of '<s>ke</s>' might be established, nevertheless such an expression being offensive to hearing should not be employed. And in this matter, auditory perception alone is the authority for poets.
Where there is deficiency or excess of syllables, or the misplacement of heavy and light syllables,
that constitutes a broken meter — this fault is severely censured. || 156 ||

children.text: वर्णानां शास्त्रतः प्रतिनियतानां श्लोकभाविनां न्यूनता हीनत्वमाधिक्यमतिरेको वा । न्यूनताधिक्ये द्वे । गुरोः संयोगपरस्य दीर्घस्य लघोश्च ह्रस्वस्याक्षरस्यायथास्थितिः तद्विद्याव्यवस्थातिक्रमेण वृत्तेर्यत्र पद्ये स्यात् कविप्रमादात् तत् तादृशम् । भिन्नं च तद्वृत्तं चेति भिन्नवृत्तम् । भिन्नं वा वृत्तं यस्मिन् काव्ये इति भेदविवक्षया भिन्नवृत्तम् । एष भिन्नवृत्तलक्षणो दोषः सुनिन्दितः सुष्ठु गर्हितः कविभिः काव्यशरीरस्यैवंविधत्वे कुत एव तत्र विशेषवित्ता [कवेः] इति ॥
children.translated_text: Of syllables that are prescribed by the science [of prosody] and fixed for the verse — deficiency, that is, reduction, or excess, that is, surplus. Deficiency and excess are two [types]. The misplacement of the heavy syllable — one that follows a conjunct consonant or a long vowel — and of the light syllable — the short one — the deviation from the rules of that science — where this occurs in a verse, due to the poet's carelessness, that is of such a nature. It is <s>bhinnavṛtta</s> (broken meter) — 'broken' and 'that is the meter.' Or, a verse in which the meter has been broken — intending the distinction. This fault characterized by broken meter is severely censured, strongly condemned by poets — for when the very body of the poem is of such a nature, where then is the poet's special discernment?
He illustrates the four types in order —
'The rays of the moon, cool, touch' — this is syllable-deficiency;
'the tender shoots of the mango tree are moist' — this has an excess syllable. || 157 ||

children.text: इन्दुपादाः शिशिराः स्पृशन्ति इत्यत्र प्रथमपाद ऊनवर्णता । ऊनो न्यूनो वर्णो यत्र तद्भाव ऊनवर्णतेति कृत्वा । अनुष्टुप्पादो ह्यष्टाक्षरः । अयं तु सप्ताक्षर इति वर्णहानिः । सहकारस्य किसलयान्यार्द्राणी[ति] अत्रापि पूर्वपादे अधिकमक्षर[म]स्मिन्निति अधिकाक्षरम् । अधिकाक्षरमिति भावप्रधानो निर्देशः । यद्वा अधिकाक्षरं पादं रूपं वृत्तमिति वा योज्यम्, अनुष्टुप्पादस्याष्टाक्षरस्य नवाक्षरीकरणादिति ॥
children.translated_text: 'The rays of the moon, cool, touch' (<s>indupādāḥ śiśirāḥ spṛśanti</s>) — here in the first quarter-verse there is syllable-deficiency. '<s>Ūnavarṇatā</s>' (deficiency of syllables) — a condition where a syllable is deficient. For the quarter-verse of the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> meter has eight syllables, but this one has only seven — hence a syllable-loss. 'The tender shoots of the mango tree are moist' (<s>sahakārasya kisalayānyārdrāṇī</s>) — here too in the first quarter-verse there is an excess syllable — '<s>adhikākṣara</s>' (excess syllable). '<s>Adhikākṣara</s>' is stated with emphasis on the condition. Or, it should be construed as 'a quarter-verse or form or meter with an excess syllable,' since the eight-syllable <s>anuṣṭubh</s> quarter-verse has been made nine-syllabled.
at doe-eyed women' — this is misplaced heaviness of syllable;
'By <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), sharp arrows have been released
upon women of sidelong glances' — this is misplaced lightness of syllable. || 158 ||
'The arrows of <s>Madana</s>, sharpened, fall

children.text: अयथा शास्त्रविरुद्धो गुरुर्यस्मिन् तस्य भावः अयथागुरुत्वम् । उपेन्द्रवज्रायां प्रथमलघुविधानात् तदपेक्षयेति द्रष्टव्यम् । उपजात्यपेक्षया त्वदोष इति । मदनेत्यादि । अयथालघुत्वमिति पूर्व[वच्च] व्युत्पत्तिः । उपेन्द्रवज्रायां द्वितीयमक्षरं गुरु विहितमिति । इदं तु लघ्विति तद्विद्याविरोधादयथालघुत्वमिति ॥
children.translated_text: Heaviness of syllable that is improper, contrary to the rules of the science — the state of that is '<s>ayathāgurutva</s>' (misplaced heaviness). Since the <s>upendravajrā</s> meter prescribes the first syllable as light, it should be viewed in relation to that prescription. From the standpoint of the <s>upajāti</s> (mixed meter), however, it would not be a fault. '<s>Madana</s>' and so forth — '<s>ayathālaghutva</s>' (misplaced lightness) has the same etymological derivation as before. Since in the <s>upendravajrā</s> meter the second syllable is prescribed as heavy, but here it is light — due to the contradiction with the rules of that science, this is a case of misplaced lightness.
When there is non-combination in words [despite the rules requiring it], out of the intention 'I do not wish to make the <s>sandhi</s>,'
that is designated as <s>visandhi</s> (broken <s>sandhi</s>) — but not when it is caused by <s>pragṛhya</s> (non-combinable endings) and the like. || 159 ||

children.text: संहितां सन्धिमेकपदे भिन्नपदे वा प्राप्तामपि न विवक्षामि । असंहितैव मयात्र विवक्षितेति बुद्ध्या पदेषु यदसन्धानमसंहिता तत् तादृशं विगतः सन्धिरस्मादिति विसन्धीति निर्दिष्टमुक्तं काव्यदूषणम् । यत् पुनरसन्धानं प्रगृह्यमादिर्यस्य यलोपादेः स हेतुः कारणमस्येति प्रगृह्यादिहेतुकम्, न तद् विसन्धीति निर्दिष्टं तादृशमसन्धानं युक्तं शास्त्रीयत्वात् । अनेन च यत् प्रगृह्यादिहेतुकमपि विसन्धानं भामहेन वर्जितम्, तन्निरस्तम् । यदाह—

children.translated_text: O beloved! The crest-jewel of the moon, bearing the shining rays —
may the feet of <s>Śambhu</s> and <s>Śarvāṇī</s> protect you! — thus they call this a case of <s>visandhi</s>. ||

children.text: इति । लक्षणानुगतं हीदृशं कथमप्रमाणयितुं शक्यते स्वस्थचेतसेति भावः ॥
children.translated_text: But how can such a construction, which conforms to grammatical rule, be considered unauthoritative by one of sound mind? — this is the purport.

The <s>sandhi</s> (euphonic combination), whether within a single word or between separate words, even when applicable — 'I do not wish to make the combination, the uncombined form is intended by me here' — with this understanding, whatever non-combination (<s>asandhāna</s>) occurs in words — that is designated, stated, as <s>visandhi</s> (broken <s>sandhi</s>), the poetic fault of absent <s>sandhi</s>. But whatever non-combination is caused by <s>pragṛhya</s> (non-combinable endings, such as dual endings) and other reasons such as <s>ya</s>-elision and the like — that is not designated as <s>visandhi</s>; such non-combination is proper, being sanctioned by the grammatical science. And by this, that which was prohibited even when caused by <s>pragṛhya</s> and the like by <s>Bhāmaha</s>, has been refuted. As he says —
He illustrates that —
The perspiration on the cheek-circles of women, effaced by the gentle breeze moving about,
is [both] lost and emergent; in the autumn sky and in our minds too. || 160 ||

children.text: एतस्मात् पूर्वं मानेर्ष्ये इह शीर्येते स्त्रीणां हिमऋतौ प्रिये इति श्लोकार्ध बहुत्र पठितमपि न रत्नश्रीसम्मतम्, न वा भोटपाठानुगतमिति परित्यक्तम् ॥

children.translated_text: On these nights — such a construction, whose fault is unknown, is [acceptable] to the wise. || 161 ||

children.text: मन्दानिलेन नभसि । अस्माकं मनस्यपि चेतसि च

मनोहरतया चरता अङ्गनागण्डमण्डले उद्भेदि उद्नतं घर्माम्भः स्वेदजलं लुप्तम् आसु रात्रिष्विति । अर्थसंगतिरियम् । उदाहरणं तु विसन्धेः- अनिलेन चरता अङ्गनागण्डमण्डले इत्येतत् । अत्र हि चरता अङ्गनेत्यत्र अकोऽकि दीर्घः [इत्यनेन प्राप्तोऽपि] सन्धिः न कृत इति विसन्ध्येतद् द्रष्टव्यम् । द्वयोरन्तादिविषयं तु असन्धानमिष्टम्, [महाजनप्र]सिद्धेरिति दर्शयति लुप्तमुद्भेदि घर्माम्भो नभस्यस्मन्मनस्यपि आसु रात्रिष्विति ।
children.translated_text: moving charmingly about on the cheek-circles of women, the perspiration (<s>gharmāmbhas</s>), the sweat-water, both emergent and effaced — on these nights. This is the coherence of meaning. The example of <s>visandhi</s> (broken <s>sandhi</s>), however, is: '<s>anilena caratā aṅganāgaṇḍamaṇḍale</s>' (by the breeze moving on the cheek-circles of women). For here, in '<s>caratā aṅganā</s>,' although the <s>sandhi</s> required by the rule of vowel lengthening when '<s>a</s>' meets '<s>a</s>' is applicable, it has not been made — this should be viewed as a <s>visandhi</s>. But the non-combination at the boundary between two half-verses is accepted,

children.text: ईदृशमर्धान्तादिगोचरमसन्धानम् अज्ञातं न्यङ्गमस्मिन्निति अज्ञातन्यङ्गमविदितदोषम् अदुष्टं ज्ञातं प्राज्ञैः शिष्टैरिति यावत् ।
children.translated_text: as the learned demonstrate: 'such non-combination at the end of half-verses and the like — whose fault is unknown (<s>ajñātanyaṅga</s>), whose defect is not recognized — is not faulty; it is known [as acceptable] by the wise, the learned' — that is the meaning.
the mark on the moon, though dark, extends

children.text: अत्र शोभामिति मातृकापाठः । स तु न दण्डिधृतपाठानुसारी । तुल

children.translated_text: its beauty;
A lotus, though entangled with water-weeds, is lovely;
what indeed is not an ornament for beautiful forms? ||
this slender woman, even in bark-garments, is exceedingly charming —

children.text: तस्मादीदृशमसन्धानं प्रयुज्यते शि[ष्टैरि]ष्टत्वात् । प्रथमद्वितीययोः तृतीयचतुर्थयोश्च पादयोस्तु अन्तादिविषयमन्यत्र चापि [पादाभ्यन्तरे] सन्धानमिष्टमिति प्रतिपत्तव्यम् ॥
children.translated_text: Therefore such non-combination is employed by the learned, because it is accepted. It should be understood that the <s>sandhi</s> at the boundary between the first and second, and between the third and fourth quarter-verses, as well as elsewhere within the quarter-verses, is the accepted practice.
By the gentle breeze, in the autumn sky, and in our minds too,
Place (<s>deśa</s>) means mountains, forests, kingdoms, and the like; time (<s>kāla</s>) means night, day, and the seasons;
the arts (<s>kalās</s>) begin with dance and song, and they pertain to pleasure (<s>kāma</s>) and wealth (<s>artha</s>). || 162 ||

children.text: अद्रिः मलयपर्वतादिः । वनं कालिङ्गादि । राष्ट्रं दक्षिणापथादिकम् । आदिशब्देन नदीधन्वादिपरिग्रहः । स तादृशो देशो विज्ञायते । रात्रिर्दिवा च रात्रिंदिवम् । ऋतवश्च प्रावृडादयः षडिति रात्रिंदिवर्तवः कालविशेषत्वात् कालः सामान्येन विज्ञायते । नृत्यं ताण्डवं लास्यं च । नानारसभावाभिनयाङ्गहारादिरूपं गीतं ज्ञेयम् । तच्च

children.translated_text: the <s>gāndharva</s> (musical art) should be known as threefold, consisting of <s>svara</s> (melody), <s>tāla</s> (rhythm), and <s>pada</s> (lyrics) —
thus threefold;

children.text: तस्य योनिर्भवेत् कण्ठो वीणा वंशस्तथैव च ॥
children.translated_text: its source is the throat, the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), and the flute (<s>vaṃśa</s>) likewise. ||

children.text: इति त्रियोनिकम् । विस्तरतया तच्छास्त्र एवाधिकृतम् । तादर्थ्यात् तत्प्रतिपादकं शास्त्रं नृत्तं गीतं प्रभृति प्रमुखं यासां वाद्यादिविद्यानां ता नृत्तगीतप्रभृतयः कलाविद्याः । कामो विशिष्टो विषयोपभोगः । अर्थश्च विचित्रोपकरणरूपः । संश्रयः अधिष्ठानम्,
children.translated_text: Thus it has three sources. In detail, it is treated in the relevant treatise [on music]. For the purpose of those [arts], the treatise that teaches them — the arts (<s>kalās</s>) whose foremost representatives are dance and song, along with the sciences of instrumental music and the like — are '<s>nṛtyagītaprabhṛtayaḥ kalāvidyāḥ</s>' (arts beginning with dance and song). <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure) is the special enjoyment of sense-objects. <s>Artha</s> (wealth) is of the nature of various resources and instruments. Their abode (<s>saṃśraya</s>),

children.text: तद्भावभावित्वाद् यासां [कलानां]मिति कामार्थयोः संश्रयाः । साक्षात् पारम्पर्येण तु धर्मोऽप्यासामाश्रयः स्यात्, तन्मूलत्वादर्थकामयोः ॥
children.translated_text: since the arts are conditioned by pleasure and wealth — thus they 'pertain to <s>kāma</s> and <s>artha</s>.' Directly or indirectly, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) too may be their support, since <s>artha</s> and <s>kāma</s> are rooted in <s>dharma</s>.

Mountain (<s>adri</s>) means <s>Malaya</s> mountain and the like. Forest (<s>vana</s>) means <s>Kaliṅga</s> and the like. Kingdom (<s>rāṣṭra</s>) means the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>) and the like. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), rivers, deserts, and the like are included. Such is the category of place (<s>deśa</s>). Night and day together form '<s>rātriṃdiva</s>'; and the seasons (<s>ṛtus</s>) such as the rainy season and the like are six — thus '<s>rātriṃdivartavas</s>' (night, day, and seasons), being specific divisions of time, are understood generally as time (<s>kāla</s>). Dance (<s>nṛtya</s>) includes the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous) and <s>lāsya</s> (graceful) types. Song (<s>gīta</s>) should be understood as consisting of the representation of various <s>rasas</s> (sentiments), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), <s>abhinaya</s> (acting), <s>aṅgahāra</s> (gestures), and the like. And
The activity of sentient and insentient beings is designated as 'the world' (<s>loka</s>);
<s>nyāya</s> (logic) is that whose essence is the science of reasoning; <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is <s>śruti</s> (the <s>Vedas</s>) together with <s>smṛti</s> (the law-codes). || 163 ||

children.text: चराचराणां स्थावरजङ्गमानां भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः यथास्थिति लोक इति संज्ञिता समाख्या[ता] लोकसंज्ञिता
लोके विज्ञायते । हेतुविद्या तर्कशास्त्रम् आत्मा यस्य स हेतुविद्यात्मको न्यायोऽत्र गृह्यते । श्रुतिः वेदः सह स्मृत्या मन्वादिप्रणीतया वर्तते इति सस्मृतिरागमो वेदितव्यः ॥
children.translated_text: it is known in the world. The science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of logic — that whose essence is this is '<s>hetuvidyātmaka</s>'; <s>nyāya</s> (logic) is what is accepted here. <s>Śruti</s> is the <s>Vedas</s>; together with <s>smṛti</s>, the codes composed by <s>Manu</s> and others — thus '<s>sasmṛti āgama</s>' (scripture with the law-codes) should be understood.
The activity, the natural behavior, of sentient and insentient beings (<s>carācara</s>), of mobile and immobile creatures — that is designated as '<s>loka</s>' (the world), so called —
If anything is employed in those various [domains] in a manner that is not properly established,
due to the poet's carelessness, it would be called a contradiction with place and the like. || 164 ||

children.text: तेषु तेषु यथोक्तेषु देशादिष्वागमपर्यन्तेषु अयथारूढं तत्तद्विधिप्रतिषेधातिक्रमाद् वैपरी[त्येन] यदि किञ्चिदर्थरूपं प्रवर्तते प्रयोगेषु कवेः प्रयोक्तुः प्रमादाद् विस्मरणहेतोः यथारूढं यदि किञ्चिन्न वर्तत इत्यपि पाठः । अर्थस्तु स एव । तदेवं तद्यथा आरूढं प्रवृत्तं देशविरोधीति उच्यते । आदिशब्देन कलादिपरिग्रहः । देशादिभिर्विरोधो बाधा अस्तीति कृत्वा, देशादयोऽन्यथा व्यवस्थिताः, अन्यथा च कल्प्यन्त इति तादृशी तैर्बाध्यते ॥
children.translated_text: In those various domains as described — from place and the like up to scripture — if anything of the nature of meaning is employed in a manner not properly established, through the transgression of the respective prescriptions and prohibitions, contrarily — in compositions, due to the poet's, the composer's, carelessness, due to the cause of forgetfulness. There is also the reading: 'if anything properly established is not present.' The meaning, however, is the same. Thus, that which has been improperly employed is called a contradiction with place. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), the arts and the rest are included. The contradiction, the conflict, with place and the like exists — meaning: the places and the like are established in one way, but are conceived otherwise — thus such a [statement] is violated by them.
The <s>Malaya</s> breeze, fragrant from touching camphor trees;
elephants born in the <s>Kaliṅga</s> forest, mostly of the deer variety. || 165 ||

children.text: कर्पूरपादपानामामर्शे[न संस]र्गेण सुरभिः सुगन्धिर्मलयानिलः । [इद]मद्रिलक्षणदेशविरुद्धमुदाहृतम्, मलयपर्वते कर्पूरसम्भूतेरयथारूढत्वात् । कलिङ्गो नाम वनमरण्यं तत्र तस्माद् वा संभूता मतङ्गजा हस्तिनः मृगप्राया मृगलक्षणा हस्तिजातिः प्राया भूयसी ये[षु] तया वा प्रायाः समधिका मृगप्रायाः । एतद् वनरूपदेशव्याहतम् । कलिङ्गवनजन्मनां हस्तिनां भद्रजाति प्रायत्वात् ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>Malaya</s> breeze is fragrant through contact with, through touching, the camphor trees. This is illustrated as a contradiction with mountain-type place (<s>deśa</s>), since the birth of camphor on Mount <s>Malaya</s> is not properly established. The <s>Kaliṅga</s> forest — from that forest, or in that forest, the elephants (<s>mataṅgajas</s>) that are born are mostly of the deer variety, that is, of the nature of deer — the elephant species being predominant among deer there, or predominating over deer. This is contradicted by the forest-type place, since elephants born in the <s>Kaliṅga</s> forest are predominantly of the <s>bhadra</s> (noble) variety.
The <s>Chola</s> lands on the banks of the <s>Kāverī</s> are dark with black aloe-wood;
such is the manner of speech that contradicts place. || 166 ||

children.text: कावेरी नाम नदी । तस्यास्तीरे तद्रूपा वा भूमयः । चोलाश्चोलजनपदरूपाः कालैः कृष्णैरगरुभिः श्यामा नीला । इदं राष्ट्ररूपं देशविरुद्धम् । चोलराष्ट्रस्वभावानां कावेरीतीरभूमीनां कालागरुशून्यत्वात् ।
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāverī</s> is a well-known river. Its banks, or the lands of that nature. The <s>Chola</s> lands, of the <s>Chola</s> kingdom, are dark, dark-hued, with black aloe-wood (<s>agaru</s>). This is a contradiction with the kingdom-type place, since the lands of the <s>Kāverī</s> banks, being by nature <s>Chola</s> territory, are devoid of black aloe-wood.

children.text: देशविरोधं निगमयति । देशोऽद्रिवनादि[ना] यथोक्तेन विरोधो बाधा यस्यामिति देशविरोधिन्या [वाचः] वाक्यस्य ईदृशमेवंविधं प्रस्थानं स्वरूपं वेदितव्यमिति ॥
children.translated_text: He concludes the discussion of place-contradiction. The speech, the statement, that has a contradiction — a conflict — with place as described, characterized by mountains, forests, and the like — such is its manner, its nature, that should be understood.
Illustrating the contradiction with time (<s>kāla</s>), he says —
The lotus-bed blooms at night; the <s>kumud</s> (night-lotus) bed opens in daytime.

children.text: नक्तं रात्रौ उन्निद्रा विकसिता पद्मिनी, रात्रिरूपकालविरुद्धमेतत् । पद्मिन्या नक्तं प्रबोधासम्भवात् । कुमुद्वती कुमुदिनी स्फुटति विकसति अह्नि दिने । एतद् दिवसरूपसमयविरुद्धम्, दिवा कुमुद्वतीविकासाभावात् ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Unnidrā</s>' (blooming, awakened) at night — this is a contradiction with the time characterized by night, since the lotus does not bloom at night. The <s>kumudvatī</s> (night-lotus bed) opens, blooms, during the day — this is a contradiction with the time characterized by daytime, since the night-lotus does not open during the day.
The summer has <s>niculas</s> (barringtonia trees) in full bloom; the hot season has cloudy, overcast days. || 167 ||
The rainy season has the pleasing songs of swans; the autumn has peacocks dancing in a frenzy;
the early winter (<s>hemanta</s>) has a spotless sun; the late winter (<s>śiśira</s>) has praiseworthy sandalwood. || 168 ||

children.text: मधुर्वसन्त उत्फुल्लः कुसुमितो निचुलो वञ्जुलोऽस्मिन्निति उत्फुल्लनिचुलः । निदाघो ग्रीष्मः मेघैर्दुर्दिनो मलिनः । श्रव्या मधुरा हंसानां गिरः शब्दा यासु इति श्रव्यहंसगिरो वर्षाः प्रावृट् । आमत्ता वर्हिण्यो मयूर्यो यस्यामिति आमत्तबर्हिणी शरत् । निर्मल आदित्यो यस्मिन्निति निर्मलादित्यो हेमन्तः । शिशिरः श्लाघ्यं सेव्यं चन्दनम् अस्मिन्निति श्लाघ्यचन्दनः । सर्वमेतद् ऋतुषट्कलक्षणं कालविरुद्धं मध्वादिषु ऋतुषु उत्फुल्लनिचुलादीनामसम्भवात् ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Madhu</s>' (spring) — the spring season; '<s>utphulla-nicula</s>' means the <s>nicula</s> (<s>vañjula</s>, barringtonia tree) has bloomed, blossomed. '<s>Nidāgha</s>' (summer) — the hot season; darkened by clouds (<s>durdina</s>). '<s>Śravyahaṃsagiraḥ</s>' — the rainy season (<s>varṣā</s>), in which the sweet, melodious sounds of swans are heard. '<s>Āmattabarhiṇī</s>' — autumn (<s>śarat</s>), in which the peahens are intoxicated. '<s>Nirmalāditya</s>' — the early winter (<s>hemanta</s>), in which the sun is clear. '<s>Śiśira</s>' (late winter) — '<s>ślāghyacandana</s>' means it has praiseworthy, enjoyable sandalwood. All of this, characterized by the six seasons, is contradictory with time — since the blooming of <s>nicula</s> and the like is impossible in spring and the other seasons [as described].
He concludes the contradiction with time —
Thus the course of the contradiction with time has been shown to be of such a kind;
the path of the contradiction with craft is briefly indicated as follows. || 169 ||

children.text: कालेन रात्र्यादिना यथोक्तेन विरोधस्य व्याघातस्य भारतीविषयस्य ईदृशी गतिः प्रस्थानं दर्शिता । कलया नृत्यगीतादिविद्यया विरोधस्य वचनगोचरस्य मार्गः प्रस्थानं मनाक् किञ्चिद् उद्दिश्यते उदाह्रियते यथेति दर्शयति ॥
children.translated_text: The course, the direction, of the contradiction with time — with night and so forth as described — in the domain of speech, has been shown to be of such a kind. The path, the direction, of the contradiction with craft (<s>kalā</s>) — the arts such as dance, song, and the like — in the domain of expression, is briefly, in some measure, indicated, illustrated — he shows with 'as follows.'
The <s>sthāyin bhāvas</s> (permanent emotions) of the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiments are anger and wonder;
and this <s>bhinnamārga</s> (broken mode) with complete seven notes proceeds. || 170 ||

children.text: वीरश्च शृङ्गारश्च [तयोर्वीर]शृङ्गारयो रसयोः प्रभवौ भावौ मनोवस्थाविशेषलक्षणौ क्रोधश्च विस्मयश्च क्रोधविस्मयौ स्थायिनौ यावद्रसमवस्थानात् । न तु व्यभिचारिभाववदस्थायिनौ । पूर्णाः समग्राः सप्त ऋषभमध्यमगान्धारषड्जधैवत्पञ्चमनिषादाख्याः स्वरा यस्मिन्निति पूर्णसप्तस्वराः । [ते सन्ति] यस्मिन्निति पूर्णसप्तस्वरः सोऽयं भिन्नमार्गो गान्धर्वप्रकारः कश्चित् प्रवर्तते । एतत् कलाविरुद्धम् । क्रोधविस्मययोः स्थायिनोर्भावयोः शृङ्गारवीरयोरयोनित्वेन कलायां व्यवस्थानात् । रौद्राद्भुतयोरेव हि क्रोधविस्मयौ स्थायिनौ भावौ तत्र व्यवस्थाप्येते । वीरशृङ्गारयोस्तु उत्साहरती एव स्थायिनौ भावौ । अन्यतरस्वरहीनस्यैव च भिन्नमार्गतया व्यवस्थानादिति ॥
children.translated_text: Of the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) — of those two <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), the originating <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), the mental states of a particular character, anger and wonder — are the <s>sthāyin bhāvas</s> (permanent emotions), abiding as long as the <s>rasa</s> endures, not transient like the <s>vyabhicārin bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions). '<s>Pūrṇa-sapta-svara</s>' — the complete seven notes, called <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, and <s>niṣāda</s>. That which has the complete seven notes — that <s>bhinnamārga</s> (broken mode), a certain type of musical practice (<s>gāndharva</s>), proceeds. This is contradictory with craft (<s>kalā</s>). Since in the science of the arts, anger and wonder are established as <s>sthāyin bhāvas</s> not of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>vīra</s> but of <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) respectively. For indeed, anger and wonder are the <s>sthāyin bhāvas</s> established only for <s>raudra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s>. But for <s>vīra</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) and <s>rati</s> (love) alone are the <s>sthāyin bhāvas</s>. And the <s>bhinnamārga</s> (broken mode) is established as lacking one or another note.
Extending the contradiction with craft, he says —
In this manner, let the contradiction in the sixty-four arts be properly understood;
its form will become manifest in the section on the arts. || 171 ||

children.text: इत्थमनेन प्रकारेण कलानां कलारूपाणां चतुःषष्टौ द्विविधायामपि विरोधः तद्व्यवस्थातिक्रम[

)रूपो वि]षयः साधु सम्यक् नीयताम् अनुगम्यताम् । क्व पुनरियं कलाचतुःषष्टिः परिज्ञायते, यतस्तद्विरोधगतिरनाकुला स्यादित्याह— तस्या इत्यादि । तस्याः कलाचतुःषष्ट्या रूपम् स्वभावोऽर्थतः [शब्दतश्चा]विर्भविष्यति । यथावदवगम्यते । कलापरिच्छेदे चतुर्थकलापरिच्छेदोऽस्य दण्डिनोऽस्ति स त्विह न प्रवर्तते । यद् वा कलानां परिच्छेदेऽभ्यासे सति तस्याः कलाचतुःषष्टे रूपमाविर्भविष्यति । तस्मात् कलाभ्यासः करणीयः, यतस्तद्विरोधः सर्वो यथावदवगम्यते इति ॥
children.translated_text: Where then is this system of sixty-four arts to be learned, so that the understanding of contradiction with them may be unconfused? He says 'of that' and so forth. Of that system of sixty-four arts, the form, the nature, will become manifest both in substance and in words — will be properly understood — in the section on the arts. <s>Daṇḍin</s> has a fourth section on the arts, but it does not appear here. Or, when the study, the practice, of the arts has been accomplished, the form of that system of sixty-four arts will become manifest. Therefore, the practice of the arts should be undertaken, so that all contradiction with them may be properly understood.
In this manner, by this method, let the contradiction — the transgression of the established conventions — in the sixty-four arts, in both their aspects, be properly, correctly, understood, followed.
Illustrating contradiction with common practice, he says —
An elephant with shaking mane, a horse with sharp horns,
this castor-oil plant heavy with substance, the <s>khadira</s> (acacia) tree without substance. || 172 ||

children.text: सुगमम् । हस्त्यादेः तुरङ्गमादेरिव केशराद्यसम्भवादीदृशं लोकविरोधि वचनमिति उक्तरूपोऽयं विरोधः ॥
children.translated_text: Easy to understand. Since mane and the like are impossible for an elephant as they are for a horse and the like, such speech is contradictory with common practice — this is the stated type of contradiction.
Thus this contradiction with common practice is condemned by all.

children.text: लौकिको लोकविदित एव अत एव सर्वैः शिष्टै[रन्यै]श्च गर्हितो निन्दितः । नैवेदृशं कश्चित् स्वस्थ[ः/?/] प्रयुङ्क्ते । केवलं लोकविरुद्धो भवन्नेवं भवेदिति इत्थं सम्भवमात्रेण दर्शितः ॥
children.translated_text: It is known in the world, evident to all — and therefore condemned, censured, by all the learned and by others too. No one of sound mind would ever employ such a thing. It has been shown merely as a theoretical possibility, to demonstrate the kind of result that would follow from contradicting common practice.
The contradiction with the sciences of reasoning, called logic (<s>nyāya</s>), is now illustrated. || 173 ||

children.text:
हेतुविद्यासु आन्वीक्षिकीषु न्याय [इत्य]ा/?/ख्या[युक्ता]सु इति न्यायाख्यासु उद्देशे
न्यायशब्दोपादानात् । एवमनुसृतो विरो[धो] निर्दिश्यते ॥
children.translated_text: In the sciences of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), those called <s>nyāya</s> (logic), that is, in <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (the science of inquiry), named with the word '<s>nyāya</s>' — since the word '<s>nyāya</s>' has been employed in the initial enumeration. The contradiction thus pursued is illustrated.
The <s>Sugata</s> (the Buddha) has truly spoken: the <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned phenomena) are imperishable;

children.text: तथा हि सा चकोराक्षी स्थितैवाद्यापि मे हृदि ॥ १७४ ॥
children.translated_text: for indeed, that doe-eyed woman remains in my heart even to this day. || 174 ||

children.text: सुगतस्तथागतः संस्कारान् सम्भवहेतुप्रत्ययैः क्रियन्त इति पदार्थानविनश्वरान् नित्यानक्षणिकान् सत्यमाहाब्रवीत् । सत्यमिति वचनविशेषणम् । कथं सत्यमिति ? तदेव समर्थ्यते । तथाहि समर्थने । सा काचिदिष्टा चकोराक्षी स्त्री मे मम हृदि मनसि अद्यापि चिर[कालादा]रभ्य स्थिता इति । यदि तु संस्कारा नश्वराः, कथमेवं घटते ? तदेतत् न्यायविरुद्धम् । संस्काराणां सर्वेषां सौगते न्यायशास्त्रे प्रतिक्षणं विशरारु [त]या व्यवस्थापनादिति ॥
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (the Buddha), has truly spoken that the <s>saṃskāras</s> — entities produced by causal conditions and factors — are imperishable, permanent, not momentary. '<s>Satyam</s>' (truly) qualifies the speech. How so, truly? He demonstrates that very point. '<s>Tathā hi</s>' introduces the demonstration. That certain beloved doe-eyed woman remains in my heart, in my mind, even to this day, from a long time past. But if the <s>saṃskāras</s> were perishable, how could this be consistent? This is contradictory with logic (<s>nyāya</s>). Because in the Buddhist logical system, all <s>saṃskāras</s> are established as perishing at every moment.
By the <s>Kāpilas</s> (Sāṃkhya philosophers), the arising of what is non-existent is described as truly so;
for arisings of non-existent things are indeed observed by us. || 175 ||

children.text: कापिलैः सांख्यैरसतां शक्तिरूपेणाप्यविद्यमानानां उद्भूतिरुत्पादः स्थान एव सत्यमेव । स्थान इत्येकारान्तो निपातो युक्तार्थसूचकः । उपवर्ण्यते विवृतः । यस्माद् असतामेवार्थानाम् उद्भवा जन्मान्यस्माभिर्दृश्यन्ते । एतदपि हेतुविद्याव्याहतम् । सांख्यमते सतामेव भावानां कथञ्चिदाविर्भावस्य व्यवस्थापनात् ॥
children.translated_text: By the <s>Kāpilas</s>, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> philosophers, the arising, the production, of non-existent things — those not existing even in the form of potency — is described as truly so, as a fact. '<s>Sthāna</s>' is a particle ending in '<s>e</s>' that indicates an established truth. Because arisings, births, of non-existent things are indeed observed by us. This too is contradictory with the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>). Since in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine, it is established that only existent things somehow manifest, not that non-existent things arise.
He concludes the contradiction with logic —
This is the course of the contradiction with logic; let it be observed everywhere.
Now, the direction of the contradiction with scripture will be shown. || 176 ||

children.text: न्यायविरोधस्य हेतुविद्याव्याहतेः काव्ये यस्य यस्य गतिः सैषा यथोक्तप्रकारा सर्वत्र अन्यत्रापि यथासम्भवं दृश्यतामवगम्यताम् । अथानन्तरमागमेन धर्मशास्त्रसहितेन वेदेन विरोधस्य बाधाया भारतीभूमेः प्रस्थानं नीतिः दर्शयिष्यते उदाह्रियते ॥
children.translated_text: The course of the contradiction with logic, the obstruction by the science of reasoning, in poetry — this course, of such a kind as described, should be observed, understood, everywhere, in other cases too, as appropriate. Now, next, the direction, the approach, of the contradiction with scripture (<s>āgama</s>) — the <s>Vedas</s> together with the <s>dharmaśāstras</s> — in the domain of speech, will be shown, illustrated.
Even these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who have not established the sacred fires, though they have begotten sons, perform
the <s>Vaiśvānarī iṣṭi</s> (fire-sacrifice), adorned with unblemished conduct. || 177 ||

children.text: आहितो वैदिकेन विधिना परिगृहीतोऽग्निः परिणयकालभावी यैरिति आहिताग्नयः । न तथा अनाहिताग्नयो ये [ते] अपि । अपिशब्दो योगं सूचयति । एते विप्राः । जाताः पुत्रा एषामिति जातपुत्राः । विश्वानरो देवता अस्यामिति वैश्वानरीमिष्टिमिज्याम् । आग्नेय[यज्ञं] वितन्वते कुर्वन्ति । अक्लिष्टः परिशुद्धः आचारश्चारित्रं शास्त्रविहितं भूषणमलङ्कारो येषामित्यक्लिष्टाचारभूषणाः । इदमागमविरुद्धम् । ये हि [साग्निका] उत्पन्नतनयाश्च [त एव] वैश्वानरं यागमनुतिष्ठन्तीति श्रुतेः । कथमन्यथा अक्लिष्टाचारा इति ॥
children.translated_text: '<s>Āhitāgni</s>' — one who has received, accepted, the sacred fire by the Vedic rite, the fire that comes into existence at the time of marriage. Those who have not done so are '<s>anāhitāgni</s>' (ones who have not established the fires) — yet even they. The particle '<s>api</s>' (even) indicates their conjunction [with the ritual]. These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who have begotten sons (<s>jātaputra</s>). They perform, carry out, the <s>Vaiśvānarī iṣṭi</s>, the sacrifice whose deity is <s>Viśvānara</s> — that is, the fire-sacrifice (<s>āgneya yajña</s>). Adorned with unblemished conduct — those whose pure, scripture-ordained behavior is their ornament. This is contradictory with scripture (<s>āgama</s>). For indeed, by <s>Vedic</s> injunction, only those who have established the fires and have begotten sons perform the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> sacrifice. How could it be otherwise and still be called 'unblemished conduct'?
This one, though not yet having undergone the sacred thread ceremony (<s>upanayana</s>), studied the <s>Vedas</s> from his teacher;
a crystal, naturally pure, does not require polishing. || 178 ||

children.text: असौ विवक्षितः कश्चित् । अनुपनीतोऽप्रयुक्तवैदिकसंस्कारविशेषोऽपि गुरोः सकाशाद् वेदा[न्] सामादीन् अधिजगेऽधीतवान् । तथाहि, स्वभावेन प्रकृत्यैव न संस्कारतः । शुद्धो निर्मलः स्फटिको मणिः संस्कारमुत्कर्षाधानं नापेक्षते । इदमपि आगमव्याहतम् । उपनीतो वेदानधीयीतेति श्रुतेः । कथमन्यथा शुद्धिरिति ॥
children.translated_text: This certain intended person, though not yet invested with the sacred thread (<s>anupanīta</s>), that is, without having undergone the particular Vedic sacrament, studied the <s>Vedas</s> — the <s>Sāma</s> and the like — from his teacher. As the analogy states: a crystal gem is naturally, by its very nature, not through polishing, pure, spotless — it does not require polishing, the imposition of refinement. This too is contradictory with scripture. Because by <s>Vedic</s> injunction, one who has undergone <s>upanayana</s> alone should study the <s>Vedas</s>. How can there be purity otherwise?
Yet this entire contradiction may sometimes, through the skill of the poet,
transcend the enumeration of faults and enter the path of qualities. || 179 ||

children.text: सकलोऽप्येष विरोधो देशादिकृतः.........एव कश्चिद् दोषरूपेण गणनां संख्यानं दोषात्मतामुत्क्रम्य परित्यज्य गुणानां वीथीं पदवीं गुणस्वभावतां विगाहते स्वीकरोति कदाचित् । न सर्वदा । कुतः ? कवेः प्रयो[गस्य] कौशलात् तादृग्विषयपरिग्रहलक्षणात् नैपुणात् कारणात् । न तु यथा तथा वेति ॥
children.translated_text: This entire contradiction — caused by place and the like — though indeed being a fault, some particular one, transcending, abandoning, the enumeration, the counting, as a fault, its identity as a fault — enters the path, the lane, of qualities, the nature of a quality — sometimes. Not always. Why? Through the skill, the expertise characterized by the appropriate choice of subject matter, of the poet, of the practitioner. Not in just any manner.
By the power of that king, his gardens came into being,
as the abode of wish-fulfilling trees with garments as their tender shoots. || 180 ||

children.text: तस्याभिमतस्य राज्ञः कस्यचित् प्रभावेण पुण्यानुभावात् अतिमानुषात् तस्यो

द्यानानि । आर्द्राणि स्निग्धानि अंशुकानि वस्त्राण्येव प्रवालानि किसलयानि येषामित्यार्द्रांशुकप्रवालानां सुरशाखिंनां कल्पवृक्षाणामाम्पदं सद्म । आस्पदार्थस्य एकार्थ्येन विवक्षितत्वात् उद्यानादिबहुत्वसमानाधिकरण्येऽपि एकवचनम् । जज्ञिरे जातानि । पुण्यप्रभावस्याचिन्त्यत्वात् मनुष्यलोकेऽपि सुरशाखिनः सम्भवः । एवमुक्त
children.translated_text: gardens: the abode, the dwelling-place, of wish-fulfilling trees (<s>suravṛkṣa</s>, <s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>), whose tender shoots (<s>pravāla</s>) are moist, lustrous garments (<s>aṃśuka</s>) — came into being, arose. The singular number, despite the plurality of gardens and the like that share the same reference, is due to the intention of expressing the meaning of '<s>āspada</s>' (abode) as a single concept. Because the meritorious power is inconceivable, even wish-fulfilling trees can occur in the world of men. As similarly stated
by the teacher <s>Śūra</s> (<s>Ācāryaśūra</s>) —
[place], a lotus arose, [though] without mud.
By the power of his merit, there in that
with the white row of its stamen-teeth. ||
As if with disdain, it laughed at <s>Māra</s> (the Evil One),
Thus there is no contradiction with place.
By the power, the meritorious influence, superhuman, of that certain esteemed king, his
A harsh wind blew, portending the destruction of kings,
scattering, along with the pollen of <s>kadamba</s> flowers, the blossoms of the <s>saptacchada</s> (seven-leaved tree). || 181 ||

children.text: खरो रूक्षो मारुतः कदम्बरजसा कदम्बपुष्परेणुना सह सप्तच्छदोद्गमान् सप्तपर्णकुसुमानि धुन्वन् विकिरन् राज्ञां विनाशस्य पिशुनः पञ्चतां सूचयन् चचार प्रववौ । यद्यपि एकदा कदम्बसप्तपर्णकुसुमासम्भवः कदम्बकुसुमस्य प्रावृषेण्यत्वात् सप्तच्छदपुष्पस्य च शारदत्वात्, तथापि राजविनाशनिमित्तमीदृशमौत्पातिकं सम्भवतीति न कालविरोधः ॥
children.translated_text: A harsh, rough wind, along with the pollen of <s>kadamba</s> flowers — scattering, dispersing, the blossoms of the <s>saptacchada</s> (<s>saptaparṇa</s>, seven-leaved tree) — portending, indicating, the destruction, the death, of kings — blew, proceeded. Although the simultaneous occurrence of <s>kadamba</s> and <s>saptaparṇa</s> blossoms is impossible, since <s>kadamba</s> flowers belong to the rainy season and <s>saptacchada</s> flowers to autumn, nevertheless such a portentous phenomenon, signaling the death of a king, is possible — thus there is no contradiction with time.
The song issuing from the mouths of women, frightened by the excessive swaying of the swing,
intensified the passion of lovers, due to the irregularity of rhythm. || 182 ||

children.text: दोला प्रेङ्खा तस्या अतिप्रेरणादतिकम्पनाद् । [अन]तिमात्रतत्प्रेरणतो हि न भवेदपि लयवैषम्यम् । तस्मात् त्रस्तस्य भीतवधूजनस्य स्त्रीणां मुखादुद्भवं गेयं गीतं कामिनां रागमवर्धयत् उद्दीपितवत् । कुतः ? लयस्य क्रियामानकाललक्षणस्य द्रुतमध्यादिप्रभेदस्य तत्कालपरिदृष्टस्य वैषम्यादयथाकालं प्रवृत्तेः । एतच्च विरुद्धम् । कथं हि लयविषममलक्षणदुष्टं गेयं रञ्जकं भवति ? तथापि ईदृशं स्थूलं गीतं शीत्कारायमाणं कामिनां सुतरां रञ्जकम् । कि मव हि तेषामरञ्जकमिति न कालविरोधः ॥
children.translated_text: From the excessive swaying, the excessive oscillation, of the swing (<s>dolā</s>, <s>preṅkhā</s>). For a rhythmic irregularity would not occur from moderate swaying. Therefore, from the mouths of the frightened women, the song, the melody, intensified, inflamed the passion of lovers. Why? Due to the irregularity, the untimely progression, of rhythm (<s>laya</s>), characterized by the time-measure of the action being performed, with its varieties of fast, medium, and so forth, as observed at that time. This is contradictory [with craft]. For how could a song irregular in rhythm, faulty and ill-formed, be pleasing? Nevertheless, such coarse singing, gasping and panting, is all the more pleasing to lovers. For indeed, what is not pleasing to them? — thus there is no contradiction with craft.
This lover, distressed by the agony of separation from his beloved,
considers even the fire (<s>havyavāhana</s>) to be colder than the rays of the moon. || 183 ||

children.text: ऐन्दवादिन्दोः सम्बन्धिनोऽर्चिषो रश्मेरप्यधिकशिशिरं शीतं हव्यवाहमग्निं गणयति । [कः ?] अधैर्योऽयं विवक्षितः कश्चित् कामी । [कथम् ?] अबलायाः प्रियाया विरहो दुःखं स एव वा क्लेशः । तेन विक्लवो विप्लुतः सन् । विरहविकारविप्लुतस्य हि तथा प्रतिभास इति न लोकविरोधः ॥
children.translated_text: He considers even the fire (<s>havyavāhana</s>), the carrier of oblations, to be colder than even the moonbeams (<s>aindu arciṣ</s>), the rays belonging to the moon. Who? This intended certain lover, devoid of fortitude. How so? Distressed, overwhelmed, by the agony of separation from his beloved woman, by that suffering. For indeed, one overwhelmed by the distortion of separation perceives things in such a way — thus there is no contradiction with common practice.
Though measurable, you are immeasurable; though whole, you are without parts;
though one, you are many — homage to you, O one of universal form! || 184 ||

children.text: प्रमेयः परिच्छेद्योऽपि व्यक्तक्षित्यादिमूर्त्त्यपेक्षया अप्रमेयोऽसि अव्यक्तः परमरूपतः । प्रमेयोऽपि वा

अनुमानप्रमाणगम्यत्वादप्रमेयोऽसि [इन्द्रिया]विषयत्वात् । सकलः सावयवोऽपि [आ]रब्धक्षित्यादिमूर्तत्वात्, निष्कलो निरवयवः असि परमात्मरूपतः । एकोऽपि त्वं शाश्वतब्रह्मरूपेण, अनेकोऽसि परिणामवैचित्राद् इत्येवं विश्वमूर्तये सर्वमयाय [ते] तुभ्यं नमः । इतीदृशं न न्यायविरुद्धम्, एवंविधत्वाद् ब्रह्मणः परमस्येति ॥
children.translated_text: being accessible to the means of knowledge such as inference — you are immeasurable, being beyond the scope of the senses. Though whole (<s>sakala</s>), possessing parts, because of your composite manifest forms of earth and the like — you are without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), partless, in your nature as the supreme Self. Though one, in your eternal <s>Brahman</s> form — you are many, due to the variety of transformations. Thus to you of universal form (<s>viśvamūrti</s>), who pervades all — homage. This is not contradictory with logic, because <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme, is indeed of such a nature.
Though measurable, delimited, in respect of your manifest forms such as earth and the like — you are immeasurable, unmanifest, in your supreme nature. Or, though measurable,
The princess of <s>Pañcāla</s> was the wife of the five sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
yet she was also the foremost among virtuous women — for the decree of destiny is such! || 185 ||

children.text: पञ्चानां यु[धि]ष्ठिरादीनां पाण्डोः पुत्राणां पत्नी पञ्चालकन्यका द्रौपदी बभूव । हन्त न तर्हि दृष्टपञ्चपुरुषा सा कुलस्त्री स्यादिति चेदाह— सतीनां पतिव्रतानां मध्ये अग्रणीः प्रधानभूता चासीत् । कथमेवम् ? दैवो देवसम्बन्धी हि विधिः प्रभाव ईदृशः एवंभूतो यदेवंविधमपि घटते । किमत्र क्रियताम् ? को हि दैवं विधानमप्रमाणयितुं शक्नोति । हिशब्देनेदमेव प्रसिद्धं द्योत्यते । ततश्च नागमविरोधः ।
children.translated_text: The princess of <s>Pañcāla</s>, <s>Draupadī</s>, became the wife of the five sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> — <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others. If one objects: then, having been seen with five husbands, she would not be a virtuous woman of noble family — he says: yet she was also the foremost, the chief, among virtuous, devoted wives. How is this possible? The decree, the power, connected with the gods — destiny — is of such a nature, such that even such a thing can come about. What can be done about it? For who can gainsay the divine decree? By the particle '<s>hi</s>' this very well-known fact is indicated. Therefore there is no contradiction with scripture.
Concluding the treatise on poetics as promised, he says —
The ornaments of word and meaning, the artistic paths both easy and difficult,
and the merits and faults of poetry — all these have been shown in summary. || 186 ||

children.text: काव्यानां शब्दश्चार्थश्च शब्दार्थौ शरीरम् । तयोश्चालंक्रिया शब्दालङ्कारा अर्थालङ्काराश्च । चित्रा नानाप्रकारा सुकराः दुष्कराश्च मार्गा यमकादिरूपाः, चित्रा गुणाः समुदायार्थसम्पत्त्यादयः । दोषाश्च तद्विपक्षाः साधारणा असाधारणाश्च श्लेषविपर्ययादयः । उक्तेन विधिना [एतत् सर्वं] संक्षिप्य समासतो दर्शिताः प्रतिपादिताः ॥
children.translated_text: Of poetry: word and meaning — word and meaning are the body. And the ornamentation of these two — the ornaments of word and the ornaments of meaning. The varied, multifarious, easy and difficult paths (<s>mārga</s>) in the form of <s>yamaka</s> and the like; the varied merits such as the attainment of sentence-meaning and the like; and the faults, their opposites — both common and specific, such as incongruity through <s>śleṣa</s>, reversal, and the like. All this, in the manner stated, has been shown, demonstrated, in summary, in concise form. ||

children.text: दर्शिता नाम । किमतः इति सर्वारम्भस्य तन्निष्ठत्वात् प्रयोजनदर्शनद्वारेण समापयन्नाह—
children.translated_text: They have been shown, indeed. What of it? Since all undertakings have their culmination in their purpose, he concludes by showing the purpose —
approached by speeches that are submissive regarding faults and merits —
One whose intellect has been cultivated through this path shown by the method,

children.text: र्धन्यो युवेव रमते लभते च कीर्तिम् ॥ १८७ ॥
children.translated_text: he delights and also attains fame. || 187 ||
like a fortunate youth approached by doe-eyed women,

children.text: अमुना अनेन मार्गेण काव्यलक्षणविधिना यथावद् दर्शितेन प्रकाशितेन हेतुना, दोषश्च हेयो भागः, गुणश्चोपादेयः । यथोक्तयोस्तयोः कार्यसम्बन्धिनोः व्युत्पन्ना विवेकिनी हानोपादानसमर्था बुद्धि[र्यस्य तादृशः] काव्यदोषगुणज्ञः पुमान् । अत एव वशवर्तिनी[भिरा]यत्ताभिर्वाग्भिः काव्यरूपाभिरनवद्याभिः कृतमभिसरणं स्वरसत एवोपसर्पणमस्मिन्निति वाक्कृताभिसरणः अभिसृतो रमते प्रीतिमनुत्तरामनुभवति । कीर्तिं च
सत्पुरुषतनुमनश्वरीं गुणमर्यो भुव[नातिशा]यिनीमतिमनोहरां लभते प्राप्नोति । उपलक्षणं चैतत् । चतुर्वर्गसिद्धिमपि चाधिगच्छति । यथोक्तं प्रथमे परिच्छेदे
children.translated_text: imperishable like the body of the virtuous, worthy of the limit of merits, surpassing the worlds, supremely captivating — he attains, he obtains. And this is merely indicative. He also achieves the attainment of the four goals of human life. As stated in the first chapter —
How is this illustrated? Like a fortunate man approached by doe-eyed women who are submissive,

children.text: .......सुभगो युवा तरुण इ[व] । यथायं रमते प्रीत्युत्मवं निर्विशति, लभते च कीर्तिं सुभग इति ख्यातिं तथा [व्युत्पन्न]बुद्धिरयमित्युपनेयम् ॥
